ITID-21111.def: Unauthorized replacement of website content with domestic political or election-related messaging, intended to associate the company's public web presence with a partisan position it did not authorize.
ITID-21111.purpose: Captures website defacement where the replacement content pushes a domestic political message tied to an election or partisan cause, rather than a broader ideological or state-attributed narrative.
scopeIncludes: Homepage or key page content replaced with election endorsement, campaign, or partisan messaging
Defacement timed to coincide with a domestic election cycle or ballot measure
Messaging referencing domestic candidates, parties, or referenda
scopeExcludes: State-sponsored propaganda attributed to a foreign government actor (ITID-21112)
General anti-government or protest messaging without an election/partisan angle (ITID-21113)
Political messaging delivered via social media rather than the website (ITID-21200 branch)
ITID-21111.severity: Medium-High. Reputational risk is elevated near active election periods and if the message could be read as a corporate endorsement.
ITID-21111.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the defacement remains live during high-traffic periods or is picked up by media.
ITID-21111.escalation: Escalate to communications/legal immediately given the risk of perceived corporate political endorsement; loop in executive comms for any public statement.
indicators: Unexpected page content referencing election candidates or parties
Web integrity monitoring alert on homepage/CMS content hash change
Public reports or screenshots circulating on social media
vectors: Exploitation of an unpatched CMS or plugin vulnerability
Compromised CMS administrator credentials
Vulnerable third-party web component
rootCauses: Outdated CMS/plugin versions
Lack of file-integrity monitoring on public web content
Weak or reused CMS admin credentials
controls: Web application firewall
CMS patch management
File-integrity monitoring on public web content
MFA on CMS admin accounts
ITID-21111.detection: Web integrity/change-detection monitoring provides direct technical signal; otherwise typically first reported externally.
ITID-21111.response: Restore content from known-good backup, revoke/rotate any compromised CMS credentials, and identify the entry vector before republishing.
metrics: Time-to-restore for defaced pages
Count of political-messaging defacements per election cycle
ITID-21111.notes: Differentiated from ITID-21112 by actor attribution (domestic, not state-sponsored) and from ITID-21113 by having an explicit election/partisan angle rather than general anti-government sentiment.

playbook.name: Response: Domestic Political/Election Messaging Defacement
playbook.description: For a website defacement that inserts domestic political or election-related messaging (candidate endorsements, election misinformation, partisan slogans) onto company-controlled pages.

steps.title: Capture and preserve the defaced content
steps.desc: Screenshot and save the raw HTML/source of the affected page(s) before any remediation begins, noting the exact political claim or messaging inserted.
steps.guidance: Election-related content can attract regulatory or media scrutiny quickly; an accurate, timestamped record protects the company from mischaracterization.

steps.title: Take the affected page(s) offline or serve a maintenance page
steps.desc: Immediately prevent further public visibility of the political messaging.
steps.guidance: Use a CDN-level maintenance page if possible to avoid a longer outage than necessary.
steps.outcome: Defaced content no longer publicly visible.

steps.title: Patch or remove the exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Update the vulnerable CMS/plugin version or close the misconfiguration identified during identification.
steps.outcome: The specific access vector is closed.

steps.title: Restore legitimate content from a known-good backup
steps.desc: Restore the site to its pre-defacement state.
steps.guidance: Verify the backup predates the compromise, not just the defacement, in case the attacker had access for a while before defacing.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector and one concrete improvement (patch cadence, credential hygiene, WAF rule).

steps.title: Determine the access vector used
steps.desc: Review CMS/hosting audit logs to determine how the attacker gained the access needed to alter site content.
steps.guidance: Check for compromised admin credentials, a vulnerable plugin/CMS version, or a misconfigured deployment pipeline.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment using the broadest reasonable lockdown (rotate all CMS credentials) rather than waiting.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS/hosting credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and API keys for all accounts with content-publishing access.

steps.title: Scan for additional backdoor or persistence
steps.desc: Review the file system and CMS for any web shell, unauthorized admin account, or scheduled task the attacker may have added.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean, or additional persistence found and removed.

steps.title: Coordinate a public, politically-neutral statement with PR/Comms
steps.desc: Loop in PR/Comms and Legal to decide whether a public disclaimer distancing the company from the inserted political messaging is warranted.
steps.guidance: Keep the statement factual and non-partisan; avoid amplifying the political content itself.
steps.outcome: Consistent, neutral public messaging issued if needed.

steps.title: Assess whether the content implies a company political endorsement
steps.desc: Determine whether the inserted messaging could be read by the public as the company's own political position, which raises the urgency of the response.
steps.guidance: Loop in Legal/Comms immediately if the content names a specific candidate, party, or ballot measure.
steps.outcome: Risk level and required stakeholders identified.

ITID-21112.def: Unauthorized replacement of website content with propaganda messaging attributed to, or bearing the hallmarks of, a state-sponsored actor, used to advance a geopolitical narrative through the company's public web presence.
ITID-21112.purpose: Captures website defacement where the replacement content is attributed to, or consistent with, a nation-state propaganda operation.
scopeIncludes: Defacement content referencing a foreign government's official narrative or symbols
Defacement correlated with a known state-sponsored threat actor's TTPs or infrastructure
Coordinated defacement across multiple organizations consistent with a state-run influence campaign
scopeExcludes: Domestic political/election messaging with no state attribution (ITID-21111)
Hacktivist collective activity without state attribution (ITID-21120 branch)
ITID-21112.severity: High. State-sponsored attribution carries geopolitical and regulatory notification implications beyond typical defacement.
ITID-21112.escalation: Escalate immediately to CISO, legal, and executive leadership; consider law enforcement/national CERT notification given suspected state involvement.
indicators: Content referencing a foreign state narrative or emblem
Infrastructure/TTP overlap with known state-sponsored threat intelligence
Simultaneous defacement of multiple organizations in the same sector or region
vectors: Exploitation of an unpatched public-facing application
Supply-chain compromise of a web hosting/CDN provider
Compromised privileged web administrator credentials
rootCauses: Unpatched internet-facing infrastructure
Insufficient threat-intelligence-informed monitoring for state-sponsored TTPs
controls: Threat-intelligence-driven monitoring
Web application firewall
CMS patch management
Executive/crisis communications plan
ITID-21112.detection: Web integrity monitoring detects the defacement; threat intelligence correlation is needed to establish state attribution.
ITID-21112.response: Restore content, preserve forensic evidence for attribution, and coordinate any public/regulatory statement with legal and comms.
metrics: Count of state-attributed defacements per year
Time-to-restore
Time-to-attribution
ITID-21112.notes: Scope is limited to cases with credible state attribution; unattributed or domestic political defacement belongs under ITID-21111 or ITID-21113.

playbook.name: Response: State-Sponsored Political Propaganda Defacement
playbook.description: For a website defacement attributed to or bearing the hallmarks of a state-sponsored actor inserting political propaganda onto company-controlled pages.

steps.title: Capture and preserve the defaced content and any attribution indicators
steps.desc: Screenshot and save the raw HTML/source, along with any technical indicators (IPs, TTPs, malware artifacts) that may support attribution to a state-sponsored actor.
steps.guidance: Preserve evidence to the standard needed for law enforcement and national CERT referral.
steps.outcome: Defaced content and indicators preserved with timestamp.

steps.title: Take the affected page(s) offline or serve a maintenance page
steps.desc: Immediately prevent further public visibility of the propaganda content.
steps.outcome: Defaced content no longer publicly visible.

steps.title: Patch or remove the exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Close the specific access vector identified during identification.

steps.title: Restore legitimate content from a known-good, pre-compromise backup
steps.desc: Restore the site to a verified clean state, using a backup confirmed to predate the intrusion.

steps.title: Document the incident, attribution assessment, and hardening recommendations
steps.desc: Record the access vector, indicators, attribution confidence, and concrete hardening improvements for a nation-state threat model.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and shared with threat intelligence function.

steps.title: Determine the access vector and assess for broader compromise
steps.desc: Review CMS/hosting/network logs; state-sponsored actors often use the defacement as a visible symptom of a deeper, longer-running intrusion.
steps.guidance: Treat this as a potential full network compromise investigation, not just a website incident, until ruled out.
steps.outcome: Access vector identified and scope of compromise assessed.
steps.abort: If scope cannot be bounded quickly, escalate to full incident response / threat hunting rather than treating as a simple defacement.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials and isolate potentially compromised systems
steps.desc: Reset CMS/hosting/network credentials broadly and isolate any host suspected of deeper compromise pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Old credentials invalidated; suspected hosts isolated.

steps.title: Conduct a thorough persistence and lateral-movement hunt
steps.desc: State-sponsored actors frequently leave multiple footholds; search broadly for web shells, unauthorized accounts, and lateral movement into adjacent systems.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean across the affected environment, or additional footholds found and removed.

steps.title: Coordinate public statement and regulatory notifications with PR/Comms and Legal
steps.desc: Determine whether a public statement and any regulatory disclosure obligations apply given the state-sponsored attribution.
steps.outcome: Consistent public messaging and any required disclosures issued.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal, executive leadership, and national CERT/law enforcement
steps.desc: State-sponsored activity carries geopolitical and regulatory implications beyond a typical defacement.
steps.outcome: Appropriate external and internal stakeholders notified early.

ITID-21113.def: Unauthorized replacement of website content with anti-government or protest-themed messaging, reflecting general dissent rather than an election-specific or state-attributed narrative.
ITID-21113.purpose: Captures website defacement carrying anti-government or protest messaging that is not tied to a specific election/partisan campaign or confirmed state actor.
scopeIncludes: Messaging protesting government policy, regulation, or authority generally
Messaging referencing a protest movement without a named hacktivist collective claiming credit
scopeExcludes: Election/partisan-specific messaging (ITID-21111)
State-sponsored propaganda with credible attribution (ITID-21112)
Messaging explicitly claimed by a known hacktivist collective (ITID-21121)
ITID-21113.severity: Medium. Reputational exposure depends on how directly the message implicates the company in the protested issue.
ITID-21113.escalation: Escalate to communications for message assessment; escalate further if the protest theme is directly tied to the company's own operations or a live controversy.
indicators: Web content replaced with protest slogans or imagery
Web integrity monitoring alert on public page content
vectors: Exploitation of an unpatched CMS or plugin vulnerability
Compromised CMS administrator credentials
rootCauses: Outdated CMS/plugin versions
Lack of file-integrity monitoring on public web content
controls: Web application firewall
CMS patch management
File-integrity monitoring on public web content
ITID-21113.detection: Web integrity monitoring provides direct technical signal.
ITID-21113.response: Restore content from known-good backup and identify the entry vector before republishing.
metrics: Time-to-restore for defaced pages
ITID-21113.notes: Used when the message is protest/anti-government in tone but lacks a named collective claim (ITID-21121) or a clear election/partisan or state-attribution angle.

playbook.name: Response: Anti-Government/Protest Messaging Defacement
playbook.description: For a website defacement inserting anti-government or protest-movement messaging onto company-controlled pages.

steps.title: Capture and preserve the defaced content
steps.desc: Screenshot and save the raw HTML/source of the affected page(s) before any remediation begins.

steps.title: Take the site offline or serve a maintenance page
steps.desc: Immediately prevent further public visibility of the defaced content.
steps.guidance: Use a CDN-level maintenance page if possible to avoid a longer outage than necessary.
steps.outcome: Defaced content no longer publicly visible.

steps.title: Patch or remove the exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Update the vulnerable CMS/plugin version or close the misconfiguration identified during identification.
steps.outcome: The specific access vector is closed.

steps.title: Restore legitimate content from a known-good backup
steps.desc: Restore the site to its pre-defacement state.
steps.guidance: Verify the backup predates the compromise, not just the defacement.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector and one concrete improvement (patch cadence, credential hygiene, WAF rule).

steps.title: Determine the access vector used
steps.desc: Review CMS/hosting audit logs to determine how the attacker gained the access needed to alter site content.
steps.guidance: Check for compromised admin credentials, a vulnerable plugin/CMS version, or a misconfigured deployment pipeline.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment using the broadest reasonable lockdown (rotate all CMS credentials) rather than waiting.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS/hosting credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and API keys for all accounts with content-publishing access.

steps.title: Scan for additional backdoor or persistence
steps.desc: Review the file system and CMS for any web shell, unauthorized admin account, or scheduled task the attacker may have added.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean, or additional persistence found and removed.

steps.title: Coordinate a public statement with PR/Comms if the defacement was widely seen
steps.desc: Loop in PR/Comms to decide whether a public acknowledgment is warranted, and to avoid the company appearing to take a side in the underlying protest movement.
steps.guidance: Keep any statement neutral and focused on the security incident rather than the political content.

ITID-21114.def: Website defacement with political content, not clearly matching the domestic/election, state-sponsored, or anti-government/protest leaves under this Type.
ITID-21114.purpose: Catch-all for website defacement carrying political messaging that does not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a more specific political-messaging leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-21111, ITID-21112, or ITID-21113
ITID-21114.severity: Reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-21114.escalation: Reclassify once the specific political narrative and attribution are clarified.
indicators: Political-themed content replacing a public web page, of unclear specific narrative or attribution
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Web application firewall with virtual patching
File integrity monitoring on public-facing web content
CMS admin account MFA enforcement
ITID-21114.detection: Same web integrity telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-21114.response: Restore content and investigate to reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-21114.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Political Messaging Defacement
playbook.description: Catch-all response for a website defacement inserting political messaging that does not clearly fit the domestic-election, state-sponsored, or anti-government/protest categories.

steps.title: Capture and preserve the defaced content
steps.desc: Screenshot and save the raw HTML/source of the affected page(s), and classify the political messaging as precisely as possible to inform response.
steps.outcome: Defaced content preserved with timestamp; content characterized.

steps.title: Take the site offline or serve a maintenance page
steps.desc: Immediately prevent further public visibility of the defaced content.
steps.outcome: Defaced content no longer publicly visible.

steps.title: Patch or remove the exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Close the access vector identified during identification.

steps.title: Restore legitimate content from a known-good backup
steps.desc: Restore the site to its pre-defacement state.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector and one concrete improvement, and note whether a more specific ITID category should have been used.

steps.title: Determine the access vector used
steps.desc: Review CMS/hosting audit logs to determine how the attacker gained the access needed to alter site content.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment using the broadest reasonable lockdown.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS/hosting credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and API keys for all accounts with content-publishing access.

steps.title: Notify PR/Comms if public visibility warrants a statement
steps.desc: Loop in PR/Comms to decide whether a public acknowledgment is warranted.

ITID-21121.def: Unauthorized replacement of website content where a specific, previously identified hacktivist group claims credit for the act, typically via a signature, logo, or public claim of responsibility.
ITID-21121.purpose: Captures website defacement explicitly claimed by a named, known hacktivist collective.
scopeIncludes: Defacement signed with a known collective's name/logo
Defacement followed by a public claim-of-responsibility post from a tracked group
scopeExcludes: Claim-of-responsibility social media posts themselves, tracked separately (ITID-23432)
Mass/coordinated campaigns hitting many unrelated organizations at once (ITID-21122)
Single-target cause-driven defacement with no named-group attribution (ITID-21123)
ITID-21121.severity: Medium-High. Attribution to a tracked collective allows threat-intel-informed response but the reputational hit is similar to other defacements.
ITID-21121.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the group has a history of follow-on attacks against the company.
ITID-21121.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence for group profiling and to communications for message assessment.
indicators: Defacement page signed with a tracked collective's branding
Correlated claim-of-responsibility post on the group's known channels
vectors: Exploitation of an unpatched CMS or plugin vulnerability
Compromised CMS administrator credentials
rootCauses: Outdated CMS/plugin versions
Public profile making the company a visible target for the collective's stated cause
controls: Threat-intelligence tracking of known hacktivist collectives
Web application firewall
CMS patch management
ITID-21121.detection: Web integrity monitoring detects the defacement; threat intel confirms group attribution.
ITID-21121.response: Restore content, correlate with threat intelligence on the named group, and assess likelihood of follow-on activity.
metrics: Count of defacements attributed to tracked collectives
Time-to-restore
ITID-21121.notes: Scope is the defacement act itself; the group's own claim-of-responsibility social post is tracked separately under ITID-23432 to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Known Hacktivist Collective Claimed Defacement
playbook.description: For a confirmed website defacement where a known hacktivist group has publicly claimed responsibility.

steps.title: Capture and preserve the defaced content
steps.desc: Screenshot and save the raw HTML/source of the defaced page before any remediation begins.
steps.guidance: This evidence may be needed for law enforcement referral and for the post-incident PR narrative.

steps.title: Take the site offline or serve a maintenance page
steps.desc: Immediately prevent further public visibility of the defaced content.
steps.guidance: Use a CDN-level maintenance page if possible to avoid a longer outage than necessary.
steps.outcome: Defaced content no longer publicly visible.

steps.title: Patch or remove the exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Update the vulnerable CMS/plugin version or close the misconfiguration identified during identification.
steps.outcome: The specific access vector is closed.

steps.title: Restore legitimate content from a known-good backup
steps.desc: Restore the site to its pre-defacement state.
steps.guidance: Verify the backup predates the compromise, not just the defacement, in case the attacker had access for a while before defacing.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector and one concrete improvement (patch cadence, credential hygiene, WAF rule).

steps.title: Determine the access vector used
steps.desc: Review CMS/hosting audit logs to determine how the attacker gained the access needed to alter site content.
steps.guidance: Check for compromised admin credentials, a vulnerable plugin/CMS version, or a misconfigured deployment pipeline.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment using the broadest reasonable lockdown (rotate all CMS credentials) rather than waiting.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS/hosting credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and API keys for all accounts with content-publishing access.

steps.title: Scan for any additional backdoor or persistence left by the attacker
steps.desc: Review the file system and CMS for any web shell, unauthorized admin account, or scheduled task the attacker may have added.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean, or additional persistence found and removed.

steps.title: Coordinate a public statement with PR/Comms if the defacement was widely seen
steps.desc: Loop in PR/Comms to decide whether a public acknowledgment is warranted.

ITID-21122.def: Unauthorized website content replacement occurring as part of a broader, coordinated campaign in which a hacktivist group or affiliated actors deface many organizations' websites within a short time window, typically using a common tool or shared vulnerability.
ITID-21122.purpose: Captures the company's website being one target within a mass, coordinated hacktivist defacement campaign hitting many organizations at once.
scopeIncludes: Defacement using a mass-defacement tool/script also observed against other unrelated organizations
Defacement occurring within a documented campaign wave affecting many sites
scopeExcludes: A single-target, cause-specific defacement of only the company (ITID-21123)
Defacement claimed by one named group but not part of a mass campaign (ITID-21121)
ITID-21122.severity: Medium. Individual severity is often lower than a targeted attack since the company is typically opportunistic collateral rather than specifically chosen.
ITID-21122.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence to confirm campaign scope and shared vulnerability/tooling; patch the underlying flaw across all affected assets.
indicators: Defacement page matching a template seen across many unrelated victim sites
Public defacement mirror/archive sites listing the company alongside many others in the same campaign
vectors: Mass scanning and exploitation of a common CMS/plugin vulnerability
Automated defacement toolkits/scripts
rootCauses: Unpatched, widely-exploited CMS or plugin vulnerability
Lack of automated vulnerability scanning on public web assets
controls: Vulnerability scanning of public-facing assets
Web application firewall
CMS patch management
ITID-21122.detection: Web integrity monitoring detects the defacement; correlation with public defacement archives confirms campaign membership.
ITID-21122.response: Restore content, patch the exploited vulnerability, and check for the same flaw across other internet-facing assets.
metrics: Count of mass-campaign defacements
Time-to-patch shared vulnerability
ITID-21122.notes: Differentiated from ITID-21123 by scale/opportunism: the company was one of many, not specifically targeted.

playbook.name: Response: Mass/Coordinated Hacktivist Defacement Campaign
playbook.description: For a website defacement that is part of a mass, automated hacktivist campaign targeting many organizations sharing a common vulnerability (e.g. a shared CMS/plugin flaw).

steps.title: Capture and preserve the defaced content
steps.desc: Screenshot and save the raw HTML/source of the defaced page(s) before any remediation begins.

steps.title: Take the site offline or serve a maintenance page
steps.desc: Immediately prevent further public visibility of the defaced content.
steps.outcome: Defaced content no longer publicly visible.

steps.title: Apply the vendor patch or mitigation for the mass-exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Patch the CMS/plugin across all affected instances, not just the one defaced.
steps.outcome: All known instances of the vulnerability are closed.

steps.title: Restore legitimate content from a known-good backup
steps.desc: Restore each affected site to its pre-defacement state.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend patch-management improvements
steps.desc: Record the vulnerability, patch timeline, and recommend faster patch cadence for internet-facing CMS software.

steps.title: Identify the shared/mass campaign vulnerability
steps.desc: Check public advisories, ISAC bulletins, and vendor notices for a known mass-exploitation campaign matching the defacement signature.
steps.guidance: Mass campaigns typically exploit a single common CMS/plugin CVE across many victims; identifying it quickly points directly to the fix.
steps.outcome: Underlying mass-campaign vulnerability identified, or ruled out.
steps.abort: If no matching public campaign is found, treat as an unclassified hacktivist defacement and investigate independently.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS/hosting credentials and check for other affected properties
steps.desc: Reset credentials and check whether any other company-owned sites run the same vulnerable software and may be next targeted.
steps.guidance: Mass campaigns are automated and will hit every vulnerable instance the company operates.
steps.outcome: Old credentials invalidated; other exposed properties identified.

steps.title: Scan for additional backdoor or persistence
steps.desc: Automated campaigns often drop a web shell alongside the visible defacement; check for it explicitly.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean, or additional persistence found and removed.

steps.title: Coordinate a public statement with PR/Comms if the defacement was widely seen
steps.desc: Loop in PR/Comms to decide whether a public acknowledgment is warranted, noting this was part of a broad, non-targeted campaign.

ITID-21123.def: Unauthorized website content replacement carried out by an individual or small ad-hoc group specifically targeting the company for a stated grievance or cause, distinct from a mass campaign or an established hacktivist collective's branded operation.
ITID-21123.purpose: Captures a website defacement specifically targeting the company for a stated cause, without being part of a mass campaign or a formally named/tracked collective.
scopeIncludes: Defacement message referencing a specific grievance against the company (e.g., labor dispute, environmental complaint, customer controversy)
Defacement with no branding tying it to a tracked collective and no evidence of a mass campaign
scopeExcludes: Defacement branded/claimed by a tracked collective (ITID-21121)
Defacement occurring as part of a documented mass campaign (ITID-21122)
ITID-21123.severity: Medium-High. Being specifically singled out for a company-related grievance often signals sustained targeting risk.
ITID-21123.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if tied to an active public controversy involving the company.
ITID-21123.escalation: Escalate to communications and legal to assess the underlying grievance and any reputational/legal follow-up needed.
indicators: Defacement message referencing a specific company controversy or grievance
No corroborating evidence of a named-group brand or a multi-victim campaign
vectors: Exploitation of an unpatched CMS or plugin vulnerability
Compromised CMS administrator credentials
rootCauses: Public controversy raising the company's profile as a target
Outdated CMS/plugin versions
controls: Web application firewall
CMS patch management
Reputational/social listening monitoring
ITID-21123.detection: Web integrity monitoring detects the defacement; social listening may surface the underlying grievance context.
ITID-21123.response: Restore content, assess the underlying grievance with communications/legal, and monitor for follow-on targeted activity.
metrics: Count of grievance-specific targeted defacements
Time-to-restore
ITID-21123.notes: Used when the company is specifically and individually targeted for a stated cause but no named collective or mass campaign is evident.

playbook.name: Response: Cause-Based Single-Target Hacktivist Defacement
playbook.description: For a website defacement where the company was deliberately and specifically targeted by a hacktivist actor over a particular cause, policy, or grievance.

steps.desc: Screenshot and save the raw HTML/source of the defaced page, including the attacker's stated reason for targeting the company.
steps.guidance: Understanding the specific grievance helps assess whether further targeted action (DDoS, data leak) should be anticipated.
steps.outcome: Defaced content preserved with timestamp; grievance documented.

steps.title: Take the site offline or serve a maintenance page
steps.desc: Immediately prevent further public visibility of the defaced content.
steps.outcome: Defaced content no longer publicly visible.

steps.title: Patch or remove the exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Close the specific access vector identified during identification.

steps.title: Restore legitimate content from a known-good backup
steps.desc: Restore the site to its pre-defacement state.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector, the attacker's motive, and one concrete improvement.

steps.title: Determine the access vector used
steps.desc: Review CMS/hosting audit logs to determine how the attacker gained the access needed to alter site content.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment using the broadest reasonable lockdown.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS/hosting credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and API keys for all accounts with content-publishing access.

steps.title: Scan for additional backdoor or persistence
steps.desc: Review the file system and CMS for any web shell, unauthorized admin account, or scheduled task the attacker may have added.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean, or additional persistence found and removed.

steps.title: Coordinate a public statement with PR/Comms addressing the specific grievance if needed
steps.desc: Loop in PR/Comms and Legal to decide whether to publicly address the underlying cause the attacker raised.

steps.title: Assess likelihood of follow-on targeted attacks
steps.desc: Given the company was deliberately singled out, assess whether DDoS, data leaks, or repeat defacement attempts should be expected.
steps.guidance: Brief the SOC to watch for follow-on activity from the same actor/collective.
steps.outcome: Heightened monitoring posture established if warranted.

ITID-21124.def: Website defacement bearing hacktivist characteristics, not clearly matching the named-collective, mass-campaign, or single-target cause-based leaves under this Type.
ITID-21124.purpose: Catch-all for hacktivist-motivated website defacement that does not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a more specific hacktivist leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-21121, ITID-21122, or ITID-21123
ITID-21124.severity: Reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-21124.escalation: Reclassify once attribution and scale are clarified.
indicators: Defacement content with hacktivist tone, of unclear attribution or scale
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Web application firewall with virtual patching
Regular vulnerability scanning of public-facing web servers
Automated website content-change alerting
ITID-21124.detection: Same web integrity telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-21124.response: Restore content and investigate to reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-21124.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Hacktivist Defacement
playbook.description: Catch-all response for a hacktivist-motivated website defacement that does not clearly fit the known-collective, mass-campaign, or cause-based-targeted categories.

steps.title: Capture and preserve the defaced content
steps.desc: Screenshot and save the raw HTML/source of the defaced page before any remediation begins.

steps.title: Take the site offline or serve a maintenance page

ITID-21131.purpose: Captures website defacement replacing content with graphic or obscene material, with no political or hacktivist framing.

Graphic/shock content with no accompanying political, hacktivist, or brand-trophy messaging

ITID-21133.def: Unauthorized replacement of website content with a low-content vandalism tag, signature, or 'pwned by' message intended to demonstrate compromise capability rather than convey any specific message.
ITID-21133.purpose: Captures website defacement that is essentially vandalism or bragging rights (a 'pwned by' tag), without political, hacktivist, obscene, or discriminatory content.
scopeIncludes: Simple 'hacked by' / 'pwned by' text or logo replacing a page
Defacement whose sole apparent purpose is to demonstrate the compromise, with no political, hate, or obscene content
scopeExcludes: Graphic/obscene content (ITID-21131)
Hate speech/discriminatory content (ITID-21132)
Defacement branded by a tracked hacktivist collective, tracked under the Hacktivist Defacement Type (ITID-21120 branch)
ITID-21133.severity: Medium. Reputational impact is real but typically lower than content-laden defacements since no message beyond capability is conveyed.
ITID-21133.escalation: Escalate to web/IT operations for restoration; escalate further only if the same actor pattern recurs.

Web integrity monitoring alert on public page content

Automated defacement/vulnerability scanning tools

Lack of file-integrity monitoring on public web content

CMS patch management

ITID-21133.notes: Reserved for low-content, bragging-rights defacement with no political, hate, or obscene messaging; if a named hacktivist signature is present, classify under the Hacktivist Defacement Type instead.

playbook.name: Response: Vandalism/Trophy ("Pwned By") Defacement
playbook.description: For a website defacement consisting of a simple vandalism/trophy message (e.g. "Pwned by...", a handle, a shoutout) left by an attacker to claim credit rather than convey a political or offensive message.

steps.title: Capture and preserve the defaced content
steps.desc: Screenshot and save the raw HTML/source of the defaced page, including the attacker handle/group name left behind.
steps.guidance: The handle can help correlate against known defacement-crew databases (e.g. Zone-H style archives) to assess sophistication and pattern.

steps.title: Take the site offline or serve a maintenance page
steps.desc: Immediately prevent further public visibility of the defaced content.
steps.outcome: Defaced content no longer publicly visible.

steps.title: Patch or remove the exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Close the access vector identified during identification.

steps.title: Restore legitimate content from a known-good backup
steps.desc: Restore the site to its pre-defacement state.

steps.title: Determine the access vector used

steps.guidance: Trophy defacements are frequently the result of automated scanning for known CMS/plugin vulnerabilities rather than targeted effort.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment using the broadest reasonable lockdown.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS/hosting credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and API keys for all accounts with content-publishing access.

steps.title: Scan for additional backdoor or persistence
steps.desc: Even simple trophy defacements can leave a web shell behind for later reuse or resale of access; check explicitly.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean, or additional persistence found and removed.

ITID-21134.def: Website defacement with offensive content, not clearly matching the graphic/obscene, discriminatory, or vandalism/trophy leaves under this Type.
ITID-21134.purpose: Catch-all for offensive-content website defacement that does not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a more specific offensive-content leaf

Web application firewall

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Offensive Content Defacement
playbook.description: Catch-all response for a website defacement inserting offensive content that does not clearly fit the graphic/obscene, hate-speech, or vandalism-trophy categories.

steps.title: Capture and preserve evidence with restricted access, and remove from public view immediately
steps.desc: Record the defacement for evidentiary purposes, restricting access to the captured content given its offensive nature.

ITID-21141.def: A defacement in which the company's website is altered to serve malware to a targeted population of visitors (customers, employees, or an industry community) who are known or expected to visit the site, as opposed to opportunistic mass infection.
ITID-21141.purpose: Captures visible website defacement used as a watering-hole lure, where the defaced/altered page is designed to compromise visitors from a targeted community rather than merely display a message.
scopeIncludes: Visibly altered page content combined with a malicious payload or redirect targeting a specific visitor population
Defacement observed to precede or accompany a documented watering-hole campaign against the company's industry or customer base
scopeExcludes: Silent, non-defacement malicious code injection into an otherwise-unaltered legitimate page (ITID-32412, Drive-By Download via Compromised Legitimate Website)
Generic drive-by download campaigns not targeting a specific visitor population (ITID-32411/ITID-32413/ITID-32414)
Exploit-kit-driven drive-by delivery, tracked as its own leaf (ITID-21142)
ITID-21141.severity: High. Visitors may be infected before the defacement is discovered and remediated.
ITID-21141.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC/IR for emergency takedown and to threat intelligence to identify the targeted population and downstream victims.
indicators: Web integrity monitoring alert combined with anomalous outbound redirects from the site
Endpoint detections on machines that recently visited the company's site
Malicious script/iframe embedded in page source
vectors: Exploitation of an unpatched CMS or plugin vulnerability
Compromised CMS administrator credentials
Injected malicious script/iframe
rootCauses: Outdated CMS/plugin versions
Lack of file-integrity and outbound-content monitoring on public web content
controls: Web application firewall
CMS patch management
File-integrity monitoring on public web content
Outbound content/script monitoring
ITID-21141.detection: Web integrity monitoring and outbound-redirect monitoring together provide strong technical signal.
ITID-21141.response: Take the site offline immediately, remove the malicious payload, restore from known-good backup, and notify potentially-affected visitors/customers.
metrics: Time-to-takedown
Count of visitors potentially exposed
ITID-21141.notes: Scope decision: reserved for cases where the defacement is visibly evident (the brand-facing act); silent injection with no visible defacement is scoped to the drive-by-download domain (ITID-32411-ITID-32414) to avoid duplicating that domain's detailed technique coverage.

playbook.name: Response: Watering-Hole Malware Delivery via Defacement
playbook.description: For a website defacement used to turn the site into a watering hole, silently serving malware to visitors who match a targeted profile.

steps.title: Capture the injected malicious code and preserve evidence
steps.desc: Save the injected script/redirect and identify the malware payload or C2 infrastructure it points to.
steps.guidance: Watering-hole injections are often stealthy and only trigger for specific visitor profiles (IP range, referrer, browser) — review page source directly, not just the rendered page.
steps.outcome: Malicious code and payload/C2 details captured.

steps.title: Take the site offline immediately
steps.desc: Given active malware delivery to visitors, prioritize an immediate full takedown over a partial fix.
steps.outcome: Site no longer serving the malicious payload to any visitor.

steps.title: Remove the malicious injection and patch the exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Strip the injected script/redirect from every affected page and close the access vector.
steps.outcome: Injection removed and vulnerability closed across all affected pages.

steps.title: Restore legitimate content from a known-good backup and re-verify
steps.desc: Restore the site to its pre-compromise state and re-scan before bringing it back online.
steps.outcome: Site restored, verified clean, and back online.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector, exposure window, and one concrete improvement (WAF rule, subresource integrity, CSP).

steps.title: Determine the access vector and scope of injection
steps.desc: Review CMS/hosting audit logs and identify every page/template carrying the injection, not just the one first noticed.
steps.outcome: Access vector and full scope of injected pages identified.
steps.abort: If scope can't be fully bounded quickly, treat the entire site as compromised and take it offline rather than removing the injection piecemeal.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS/hosting credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and API keys for all accounts with content-publishing access.

steps.title: Scan for additional backdoor or persistence
steps.desc: Review the file system and CMS for any web shell, unauthorized admin account, or scheduled task the attacker may have added.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean, or additional persistence found and removed.

steps.title: Notify affected visitors/customers and coordinate with PR/Comms and Legal
steps.desc: Given visitors were exposed to malware, work with PR/Comms and Legal on a public notice and any required disclosure, and advise visitors to run a security scan.
steps.outcome: Affected visitors notified where feasible; consistent public messaging issued.

steps.title: Estimate visitor exposure window
steps.desc: Determine how long the malicious injection was live and approximately how many visitors may have been served the payload.
steps.guidance: Use web server/CDN access logs.
steps.outcome: Exposure window and approximate affected visitor count identified.

ITID-21142.def: A defacement in which the visibly altered page also loads an exploit kit that fingerprints visiting browsers/plugins and delivers a browser or plugin exploit to vulnerable visitors.
ITID-21142.purpose: Captures visible website defacement combined with an embedded exploit kit that fingerprints and exploits visitor browsers.
scopeIncludes: Defaced page with an embedded exploit-kit landing page or redirect chain
Automated browser/plugin fingerprinting observed alongside the defacement
scopeExcludes: Standalone exploit-kit infrastructure with no defacement of the referring site (ITID-32711-ITID-32723)
Watering-hole malware delivery without an exploit-kit fingerprinting component (ITID-21141)
ITID-21142.severity: High. Exploit kits can achieve silent compromise of vulnerable visitors with no user interaction required.
ITID-21142.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC/IR for emergency takedown; coordinate with threat intelligence on exploit-kit family identification.
indicators: Obfuscated redirect chain from the defaced page to an exploit-kit landing page
Browser/plugin fingerprinting requests in web logs
Endpoint exploitation detections correlated with recent site visits
vectors: Exploitation of an unpatched CMS or plugin vulnerability to inject the redirect
Compromised CMS administrator credentials
rootCauses: Outdated CMS/plugin versions
Lack of outbound content/script monitoring on public web content
controls: Web application firewall
CMS patch management
Outbound content/script monitoring
Endpoint exploit protection
ITID-21142.detection: Web integrity monitoring plus outbound-redirect analysis provides strong technical signal.
ITID-21142.response: Take the site offline immediately, remove the injected redirect/exploit-kit reference, restore from known-good backup, and notify potentially-affected visitors.
metrics: Time-to-takedown
Count of visitors potentially exposed
ITID-21142.notes: Scope decision: reserved for cases where the company's own visibly-defaced page is the referring/landing point; the exploit-kit infrastructure domain itself (ITID-32711-ITID-32723) covers the kit's operation in general, independent of any specific defaced referrer.

steps.desc: Save the injected script/iframe pointing to the exploit kit landing page, and identify the vulnerabilities it targets.
steps.guidance: Do not browse to the exploit kit URL from an unprotected machine — use an isolated analysis environment.
steps.outcome: Exploit kit reference and targeted vulnerabilities captured.

steps.title: Take the site offline immediately
steps.desc: Given active exploit delivery to visitors, prioritize an immediate full takedown over a partial fix.
steps.outcome: Site no longer serving the exploit kit to any visitor.

steps.title: Remove the injected exploit kit reference and patch the exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Strip the malicious script/iframe from every affected page and close the CMS/hosting access vector.

steps.title: Restore legitimate content from a known-good backup and re-verify
steps.desc: Restore the site to its pre-compromise state and re-scan before bringing it back online.
steps.outcome: Site restored, verified clean, and back online.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector, exploit kit details, and one concrete improvement (WAF rule, CSP, subresource integrity).

steps.title: Determine the access vector and full scope of injection
steps.desc: Review CMS/hosting audit logs and identify every page/template carrying the injection.
steps.outcome: Access vector and full injection scope identified.
steps.abort: If scope can't be fully bounded quickly, treat the entire site as compromised and take it offline rather than removing the injection piecemeal.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS/hosting credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and API keys for all accounts with content-publishing access.

steps.title: Scan for additional backdoor or persistence
steps.desc: Review the file system and CMS for any web shell, unauthorized admin account, or scheduled task.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean, or additional persistence found and removed.

steps.title: Notify affected visitors/customers and coordinate with PR/Comms and Legal
steps.desc: Given visitors may have been auto-compromised, work with PR/Comms and Legal on a public notice advising visitors to check their devices.
steps.outcome: Affected visitors notified where feasible; consistent public messaging issued.

ITID-21143.def: A defacement in which the altered page presents a fake browser/software update, codec, or plugin-install prompt, socially engineering visitors into voluntarily downloading and running malware.
ITID-21143.purpose: Captures website defacement that displays a fake software update or download prompt to trick visitors into installing malware, relying on social engineering rather than a browser exploit.
scopeIncludes: Fake 'update your browser/Flash/codec' prompts overlaid on or replacing legitimate page content
Defaced page linking to an attacker-controlled fake installer
scopeExcludes: Exploit-kit-driven silent browser exploitation with no user-facing prompt (ITID-21142)
Fraudulent link posts on social media using the same lure theme (ITID-21242, Malware Download Link Post)
ITID-21143.severity: Medium-High. Requires user action to execute, somewhat limiting scale versus a silent exploit, but still a real infection vector.
ITID-21143.escalation: Escalate immediately to SOC/IR for emergency takedown; issue visitor advisory if the prompt was live for a meaningful period.
indicators: Fake update/download prompt visible on a public page
Web integrity monitoring alert
Endpoint detections of the resulting malware family on visitor machines
vectors: Exploitation of an unpatched CMS or plugin vulnerability
Compromised CMS administrator credentials
rootCauses: Outdated CMS/plugin versions
Lack of file-integrity monitoring on public web content
controls: Web application firewall
CMS patch management
File-integrity monitoring on public web content
Endpoint protection against known fake-updater payloads
ITID-21143.detection: Web integrity monitoring detects the prompt; endpoint telemetry confirms whether visitors executed the payload.
ITID-21143.response: Take the site offline immediately, remove the fake prompt, restore from known-good backup, and issue a visitor advisory if warranted.
metrics: Time-to-takedown
Count of confirmed visitor infections
ITID-21143.notes: Differentiated from ITID-21142 by mechanism: social-engineering prompt requiring user action, not a silent browser/plugin exploit.

steps.desc: Screenshot the fake prompt and identify the file/installer it links to, without executing it.

steps.title: Take the site offline immediately

steps.title: Restore legitimate content from a known-good backup and re-verify
steps.desc: Restore the site to its pre-compromise state and re-scan before bringing it back online.
steps.outcome: Site restored, verified clean, and back online.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector and one concrete improvement (WAF rule, CSP, subresource integrity).

steps.title: Determine the access vector and full scope of injection
steps.desc: Review CMS/hosting audit logs and identify every page/template carrying the fake prompt.
steps.outcome: Access vector and full injection scope identified.
steps.abort: If scope can't be fully bounded quickly, treat the entire site as compromised and take it offline.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS/hosting credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and API keys for all accounts with content-publishing access.

steps.title: Scan for additional backdoor or persistence
steps.desc: Review the file system and CMS for any web shell, unauthorized admin account, or scheduled task.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean, or additional persistence found and removed.

steps.desc: Warn visitors who may have downloaded the fake update to run a security scan, and coordinate messaging with PR/Comms.

scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-21141, ITID-21142, or ITID-21143

steps.outcome: Site no longer serving malicious content to any visitor.

steps.title: Remove the malicious injection and patch the exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Strip the injected content from every affected page and close the access vector.

steps.title: Restore legitimate content from a known-good backup and re-verify
steps.desc: Restore the site to its pre-compromise state and re-scan before bringing it back online.
steps.outcome: Site restored, verified clean, and back online.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector and one concrete improvement, and note whether a more specific ITID category should have been used.

steps.title: Determine the access vector and full scope of injection
steps.desc: Review CMS/hosting audit logs and identify every page/template carrying the injection.
steps.outcome: Access vector and full injection scope identified.
steps.abort: If scope can't be fully bounded quickly, treat the entire site as compromised and take it offline.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS/hosting credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and API keys for all accounts with content-publishing access.

steps.title: Scan for additional backdoor or persistence
steps.desc: Review the file system and CMS for any web shell, unauthorized admin account, or scheduled task.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean, or additional persistence found and removed.

steps.title: Notify affected visitors and coordinate with PR/Comms and Legal
steps.desc: Where visitors may have been exposed, coordinate a public notice with PR/Comms and Legal.
steps.outcome: Consistent public messaging issued if needed.

ITID-21151.def: Unauthorized replacement of website content with a fake statement claiming the company suffered a data breach or security incident that did not occur, or misrepresenting the scope of a real one.
ITID-21151.purpose: Captures website defacement that fabricates a data breach or security incident announcement to damage trust or trigger panic.
scopeIncludes: Fake breach notification banner or press-release-style statement posted to the website
Fabricated claims of stolen customer data or system compromise
scopeExcludes: A genuine breach notification published by the company itself
Fake executive/personnel statements with no breach claim (ITID-21153)
ITID-21151.severity: High. Can trigger customer panic, stock impact, and regulatory inquiries even though fabricated.
ITID-21151.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, communications, and investor relations to issue a rapid correction; involve executive leadership given potential market impact.
indicators: Fake breach/incident announcement appearing on the public website
Web integrity monitoring alert
Media or social media pickup of the fake announcement
vectors: Exploitation of an unpatched CMS or plugin vulnerability
Compromised CMS administrator credentials
rootCauses: Outdated CMS/plugin versions
Lack of file-integrity monitoring on public web content
controls: Web application firewall
CMS patch management
File-integrity monitoring on public web content
Crisis communications plan
ITID-21151.detection: Web integrity monitoring provides direct technical signal; rapid external reporting is also common given the alarming content.
ITID-21151.response: Restore content immediately, issue a public correction confirming no genuine breach occurred (or clarifying the real scope), and identify the entry vector.
metrics: Time-to-correction published
Media/social pickup volume
ITID-21151.notes: This leaf is about a fabricated public claim of a breach displayed via defacement, not an actual data breach; a genuine breach is tracked under the applicable data-breach ITID elsewhere in the taxonomy.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Data Breach/Security Incident Announcement
playbook.description: For a website defacement that posts a fabricated announcement claiming the company suffered a data breach or security incident that did not actually occur (or misrepresents one that did).

steps.title: Capture and preserve the fake announcement
steps.desc: Screenshot and save the raw HTML/source of the fake announcement before any remediation begins.

steps.title: Take the site offline or serve a maintenance page
steps.desc: Immediately prevent further public visibility of the fake announcement.
steps.outcome: Fake announcement no longer publicly visible.

steps.title: Patch or remove the exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Close the access vector identified during identification.

steps.title: Restore legitimate content from a known-good backup
steps.desc: Restore the site to its pre-defacement state.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector, the correction timeline, and one concrete improvement (patch cadence, credential hygiene, WAF rule).

steps.title: Verify whether any actual breach exists behind the fake claim
steps.desc: Before dismissing the claim as purely fabricated, quickly verify with the security team whether there is any real underlying incident the defacement is exaggerating or referencing.
steps.guidance: Treat this with urgency — a fake breach announcement can itself trigger customer panic and regulatory inquiries within hours.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the claim is fabricated (or a real underlying incident is identified and handled via the appropriate ITID).
steps.abort: If a real incident is found, pause this playbook and escalate to the appropriate data-breach incident response process.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS/hosting credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and API keys for all accounts with content-publishing access.

steps.title: Issue an urgent public correction with PR/Comms and Legal
steps.desc: Publish a clear, fast public statement confirming no genuine breach occurred (or clarifying the real facts), since a fake breach claim can spread rapidly on social media and news outlets.
steps.guidance: Speed matters more than polish here — a same-day factual correction limits reputational and stock-price impact.
steps.outcome: Public correction issued and confirmed reaching key channels (press, customer support scripts, social media).

ITID-21152.def: Unauthorized replacement of website content with a fake statement claiming the company is ceasing operations, filing for bankruptcy, or otherwise financially collapsing.
ITID-21152.purpose: Captures website defacement that fabricates an announcement of company shutdown, insolvency, or bankruptcy.
scopeIncludes: Fake 'we are closing' or bankruptcy-filing statement posted to the website
Fabricated financial-distress claims intended to alarm customers, investors, or partners
scopeExcludes: Fake data breach announcements (ITID-21151)
Fake executive/personnel statements not concerning company solvency (ITID-21153)
ITID-21152.severity: High. Can cause immediate stock, partner, and customer-confidence impact even though fabricated.
ITID-21152.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, communications, investor relations, and executive leadership for an urgent public correction.
indicators: Fake shutdown/bankruptcy statement on the public website
Web integrity monitoring alert
Unusual trading activity or investor inquiries following the announcement
vectors: Exploitation of an unpatched CMS or plugin vulnerability
Compromised CMS administrator credentials
rootCauses: Outdated CMS/plugin versions
Lack of file-integrity monitoring on public web content
controls: Web application firewall
CMS patch management
File-integrity monitoring on public web content
Crisis communications plan
ITID-21152.detection: Web integrity monitoring provides direct technical signal; investor relations often receives inbound inquiries quickly.
ITID-21152.response: Restore content immediately, issue a public correction, and coordinate with investor relations on any market-facing statement.
metrics: Time-to-correction published
Market/investor inquiry volume
ITID-21152.notes: Scoped to fabricated solvency/shutdown claims specifically, distinguishing it from other fake-announcement subtypes by subject matter.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Company Shutdown/Bankruptcy Announcement
playbook.description: For a website defacement that posts a fabricated announcement claiming the company is shutting down, filing for bankruptcy, or ceasing operations.

steps.title: Capture and preserve the fake announcement
steps.desc: Screenshot and save the raw HTML/source of the fake announcement before any remediation begins.

steps.title: Take the site offline or serve a maintenance page
steps.desc: Immediately prevent further public visibility of the fake announcement.
steps.guidance: A fake bankruptcy/shutdown claim can move markets and trigger vendor/partner panic within minutes — speed is critical.
steps.outcome: Fake announcement no longer publicly visible.

steps.title: Patch or remove the exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Close the access vector identified during identification.

steps.title: Restore legitimate content from a known-good backup
steps.desc: Restore the site to its pre-defacement state.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector, the correction timeline, and one concrete improvement.

steps.title: Determine the access vector used
steps.desc: Review CMS/hosting audit logs to determine how the attacker gained the access needed to alter site content.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment using the broadest reasonable lockdown.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS/hosting credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and API keys for all accounts with content-publishing access.

steps.title: Issue an urgent public correction with PR/Comms, Legal, and Investor Relations
steps.desc: Publish a fast, clear public statement confirming the company is operating normally, and alert Investor Relations given potential stock-price impact.
steps.outcome: Public correction issued; IR briefed to handle investor/analyst inquiries.

ITID-21153.def: Unauthorized replacement of website content with a fake statement, resignation notice, confession, or quote falsely attributed to a named executive or employee.
ITID-21153.purpose: Captures website defacement that fabricates a statement attributed to a company executive or employee.
scopeIncludes: Fake resignation or 'confession' statement attributed to a named executive
Fabricated quotes presented as an official personnel statement
scopeExcludes: Fake breach announcements (ITID-21151)
Fake shutdown/bankruptcy announcements (ITID-21152)
Fake executive statements posted via a compromised social media account rather than the website (ITID-21212/ITID-21217)
ITID-21153.severity: High. Personal and reputational harm to the named individual compounds the corporate brand risk.
ITID-21153.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, communications, and HR; notify the named individual directly given personal reputational impact.
indicators: Fake statement attributed to a named executive/employee on the public website
Web integrity monitoring alert
Media inquiries referencing the fake quote
vectors: Exploitation of an unpatched CMS or plugin vulnerability
Compromised CMS administrator credentials
rootCauses: Outdated CMS/plugin versions
Lack of file-integrity monitoring on public web content
controls: Web application firewall
CMS patch management
File-integrity monitoring on public web content
Crisis communications plan
ITID-21153.detection: Web integrity monitoring provides direct technical signal.
ITID-21153.response: Restore content immediately, issue a public correction, and support the named individual through HR/legal channels as needed.
metrics: Time-to-correction published
ITID-21153.notes: Scoped to the website-hosted fake statement; the analogous scenario delivered via a compromised executive social account is tracked under the Account Takeover Type (ITID-21212/ITID-21217) to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Executive/Personnel Statement
playbook.description: For a website defacement that posts a fabricated statement falsely attributed to a company executive or employee.

steps.title: Capture and preserve the fake statement
steps.desc: Screenshot and save the raw HTML/source of the fake statement, noting which individual it is falsely attributed to.

steps.title: Take the site offline or serve a maintenance page
steps.desc: Immediately prevent further public visibility of the fake statement.
steps.outcome: Fake statement no longer publicly visible.

steps.title: Patch or remove the exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Close the access vector identified during identification.

steps.title: Restore legitimate content from a known-good backup
steps.desc: Restore the site to its pre-defacement state.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector, the correction timeline, and one concrete improvement.

steps.title: Notify the impersonated individual and determine the access vector
steps.desc: Alert the named executive/employee directly, and review CMS/hosting audit logs to determine the access vector used.
steps.guidance: The impersonated individual may face personal reputational fallout and should hear about it from the company before the press.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment using the broadest reasonable lockdown.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS/hosting credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and API keys for all accounts with content-publishing access.

steps.title: Issue a public correction with PR/Comms and Legal
steps.desc: Publish a statement clarifying the individual did not make the attributed remarks, coordinated with Legal for any defamation/impersonation considerations.
steps.outcome: Public correction issued; impersonated individual's reputation addressed.

ITID-21154.def: Website defacement fabricating a company announcement, not clearly matching the breach, shutdown, or executive-statement leaves under this Type.
ITID-21154.purpose: Catch-all for fake-announcement website defacement that does not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a more specific fake-announcement leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-21151, ITID-21152, or ITID-21153
ITID-21154.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High pending investigation given the impersonation/misinformation component.
ITID-21154.escalation: Reclassify once the specific announcement subject is clarified.
indicators: Fabricated company announcement of unclear specific subject on a public page
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: CMS admin account MFA enforcement
Content approval/publishing workflow requiring dual authorization
Automated website content-change alerting
ITID-21154.detection: Same web integrity telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-21154.response: Restore content and investigate to reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-21154.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Fake Announcement Defacement
playbook.description: Catch-all response for a website defacement posting a fabricated announcement that does not clearly fit the fake-breach, fake-shutdown, or fake-executive-statement categories.

steps.title: Capture and preserve the fake announcement
steps.desc: Screenshot and save the raw HTML/source of the fake announcement before any remediation begins.

steps.title: Take the site offline or serve a maintenance page
steps.desc: Immediately prevent further public visibility of the fake announcement.
steps.outcome: Fake announcement no longer publicly visible.

steps.title: Patch or remove the exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Close the access vector identified during identification.

steps.title: Restore legitimate content from a known-good backup
steps.desc: Restore the site to its pre-defacement state.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector and one concrete improvement, and note whether a more specific ITID category should have been used.

steps.title: Determine the access vector used
steps.desc: Review CMS/hosting audit logs to determine how the attacker gained the access needed to alter site content.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment using the broadest reasonable lockdown.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS/hosting credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and API keys for all accounts with content-publishing access.

steps.title: Issue a public correction with PR/Comms if the fake announcement was widely seen
steps.desc: Publish a clarifying statement if the fabricated announcement gained public traction.

ITID-21211.def: Unauthorized access to and control of the company's official corporate social media account (the primary brand-handle presence, not an executive's personal account), obtained through credential compromise or session hijacking.
ITID-21211.purpose: Captures unauthorized takeover of the company's official/corporate brand social media account.
scopeIncludes: Login to the official brand account by an unauthorized party
Attacker changing the account password/recovery details/profile to lock out legitimate admins
scopeExcludes: Executive or personal-branded account takeover (ITID-21212)

The underlying credential-theft technique itself (e.g., credential stuffing, password spraying, SIM swap), tracked under ITID-12219/ITID-12229/ITID-12649 — this leaf is scoped to the brand-facing consequence once the social media account itself is compromised
Confirmed defacement content actually posted after takeover, tracked as its own escalation leaf (ITID-21217)
ITID-21211.severity: High. The official brand account is the company's primary social voice; compromise is immediately and widely visible.
ITID-21211.escalation: Escalate immediately to social media/communications team and the platform's trusted-partner channel for emergency account recovery.
indicators: Unexpected login location/device on the account
Password/recovery email changed without authorization
Admin lockout reported by the social media team
vectors: Credential stuffing or password spraying against the account
Phishing of an admin's account credentials
SIM swap enabling SMS-based recovery bypass
rootCauses: No MFA enforced on the social media account
Shared/weak account password
Recovery contact info not restricted to a monitored, secured channel
controls: MFA on all official social media accounts
Restricted, monitored recovery contact details
Social media account access review/least-privilege admin list
ITID-21211.detection: Platform login-alert and admin-change notifications provide direct technical signal.
ITID-21211.response: Initiate platform emergency account recovery, rotate credentials and MFA, and audit for any content posted or settings changed during the compromise window.
metrics: Time-to-recovery of the account
Count of official account takeovers per year
ITID-21211.notes: Scope decision: this leaf and its siblings describe the social-media-account-compromise event and its brand impact; the credential-theft technique used to obtain access (credential stuffing, password spraying, SIM swap) is documented in full under ITID-12219, ITID-12229, and ITID-12649 respectively and is referenced here rather than re-described.

playbook.name: Response: Official Brand/Corporate Account Takeover
playbook.description: For a confirmed takeover of the organization's official social media account by an unauthorized party.

steps.title: Confirm loss of account control
steps.desc: Attempt normal login and check for signs of unauthorized password/email/2FA changes.
steps.outcome: Confirmed extent of unauthorized control (partial vs. total lockout).

steps.title: Initiate the platform's official account-recovery process
steps.desc: Use the platform's verified-business/priority support channel to report the takeover and begin recovery.
steps.guidance: A verified/branded account often has a faster, dedicated recovery path than general support.
steps.outcome: Recovery case opened with the platform.

steps.title: Remove all unauthorized content once access is regained
steps.desc: Delete posts, restore the bio/profile, and remove any unauthorized linked apps or admins.
steps.outcome: Account content restored to legitimate state.

steps.title: Re-secure the account with MFA and a new admin roster
steps.desc: Enable/re-enable MFA and review who has admin access to the account going forward.
steps.outcome: Account regained with stronger access controls.

steps.title: Document root cause and update social media access policy if needed
steps.desc: Record how the account was compromised and recommend a control improvement (password manager use, admin count reduction, MFA enforcement).

steps.title: Document all unauthorized posts/changes made
steps.desc: Screenshot and log every post, bio change, or DM sent while the account was compromised.
steps.guidance: Needed both for cleanup and for the platform's own account-recovery support process.

steps.title: Alert followers of the compromise via an alternate official channel
steps.desc: Post a warning via another owned channel (website banner, a different verified account) that the account is compromised and its content should not be trusted.

steps.title: Revoke all sessions and connected app authorizations
steps.desc: Force-logout all sessions and review/revoke any third-party app connected to the account.

ITID-21212.def: Unauthorized access to and control of a named executive's personal or personal-branded social media account, where the account's association with the company creates a brand and reputational exposure distinct from the official corporate account.
ITID-21212.purpose: Captures unauthorized takeover of a company executive's personal or personal-branded social media account that is closely associated with the company.
scopeIncludes: Takeover of a CEO's or other named executive's personal account known to be closely identified with the company
Attacker posting content attributed to the executive personally
scopeExcludes: Takeover of the official brand/corporate account (ITID-21211)
An employee's unrelated personal account mistaken for an official channel (ITID-21213)
ITID-21212.severity: High. Executive impersonation carries both corporate brand risk and personal reputational/legal risk to the individual.
ITID-21212.escalation: Escalate immediately to communications, legal, and the affected executive personally; engage platform trusted-partner channel for recovery.
indicators: Unexpected posts attributed to the executive inconsistent with their normal voice
Admin/recovery-info change alert on the account
Executive reports being locked out
vectors: Spearphishing of the executive's credentials
Credential stuffing/password spraying against the account
SIM swap enabling SMS-based recovery bypass
rootCauses: No MFA enforced on the executive's account
Executive using a personal, unmanaged device/account with weak security hygiene
controls: MFA on executive personal accounts used for company-related communication
Executive digital protection/monitoring program
Restricted, monitored recovery contact details
ITID-21212.detection: Platform login-alert and admin-change notifications provide direct technical signal; executive self-report is also common.
ITID-21212.response: Initiate platform emergency account recovery, rotate credentials and MFA, and audit for any content posted during the compromise window.
metrics: Time-to-recovery of the account
Count of executive account takeovers per year
ITID-21212.notes: Scoped to accounts with a genuine, recognized association to the company; the technique used to obtain credentials is referenced from the relevant credential-theft domain rather than re-described here.

playbook.name: Response: Executive/Personal-Branded Account Takeover
playbook.description: For a takeover of an executive's or other prominent personal-brand account that is closely associated with the organization.

steps.title: Confirm compromise and identify the affected executive/individual
steps.desc: Verify loss of control and confirm with the individual directly (out of band) that they did not make the changes.
steps.guidance: Use a phone call or in-person contact, not the compromised account's own channels.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed and account owner identified.

steps.title: Engage platform support via verified/executive escalation channel
steps.desc: Report the takeover through the platform's verified-account or high-profile escalation path.

steps.title: Remove unauthorized posts and restore profile once access is regained
steps.desc: Delete all unauthorized content and confirm the profile matches its pre-incident state.

steps.title: Re-secure the account and enroll in a password manager/MFA
steps.desc: Work with the executive to implement stronger credential hygiene and hardware-key MFA where supported.

steps.title: Document incident and brief executive protection/security awareness program
steps.desc: Log the root cause and feed findings into executive digital-security training.

steps.title: Assess brand and reputational exposure of posted content
steps.desc: Review unauthorized posts for content that could be attributed to the company or misconstrued as executive commentary.
steps.guidance: Loop in Communications/PR early given executive visibility.

steps.title: Coordinate a joint Comms/Legal holding statement
steps.desc: Prepare a brief statement for use if press or followers ask about the unauthorized activity before the account is recovered.
