steps.title: Revoke sessions, connected apps, and check for credential reuse elsewhere
steps.desc: Force-logout sessions and check whether the compromised credentials were reused on other executive accounts.
steps.outcome: Attacker access fully removed across related accounts.

ITID-21213.def: A scenario in which an employee's personal social media account (not an officially designated or brand-associated account) is compromised or misused, and the resulting content is mistaken by the public, media, or customers for an official company statement due to the employee's visible role or affiliation disclosure.
ITID-21213.purpose: Captures cases where an employee's personal social media account is compromised or misused and mistaken by the public for an official company channel.
scopeIncludes: Compromise of an employee's personal account that lists the company as employer and is publicly misread as an official statement
Public/media confusion requiring the company to issue a clarification that the account was not official
scopeExcludes: Takeover of the designated official brand account (ITID-21211)
Takeover of an executive's recognized personal-branded account (ITID-21212)
Deliberate insider misuse of a personal account with intent, tracked under insider-threat ITIDs elsewhere in the taxonomy
ITID-21213.severity: Medium. Reputational confusion risk exists but is more easily corrected than a true official-channel compromise.
ITID-21213.escalation: Escalate to communications to issue a public clarification; support the affected employee in recovering their account.
indicators: Public/media inquiries treating an employee's personal post as an official company statement
Employee reports personal account compromise
vectors: Credential phishing or stuffing against the employee's personal account
rootCauses: Employee publicly listing employer affiliation without company guidance on personal account security
No employee social media policy addressing affiliation disclosure
controls: Employee social media use/affiliation-disclosure policy
Employee security awareness training on personal account protection
ITID-21213.detection: Typically first surfaced by public/media inquiry rather than internal technical monitoring, since the account is not company-owned.
ITID-21213.response: Issue a prompt public clarification distinguishing personal from official statements; assist the employee with account recovery.
metrics: Time-to-public-clarification
ITID-21213.notes: This leaf covers the perception/misattribution risk of a personal (non-official) account, not a true compromise of company-controlled social infrastructure.

playbook.name: Response: Employee Personal Account Mistaken for Official Account
playbook.description: For confusion where an employee's personal social media account is being mistaken by the public for an official company account, without any actual account compromise.

steps.title: Confirm no compromise occurred and identify the source of confusion
steps.desc: Verify the account belongs to the employee legitimately and determine why it is being perceived as official (naming, logo use, bio wording).
steps.outcome: Confirmed this is a perception/branding issue, not a security compromise.
steps.abort: If evidence of actual compromise is found, redirect to the account-takeover playbook.

steps.title: Contact the employee to request clarification of their bio/handle
steps.desc: Ask the employee to add a disclaimer (e.g. 'personal account, views my own') or adjust branding elements causing confusion.
steps.guidance: Handle collaboratively; this is not a disciplinary action by default.
steps.outcome: Employee agrees to update their profile.

steps.title: Verify the employee's profile has been updated
steps.desc: Confirm the bio/handle/branding changes were made as agreed.

steps.title: Review brand/trademark usage guidance with employee population
steps.desc: Remind employees of the social media policy regarding use of company branding on personal accounts.

steps.title: Document the incident and consider a verified-badge/handle strategy
steps.desc: Record the confusion pattern and evaluate whether official accounts need clearer differentiation (verification badges, consistent handle naming).

steps.title: Assess public confusion and reputational impact
steps.desc: Review public comments/replies to gauge how many people believe the account is official and whether misinformation is spreading.

steps.title: Issue a public clarification from the official account if confusion is material
steps.desc: Post from the verified official account clarifying which handle is the legitimate company channel.

ITID-21214.def: Unauthorized takeover of a platform-verified social media account belonging to the company or an executive, where the verification status causes audiences to treat any posted content as especially credible.
ITID-21214.purpose: Captures takeover of a verified/authenticated ('blue-check') company or executive social media account, where the verification badge amplifies the credibility and reach of any posted content.
scopeIncludes: Takeover of any officially verified/authenticated account, regardless of whether it is the primary brand handle or an executive's
Cases where the verification badge itself is highlighted in follow-on media coverage as lending false credibility
scopeExcludes: Takeover of an unverified official or executive account (covered under ITID-21211/ITID-21212 without this additional verification-amplification factor)
ITID-21214.severity: High-Critical. Verification status significantly amplifies reach and perceived credibility of malicious content, increasing potential for market or public-safety impact.
ITID-21214.escalation: Escalate immediately given amplified reach; engage platform trusted-partner/verified-account emergency channel.
indicators: Unexpected posts from a verified account inconsistent with normal content
Rapid, unusually high engagement/spread on the malicious post consistent with verified-account reach
Admin/recovery-info change alert
vectors: Spearphishing or credential stuffing against the account
SIM swap enabling SMS-based recovery bypass
Compromise of a connected management tool with access to the verified account
rootCauses: No MFA enforced on the verified account
Verified accounts not subject to elevated access-control requirements
controls: MFA and elevated access controls on verified accounts
Dedicated monitoring/alerting for verified-account activity
Restricted, monitored recovery contact details
ITID-21214.detection: Platform login-alert and admin-change notifications provide direct technical signal; rapid social listening detects abnormal engagement spikes.
ITID-21214.response: Initiate emergency recovery via the platform's verified-account channel, rotate credentials/MFA, and issue a public correction given the amplified reach.
metrics: Time-to-recovery
Engagement/reach of the malicious content before removal
ITID-21214.notes: Differentiator from sibling account-type leaves is the verification badge itself, which is tracked because it materially changes severity and response urgency regardless of whether the account is the brand handle or an executive's.

playbook.name: Response: Verified/Blue-Check Account Takeover
playbook.description: For a takeover of a verified (badge-holding) official account, where the verification status itself amplifies the credibility and reach of unauthorized content.

steps.title: Confirm loss of account control
steps.desc: Attempt login and check for unauthorized password/email/2FA/verification-status changes.

steps.title: Escalate via the platform's verified-account priority support path
steps.desc: Use the highest-priority recovery channel available to verified/business accounts.

steps.title: Remove unauthorized content and confirm verification badge integrity
steps.desc: Delete posts and confirm the verification status has not itself been altered or stripped.
steps.outcome: Account and badge restored to legitimate state.

steps.title: Re-secure the account with MFA and restrict admin roster
steps.desc: Enable strong MFA and reduce number of accounts with admin access given the elevated value of a verified account.

steps.title: Document root cause and reassess verified-account access controls
steps.desc: Log findings and evaluate whether verified accounts warrant stricter controls than standard accounts.

steps.title: Assess amplified reach due to verified status
steps.desc: Check engagement metrics and whether the unauthorized content is being algorithmically boosted or picked up by media due to the verified badge.
steps.guidance: Verified accounts often carry higher trust and reach, escalating urgency.

steps.title: Request the platform flag or remove the unauthorized content pending recovery
steps.desc: Ask platform trust and safety to interim-remove clearly malicious posts even before full account control is restored.

steps.title: Revoke all sessions and connected app authorizations
steps.desc: Force-logout all sessions and review/revoke any third-party app connected to the account.

ITID-21215.def: Unauthorized takeover of an inactive, legacy, or otherwise unmonitored company social media account (e.g., an old campaign or regional handle) that remains publicly visible and attributable to the brand.
ITID-21215.purpose: Captures takeover of a dormant or legacy company social media account that is no longer actively managed but still publicly visible and associated with the brand.
scopeIncludes: Compromise of an inactive account not covered by current social media governance/monitoring
Legacy regional, product, or campaign accounts still bearing company branding
scopeExcludes: Compromise of the actively-managed primary brand account (ITID-21211)
ITID-21215.severity: Medium-High. Reach is typically lower than the primary account, but detection is often delayed precisely because the account is unmonitored.
ITID-21215.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the account retains a significant follower base.
ITID-21215.escalation: Escalate to social media/communications team; prioritize a full inventory review of other dormant accounts once one is found compromised.
indicators: Unexpected activity reported by a customer/follower rather than internal monitoring
Account discovered during a periodic social media inventory audit
vectors: Credential stuffing against a legacy, unrotated password
Account recovery via an outdated/abandoned associated email
rootCauses: No formal inventory or offboarding process for legacy social media accounts
Legacy accounts excluded from MFA enforcement and monitoring
controls: Full inventory of all company-associated social media accounts
Deactivation or MFA enforcement on all remaining active-but-dormant accounts
ITID-21215.detection: Weak; dormant accounts typically lack monitoring, so detection often relies on external reports or periodic audits.
ITID-21215.response: Recover or permanently deactivate the account, and extend the inventory/governance review to other dormant accounts.
metrics: Count of dormant accounts identified and remediated
Time-to-discovery
sops: Social Media Account Inventory and Governance SOP
ITID-21215.notes: Highlights a governance gap (unmanaged legacy accounts) distinct from the actively-monitored primary/executive account leaves.

playbook.name: Response: Dormant/Legacy Account Takeover
playbook.description: For a takeover of an old, inactive, or forgotten company social media account that was not actively monitored.

steps.title: Confirm the account's legitimate ownership and dormancy history
steps.desc: Verify the account is genuinely a company-owned legacy account and establish when it was last actively used.
steps.guidance: Legacy accounts are often unknown to current staff; check with Legal/Marketing/Brand history if ownership is unclear.
steps.outcome: Ownership confirmed and dormancy period established.

steps.title: Initiate the platform's account-recovery process
steps.desc: Report the takeover through the platform's support channel, providing proof of original ownership.
steps.guidance: Recovery of dormant accounts may require additional ownership verification since original registration details may be outdated.

steps.title: Remove unauthorized content or complete deactivation
steps.desc: Once access is regained, delete unauthorized posts, or complete the deactivation request if that path was chosen.

steps.title: Inventory all company social accounts and assign an owner
steps.desc: Ensure the recovered/retired account is added to a maintained inventory of company social media assets with a designated owner.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend periodic dormant-account audits
steps.desc: Record how the account went unmonitored and recommend a recurring audit of all registered social media assets.

steps.title: Assess current follower base and exposure
steps.desc: Check whether the account still has an active audience that would see unauthorized posts.

steps.title: Decide whether to recover or permanently deactivate the account
steps.desc: If the account has negligible ongoing value, consider requesting permanent deactivation instead of recovery.
steps.outcome: A clear decision on the account's future disposition.

ITID-21216.def: Unauthorized access to a company social media account obtained through the compromise of one of multiple shared administrator credentials, agency logins, or management-tool integrations with standing access to the account.
ITID-21216.purpose: Captures takeover risk arising specifically from an account being shared across multiple administrators, agencies, or tools with broad or poorly-governed access.
scopeIncludes: Compromise traced to one of several shared admin logins or an external agency's credentials
Account access sprawl across many individuals/agencies with no individualized accountability
scopeExcludes: Compromise of a single, individually-owned account credential (ITID-21211/ITID-21212)
Compromise via a management tool's own API integration, tracked as a Fake Post leaf (ITID-21222) when the compromise manifests as unauthorized posting rather than full account lockout
ITID-21216.severity: High. Multi-admin sprawl often means slower identification of the compromised credential and broader blast radius.
ITID-21216.escalation: Escalate immediately; rotate all shared credentials and review the full admin/agency access list, not just the compromised one.
indicators: Unauthorized login traced to a shared/agency credential
Admin access list larger than expected or undocumented
vectors: Compromise of one agency's or contractor's shared login
Phishing of a specific shared-account holder
rootCauses: No individualized, role-based access to shared social accounts
Lack of periodic admin access review
Shared credentials not rotated after personnel/agency changes
controls: Individualized, role-based social media access management
Periodic admin/agency access review
MFA on all shared account access
ITID-21216.detection: Platform login-alert and admin-change notifications provide direct technical signal, but attribution to the specific compromised credential can be slow given shared access.
ITID-21216.response: Rotate all shared credentials, review and prune the full admin/agency access list, and recover the account.
metrics: Time-to-recovery
Size of admin/agency access list post-remediation
sops: Social Media Account Access Governance SOP
ITID-21216.notes: Differentiator is the governance failure mode (shared/sprawling access) rather than the account's role or verification status.

playbook.name: Response: Multi-Admin Shared Account Takeover
playbook.description: For a takeover of an account with multiple administrators/managers, where the compromise vector may be any one of several credentialed users.

steps.title: Confirm compromise and enumerate all current admins
steps.desc: Confirm loss of control and pull a full list of accounts/individuals with admin or manager access.

steps.title: Suspend or force-reset credentials for all admins pending investigation
steps.desc: Temporarily disable or force password/MFA reset for every admin, not just the suspected compromised one, until the vector is confirmed.

steps.title: Remove unauthorized content and any rogue admin accounts
steps.desc: Delete unauthorized posts and remove any admin accounts added by the attacker.
steps.outcome: Admin roster restored to legitimate members only.

steps.title: Establish least-privilege admin roles going forward
steps.desc: Reduce the number of full-admin accounts and use role-based/limited permissions where the platform supports it.

steps.title: Document root cause and update shared-account governance policy
steps.desc: Record which credential was compromised and how, and update the policy for managing multi-admin social accounts.

steps.title: Identify which admin's credentials were the compromise vector
steps.desc: Review login/activity logs to determine which admin account was used to make unauthorized changes.
steps.guidance: Interview the identified admin about phishing, password reuse, or malware.
steps.abort: If logs are unavailable, treat all admin credentials as potentially compromised.

steps.title: Engage the platform's official recovery process if full lockout occurred
steps.desc: If the attacker removed all legitimate admins, escalate to the platform's business support channel.

steps.title: Reissue credentials and MFA to all remaining legitimate admins
steps.desc: Rotate passwords and re-enroll MFA for every legitimate admin before restoring access.

ITID-21217.def: The escalation of any Social Media Account Takeover leaf to a confirmed state: the attacker not only gained account control but successfully posted unauthorized, brand-damaging content that was publicly visible before removal.
ITID-21217.purpose: Captures the confirmed, higher-severity outcome where an account takeover has resulted in actual unauthorized defacement content being posted and seen publicly.
scopeIncludes: Any account-takeover scenario where malicious content was confirmed live and publicly visible
Cases requiring public correction/retraction because content was seen by followers or picked up by media
scopeExcludes: Account takeover where access was gained but no content was successfully posted before recovery (the corresponding attempt-level leaf, e.g. ITID-21211-ITID-21216)
ITID-21217.severity: Critical. Confirmed public posting materially increases reputational damage, follower/customer confusion, and potential downstream harm versus a contained takeover.
ITID-21217.escalation: Escalate immediately to the highest applicable crisis communications tier; executive and legal involvement is expected by default given confirmed public exposure.
indicators: Screenshots or archived captures of the malicious post circulating externally
Follower/customer engagement (likes, shares, replies) on the malicious content prior to removal
Media coverage of the posted content
vectors: Any account-takeover vector applicable to the underlying account (see sibling leaves)
Delay in detection/recovery allowing the post to remain live
rootCauses: Slow detection/recovery response allowing content to remain visible
No pre-approved rapid-correction messaging template
controls: Rapid account-recovery runbook with defined SLAs
Pre-approved crisis correction messaging templates
Real-time social listening for brand-account anomalies
ITID-21217.detection: Combination of platform alerts and social listening/external reporting confirms live public exposure.
ITID-21217.response: Remove the content immediately, recover the account, issue a public correction, and conduct a full post-incident review of detection/recovery timing.
metrics: Time content remained publicly visible
Engagement/reach of the malicious content
Time-to-public-correction
ITID-21217.notes: This is the outcome-confirmed escalation of the Account Takeover Type: severity and priority guidance are markedly higher than the attempt/access-only sibling leaves since public brand damage is confirmed rather than averted.

playbook.name: Response: Successful Account Takeover with Confirmed Unauthorized Defacement Posted
playbook.description: For an account takeover where unauthorized defacement content has already been confirmed posted and publicly visible.

steps.title: Confirm and capture all posted defacement content
steps.desc: Screenshot and archive every unauthorized post, including engagement counts and timestamps, before any removal.
steps.guidance: Preserve evidence for the platform's abuse report and any downstream legal/PR needs.
steps.outcome: Complete evidentiary record of the defacement.

steps.title: Initiate the platform's account-recovery process
steps.desc: Report the takeover and the specific defacing posts through the platform's priority support channel.

steps.title: Delete all unauthorized defacement content once access is regained
steps.desc: Remove every unauthorized post, comment, and profile/bio change made during the compromise.

steps.title: Re-secure the account and monitor for reposted/mirrored content
steps.desc: Enable MFA, and continue monitoring for the defacement content being mirrored on other platforms after recovery.
steps.outcome: Account secured and residual spread tracked.

steps.title: Document root cause, spread, and response timeline
steps.desc: Record the full incident timeline from compromise to public content removal for after-action review.

steps.title: Assess reach and any reposting/screenshotting by third parties
steps.desc: Search for the content being reshared, quote-posted, or screenshotted elsewhere to gauge how far it has already spread.

steps.title: Issue a public statement disavowing the unauthorized content
steps.desc: Post from an alternate owned channel that the account is compromised and the visible content is not authorized company communication.
steps.guidance: Coordinate wording with Communications/PR.

steps.title: Revoke sessions and connected app authorizations
steps.desc: Force-logout all sessions and revoke any third-party app access added by the attacker.

ITID-21218.def: Unauthorized takeover of a company-associated social media account, not clearly matching the official/corporate, executive, verified, dormant, or shared-access leaves under this Type.
ITID-21218.purpose: Catch-all for social media account takeover that does not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a more specific account-takeover leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-21211 through ITID-21217
ITID-21218.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High pending investigation.
ITID-21218.escalation: Reclassify once the account type and outcome are clarified.
indicators: Account takeover of unclear specific account type or outcome
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Social media account MFA enforcement
Centralized social media account credential vaulting
Social media platform login-anomaly monitoring
ITID-21218.detection: Same platform-alert telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-21218.response: Recover the account and investigate to reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-21218.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Social Media Account Takeover
playbook.description: General-purpose response for a social media account takeover that does not fit a more specific account-takeover subtype.

steps.title: Confirm loss of account control and gather initial facts
steps.desc: Attempt login, check for unauthorized credential/2FA changes, and determine which platform and account are affected.

steps.title: Initiate the platform's account-recovery process
steps.desc: Report the takeover through the appropriate support channel for the affected platform.

steps.title: Remove unauthorized content once access is regained
steps.desc: Delete unauthorized posts and restore profile/bio to its legitimate state.

steps.title: Re-secure the account with MFA and review admin access
steps.desc: Enable/strengthen MFA and confirm the admin roster is accurate.

steps.title: Document root cause and remediation
steps.desc: Log how the compromise occurred and any control improvements identified.

steps.title: Document unauthorized activity
steps.desc: Screenshot and log all unauthorized posts, messages, or profile changes.

steps.title: Notify relevant internal stakeholders
steps.desc: Alert Communications, Legal, and Security leadership as appropriate to the account's visibility.

steps.title: Revoke sessions and connected app authorizations
steps.desc: Force-logout all sessions and revoke any unauthorized third-party app access.

ITID-21221.def: A fake or misleading post published from an account that impersonates or parodies the company but is not itself the compromised official account, creating public confusion about the post's legitimacy.
ITID-21221.purpose: Captures brand-damaging content posted from a parody or impersonator account rather than the real company account, where the distinction may not be obvious to the audience.
scopeIncludes: A convincing lookalike/parody handle publishing content that could plausibly be mistaken for an official statement
Public or media confusion requiring a company clarification
scopeExcludes: Any scenario involving actual compromise/control of the real official or executive account (ITID-21210 branch)
ITID-21221.severity: Medium-High, depending on how convincingly the impersonator mimics the real account and how far the content spreads before correction.
ITID-21221.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the content spreads widely or causes safety/financial harm to followers.
ITID-21221.escalation: Escalate to communications for a public clarification and to legal/trust-and-safety for a platform impersonation takedown request.
indicators: Lookalike handle/username with minor variations from the real account
Public inquiries asking whether a post is genuine
Platform impersonation report submitted
vectors: Registration of a lookalike handle/profile with copied branding
Reuse of stolen official logos/imagery to increase credibility
rootCauses: No proactive lookalike-account monitoring
Lack of clear account verification cues communicated to followers
mitreTechniques: T1585.001 Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts
controls: Proactive brand/lookalike-account monitoring
Platform impersonation reporting process
Public account-verification guidance for followers
ITID-21221.detection: Primarily external (social listening or public reports); no internal account telemetry since the real account is uncompromised.
ITID-21221.response: File a platform impersonation takedown request and issue a public clarification distinguishing the real account.
metrics: Time-to-takedown of impersonator account
Number of lookalike accounts identified per quarter
ITID-21221.notes: No real account is compromised here; this is a spoofing/impersonation scenario, differentiated from every other Fake Post leaf which involves some level of access to a legitimate posting channel.

playbook.name: Response: Impersonator/Parody Account Fake Post
playbook.description: For fake/misleading posts originating from a look-alike impersonator or parody account rather than any actual compromise of company-owned accounts.

steps.title: Confirm the posting account is not company-owned
steps.desc: Verify the impersonator/parody account is distinct from any legitimate company account and has no admin overlap.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no actual company account compromise occurred.
steps.abort: If the account turns out to be legitimately company-owned, redirect to the account-takeover playbook.

steps.title: Report the impersonator account to the platform for policy violation
steps.desc: File an impersonation report through the platform's trust and safety reporting tools.
steps.outcome: Takedown request submitted to the platform.

steps.title: Confirm removal or suspension of the impersonator account
steps.desc: Verify the platform has removed the fake post or suspended the impersonator account.
steps.outcome: Fake content no longer publicly accessible.
steps.abort: If the platform declines to act, escalate through Legal for a trademark/brand-abuse complaint.

steps.title: Consider proactive trademark/handle registration to reduce future impersonation
steps.desc: Register key handle variants on major platforms if not already held.

steps.title: Document the incident and platform response time
steps.desc: Log the incident, the platform's takedown turnaround, and any recommended monitoring improvements.

steps.title: Assess whether the account is causing genuine public confusion
steps.desc: Review engagement and comments to determine whether followers believe the impersonator is the real brand.
steps.guidance: Parody accounts that are clearly labeled as such may not require action; deceptive impersonation should be escalated.

steps.title: Issue a public clarification from the verified official account
steps.desc: Post clarifying which account is official if the fake post is causing material confusion.

ITID-21222.def: Unauthorized content published to a company's real social media account(s) via a compromised third-party scheduling/management platform or API integration (e.g., a social media management SaaS tool), rather than direct compromise of the platform account credentials themselves.
ITID-21222.purpose: Captures unauthorized posts published through a compromised third-party social media management tool or API integration that has legitimate publishing access to company accounts.
scopeIncludes: Compromise of a connected management tool (e.g., a scheduling/publishing SaaS) resulting in unauthorized posts across one or more linked accounts
Abuse of an overly-permissive API token/integration
scopeExcludes: Direct compromise of platform-native account credentials (ITID-21211-ITID-21218)
Compromise specifically of the scheduled-post queue within the native platform tool, tracked separately (ITID-21224)
ITID-21222.severity: High. A single compromised integration can post to multiple linked accounts simultaneously, multiplying reach.
ITID-21222.escalation: Escalate immediately; revoke the integration's API access/tokens across all linked accounts as a first containment step.
indicators: Unauthorized posts appearing simultaneously across multiple linked accounts
Anomalous API activity logged by the management tool vendor
Vendor security notification of a breach
vectors: Compromise of the third-party tool's own credentials or infrastructure
Overly broad API token scope/permissions
Stolen OAuth token
rootCauses: Excessive permission scope granted to the third-party integration
No periodic review of connected app/API integrations
Vendor-side security failure
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Least-privilege API/OAuth scoping for connected tools
Periodic review and pruning of connected app integrations
Vendor security assessment for social media management tools
ITID-21222.detection: Vendor breach notifications and API activity logs provide technical signal; simultaneous multi-account posting is a strong indicator.
ITID-21222.response: Revoke the compromised integration's access immediately, remove unauthorized content, and reassess third-party integration permissions.
metrics: Number of linked accounts affected
Time-to-revocation of compromised integration
ITID-21222.notes: Distinguished from native-account takeover by the compromise point being a third-party tool/API rather than the platform account credentials directly.

playbook.name: Response: Compromised Social Media Management Tool/API Integration Fake Post
playbook.description: For fake posts published through a compromised third-party social media management tool (e.g. scheduling/publishing platform) or API integration connected to company accounts.

steps.title: Confirm the posting originated from the connected tool/API, not the platform account directly
steps.desc: Check post metadata/source labels and the tool's own activity logs to confirm the publishing path.
steps.outcome: Compromise vector confirmed as the third-party tool/integration.
steps.abort: If the native account itself was compromised, redirect to the account-takeover playbook.

steps.title: Revoke the compromised tool's API access/OAuth token from all connected accounts
steps.desc: Immediately disconnect the third-party integration from every linked social account to stop further unauthorized posting.
steps.outcome: No further posts possible via the compromised integration.

steps.title: Remove unauthorized posts across all affected accounts
steps.desc: Delete the fake posts from every connected social account.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized content removed everywhere it appeared.

steps.title: Re-evaluate and reconnect the tool only after vendor confirms remediation
steps.desc: Confirm with the vendor that the root cause is fixed before restoring the integration, or select an alternative tool.

steps.title: Document root cause and review third-party integration security requirements
steps.desc: Record findings and reassess vendor security review requirements for social media management tools.

steps.title: Enumerate all accounts connected to the compromised tool
steps.desc: Identify every social account and channel linked to the affected tool/API key, since all are potentially exposed.

steps.title: Contact the tool vendor to report the compromise
steps.desc: Notify the vendor's security/support team and request their own incident response actions.

steps.title: Rotate credentials and API keys before reconnecting the tool
steps.desc: Rotate the tool's login credentials and any API keys/secrets prior to any reconnection.

ITID-21223.def: A post published to a company social media account by an employee or contractor who had legitimate access to the account, but who posted the content without authorization, in violation of policy, or after their access should have been revoked.
ITID-21223.purpose: Captures unauthorized brand-damaging posts published by an employee with legitimate access, acting outside their authorization.
scopeIncludes: A current employee with legitimate access posting unauthorized content (e.g., in anger, protest, or error)
A former employee/contractor posting after access should have been revoked but was not
scopeExcludes: Content posted by an attacker who obtained access through credential compromise (ITID-21211-ITID-21218)
ITID-21223.severity: Medium-High, depending on content severity and whether access should have already been revoked (the latter indicating an offboarding control failure).
ITID-21223.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the post is offensive/damaging or access should have been revoked.
ITID-21223.escalation: Escalate to HR and legal in addition to communications, given the insider/employment dimension.
indicators: Post traced to a known employee/former-employee account with legitimate credentials, no signs of external compromise
Access-log review showing the posting account matches an internal identity
vectors: Misuse of standing legitimate access
Access not revoked promptly after termination/role change
rootCauses: No prompt offboarding process for social media access
Overly broad standing access to social accounts not tied to current role
controls: Prompt offboarding/access revocation process for social media tools
Role-based, time-limited access to social media accounts
Employee social media acceptable-use policy
ITID-21223.detection: Access logs clearly attribute the post to a known internal identity, distinguishing this from external compromise.
ITID-21223.response: Remove the content, revoke the individual's access, and route to HR/legal for policy or employment action as applicable.
metrics: Time-to-access-revocation after offboarding
Count of insider-sourced unauthorized posts
ITID-21223.notes: Scoped to legitimate-access misuse; distinguished from every takeover leaf by the absence of any credential compromise.

playbook.name: Response: Insider/Employee Unauthorized Fake Post
playbook.description: For a fake or unauthorized post made by an insider or employee with legitimate access, acting outside their authority.

steps.title: Confirm the post was made by an authorized insider without approval
steps.desc: Review the posting account's access logs to identify which employee credential/session made the post and confirm it was not externally compromised.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR/Legal before contacting the individual.
steps.abort: If the credential itself appears externally compromised, redirect to the account-takeover playbook.

steps.title: Suspend the employee's posting access pending investigation
steps.desc: Temporarily revoke the individual's access to the social media account/tool while HR and Security investigate.

steps.title: Remove the unauthorized post
steps.desc: Delete the fake/unauthorized post from the account.

steps.title: Restore or reassign posting access per HR/Legal outcome
steps.desc: Once the personnel matter is resolved, restore, reassign, or permanently revoke the individual's access as decided.
steps.outcome: Access rights finalized per investigation outcome.

steps.title: Document the incident and review social media approval workflow
steps.desc: Log findings and evaluate whether a post-approval workflow would reduce risk of unauthorized posting.

steps.title: Assess content and reputational impact of the post
steps.desc: Determine what was posted and how far it has spread before removal.

steps.title: Engage HR and Legal on the personnel aspect
steps.desc: Loop in HR/Legal early since this is a policy-violation/personnel matter as well as a security event.

ITID-21224.def: Unauthorized modification, insertion, or reordering of content within a social media account's native scheduled-post queue, such that malicious content publishes automatically without requiring the attacker to be present at post time.
ITID-21224.purpose: Captures manipulation of a legitimate account's scheduled/queued posts, causing unauthorized content to publish automatically at a future time.
scopeIncludes: Insertion of malicious scheduled posts into the native platform queue
Deletion or reordering of legitimate scheduled content to allow malicious content to publish
scopeExcludes: Compromise of a third-party scheduling tool/API integration used to manage the queue (ITID-21222)
ITID-21224.severity: Medium-High. Delayed publication can mean the malicious post surfaces after the attacker's access is already revoked, complicating detection.
ITID-21224.priority: P2, escalating to P1 once content is confirmed live.
ITID-21224.escalation: Escalate to social media/communications team; audit the entire scheduled queue for other tampered entries, not just the one that published.
indicators: Unexpected content publishing at an unscheduled time with no recent live login
Scheduled-queue audit revealing unauthorized entries
vectors: Session hijacking used briefly to modify the queue before logging out
Compromised credentials used to insert scheduled content in advance
rootCauses: No periodic audit of the scheduled-post queue
Session tokens with excessive lifetime
controls: Periodic scheduled-queue audit
Session timeout/token lifetime limits
MFA and login alerting
ITID-21224.detection: Weak in real time since the malicious action (queue insertion) may predate publication by days; queue audits are the primary proactive control.
ITID-21224.response: Remove the published content, purge and audit the full queue, and rotate credentials/sessions.
metrics: Time between queue tampering and detection
Count of tampered queue entries found on audit
ITID-21224.notes: Differentiated from other Fake Post leaves by the delayed-publication mechanism via the native scheduling feature, not a third-party tool.

playbook.name: Response: Scheduled-Post Queue Manipulation Fake Post
playbook.description: For unauthorized fake posts introduced into a scheduled/queued content pipeline that later auto-publish.

steps.title: Confirm the fake post originated from the scheduling queue
steps.desc: Check the content-scheduling tool's audit trail to confirm the post was injected into the queue rather than posted live.
steps.outcome: Injection point confirmed as the scheduling pipeline.

steps.title: Pause the scheduling queue and all pending auto-publish jobs
steps.desc: Halt the scheduling tool immediately to prevent further unauthorized content from auto-publishing.
steps.outcome: No further unauthorized posts will publish.

steps.title: Remove any already-published fake posts and purge remaining tampered queue entries
steps.desc: Delete published unauthorized content and clear any remaining malicious items from the queue.
steps.outcome: All unauthorized content removed, queue clean.

steps.title: Resume scheduled publishing with a manual review checkpoint
steps.desc: Reinstate the queue with a temporary manual approval step before auto-publish resumes normally.
steps.outcome: Publishing pipeline restored with added oversight.

steps.title: Document root cause and harden the scheduling tool's access controls
steps.desc: Log how the queue was accessed and recommend access-control or approval-workflow improvements.

steps.title: Audit the full remaining queue for additional unauthorized entries
steps.desc: Review all pending scheduled posts across all accounts fed by the same tool for other tampered content.
steps.outcome: Full extent of queue manipulation identified.

steps.title: Revoke and rotate access credentials to the scheduling tool
steps.desc: Identify and remove the access path used to manipulate the queue, then rotate credentials/API keys.

ITID-21225.def: Unauthorized social media content published as a result of the compromise of a separately-hosted contest, giveaway, or marketing-campaign microsite that holds an authorized integration or credential to post to company social accounts.
ITID-21225.purpose: Captures unauthorized posts resulting from compromise of a third-party contest, campaign, or promotional microsite that has an integration to post on the company's behalf.
scopeIncludes: Compromise of a vendor-run contest/campaign microsite that has social posting integration
Malicious content published via that integration's access
scopeExcludes: Compromise of a general-purpose social media management tool (ITID-21222)
The microsite itself being defaced or used for phishing without a social-posting integration, tracked under the relevant website/third-party-vendor ITIDs elsewhere
ITID-21225.severity: Medium-High, depending on the scope of posting access the microsite integration held.
ITID-21225.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if content is confirmed live.
ITID-21225.escalation: Escalate to marketing/vendor management to revoke the microsite's posting integration immediately; assess the vendor's broader security posture.
indicators: Unauthorized posts correlated with a known campaign microsite's posting integration
Vendor security notification regarding the microsite
vectors: Exploitation of a vulnerability in the vendor-run microsite
Compromised vendor credentials with posting integration access
rootCauses: Insufficient security vetting of campaign/contest vendors before granting posting integrations
Integration access not time-limited to the campaign duration
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Vendor security assessment before granting social posting integrations
Time-limited, campaign-scoped integration access
Periodic review of active third-party posting integrations
ITID-21225.detection: Vendor notification and API activity correlation provide technical signal.
ITID-21225.response: Revoke the microsite's integration access immediately, remove unauthorized content, and reassess vendor security requirements.
metrics: Time-to-revocation of compromised integration
Number of active third-party posting integrations under management
sops: Vendor Social Posting Integration Review SOP
ITID-21225.notes: Scoped specifically to campaign/contest microsites with a social-posting integration, distinct from general social media management tools (ITID-21222).

playbook.name: Response: Fake Post via Compromised Third-Party Contest/Campaign Microsite Integration
playbook.description: For fake posts published through a compromised third-party contest, sweepstakes, or campaign microsite that is integrated with company social accounts.

steps.title: Confirm the microsite/campaign integration as the compromise source
steps.desc: Review the campaign vendor's integration logs and posting API usage to confirm the microsite was the entry point.

steps.title: Disconnect the microsite integration from social accounts
steps.desc: Revoke the API/OAuth connection between the campaign microsite and all linked social accounts.
steps.outcome: No further unauthorized posting via the integration.

steps.title: Remove unauthorized posts from all affected accounts
steps.desc: Delete the fake campaign-related posts from every connected social account.

steps.title: Relaunch the campaign only after vendor confirms remediation and a security review
steps.desc: Do not reconnect or relaunch the microsite until the vendor demonstrates the vulnerability is fixed.

steps.title: Document root cause and update third-party campaign vendor security requirements
steps.desc: Record findings and add security review requirements for future marketing microsite integrations.

steps.title: Assess exposure of any participant data collected by the microsite
steps.desc: Determine if the same compromise exposed entrant personal data collected for the contest/campaign, since this may trigger separate data-breach obligations.
steps.guidance: Loop in Privacy/Legal if participant data may be exposed.

steps.title: Take the microsite offline and notify the vendor
steps.desc: Coordinate with the campaign vendor/agency to take the compromised microsite offline and begin their own investigation.

ITID-21226.def: Unauthorized or fabricated content published to a company-associated social media channel where the deceptive core is an AI-generated deepfake (synthetic video, voice, or image) of a company representative, product, or event.
ITID-21226.purpose: Captures a fake post published to a company social media channel that uses AI-generated deepfake video, audio, or image content as its core deceptive element.
scopeIncludes: Deepfake video/audio of an executive or spokesperson published via a compromised or impersonating account
AI-generated synthetic imagery/video misrepresenting a company event or product
scopeExcludes: Broader, multi-channel AI-generated misinformation campaigns not centered on a single social media post, tracked under ITID-23514 (AI-Generated Deepfake Misinformation Campaign)
Non-deepfake fake posts (other Fake Post leaves)
ITID-21226.severity: High-Critical. Deepfake realism can make correction difficult even after takedown, and content may spread faster than fact-checking.
ITID-21226.escalation: Escalate immediately to communications, legal, and executive leadership; consider proactive media outreach to pre-empt further spread.
indicators: Video/audio content with subtle visual or audio artifacts inconsistent with genuine recordings
Content inconsistent with the purported speaker's known statements/schedule
Rapid, unusually high engagement/spread
vectors: Publication via a compromised official/executive account (see Account Takeover Type)
Publication via an impersonator/parody account (ITID-21221)
rootCauses: Publicly available source footage/audio of executives enabling deepfake creation
No established rapid deepfake-verification process
controls: Rapid deepfake-detection/verification capability
Pre-approved rapid-correction messaging templates
Media/press relationships for rapid fact-check outreach
ITID-21226.detection: Limited automated coverage; typically relies on manual review, media/public reporting, and any available deepfake-detection tooling.
ITID-21226.response: Take the content down via platform reporting, publish a clear public correction with supporting evidence, and coordinate with media contacts to limit further spread.
metrics: Time-to-takedown
Engagement/reach before correction
Time-to-public-correction
ITID-21226.notes: Scope decision: limited to a deepfake posted through a specific social media channel/post; a sustained, multi-platform synthetic-media disinformation campaign is tracked separately under ITID-23514 to avoid duplicating that broader campaign-level ITID.

playbook.name: Response: AI-Generated Deepfake Fake Post
playbook.description: For a fake post using AI-generated deepfake video, audio, or imagery falsely attributed to the company or an executive, posted without any actual account compromise.

steps.title: Confirm the content is a synthetic/deepfake fabrication
steps.desc: Analyze the video/audio/image for signs of AI generation and confirm it did not originate from a compromised company account.
steps.guidance: Engage digital forensics or a deepfake-detection resource where available.
steps.outcome: Content confirmed fabricated and account confirmed uncompromised.
steps.abort: If the posting account is company-owned and compromised, redirect to the account-takeover playbook.

steps.title: Report the content to the hosting platform(s) as synthetic/manipulated media
steps.desc: File takedown requests under the platform's synthetic-media or impersonation policy.

steps.title: Confirm takedown across all platforms hosting the deepfake
steps.desc: Track and confirm removal on each platform where the content was reported.
steps.outcome: Deepfake content removed or demoted where possible.
steps.abort: Where platforms decline removal, pursue Legal escalation.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence and mirrored copies
steps.desc: Continue monitoring brand mentions for reposted or newly-generated variants of the deepfake.

steps.title: Document the incident and update deepfake response playbook/media literacy guidance
steps.desc: Log findings and refine detection/response processes for future synthetic-media incidents.

steps.title: Assess spread and credibility risk of the deepfake
steps.desc: Track where the deepfake is circulating and how convincingly it is being received by audiences and media.

steps.title: Issue a public statement debunking the deepfake
steps.desc: Publish a clear, fast statement from verified official channels stating the content is fabricated.
steps.guidance: Coordinate closely with Communications/PR and Legal on wording.
steps.outcome: Public record established disavowing the content.

ITID-21227.def: A fake or unauthorized post on a company-associated social media channel, not clearly matching the impersonator, third-party-tool, insider, scheduled-queue, microsite, or deepfake leaves under this Type.
ITID-21227.purpose: Catch-all for fake posts on company-associated social media channels that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a more specific fake-post leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-21221 through ITID-21226
ITID-21227.severity: Reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-21227.escalation: Reclassify once the specific posting mechanism is clarified.
indicators: Fake post of unclear specific mechanism
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Social media account MFA enforcement
Content approval/publishing workflow requiring dual authorization
Brand monitoring for unauthorized social posts
ITID-21227.detection: Same social listening/platform telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-21227.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-21227.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Fake Post
playbook.description: General-purpose response for a fake or unauthorized post that does not fit a more specific fake-post subtype.

steps.title: Confirm the post is unauthorized and identify its source
steps.desc: Determine whether the fake post came from a compromised account, an insider, an impersonator, or a third-party integration.
steps.outcome: Source and category of the fake post identified.
steps.abort: If a more specific category is identified, redirect to that dedicated playbook.

steps.title: Report or remove the content through the appropriate channel
steps.desc: Use platform reporting tools or direct account access to stop further visibility of the fake post.

steps.title: Confirm removal of the fake post
steps.desc: Verify the content has been taken down or is no longer publicly accessible.

steps.title: Restore any affected account or integration to normal operation
steps.desc: Confirm normal posting/operations have resumed and access controls are intact.

steps.title: Document the incident and root cause
steps.desc: Log findings for trend analysis and future prevention.

steps.title: Document the content and assess impact
steps.desc: Screenshot the post and assess reach and reputational risk.
steps.outcome: Evidentiary record and impact assessment captured.

steps.title: Notify Communications/PR if public-facing impact is likely
steps.desc: Loop in Communications early for any reputational messaging needs.

ITID-21231.def: A mass or automated blast of offensive, threatening, or otherwise inappropriate direct messages sent from a compromised company social media account to its followers, contacts, or a purchased/scraped contact list.
ITID-21231.purpose: Captures offensive direct messages sent in bulk to followers/contacts from a compromised company social media account.
scopeIncludes: Bulk offensive DMs sent to followers from a compromised account
Offensive DMs sent as part of an automated script following takeover
scopeExcludes: Offensive content posted publicly rather than via direct message (ITID-21232)
The account-takeover technique itself, tracked under the Account Takeover Type
ITID-21231.severity: High. Direct, personal delivery to followers can cause significant individual distress and generates direct complaints.
ITID-21231.escalation: Escalate immediately to recover the account and halt the ongoing DM blast; notify affected followers if feasible.
indicators: Surge of follower complaints about receiving offensive DMs
Abnormal outbound DM volume detected by the platform
Account flagged/restricted by the platform for spam-like DM behavior
vectors: Credential compromise of the account (see Account Takeover Type)
Automated DM-blast scripting/bot tooling post-compromise
rootCauses: No MFA on the account enabling takeover
No outbound message-rate monitoring/alerting
controls: MFA on social media accounts
Outbound message-rate anomaly monitoring
Rapid account-recovery runbook
ITID-21231.detection: Follower complaints and platform spam-behavior flags provide the primary signal; outbound-rate monitoring can catch it faster where available.
ITID-21231.response: Recover the account immediately, halt the DM blast, and issue a follower-facing apology/clarification.
metrics: Number of followers who received the offensive DM
Time-to-account-recovery
ITID-21231.notes: Scoped to the direct-message channel specifically; public-facing offensive content is tracked under ITID-21232.

playbook.name: Response: Offensive Direct Message (DM) Blast from Compromised Account
playbook.description: For offensive/abusive direct messages sent in bulk to followers or contacts from a compromised company social media account.

steps.title: Confirm the account is compromised and DMs were sent without authorization
steps.desc: Check outbound message logs and confirm the DM blast was not sent by an authorized user.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed and DM blast scope identified.

steps.title: Initiate the platform's account-recovery process
steps.desc: Report the compromise and abusive messaging through the platform's priority support channel.

steps.title: Revoke sessions and connected app authorizations once access is regained
steps.desc: Force-logout all sessions and revoke any unauthorized third-party app access.

steps.title: Send a public and/or direct apology to affected recipients
steps.desc: Issue an apology explaining the account was compromised, once control is regained.
steps.guidance: Coordinate wording with Communications/PR.

steps.title: Document root cause and update access controls
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend control improvements.

steps.title: Identify recipients of the offensive DMs
steps.desc: Pull the list or estimate of accounts that received the offensive messages.
steps.guidance: Needed for follow-up apology/notification.

steps.title: Disable direct messaging capability on the account if possible
steps.desc: Temporarily restrict DM functionality to stop further offensive messages while recovery is in progress.

steps.title: Re-secure the account with MFA
steps.desc: Enable/strengthen MFA before resuming normal use.

ITID-21232.def: Offensive, threatening, or spam comments/replies posted publicly under other users' or the company's own content from a compromised or misused company social media account.
ITID-21232.purpose: Captures offensive content posted publicly as comments or replies from a compromised or misused company account.
scopeIncludes: Offensive replies posted on third-party posts using the company account's identity
Offensive comments posted under the company's own posts by an attacker with account access
scopeExcludes: Offensive direct messages (ITID-21231)
Automated bot-posted offensive content at scale, tracked separately given its distinct detection profile (ITID-21233)
ITID-21232.severity: Medium-High. Public visibility under third-party content can spread faster than a standalone post.
ITID-21232.escalation: Escalate to recover the account and mass-delete the offensive comments/replies.
indicators: Offensive comments/replies visible under third-party or own posts, attributed to the company account
Public complaints/screenshots circulating
vectors: Credential compromise of the account (see Account Takeover Type)
rootCauses: No MFA on the account enabling takeover
No monitoring of the account's outbound comment/reply activity
controls: MFA on social media accounts
Comment/reply activity monitoring
Rapid account-recovery runbook
ITID-21232.detection: Social listening and public reporting provide the primary signal; native platform activity logs confirm authorship.
ITID-21232.response: Recover the account, delete the offensive comments/replies, and issue a public clarification if the content spread meaningfully.
metrics: Number of offensive comments/replies removed
Time-to-account-recovery
detections: Social listening detection of offensive comment activity
ITID-21232.notes: Scoped to manually-attributable public comments/replies; large-scale automated posting is tracked under ITID-21233.

playbook.name: Response: Offensive Public Comment/Reply Spam
playbook.description: For a burst of offensive comments or replies posted publicly from a compromised or abused company account.

steps.title: Confirm the source of the offensive comments/replies
steps.desc: Determine whether the comments came from a compromised account, an insider, or an automated bot exploiting an integration.

steps.title: Lock down the source account/integration to stop further posting
steps.desc: Suspend the compromised account, revoke the abused integration, or disable the offending insider's access as applicable.

steps.title: Delete the offensive comments/replies
steps.desc: Remove every identified offensive comment from public threads.

steps.title: Re-secure the account and resume normal posting
steps.desc: Enable MFA and confirm the account is safe to resume normal operations.

steps.title: Document root cause and control improvements
steps.desc: Log findings for future prevention.

steps.title: Catalog the affected posts/threads where offensive comments appear
steps.desc: Identify every post or thread where the offensive replies were made for targeted cleanup.
steps.outcome: Full list of affected threads compiled.

steps.title: Revoke sessions/tokens tied to the compromise vector
steps.desc: Force-logout sessions or rotate API keys associated with the compromised source.

ITID-21233.def: Offensive content published at high volume across posts, comments, or replies via automated scripts or bots operating through a compromised company social media account or connected integration.
ITID-21233.purpose: Captures offensive content posted at scale through automated or bot-driven posting following account or integration compromise.
scopeIncludes: High-volume, scripted/bot-driven offensive posting distinguishable from a single manual post
Automated posting continuing after the attacker is no longer actively controlling the session
scopeExcludes: A single manually-posted offensive comment/reply (ITID-21232)
A single manually-posted offensive DM blast without bot automation (ITID-21231, if manually driven rather than scripted)
ITID-21233.severity: High. Automation can generate offensive content faster than manual moderation/removal can keep pace.
ITID-21233.escalation: Escalate immediately; revoke API/session access to stop the automated posting at the source rather than deleting content one item at a time.
indicators: Abnormally high posting-rate/volume from the account
Content pattern consistent with scripted/templated generation
Platform automated-behavior flag/restriction on the account
vectors: Compromised API token/integration used to drive automated posting
Malicious bot script run against a compromised session
rootCauses: No outbound posting-rate limiting/anomaly detection
Overly broad API/integration permissions
controls: Outbound posting-rate anomaly monitoring
Least-privilege API/integration scoping
Rapid API token revocation runbook
ITID-21233.detection: Posting-rate anomaly monitoring provides a strong, fast technical signal distinct from manual-post scenarios.
ITID-21233.response: Revoke the compromised API/session access immediately to stop further automated posting, then clean up and audit posted content.
metrics: Volume of automated offensive posts
Time-to-access-revocation
ITID-21233.notes: Differentiated from manual-post siblings by the scale/automation signature, which drives a different (access-revocation-first) response approach.

playbook.name: Response: Offensive Content via Automated/Bot-Posted Messaging
playbook.description: For offensive content posted by a compromised or malicious automated bot/integration connected to company social accounts.

steps.title: Confirm the offensive content originated from an automated bot/integration
steps.desc: Review posting metadata and integration logs to confirm a bot or automated process, not a human, published the content.

steps.title: Disable the bot/automation immediately
steps.desc: Pause or disconnect the automated posting integration to stop further offensive output.

steps.title: Remove the offensive posted content
steps.desc: Delete all offensive posts generated by the bot.

steps.title: Re-enable the bot only after fixing the root cause and adding content safeguards
steps.desc: Add output filtering/review safeguards before restoring automated posting, or discontinue the automation.

steps.title: Document root cause and add bot output monitoring
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend ongoing monitoring/guardrails for automated social posting tools.

steps.title: Identify which bot/integration and what triggered it
steps.desc: Determine whether the bot was compromised, misconfigured, or manipulated (e.g. via adversarial input) into posting offensive content.

steps.title: Rotate credentials/API keys used by the bot
steps.desc: Rotate any credentials or tokens the bot used, in case they were compromised.

ITID-21234.def: Offensive, threatening, or inappropriate content broadcast in real time via a compromised company social media account's livestream or live video feature.
ITID-21234.purpose: Captures offensive content broadcast live through a compromised company social media account's livestream/live video feature.
scopeIncludes: Live video broadcast displaying offensive content from a compromised account
Live audio/video stream hijacked mid-broadcast
scopeExcludes: Pre-recorded offensive content posted as a standard post (other Offensive Messaging leaves)
ITID-21234.severity: High. Live content cannot be pre-moderated and may be viewed and clipped/re-shared before the stream can be terminated.
ITID-21234.escalation: Escalate immediately for emergency stream termination; monitor for re-uploaded clips post-termination.
indicators: Active live stream displaying unexpected offensive content
Viewer reports/complaints during the live broadcast
Platform live-content flag/takedown notice
vectors: Credential compromise of the account (see Account Takeover Type)
Compromise of connected streaming hardware/software credentials
rootCauses: No MFA on the account enabling takeover
No real-time monitoring of active company livestreams
controls: MFA on social media and streaming accounts
Real-time livestream monitoring during scheduled broadcasts
Emergency stream-termination runbook
ITID-21234.detection: Real-time viewer reports and any active livestream monitoring provide the primary signal; detection is inherently time-critical.
ITID-21234.response: Terminate the live broadcast immediately, recover the account, and search for and request removal of any re-uploaded clips.
metrics: Time-to-stream-termination
Peak concurrent viewers exposed
ITID-21234.notes: Scoped to the real-time/live broadcast format specifically, which requires a faster, different response path than standard post removal.

playbook.name: Response: Offensive Livestream/Live Video Messaging
playbook.description: For offensive content broadcast live via a compromised company social media account's livestream/live-video feature, requiring real-time takedown.

steps.title: Confirm the livestream is unauthorized and offensive in real time
steps.desc: Verify the live broadcast is not an authorized event and assess its offensive content immediately.
steps.guidance: Speed is critical — livestreams reach viewers in real time.

steps.title: End the livestream immediately via platform emergency controls or account recovery
steps.desc: Use the platform's emergency livestream-termination process or urgent account-recovery escalation to end the broadcast as fast as possible.
steps.guidance: Many platforms offer an expedited path specifically for live-content abuse.

steps.title: Remove the archived/recorded version of the stream
steps.desc: Delete any saved replay of the livestream from the account and request removal of any platform-cached copies.

steps.title: Re-secure the account and issue a public statement if the stream was widely viewed
steps.desc: Enable MFA and, if viewership was significant, issue a statement addressing the incident.
steps.outcome: Account secured and public confidence addressed.

steps.title: Document root cause and response time to the live incident
steps.desc: Log the full timeline, focusing on time-to-termination, for after-action review.

steps.title: Capture evidence of the live broadcast for reporting purposes
steps.desc: Record/screen-capture the stream where possible for the abuse report and internal record.

steps.title: Initiate full account-recovery process
steps.desc: Continue with standard account-recovery steps once the immediate live broadcast is stopped.

steps.title: Revoke sessions and connected app authorizations
steps.desc: Force-logout all sessions and revoke any third-party streaming-tool access used to compromise the account.

ITID-21235.def: Offensive, threatening, or inappropriate content posted to a company social media account's ephemeral story or status feature, where the content auto-expires after a short period, complicating detection and evidence capture.
ITID-21235.purpose: Captures offensive content posted via a company account's ephemeral story/status feature, which typically disappears after a short period.
scopeIncludes: Offensive content in a story/status format that auto-expires within 24 hours or similar
Cases where the ephemeral nature delayed or complicated internal detection
scopeExcludes: Offensive content in a standard, persistent post format (ITID-21232)
ITID-21235.severity: Medium-High. Audience exposure can be significant despite the short lifespan, and evidence capture for investigation is harder.
ITID-21235.escalation: Escalate immediately; capture evidence (screenshots/archive) before the content expires on its own.
indicators: Viewer reports of an offensive story/status before it expires
Screenshots circulating externally after the original content has expired
vectors: Credential compromise of the account (see Account Takeover Type)
rootCauses: No MFA on the account enabling takeover
No monitoring of ephemeral-content posting activity
controls: MFA on social media accounts
Ephemeral-content posting activity monitoring/alerting
Rapid account-recovery runbook
ITID-21235.detection: Weak by default given content auto-expiry; relies on real-time viewer reports or activity-monitoring alerts rather than post-hoc review.
ITID-21235.response: Recover the account, manually remove the story if still active, and preserve any available evidence for investigation.
metrics: Time-to-account-recovery
Estimated story/status view count before expiry
ITID-21235.notes: Scoped to the ephemeral-content format specifically, given the distinct evidence-capture and detection challenges versus persistent posts.

playbook.name: Response: Offensive Content in Story/Ephemeral Post Format
playbook.description: For offensive content posted via a compromised account's disappearing/ephemeral story format, which may expire before standard response actions complete.

steps.title: Confirm the compromise and capture the ephemeral content before it expires
steps.desc: Screenshot/record the story content immediately, since it may auto-delete within hours.

steps.title: Manually delete the story immediately if any access remains
steps.desc: If partial account access is still available, delete the offensive story directly rather than waiting for its natural expiry.
steps.guidance: Do not rely on auto-expiry — screenshots and reshares can outlive the original post.

steps.title: Revoke sessions and connected app authorizations once access is regained
steps.desc: Force-logout all sessions and revoke unauthorized third-party access.

steps.title: Re-secure the account with MFA
steps.desc: Enable/strengthen MFA before resuming normal use.

steps.title: Document root cause and note detection lag for ephemeral content
steps.desc: Log findings, including how quickly the incident was detected relative to the story's expiry window.

steps.title: Assess viewer reach while the story is still live
steps.desc: Check story view counts and any screenshots/reshares already circulating.

steps.title: Initiate the platform's account-recovery process
steps.desc: Report the compromise through the platform's priority support channel.

ITID-21236.def: Offensive content delivered via a company social media channel, not clearly matching the direct-message, public-comment, automated, livestream, or ephemeral-content leaves under this Type.
ITID-21236.purpose: Catch-all for offensive messaging via company social media channels that does not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a more specific offensive-messaging leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-21231 through ITID-21235
ITID-21236.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High pending investigation.
ITID-21236.escalation: Reclassify once the specific delivery format is clarified.
indicators: Offensive content of unclear specific delivery format
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Social media account MFA enforcement
Content approval/publishing workflow requiring dual authorization
Brand monitoring for unauthorized social posts
ITID-21236.detection: Same social listening/platform telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-21236.response: Recover the account and investigate to reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-21236.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Offensive Messaging
playbook.description: General-purpose response for offensive/abusive messaging posted via a company social media account that does not fit a more specific offensive-messaging subtype.

steps.title: Confirm the offensive messaging is unauthorized and identify its source
steps.desc: Determine whether the messaging originated from a compromised account, an insider, or an automated integration.
steps.abort: If a more specific category applies, redirect to that dedicated playbook.

steps.title: Stop further offensive messaging at the source
steps.desc: Suspend the compromised account, disable the automation, or revoke the insider's access as applicable.

steps.title: Remove all offensive content
steps.desc: Delete the offensive messages/posts/comments.

steps.title: Re-secure the account and resume normal operations
steps.desc: Enable MFA and confirm safety before resuming normal posting.

steps.title: Document root cause and control improvements
steps.desc: Log findings for future prevention.

steps.title: Document the offensive content and its reach
steps.desc: Screenshot the content and assess how widely it was seen or shared.
steps.outcome: Evidentiary record and reach assessment captured.

steps.title: Revoke sessions/credentials tied to the compromise vector
steps.desc: Force-logout sessions or rotate credentials associated with the compromise.

ITID-21241.def: A post from a company social media account linking to a fraudulent cryptocurrency, token, or investment scheme, exploiting the account's trusted brand identity to lend the scam credibility.
ITID-21241.purpose: Captures a cryptocurrency or investment scam link posted from a compromised or misused company social media account.
scopeIncludes: Posts promoting a fake token giveaway, crypto doubling scheme, or investment opportunity via the company account
Links to attacker-controlled wallet/investment sites
scopeExcludes: Direct-message crypto/investment scams sent to individuals, tracked under the relevant social-engineering ITID elsewhere (e.g., ITID-11723)
Generic malware download links with no crypto/investment framing (ITID-21242)
ITID-21241.severity: High. Followers may suffer direct financial loss trusting the brand's credibility, creating both reputational and potential legal exposure.
ITID-21241.escalation: Escalate immediately to recover the account, remove the post, and issue a public fraud warning to followers.
indicators: Post promoting an unfamiliar cryptocurrency/investment opportunity from the company account
Follower reports of financial loss after clicking the link
Link resolving to a known scam/wallet-drain site
vectors: Credential compromise of the account (see Account Takeover Type)
rootCauses: No MFA on the account enabling takeover
No outbound link-monitoring/reputation checking on posted content
controls: MFA on social media accounts
Outbound link reputation monitoring
Public follower fraud-warning template
ITID-21241.detection: Follower complaints and social listening provide the primary signal; link-reputation checks can flag known scam infrastructure.
ITID-21241.response: Recover the account, remove the post, issue a public fraud warning, and report the scam infrastructure to the platform/registrar.
metrics: Estimated follower financial loss reported
Time-to-takedown
ITID-21241.notes: Scope decision: limited to links posted via a company social channel; the same scam delivered by DM to individual targets is tracked under the social-engineering domain (e.g., ITID-11723) to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Cryptocurrency/Investment Scam Link Post
playbook.description: For a fraudulent post promoting a cryptocurrency or investment scam link, published via a compromised company social media account.

steps.title: Confirm the compromise and capture the scam link/post
steps.desc: Screenshot the post and record the exact scam URL and any wallet addresses or payment details referenced.
steps.outcome: Evidentiary record captured, including the malicious URL.

steps.title: Initiate the platform's account-recovery process
steps.desc: Report the takeover through the platform's priority support channel.

steps.title: Delete the scam post and revoke sessions once access is regained
steps.desc: Remove the fraudulent post and force-logout all sessions/revoke connected apps.
steps.outcome: Content removed and attacker access revoked.

steps.title: Re-secure the account with MFA
steps.desc: Enable/strengthen MFA before resuming normal use.

steps.title: Document root cause and coordinate with fraud/financial crimes team if needed
steps.desc: Log findings and refer confirmed financial fraud activity to the appropriate internal fraud team or law enforcement.

steps.title: Assess follower click/engagement exposure
steps.desc: Review engagement metrics (likes, replies, click counts if available) to estimate how many followers may have interacted with the scam link.

steps.title: Report the scam domain/link for blocking
steps.desc: Submit the fraudulent link to the platform's link-safety team and to relevant domain registrars/browser safe-browsing lists to get it blocked network-wide.

steps.title: Warn followers who may have already clicked the link
steps.desc: Post a public warning via an alternate owned channel that the scam link is not legitimate and followers should not enter wallet/payment details.
steps.guidance: Coordinate wording with Communications/PR.

ITID-21242.def: A post from a company social media account linking directly to a malware payload or a fake download page, exploiting the account's trusted identity to drive follower infections.
ITID-21242.purpose: Captures a malware-download link posted from a compromised or misused company social media account.
scopeIncludes: Posts linking to an executable, installer, or fake 'download our app/tool' page that delivers malware
Links using URL shorteners specifically to disguise a known-malicious download, when the primary intent is malware delivery
scopeExcludes: Fake software update prompts delivered via a defaced website (ITID-21143)
Credential phishing links (ITID-21243)
ITID-21242.severity: High. Followers infected via a trusted brand link may not suspect malicious intent, increasing successful infection rates.
ITID-21242.escalation: Escalate immediately to recover the account, remove the post, and issue a public malware warning with remediation guidance for anyone who clicked.
indicators: Post linking to an unfamiliar download from the company account
Follower reports of malware infection after downloading
Link resolving to known-malicious file hosting
