vectors: Credential compromise of the account (see Account Takeover Type)
rootCauses: No MFA on the account enabling takeover
No outbound link-monitoring/reputation checking on posted content
controls: MFA on social media accounts
Outbound link reputation monitoring
Public follower malware-warning template
ITID-21242.detection: Follower complaints and endpoint detections on affected followers (where visible) provide the primary signal; link-reputation checks can flag known-malicious hosting.
ITID-21242.response: Recover the account, remove the post, issue a public malware warning with removal guidance, and report the malicious infrastructure for takedown.
metrics: Estimated follower click-through/infection count
Time-to-takedown
ITID-21242.notes: Distinguished from the website-based fake-update-prompt leaf (ITID-21143) by the delivery channel being social media rather than the company's own website.

playbook.name: Response: Malware Download Link Post
playbook.description: For a fraudulent post distributing a malware download link, published via a compromised company social media account.

steps.title: Confirm the compromise and capture the malicious link
steps.desc: Screenshot the post and record the malware download URL without visiting it from an unprotected device.
steps.guidance: Use an isolated/sandboxed environment for any further analysis of the link.

steps.title: Initiate the platform's account-recovery process
steps.desc: Report the takeover through the platform's priority support channel.

steps.title: Delete the malicious post and revoke sessions once access is regained
steps.desc: Remove the fraudulent post and force-logout all sessions/revoke connected apps.
steps.outcome: Content removed and attacker access revoked.

steps.title: Re-secure the account with MFA
steps.desc: Enable/strengthen MFA before resuming normal use.

steps.title: Document root cause and share indicators of compromise with security teams
steps.desc: Log findings and distribute the malware URL/hash indicators internally for blocking on corporate networks.

steps.title: Assess follower click exposure
steps.desc: Review engagement metrics to estimate how many followers may have clicked the link.

steps.title: Report the malicious domain to threat-intel/blocklist services and the platform
steps.desc: Submit the malware URL to the platform's link-safety team and to threat-intelligence/safe-browsing blocklists for network-wide blocking.

steps.title: Warn followers who may have already clicked the link
steps.desc: Post a public warning via an alternate owned channel advising followers who clicked the link to run a malware scan and avoid entering credentials on any resulting page.

ITID-21243.def: A post from a company social media account linking to a fake login/credential-harvesting page, exploiting the account's trusted identity to drive followers to enter credentials on attacker-controlled infrastructure.
ITID-21243.purpose: Captures a credential-phishing link posted from a compromised or misused company social media account.
scopeIncludes: Posts linking to a fake login page impersonating the company or a related service, from the company's own account
Links directing followers to enter account credentials, payment details, or personal data on a phishing page
scopeExcludes: Malware-download links (ITID-21242)
Cryptocurrency/investment scam links (ITID-21241)
Meeting-invite-themed credential phishing links, tracked under its own ITID (ITID-62831)
ITID-21243.severity: High. Followers may have their credentials or personal data harvested, creating direct customer harm and potential regulatory notification obligations.
ITID-21243.escalation: Escalate immediately to recover the account, remove the post, and issue a public phishing warning advising affected followers to change credentials.
indicators: Post linking to a fake login page from the company account
Follower reports of credential compromise after clicking the link
Link resolving to known phishing infrastructure
vectors: Credential compromise of the account (see Account Takeover Type)
rootCauses: No MFA on the account enabling takeover
No outbound link-monitoring/reputation checking on posted content
controls: MFA on social media accounts
Outbound link reputation monitoring
Public follower phishing-warning template
ITID-21243.detection: Follower complaints and link-reputation checks provide the primary signal.
ITID-21243.response: Recover the account, remove the post, issue a public phishing warning, and report the phishing infrastructure for takedown.
metrics: Estimated follower click-through/credential-harvest count
Time-to-takedown
ITID-21243.notes: Scope decision: covers phishing links posted via the company's own social account; the pre-existing ITID-62831 covers a distinct meeting-invite phishing theme and is excluded here to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Credential Phishing Link Post
playbook.description: For a fraudulent post distributing a credential-phishing link, published via a compromised company social media account.

steps.title: Confirm the compromise and capture the phishing link
steps.desc: Screenshot the post and record the phishing URL and the impersonated login page it targets (e.g. a fake company or bank login).

steps.title: Initiate the platform's account-recovery process
steps.desc: Report the takeover through the platform's priority support channel.

steps.title: Delete the phishing post and revoke sessions once access is regained
steps.desc: Remove the fraudulent post and force-logout all sessions/revoke connected apps.
steps.outcome: Content removed and attacker access revoked.

steps.title: Re-secure the account with MFA
steps.desc: Enable/strengthen MFA before resuming normal use.

steps.title: Document root cause and refer confirmed victim credential exposure to fraud team
steps.desc: Log findings and refer any confirmed follower credential compromise to the fraud/incident response team for follow-up.

steps.title: Assess follower click and credential-entry exposure
steps.desc: Review engagement metrics to estimate exposure and check whether the phishing kit has any visible victim counter.

steps.title: Report the phishing domain for takedown/blocking
steps.desc: Submit the phishing URL to the platform, the hosting provider's abuse desk, and browser safe-browsing lists to get it blocked and taken down.

steps.title: Warn followers who may have entered credentials
steps.desc: Post a public warning via an alternate owned channel urging anyone who entered credentials on the fake page to change their password immediately.

ITID-21244.def: A post from a company social media account announcing a fake giveaway, sweepstake, or contest with a link that harvests personal data, payment details, or drives a follow-on scam, exploiting the account's trusted identity.
ITID-21244.purpose: Captures a fake giveaway or contest scam link posted from a compromised or misused company social media account.
scopeIncludes: Posts announcing a fake free-product/prize giveaway requiring a click-through
Fake contest requiring entrants to submit payment or personal information via the linked page
scopeExcludes: Cryptocurrency-specific giveaway scams (ITID-21241)
Counterfeit storefront scams not framed as a giveaway/contest (ITID-21245)
ITID-21244.severity: Medium-High. Financial/data harm to followers is typically smaller-scale per victim than a crypto or storefront scam but volume can be high.
ITID-21244.escalation: Escalate to recover the account, remove the post, and issue a public warning clarifying the giveaway is fake.
indicators: Post announcing an unfamiliar giveaway/contest from the company account
Follower reports of data/payment harvesting after entering
Link resolving to a known scam entry-form site
vectors: Credential compromise of the account (see Account Takeover Type)
rootCauses: No MFA on the account enabling takeover
No outbound link-monitoring/reputation checking on posted content
controls: MFA on social media accounts
Outbound link reputation monitoring
Public follower fraud-warning template
ITID-21244.detection: Follower complaints and social listening provide the primary signal.
ITID-21244.response: Recover the account, remove the post, and issue a public clarification that the giveaway is fraudulent.
metrics: Estimated follower click-through/data-harvest count
Time-to-takedown
ITID-21244.notes: Differentiated from crypto scams (ITID-21241) and storefront scams (ITID-21245) by the giveaway/contest framing specifically.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Giveaway/Contest Scam Link Post
playbook.description: For a fraudulent post advertising a fake giveaway or contest with a scam link, published via a compromised company social media account.

steps.title: Confirm the compromise and capture the fake giveaway post
steps.desc: Screenshot the post and record the scam link and any requested personal/payment information.

steps.title: Initiate the platform's account-recovery process
steps.desc: Report the takeover through the platform's priority support channel.

steps.title: Delete the fake giveaway post and revoke sessions once access is regained
steps.desc: Remove the fraudulent post and force-logout all sessions/revoke connected apps.
steps.outcome: Content removed and attacker access revoked.

steps.title: Re-secure the account with MFA
steps.desc: Enable/strengthen MFA before resuming normal use.

steps.title: Document root cause and coordinate with fraud team on victim follow-up
steps.desc: Log findings and refer any followers who submitted personal/payment information to the fraud team.

steps.title: Assess follower engagement and entry exposure
steps.desc: Review comments/shares to estimate how many followers engaged with or entered the fake giveaway.

steps.title: Report the scam link/domain for blocking
steps.desc: Submit the fraudulent link to the platform's trust and safety team for blocking.

steps.title: Publicly clarify the company is not running the advertised giveaway
steps.desc: Post a warning via an alternate owned channel that the giveaway is fraudulent and followers should not click the link or submit information.

ITID-21245.def: A post from a company social media account linking to a counterfeit or entirely fake e-commerce storefront, exploiting the account's trusted identity to sell fraudulent or nonexistent goods.
ITID-21245.purpose: Captures a counterfeit or fake storefront link posted from a compromised or misused company social media account.
scopeIncludes: Posts linking to a lookalike storefront selling counterfeit branded goods
Posts linking to a fake storefront that takes payment for goods never shipped
scopeExcludes: Fake giveaway/contest scams (ITID-21244)
Counterfeit goods sold through channels unrelated to a compromised company social account, tracked under brand-protection/counterfeit ITIDs elsewhere in the taxonomy
ITID-21245.severity: High. Direct financial loss to customers combined with counterfeit-goods brand/legal exposure.
ITID-21245.escalation: Escalate to recover the account, remove the post, and engage brand protection/legal on the counterfeit storefront takedown.
indicators: Post linking to an unfamiliar storefront from the company account
Customer reports of undelivered goods or counterfeit products after purchase
Storefront domain registered recently and unaffiliated with the company
vectors: Credential compromise of the account (see Account Takeover Type)
rootCauses: No MFA on the account enabling takeover
No outbound link-monitoring/reputation checking on posted content
controls: MFA on social media accounts
Outbound link reputation monitoring
Brand protection/counterfeit storefront monitoring
ITID-21245.detection: Customer complaints and brand-protection monitoring provide the primary signal.
ITID-21245.response: Recover the account, remove the post, and pursue takedown of the counterfeit storefront with brand protection/legal.
metrics: Estimated customer financial loss reported
Time-to-storefront-takedown
ITID-21245.notes: Scoped to storefront scams distributed via a compromised company social account; counterfeit goods sold through independent, unrelated channels are tracked under the taxonomy's brand-protection ITIDs.

playbook.name: Response: Counterfeit/Fake Storefront Scam Link Post
playbook.description: For a fraudulent post promoting a counterfeit or fake e-commerce storefront link, published via a compromised company social media account.

steps.title: Confirm the compromise and capture the fake storefront link
steps.desc: Screenshot the post and document the fraudulent storefront URL and any products/pricing being advertised.

steps.title: Initiate the platform's account-recovery process
steps.desc: Report the takeover through the platform's priority support channel.

steps.title: Delete the scam post and revoke sessions once access is regained
steps.desc: Remove the fraudulent post and force-logout all sessions/revoke connected apps.
steps.outcome: Content removed and attacker access revoked.

steps.title: Re-secure the account with MFA
steps.desc: Enable/strengthen MFA before resuming normal use.

steps.title: Document root cause and refer confirmed victim purchases to fraud team
steps.desc: Log findings and refer any confirmed follower financial loss to the fraud/incident response team.

steps.title: Assess follower click and purchase exposure
steps.desc: Review engagement metrics to estimate how many followers may have clicked or attempted a purchase on the fake storefront.

steps.title: Report the counterfeit storefront for takedown
steps.desc: Submit the fake storefront domain to the platform, hosting provider abuse desk, and payment processor (if identifiable) for takedown.

steps.title: Warn followers who may have made a purchase or entered payment details
steps.desc: Post a public warning via an alternate owned channel advising anyone who purchased from the fake store to dispute the charge with their bank.

ITID-21246.def: A post from a company social media account containing a URL-shortener-wrapped link whose ultimate destination and scam type are obfuscated at post time, requiring resolution before the underlying fraud (crypto, malware, phishing, giveaway, or storefront) can be identified.
ITID-21246.purpose: Captures a fraudulent link posted from a compromised company social media account where the scam's specific type is deliberately obscured behind a URL shortener, complicating triage.
scopeIncludes: Posts using a URL shortener specifically to conceal the destination pending investigator resolution
Cases logged at the point of discovery before the shortened link has been resolved to a specific scam category
scopeExcludes: Cases where the destination has been resolved and clearly matches a specific sibling leaf (ITID-21241 through ITID-21245) — reclassify once resolved
ITID-21246.severity: High pending resolution; treat as equivalent to the most severe plausible destination type until confirmed otherwise.
ITID-21246.escalation: Escalate immediately to resolve the shortened URL's true destination and reclassify to the applicable specific leaf.
indicators: Post containing a shortened/obfuscated link with no visible preview of the destination
Follower reports without a clear description of what the link led to
vectors: Credential compromise of the account (see Account Takeover Type)
Deliberate use of URL shorteners to evade link-reputation filtering
rootCauses: No MFA on the account enabling takeover
No automated expansion/scanning of shortened URLs before or after posting
controls: Automated URL-shortener expansion and reputation scanning
MFA on social media accounts
ITID-21246.detection: Requires active link resolution/sandboxing since the destination is not visible from the post alone.
ITID-21246.response: Resolve the shortened URL's destination immediately, recover the account, remove the post, and reclassify to the specific scam-type leaf once known.
metrics: Time-to-URL-resolution
Time-to-reclassification
ITID-21246.notes: This is a triage/obfuscation-driven leaf, distinct from the catch-all ITID-21247: it is used specifically when a shortener is actively concealing the destination, not merely when detail is generally lacking.

playbook.name: Response: URL Shortener-Obfuscated Fraudulent Link Post
playbook.description: For a fraudulent post using a shortened/obfuscated URL to disguise its true malicious destination, published via a compromised company social media account.

steps.title: Confirm the compromise and resolve the shortened URL's true destination
steps.desc: Use a safe URL-expansion/sandbox tool to resolve the shortened link without visiting it directly, and classify the underlying scam type (phishing, malware, storefront, etc.).
steps.guidance: Never click a suspicious shortened link directly from a production device.
steps.outcome: True destination and scam category identified.

steps.title: Initiate the platform's account-recovery process
steps.desc: Report the takeover through the platform's priority support channel.

steps.title: Delete the post and revoke sessions once access is regained
steps.desc: Remove the fraudulent post and force-logout all sessions/revoke connected apps.
steps.outcome: Content removed and attacker access revoked.

steps.title: Re-secure the account with MFA
steps.desc: Enable/strengthen MFA before resuming normal use.

steps.title: Document root cause and consider restricting use of URL shorteners in official posts
steps.desc: Log findings and evaluate a policy of using only fully-visible, branded links in official communications going forward.

steps.title: Assess follower click exposure
steps.desc: Review engagement/click metrics where available to estimate exposure.

steps.title: Report both the shortener link and its resolved destination for blocking
steps.desc: Submit the shortened URL to the shortening service's abuse desk and the resolved destination domain to relevant blocklists/platform trust and safety.
steps.guidance: Blocking only the resolved domain is insufficient if the attacker can repoint the shortener.

steps.title: Warn followers based on the resolved scam category
steps.desc: Issue a public warning via an alternate owned channel tailored to the actual scam type discovered (e.g. credential exposure vs. malware vs. financial loss).

ITID-21247.def: A fraudulent link posted from a company-associated social media channel, not clearly matching the crypto, malware, phishing, giveaway, storefront, or shortener-obfuscated leaves under this Type.
ITID-21247.purpose: Catch-all for fraudulent links posted via company social media channels that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a more specific fraudulent-link leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-21241 through ITID-21246
ITID-21247.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High pending investigation.
ITID-21247.escalation: Reclassify once the destination and scam type are clarified.
indicators: Fraudulent link of unclear specific scam type
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Social media account MFA enforcement
URL/link scanning before publishing on official accounts
Brand monitoring for unauthorized social posts
ITID-21247.detection: Same outbound-link telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-21247.response: Recover the account, remove the post, and investigate to reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-21247.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Fraudulent Link Post
playbook.description: General-purpose response for a fraudulent link post that does not fit a more specific fraudulent-link subtype.

steps.title: Confirm the compromise and classify the fraudulent link's purpose
steps.desc: Screenshot the post and determine, where possible, whether the link leads to phishing, malware, a scam storefront, or another fraud type.
steps.outcome: Evidentiary record captured and link category identified where possible.
steps.abort: If a more specific category is confirmed, redirect to that dedicated playbook.

steps.title: Initiate the platform's account-recovery process
steps.desc: Report the takeover through the platform's priority support channel.

steps.title: Delete the post and revoke sessions once access is regained
steps.desc: Remove the fraudulent post and force-logout all sessions/revoke connected apps.
steps.outcome: Content removed and attacker access revoked.

steps.title: Re-secure the account with MFA
steps.desc: Enable/strengthen MFA before resuming normal use.

steps.title: Document root cause and control improvements
steps.desc: Log findings for future prevention.

steps.title: Assess follower click exposure
steps.desc: Review engagement metrics to estimate exposure.

steps.title: Report the fraudulent link for blocking
steps.desc: Submit the link to the platform and relevant blocklist services.

steps.title: Warn followers who may have clicked the link
steps.desc: Post a public warning via an alternate owned channel.

ITID-21311.def: Unauthorized publication of a malicious update to the company's mobile app through the compromise of its official developer account/listing on an authorized app store (e.g., Google Play, Apple App Store), such that the malicious version is distributed as if it were a legitimate release.
ITID-21311.purpose: Captures a malicious app update distributed after an attacker compromises the company's official app store developer listing.
scopeIncludes: Compromise of the developer console/publisher account used to push app updates
A malicious build uploaded and approved through the legitimate store submission process using stolen credentials
scopeExcludes: Compromise occurring earlier in the pipeline, at the CI/CD/build stage before store submission (ITID-21312)
Compromise of an auto-update/OTA server operating outside the app store (ITID-21313)
Malicious versions distributed only via sideloading/third-party stores, with the official listing unaffected (ITID-21314)
ITID-21311.severity: Critical. A compromised official listing can push malware to the entire active user base through a channel users implicitly trust.
ITID-21311.escalation: Escalate immediately to the app store's security/trusted-developer channel for emergency listing suspension and to SOC/IR for malware analysis.
indicators: Unexpected update published without an internal release record
App store developer console login/access anomaly
User reports of unusual app behavior post-update
Spike in malware/endpoint detections correlated with the update timing
vectors: Phishing of developer console credentials
Credential stuffing against the developer account
Compromised session/API key used to push the update
rootCauses: No MFA on the developer/publisher account
Overly broad standing access to the publisher account
No internal change-control gate before store submission
mitreTechniques: T1475 Deliver Malicious App via Authorized App Store
controls: MFA on the app store developer/publisher account
Internal release change-control/approval gate
Post-publish binary verification against internal release records
ITID-21311.detection: App store console access logs and internal release-record reconciliation provide direct technical signal.
ITID-21311.response: Suspend the malicious update via the app store, roll back to the last known-good version, rotate developer account credentials, and notify affected users.
metrics: Time-to-suspension of the malicious update
Number of users who installed the malicious version
sops: App Store Developer Account Security SOP
ITID-21311.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves by the specific compromise point: the app store developer/publisher account itself, rather than the build pipeline or an OTA server.

playbook.name: Response: Malicious Update via Compromised Official App Store Listing
playbook.description: For a malicious mobile app update published to the official app store listing after the developer account or listing was compromised.

steps.title: Confirm the malicious update and identify the compromised app-store account/access path
steps.desc: Verify the published update was not authorized and review app-store developer console access/audit logs to identify the compromise vector.
steps.outcome: Malicious update confirmed and compromise vector identified.

steps.title: Pull the malicious build from the app store immediately
steps.desc: Remove or halt distribution of the compromised version via the app store developer console.
steps.outcome: Malicious build no longer distributed to new users.

steps.title: Publish and force-push a clean, verified rollback build
steps.desc: Revert to the last known-good build and publish it as an emergency update, using forced-update mechanisms where available.
steps.outcome: Clean build distributed to replace the malicious one.

steps.title: Review and harden app-store publishing access controls
steps.desc: Reduce the number of accounts with publish rights and require hardware-key MFA for the developer account.

steps.title: Document root cause and update mobile release security requirements
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend controls such as mandatory code signing verification and release approval gates.

steps.title: Assess install/update reach of the malicious build
steps.desc: Determine how many devices have already downloaded or auto-updated to the malicious version.

steps.title: Revoke and rotate all app-store developer account credentials and API keys
steps.desc: Force-reset the developer account password, MFA, and any CI/CD API keys with publishing rights.

steps.title: Notify affected users of the malicious update
steps.desc: Push a user-facing notification (in-app, email, or push where safe) warning installed users about the malicious update and advising against interacting with it.
steps.guidance: A malicious mobile update reaches installed devices directly, so user notification is time-critical.

ITID-21312.def: Unauthorized injection of malicious code into the mobile app's build artifact via compromise of the CI/CD pipeline, build server, or code-signing process, such that the malicious code is baked into an otherwise normally-published update.
ITID-21312.purpose: Captures a malicious app update introduced earlier in the software delivery pipeline, through compromise of the CI/CD or build system, before the app ever reaches the app store.
scopeIncludes: Compromise of build/CI-CD infrastructure resulting in a tampered build artifact
Malicious code injected into the codebase or build process prior to compilation/signing
scopeExcludes: Compromise of the app store developer/publisher account itself, with the build artifact unaffected (ITID-21311)
The general CI/CD service-account exploitation technique in isolation with no resulting malicious mobile app update, tracked under ITID-12426
General CI/CD supply-chain attack ITIDs elsewhere in the taxonomy (ITID-61341) that are not scoped to this app's brand-facing consequence
ITID-21312.severity: Critical. Pipeline-level compromise can persist across multiple future releases if not fully remediated.
ITID-21312.escalation: Escalate immediately to engineering/security for full pipeline forensic review; treat all recent builds as suspect until the pipeline is verified clean.
indicators: Anomalous CI/CD job execution or configuration change
Build artifact hash mismatch against source-controlled code
Unexpected outbound network behavior in the compiled app
vectors: Compromised CI/CD service account or credentials
Malicious dependency/package introduced into the build
Compromised code-signing certificate/key
rootCauses: Insufficient access controls on CI/CD infrastructure
No build artifact integrity verification
Unvetted third-party build dependencies
mitreTechniques: T1474.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: CI/CD access hardening and MFA
Build artifact integrity/hash verification
Dependency vetting and software composition analysis
Code-signing key protection (HSM-backed)
ITID-21312.detection: Build artifact hash verification and CI/CD activity logging provide direct technical signal if in place; otherwise detection often relies on downstream malware behavior.
ITID-21312.response: Halt further releases from the pipeline, roll back to a verified-clean build, rotate CI/CD and signing credentials, and conduct a full pipeline forensic review.
metrics: Time-to-pipeline-lockdown
Number of releases affected before detection
ITID-21312.notes: Scope decision: the underlying CI/CD compromise technique is documented under ITID-12426 and the general supply-chain ITID-61341; this leaf is scoped specifically to the case where that compromise results in a malicious mobile app update reaching the company's own users, to avoid duplicating the general CI/CD attack documentation.

playbook.name: Response: Malicious Update via Compromised CI/CD or Build Pipeline
playbook.description: For a malicious mobile app update introduced through a compromised CI/CD pipeline or automated build system before being published.

steps.title: Confirm malicious code in the shipped build and trace it to the CI/CD pipeline
steps.desc: Compare the shipped build's artifacts/hashes against expected source and pipeline logs to confirm the injection point was the build system rather than the app-store listing itself.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed as originating in the build pipeline.
steps.abort: If the app-store listing itself was compromised directly, redirect to that playbook.

steps.title: Freeze the CI/CD pipeline and disable auto-publish
steps.desc: Immediately halt the build pipeline and disable any automatic publishing to the app store or OTA server until the compromise is contained.
steps.outcome: No further malicious builds can be produced or shipped.

steps.title: Audit and rebuild the CI/CD pipeline from a known-clean state
steps.desc: Rotate all pipeline credentials/secrets, review build scripts and dependencies for tampering, and rebuild the pipeline environment from trusted sources.
steps.outcome: Pipeline confirmed clean and access rotated.

steps.title: Harden CI/CD access controls and add build integrity verification
steps.desc: Implement least-privilege pipeline access, secrets rotation policy, and artifact signing/verification steps.

steps.title: Document root cause and update build pipeline security requirements
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend controls such as mandatory code review gates and dependency integrity checks.

steps.title: Assess install/update reach of the malicious build
steps.desc: Determine how many devices have already downloaded or auto-updated to the malicious version.

steps.title: Pull the malicious build from distribution
steps.desc: Remove the compromised version from the app store and any OTA/update servers.

steps.title: Publish a verified clean rollback build
steps.desc: Build and publish a clean version from the rebuilt pipeline, forcing update where possible.
steps.outcome: Clean build distributed to replace the malicious one.

steps.title: Notify affected users of the malicious update
steps.desc: Push a user-facing notification warning installed users about the malicious update.
steps.guidance: A malicious mobile update reaches installed devices directly, so user notification is time-critical.

ITID-21313.def: Unauthorized delivery of a malicious update via compromise of the company's own auto-update or OTA distribution infrastructure (used, for example, for enterprise-distributed or non-store-managed app updates), bypassing the official app store's review process entirely.
ITID-21313.purpose: Captures a malicious app update delivered through compromise of a proprietary auto-update or over-the-air (OTA) distribution server operating outside the official app store.
scopeIncludes: Compromise of a self-hosted or third-party OTA update server used to push updates directly to installed apps
Malicious update manifest or payload served from compromised update infrastructure
scopeExcludes: Compromise of the official app store listing itself (ITID-21311)
Compromise of the CI/CD build pipeline with the update still distributed via the app store (ITID-21312)
ITID-21313.severity: Critical. OTA-delivered updates often bypass app store review, removing a key safety check and enabling faster, less-scrutinized distribution of malicious code.
ITID-21313.escalation: Escalate immediately to take the OTA server offline and push an emergency clean update or kill-switch to affected installations.
indicators: Anomalous update manifest served from the OTA server
Unauthorized access detected on OTA server infrastructure
User reports of unusual app behavior following an update with no corresponding app store release
vectors: Compromise of OTA server credentials or infrastructure
Man-in-the-middle interception of unsecured update channels
Exploitation of a vulnerability in the OTA update server software
rootCauses: Unpatched or misconfigured OTA server infrastructure
Update channel not using signed/verified update packages
No update-manifest integrity verification on the client
mitreTechniques: T1474.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Signed and verified OTA update packages
OTA server hardening and access control
Client-side update-manifest integrity verification
ITID-21313.detection: OTA server access logging and update-manifest integrity verification provide direct technical signal.
ITID-21313.response: Take the OTA server offline, push a verified clean update or emergency kill-switch, and rotate OTA infrastructure credentials/signing keys.
metrics: Time-to-OTA-server-lockdown
Number of devices that received the malicious update
ITID-21313.notes: Distinguished from ITID-21311 by bypassing the app store entirely via the company's own OTA distribution channel.

playbook.name: Response: Malicious Update via Compromised Auto-Update/OTA Server
playbook.description: For a malicious mobile app update pushed via a compromised over-the-air (OTA) or auto-update server, bypassing the official app store review process.

steps.title: Confirm the malicious update was delivered via the OTA server, not the app store
steps.desc: Review OTA server logs and update manifests to confirm the malicious payload was pushed directly to installed devices, bypassing the app store.
steps.guidance: OTA/CodePush-style channels can update app behavior without a new store submission, making this a distinct and faster-moving vector.
steps.outcome: OTA server confirmed as the compromise vector.

steps.title: Disable the OTA/auto-update server immediately
steps.desc: Halt the OTA distribution service to stop further devices from receiving the malicious update.

steps.title: Push a verified clean rollback via the restored OTA channel
steps.desc: Once the OTA server is confirmed clean, push a corrective update reverting affected devices to a known-good state.
steps.outcome: Affected devices restored to a clean state.

steps.title: Harden OTA server access and add update integrity verification
steps.desc: Implement signed-update verification on the client side and restrict OTA server publish access.

steps.title: Document root cause and update OTA pipeline security requirements
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend controls such as mandatory update signing and anomaly detection on push volume.

steps.title: Assess how many devices received the malicious OTA push
steps.desc: Check OTA delivery telemetry to determine the install/update reach of the malicious payload.

steps.title: Revoke and rotate OTA server credentials/signing keys
steps.desc: Rotate all credentials, API keys, and code-signing keys used by the OTA update pipeline.

steps.title: Notify affected users of the malicious update
steps.desc: Push a user-facing notification warning installed users about the malicious update.
steps.guidance: A malicious OTA update reaches installed devices directly, so user notification is time-critical.

ITID-21314.def: Distribution of a malicious, repackaged, or fake version of the company's mobile app via sideloading (direct APK/IPA distribution) or unofficial third-party app stores, while the company's own official app store listing and build pipeline remain uncompromised.
ITID-21314.purpose: Captures a malicious version of the company's app being distributed via sideloading or unofficial third-party app stores, without any compromise of the company's own official channels.
scopeIncludes: A trojanized clone of the app hosted on an unofficial app marketplace
Sideloaded APK files impersonating the official app distributed via phishing or third-party sites
scopeExcludes: Compromise of the company's own official listing, pipeline, or OTA infrastructure (ITID-21311/ITID-21312/ITID-21313)
The trojanization/repackaging technique's malware content details, tracked under the Embedded Malware Type (ITID-21341-ITID-21345), which this leaf references rather than re-describes
ITID-21314.severity: High. The company's own infrastructure is not compromised, but affected users still associate the malicious app with the brand, and legitimate users may be tricked into installing it.
ITID-21314.priority: P1, escalating if the fake app is actively being promoted/advertised to appear legitimate.
ITID-21314.escalation: Escalate to legal/brand protection for takedown of the unofficial listing and to communications for a public warning to users.
indicators: Discovery of a lookalike app on an unofficial marketplace using the company's branding
User reports of installing a fake version from outside the official store
Malware/endpoint detections traced to the sideloaded app
vectors: Repackaging the legitimate app with injected malicious code and redistributing it
Hosting on unofficial app marketplaces with lax vetting
Phishing campaigns directing users to sideload the fake app
rootCauses: No proactive monitoring for unofficial distributions of the app
App lacks anti-tampering/repackaging protections
Users on platforms/configurations that permit sideloading by default
mitreTechniques: T1476 Deliver Malicious App via Other Means
controls: Brand/app-marketplace monitoring for unofficial distributions
App anti-tampering and repackaging-detection protections
User education on official download sources
ITID-21314.detection: Primarily external (brand monitoring, user reports); no internal telemetry since the company's own infrastructure is uninvolved.
ITID-21314.response: File a takedown request for the unofficial listing, issue a public warning directing users to the official source, and analyze the malicious app to assess data/harm exposure.
metrics: Time-to-takedown of the unofficial listing
Estimated number of users who installed the fake app
ITID-21314.notes: Scope decision: this leaf covers the distribution event and brand impact of a sideloaded/third-party-store fake app; the technical details of how the app was trojanized are documented once under the Embedded Malware Type to avoid duplicating that content.

playbook.name: Response: Sideloaded/Third-Party Store Malicious Update
playbook.description: For a malicious app update distributed through unofficial sideloading channels or unauthorized third-party app stores impersonating the legitimate app.

steps.title: Confirm the malicious build is not from an official company-controlled channel
steps.desc: Compare the sideloaded/third-party-store package's signing certificate and package ID against the legitimate app to confirm it is unauthorized.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the malicious build did not originate from company-controlled infrastructure.
steps.abort: If the official pipeline or store listing is actually compromised, redirect to that dedicated playbook.

steps.title: Report the malicious package for takedown
steps.desc: File abuse/takedown reports with the third-party store operator and the hosting provider.

steps.title: Analyze the malicious package for embedded malware/data theft functionality
steps.desc: Perform malware analysis on the sideloaded package to determine what it actually does, since it is a repackaged/trojanized variant.
steps.guidance: Use an isolated analysis environment.
steps.outcome: Malware behavior and any data-theft impact characterized.

steps.title: Advise affected users who may have sideloaded the fake app to uninstall and reset credentials
steps.desc: Provide clear remediation guidance for anyone who installed the fake app, including uninstall steps and password/credential resets.

steps.title: Document root cause and evaluate app-integrity/anti-tampering monitoring
steps.desc: Log findings and consider ongoing brand/app monitoring for unauthorized third-party distributions.

steps.title: Identify the distribution source(s) hosting the fake build
steps.desc: Locate the third-party store, forum, or sideload-hosting site distributing the malicious package.

steps.title: Publish a public warning about the unofficial/malicious version
steps.desc: Communicate via official channels (website, app store description, social media) that the app should only be installed from official stores and naming the fake source if helpful.
steps.outcome: Users warned away from the malicious source.

ITID-21315.def: An unauthorized or malicious update to the company's mobile app, not clearly matching the app-store, CI/CD, OTA, or sideloading leaves under this Type.
ITID-21315.purpose: Catch-all for unauthorized mobile app updates that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a more specific unauthorized-update leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-21311 through ITID-21314
ITID-21315.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Critical pending investigation given the app-update vector.
ITID-21315.escalation: Reclassify once the specific compromise point in the delivery chain is clarified.
indicators: Unauthorized app update of unclear specific delivery mechanism
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Code-signing enforcement for mobile app releases
App store publishing account MFA enforcement
Release pipeline change-approval workflow
ITID-21315.detection: Same release-integrity telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-21315.response: Roll back to a known-good version and investigate to reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-21315.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Unauthorized App Update
playbook.description: General-purpose response for an unauthorized mobile app update that does not fit a more specific unauthorized-update subtype.

steps.title: Confirm the update is unauthorized and identify the distribution channel
steps.desc: Determine whether the malicious update came via the app store, CI/CD pipeline, OTA server, or an unofficial sideload source.
steps.abort: If a more specific category is confirmed, redirect to that dedicated playbook.

steps.title: Halt further distribution of the malicious update
steps.desc: Pull the build from its distribution channel and disable any automated publishing.
steps.outcome: No further devices receive the malicious update.

steps.title: Publish a verified clean rollback build
steps.desc: Revert to a known-good build and distribute it to replace the malicious version.

steps.title: Review and harden publishing/access controls for the affected channel
steps.desc: Reduce access and add verification controls appropriate to the compromised distribution path.

steps.title: Document root cause and remediation
steps.desc: Log findings for future prevention.

steps.title: Assess install/update reach of the malicious build
steps.desc: Determine how many devices have received the unauthorized update.

steps.title: Notify affected users
steps.desc: Push a user-facing notification warning installed users about the malicious update.

ITID-21321.def: An unauthorized push notification sent via the company's mobile app notification infrastructure, falsely claiming a security threat, account compromise, or required security action, exploiting the app's trusted push channel to alarm or manipulate users.
ITID-21321.purpose: Captures a fake security-alert push notification sent through the company's own mobile app notification channel.
scopeIncludes: Push notification falsely claiming the user's account or device is compromised
Push notification urging an urgent security action (e.g., 'verify your account now') that is not a genuine company communication
scopeExcludes: Fake promotional/discount notifications (ITID-21322)
Fake system/account update notifications not framed as a security threat (ITID-21323)

Push notification approval-fatigue/MFA-bombing attacks against a user's own authentication app, tracked under ITID-12613/ITID-12622 — this leaf is scoped to abuse of the company's own branded notification channel, not a third-party MFA prompt
ITID-21321.severity: High. A fake security alert can itself be used to drive users toward a phishing link or panic-driven action, compounding harm.
ITID-21321.escalation: Escalate immediately to identify and revoke the compromised notification-sending capability; issue a corrective in-app/push message.
indicators: User reports of an unexpected security-alert push notification
Notification-sending platform showing an unauthorized campaign/send
Spike in support inquiries about a security alert the company did not send
vectors: Compromise of the push notification service/API credentials
Compromise of the backend admin console used to trigger notifications
rootCauses: No MFA on the push notification service/admin console
Overly broad access to the notification-sending platform
controls: MFA and least-privilege access on the push notification platform
Notification content approval workflow
Rapid notification-service credential rotation runbook
ITID-21321.detection: Notification platform send-logs provide direct technical signal once investigated; initial detection is often via user/support reports.
ITID-21321.response: Revoke the compromised notification-sending access, issue a corrective notification/in-app message, and audit recent send history for other unauthorized campaigns.
metrics: Number of users who received the fake notification
Time-to-access-revocation
ITID-21321.notes: Scope decision: this leaf covers abuse of the company's own app push channel to send a fake security alert; MFA/authenticator push-bombing attacks against a user's own auth app are a distinct technique tracked under ITID-12613/ITID-12622.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Security Alert Push Notification
playbook.description: For a fake security-alert push notification sent to app users via a compromised push-notification system, intended to alarm or manipulate users.

steps.title: Confirm the push notification was unauthorized and identify the sending mechanism
steps.desc: Review the push-notification service/dashboard's send logs to confirm the alert did not originate from an authorized campaign and identify how it was triggered.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized send confirmed and mechanism identified.

steps.title: Revoke access to the push-notification service and rotate API keys
steps.desc: Lock out the compromised access path (account, API key, or integration) used to send the fake alert.

steps.title: Confirm no follow-on malicious action was taken via the fake alert (e.g. embedded link)
steps.desc: Check whether the fake alert contained a phishing link or instructed users to take an action, and assess any resulting exposure.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of any secondary exposure from the alert's content.

steps.title: Re-secure the push-notification service and review sending permissions
steps.desc: Rotate credentials, enable MFA, and restrict which systems/accounts can trigger push campaigns.

steps.title: Document root cause and add push-content approval workflow
steps.desc: Log findings and consider a review/approval step for outbound push campaigns.

steps.title: Assess how many users received the fake alert
steps.desc: Check delivery telemetry to estimate the number of affected devices/users.

steps.title: Send a corrective notification/in-app banner clarifying the alert was fake
steps.desc: Push a legitimate follow-up notification or in-app message explaining the prior alert was unauthorized and should be disregarded.
steps.guidance: Users may be alarmed by a fake security alert; a fast, clear correction reduces support load and panic.
steps.outcome: Users informed the prior alert was fake.

ITID-21322.def: An unauthorized push notification sent via the company's mobile app notification infrastructure, falsely advertising a discount, sale, or promotional offer, typically to drive users to a fraudulent link or app.
ITID-21322.purpose: Captures a fake promotional or discount push notification sent through the company's own mobile app notification channel.
scopeIncludes: Push notification advertising an unauthorized discount/promo code linking to a fraudulent site
Fake 'flash sale' notification designed to drive impulsive clicks
scopeExcludes: Fake security-alert notifications (ITID-21321)
Fake system/account update notifications (ITID-21323)
ITID-21322.severity: Medium-High. Financial/data harm depends on where the linked content leads, but brand trust in the notification channel itself is also damaged.
ITID-21322.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the notification links to malware or a phishing page.
ITID-21322.escalation: Escalate to identify and revoke the compromised notification-sending capability; assess the linked content's payload.
indicators: User reports of an unexpected promotional push notification
Notification platform showing an unauthorized campaign/send
Customer complaints after acting on a fake promo
vectors: Compromise of the push notification service/API credentials
Compromise of the backend admin console used to trigger notifications
rootCauses: No MFA on the push notification service/admin console
Overly broad access to the notification-sending platform
controls: MFA and least-privilege access on the push notification platform
Notification content approval workflow
ITID-21322.detection: Notification platform send-logs provide direct technical signal once investigated; initial detection is often via user/support reports.
ITID-21322.response: Revoke the compromised notification-sending access, issue a corrective notification clarifying the promotion is fake, and assess the linked content for further harm.
metrics: Number of users who received the fake notification
Time-to-access-revocation
ITID-21322.notes: Differentiated from other fake-notification leaves by the promotional/discount framing specifically.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Promotional/Discount Push Notification
playbook.description: For a fake promotional or discount push notification sent to app users via a compromised push-notification system, often used to drive traffic to a scam or fraudulent offer.

steps.title: Confirm the push notification was unauthorized and capture its content
steps.desc: Confirm the promotion did not originate from Marketing and record the exact notification text and any linked offer/URL.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized send confirmed and content documented.

steps.title: Revoke access to the push-notification service and rotate API keys
steps.desc: Lock out the compromised access path used to send the fake promotion.

steps.title: Identify and remediate any users who completed a purchase through the fake offer
steps.desc: Cross-check order/payment systems for transactions tied to the fake promotion and refer them to fraud/customer support.

steps.title: Re-secure the push-notification service and review sending permissions
steps.desc: Rotate credentials, enable MFA, and restrict which systems/accounts can trigger push campaigns.

steps.title: Document root cause and add push-content approval workflow
steps.desc: Log findings and consider a review/approval step for outbound push campaigns.

steps.title: Assess reach and whether users acted on the fake offer (e.g. clicked through, attempted purchase)
steps.desc: Review delivery and click-through telemetry to estimate exposure and engagement with any linked offer.

steps.title: Take down or report any linked fraudulent offer page
steps.desc: If the notification linked to a fake storefront or offer page, report it for takedown/blocking.

steps.title: Send a corrective notification clarifying the promotion is not valid
steps.desc: Push a legitimate follow-up message informing users the promotion was fake and any orders placed against it will not be honored/should be disputed.
steps.outcome: Users informed the promotion was fraudulent.

ITID-21323.def: An unauthorized push notification sent via the company's mobile app notification infrastructure, falsely claiming a system, policy, or account update requiring user action, distinct from a security-alert or promotional framing.
ITID-21323.purpose: Captures a fake system or account update push notification sent through the company's own mobile app notification channel.
scopeIncludes: Push notification claiming a fake terms-of-service, policy, or account-settings update requiring the user to click through
Notification falsely announcing a system change or maintenance requiring action
scopeExcludes: Fake security-alert notifications (ITID-21321)
Fake promotional/discount notifications (ITID-21322)
Fake emergency/urgent-action notifications, tracked separately given the higher-pressure framing (ITID-21324)
ITID-21323.severity: Medium-High. Depends on whether the notification drives users to a phishing/malware link.
ITID-21323.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the notification links to malware or a phishing page.
ITID-21323.escalation: Escalate to identify and revoke the compromised notification-sending capability; assess the linked content's payload.
indicators: User reports of an unexpected system/account update push notification
Notification platform showing an unauthorized campaign/send
vectors: Compromise of the push notification service/API credentials
Compromise of the backend admin console used to trigger notifications
rootCauses: No MFA on the push notification service/admin console
Overly broad access to the notification-sending platform
controls: MFA and least-privilege access on the push notification platform
Notification content approval workflow
ITID-21323.detection: Notification platform send-logs provide direct technical signal once investigated; initial detection is often via user/support reports.
ITID-21323.response: Revoke the compromised notification-sending access, issue a corrective notification, and assess the linked content for further harm.
metrics: Number of users who received the fake notification
Time-to-access-revocation
ITID-21323.notes: Differentiated from ITID-21324 by tone/urgency: a routine-sounding update claim rather than an emergency/urgent-action framing.

playbook.name: Response: Fake System/Account Update Push Notification
playbook.description: For a fake push notification impersonating a system or account update prompt, often used to lure users into a phishing flow or malicious action within the app.

steps.title: Confirm the push notification was unauthorized and capture its content and any action it prompts
steps.desc: Confirm the notification did not originate from the legitimate release/account-management process, and document exactly what action it asks users to take.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized send confirmed and prompted action documented.

steps.title: Revoke access to the push-notification service and rotate API keys
steps.desc: Lock out the compromised access path used to send the fake update prompt.

steps.title: Remediate users who followed the fake update instructions
steps.desc: For users who completed the fake update/account action (e.g. entered credentials, changed settings), guide them through credential reset and account review.

steps.title: Re-secure the push-notification service and review sending permissions
steps.desc: Rotate credentials, enable MFA, and restrict which systems/accounts can trigger push campaigns.

steps.title: Document root cause and add push-content approval workflow
steps.desc: Log findings and consider a review/approval step for outbound push campaigns, especially ones prompting user action.

steps.title: Assess how many users received and acted on the fake update prompt
steps.desc: Review delivery and interaction telemetry to estimate how many users followed the fake update instructions.

steps.title: Send a corrective notification clarifying the update prompt was fake
steps.desc: Push a legitimate follow-up message telling users to disregard the prior notification and not take the requested action if they have not already.
steps.outcome: Users informed and instructed not to act on the fake prompt.

ITID-21324.def: An unauthorized push notification sent via the company's mobile app notification infrastructure, using urgent or emergency framing (e.g., account suspension, imminent deadline, safety alert) to pressure users into immediate, unconsidered action.
ITID-21324.purpose: Captures a fake emergency or urgent-action-required push notification sent through the company's own mobile app notification channel, designed to pressure immediate user action.
scopeIncludes: Push notification claiming imminent account suspension/closure unless the user acts immediately
Notification using emergency/urgent language to drive rapid click-through with no time to verify legitimacy
scopeExcludes: Fake security-alert notifications framed around a compromise claim specifically (ITID-21321)
Fake system/account update notifications without urgent-action pressure (ITID-21323)
ITID-21324.severity: High. Urgency framing is deliberately designed to bypass user skepticism, increasing click-through and harm rates.
ITID-21324.escalation: Escalate immediately to identify and revoke the compromised notification-sending capability; issue a corrective notification promptly given the pressure tactic's effectiveness.
indicators: User reports of an unexpected urgent/emergency push notification
Notification platform showing an unauthorized campaign/send
Spike in support inquiries or panicked user action following the notification
vectors: Compromise of the push notification service/API credentials
Compromise of the backend admin console used to trigger notifications
rootCauses: No MFA on the push notification service/admin console
Overly broad access to the notification-sending platform
controls: MFA and least-privilege access on the push notification platform
Notification content approval workflow
Rapid corrective-notification runbook
ITID-21324.detection: Notification platform send-logs provide direct technical signal once investigated; initial detection is often via user/support reports.
ITID-21324.response: Revoke the compromised notification-sending access, issue a corrective notification immediately given the urgency framing's effectiveness, and assess the linked content for further harm.
metrics: Number of users who received the fake notification
Time-to-corrective-notification
ITID-21324.notes: Differentiated from siblings by the urgency/pressure framing itself, which materially raises expected click-through and harm rates.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Emergency/Urgent Action Required Push Notification
playbook.description: For a fake push notification using urgency/emergency framing to pressure users into an immediate, unsafe action.

steps.title: Confirm the push notification was unauthorized and capture its urgent call-to-action
steps.desc: Confirm the notification did not originate from an authorized emergency-communication process and document the exact urgency framing and requested action.
steps.guidance: Urgent/fear-based framing is designed to bypass normal user caution, raising response priority.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized send confirmed and content documented.

steps.title: Revoke access to the push-notification service and rotate API keys immediately
steps.desc: Lock out the compromised access path used to send the fake urgent alert without delay given the pressure it places on users.

steps.title: Remediate users who followed the fake urgent instructions
steps.desc: For users who completed the requested action, guide them through credential reset, account review, or transaction reversal as applicable.

steps.title: Re-secure the push-notification service and review sending permissions
steps.desc: Rotate credentials, enable MFA, and restrict which systems/accounts can trigger push campaigns.

steps.title: Document root cause and response time to the urgent fake alert
steps.desc: Log findings, focusing on time-to-correction, and consider a review/approval step for outbound push campaigns.

steps.title: Assess how many users received and acted on the fake urgent prompt
steps.desc: Review delivery and interaction telemetry to estimate how many users took the requested urgent action.

steps.title: Send an immediate corrective notification and, if severe, an in-app banner
steps.desc: Push a fast, clear follow-up telling users to disregard the prior alert and not take the requested action.
steps.guidance: Speed matters most here since the fake alert is designed to prompt immediate action.
steps.outcome: Users informed as quickly as possible.

ITID-21325.def: An unauthorized push notification sent via the company's mobile app notification infrastructure, not clearly matching the security-alert, promotional, system-update, or urgent-action leaves under this Type.
ITID-21325.purpose: Catch-all for fake push notifications sent via the company's mobile app that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a more specific fake-notification leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-21321 through ITID-21324
ITID-21325.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High pending investigation.
ITID-21325.escalation: Reclassify once the specific notification theme is clarified.
indicators: Fake push notification of unclear specific theme
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Push notification service account MFA enforcement
Notification content approval workflow
Mobile backend API access-key rotation
ITID-21325.detection: Same notification platform telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-21325.response: Revoke the compromised notification-sending access and investigate to reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-21325.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Fake Push Notification
playbook.description: General-purpose response for a fake push notification that does not fit a more specific fake-notification subtype.

steps.title: Confirm the push notification was unauthorized and capture its content
steps.desc: Confirm the notification did not originate from an authorized campaign and document its exact content and any requested action.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized send confirmed and content documented.
steps.abort: If a more specific category is confirmed, redirect to that dedicated playbook.

steps.title: Revoke access to the push-notification service and rotate API keys
steps.desc: Lock out the compromised access path used to send the fake notification.

steps.title: Remediate any users who acted on the fake notification
steps.desc: Guide affected users through appropriate remediation based on what the notification requested.

steps.title: Re-secure the push-notification service and review sending permissions
steps.desc: Rotate credentials, enable MFA, and restrict which systems/accounts can trigger push campaigns.

steps.title: Document root cause and remediation
steps.desc: Log findings for future prevention.

steps.title: Assess reach and user interaction with the fake notification
steps.desc: Review delivery and interaction telemetry to estimate exposure.

steps.title: Send a corrective notification
steps.desc: Push a legitimate follow-up message clarifying the prior notification was unauthorized.

ITID-21331.def: Unauthorized modification of the mobile app's remote configuration or feature-flag settings, causing the live app to behave, display, or expose features in an unintended and potentially damaging way without any code update.
ITID-21331.purpose: Captures unauthorized tampering with the mobile app's remote configuration or feature-flag system, altering in-app behavior for users without a code release.
scopeIncludes: Unauthorized toggling of a feature flag that exposes hidden/unfinished functionality or disables a security control
Tampering with remote config values that alter displayed content, pricing logic, or app behavior at runtime
scopeExcludes: Tampering with the CMS/content feed specifically (ITID-21332)
Tampering with product catalog/pricing data specifically (ITID-21333)
ITID-21331.severity: High. Remote config/feature-flag changes take effect immediately across the live user base with no app-store review step.
ITID-21331.escalation: Escalate immediately to engineering to revert the configuration and lock down access to the remote config platform.
indicators: Unexpected app behavior change with no corresponding release
Remote config platform showing an unauthorized change
User reports of unexpected features or broken functionality appearing suddenly
vectors: Compromise of remote config/feature-flag platform credentials
Overly broad access to the configuration management console
rootCauses: No MFA on the remote config platform
No change-approval workflow for configuration changes
Overly broad standing access to the config platform
controls: MFA and least-privilege access on the remote config/feature-flag platform
Configuration change-approval workflow
Configuration change audit logging and alerting
ITID-21331.detection: Configuration platform audit logs provide direct technical signal when change-alerting is in place.
ITID-21331.response: Revert the configuration to the last known-good state, revoke the unauthorized access, and audit for other unauthorized changes.
metrics: Time-to-revert unauthorized configuration change
Number of users exposed to the altered behavior
ITID-21331.notes: Scoped to configuration/feature-flag tampering specifically, distinct from content-feed or catalog data tampering which are tracked as separate sibling leaves.

playbook.name: Response: In-App Remote Config/Feature Flag Tampering
playbook.description: For unauthorized tampering with a mobile app's remote configuration or feature-flag system, altering in-app behavior for installed users without a new build.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized changes in the remote config/feature-flag dashboard
steps.desc: Review the remote config/feature-flag platform's change history to identify unauthorized modifications and who/what made them.

steps.title: Revert the remote config/feature flags to their last known-good values
steps.desc: Roll back the configuration immediately to stop the malicious behavior from continuing to affect users.
steps.outcome: App behavior restored to intended state for all connected clients.

steps.title: Audit all other config/flag values for additional tampering
steps.desc: Review the full configuration set, not just the discovered change, for other unauthorized modifications.
steps.outcome: Full extent of tampering identified and corrected.

steps.title: Add change-approval and audit logging to the remote config platform
steps.desc: Implement a review/approval workflow and enhanced audit logging for future configuration changes.
steps.outcome: Reduced risk of undetected future tampering.

steps.title: Document root cause and update remote config access policy
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend access-control improvements for the remote config/feature-flag system.

steps.title: Assess what app behavior was altered and its user-facing impact
steps.desc: Determine exactly what functionality, content, or flags were changed and how that manifests to end users.

steps.title: Revoke and rotate access credentials to the remote config platform
steps.desc: Lock out the compromised account/API key used to make the unauthorized change.

ITID-21332.def: Unauthorized modification of the backend CMS or content feed that supplies text, images, or articles displayed within the mobile app, causing unintended or brand-damaging content to appear in-app without a code release.
ITID-21332.purpose: Captures unauthorized tampering with the content management system (CMS) or content feed that populates the mobile app's in-app content.
scopeIncludes: Unauthorized edits to in-app articles, banners, or editorial content served from a CMS
Injection of offensive or fraudulent content into an in-app news/content feed
scopeExcludes: Remote config/feature-flag tampering (ITID-21331)
Product catalog/pricing tampering (ITID-21333)
User-generated content injected by an end user through normal app functionality (ITID-21334)
ITID-21332.severity: High. In-app content is trusted by users as company-authored, amplifying reputational impact of tampered content.
ITID-21332.escalation: Escalate immediately to content/editorial and engineering teams to revert the content and lock down CMS access.
indicators: Unexpected in-app content change with no corresponding editorial approval
CMS audit log showing an unauthorized edit
User reports of offensive or incorrect in-app content
vectors: Compromise of CMS administrator credentials
Exploitation of a CMS vulnerability
Overly broad editorial access permissions
rootCauses: No MFA on the CMS
No editorial approval workflow for published content
Outdated CMS software
controls: MFA and least-privilege access on the CMS
Editorial content approval workflow
CMS patch management
ITID-21332.detection: CMS audit logs provide direct technical signal when change-alerting is in place; user reports also common.
ITID-21332.response: Revert the content to the last approved state, revoke unauthorized CMS access, and audit for other unauthorized edits.
metrics: Time-to-revert unauthorized content
Number of users exposed to the tampered content
sops: CMS Access and Editorial Workflow Security SOP
ITID-21332.notes: Scoped to company-authored/editorial content served via the CMS, distinguishing it from end-user-generated content (ITID-21334) and from structured commerce data (ITID-21333).

playbook.name: Response: In-App CMS/Content Feed Tampering
playbook.description: For unauthorized tampering with the content management system or content feed powering in-app screens, injecting defacing or malicious content into the app experience.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized changes in the in-app CMS/content feed
steps.desc: Review the CMS's change history/audit log to identify unauthorized content modifications and who/what made them.

steps.title: Remove or revert the tampered content immediately
steps.desc: Roll back the CMS/content feed to its last known-good state to stop the malicious content from displaying in-app.
steps.outcome: Malicious content no longer visible to users.

steps.title: Audit remaining CMS content for additional tampering
steps.desc: Review other content entries/feeds for further unauthorized modifications beyond the initial discovery.
steps.outcome: Full extent of tampering identified and corrected.

steps.title: Add content-change approval workflow and audit logging
steps.desc: Implement a review/approval step and enhanced logging for future CMS content changes.
steps.outcome: Reduced risk of undetected future tampering.

steps.title: Document root cause and update CMS access policy
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend access-control improvements for the CMS/content feed.

steps.title: Assess the injected content for malicious links, offensive material, or fraud
steps.desc: Review the tampered content for embedded links, phishing prompts, or other harmful material and classify the risk.
steps.outcome: Nature and risk of injected content understood.

steps.title: Revoke and rotate CMS access credentials
steps.desc: Lock out the compromised account/API key used to tamper with the content.

ITID-21333.def: Unauthorized modification of product catalog listings or pricing data displayed within the mobile app, causing incorrect, fraudulent, or brand-damaging product/price information to be shown to users.
ITID-21333.purpose: Captures unauthorized tampering with the mobile app's product catalog or pricing data, causing incorrect or fraudulent product/price information to display to users.
scopeIncludes: Unauthorized price changes displayed in-app (e.g., drastically reduced or inflated prices)
Injected fake or altered product listings
scopeExcludes: General editorial/content-feed tampering with no product/pricing component (ITID-21332)
Remote config/feature-flag tampering (ITID-21331)
ITID-21333.severity: High. Pricing errors can create direct financial exposure (honoring fraudulent prices) alongside reputational harm.
ITID-21333.escalation: Escalate immediately to e-commerce/product and legal teams given potential contractual/financial exposure from displayed pricing errors.
indicators: Unexpected pricing/catalog change with no corresponding business approval
Catalog system audit log showing an unauthorized edit
Customer reports or order surges tied to an incorrect price
vectors: Compromise of catalog/pricing management system credentials
Exploitation of a vulnerability in the catalog management API
rootCauses: No MFA on the catalog/pricing management system
No approval workflow for pricing changes
Overly broad access to catalog management tools
controls: MFA and least-privilege access on the catalog/pricing system
Pricing change approval workflow
Anomalous pricing-change alerting
ITID-21333.detection: Catalog/pricing system audit logs provide direct technical signal when change-alerting is in place.
ITID-21333.response: Revert pricing/catalog data to the last approved state, assess and address any orders placed at the fraudulent price, and revoke unauthorized access.
metrics: Time-to-revert unauthorized pricing change
Financial exposure from orders at the fraudulent price
sops: Catalog and Pricing System Security SOP
ITID-21333.notes: Scoped to structured commerce data (product/pricing) specifically, given its distinct financial-exposure dimension versus general editorial content tampering.

playbook.name: Response: In-App Product Catalog/Pricing Tampering
playbook.description: For unauthorized tampering with in-app product catalog data or pricing, potentially causing customer confusion, financial loss, or fraudulent orders.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized changes to catalog/pricing data
steps.desc: Review the catalog/pricing system's change history to identify unauthorized modifications and who/what made them.

steps.title: Revert catalog/pricing data to last known-good state immediately
steps.desc: Roll back the tampered data to stop further incorrect pricing/product display and prevent additional fraudulent orders.
steps.outcome: Correct catalog/pricing restored for all users.

steps.title: Revoke and rotate access credentials to the catalog/pricing system
steps.desc: Lock out the compromised account/API key used to tamper with the data.

steps.title: Add change-approval and audit logging to catalog/pricing changes
steps.desc: Implement a review/approval workflow for pricing and catalog changes going forward.
steps.outcome: Reduced risk of undetected future tampering.

steps.title: Document root cause and financial impact
steps.desc: Log findings, including financial impact and remediation, for future prevention.

steps.title: Assess financial and order impact of the tampered pricing/catalog data
steps.desc: Determine whether any orders were placed at the incorrect/fraudulent prices and estimate financial exposure.
steps.guidance: Loop in Finance if orders were placed at incorrect prices.

steps.title: Pause checkout/order processing if fraudulent orders are actively being placed
steps.desc: If tampered pricing is actively enabling fraudulent orders, temporarily pause checkout until the data is confirmed clean.
steps.abort: Resume checkout once catalog integrity is confirmed.

steps.title: Audit and cancel/adjust any orders placed at fraudulent prices
steps.desc: Work with Finance/Customer Support to identify and resolve orders placed during the tampering window.

ITID-21334.def: Injection of malicious, offensive, or fraudulent content into the mobile app via legitimate user-generated-content features (e.g., reviews, comments, profile fields, uploaded media), exploiting insufficient content moderation or input validation rather than any backend system compromise.
ITID-21334.purpose: Captures the injection of malicious or offensive user-generated content into the mobile app through abuse of legitimate user-content submission features.
scopeIncludes: Offensive or fraudulent content submitted through a review/comment/profile feature and displayed to other users without adequate moderation
Scripted/bulk submission of malicious content via the user-content API
scopeExcludes: Tampering with company-authored CMS content (ITID-21332)
Backend system compromise resulting in content changes (ITID-21331/ITID-21332/ITID-21333)
ITID-21334.severity: Medium-High, depending on content severity and how widely other users are exposed before moderation.
ITID-21334.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the content is offensive/fraudulent at scale.
ITID-21334.escalation: Escalate to trust-and-safety/moderation team to remove the content and to engineering to assess input-validation/rate-limiting gaps.
indicators: User reports of offensive/fraudulent content in reviews, comments, or profiles
Automated moderation flag triggered by submitted content
Abnormal volume of user-content submissions from a small set of accounts
vectors: Abuse of a legitimate user-content submission feature with insufficient moderation
Scripted/bulk account creation to submit malicious content at scale
Insufficient input validation allowing embedded scripts/links
rootCauses: Inadequate automated content moderation/filtering
No rate limiting on user-content submission
Insufficient input validation/sanitization
controls: Automated content moderation/filtering
Rate limiting on user-content submission APIs
Input validation and sanitization on user-submitted fields
ITID-21334.detection: Automated moderation tooling and user reports provide the primary signal.
ITID-21334.response: Remove the offending content, strengthen moderation/rate-limiting controls, and review for other similarly-injected content.
metrics: Volume of injected content removed
Time-to-moderation-action
ITID-21334.notes: Scoped to abuse of legitimate user-content features via moderation/validation gaps, not a backend system compromise, distinguishing it from the other Content Tampering leaves.

playbook.name: Response: In-App User-Generated Content Injection
