playbook.description: For unauthorized injection of malicious or offensive content into in-app user-generated-content surfaces (reviews, comments, community feeds) via a compromised moderation/backend access path.

steps.title: Confirm the injected content bypassed normal UGC submission/moderation
steps.desc: Review moderation and backend logs to confirm the content was injected directly rather than submitted through the normal user flow, and identify the access path used.

steps.title: Remove the injected content immediately
steps.desc: Delete or hide the malicious/offensive content from all affected UGC surfaces.
steps.outcome: Content no longer visible to users.

steps.title: Audit other UGC surfaces for additional injected content
steps.desc: Review other feeds/sections for further unauthorized content injections beyond the initial discovery.
steps.outcome: Full extent of injection identified and corrected.

steps.title: Harden backend/moderation access controls
steps.desc: Reduce privileged access to the UGC backend and add audit logging for direct content writes.

steps.title: Document root cause and update UGC backend access policy
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend access-control improvements.

steps.title: Assess the nature and reach of the injected content
steps.desc: Determine whether the content is offensive, contains malicious links, or otherwise poses a risk, and how many users may have seen it.

steps.title: Revoke and rotate access credentials to the moderation/backend system
steps.desc: Lock out the compromised account/API key used to inject the content.

ITID-21335.def: Unauthorized tampering with the mobile app's displayed content, not clearly matching the remote-config, CMS, catalog/pricing, or user-generated-content leaves under this Type.
ITID-21335.purpose: Catch-all for in-app content tampering that does not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a more specific content-tampering leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-21331 through ITID-21334
ITID-21335.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High pending investigation.
ITID-21335.escalation: Reclassify once the specific tampering mechanism and content type are clarified.
indicators: In-app content change of unclear specific mechanism or source
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Code-signing enforcement for mobile app releases
Backend content-management access controls with least privilege
Content integrity checks at app runtime
ITID-21335.detection: Same platform/CMS telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-21335.response: Revert the content and investigate to reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-21335.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General In-App Content Tampering
playbook.description: General-purpose response for in-app content tampering that does not fit a more specific content-tampering subtype.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized changes and identify the affected system
steps.desc: Determine whether the tampering occurred via remote config, CMS, catalog/pricing, or UGC systems, and identify who/what made the change.
steps.abort: If a more specific category is confirmed, redirect to that dedicated playbook.

steps.title: Revert the tampered content/configuration to its last known-good state
steps.desc: Roll back the affected system to stop the malicious content/behavior from continuing to affect users.

steps.title: Audit for additional tampering across related systems
steps.desc: Review other content/configuration for further unauthorized modifications.
steps.outcome: Full extent of tampering identified and corrected.

steps.title: Add change-approval and audit logging
steps.desc: Implement a review/approval workflow for future changes to the affected system.

steps.title: Document root cause and remediation
steps.desc: Log findings for future prevention.

steps.title: Assess user-facing impact of the tampering
steps.desc: Determine what content/behavior was altered and how it affects users.

steps.title: Revoke and rotate access credentials used for the tampering
steps.desc: Lock out the compromised account/API key.

ITID-21341.def: The presence of malicious functionality within the company's official mobile app that originates from a third-party SDK or library dependency, either because the SDK vendor was compromised or because the SDK itself was malicious from the outset, resulting in the malware shipping inside an otherwise legitimate company app.
ITID-21341.purpose: Captures malware embedded in the company's official mobile app via a compromised or malicious third-party SDK or library integrated into the app.
scopeIncludes: A legitimate-seeming ad, analytics, or utility SDK later found to exfiltrate data or execute unauthorized code
Compromise of an SDK vendor's distribution channel resulting in a malicious SDK version being pulled into the app's build
scopeExcludes: Malicious code injected directly into the company's own codebase via a compromised build/signing process, with no third-party SDK involved (ITID-21343)
A fully trojanized/repackaged unofficial copy of the app (ITID-21342)
General credential-harvesting-malware-via-trojanized-software cases unrelated to the company's own mobile app (ITID-12139)
ITID-21341.severity: Critical. The malware ships inside the official, trusted app and can affect the entire active install base.
ITID-21341.escalation: Escalate immediately to engineering/security to identify all affected app versions, remove or replace the SDK, and issue an emergency update.
indicators: Anomalous outbound network traffic from the app traced to the SDK's endpoints
Security research or vendor disclosure identifying the SDK as malicious/compromised
Unexpected permissions usage inconsistent with the SDK's stated function
vectors: Supply-chain compromise of the SDK vendor's build/distribution infrastructure
Adoption of a malicious SDK without adequate vetting
A previously benign SDK sold to a new owner who adds malicious functionality
rootCauses: Insufficient vetting/security review of third-party SDKs before integration
No software composition analysis (SBOM) on the app's dependencies
No monitoring of SDK behavior post-integration
mitreTechniques: T1474.001 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
controls: Third-party SDK security vetting process
Software composition analysis / SBOM for mobile app dependencies
Runtime SDK network-behavior monitoring
ITID-21341.detection: Outbound traffic analysis and software composition analysis provide the primary technical signal; often first surfaced by external security research.
ITID-21341.response: Remove or replace the malicious SDK, issue an emergency app update, and notify users if data exfiltration is confirmed.
metrics: Time-to-remediation (SDK removal/update)
Number of app versions/users affected
ITID-21341.notes: Scope decision: limited to the company's own official app being affected by a compromised/malicious SDK; the general credential-harvesting-via-trojanized-software ITID-12139 and general software supply-chain leaves elsewhere in the taxonomy cover the broader technique independent of this specific app.

playbook.name: Response: Malicious Third-Party SDK/Library Embedded Malware
playbook.description: For malware embedded in the app via a compromised or malicious third-party SDK/library dependency, distributed to users through an otherwise-legitimate app update.

steps.title: Identify which SDK/library is the source of the malicious behavior
steps.desc: Perform malware/dependency analysis to pinpoint the specific third-party SDK or library version introducing the malicious code.
steps.guidance: Use an isolated analysis environment.
steps.outcome: Malicious SDK/library and affected version(s) identified.

steps.title: Pull affected app versions from distribution and coordinate app-store emergency takedown if needed
steps.desc: Remove the affected build(s) from the app store and, for severe cases, request an emergency takedown/expedited review from the app store's security team.

steps.title: Remove the malicious SDK/library and publish a clean rebuilt version
steps.desc: Strip out or replace the compromised dependency, rebuild, and publish a clean version, forcing update where possible.

steps.title: Review and vet all remaining third-party SDKs/dependencies
steps.desc: Audit the app's full dependency tree for other risky or unvetted third-party components.

steps.title: Document root cause and establish SDK vetting/approval process
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend a formal review process for introducing new third-party SDKs.

steps.title: Characterize the malware's behavior and data-theft/impact scope
steps.desc: Determine what the malicious code does (data exfiltration, ad fraud, remote code execution, etc.) and which app versions/users are affected.
steps.outcome: Malware behavior and exposure scope understood.

steps.title: Notify affected users of the embedded malware
steps.desc: Push a user-facing notification (in-app, email, or push where safe) warning installed users about the malware and recommended action (e.g. uninstall, update).
steps.guidance: Embedded malware reaches installed devices directly, so user notification is time-critical.

ITID-21342.def: An unofficial, repackaged copy of the company's mobile app in which an attacker has decompiled the legitimate app, embedded malicious code, and re-signed/redistributed it, typically outside the official app store, to deceive users into installing it in place of the genuine app.
ITID-21342.purpose: Captures a fully trojanized or repackaged unofficial clone of the company's mobile app that embeds malware and is distributed as if it were the real app.
scopeIncludes: A decompiled-and-reassembled clone of the app carrying embedded malware
Redistribution of the trojanized clone via unofficial channels using the company's branding to appear legitimate
scopeExcludes: Malicious third-party SDK embedded in the company's own official build (ITID-21341)
Malicious code injected into the official build via a compromised build/signing process (ITID-21343)

The distribution-channel aspect of sideloaded/third-party-store malicious updates, tracked under ITID-21314, which this leaf's malware-content details support without duplicating the distribution narrative
ITID-21342.severity: High. The company's own official infrastructure is not compromised, but users and the brand are still directly harmed by a convincing fake.
ITID-21342.escalation: Escalate to legal/brand protection for takedown and to security for malware analysis of the trojanized clone.
indicators: Discovery of a repackaged app with modified/added code compared to the official build
Endpoint/malware detections traced to a clone of the app installed outside the official store
User reports of installing an app that behaved unlike the genuine version
vectors: Decompilation and reassembly of the legitimate app binary with injected malicious code
Distribution via unofficial marketplaces or phishing-driven sideloading
rootCauses: App lacks anti-tampering, obfuscation, or repackaging-detection protections
No proactive monitoring for unofficial clones of the app
mitreTechniques: T1476 Deliver Malicious App via Other Means
controls: App anti-tampering, obfuscation, and repackaging-detection protections
Brand/app-marketplace monitoring for unofficial clones
User education on official download sources
ITID-21342.detection: Primarily external (brand monitoring, malware research, user reports); no internal telemetry since the official app/infrastructure is uninvolved.
ITID-21342.response: File a takedown request for the trojanized clone, analyze the malware to assess data/harm exposure, and issue a public warning directing users to the official app.
metrics: Time-to-takedown of the trojanized clone
Estimated number of users who installed it
ITID-21342.notes: Scope decision: this leaf documents the trojanized-clone malware itself; the sideloading/third-party-store distribution mechanics are tracked once under ITID-21314 to avoid duplicating that leaf's distribution-channel content.

playbook.name: Response: Trojanized/Repackaged App Embedded Malware
playbook.description: For malware embedded via a trojanized or repackaged version of the app being distributed to users, whether through unofficial channels or a compromised legitimate one.

steps.title: Confirm the app is trojanized and identify its distribution source
steps.desc: Compare the suspect package's signing certificate and binary against the legitimate app to confirm repackaging, and identify where it is being distributed (official store, sideload site, third-party store).
steps.outcome: Trojanized package confirmed and distribution source identified.

steps.title: Report the trojanized package for takedown and coordinate app-store emergency takedown if it reached an official store
steps.desc: File takedown requests with the distributing platform/store, and if the trojanized package reached an official app store, request emergency takedown from the store's security/trust team.

steps.title: Confirm removal of the trojanized package from its distribution source
steps.desc: Verify the malicious package is no longer available for download.

steps.title: Advise affected users to uninstall and reset credentials
steps.desc: Provide clear remediation guidance for anyone who installed the trojanized app, including uninstall steps and credential resets.

steps.title: Document root cause and evaluate app-integrity monitoring
steps.desc: Log findings and consider ongoing monitoring for unauthorized repackaged distributions of the app.

steps.title: Characterize the embedded malware's behavior and impact
steps.desc: Determine what the malicious code does and estimate how many users may have installed the trojanized version.
steps.outcome: Malware behavior and exposure scope understood.

steps.title: Notify users of the trojanized version via official channels
steps.desc: Publish a warning through the app's official channels (in-app, website, social media, push where the legitimate app is still reachable) identifying the malicious version and instructing users to uninstall it.
steps.outcome: Users warned and given remediation instructions.

ITID-21343.def: Malicious functionality embedded directly into the company's official mobile app codebase or binary through compromise of the internal build system or code-signing process, resulting in the malicious code shipping under the company's own legitimate signature.
ITID-21343.purpose: Captures malicious code injected directly into the company's official app via compromise of its own build or code-signing process, distinct from a third-party SDK or a fully cloned app.
scopeIncludes: Malicious code committed directly to the app's source repository and compiled into an official release
Tampering with the compiled binary between build and signing
scopeExcludes: Malware arriving via a compromised third-party SDK dependency (ITID-21341)
A fully external trojanized clone with no access to the company's own build/signing process (ITID-21342)
The general CI/CD compromise leading to a published malicious update, tracked as its own distribution-focused leaf (ITID-21312), which this leaf's malware-content details support without duplicating
ITID-21343.severity: Critical. Malicious code shipped under the company's own legitimate code signature is maximally difficult for users or platforms to distinguish from a genuine release.
ITID-21343.escalation: Escalate immediately to engineering/security for full source-control and build-system forensic review; treat the signing key as compromised until proven otherwise.
indicators: Source-control diff revealing unauthorized code additions
Build artifact behavior inconsistent with reviewed/approved source code
Anomalous access to the build system or signing infrastructure
vectors: Compromised developer or build-system credentials used to commit/inject code
Compromised code-signing key/certificate
Insufficient code review allowing malicious commits to merge
rootCauses: Insufficient code review/approval requirements before merge
Inadequate protection of code-signing keys (e.g., not HSM-backed)
Overly broad commit/build access
mitreTechniques: T1474.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Mandatory code review/approval for all merges
HSM-backed code-signing key protection
Build artifact integrity/hash verification against reviewed source
ITID-21343.detection: Source-control audit and build-artifact verification provide direct technical signal if in place; otherwise detection often relies on downstream malware behavior.
ITID-21343.response: Roll back to a verified-clean build, rotate the signing key and developer credentials, and conduct a full source-control and build-system forensic review.
metrics: Time-to-lockdown of build/signing infrastructure
Number of releases affected before detection
ITID-21343.notes: Scope decision: this leaf documents the injected malware's presence in the company's own signed build; the distribution/publication consequence of a compromised CI/CD pipeline is tracked under ITID-21312 to avoid duplicating that leaf's content.

playbook.name: Response: Malicious Code Injected via Compromised Build/Signing Process
playbook.description: For malware injected into the legitimate app through a compromise of the internal build or code-signing process, resulting in a maliciously modified official release.

steps.title: Confirm malicious code in the signed release and trace it to the build/signing process
steps.desc: Compare the shipped signed build against expected source and confirm the injection point was the build/signing pipeline.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed as originating in the build/signing process.
steps.abort: If the compromise is a third-party SDK or trojanized redistribution rather than the internal build process, redirect to that dedicated playbook.

steps.title: Freeze the build/signing pipeline and revoke the compromised signing certificate
steps.desc: Halt all builds and revoke/rotate the code-signing certificate used to sign the malicious release.
steps.outcome: No further maliciously signed builds can be produced.

steps.title: Rebuild the pipeline from a known-clean state with a new signing key
steps.desc: Rotate all pipeline credentials/secrets, obtain a new signing certificate, and rebuild the environment from trusted sources.

steps.title: Document root cause and harden build/signing security
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend controls such as hardware security module (HSM)-backed signing keys and build provenance verification.

steps.title: Characterize the injected malware and its impact/reach
steps.desc: Determine what the malicious code does and how many devices received the maliciously signed build.
steps.outcome: Malware behavior and exposure scope understood.

steps.title: Pull the malicious build and coordinate app-store emergency takedown
steps.desc: Remove the affected release from distribution and request expedited emergency takedown/review from the app store.

steps.title: Publish a verified clean rebuilt release
steps.desc: Build and publish a clean version signed with the new certificate, forcing update where possible.

steps.title: Notify affected users of the embedded malware
steps.desc: Push a user-facing notification warning installed users about the malicious release.

ITID-21344.def: Malicious functionality that is not present in the app binary at install time but is fetched and executed dynamically from an attacker-controlled or compromised remote server after the app is installed and running, evading app store static/dynamic review of the submitted binary.
ITID-21344.purpose: Captures malware that ships clean in the initial app release but is dynamically fetched and loaded from a remote server after installation, evading app store review.
scopeIncludes: An app design that legitimately supports dynamic code/plugin loading, abused to fetch and execute a malicious payload post-install
Compromise of the remote server/endpoint that the app trusts for dynamic content or code delivery
scopeExcludes: Malware present in the binary at install/build time (ITID-21341/ITID-21342/ITID-21343)
Compromise of a dedicated OTA update server that pushes a full app update (ITID-21313) rather than fetching a runtime payload within the existing installed version
ITID-21344.severity: Critical. This technique is specifically designed to evade app store review, making it especially difficult to catch before broad user exposure.
ITID-21344.escalation: Escalate immediately to identify and take down the malicious remote endpoint, and to assess whether the app's dynamic-loading capability itself needs to be disabled or restricted.
indicators: Anomalous outbound requests from the app fetching executable/script content post-install
Behavior differing from what was present in the reviewed/submitted binary
Security research or endpoint detections identifying the dynamically-loaded payload
vectors: Compromise of the remote server/endpoint the app calls for dynamic content
Abuse of a legitimate dynamic-loading or plugin framework built into the app
Man-in-the-middle interception of the dynamic-content fetch if unsecured
rootCauses: App architecture permits fetching and executing unreviewed remote code
Insufficient integrity verification (signing/hashing) of dynamically-loaded content
Unsecured or inadequately monitored remote content-delivery endpoint
mitreTechniques: T1474.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Integrity verification (signing/hashing) of any dynamically-loaded code
Restriction or removal of unreviewed dynamic code-execution capability
Monitoring/alerting on the remote content-delivery endpoint
ITID-21344.detection: Outbound traffic analysis and endpoint behavior monitoring provide the primary technical signal; static app store review alone will not catch this.
ITID-21344.response: Take down or secure the malicious remote endpoint, disable the affected dynamic-loading capability if necessary, and issue an emergency update if the loading mechanism itself must change.
metrics: Time-to-endpoint-takedown
Number of users who executed the dynamically-loaded payload
ITID-21344.notes: Differentiated from OTA-server compromise (ITID-21313) by mechanism: a runtime payload fetch within an already-installed app version, not a full app update push.

playbook.name: Response: Dynamically-Loaded Malicious Code (Post-Install Payload Fetch)
playbook.description: For malware that is not present in the installed app binary itself but is fetched and executed dynamically after installation, evading app-store static review.

steps.title: Confirm dynamic payload fetching and identify the remote source
steps.desc: Analyze the app's runtime network behavior to confirm it is fetching and executing code post-install, and identify the malicious remote endpoint.
steps.guidance: This vector often evades static app-store review since the malicious code is not in the shipped binary.
steps.outcome: Dynamic-loading mechanism and remote source confirmed.
steps.tool: Malware analysis sandbox / network traffic analysis

steps.title: Block the malicious remote endpoint and disable the dynamic-loading mechanism
steps.desc: Block network access to the malicious payload server where possible, and disable the app feature/code path that fetches and executes remote code.
steps.outcome: No further malicious payloads can be fetched.

steps.title: Remove the dynamic-loading capability and publish a clean rebuilt version
steps.desc: Eliminate the remote-code-execution capability from the app and publish a clean version, forcing update where possible.
steps.outcome: Clean build distributed without dynamic-loading risk.

steps.title: Review app architecture for any remaining dynamic code-loading features
steps.desc: Audit the app for other features that fetch and execute remote code, which are inherently higher risk and harder to review.
steps.outcome: Remaining dynamic-loading risk identified and addressed.

steps.title: Document root cause and update app architecture security review requirements
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend restricting or prohibiting dynamic code loading in future app architecture.

steps.title: Characterize the fetched payload's behavior and impact
steps.desc: Determine what the dynamically loaded code does and how many active devices have fetched it.
steps.outcome: Payload behavior and exposure scope understood.

steps.title: Coordinate app-store emergency review given the evasion of static review
steps.desc: Proactively notify the app store's security team since this technique is specifically designed to bypass static app review, and request their assessment.

steps.title: Notify affected users of the embedded malware
steps.desc: Push a user-facing notification warning installed users about the malicious behavior.

ITID-21345.def: Malware embedded in or delivered through the company's mobile app, not clearly matching the third-party-SDK, trojanized-clone, build-compromise, or dynamic-payload leaves under this Type.
ITID-21345.purpose: Catch-all for embedded malware in the company's mobile app that does not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a more specific embedded-malware leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-21341 through ITID-21344
ITID-21345.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Critical pending investigation given the malware component.
ITID-21345.escalation: Reclassify once the specific insertion point (SDK, clone, build, or dynamic load) is clarified.
indicators: Malware associated with the app of unclear specific insertion point
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Code-signing enforcement for mobile app releases
Static and dynamic malware analysis in release pipeline
App store publishing account MFA enforcement
ITID-21345.detection: Same telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-21345.response: Contain and investigate to reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-21345.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Embedded Malware in Mobile App
playbook.description: General-purpose response for embedded malware in the mobile app that does not fit a more specific embedded-malware subtype.

steps.title: Confirm the presence of embedded malware and identify its source
steps.desc: Perform malware analysis to confirm the malicious behavior and determine whether it came from a third-party SDK, a trojanized redistribution, a compromised build process, or dynamic post-install loading.
steps.outcome: Malware confirmed and source category identified.
steps.abort: If a more specific category is confirmed, redirect to that dedicated playbook.

steps.title: Pull affected app versions from distribution
steps.desc: Remove the affected build(s) from all distribution channels.

steps.title: Remove the malicious code and publish a clean rebuilt version
steps.desc: Eliminate the malicious component, rebuild, and publish a clean version, forcing update where possible.

steps.title: Review app dependencies and build process for related risk
steps.desc: Audit the app's dependencies and build/signing process for other potential weaknesses.

steps.title: Document root cause and remediation
steps.desc: Log findings for future prevention.

steps.title: Characterize the malware's behavior and exposure scope
steps.desc: Determine what the malicious code does and how many devices/users are affected.
steps.outcome: Malware behavior and exposure scope understood.

steps.title: Notify affected users of the embedded malware
steps.desc: Push a user-facing notification warning installed users about the malware and recommended action.

ITID-21411.def: Unauthorized alteration of content on the corporate intranet portal or internal wiki, replacing or overlaying legitimate internal content with unauthorized material.
ITID-21411.purpose: Captures defacement of the internal intranet home page or wiki, the platform employees rely on for company-wide announcements and reference material.
scopeIncludes: Homepage banner/announcement replaced with unauthorized content on the intranet
Wiki pages edited to inject defacement content, offensive imagery, or false announcements
Internal news feed or all-staff bulletin hijacked to display unauthorized content
scopeExcludes: Defacement of externally-facing customer or partner portals (see ITID-2142x/2143x)
Defacement achieved specifically via compromised insider credentials as the differentiating factor (ITID-21414)
Defacement achieved specifically via a compromised CMS/admin panel as the differentiating factor (ITID-21415)
ITID-21411.severity: Medium. Low external brand exposure but can damage internal trust, morale, and be mistaken for an official (mis)communication.
ITID-21411.priority: P2; escalate to P1 if the defaced content impersonates executive communication or spreads false urgent instructions (e.g. fake layoff notice, fake security alert).
ITID-21411.escalation: Escalate to IT/internal comms and the SOC immediately; notify HR/Legal if the content is defamatory, discriminatory, or could trigger workforce panic.
indicators: Unexpected content change on intranet homepage or wiki page
Employee reports of an unfamiliar or offensive announcement
Wiki edit history showing unauthorized edits from an unexpected account
vectors: Weak/reused wiki editor account credentials
Unpatched intranet/wiki CMS software (e.g. Confluence, SharePoint) vulnerability
Overly broad edit permissions granted to non-admin staff
rootCauses: Excessive default edit permissions on intranet/wiki pages
Lack of change-approval workflow for homepage content
Delayed patching of internal collaboration platforms
controls: Role-based edit permissions on intranet/wiki content
Change-approval workflow for homepage/banner content
Patch management for internal collaboration platforms
ITID-21411.detection: Wiki/CMS edit-history logging and version control provide a reliable technical signal; content-integrity monitoring on the homepage can supplement.
ITID-21411.response: Revert to last known-good content, identify and lock the compromised or misused account, and confirm no further unauthorized edits are pending.
metrics: Time to revert defaced intranet/wiki content
Count of unauthorized wiki edits per quarter
ITID-21411.notes: Scoped to the defacement act on the intranet/wiki itself; access-vector-specific siblings (compromised insider credential, compromised CMS/admin panel) carry the underlying-cause detail so this leaf does not need to restate it.

playbook.name: Response: Intranet/Internal Wiki Defacement
playbook.description: For unauthorized defacement of the internal intranet or employee wiki, requiring an admin/CMS/SSO access review specific to that platform.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized changes and identify the access path used
steps.desc: Review the intranet/wiki's edit history and authentication logs to confirm the defacement and identify which account or access path was used.
steps.outcome: Defacement confirmed and access path identified.

steps.title: Review and lock down admin/CMS access to the intranet platform
steps.desc: Audit current admin accounts, disable the compromised account, and restrict further edits pending investigation.

steps.title: Restore defaced pages from backup/version history
steps.desc: Revert affected pages to their last known-good version.

steps.title: Notify affected employees if sensitive content was exposed
steps.desc: Inform relevant staff if internal information was altered or exposed during the defacement.

steps.title: Document root cause and review internal platform access controls
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend access-control or SSO hardening improvements.

steps.title: Assess employee exposure and content sensitivity affected
steps.desc: Determine which pages were defaced and whether any sensitive internal information was altered, deleted, or exposed.

steps.title: Review SSO/identity provider logs for the compromised account
steps.desc: Check the organization's SSO logs for suspicious login activity tied to the compromised account, since internal platforms are typically SSO-integrated.

steps.title: Reset credentials and force MFA re-enrollment for the compromised account
steps.desc: Rotate the affected employee's credentials and re-verify MFA before restoring access.

ITID-21412.def: Unauthorized alteration of content or display on the HR/benefits self-service portal, distinct from the intranet/wiki by its sensitive-data context and its links to payroll/benefits actions.
ITID-21412.purpose: Captures defacement of the HR/benefits self-service portal employees use for payroll, benefits enrollment, and personal HR data.
scopeIncludes: Defaced landing page or dashboard on the HR/benefits self-service portal
Injected unauthorized banners or notices on open-enrollment or payroll pages
scopeExcludes: Theft or exposure of HR/PII records without a defacement component (see insider data-theft leaves, e.g. ITID-13113)
Intranet/wiki defacement not involving the HR/benefits portal specifically (ITID-21411)
ITID-21412.severity: Medium-High, given the sensitive payroll/benefits context; higher if the defaced content attempts to redirect employees to a fraudulent payroll-update page.
ITID-21412.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the defacement includes a phishing/redirect component targeting payroll or banking details.
ITID-21412.escalation: Escalate to HR, IT security, and payroll immediately given the risk of employee-facing payroll fraud riding on the defacement.
indicators: Unexpected banner or redirect on the HR/benefits portal
Employee reports of a suspicious payroll-update prompt
HR portal admin logs showing unauthorized content changes
vectors: Compromised HR portal admin account
Third-party HR/benefits SaaS vendor vulnerability
Unpatched HR portal middleware
rootCauses: Insufficient MFA on HR portal admin accounts
Vendor patching lag on third-party HR/benefits platforms
controls: MFA on HR portal admin accounts
Vendor patch-cadence review for HR/benefits SaaS
Content-integrity monitoring on payroll/benefits pages
ITID-21412.detection: HR portal admin audit logs and content-integrity checks on payroll pages provide the primary technical signal.
ITID-21412.response: Revert content, verify no payroll/banking redirect harvested employee data, and force-reset the compromised admin account.
metrics: Time to detect and revert HR portal defacement
Number of employees exposed to a fraudulent redirect
ITID-21412.notes: If the incident is primarily payroll-fraud (e.g. direct-deposit redirection) without a visible defacement, classify under the relevant fraud ITID instead; this leaf requires an actual content-alteration/defacement element.

playbook.name: Response: HR/Benefits Self-Service Portal Defacement
playbook.description: For unauthorized defacement of the HR/benefits self-service portal, which also carries sensitive employee personal data risk.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized changes and identify the access path used
steps.desc: Review the HR portal's edit history and authentication/admin logs to confirm the defacement and identify the compromised access path.
steps.outcome: Defacement confirmed and access path identified.

steps.title: Review and lock down admin/CMS access to the HR portal
steps.desc: Audit current admin accounts, disable the compromised account, and restrict further changes pending investigation.

steps.title: Restore defaced content from backup/version history
steps.desc: Revert affected pages/records to their last known-good version.

steps.title: Notify affected employees if personal/benefits data exposure is confirmed
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR, Legal, and Privacy on employee notification obligations if data exposure occurred.

steps.title: Document root cause and review HR platform access controls
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend access-control improvements given the sensitivity of HR data.

steps.title: Assess whether employee personal/benefits data was accessed or exposed
steps.desc: Determine if the same access used for defacement could have exposed sensitive HR/benefits data, triggering separate data-breach obligations.
steps.guidance: Loop in Privacy/Legal and HR leadership if personal data exposure is possible.

steps.title: Review SSO/identity provider logs for the compromised account
steps.desc: Check SSO logs for suspicious login activity tied to the compromised account.

steps.title: Reset credentials and force MFA re-enrollment for the compromised account
steps.desc: Rotate the affected credentials and re-verify MFA before restoring access.

ITID-21413.def: Unauthorized alteration of the IT helpdesk or ticketing portal's content or display, distinct from other employee portals by the risk of undermining trust in IT support channels themselves.
ITID-21413.purpose: Captures defacement of the IT helpdesk/ticketing portal employees use to request IT support.
scopeIncludes: Defaced helpdesk portal landing page or knowledge-base article
Unauthorized announcement injected into the ticketing system dashboard
scopeExcludes: Malicious tickets or social-engineering submitted through a functioning, non-defaced helpdesk (separate social-engineering ITIDs)
Intranet/wiki defacement not involving the helpdesk platform specifically (ITID-21411)
ITID-21413.severity: Medium; elevated if the defacement is used to distribute fake IT instructions (e.g. fake password-reset link) that could facilitate further compromise.
ITID-21413.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the defaced content is being used as a phishing/malware-distribution vector.
ITID-21413.escalation: Escalate to IT security immediately; suspend the affected knowledge-base article or announcement pending review, and warn staff not to follow embedded links until verified.
indicators: Unauthorized content on the helpdesk portal or knowledge base
Ticketing system dashboard displaying unexpected announcements
Spike in employee tickets asking about a suspicious portal message
vectors: Compromised helpdesk admin/agent account
Vulnerable ticketing system plugin or knowledge-base module
rootCauses: Shared or weakly protected helpdesk admin credentials
Unpatched ticketing platform software
controls: MFA on helpdesk admin/agent accounts
Patch management for ticketing platform
Content-approval workflow for knowledge-base articles
ITID-21413.detection: Ticketing platform audit logs and knowledge-base version history give reliable detection; user-reported tickets often serve as the first signal.
ITID-21413.response: Revert unauthorized content, verify no embedded malicious links were clicked, and reset compromised agent/admin accounts.
metrics: Time to revert helpdesk portal defacement
Count of employees who interacted with defaced content
ITID-21413.notes: Distinguished from ITID-21411 by targeting the helpdesk/ticketing system specifically rather than the general intranet/wiki.

playbook.name: Response: IT Helpdesk/Ticketing Portal Defacement
playbook.description: For unauthorized defacement of the internal IT helpdesk/ticketing portal, a platform with elevated trust since employees rely on it for security-sensitive support requests.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized changes and identify the access path used
steps.desc: Review the helpdesk/ticketing system's edit history and admin/authentication logs to confirm the defacement and identify the compromised access path.
steps.outcome: Defacement confirmed and access path identified.

steps.title: Review and lock down admin/CMS access to the helpdesk portal
steps.desc: Audit current admin accounts, disable the compromised account, and restrict further changes pending investigation.

steps.title: Restore defaced content from backup/version history
steps.desc: Revert affected pages/ticket templates to their last known-good version.

steps.title: Alert employees if any fake instructions were displayed
steps.desc: Notify staff if the defacement contained fake support instructions they may have followed.

steps.title: Document root cause and review helpdesk platform access controls
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend access-control improvements given the portal's trusted role in employee security interactions.

steps.title: Assess whether the defacement could be used to social-engineer employees
steps.desc: Determine if the altered content could trick employees into taking unsafe actions (e.g. fake password reset instructions, fake IT contact info), given the portal's trusted role.

steps.title: Review SSO/identity provider logs for the compromised account
steps.desc: Check SSO logs for suspicious login activity tied to the compromised account.

steps.title: Reset credentials and force MFA re-enrollment for the compromised account
steps.desc: Rotate the affected credentials and re-verify MFA before restoring access.

ITID-21414.def: Defacement of any internal employee-facing portal performed after an attacker (or a malicious insider) authenticates using a compromised legitimate employee credential, rather than through a platform-level exploit.
ITID-21414.purpose: Captures employee-portal defacement carried out through a compromised legitimate insider credential, where the credential itself (not a CMS exploit) is the access vector.
scopeIncludes: Defacement performed after logging in with a phished, stuffed, or otherwise stolen employee credential
Defacement performed by a malicious insider using their own legitimate but misused credential
scopeExcludes: The underlying credential phishing/compromise event itself, tracked under the relevant ITID-12xxx credential-attack leaf (e.g. ITID-12111 Phishing with Credential Harvest, ITID-12216 Credential Stuffing Against SSO/Identity Provider)
Malicious insider activity with no defacement component, tracked under the ITID-13xxx insider-threat domain (e.g. ITID-13511 Insider Providing Access Credentials to External Attacker)
Defacement via a compromised CMS/admin panel rather than a compromised end-user credential (ITID-21415)
ITID-21414.severity: Medium-High; the confirmed credential compromise implies broader account-takeover risk beyond just the visible defacement.
ITID-21414.priority: P1 given the dual concern of active account compromise plus public/internal-facing content risk.
ITID-21414.escalation: Escalate to IT security for immediate credential revocation and session termination; escalate to insider-threat/HR review if a malicious insider is suspected rather than external account takeover.
indicators: Portal edit/audit logs showing a legitimate employee account performing out-of-pattern content changes
Login from an unusual location/device immediately preceding the defacement
Employee report of not having made the change
vectors: Phished employee credential used to log into the portal
Credential-stuffed or password-sprayed employee account
Malicious insider using their own valid access
rootCauses: Lack of MFA on portal accounts with content-edit rights
Insufficient anomaly detection on portal login/edit behavior
controls: MFA on all portal accounts with content-edit rights
User and entity behavior analytics (UEBA) on portal login/edit activity
Immediate credential revocation procedure upon suspected compromise
ITID-21414.detection: Portal audit logs correlated with identity/authentication logs give strong detection; UEBA anomaly alerts add an earlier signal.
ITID-21414.response: Revoke the compromised session/credential immediately, revert defaced content, and investigate whether the credential was externally phished/stuffed or insider-misused before final classification.
metrics: Time from anomalous login to credential revocation
Count of portal defacements attributable to credential compromise
detections: Portal audit-log correlation with authentication logs
ITID-21414.notes: This leaf is scoped strictly to the defacement act and its brand/operational impact; the underlying credential-compromise technique is tracked and metriced under its own ITID-12xxx or ITID-13xxx leaf to avoid duplicating that analysis here.

playbook.name: Response: Employee Portal Defacement via Compromised Insider Credentials
playbook.description: For defacement of an internal employee portal carried out using the compromised credentials of a legitimate employee, rather than an external system exploit.

steps.title: Confirm the compromised employee credential and how it was obtained
steps.desc: Review authentication logs to confirm which employee's credentials were used, and interview the employee about possible phishing, password reuse, or malware.
steps.outcome: Compromised credential and likely compromise method identified.

steps.title: Disable the compromised account and force a global credential reset
steps.desc: Immediately disable the account across all connected systems (typically via SSO/identity provider) and force a password/MFA reset.
steps.outcome: Compromised credential can no longer be used anywhere.

steps.title: Restore defaced content from backup/version history
steps.desc: Revert affected portal pages to their last known-good version.

steps.title: Restore account access with re-verified identity and MFA
steps.desc: Restore the employee's access only after identity re-verification and MFA re-enrollment.

steps.title: Document root cause and reinforce phishing/credential-hygiene awareness
steps.desc: Log findings and feed into security awareness training given the insider-credential vector.

steps.title: Assess what else the compromised credential had access to
steps.desc: Determine whether the same credential grants access to other systems that may also be at risk (email, other portals, VPN).
steps.outcome: Full access scope of the compromised credential understood.

steps.title: Review for lateral movement or additional unauthorized activity by the credential
steps.desc: Check other systems the credential had access to for any unauthorized activity beyond the portal defacement.
steps.outcome: Scope of unauthorized activity confirmed or ruled out elsewhere.

ITID-21415.def: Defacement of an internal employee-facing portal achieved by compromising the CMS or admin panel that controls its content, granting broad content-editing power beyond a single user account.
ITID-21415.purpose: Captures employee-portal defacement carried out via a compromised content-management-system (CMS) or administrative panel, where the platform-level admin access (not a single user credential) is the vector.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a CMS/admin-panel vulnerability to alter portal content platform-wide
Compromise of a shared CMS super-admin account distinct from an individual employee's own login
scopeExcludes: Defacement via a single compromised end-user employee credential without a CMS/platform-level compromise (ITID-21414)
The underlying CMS vulnerability exploitation as a standalone intrusion without any defacement (tracked as a vulnerability-exploitation ITID elsewhere)
ITID-21415.severity: High; platform-level compromise typically enables mass or repeated content alteration across the entire portal, not a single page.
ITID-21415.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT security and the platform/CMS vendor (if third-party hosted) to contain the admin-panel compromise before further content changes occur.
indicators: CMS admin panel showing unauthorized configuration or template changes
Unexpected new admin accounts in the CMS
Widespread/multi-page content alteration inconsistent with a single-user edit
vectors: Exploitation of an unpatched CMS vulnerability
Compromised shared CMS super-admin credential
Exposed CMS admin interface reachable without adequate access restriction
rootCauses: Delayed CMS patching
CMS admin panel exposed beyond intended network segment
Lack of MFA on CMS super-admin accounts
controls: CMS patch management program
Network segmentation restricting CMS admin panel access
MFA on CMS super-admin accounts
ITID-21415.detection: CMS admin audit logs and configuration-change monitoring provide strong detection; web application firewall (WAF) logs can reveal the exploit attempt.
ITID-21415.response: Contain the CMS admin panel, rotate all admin credentials, patch the exploited vulnerability, and restore content from a known-good backup.
metrics: Time to contain compromised CMS admin access
Number of pages/templates affected per incident
detections: WAF alerting on exploit attempts against CMS admin endpoints
ITID-21415.notes: Differentiated from ITID-21414 by the access vector: platform/CMS-level compromise here versus a single compromised end-user credential there.

playbook.name: Response: Employee Portal Defacement via Compromised CMS/Admin Panel
playbook.description: For defacement of an internal employee portal carried out via a compromise of the underlying CMS or admin panel itself, rather than a single employee's credentials.

steps.title: Confirm the CMS/admin panel compromise and identify the exploited vulnerability or access path
steps.desc: Review CMS logs and, where applicable, recent vulnerability disclosures for the platform to determine how the admin panel was compromised.
steps.abort: If a single employee credential is the sole vector, redirect to the insider-credential playbook.

steps.title: Take the CMS/admin panel offline or into maintenance mode
steps.desc: Restrict public/internal access to the CMS admin panel while the compromise is contained.

steps.title: Restore defaced content from backup and scan for planted backdoors
steps.desc: Revert content to a known-good backup and scan the CMS installation for any webshells or backdoors the attacker may have planted.
steps.outcome: Content restored and no persistent attacker access remains.

steps.title: Restore the CMS to normal operation with monitoring in place
steps.desc: Bring the portal back online with enhanced logging/monitoring for a defined period post-incident.

steps.title: Document root cause and add the CMS to the regular patch-management cycle
steps.desc: Log findings and ensure the CMS platform is included in ongoing vulnerability/patch management.

steps.title: Assess whether the CMS compromise affects other sites/portals sharing the same platform
steps.desc: Determine if other internal or external sites run on the same compromised CMS instance/version.
steps.outcome: Full blast radius across CMS-hosted properties identified.

steps.title: Patch or upgrade the vulnerable CMS component
steps.desc: Apply the relevant security patch/upgrade to close the exploited vulnerability before restoring service.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS admin credentials and API keys
steps.desc: Force-reset credentials for all CMS admin accounts and any integration keys.

ITID-21416.def: Defacement of an internal employee-facing portal, not clearly matching a more specific leaf (intranet/wiki, HR portal, helpdesk portal, compromised-credential, or compromised-CMS access vector).
ITID-21416.purpose: Catch-all for employee portal defacement cases that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a specific employee-portal leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (ITID-21411 through ITID-21415)
ITID-21416.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Medium pending clarification.
ITID-21416.escalation: Reclassify once the specific portal and access vector are clarified.
indicators: Report of defaced internal portal content with unclear platform or vector
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Internal portal admin account MFA enforcement
File integrity monitoring on internal web content
Least-privilege access controls on portal CMS
ITID-21416.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-21416.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-21416.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Employee Portal Defacement
playbook.description: General-purpose response for employee portal defacement that does not fit a more specific employee-portal-defacement subtype.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized changes and identify the compromise vector
steps.desc: Determine whether the defacement resulted from compromised insider credentials, a compromised CMS/admin panel, or another access path.
steps.abort: If a more specific category is confirmed, redirect to that dedicated playbook.

steps.title: Lock down the compromised access path
steps.desc: Disable the compromised account or restrict admin panel access as appropriate.

steps.title: Restore defaced content from backup/version history
steps.desc: Revert affected content to its last known-good version.

steps.title: Restore normal portal operation with monitoring
steps.desc: Bring the portal back online with heightened monitoring for a defined period.

steps.title: Document root cause and remediation
steps.desc: Log findings for future prevention.

steps.title: Assess employee exposure and content sensitivity affected
steps.desc: Determine which pages/data were affected and any sensitivity concerns.

steps.title: Review SSO/identity provider logs for related suspicious activity
steps.desc: Check SSO logs for related suspicious login activity.

steps.title: Reset credentials and rotate any compromised admin access
steps.desc: Rotate affected credentials before restoring access.

ITID-21421.def: Unauthorized alteration of content or display within the customer account dashboard, visible to authenticated customers viewing their own account.
ITID-21421.purpose: Captures defacement of the customer-facing account dashboard where customers view and manage their own account.
scopeIncludes: Defaced account dashboard homepage or account-summary view
Unauthorized banners/notices injected into the logged-in customer dashboard
scopeExcludes: Defacement of the public-facing e-commerce/storefront pages seen by unauthenticated visitors (ITID-21423)
Defacement injecting fraudulent payment/billing content specifically (ITID-21425)
ITID-21421.severity: High, given direct customer visibility and potential erosion of trust in account security.
ITID-21421.priority: P1, given the customer-facing and authenticated-session context.
ITID-21421.escalation: Escalate to IT security and customer support leadership immediately; prepare customer communications if the defacement was visible broadly.
indicators: Customer reports of unusual content in their account dashboard
Application logs showing unauthorized template/content changes to the dashboard
Support ticket spike referencing an odd dashboard message
vectors: Compromised admin/CMS access to the customer-facing application
Exploited vulnerability in the dashboard application layer
rootCauses: Insufficient input validation/output encoding allowing content injection
Overly broad admin access to dashboard templates
controls: Web application firewall on the customer dashboard
Content-integrity monitoring on dashboard templates
Least-privilege admin access to dashboard content
ITID-21421.detection: Application-layer content-integrity monitoring and customer-reported tickets provide the primary detection signal.
ITID-21421.response: Revert dashboard content, verify no customer data was exposed or manipulated, and notify affected customers if warranted.
metrics: Time to detect and revert dashboard defacement
Number of customers exposed
ITID-21421.notes: Scoped to dashboard content shown to authenticated customers; storefront and payment-content variants are tracked separately to preserve a clean differentiating axis.

playbook.name: Response: Customer Account Dashboard Defacement
playbook.description: For unauthorized defacement of the customer-facing account dashboard, requiring urgent attention given direct customer visibility.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized changes and identify the access path used
steps.desc: Review the dashboard platform's edit history and admin logs to confirm the defacement and identify the compromised access path.
steps.outcome: Defacement confirmed and access path identified.

steps.title: Review and lock down admin/CMS access to the customer portal
steps.desc: Audit current admin accounts, disable the compromised account, and restrict further changes pending investigation.

steps.title: Restore defaced content from backup/version history
steps.desc: Revert affected pages to their last known-good version.

steps.title: Notify customers if account data integrity was affected
steps.desc: Communicate with affected customers if their account data (not just display content) was altered.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with Customer Support/Communications.

steps.title: Document root cause and review customer portal access controls
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend access-control improvements.

steps.title: Assess customer exposure and whether any account data was altered or exposed
steps.desc: Determine how many customers are seeing the defaced dashboard and whether any account data was tampered with beyond visual defacement.

steps.title: Consider a temporary maintenance page if defacement is severe
steps.desc: If the defacement is offensive or misleading, temporarily take the dashboard offline behind a maintenance page rather than leave it publicly visible.
steps.outcome: Customer exposure to the defaced content stopped.
steps.abort: Restore normal access once content is cleaned.

steps.title: Reset credentials and force MFA re-enrollment for the compromised account
steps.desc: Rotate the affected credentials and re-verify MFA before restoring access.

ITID-21422.def: Unauthorized alteration of content on the customer-facing support portal or help center, including knowledge-base articles and support-ticket landing pages.
ITID-21422.purpose: Captures defacement of the customer support/help center where customers seek self-service assistance and knowledge-base content.
scopeIncludes: Defaced help-center landing page or knowledge-base article
Unauthorized content injected into customer-facing support-ticket status pages
scopeExcludes: Defacement of the authenticated account dashboard (ITID-21421)
Defacement of the storefront/e-commerce pages (ITID-21423)
ITID-21422.severity: Medium-High; particularly damaging if the defaced content is mistaken for official support guidance (e.g. fake refund instructions).
ITID-21422.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the defacement includes fraudulent instructions that could cause customer financial harm.
ITID-21422.escalation: Escalate to IT security and customer support leadership; suspend affected knowledge-base content pending review.
indicators: Unexpected content on the help center or knowledge base
Customer reports referencing a suspicious support article
Knowledge-base CMS logs showing unauthorized edits
vectors: Compromised support-portal CMS admin account
Vulnerable third-party help-center/knowledge-base platform
rootCauses: Weak access controls on knowledge-base editing
Unpatched third-party help-center platform
controls: MFA on support-portal CMS admin accounts
Vendor patch-cadence review for third-party help-center platforms
Content-approval workflow for published knowledge-base articles
ITID-21422.detection: Knowledge-base version history and CMS audit logs provide the primary technical signal.
ITID-21422.response: Revert content, verify whether customers acted on fraudulent guidance, and notify support staff to flag related inbound tickets.
metrics: Time to revert help-center defacement
Number of customer tickets referencing the defaced content
ITID-21422.notes: Distinguished from ITID-21421 by targeting the public/self-service support surface rather than the authenticated account dashboard.

playbook.name: Response: Customer Support/Help Center Defacement
playbook.description: For unauthorized defacement of the customer support/help center portal, a platform customers trust for accurate guidance.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized changes and identify the access path used
steps.desc: Review the help center's edit history and admin logs to confirm the defacement and identify the compromised access path.
steps.outcome: Defacement confirmed and access path identified.

steps.title: Review and lock down admin/CMS access to the help center
steps.desc: Audit current admin accounts, disable the compromised account, and restrict further changes pending investigation.

steps.title: Restore defaced articles/pages from backup/version history
steps.desc: Revert affected help articles to their last known-good version.

steps.title: Warn customers if fake instructions/links may have already misled them
steps.desc: Issue a notice via other support channels if customers may have already acted on fraudulent guidance.

steps.title: Document root cause and review help center access controls
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend access-control improvements.

steps.title: Assess whether altered help content could mislead customers into unsafe action
steps.desc: Check whether the defacement includes fake support contact info, fake instructions, or malicious links that could be used to social-engineer customers.

steps.title: Reset credentials and force MFA re-enrollment for the compromised account
steps.desc: Rotate the affected credentials and re-verify MFA before restoring access.

ITID-21423.def: Unauthorized alteration of content on the public-facing e-commerce or storefront portal, visible to any visitor without requiring authentication.
ITID-21423.purpose: Captures defacement of the public e-commerce/storefront pages seen by unauthenticated visitors and shoppers.
scopeIncludes: Defaced storefront homepage, category, or product listing pages
Unauthorized banners or pop-ups injected into the public shopping experience
scopeExcludes: Defacement confined to the authenticated customer account dashboard (ITID-21421)
Defacement specifically injecting fraudulent payment/billing content (ITID-21425)
ITID-21423.severity: High, given maximum public visibility and potential direct revenue/reputational impact.
ITID-21423.escalation: Escalate to IT security, e-commerce operations, and communications/PR immediately given public exposure.
indicators: Public reports/screenshots of the defaced storefront circulating on social media
Sudden drop in conversion or checkout completion correlating with a content change
Storefront CMS logs showing unauthorized page edits
vectors: Compromised storefront CMS/admin access
Exploited vulnerability in the e-commerce platform or a storefront plugin
Supply-chain compromise of a third-party storefront widget
rootCauses: Unpatched e-commerce platform or plugins
Insufficient monitoring of storefront content integrity
controls: Web application firewall on the storefront
Content-integrity monitoring on public storefront pages
Third-party plugin/widget vetting and patch management
ITID-21423.detection: Public content-integrity monitoring, social-media/brand monitoring, and storefront CMS audit logs together provide strong detection coverage.
ITID-21423.response: Take the affected page(s) down or revert to a known-good version immediately, verify checkout/payment integrity was not also compromised, and coordinate a public statement if needed.
metrics: Time to detect and revert storefront defacement
Estimated visitor exposure/traffic during defacement window
ITID-21423.notes: Highest-visibility leaf in this Tier-4 group given unauthenticated public reach; kept distinct from the payment-content-injection leaf (ITID-21425) which requires a fraud/financial element.

playbook.name: Response: E-Commerce/Storefront Portal Defacement
playbook.description: For unauthorized defacement of the customer-facing e-commerce storefront, potentially disrupting sales and customer trust.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized changes and identify the access path used
steps.desc: Review the storefront platform's edit history and admin logs to confirm the defacement and identify the compromised access path.
steps.outcome: Defacement confirmed and access path identified.

steps.title: Review and lock down admin/CMS access to the storefront
steps.desc: Audit current admin accounts, disable the compromised account, and restrict further changes pending investigation.

steps.title: Restore defaced content from backup/version history
steps.desc: Revert affected pages to their last known-good version.

steps.title: Verify order integrity and resume normal storefront operation
steps.desc: Confirm no fraudulent orders were placed during the defacement window before fully resuming normal operations.
steps.outcome: Storefront confirmed clean and fully operational.

steps.title: Document root cause and review storefront access controls
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend access-control improvements.

steps.title: Assess impact on active shopping/checkout flows
steps.desc: Determine whether the defacement affects product pages, pricing, or the checkout flow, and whether orders are still processing correctly.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with e-commerce operations to check order processing integrity.

steps.title: Consider pausing checkout if defacement affects pricing or payment flows
steps.desc: If the defacement risks fraudulent transactions, temporarily pause checkout until content is verified clean.
steps.abort: Resume checkout once storefront integrity is confirmed.

steps.title: Reset credentials and force MFA re-enrollment for the compromised account
steps.desc: Rotate the affected credentials and re-verify MFA before restoring access.

ITID-21424.def: Defacement of any customer-facing portal (dashboard, support, or storefront) achieved through compromise of the platform's administrative or CMS access, rather than a customer-facing application vulnerability alone.
ITID-21424.purpose: Captures customer-portal defacement carried out via a compromised admin or CMS account controlling the customer-facing platform.
scopeIncludes: Compromised customer-portal CMS super-admin account used to alter content platform-wide
Exploited admin-panel authentication weakness enabling content changes
scopeExcludes: Defacement via a customer-facing application vulnerability without admin-account compromise (tracked under the specific portal-type leaf, e.g. ITID-21423)
The underlying admin-credential phishing/compromise mechanics, tracked under the relevant ITID-12xxx credential-attack leaf
ITID-21424.severity: High; admin/CMS-level compromise typically enables broad or repeated content alteration across multiple customer-facing pages.
ITID-21424.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT security to revoke admin access and rotate all CMS credentials before further content changes occur.
indicators: CMS admin panel showing unauthorized configuration changes
New or modified admin accounts not recognized by the platform team
Multi-page defacement inconsistent with a single content-editor's scope
vectors: Phished or stuffed CMS admin credential
Exploited CMS admin-panel vulnerability
Insufficiently restricted admin-panel network exposure
rootCauses: Lack of MFA on CMS super-admin accounts
CMS admin panel reachable from the public internet without restriction
controls: MFA on CMS super-admin accounts
Network restriction on CMS admin panel access
CMS patch management program
ITID-21424.detection: CMS admin audit logs and configuration-change monitoring provide the primary detection signal.
ITID-21424.response: Contain and rotate all admin credentials, patch any exploited vulnerability, and restore all affected pages from a known-good backup.
metrics: Time to contain compromised admin access
Number of customer-facing pages affected
ITID-21424.notes: This leaf is scoped strictly to the defacement act enabled by admin/CMS compromise; the underlying credential-compromise or exploit technique is tracked under its own ITID-12xxx leaf to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Customer Portal Defacement via Compromised Admin/CMS Access
playbook.description: For defacement of a customer-facing portal carried out via a compromise of the underlying admin/CMS access itself, rather than a single credential's misuse elsewhere.

steps.title: Confirm the admin/CMS compromise and identify the exploited access path
steps.desc: Review CMS admin logs and any recent vulnerability disclosures for the platform to determine how admin access was obtained.

steps.title: Take the CMS/admin panel offline or into maintenance mode
steps.desc: Restrict access to the CMS admin panel while the compromise is contained.

steps.title: Restore defaced content from backup and scan for planted backdoors
steps.desc: Revert content to a known-good backup and scan for webshells or backdoors the attacker may have planted.
steps.outcome: Content restored and no persistent attacker access remains.

steps.title: Restore the portal to normal operation with monitoring in place
steps.desc: Bring the portal back online with enhanced logging/monitoring for a defined period post-incident.

steps.title: Document root cause and add the CMS to the regular patch-management cycle
steps.desc: Log findings and ensure the CMS platform is included in ongoing vulnerability/patch management.

steps.title: Assess whether the compromise affects other properties sharing the same CMS instance
steps.desc: Determine if other customer-facing sites/portals run on the same compromised CMS instance/version.

steps.title: Patch or upgrade the vulnerable CMS component
steps.desc: Apply the relevant security patch/upgrade to close the exploited vulnerability before restoring service.

steps.title: Rotate all CMS admin credentials and API keys
steps.desc: Force-reset credentials for all CMS admin accounts and any integration keys.

ITID-21425.def: Defacement of a customer-facing portal in which the injected content includes fraudulent payment instructions, fake billing notices, or altered payment forms intended to capture customer financial data or divert payments.
ITID-21425.purpose: Captures the specific and higher-severity case of customer-portal defacement that injects fraudulent payment or billing content, creating direct financial-fraud risk for customers.
scopeIncludes: Injected fake payment form or redirect designed to capture customer card/bank details
Altered billing notice directing customers to pay a fraudulent account
Defaced checkout flow inserting an unauthorized payment step
scopeExcludes: Defacement with no payment/billing fraud element (ITID-21421, ITID-21422, ITID-21423)
Standalone payment fraud/skimming without a visible content-defacement component (tracked under a payment-fraud/skimming ITID elsewhere)
ITID-21425.severity: Critical; combines brand-damaging defacement with direct customer financial harm.
ITID-21425.priority: P1, treated as a financial-fraud incident in addition to a defacement incident.
ITID-21425.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT security, fraud/financial-crimes, legal, and communications; consider regulatory notification obligations given potential payment-card or financial-data exposure.
indicators: Customer reports of fraudulent charges following a portal visit
Unexpected payment form or field injected into checkout/billing pages
Discrepancy between logged transactions and actual customer billing records
vectors: Web-skimming (Magecart-style) script injection into checkout pages
Compromised admin/CMS access used to alter payment-form content
Exploited vulnerability in a third-party payment-page component
rootCauses: Lack of subresource integrity/content-security-policy controls on payment pages
Unpatched third-party checkout/payment widget
mitreTechniques: T1059.007 Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript
controls: Content Security Policy and Subresource Integrity on payment pages
PCI-DSS compliant checkout page-integrity monitoring
Third-party payment widget vetting
ITID-21425.detection: Payment-page integrity monitoring (script-tampering detection) and customer fraud-complaint correlation together provide strong detection coverage.
ITID-21425.response: Take checkout/payment pages offline immediately, remove the injected content, notify payment processors and affected customers, and coordinate any required breach notification.
metrics: Number of customers with confirmed fraudulent charges
Time to take down the fraudulent payment content
ITID-21425.notes: Reserved for defacement with a confirmed payment/billing fraud injection; treat as the more severe sibling within this Tier-4 group and cross-file with the payment-fraud program.

playbook.name: Response: Customer Portal Defacement Injecting Fraudulent Payment/Billing Content
playbook.description: For defacement of a customer-facing portal that injects fraudulent payment or billing content, requiring an urgent customer-facing fraud warning given direct financial risk to customers.

steps.title: Confirm the fraudulent payment/billing content and identify the access path used
steps.desc: Review the portal's edit history and admin logs to confirm the injected fraudulent payment/billing content and identify the compromised access path.
steps.outcome: Fraudulent content confirmed and access path identified.

steps.title: Take the affected payment/billing page offline immediately
steps.desc: Remove or disable the fraudulent payment/billing content from customer view without delay.
steps.guidance: Financial fraud content requires the fastest possible containment given direct customer monetary risk.
steps.outcome: Fraudulent content no longer visible to customers.

steps.title: Restore legitimate payment/billing content from backup
steps.desc: Revert the payment/billing page to its verified last known-good version.

steps.title: Refer affected customer payments to the fraud team for reversal/dispute support
steps.desc: Work with Finance/fraud team to identify and assist customers who paid against fraudulent billing details.

steps.title: Document root cause, financial impact, and access-control improvements
steps.desc: Log findings including financial impact and recommend stronger controls given the payment-fraud severity of this incident type.

steps.title: Assess how many customers were exposed and whether any payments were made against the fraudulent content
steps.desc: Determine customer exposure window and check transaction records for payments made against the fraudulent billing information.
steps.guidance: Loop in Finance/Fraud team immediately given direct financial risk.

steps.title: Issue an urgent customer-facing fraud warning
steps.desc: Publish an urgent notice via email, SMS, and the portal itself warning customers not to use the fraudulent payment/billing details and providing verified correct information.
steps.guidance: Coordinate wording with Communications/PR and Legal given the financial fraud angle.
steps.outcome: Customers warned before further payments are made.

steps.title: Reset credentials and force MFA re-enrollment for the compromised account
steps.desc: Rotate the affected credentials and re-verify MFA before restoring access.

steps.title: Review and lock down admin/CMS access
steps.desc: Audit current admin accounts, disable the compromised account, and restrict further changes pending investigation.

ITID-21426.def: Defacement of a customer-facing portal, not clearly matching a more specific leaf (account dashboard, support/help center, storefront, compromised admin/CMS access, or fraudulent payment injection).
ITID-21426.purpose: Catch-all for customer portal defacement cases that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a specific customer-portal leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (ITID-21421 through ITID-21425)
ITID-21426.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Medium-High pending clarification given customer-facing exposure.
ITID-21426.escalation: Reclassify once the specific portal and vector are clarified.
indicators: Report of defaced customer-facing content with unclear platform or vector
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Web application firewall with virtual patching
Customer portal admin account MFA enforcement
Automated content-change alerting
ITID-21426.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-21426.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-21426.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Customer Portal Defacement
playbook.description: General-purpose response for customer portal defacement that does not fit a more specific customer-portal-defacement subtype.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized changes and identify the compromise vector
steps.desc: Determine whether the defacement resulted from a compromised admin/CMS access, injected payment/billing fraud, or another access path.
steps.abort: If a more specific category is confirmed (especially payment/billing fraud), redirect to that dedicated playbook.

steps.title: Lock down the compromised access path
steps.desc: Disable the compromised account or restrict admin panel access as appropriate.

steps.title: Restore defaced content from backup/version history
steps.desc: Revert affected content to its last known-good version.

steps.title: Notify customers if data or transactions were affected
steps.desc: Coordinate customer notification if warranted by the impact assessment.

steps.title: Document root cause and remediation
steps.desc: Log findings for future prevention.

steps.title: Assess customer exposure and impact
steps.desc: Determine how many customers were exposed and whether any customer data or transactions were affected.

steps.title: Reset credentials and rotate any compromised admin access
steps.desc: Rotate affected credentials before restoring access.

ITID-21431.def: Unauthorized alteration of content on the company's vendor/supplier extranet portal, visible to external supply-chain partners.
ITID-21431.purpose: Captures defacement of the vendor/supplier extranet used by external supply-chain partners to exchange operational data with the company.
scopeIncludes: Defaced extranet landing page or supplier-facing dashboard
Unauthorized announcement injected into vendor-facing order/status pages
scopeExcludes: Defacement of the developer/API portal (ITID-21432)
Defacement of the reseller/channel-partner portal (ITID-21433)
ITID-21431.severity: Medium-High; damages trust with supply-chain partners and can disrupt operational exchanges (orders, shipment status).
ITID-21431.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if it disrupts active supply-chain transactions.
