ITID-21431.escalation: Escalate to IT security and supply-chain/procurement leadership; notify affected vendors if the defacement could be mistaken for legitimate operational instructions.
indicators: Vendor reports of unusual extranet content
Extranet CMS logs showing unauthorized edits
Unexpected downtime or content change on vendor order-status pages
vectors: Compromised extranet admin account
Exploited vulnerability in the extranet platform
rootCauses: Weak access controls on extranet content management
Unpatched extranet platform software
controls: MFA on extranet admin accounts
Patch management for extranet platform
Content-integrity monitoring on vendor-facing pages
ITID-21431.detection: Extranet CMS audit logs and vendor-reported issues provide the primary detection signal.
ITID-21431.response: Revert content, verify no supply-chain transaction data was manipulated, and notify affected vendors.
metrics: Time to revert extranet defacement
Number of vendors affected
ITID-21431.notes: Scoped to the vendor/supplier extranet specifically, distinct from developer and reseller partner portals.

playbook.name: Response: Vendor/Supplier Extranet Defacement
playbook.description: For unauthorized defacement of the vendor/supplier extranet, requiring coordination with affected external vendors and suppliers.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized changes and identify the access path used
steps.desc: Review the extranet platform's edit history and admin logs to confirm the defacement and identify the compromised access path.
steps.outcome: Defacement confirmed and access path identified.

steps.title: Review and lock down admin/CMS/SSO access to the extranet
steps.desc: Audit current admin accounts, disable the compromised account, and restrict further changes pending investigation.

steps.title: Restore defaced content from backup/version history
steps.desc: Revert affected pages to their last known-good version.

steps.title: Confirm with vendors/suppliers that access has been restored safely
steps.desc: Follow up with affected external parties to confirm the extranet is safe to use again.

steps.title: Document root cause and review extranet access controls
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend access-control improvements, including external-party access review.

steps.title: Assess which vendors/suppliers were exposed to the defaced content
steps.desc: Determine which external vendor/supplier organizations have active access and would have seen the defacement.

steps.title: Notify affected vendors/suppliers of the defacement
steps.desc: Proactively inform vendor/supplier contacts that the extranet was defaced and any content or links they saw should be disregarded.
steps.outcome: External partners informed and coordinated with.

steps.title: Reset credentials and force MFA re-enrollment for the compromised account
steps.desc: Rotate the affected credentials and re-verify MFA before restoring access.

ITID-21432.def: Unauthorized alteration of content on the company's API developer portal, visible to external developers and integration partners.
ITID-21432.purpose: Captures defacement of the partner-facing API developer portal used by integration partners to access documentation and API keys.
scopeIncludes: Defaced developer portal landing page or API documentation
Unauthorized content injected into API key management or sandbox pages
scopeExcludes: Defacement of the vendor/supplier extranet (ITID-21431)
Theft or misuse of API keys without a defacement component (tracked under an API-security ITID elsewhere)
ITID-21432.severity: Medium-High; particularly damaging if altered documentation could mislead developers into insecure integration practices.
ITID-21432.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the defacement includes tampered API documentation that could introduce security risk into partner integrations.
ITID-21432.escalation: Escalate to IT security and the API/platform engineering team; suspend affected documentation pages pending review.
indicators: Developer/partner reports of unusual portal content
Developer portal CMS logs showing unauthorized edits
Unexpected changes to published API documentation
vectors: Compromised developer portal admin account
Exploited vulnerability in the developer portal platform
rootCauses: Weak access controls on developer portal content management
Unpatched developer portal software
controls: MFA on developer portal admin accounts
Patch management for developer portal platform
Content-approval workflow for published API documentation
ITID-21432.detection: Developer portal CMS audit logs and partner-reported issues provide the primary detection signal.
ITID-21432.response: Revert content, verify no malicious API documentation was published, and notify integration partners if needed.
metrics: Time to revert developer portal defacement
Number of partners exposed to altered documentation
ITID-21432.notes: Scoped to the developer/API portal content specifically; API key/credential misuse without defacement is tracked separately.

playbook.name: Response: Partner API Developer Portal Defacement
playbook.description: For unauthorized defacement of the partner API developer portal, which may also impact partner integrations relying on documentation and credentials hosted there.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized changes and identify the access path used
steps.desc: Review the developer portal's edit history and admin logs to confirm the defacement and identify the compromised access path.
steps.outcome: Defacement confirmed and access path identified.

steps.title: Review and lock down admin/CMS access to the developer portal
steps.desc: Audit current admin accounts, disable the compromised account, and restrict further changes pending investigation.

steps.title: Restore defaced content from backup/version history
steps.desc: Revert affected pages/documentation to their last known-good version.

steps.title: Confirm with partners that integrations remain functional and secure
steps.desc: Follow up with partner developers to confirm no integration issues resulted from the incident.

steps.title: Document root cause and review developer portal access controls
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend access-control improvements.

steps.title: Assess whether API credentials, keys, or documentation integrity were affected
steps.desc: Determine if the compromise could have exposed or altered API keys, sample credentials, or integration documentation that partners rely on.

steps.title: Notify partner developers of the defacement
steps.desc: Alert partner development teams that the portal was compromised and any recently viewed keys/documentation should be treated with caution.

steps.title: Rotate any API keys/credentials that may have been exposed
steps.desc: Rotate sample or shared API credentials displayed on the portal if there is any chance they were exposed or altered.

ITID-21433.def: Unauthorized alteration of content on the company's reseller/channel-partner portal, visible to external sales and distribution partners.
ITID-21433.purpose: Captures defacement of the reseller/channel-partner portal used by resellers and channel partners for sales enablement and order management.
scopeIncludes: Defaced reseller portal landing page or sales-enablement content
Unauthorized announcement injected into channel-partner order-management pages
scopeExcludes: Defacement of the vendor/supplier extranet (ITID-21431)
Defacement of the developer/API portal (ITID-21432)
ITID-21433.severity: Medium-High; damages trust with the reseller/channel network and can disrupt sales operations.
ITID-21433.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if it disrupts active order processing or pricing information relied on by resellers.
ITID-21433.escalation: Escalate to IT security and channel/sales leadership; notify affected resellers if the defacement could be mistaken for legitimate pricing or order guidance.
indicators: Reseller reports of unusual portal content
Channel portal CMS logs showing unauthorized edits
Unexpected changes to pricing or order-status pages
vectors: Compromised channel portal admin account
Exploited vulnerability in the channel portal platform
rootCauses: Weak access controls on channel portal content management
Unpatched channel portal software
controls: MFA on channel portal admin accounts
Patch management for channel portal platform
Content-integrity monitoring on pricing/order pages
ITID-21433.detection: Channel portal CMS audit logs and reseller-reported issues provide the primary detection signal.
ITID-21433.response: Revert content, verify no pricing or order data was manipulated, and notify affected resellers.
metrics: Time to revert channel portal defacement
Number of resellers affected
ITID-21433.notes: Scoped to the reseller/channel-partner portal specifically, distinct from vendor extranet and developer portals.

playbook.name: Response: Reseller/Channel Partner Portal Defacement
playbook.description: For unauthorized defacement of the reseller/channel partner portal, which may affect partner sales operations and require partner-facing notification.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized changes and identify the access path used
steps.desc: Review the reseller portal's edit history and admin logs to confirm the defacement and identify the compromised access path.
steps.outcome: Defacement confirmed and access path identified.

steps.title: Review and lock down admin/CMS access to the reseller portal
steps.desc: Audit current admin accounts, disable the compromised account, and restrict further changes pending investigation.

steps.title: Restore defaced content from backup/version history
steps.desc: Revert affected pages/pricing data to their last known-good version.

steps.title: Verify any orders/commissions submitted during the incident window
steps.desc: Cross-check orders or commission entries made during the defacement window for accuracy before resuming normal operations.

steps.title: Document root cause and review partner portal access controls
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend access-control improvements.

steps.title: Assess impact on partner sales operations (pricing, order submission, commission data)
steps.desc: Determine whether the defacement affects pricing sheets, order submission tools, or commission/reporting data that resellers rely on.
steps.outcome: Business impact on partner operations understood.

steps.title: Notify channel partners of the defacement
steps.desc: Proactively inform reseller/channel partner contacts that the portal was compromised and any pricing or order data seen during the window should be verified.
steps.outcome: Channel partners informed and coordinated with.

steps.title: Reset credentials and force MFA re-enrollment for the compromised account
steps.desc: Rotate the affected credentials and re-verify MFA before restoring access.

ITID-21434.def: Defacement of a partner-facing platform (extranet, developer portal, or reseller portal) achieved after compromising a federated/SSO identity trust relationship, granting the attacker partner-level access without directly compromising the target platform's own credentials.
ITID-21434.purpose: Captures partner-platform defacement carried out through compromised federated identity or single-sign-on (SSO) access shared across partner organizations.
scopeIncludes: Defacement performed after abusing a compromised federated identity token or SAML/OIDC trust relationship with a partner organization
Defacement enabled by a compromised partner-side SSO identity provider account
scopeExcludes: The underlying SSO/identity-provider credential compromise itself, tracked under the relevant ITID-12xxx credential-attack leaf (e.g. ITID-12113 Phished Corporate SSO/Identity Provider Credential, ITID-12216 Credential Stuffing Against SSO/Identity Provider)
Defacement via a directly compromised platform-specific admin/CMS account not involving federation (see ITID-21431/21432/21433)
ITID-21434.severity: High; federated access compromise can extend beyond a single portal and implies a broader trust-boundary failure between the company and its partner.
ITID-21434.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT security and identity/IAM teams to revoke the compromised federation trust or token; notify the partner organization's security team in parallel.
indicators: Partner portal access logs showing content changes from a federated identity outside normal partner behavior patterns
Identity provider logs showing anomalous federated authentication immediately preceding the defacement
Partner organization reporting their own SSO environment was compromised
vectors: Compromised partner-side SSO/identity provider account used to federate into the company's partner platform
Stolen or forged federated authentication token (e.g. SAML assertion)
rootCauses: Insufficient conditional-access controls on federated partner logins
Lack of anomaly detection on federated authentication events
controls: Conditional access policies on federated partner authentication
Anomaly detection on SSO/federation login events
Rapid federation-trust revocation procedure
ITID-21434.detection: Identity provider federation logs correlated with partner-platform content-change logs provide the primary detection signal.
ITID-21434.response: Revoke or suspend the compromised federation trust/token immediately, revert defaced content, and coordinate investigation with the partner organization.
metrics: Time to revoke compromised federation trust
Number of partner platforms affected by the same federation compromise
ITID-21434.notes: This leaf is scoped strictly to the defacement act and its brand/operational impact via a compromised federated access path; the underlying credential-compromise technique on the partner's own SSO/identity provider is tracked under its own ITID-12xxx leaf to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Partner Platform Defacement via Compromised Federated/SSO Access
playbook.description: For defacement of a partner-facing platform carried out via a compromise of the federated identity/SSO trust relationship with an external partner organization.

steps.title: Confirm the federated/SSO compromise and identify the affected identity provider relationship
steps.desc: Review federation/SSO logs to determine whether the compromise originated on the company's side, the partner's identity provider side, or the trust configuration between them.
steps.outcome: Compromise vector and affected federation relationship identified.

steps.title: Suspend the affected federated/SSO trust relationship
steps.desc: Temporarily disable the federation link or affected partner identity provider connection to stop further unauthorized access.
steps.outcome: No further unauthorized access via the federated identity is possible.

steps.title: Restore defaced content from backup/version history
steps.desc: Revert affected pages to their last known-good version.

steps.title: Re-establish the federated trust only after joint verification with the partner
steps.desc: Restore the SSO/federation link only once both sides confirm the compromise is remediated.

steps.title: Document root cause and review federated identity trust management
steps.desc: Log findings and recommend improvements to how federated/SSO trust relationships with partners are established and monitored.

steps.title: Assess whether the compromised federated trust grants access to other systems
steps.desc: Determine what else the compromised federated identity/trust relationship has access to beyond the defaced platform.
steps.outcome: Full access scope of the compromised federation understood.

steps.title: Coordinate with the partner organization's security team
steps.desc: Notify the partner's security/IT team, particularly if the compromise originated on their identity provider side.
steps.outcome: Partner security team engaged and coordinating.

steps.title: Rotate federation certificates/keys before re-establishing trust
steps.desc: Rotate SAML/OAuth signing certificates or keys used in the federation relationship prior to restoring the connection.

ITID-21435.def: Defacement of a partner-facing platform, not clearly matching a more specific leaf (vendor extranet, developer portal, reseller portal, or compromised federated/SSO access).
ITID-21435.purpose: Catch-all for partner platform defacement cases that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a specific partner-platform leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (ITID-21431 through ITID-21434)
ITID-21435.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Medium-High pending clarification.
ITID-21435.escalation: Reclassify once the specific partner platform and vector are clarified.
indicators: Report of defaced partner-facing content with unclear platform or vector
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Third-party/partner access review and least-privilege enforcement
Partner platform admin account MFA enforcement
Automated content-change alerting
ITID-21435.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-21435.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-21435.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Partner Platform Defacement
playbook.description: General-purpose response for partner platform defacement that does not fit a more specific partner-platform-defacement subtype.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized changes and identify the compromise vector
steps.desc: Determine whether the defacement resulted from compromised admin/CMS access, compromised federated/SSO access, or another path.
steps.abort: If a more specific category is confirmed, redirect to that dedicated playbook.

steps.title: Lock down the compromised access path
steps.desc: Disable the compromised account, restrict admin panel access, or suspend the affected federation link as appropriate.

steps.title: Restore defaced content from backup/version history
steps.desc: Revert affected content to its last known-good version.

steps.title: Confirm with partners that access has been restored safely
steps.desc: Follow up with affected partners to confirm the platform is safe to use again.

steps.title: Document root cause and remediation
steps.desc: Log findings for future prevention.

steps.title: Assess which partner organizations were exposed to the defacement
steps.desc: Determine which external partner organizations have active access and would have seen the defaced content.

steps.title: Notify affected partners of the defacement
steps.desc: Inform affected external partner contacts that the platform was compromised.

steps.title: Reset credentials/rotate keys tied to the compromise
steps.desc: Rotate affected credentials or federation keys before restoring access.

ITID-21511.def: Unauthorized alteration of the marketing or newsletter email template, causing subscribers to receive an email containing unauthorized content.
ITID-21511.purpose: Captures defacement of marketing/newsletter email templates, altering content sent to a broad subscriber list.
scopeIncludes: Injected unauthorized content, links, or imagery into a marketing/newsletter template prior to send
Hijacked send of a legitimate newsletter with altered body content
scopeExcludes: Defacement of transactional email templates (order confirmations, receipts) (ITID-21512)
Compromise of the marketing platform itself as the differentiating access vector (ITID-21514)
ITID-21511.severity: High, given the typically large subscriber distribution list and direct customer/prospect visibility.
ITID-21511.priority: P1 given broad, largely irreversible distribution once sent.
ITID-21511.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT security and marketing leadership; halt any queued or scheduled sends before further distribution.
indicators: Subscriber reports of an unexpected/altered newsletter
Marketing platform template version history showing unauthorized edits
Send logs showing content mismatched to the approved campaign
vectors: Compromised marketing platform user account
Exploited vulnerability in the email template editor
rootCauses: Lack of approval workflow before campaign send
Insufficient access restriction on template editing
controls: Mandatory send-approval workflow for marketing campaigns
MFA on marketing platform accounts
Template version-control and diff review before send
ITID-21511.detection: Marketing platform template version history and pre-send approval logs provide the primary detection signal; subscriber complaints often surface it first.
ITID-21511.response: Halt further sends immediately, issue a correction/retraction communication if already sent broadly, and revert the template.
metrics: Number of recipients who received the defaced email
Time to halt further distribution
ITID-21511.notes: Once sent, an email defacement cannot be recalled the way a webpage can be reverted; response focus is on halting further distribution and correcting the record.

playbook.name: Response: Marketing/Newsletter Email Template Defacement
playbook.description: For tampering with a marketing/newsletter email template that alters its content, branding, or links before or during a send.

steps.title: Capture the tampered template and identify whether it has already been sent
steps.desc: Save a copy of the altered template and check the marketing platform's send history/queue to determine whether any campaign using it has already gone out, is queued, or was caught pre-send.
steps.outcome: Tampered template preserved; send status determined.

steps.title: Pause all queued and scheduled sends immediately
steps.desc: Halt any campaign in the queue that uses the tampered template before it reaches additional recipients.
steps.outcome: No further sends of the tampered template occur.

steps.title: Remove any malicious links/content from the template and close the access vector
steps.desc: Strip the tampered content and address the compromised credential, API key, or integration identified during identification.

steps.title: Restore the template from a known-good version
steps.desc: Restore the template to its last verified legitimate version.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector and one concrete improvement (API key rotation policy, template approval workflow).

steps.title: Determine the access vector used
steps.desc: Review marketing-platform audit logs to determine how the template was altered — compromised user account, exposed API key, or malicious integration.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment using the broadest reasonable lockdown.

steps.title: Rotate marketing-platform credentials and API keys
steps.desc: Reset passwords and revoke/reissue API keys for all accounts and integrations with template-editing access.

steps.title: Notify recipients if the tampered template was already sent
steps.desc: If real recipients already received the tampered email, send a follow-up clarification and coordinate with PR/Comms on messaging, especially if any malicious link was included.

ITID-21512.def: Unauthorized alteration of a transactional email template, causing customers to receive automated notices (order confirmations, receipts, account notices) containing unauthorized content.
ITID-21512.purpose: Captures defacement of transactional email templates (order confirmations, receipts, password resets), which customers rely on as trusted automated notices.
scopeIncludes: Injected unauthorized content or links into an order-confirmation, receipt, or account-notice template
Altered transactional email content that could facilitate phishing under a trusted sender identity
scopeExcludes: Defacement of marketing/newsletter templates (ITID-21511)
A phishing email spoofing the company's brand without altering the actual legitimate transactional template (tracked under a brand-impersonation/phishing ITID elsewhere)
ITID-21512.severity: Critical; transactional emails carry high customer trust, so injected malicious links here have elevated phishing/fraud potential.
ITID-21512.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT security, given the risk that customers may click a malicious link believing it is a routine automated notice.
indicators: Customer reports of an unusual link or content in an order confirmation/receipt
Transactional email template repository showing unauthorized edits
Anomalous click-through rates on transactional email links
vectors: Compromised access to the transactional email template repository or email service provider account
Exploited vulnerability in the transactional email pipeline
rootCauses: Insufficient access restriction on transactional template editing
Lack of change monitoring on the transactional email pipeline
controls: Change-control and approval workflow for transactional email templates
MFA on email service provider accounts
Link/content integrity monitoring on transactional templates
ITID-21512.detection: Template repository change monitoring and click-through anomaly detection on transactional links provide the primary technical signal.
ITID-21512.response: Halt the affected transactional flow immediately, revert the template, and warn customers if a malicious link may already have been sent.
metrics: Number of transactional emails sent with defaced content
Click-through count on any injected malicious link
ITID-21512.notes: Treated as more severe than marketing-template defacement given the elevated customer trust and phishing risk of transactional emails.

playbook.name: Response: Transactional Email Template Defacement
playbook.description: For tampering with a transactional email template (order confirmations, password resets, receipts, account notifications) that alters its content or links.

steps.title: Capture the tampered template and assess send volume/urgency
steps.desc: Save a copy of the altered template. Transactional templates trigger continuously and automatically, so assume active exposure until confirmed otherwise.
steps.guidance: Check send logs for volume already sent with the tampered version.
steps.outcome: Tampered template preserved; send volume/urgency assessed.

steps.title: Disable or roll back the tampered template immediately
steps.desc: Given transactional emails are often security- or account-sensitive (password resets, receipts), prioritize an immediate rollback over investigation.
steps.outcome: Tampered template no longer being sent.

steps.title: Remove any malicious links/content and close the access vector
steps.desc: Strip the tampered content and address the compromised credential, API key, or deployment path identified during identification.

steps.title: Restore the template from a known-good version and verify live sends
steps.desc: Restore the template to its last verified legitimate version and send a test transaction to confirm.
steps.outcome: Template restored and verified clean in production.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector and one concrete improvement (change-control on transactional templates, API key scoping).

steps.title: Determine the access vector used
steps.desc: Review the transactional email service and application logs to determine how the template was altered.
steps.guidance: Check for compromised admin credentials, an exposed API key, or a compromised CI/CD deployment path if templates are code-managed.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment using the broadest reasonable lockdown.

steps.title: Rotate credentials and API keys for the email service
steps.desc: Reset passwords and revoke/reissue API keys for all accounts and integrations with template-editing access.

steps.title: Notify affected customers if a malicious link/content was live, especially for password-reset or payment templates
steps.desc: If a tampered password-reset or payment-related template reached customers, coordinate urgent notification with PR/Comms, Legal, and Customer Support.
steps.outcome: Affected customers notified; support scripts updated.

ITID-21513.def: Unauthorized alteration of the company-standard employee email signature block (logo, tagline, disclaimer, or embedded links), typically pushed centrally via email client policy or a signature-management tool.
ITID-21513.purpose: Captures tampering with the standardized employee email signature block, a smaller-scale but persistent brand-defacement vector.
scopeIncludes: Centrally-pushed signature template altered to include unauthorized content, logo, or links
Signature-management tool compromised to alter signatures across many employees at once
scopeExcludes: An individual employee manually editing their own personal signature outside the centrally-managed template (a policy-violation matter, not a security incident unless malicious)
Defacement of email body templates rather than the signature block (ITID-21511/21512)
ITID-21513.severity: Medium; lower single-message visibility than a mass campaign but persistent across every outbound email until corrected.
ITID-21513.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the altered signature embeds a malicious link distributed across a large volume of outbound mail.
ITID-21513.escalation: Escalate to IT security if the signature-management tool itself was compromised, given the cross-organization blast radius.
indicators: Recipients reporting an unusual link or logo in a received email signature
Signature-management tool admin logs showing unauthorized template changes
vectors: Compromised signature-management tool admin account
Exploited vulnerability in the signature-management platform
rootCauses: Weak access controls on the signature-management tool
Lack of periodic review of the centrally-pushed signature template
controls: MFA on signature-management tool admin accounts
Periodic review/audit of the centrally-pushed signature template
ITID-21513.detection: Signature-management tool audit logs and recipient reports provide the primary detection signal; coverage is generally lighter than for high-volume campaign platforms.
ITID-21513.response: Revert the signature template centrally, force re-push to all employee mail clients, and assess how many outbound emails carried the altered signature.
metrics: Time to revert the signature template across the organization
Estimated volume of outbound email sent with the altered signature
ITID-21513.notes: Distinct from template-body defacement (ITID-21511/21512) by targeting the signature block specifically, typically via the signature-management tool rather than the email/marketing platform.

playbook.name: Response: Employee Email Signature Block Tampering
playbook.description: For tampering with a centrally-managed employee email signature block (e.g. inserting a malicious link, altered branding, or offensive content) that then appears on outgoing employee emails.

steps.title: Capture the tampered signature and identify scope of affected employees
steps.desc: Save the tampered signature content and determine whether it is applied org-wide, by department, or to specific mailboxes via the signature management platform.
steps.outcome: Tampered signature preserved; affected employee scope identified.

steps.title: Disable the centrally-managed signature or revert it immediately
steps.desc: Stop the tampered signature from continuing to append to outgoing employee emails.
steps.outcome: Tampered signature no longer appended to outgoing mail.

steps.title: Close the exploited access vector
steps.desc: Address the compromised credential, plugin vulnerability, or misconfiguration identified during identification.

steps.title: Restore the legitimate signature template
steps.desc: Restore the signature block to its approved, pre-tampering version.
steps.outcome: Legitimate signature restored across affected mailboxes.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector and one concrete improvement (access restriction on the signature platform, change approval process).

steps.title: Determine the access vector used
steps.desc: Review signature-management platform and mail-server admin logs to determine how the signature template was altered.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment using the broadest reasonable lockdown.
steps.tool: Signature platform / mail server audit logs

steps.title: Rotate signature-platform and mail-server admin credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and API keys for accounts with signature-management access.

steps.title: Notify recipients if a malicious link was live, and alert employees
steps.desc: If the tampered signature contained a malicious link and was sent externally, coordinate a notice to likely recipients and inform employees of the incident so they can address any inquiries.
steps.outcome: External recipients and employees informed as appropriate.

ITID-21514.def: Defacement of a company email template achieved through compromise of the marketing automation platform or email service provider (ESP) account used to design and send campaigns, rather than through a mail-server/transport-level compromise.
ITID-21514.purpose: Captures email-template defacement carried out via a compromised marketing platform (e.g. the ESP/marketing-automation tool), where the platform compromise is the differentiating access vector.
scopeIncludes: Compromised ESP/marketing-automation admin or user account used to alter templates or launch unauthorized sends
Exploited vulnerability in the marketing platform's template editor or API
scopeExcludes: Defacement achieved via a compromised mail server or transport rule rather than the marketing platform (ITID-21515)
The underlying marketing-platform account credential compromise itself, tracked under the relevant ITID-12xxx credential-attack leaf where a specific one exists
ITID-21514.severity: High; ESP-level compromise can enable large-scale unauthorized sends beyond a single template edit.
ITID-21514.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT security and the marketing platform vendor to lock down the compromised account/API access and halt any pending sends.
indicators: ESP account activity log showing logins or API calls from unrecognized sources
Unauthorized campaign scheduled or sent from the marketing platform
Marketing team unable to access their own ESP account (locked out by attacker)
vectors: Phished or stuffed ESP account credential
Exploited API key leak granting marketing-platform access
Third-party marketing platform vulnerability
rootCauses: Lack of MFA on ESP/marketing-automation accounts
Overly broad API key permissions for marketing integrations
controls: MFA on ESP/marketing-automation accounts
API key rotation and least-privilege scoping for marketing integrations
Send-approval workflow independent of the ESP account
ITID-21514.detection: ESP account activity logs and API call monitoring provide the primary detection signal.
ITID-21514.response: Lock down or reset the compromised ESP account/API keys, halt pending sends, and audit recent campaign activity for unauthorized changes.
metrics: Time to lock down the compromised ESP account
Number of unauthorized sends completed before containment
ITID-21514.notes: Differentiated from ITID-21515 by the access vector: the marketing/ESP platform account here versus the mail server or transport rule there.

playbook.name: Response: Email Template Defacement via Compromised Marketing Platform
playbook.description: For an email template defacement traced specifically to a compromise of the marketing automation platform account or tenant itself, rather than a single template edit.

steps.title: Confirm platform-level compromise and scope of access
steps.desc: Review the marketing platform's admin/audit console to confirm the attacker gained account or tenant-level access, and determine what else (contact lists, other templates, integrations) they could have touched.
steps.guidance: A compromised platform account is broader than a single template edit — assume all templates and lists are potentially affected until ruled out.
steps.outcome: Full scope of platform-level access confirmed.

steps.title: Pause all queued and scheduled sends across the platform
steps.desc: Halt every campaign in the queue, not just the one using the known-tampered template, given the platform-level compromise.
steps.outcome: No further sends occur pending investigation.

steps.title: Audit and restore every template, list, and automation for tampering
steps.desc: Given platform-level access, review all templates and automations — not just the one publicly noticed — for unauthorized changes.
steps.outcome: All platform content confirmed clean or restored.

steps.title: Restore legitimate templates from known-good versions
steps.desc: Restore any tampered templates identified during the audit.
steps.outcome: All templates restored and verified clean.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend platform-security hardening
steps.desc: Record the root cause and recommend MFA enforcement, SSO review, or third-party app governance for the marketing platform.

steps.title: Determine how the platform account/tenant was compromised
steps.desc: Identify whether the compromise stemmed from credential theft, a missing MFA requirement, a compromised SSO integration, or a third-party app connection.
steps.outcome: Root cause of the platform compromise identified.

steps.title: Rotate all platform credentials, revoke sessions, and remove unauthorized integrations
steps.desc: Reset all admin/user credentials, force logout of active sessions, enforce MFA, and remove any unauthorized third-party app connections.
steps.outcome: Attacker access to the platform fully revoked.

steps.title: Notify recipients of any sent campaigns and coordinate with PR/Comms and Legal
steps.desc: Given the broader compromise, assess whether contact/customer data was also exposed and notify accordingly.
steps.outcome: Affected recipients notified; any required data-exposure disclosures made.

ITID-21515.def: Defacement of company email content achieved through compromise of the mail server infrastructure or the insertion of a malicious mail-transport rule that alters outbound message content in transit, rather than through the marketing/ESP application layer.
ITID-21515.purpose: Captures email-template defacement carried out via a compromised mail server or a malicious transport/mail-flow rule, where infrastructure-level compromise is the differentiating access vector.
scopeIncludes: Malicious transport rule inserted into the mail server/gateway that appends or alters content in outbound email
Compromised on-premises or cloud mail server used to alter message content directly
scopeExcludes: Defacement achieved via a compromised marketing/ESP platform account rather than the mail server/transport layer (ITID-21514)
A transport rule used purely for data exfiltration (e.g. auto-forwarding) with no content-alteration/defacement component (tracked under a data-exfiltration ITID elsewhere)
ITID-21515.severity: Critical; infrastructure-level mail compromise can silently alter all outbound mail across the organization, not just a single campaign.
ITID-21515.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT security and messaging/infrastructure administrators; treat as a potential broader mail-server compromise requiring full forensic review, not just content reversion.
indicators: Unexpected mail-transport rule discovered in the mail gateway/server configuration
Outbound emails across multiple templates/departments showing the same unauthorized inserted content
Mail server admin logs showing unauthorized configuration access
vectors: Compromised mail server/gateway admin credential
Exploited vulnerability in on-premises mail server software
Malicious mailbox/transport rule created via a compromised Exchange/M365 admin account
rootCauses: Unpatched mail server software
Insufficient monitoring of mail-transport rule changes
Overly broad admin access to mail server configuration
mitreTechniques: T1114.003 Email Collection: Email Forwarding Rule
controls: Monitoring/alerting on new or modified mail-transport rules
MFA on mail server/messaging admin accounts
Mail server patch management program
ITID-21515.detection: Mail server/gateway configuration-change monitoring and transport-rule auditing provide strong detection coverage.
ITID-21515.response: Remove the malicious transport rule or contain the compromised mail server immediately, audit all mail sent during the compromise window, and rotate messaging admin credentials.
metrics: Time to detect and remove the malicious transport rule
Volume of outbound mail affected during the compromise window
ITID-21515.notes: Differentiated from ITID-21514 by targeting mail server/transport infrastructure rather than the marketing/ESP application layer; treat as the more severe sibling given the organization-wide blast radius.

playbook.name: Response: Email Template Defacement via Compromised Mail Server/Transport Rule
playbook.description: For an email template or content defacement traced to a compromise of the mail server itself or a malicious mail transport/routing rule (e.g. a hidden rule that injects content into outgoing mail).

steps.title: Identify the malicious transport rule or mail server modification
steps.desc: Review mail server/tenant transport rules, connectors, and server configuration for an unauthorized rule injecting or altering content in outgoing mail.
steps.guidance: Malicious transport rules are often hidden deep in admin consoles and configured to auto-delete evidence of forwarded mail; check rule creation/modification timestamps against known-good baselines.
steps.outcome: Malicious rule or configuration change identified.

steps.title: Disable or delete the malicious transport rule immediately
steps.desc: Remove the rule so outgoing mail is no longer altered.
steps.outcome: Outgoing mail no longer tampered with.

steps.title: Audit all transport rules, connectors, and mailbox delegations for additional tampering
steps.desc: An attacker with mail-server admin access may have created multiple rules or delegate/forwarding rules; check broadly, not just for the one already found.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean, or additional malicious configuration found and removed.

steps.title: Restore legitimate templates/content and verify outgoing mail integrity
steps.desc: Restore any tampered templates and send test messages to confirm mail is no longer altered in transit.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend mail-server hardening
steps.desc: Record the access vector and recommend admin-access restriction, transport-rule change alerting, and periodic rule audits.

steps.title: Determine how mail-server admin access was obtained
steps.desc: Review admin account activity and authentication logs to determine how the attacker gained mail-server or tenant-admin access.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment using the broadest reasonable lockdown.
steps.tool: Mail server / identity provider audit logs

steps.title: Rotate mail-server/tenant admin credentials and enforce MFA
steps.desc: Reset all admin credentials with mail-server/tenant configuration access and enforce MFA if not already required.

steps.title: Notify recipients who received tampered mail and coordinate with PR/Comms and Legal
steps.desc: Determine the window during which the rule was active and notify affected recipients accordingly.
steps.outcome: Affected recipients notified; consistent messaging issued.

ITID-21516.def: Defacement of a company email template, not clearly matching a more specific leaf (marketing/newsletter, transactional, signature block, compromised marketing platform, or compromised mail server/transport rule).
ITID-21516.purpose: Catch-all for company email template defacement cases that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a specific email-template leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (ITID-21511 through ITID-21515)
ITID-21516.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Medium-High pending clarification given email's broad reach.
ITID-21516.escalation: Reclassify once the specific email surface and vector are clarified.
indicators: Report of defaced email content with unclear template or vector
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Email platform admin account MFA enforcement
Template change approval workflow
Version control and rollback for email templates
ITID-21516.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-21516.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-21516.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Company Email Template Defacement
playbook.description: Catch-all response for email template tampering that does not clearly fit the marketing, transactional, signature, marketing-platform-compromise, or mail-server-compromise categories.

steps.title: Capture the tampered content and identify whether it has already been sent
steps.desc: Save a copy of the altered template/content and check send history to determine exposure.
steps.outcome: Tampered content preserved; send status determined.

steps.title: Pause or disable the tampered content immediately
steps.desc: Stop any further sends or exposure of the tampered content.
steps.outcome: Tampered content no longer being sent or displayed.

steps.title: Close the exploited access vector
steps.desc: Address the compromised credential, vulnerability, or misconfiguration identified during identification.

steps.title: Restore the legitimate content from a known-good version
steps.desc: Restore the template/content to its approved, pre-tampering version.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector and one concrete improvement, and note whether a more specific ITID category should have been used.

steps.title: Determine the access vector used
steps.desc: Review the relevant platform's audit logs to determine how the content was altered.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment using the broadest reasonable lockdown.

steps.title: Rotate relevant platform credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and API keys for accounts with editing access.

steps.title: Notify recipients if the tampered content was already sent
steps.desc: If real recipients already received the tampered content, coordinate a notification with PR/Comms.

ITID-21521.def: Unauthorized deployment or manipulation of an automated chatbot or workflow bot within an internal messaging platform to post unauthorized content into channels.
ITID-21521.purpose: Captures tampering via a malicious or rogue chatbot/workflow bot operating within an internal messaging platform (e.g. Slack/Teams).
scopeIncludes: A rogue bot posting unauthorized content, links, or announcements into messaging channels
A legitimate workflow bot's configuration altered to post unauthorized content
scopeExcludes: Tampering achieved via a compromised channel/workspace admin account directly (not through a bot) (ITID-21522)
Tampering via a malicious third-party app/integration that is not itself a chatbot/workflow-bot construct (ITID-21523)
ITID-21521.severity: Medium-High; bots can post to many channels simultaneously and may appear more automated/trustworthy to employees.
ITID-21521.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the bot is used to distribute phishing links or malware internally.
ITID-21521.escalation: Escalate to IT security immediately to disable the rogue bot's access token; warn employees in affected channels not to interact with its messages.
indicators: Unrecognized bot posting messages in multiple channels
Workflow bot behaving outside its documented configuration
Employee reports of a suspicious automated message
vectors: Malicious bot installed via a compromised workspace admin token
Exploited workflow-automation misconfiguration allowing unauthorized bot posting
rootCauses: Insufficient review/approval process for bot installations
Overly broad bot API scopes/permissions
controls: App/bot installation approval workflow for the messaging platform
Least-privilege API scoping for bots and workflow automations
Periodic audit of installed bots/integrations
ITID-21521.detection: Messaging platform admin console app/bot inventory and audit logs provide the primary detection signal.
ITID-21521.response: Revoke the bot's access token/permissions immediately, remove its posted content, and audit how it was installed.
metrics: Time to disable the rogue bot
Number of channels/messages affected
ITID-21521.notes: Scoped to bot/automation-driven posting specifically, distinct from direct admin-account or third-party-app compromise siblings.

playbook.name: Response: Malicious/Rogue Chatbot or Workflow Bot Tampering
playbook.description: For tampering that turns a legitimate internal chatbot or workflow automation bot malicious — posting false content, phishing links, or unauthorized actions into internal messaging channels.

steps.title: Capture the bot's malicious output and identify affected channels
steps.desc: Save examples of the malicious messages/actions and identify every channel or workspace the bot posted to.
steps.outcome: Malicious output captured; affected channels identified.

steps.title: Disable or remove the bot's access immediately
steps.desc: Revoke the bot's API token/webhook and remove it from all channels to stop further malicious activity.
steps.outcome: Bot no longer able to post or act.

steps.title: Remediate the bot's code, configuration, or hosting compromise
steps.desc: Fix the vulnerability or credential leak that allowed the bot to be tampered with before reinstating it.

steps.title: Delete or correct malicious messages and re-enable the bot only after verification
steps.desc: Clean up the malicious posts across affected channels and restore the bot to service only once confirmed safe.
steps.outcome: Channels cleaned; bot verified safe before re-enabling.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector and one concrete improvement (bot token rotation policy, least-privilege scoping, code review process).

steps.title: Determine how the bot was compromised or reconfigured
steps.desc: Review the bot's integration settings, API tokens, and hosting environment (if self-hosted) to determine how it was tampered with.
steps.guidance: Check for a leaked bot token, compromised webhook, or malicious update to the bot's own codebase/workflow definition.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment by disabling the bot outright.

steps.title: Rotate any credentials or tokens the bot had access to
steps.desc: Reset the bot's own credentials and any downstream systems/tokens it had permission to use.

steps.title: Alert employees who may have interacted with the malicious bot messages
steps.desc: If the bot posted phishing links or false instructions, notify affected employees and advise on any action needed (e.g. password reset if they clicked a link).

ITID-21522.def: Unauthorized posting or content manipulation within an internal messaging platform performed by an attacker who has compromised a channel or workspace administrator account.
ITID-21522.purpose: Captures tampering achieved via a compromised channel or workspace administrator account with broad content/configuration control over the internal messaging platform.
scopeIncludes: Compromised workspace-admin account used to post unauthorized content across multiple channels
Compromised channel-owner/moderator account used to alter pinned content or channel settings
scopeExcludes: Tampering carried out by a rogue bot/workflow automation rather than a human admin account (ITID-21521)
The underlying admin-credential compromise mechanics, tracked under the relevant ITID-12xxx credential-attack leaf
ITID-21522.severity: High; workspace-admin-level compromise can affect the entire messaging platform, not a single channel.
ITID-21522.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT security to revoke the compromised admin session and force a password/MFA reset.
indicators: Admin console showing configuration changes or postings not attributable to the legitimate admin's normal behavior
Login to the admin account from an unusual location/device immediately before the tampering
Multiple channels affected simultaneously, consistent with workspace-wide admin access
vectors: Phished or stuffed workspace-admin credential
Session token theft against a workspace-admin account
rootCauses: Lack of MFA on workspace/channel-admin accounts
Insufficient anomaly detection on admin-console activity
controls: MFA on workspace/channel-admin accounts
UEBA/anomaly detection on admin-console activity
Immediate session-revocation procedure upon suspected compromise
ITID-21522.detection: Messaging platform admin audit logs correlated with identity/authentication logs give strong detection.
ITID-21522.response: Revoke the compromised admin session/credential, revert unauthorized content/configuration changes, and investigate the compromise's root cause.
metrics: Time from anomalous admin activity to session revocation
Number of channels affected
detections: Messaging platform admin audit-log correlation with authentication logs
ITID-21522.notes: This leaf is scoped strictly to the tampering act and its impact; the underlying credential-compromise technique is tracked under its own ITID-12xxx leaf to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Compromised Channel/Workspace Admin Tampering
playbook.description: For internal messaging platform tampering carried out through a compromised channel or workspace administrator account.

steps.title: Confirm admin-level compromise and scope of actions taken
steps.desc: Review the messaging platform's admin audit log to confirm the account acted with admin privileges and catalog every change made (channel settings, member additions, integrations, deleted messages).
steps.guidance: An admin-level compromise can touch far more than the visible tampering — assume broad impact until ruled out.
steps.outcome: Full scope of admin actions confirmed.

steps.title: Suspend the compromised admin account and force logout of all sessions
steps.desc: Immediately disable the account and terminate any active sessions to stop further tampering.
steps.outcome: Attacker access via the admin account revoked.

steps.title: Audit and reverse all unauthorized admin actions
steps.desc: Review and undo every unauthorized change made during the compromise window — restored deleted content, removed rogue integrations/members added by the attacker.

steps.title: Restore tampered channels/content to their legitimate state
steps.desc: Restore pinned messages, channel topics, or content altered during the compromise.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend admin-access hardening
steps.desc: Record the root cause and recommend MFA enforcement, admin-role restriction, or session-monitoring improvements.

steps.title: Determine how the admin account was compromised
steps.desc: Review authentication logs to determine whether credential theft, missing MFA, or a compromised SSO session was the cause.
steps.outcome: Root cause of the account compromise identified.

steps.title: Rotate the admin's credentials and enforce MFA
steps.desc: Reset the account's password and enforce MFA before restoring access to the legitimate user.

steps.title: Notify affected employees of the incident
steps.desc: Inform employees in affected channels of the tampering and any action they should take (e.g. disregard false instructions posted).

ITID-21523.def: Unauthorized posting or content manipulation within an internal messaging platform performed through a malicious or compromised third-party application/integration granted access to the workspace.
ITID-21523.purpose: Captures tampering via a malicious or compromised third-party application/integration connected to the internal messaging platform.
scopeIncludes: A malicious third-party integration (installed via a supply-chain-compromised vendor app or a deceptive OAuth grant) posting unauthorized content
A legitimate third-party integration compromised at the vendor's end and used to post unauthorized content into the workspace
scopeExcludes: Tampering via a first-party/internally-built bot or workflow automation (ITID-21521)
Tampering via a directly compromised workspace-admin account rather than a third-party app grant (ITID-21522)
ITID-21523.severity: Medium-High; scope of impact depends on the third-party app's granted permissions and channel reach.
ITID-21523.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the app has broad workspace-wide posting/read permissions.
ITID-21523.escalation: Escalate to IT security immediately to revoke the third-party app's OAuth grant; notify the vendor if their platform was the compromised origin.
indicators: Unrecognized or newly-granted third-party app posting unauthorized content
Vendor security advisory indicating their integration/platform was compromised
Employee reports of a suspicious message attributed to a known integration
vectors: Supply-chain compromise of a third-party messaging integration/vendor
Deceptive OAuth consent grant (consent phishing) approved by an employee
rootCauses: Insufficient review of third-party app OAuth permission scopes before approval
Lack of periodic audit of connected third-party integrations
controls: Third-party app/integration approval and OAuth scope review process
Periodic audit of connected integrations and their permissions
Rapid OAuth-grant revocation procedure
ITID-21523.detection: Messaging platform integration audit logs and vendor security advisories provide the primary detection signal.
ITID-21523.response: Revoke the third-party app's access immediately, remove its posted content, and assess whether the compromise originated at the vendor or via a phished consent grant.
metrics: Time to revoke the compromised integration's access
Number of channels/messages affected
ITID-21523.notes: Scoped to third-party app/integration-driven tampering specifically, distinct from first-party bots and directly compromised admin accounts.

playbook.name: Response: Malicious Third-Party App/Integration Tampering
playbook.description: For internal messaging platform tampering carried out by a malicious or compromised third-party app/integration connected to the workspace.

steps.title: Identify the malicious app/integration and its granted permissions
steps.desc: Review the workspace's installed apps/integrations list to identify which one is responsible, and what scopes/permissions it was granted.
steps.guidance: Check install date and permission scope against what the app should legitimately need — an over-permissioned app is a common red flag.
steps.outcome: Malicious app identified; its permission scope understood.

steps.title: Remove/uninstall the malicious app and revoke its tokens immediately
steps.desc: Disconnect the app from the workspace and revoke any OAuth tokens or API keys it holds.

steps.title: Audit for other malicious or over-permissioned apps in the workspace
steps.desc: Review the full list of installed apps/integrations for others that may also be malicious or unnecessarily over-permissioned.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean, or additional risky apps found and removed.

steps.title: Restore any tampered content and re-establish an app allowlist
steps.desc: Clean up any tampered messages/channels and put an approval process in place for future third-party app installs.
steps.outcome: Channels restored; app-install governance in place.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend app-governance hardening
steps.desc: Record the root cause and recommend an app allowlist, permission-review cadence, or install-approval workflow.

steps.title: Determine how the app came to be installed or compromised
steps.desc: Determine whether the app was maliciously installed by a compromised user, was a legitimate app later compromised at the vendor, or was a supply-chain issue.

steps.title: Rotate credentials for any account that installed or authorized the app
steps.desc: Reset credentials for the user(s) involved in the app's installation in case their account was itself compromised.

steps.title: Notify affected employees of the incident
steps.desc: Inform employees in affected channels of the tampering and any recommended action.

ITID-21524.def: Unauthorized alteration of a pinned message or content posted into a designated company-wide announcement channel within the internal messaging platform.
ITID-21524.purpose: Captures tampering specifically with pinned messages or dedicated company-wide announcement channels, which carry outsized visibility relative to a single ordinary message.
scopeIncludes: Unauthorized editing or replacement of a pinned message in a widely-followed channel
Unauthorized post injected into a designated all-staff announcement channel
scopeExcludes: Tampering in an ordinary, non-pinned/non-announcement channel (tracked under the relevant access-vector sibling, e.g. ITID-21521/21522/21523)
ITID-21524.severity: Medium-High; the pinned/announcement designation implies broad, sustained employee visibility beyond a normal message.
ITID-21524.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the altered pinned/announcement content spreads false urgent instructions.
ITID-21524.escalation: Escalate to IT security and internal communications immediately; issue a correction in the same channel once reverted.
indicators: Pinned message content changed without a corresponding legitimate update
Unexpected post in the all-staff announcement channel
Employee reports questioning the authenticity of an announcement
vectors: Compromised account with pin/announcement-channel posting rights
Rogue bot or third-party app with permission to post in the announcement channel
rootCauses: Overly broad posting permissions on the announcement channel
Lack of change monitoring on pinned messages
controls: Restricted posting permissions on designated announcement channels
Change monitoring/alerting on pinned-message edits
ITID-21524.detection: Messaging platform channel-activity logs and pinned-message change history provide the primary detection signal; employee reports are often the first indicator given high visibility.
ITID-21524.response: Revert the pinned/announcement content immediately and post a correction; identify and remediate how posting access was obtained.
metrics: Time to revert pinned/announcement content
Estimated employee reach before correction
ITID-21524.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves by the high-visibility channel/pin context rather than the specific access vector, which should be cross-referenced to the relevant access-vector sibling when known.

playbook.name: Response: Pinned Message/Announcement Channel Tampering
playbook.description: For tampering with a pinned message or a company-wide announcement channel in the internal messaging platform, inserting false or malicious content that many employees will see.

steps.title: Capture the tampered pinned message/announcement
steps.desc: Save the tampered content and note how widely the channel is followed (company-wide vs. team-level).
steps.outcome: Tampered content preserved; audience scope identified.

steps.title: Remove or unpin the tampered content immediately
steps.desc: Given the high visibility of pinned/announcement content, prioritize immediate removal over investigation.

steps.title: Close the exploited access vector
steps.desc: Address the compromised credential or permission misconfiguration identified during identification.

steps.title: Restore the legitimate pinned message/announcement
steps.desc: Repost the correct, approved content.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector and recommend restricting announcement-channel posting rights and enabling change alerts.

steps.title: Determine the access vector used
steps.desc: Review messaging platform audit logs to determine which account made the change and how it gained the necessary permission.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment by removing the content and restricting posting rights.

steps.title: Rotate the compromised account's credentials and restrict channel-posting rights
steps.desc: Reset the compromised account's credentials and temporarily restrict who can post/pin in the announcement channel.
steps.outcome: Old credentials invalidated; posting rights restricted.

steps.title: Send a correction to employees who saw the tampered content
steps.desc: Given the broad visibility of announcement channels, proactively clarify that the prior post was fraudulent and should be disregarded.

ITID-21525.def: Unauthorized content manipulation within an internal messaging platform, not clearly matching a more specific leaf (rogue bot, compromised admin, malicious third-party app, or pinned/announcement channel).
ITID-21525.purpose: Catch-all for internal messaging platform tampering cases that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a specific messaging-tampering leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (ITID-21521 through ITID-21524)
ITID-21525.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Medium pending clarification.
ITID-21525.escalation: Reclassify once the specific access vector is clarified.
indicators: Report of unauthorized messaging platform content with unclear vector
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Messaging platform admin account MFA enforcement
Admin action audit logging with alerting
Least-privilege role assignment for platform administrators
ITID-21525.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-21525.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-21525.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Internal Messaging Platform Tampering
playbook.description: Catch-all response for internal messaging platform tampering that does not clearly fit the rogue-bot, compromised-admin, malicious-app, or pinned-announcement categories.

steps.title: Capture the tampered content and identify affected channels
steps.desc: Save examples of the tampered content and identify every channel or workspace it appeared in.
steps.outcome: Tampered content preserved; affected channels identified.

steps.title: Remove the tampered content and restrict further access
steps.desc: Delete or hide the tampered content and restrict posting/admin rights pending investigation.

steps.title: Close the exploited access vector
steps.desc: Address the compromised credential, app, or misconfiguration identified during identification.

steps.title: Restore legitimate content
steps.desc: Restore any deleted or altered content to its legitimate state.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector and one concrete improvement, and note whether a more specific ITID category should have been used.

steps.title: Determine the access vector used
steps.desc: Review messaging platform audit logs to determine how the tampering occurred.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment using the broadest reasonable lockdown.

steps.title: Rotate relevant credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords and revoke tokens for any account or integration implicated.

steps.title: Notify affected employees if the tampering was widely visible
steps.desc: Inform employees of the incident and any action they should take.

ITID-21611.def: Unauthorized alteration of content displayed on a digital billboard, achieved by compromising the ad network or CMS platform used to schedule and push that content, rather than through direct physical access to the billboard hardware.
ITID-21611.purpose: Captures defacement of a company-owned or company-controlled digital billboard achieved through the ad network or content-management system that schedules its display content.
scopeIncludes: Compromised ad-network/CMS account used to push unauthorized creative to the billboard
Exploited vulnerability in the ad-serving/CMS platform enabling unauthorized content scheduling
scopeExcludes: Defacement via direct physical console/local access to the billboard hardware (ITID-21612)
Defacement via a compromised remote management software layer distinct from the ad-serving CMS itself (ITID-21613)
ITID-21611.severity: High; public digital billboards carry maximum public visibility and can be captured/shared widely on social media within minutes.
ITID-21611.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT security, the outdoor-advertising vendor (if third-party operated), and communications/PR given public exposure risk.
indicators: Ad network/CMS scheduling log showing unauthorized content pushed
Public reports/photos of the defaced billboard circulating on social media
Billboard displaying content outside the approved creative rotation
vectors: Compromised ad-network/CMS admin credential
Exploited vulnerability in the ad-serving platform
rootCauses: Lack of MFA on ad-network/CMS accounts
Unpatched ad-serving platform software
controls: MFA on ad-network/CMS accounts
Content-approval workflow before billboard content goes live
Patch management for the ad-serving platform
ITID-21611.detection: Ad-network/CMS scheduling logs and public social-media/brand monitoring provide the primary detection signal.
ITID-21611.response: Pull the unauthorized content from rotation immediately, revert to approved creative, and coordinate a public statement if the defacement was widely observed/photographed.
metrics: Time to remove unauthorized content from the billboard rotation
Estimated public exposure duration
detections: Social/brand monitoring for billboard defacement photos
ITID-21611.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves by the ad-network/CMS access vector rather than direct physical console access or a separate remote-management layer.

playbook.name: Response: Digital Billboard Defacement via Compromised Ad Network/CMS
playbook.description: For a digital billboard displaying unauthorized content due to compromise of the ad network or content-management platform that feeds it.

steps.title: Capture the unauthorized content and confirm the delivery source
steps.desc: Photograph/record the billboard's unauthorized display and confirm whether the content originated from the ad network's creative pipeline or the billboard operator's CMS.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized content documented; delivery source confirmed.

steps.title: Pull the billboard offline or switch to a default/safe creative
steps.desc: Contact the ad network/billboard operator to immediately stop the unauthorized content from displaying.

steps.title: Close the exploited access vector
steps.desc: Work with the ad network/billboard vendor to remediate the compromised account or API vulnerability.

steps.title: Restore the approved creative content
steps.desc: Confirm the billboard is displaying only approved, verified content.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend a hardening improvement
steps.desc: Record the access vector and one concrete improvement (vendor access review, creative-approval workflow).

steps.title: Determine the access vector within the ad network/CMS
steps.desc: Review ad-network/CMS audit logs to determine how the unauthorized creative was uploaded or scheduled — compromised account, exposed API, or malicious ad-slot bidder.
steps.abort: If the vector can't be determined quickly, proceed to containment by pulling the billboard offline via the vendor.

steps.title: Rotate ad-network/CMS credentials and revoke unauthorized API access
steps.desc: Reset credentials and API keys for accounts with creative-upload or scheduling access.

steps.title: Coordinate a public statement with PR/Comms if the display was widely seen
steps.desc: Given the physical, public-facing nature of a billboard, assess whether a public acknowledgment is warranted.

ITID-21612.def: Unauthorized alteration of digital billboard content achieved by physically accessing the billboard's local control console, media player, or hardware interface on-site.
ITID-21612.purpose: Captures defacement of a digital billboard achieved through direct physical access to its local console or hardware, rather than a remote network compromise.
scopeIncludes: Unauthorized physical access to the billboard's local media player or control panel used to change displayed content
Physical insertion of unauthorized media (e.g. USB drive) into the billboard's local hardware
scopeExcludes: Defacement achieved remotely via the ad-network/CMS (ITID-21611)
Defacement achieved via a compromised remote management software layer without physical presence (ITID-21613)
ITID-21612.severity: High; requires physical proximity, indicating either an insider or an on-site trespasser, and carries the same public-visibility impact as the remote variants.
ITID-21612.priority: P1, with parallel physical-security investigation given the on-site access.
ITID-21612.escalation: Escalate to both IT security and physical security immediately; review site access logs and CCTV footage for the affected location.
indicators: Billboard displaying unauthorized content with no corresponding remote scheduling change
Evidence of physical tampering with the billboard's control cabinet/enclosure
CCTV or access-log record of an unauthorized individual at the billboard site
vectors: Unsecured or poorly locked billboard control cabinet
Insider or trespasser physically accessing the local media player
rootCauses: Insufficient physical security/locking mechanisms on billboard control cabinets
Lack of site access monitoring near unattended billboard installations
controls: Physical locks/tamper-evident enclosures on billboard control cabinets
Site access monitoring and CCTV coverage for unattended billboard installations
ITID-21612.detection: Physical tamper evidence and site CCTV/access logs are the primary detection signal; the ad-network/CMS logs will show no corresponding legitimate change, helping confirm the physical-access vector.
ITID-21612.response: Secure the site, restore approved content, and coordinate with physical security to identify how access was gained.
metrics: Time to detect and restore approved content
Number of physical-access defacement incidents per site per year
ITID-21612.notes: Differentiated from ITID-21611/21613 by the physical, on-site access vector rather than a remote network compromise.

playbook.name: Response: Digital Billboard Defacement via Physical Console/Local Access
playbook.description: For a digital billboard defaced via direct physical access to its on-site control console or local hardware, rather than a remote/network compromise.

steps.title: Capture the unauthorized content and secure the physical site
steps.desc: Photograph/record the unauthorized display and, working with physical security, secure the billboard's control cabinet/console to prevent further tampering and preserve evidence (e.g. forced locks, unfamiliar devices).
steps.guidance: This is a physical security incident as much as a technical one — coordinate with Facilities/Physical Security immediately.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized content documented; physical site secured.

steps.title: Restore physical access controls and pull the display offline
steps.desc: Re-secure or replace compromised locks/access mechanisms and take the display offline or to a default/safe state.
steps.outcome: Physical access re-secured; unauthorized content no longer displaying.

steps.title: Inspect hardware for tampering or rogue devices
steps.desc: Check for any unauthorized device connected to the console (USB drive, rogue network device) that could enable repeat access.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean, or rogue hardware found and removed.

steps.title: Restore the approved creative content
steps.desc: Confirm the billboard is displaying only approved, verified content.

steps.title: Document the incident and recommend physical-security hardening
steps.desc: Record how physical access was gained and recommend improved locks, access logging, or camera coverage at the site.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and shared with Facilities/Physical Security.

steps.title: Review physical access logs and site camera footage
steps.desc: Determine who accessed the billboard's control cabinet/location and when, using badge logs and CCTV if available.
steps.outcome: Access window and, where possible, the individual(s) responsible identified.
steps.abort: If access cannot be attributed, treat as an unknown-actor physical intrusion and proceed to containment.

steps.title: Rotate any console/local-account credentials
steps.desc: Reset any local login credentials on the console/hardware in case they were also captured during the physical access.

steps.title: Coordinate a public statement with PR/Comms if the display was widely seen
steps.desc: Given the physical, public-facing nature of a billboard, assess whether a public acknowledgment is warranted.

ITID-21613.def: Unauthorized alteration of digital billboard content achieved by compromising the remote device-management/fleet-management software used to administer and push updates to networked billboard hardware.
ITID-21613.purpose: Captures defacement of a digital billboard achieved through compromise of a dedicated remote management software layer used to administer the billboard fleet, distinct from the ad-serving CMS itself.
scopeIncludes: Compromised remote fleet-management platform account used to push unauthorized content or firmware to billboards
Exploited vulnerability in the remote management software agent running on billboard hardware
scopeExcludes: Defacement via the ad-network/CMS platform that schedules creative content (ITID-21611)
Defacement via direct physical/local access to the billboard hardware (ITID-21612)
ITID-21613.severity: High; fleet-management-level compromise can affect multiple billboards simultaneously across a wide geographic footprint.
ITID-21613.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT security and the remote-management software vendor; consider isolating the fleet-management platform from the billboard network if compromise is confirmed.
indicators: Fleet-management platform showing unauthorized configuration or content-push actions
Multiple billboards defaced simultaneously across different locations
Remote-management vendor security advisory indicating a platform compromise
