steps.desc: Review the site's branding, product catalog, and checkout flow to confirm impersonation.

steps.title: File an abuse report with the hosting provider and registrar
steps.desc: Submit a brand-impersonation and fraud takedown request.

steps.title: Confirm the site is taken down
steps.desc: Follow up until the site is confirmed offline.

steps.title: Support customers who paid on the fake storefront
steps.desc: Direct affected customers to dispute the charge with their card issuer.
steps.outcome: Affected customers supported in recovering funds.

steps.title: Document the campaign and evaluate whether it fits an existing category going forward
steps.desc: Record the site's characteristics to sharpen future detection and categorization.

steps.title: Identify the hosting provider, registrar, and payment processor
steps.desc: Determine where the site is hosted, where its domain is registered, and identify any payment gateway used at checkout.
steps.outcome: Hosting, registrar, and payment processor identified.

steps.title: Report the site to its payment processor
steps.desc: If identifiable, file a fraud/brand-abuse report with the payment processor.
steps.outcome: Payment processor notified; merchant account flagged.

ITID-22211.def: A domain-registration-level finding: a lookalike domain differing from our real domain by a common typographical error (e.g., transposed, missing, or doubled letters), registered by a third party, regardless of whether it is yet hosting active content.
ITID-22211.purpose: Captures registration of a domain that misspells our brand name (a common typo variant) for use in future phishing infrastructure.
scopeIncludes: A newly registered domain differing from ours by one common typo pattern
Passive/parked typo domains discovered via proactive domain monitoring, prior to any live phishing content
scopeExcludes: The deployed phishing website content itself once the domain is weaponized (see the relevant Fake Websites leaf, e.g. ITID-22111-22115, for the content-level incident)
ITID-22211.severity: Medium — infrastructure-level risk prior to confirmed weaponization; escalates sharply once MX records or live content appear.
ITID-22211.priority: P3 while parked/passive; P1 if MX records or live phishing content are detected.
ITID-22211.escalation: Escalate immediately if the domain acquires mail exchange (MX) records, indicating readiness for email-based BEC/phishing use.
indicators: New domain registration matching a known typo pattern of our domain
WHOIS/registration data showing privacy-shielded registrant with no legitimate business tie
vectors: Automated bulk registration of typo-variant domains ahead of a campaign
rootCauses: Low cost of domain registration enables speculative/preparatory acquisition
controls: Proactive domain/typosquat monitoring service
Defensive registration of high-risk typo variants
ITID-22211.detection: Strong — domain-monitoring feeds reliably surface new registrations matching known typo patterns.
ITID-22211.response: Log, monitor for MX/hosting changes, and pursue takedown or defensive acquisition per brand protection policy.
metrics: Count of new typosquat registrations detected per month
Percentage proactively acquired/blocked before weaponization
ITID-22211.notes: Scoped to the domain-registration/infrastructure layer, distinct from the Fake Websites category which tracks the deployed content once the domain is weaponized.

playbook.name: Response: Typosquat Domain (Common Misspelling)
playbook.description: For a domain registered as a common misspelling of this organization's own domain, used or positioned for phishing/brand abuse.

steps.title: Determine how the domain was discovered
steps.desc: Establish whether the domain was caught proactively by the domain/brand-monitoring program or reported reactively after a victim encountered it, and confirm it is a genuine typosquat of this organization's domain.
steps.outcome: Discovery channel documented and typosquat confirmed.

steps.title: File a takedown/UDRP-track report with the registrar
steps.desc: Submit an abuse or trademark-infringement report to the registrar; for a persistent squatter, initiate a UDRP or equivalent domain-dispute proceeding.

steps.title: Confirm the domain is taken down, suspended, or transferred
steps.desc: Follow up until the registrar action or dispute resolution results in the domain no longer being usable against this organization.
steps.outcome: Domain suspended, transferred, or content removed.

steps.title: Consider defensive registration of close variants
steps.desc: Evaluate whether closely related misspellings should be defensively registered to prevent recurrence.

steps.title: Document the domain pattern and tune monitoring rules
steps.desc: Record the misspelling pattern and registrar used to sharpen the domain-monitoring program's detection rules.

steps.title: Assess current weaponization state
steps.desc: Check whether the domain currently resolves to a live phishing/malware site, parks with ads, or sits dormant with no active content, and identify the registrar.

steps.title: Submit to browser/security-vendor blocklists if actively hosting phishing content
steps.desc: If the domain is live with phishing content, report it to Google Safe Browsing and relevant threat-intel feeds.
steps.outcome: URL flagged as unsafe if applicable.

ITID-22212.def: A domain-registration-level finding: a lookalike domain that embeds our full brand name alongside an added word (e.g., '-support', '-secure', '-login') or hyphenation, registered by a third party.
ITID-22212.purpose: Captures registration of a domain combining our brand name with an extra word or hyphen (combosquatting) for use in future phishing infrastructure.
scopeIncludes: A domain combining our exact brand string with a generic suffix/prefix word
Hyphenated variants of our brand name registered by unrelated third parties
scopeExcludes: The deployed phishing website content itself once weaponized (see relevant Fake Websites leaf)
ITID-22212.priority: P3 while parked; P1 if MX records or live content appear.
ITID-22212.escalation: Escalate immediately upon MX record or hosting activation.
indicators: New registration combining our exact brand string with a suggestive word (e.g., 'secure', 'billing', 'support')
vectors: Bulk registration of brand+keyword combinations ahead of a targeted campaign
rootCauses: Low cost of registration; combosquat domains often read as more 'legitimate' than pure typos to victims
controls: Proactive domain/combosquat monitoring service
Defensive registration policy for high-risk variants
ITID-22212.detection: Strong — domain monitoring reliably surfaces combosquat registrations containing our exact brand string.
ITID-22212.response: Log, monitor, and pursue takedown/defensive acquisition per policy.
metrics: Count of new combosquat registrations detected per month
ITID-22212.notes: Differentiated from ITID-22211 by mechanism: exact brand string plus an added word/hyphen, versus a misspelling of the brand string itself.

playbook.name: Response: Combosquat Domain (Brand + Extra Word/Hyphen)

steps.outcome: Discovery channel documented and combosquat confirmed.

steps.title: File a takedown report with the registrar and hosting provider

steps.title: Confirm the domain is taken down or suspended
steps.desc: Follow up until the registrar/hosting action results in the domain no longer being usable against this organization.

steps.title: Consider defensive registration of related combosquat variants
steps.desc: Evaluate whether frequently observed word/hyphen combinations should be defensively registered.

steps.title: Document the pattern and tune monitoring rules
steps.desc: Record the word/hyphen pattern to sharpen the domain-monitoring program's detection rules.

steps.title: Assess current weaponization state
steps.desc: Check whether the domain currently resolves to a live phishing/malware site, parks with ads, or sits dormant, and identify the registrar and hosting provider.
steps.outcome: Weaponization state, registrar, and hosting identified.

steps.title: Submit to browser/security-vendor blocklists if actively hosting phishing content
steps.desc: If the domain is live with phishing content, report it to Google Safe Browsing and relevant threat-intel feeds.
steps.outcome: URL flagged as unsafe if applicable.

ITID-22213.def: A domain-registration-level finding: our exact brand string registered under a different TLD or ccTLD than our official domain, by a third party.
ITID-22213.purpose: Captures registration of our exact brand domain name under a different top-level or country-code domain.
scopeIncludes: Our exact domain name registered under an unrelated TLD/ccTLD
Regional ccTLD registrations in markets where we have no presence, used to target local customers
scopeExcludes: Our own legitimately registered regional/ccTLD domains
ITID-22213.priority: P3 while parked; P1 if MX records or live content appear.
ITID-22213.escalation: Escalate immediately upon MX record or hosting activation, and where the ccTLD suggests targeting of a specific regional customer base.
indicators: Our exact brand string registered under a TLD/ccTLD we do not use
vectors: Regional-market targeting via ccTLD registration in a country where we have customers but no defensive registration
rootCauses: Incomplete defensive TLD/ccTLD registration coverage for our brand
controls: Proactive domain/TLD monitoring service
Defensive TLD/ccTLD registration program
ITID-22213.detection: Strong — TLD/ccTLD monitoring reliably surfaces exact-brand registrations under other TLDs.
ITID-22213.response: Log, monitor, and pursue takedown/defensive acquisition, prioritizing regions with active customer bases.
metrics: Count of TLD/ccTLD swap registrations detected per month
Defensive TLD coverage percentage
ITID-22213.notes: Differentiated from ITID-22211/22212 by mechanism: exact brand string preserved, only the TLD/ccTLD differs.

playbook.name: Response: TLD/ccTLD Swap Lookalike Domain
playbook.description: For a domain matching this organization's brand exactly but registered under a different top-level or country-code domain (e.g., .net, .cc, or a foreign ccTLD in place of the real .com).

steps.title: Determine how the domain was discovered
steps.desc: Establish whether the domain was caught proactively by the domain/brand-monitoring program or reported reactively, and confirm it exactly matches this organization's brand under a different TLD/ccTLD.
steps.outcome: Discovery channel documented and impersonation confirmed.

steps.title: File a takedown/dispute report with the registrar or ccTLD registry
steps.desc: Submit an abuse or trademark-dispute report through the applicable registrar or ccTLD dispute-resolution policy.
steps.guidance: Some ccTLD registries use a local dispute process rather than standard UDRP; confirm the applicable policy.

steps.title: Confirm the domain is taken down, suspended, or transferred
steps.desc: Follow up until the registry/registrar action or dispute resolution removes the threat.
steps.outcome: Domain suspended, transferred, or content removed.

steps.title: Consider defensive registration of common TLD/ccTLD variants
steps.desc: Evaluate whether the organization's brand should be defensively registered under commonly abused TLDs/ccTLDs.

steps.title: Document the pattern and tune monitoring rules
steps.desc: Record the TLD/ccTLD pattern to sharpen the domain-monitoring program's detection rules.

steps.title: Assess current weaponization state and jurisdiction
steps.desc: Check whether the domain is live with phishing content and identify the registrar and the ccTLD registry's jurisdiction, which may affect available remedies.
steps.outcome: Weaponization state, registrar, and jurisdiction identified.

steps.title: Submit to browser/security-vendor blocklists if actively hosting phishing content
steps.desc: If the domain is live with phishing content, report it to Google Safe Browsing and relevant threat-intel feeds.
steps.outcome: URL flagged as unsafe if applicable.

ITID-22214.def: A lookalike domain (of any typosquat/combosquat/TLD-swap variety) confirmed registered and dormant, assessed as likely pre-staged infrastructure for a future phishing or brand-impersonation campaign, warranting proactive monitoring ahead of weaponization.
ITID-22214.purpose: Captures a lookalike domain that has been registered but shows no active hosting or campaign yet, tracked as pre-positioned infrastructure for a future attack.
scopeIncludes: A dormant lookalike domain flagged by threat intel as associated with known phishing kit infrastructure or infrastructure clusters
A lookalike domain with SSL certificate issuance but no visible content, indicating imminent activation
scopeExcludes: A lookalike domain already hosting live content (reclassify to ITID-22211/22212/22213 or the relevant Fake Websites leaf once active)
ITID-22214.severity: Medium — pre-emptive risk, not yet realized harm.
ITID-22214.priority: P2 for continuous monitoring; escalate to P1 immediately upon activation.
ITID-22214.escalation: Escalate immediately upon any sign of activation (DNS, certificate, or content change).
indicators: SSL certificate issuance for a lookalike domain with no visible site
Infrastructure clustering with known phishing kit hosting patterns
DNS record changes on a previously dormant lookalike domain
vectors: Bulk pre-registration of domains ahead of a planned campaign for aging/reputation purposes
rootCauses: Attackers age domains to evade newly-registered-domain detection heuristics
controls: Continuous domain monitoring with certificate-transparency log watching
Threat intel infrastructure clustering
ITID-22214.detection: Strong via certificate-transparency and passive DNS monitoring, though correctly assessing intent before activation requires analyst judgment.
ITID-22214.response: Continuous watchlist monitoring; escalate to takedown workflow immediately upon activation.
metrics: Count of dormant lookalike domains on active watchlist
Mean time from activation to detection
ITID-22214.notes: This is the pre-activation/watchlist state shared by any of the lookalike-domain sibling leaves; reclassify to the specific pattern leaf once the mechanism is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Newly Registered Lookalike Domain Pre-Positioned for Future Campaign
playbook.description: For a lookalike domain caught proactively by domain-monitoring shortly after registration, before it has been weaponized with live phishing content — an opportunity to act before any victim is harmed.

steps.title: Confirm proactive detection and impersonation intent
steps.desc: Confirm the domain-monitoring program flagged the domain based on registration pattern (brand similarity, registrar, registrant patterns matching known threat actors) before any live content appeared.
steps.outcome: Confirmed lookalike registration with monitoring evidence captured.

steps.title: File a preemptive report with the registrar
steps.desc: Submit an early-warning trademark/abuse report to the registrar noting the domain's similarity to this organization's brand, even though it is not yet weaponized.
steps.guidance: Some registrars will not act until the domain is actively abused; document the report regardless to establish a paper trail.
steps.abort: If the registrar declines to act pre-weaponization, proceed to acquisition or continued monitoring.

steps.title: Confirm the domain remains inert or is acquired/suspended
steps.desc: Verify the domain has not gone live with phishing content, or that acquisition/suspension has completed.
steps.outcome: Domain confirmed inert, transferred, or suspended.

steps.title: No customer-facing recovery expected
steps.desc: Since the domain was neutralized before weaponization, confirm no customer impact occurred.

steps.title: Document the early-detection win and reinforce monitoring rules
steps.desc: Record the detection signal that caught this domain pre-weaponization to reinforce and tune the monitoring program's rules.

steps.title: Place the domain under active watch
steps.desc: Add the domain to a watchlist tracking DNS/MX record changes and content changes so any future weaponization is caught immediately.
steps.outcome: Domain under active monitoring with alerting configured.

steps.title: Evaluate acquisition or dispute action
steps.desc: Decide whether to pursue purchasing the domain from the registrant, or initiate a UDRP/dispute proceeding, based on registrant responsiveness and cost.
steps.outcome: Acquisition/dispute path selected and initiated if warranted.

ITID-22215.def: A lookalike domain registration impersonating our brand, not yet matched to a more specific typosquat/combosquat/TLD-swap/pre-positioned leaf.
ITID-22215.purpose: Catch-all for lookalike domain registrations impersonating our brand that do not fit a more specific leaf.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered lookalike domains pending classification
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-22211 through ITID-22214
ITID-22215.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; default Medium.
ITID-22215.escalation: Reclassify once the specific pattern is clarified.
indicators: Domain-monitoring alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: Registration of unclear specific pattern
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Proactive domain monitoring service
ITID-22215.detection: Same external monitoring telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-22215.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

ITID-22221.def: A domain using visually similar Latin-alphabet character substitutions to closely resemble our real domain, without requiring Unicode/IDN encoding.
ITID-22221.purpose: Captures a homograph domain using Latin character substitution (e.g., 'rn' for 'm', '1' for 'l', '0' for 'o') to visually mimic our domain.
scopeIncludes: A domain substituting visually similar ASCII characters or character pairs for our brand's letters
scopeExcludes: Unicode/IDN-based homographs (see ITID-22222)
Mixed-script homographs (see ITID-22223)
ITID-22221.priority: P3 while parked; P1 if MX records or live content appear.
ITID-22221.escalation: Escalate immediately upon MX record or hosting activation.
indicators: Domain registration using an ASCII character-substitution pattern matching our brand visually
vectors: Registration timed to precede a targeted phishing or BEC campaign
rootCauses: Visual similarity exploits quick human scanning of URLs/sender addresses
mitreTechniques: T1036.005 Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
controls: Homograph/character-substitution domain monitoring
Defensive registration of common substitution variants
ITID-22221.detection: Strong — pattern-matching monitoring tools reliably surface common Latin substitution variants.
ITID-22221.response: Log, monitor, and pursue takedown/defensive acquisition per policy.
metrics: Count of Latin-substitution homograph domains detected per month
ITID-22221.notes: Differentiated from Unicode-based homograph leaf by encoding: this leaf covers pure ASCII visual substitution.

steps.outcome: Weaponization state, registrar, and hosting identified.

steps.title: Submit to browser/security-vendor blocklists if actively hosting phishing content
steps.desc: If the domain is live with phishing content, report it to Google Safe Browsing and relevant threat-intel feeds.
steps.outcome: URL flagged as unsafe if applicable.

ITID-22222.def: A domain using internationalized domain name (IDN) encoding with non-Latin Unicode characters (e.g., Cyrillic) that render visually identical or near-identical to our real domain in a browser address bar.
ITID-22222.purpose: Captures a homograph domain using Cyrillic or other non-Latin Unicode characters encoded via punycode/IDN to visually mimic our domain.
scopeIncludes: A punycode-encoded domain using Cyrillic or other Unicode homoglyphs of our brand's Latin characters
scopeExcludes: Pure ASCII character-substitution homographs (see ITID-22221)
ITID-22222.severity: High — IDN homographs can be nearly indistinguishable from the real domain in some browser configurations.
ITID-22222.priority: P2 while parked; P1 if MX records or live content appear.
ITID-22222.escalation: Escalate immediately upon MX record or hosting activation; flag to email security for sender-domain blocking.
indicators: Punycode (xn--) domain registration resolving to a visual match of our brand
Browser rendering showing a visually identical URL to ours
vectors: IDN homograph registration for use in BEC or credential-phishing campaigns
rootCauses: Browser/registrar IDN display policies not uniformly flagging mixed-script risk
mitreTechniques: T1036.005 Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
controls: IDN/punycode homograph monitoring
Email gateway blocking of punycode sender domains
Defensive registration of common IDN homoglyph variants
ITID-22222.detection: Strong via specialized IDN-homograph monitoring tools; less visible to general keyword-based domain monitoring.
ITID-22222.response: Log, monitor, pursue takedown, and proactively block at email gateway.
metrics: Count of IDN homograph domains detected per month
ITID-22222.notes: Highest-fidelity visual deception in this Tier-4 group; prioritized for email-gateway blocking in addition to standard takedown.

vectors: Mixed-script registration specifically to evade single-script homograph detection tools
rootCauses: Detection tooling gaps for mixed-script (as opposed to single-script) homoglyph patterns
mitreTechniques: T1036.005 Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
controls: Mixed-script homograph detection tooling
Email gateway mixed-script domain blocking

metrics: Count of mixed-script homograph domains detected per month
ITID-22223.notes: Represents the evasion-focused variant within this Tier-4 group, targeting gaps in single-script detection tooling.

steps.desc: If the domain is live with phishing content, report it to Google Safe Browsing and relevant threat-intel feeds.
steps.outcome: URL flagged as unsafe if applicable.

ITID-22231.def: A phishing page impersonating our brand that is hosted on a subdomain of a legitimate, unrelated third-party domain that has been compromised, inheriting that domain's clean reputation.
ITID-22231.purpose: Captures phishing content impersonating our brand hosted on a subdomain of a compromised, otherwise-legitimate third-party domain.
scopeIncludes: A phishing page under a subdomain of a compromised legitimate business's domain, impersonating our brand's content
scopeExcludes: Content hosted on infrastructure the attacker fully registered themselves (see the Lookalike/Homograph Domains leaves)
ITID-22231.severity: High — inherited domain reputation makes detection by reputation-based filters harder.
ITID-22231.escalation: Escalate to brand protection and notify the compromised third-party domain owner to remediate.
indicators: Phishing content impersonating our brand found on an unrelated, otherwise-legitimate domain's subdomain
Compromised third-party CMS/hosting panel used to add the subdomain
vectors: Compromise of a third party's CMS/hosting credentials to add a malicious subdomain
rootCauses: Weak credential hygiene or unpatched CMS software at the compromised third party, outside our direct control
mitreTechniques: T1036.005 Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
controls: Brand/content monitoring across the web (not just registered domains)
Coordinated notification process for compromised third parties
ITID-22231.detection: External content-monitoring/crawling services; harder to detect via domain-registration monitoring alone since the base domain is legitimate.
ITID-22231.response: Notify the compromised domain's owner/host and pursue content takedown.
metrics: Count of compromised-domain subdomain abuse cases detected
ITID-22231.notes: Distinguished from lookalike/homograph domain leaves by infrastructure ownership: here the attacker abuses a compromised legitimate third party's domain rather than registering their own.

playbook.name: Response: Subdomain Abuse via Compromised Legitimate Domain
playbook.description: For a phishing/malware subdomain hosted on a third party's legitimate domain after that domain (not any infrastructure of this organization) was compromised, and used to impersonate this organization.

steps.title: Confirm the subdomain is impersonating this organization and identify the parent domain's owner
steps.desc: Confirm the subdomain content impersonates this organization, and identify the legitimate third-party organization that owns the compromised parent domain.
steps.outcome: Impersonation confirmed and parent-domain owner identified.

steps.title: Notify the third-party domain owner
steps.desc: Contact the legitimate organization whose domain was compromised, since they — not this organization — control the DNS/hosting and must remediate.
steps.guidance: Provide clear evidence (subdomain, screenshots, timestamps) to help them act quickly.
steps.abort: If unresponsive, escalate to their hosting provider/registrar directly.

steps.title: Confirm the subdomain content is removed
steps.desc: Follow up with the third-party owner until the malicious content is confirmed removed.
steps.outcome: Subdomain content removed or subdomain deleted.

steps.title: Assist any affected customers
steps.desc: For anyone known to have entered data on the fake subdomain, help secure any exposed accounts.

steps.title: Document the incident and update brand-monitoring for subdomain patterns
steps.desc: Record the compromised domain and subdomain naming pattern to sharpen future detection.

steps.title: Assess scope of the third-party compromise
steps.desc: Check whether other subdomains or paths on the same compromised domain show signs of abuse, to gauge the scope of the third party's compromise.

steps.title: File a supporting abuse report with the hosting provider
steps.desc: If the third-party owner is unresponsive, submit a phishing/brand-abuse report directly to their hosting provider.

steps.title: Submit the subdomain URL to browser/security-vendor blocklists
steps.desc: Report the phishing URL to Google Safe Browsing and relevant threat-intel feeds.
steps.outcome: URL flagged as unsafe in major browsers.

ITID-22232.def: A phishing page impersonating our brand hosted after an attacker claimed an orphaned cloud resource (e.g., a decommissioned CDN/hosting endpoint) still referenced by a stale DNS record — potentially one of our own abandoned subdomains, or a third party's.
ITID-22232.purpose: Captures phishing content impersonating our brand hosted via takeover of a dangling DNS record pointing to an orphaned subdomain.
scopeIncludes: Takeover of one of our own decommissioned subdomains with a dangling CNAME
Takeover of a third party's dangling subdomain used to impersonate our brand
scopeExcludes: A subdomain abuse case involving an actively compromised, actively-used domain (see ITID-22231)
ITID-22232.severity: High, and higher still if the dangling record is our own asset (indicates an internal asset-hygiene gap).
ITID-22232.escalation: Escalate to IT/cloud infrastructure teams immediately to reclaim or remove the dangling DNS record, in addition to brand protection takedown.
indicators: A DNS record (ours or a third party's) pointing to an unclaimed cloud resource now serving impersonating content
Recently decommissioned service with a DNS record left in place
vectors: Automated scanning for dangling CNAME records pointing to unclaimed cloud resources
rootCauses: Incomplete decommissioning process failing to remove DNS records when a cloud resource is retired
mitreTechniques: T1036.005 Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
controls: DNS hygiene/dangling-record audit process
Cloud resource decommissioning checklist requiring DNS cleanup
ITID-22232.detection: Strong when the dangling record is our own asset (internal DNS auditing); weaker for third-party dangling records, relying on external content monitoring.
ITID-22232.response: Reclaim/remove the dangling DNS record and pursue content takedown.
metrics: Count of dangling DNS takeovers detected
Count of internal dangling records proactively remediated
ITID-22232.notes: When the dangling record is our own asset, this also represents an internal control gap and should be cross-referenced with asset-management remediation tracking.

playbook.name: Response: Subdomain Abuse via Dangling DNS/Takeover of Orphaned Subdomain
playbook.description: For a phishing/malware page served from this organization's own subdomain after an attacker took it over via a dangling DNS record (a CNAME pointing to a deprovisioned cloud resource) — an incident rooted in this organization's own DNS hygiene, not a third party's infrastructure.

steps.title: Confirm the abused subdomain belongs to this organization and identify the dangling record
steps.desc: Confirm the subdomain is genuinely under this organization's own DNS zone, and locate the specific DNS record (typically a CNAME) pointing to a deprovisioned or unclaimed cloud resource that the attacker has claimed.
steps.guidance: Check the organization's own DNS zone files/console directly rather than relying solely on external reports.
steps.outcome: Dangling DNS record identified and confirmed as the entry point for the takeover.
steps.tool: DNS zone console / dig / passive DNS

steps.title: Reclaim or remove the dangling DNS record immediately
steps.desc: This is this organization's own misconfiguration: as the DNS zone owner, immediately delete the dangling CNAME/record, or re-provision and reclaim the cloud resource it points to, cutting off the attacker's control of the subdomain.
steps.guidance: This step is the primary containment action and does not depend on any third party's response time.
steps.outcome: Dangling record removed or resource reclaimed; subdomain no longer resolves to attacker-controlled content.
steps.tool: DNS zone console / cloud provider console

steps.title: Audit the full DNS zone for other dangling records
steps.desc: Scan all DNS records in the organization's zones for other CNAMEs or records pointing to deprovisioned or unclaimed cloud resources that could enable a repeat takeover.
steps.outcome: Full zone audited; any other dangling records remediated.

steps.title: Assist any users who interacted with the takeover subdomain
steps.desc: For anyone known to have submitted data or credentials to the takeover page, help secure any exposed accounts.

steps.title: Implement a DNS decommissioning process to prevent recurrence
steps.desc: Document the incident and establish or reinforce a process requiring DNS records to be removed as part of decommissioning any cloud resource, plus periodic automated scanning for dangling records.
steps.outcome: Process gap closed and finding logged.

steps.title: Assess what content the attacker is serving and any data exposure
steps.desc: Determine what the attacker is hosting on the takeover subdomain (phishing, malware) and whether the subdomain's trusted status (same-origin cookies, SSO trust, allowlisted CORS/CSP entries) exposed any additional risk.
steps.outcome: Impact of the takeover documented, including any inherited trust exploited.

steps.title: Submit the subdomain URL to browser/security-vendor blocklists if it was actively used for phishing
steps.desc: Report the URL to Google Safe Browsing and relevant threat-intel feeds if it was live with phishing content before reclamation.
steps.outcome: URL flagged as unsafe in major browsers.

ITID-22233.def: A phishing page impersonating our brand hosted on a free-tier subdomain provided by a legitimate cloud or SaaS platform (e.g., a free site-builder or storage subdomain), exploiting that platform's trusted top-level domain reputation.
ITID-22233.purpose: Captures phishing content impersonating our brand hosted on a free-tier subdomain of a legitimate cloud/SaaS provider.
scopeIncludes: Phishing content impersonating our brand hosted on a free-tier subdomain of a well-known cloud/SaaS provider
scopeExcludes: Content hosted on a compromised legitimate business's own domain (see ITID-22231)
ITID-22233.severity: High — the trusted parent platform domain can bypass reputation-based email/web filtering.
ITID-22233.escalation: Escalate to brand protection and report to the cloud/SaaS provider's abuse team for expedited removal.
indicators: Phishing content impersonating our brand found under a known free-tier hosting subdomain pattern
vectors: Free-tier account creation on a legitimate cloud/SaaS platform specifically to host phishing content
rootCauses: Low/no-cost, low-verification account creation on legitimate cloud platforms
mitreTechniques: T1036.005 Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
controls: Provider abuse-reporting relationship
Brand/content monitoring across known free-tier hosting patterns
ITID-22233.detection: External content-monitoring services; provider abuse teams typically respond faster than domain-registrar takedowns.
ITID-22233.response: Report to the provider's abuse team for expedited removal.
metrics: Count of free-tier hosting abuse cases detected/removed
Mean time to provider takedown
ITID-22233.notes: Differentiated from ITID-22231 by infrastructure type: here the abused platform is a legitimate multi-tenant SaaS/cloud provider rather than a single compromised business.

playbook.name: Response: Subdomain Abuse via Cloud/SaaS Free-Tier Subdomain
playbook.description: For a phishing/malware page hosted on a free-tier subdomain of a third-party cloud or SaaS platform (e.g., a brand-name subdomain on a page-builder, form, or app-hosting service) impersonating this organization.

steps.title: Confirm the subdomain is impersonating this organization
steps.desc: Confirm the free-tier subdomain's branding/content impersonates this organization, and identify the SaaS/cloud platform hosting it.
steps.outcome: Impersonation confirmed and hosting platform identified.

steps.title: File an abuse report with the SaaS/cloud platform's trust and safety team
steps.desc: Submit a phishing/brand-impersonation report to the platform requesting removal of the account/subdomain; this is faster than pursuing the underlying domain, which the platform — not the attacker — controls.

steps.title: Confirm the subdomain/account is removed
steps.desc: Follow up with the platform until the account or subdomain is confirmed removed.
steps.guidance: Escalate if no action within a reasonable window.

steps.title: Assist any affected customers
steps.desc: For anyone known to have entered data on the fake subdomain, help secure any exposed accounts.

steps.title: Document the platform used and add it to brand-monitoring coverage
steps.desc: Record which free-tier platform was abused and consider extending brand-monitoring searches to cover it.

steps.title: Capture evidence for the platform's trust and safety team
steps.desc: Screenshot the page, note the exact subdomain/account name, and record timestamps.

steps.title: Submit the URL to browser/security-vendor blocklists
steps.desc: Report the URL to Google Safe Browsing and relevant threat-intel feeds.
steps.outcome: URL flagged as unsafe in major browsers.

ITID-22234.def: A phishing URL impersonating our brand that places our brand name early in a long, deeply nested subdomain chain (e.g., 'ourbrand.login.secure.verify.attacker-domain.com') so that a quick visual scan of the URL appears to show our brand, obscuring the actual base domain.
ITID-22234.purpose: Captures phishing content impersonating our brand hosted behind a deeply nested subdomain string designed to obscure the true base domain from a casual reader.
scopeIncludes: A URL with our brand string embedded in a nested subdomain label ahead of an unrelated base domain
Long subdomain chains specifically engineered to push the true base domain off-screen on mobile displays
scopeExcludes: A domain where the base/registrable domain itself is a lookalike (see the Lookalike/Homograph Domains leaves)
ITID-22234.severity: High — this pattern is specifically engineered to defeat casual URL inspection and mobile display truncation.
ITID-22234.escalation: Escalate to brand protection and email/web security for URL-pattern-based blocking rules.
indicators: URL with our brand string appearing early in a long subdomain chain, unrelated base domain
Mobile-optimized phishing pages relying on address-bar truncation
vectors: Deliberate URL construction to exploit mobile browser address-bar truncation and casual scanning behavior
rootCauses: Limited user URL-literacy and mobile display constraints that truncate the visible portion of a URL
mitreTechniques: T1036.005 Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
controls: URL-pattern detection rules for nested-subdomain brand-string abuse
User education on identifying the true base/registrable domain
ITID-22234.detection: Moderate — requires URL-structure-aware detection rather than simple keyword matching on the full URL string.
ITID-22234.response: Log, pursue takedown, and add URL-pattern blocking rules at the email/web gateway.
metrics: Count of nested-subdomain obfuscation cases detected
ITID-22234.notes: Represents a display-manipulation technique layered on top of any base domain type; the base domain itself may be entirely unrelated to our brand.

playbook.name: Response: Deeply Nested Subdomain Obfuscation
playbook.description: For an attacker-owned domain that nests this organization's brand name deep within a long subdomain string (e.g., login.this-brand.com.verify-account.attacker-domain.com) to visually deceive users about the true domain owner.

steps.title: Identify the true registered domain behind the nested string
steps.desc: Parse the full hostname to identify the actual registrable domain (the rightmost portion) that the attacker controls, distinguishing it from the nested labels designed to look like this organization's real domain.

steps.title: File a takedown report with the hosting provider and registrar
steps.desc: Submit a phishing/brand-impersonation report citing the nested-subdomain deception technique as evidence of deliberate targeting.

steps.title: Confirm the site is taken down
steps.desc: Follow up until the site is confirmed offline.

steps.title: Assist any affected customers
steps.desc: For anyone known to have entered data on the fake page, help secure any exposed accounts.

steps.title: Document the obfuscation pattern and share with customers/employees
steps.desc: Record the nesting pattern and consider a brief awareness note on how to identify the true domain in a long hostname.

steps.title: Identify the hosting provider and registrar of the true domain
steps.desc: Determine where the actual domain is hosted and registered.

steps.title: Submit the URL to browser/security-vendor blocklists
steps.desc: Report the full URL to Google Safe Browsing and relevant threat-intel feeds.
steps.outcome: URL flagged as unsafe in major browsers.

ITID-22235.def: Subdomain-based abuse impersonating our brand, not yet matched to a more specific compromised-domain/dangling-DNS/cloud-abuse/nested-obfuscation leaf.
ITID-22235.purpose: Catch-all for subdomain abuse impersonating our brand that does not fit a more specific leaf.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered subdomain abuse cases pending classification
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-22231 through ITID-22234
ITID-22235.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; default Medium-High.
ITID-22235.escalation: Reclassify once the specific mechanism is clarified.
indicators: Alert of unclear specific subdomain-abuse pattern
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Domain/content monitoring
ITID-22235.detection: Same external telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-22235.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Subdomain Abuse
playbook.description: For a phishing/malware subdomain impersonating this organization, where the specific mechanism (compromised third-party domain, dangling DNS, SaaS free-tier, nested obfuscation) does not fit an existing category.

steps.title: Determine ownership of the parent domain/platform
steps.desc: Establish whether the abused subdomain sits on this organization's own infrastructure, a third party's domain, or a SaaS platform, since this determines who must act to remove it.

steps.title: Take the appropriate containment action based on ownership
steps.desc: If it is this organization's own DNS misconfiguration, reclaim/remove the record directly; otherwise, file an abuse report with the domain owner, hosting provider, or platform.
steps.outcome: Containment action initiated with the responsible party.

steps.title: Confirm the subdomain content is removed
steps.desc: Follow up until the malicious content is confirmed removed.

steps.title: Assist any affected customers
steps.desc: For anyone known to have entered data on the fake subdomain, help secure any exposed accounts.

steps.title: Document the incident and evaluate whether it fits an existing category going forward
steps.desc: Record the mechanism used to sharpen future detection and categorization.

steps.title: Confirm the subdomain is impersonating this organization
steps.desc: Confirm the content served on the subdomain impersonates this organization's brand.

steps.title: Submit the URL to browser/security-vendor blocklists
steps.desc: Report the URL to Google Safe Browsing and relevant threat-intel feeds.
steps.outcome: URL flagged as unsafe in major browsers.

ITID-22311.def: Physical, non-digital counterfeiting where our logo or trademark is reproduced on packaging for counterfeit goods sold through physical or online retail channels.
ITID-22311.purpose: Captures unauthorized use of our logo/trademark on counterfeit physical product packaging.
scopeIncludes: Counterfeit physical products bearing our logo/trademark on packaging
Counterfeit goods seized by customs/law enforcement bearing our branding
scopeExcludes: Digital-only trademark misuse with no physical goods involved (see other Brand Spoofing leaves)
ITID-22311.severity: Medium-High — primarily a brand/legal and consumer-safety issue rather than a cyber incident.
ITID-22311.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if consumer safety is at risk (e.g., counterfeit food, electronics, pharmaceuticals).
ITID-22311.escalation: Escalate to legal/brand protection and, where consumer safety is implicated, to product safety/regulatory teams.
indicators: Customer report of a suspect product bearing our logo purchased through an unofficial channel
Customs/law enforcement seizure notification
vectors: Physical counterfeit manufacturing supply chains
rootCauses: High consumer demand and brand recognition value creating a counterfeiting incentive
controls: Trademark enforcement and anti-counterfeiting program
Supply chain/authentication technology (holograms, serialization)
ITID-22311.detection: Primarily non-technical — customs, retail channel, and customer reports; no meaningful cyber telemetry.
ITID-22311.response: Legal enforcement action and consumer safety advisory where applicable.
metrics: Count of counterfeit seizures/reports per quarter
ITID-22311.notes: This leaf is intentionally scoped as a non-cyber, physical-goods brand-protection concern with no MITRE ATT&CK applicability; included for completeness of the brand-protection taxonomy.

playbook.name: Response: Counterfeit Product Packaging/Physical Goods Logo Misuse
playbook.description: For counterfeit physical goods bearing this organization's logo/branding on packaging, requiring coordination beyond digital takedown — potentially involving customs and law enforcement.

steps.title: Confirm the goods/packaging are counterfeit
steps.desc: Compare the product and packaging against genuine specifications (materials, print quality, serial numbers, security features) to confirm counterfeiting rather than genuine gray-market goods.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the brand-protection/legal team, who may have authentication criteria.
steps.outcome: Counterfeit status confirmed with physical or photographic evidence.

steps.title: Engage legal/brand-protection counsel on law enforcement and customs referral
steps.desc: Refer the case to legal/brand-protection counsel to evaluate filing a report with law enforcement and/or customs/border authorities for seizure of counterfeit shipments.
steps.guidance: Physical counterfeit goods typically require formal legal action rather than a simple takedown request.
steps.outcome: Case referred to the appropriate legal/law-enforcement/customs channel.

steps.title: Confirm seizure/removal actions are completed
steps.desc: Follow up with legal/customs/law enforcement and any marketplace on the status of seizure or listing removal.

steps.title: Support any customers who purchased counterfeit goods, especially safety-related
steps.desc: If the counterfeit product poses a safety risk (e.g., electrical, food-contact), issue guidance or a recall-style notice for affected customers.

steps.title: Document the case and reinforce supply-chain/anti-counterfeiting measures
steps.desc: Record the counterfeit source and distribution pattern, and consider whether additional product authentication features are warranted.

steps.title: Identify the sales channel and, where possible, the supply chain
steps.desc: Determine where the counterfeit goods are being sold (physical retail, marketplace, informal market) and trace back toward the source if evidence permits.
steps.outcome: Sales channel identified and supply-chain leads documented.

steps.title: If sold online, file a marketplace/platform counterfeit report
steps.desc: If the counterfeit goods are also listed online, submit a counterfeit report to the marketplace's brand-registry/trust-and-safety team in parallel.

steps.title: Warn customers through official channels
steps.desc: If the counterfeit is widespread or poses a safety risk, publish guidance on identifying genuine products.
steps.outcome: Customers warned and equipped to identify counterfeits.

ITID-22312.def: A digital trust seal, security certification badge, or 'verified by' mark falsely displayed on a third-party site, implying an association with our brand or certification program that does not exist.
ITID-22312.purpose: Captures fraudulent use of a fake trust seal or security certification badge falsely claiming association with us.
scopeIncludes: A fake 'certified partner' or 'verified' badge referencing our brand displayed on an unaffiliated site
Misuse of an expired or revoked certification mark after the relationship ended
scopeExcludes: A currently-valid partner legitimately displaying an authorized badge
ITID-22312.severity: Medium — primarily a trust/credibility issue used to lend legitimacy to other scams.
ITID-22312.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if paired with active phishing/scam activity.
ITID-22312.escalation: Escalate to brand protection and legal for cease-and-desist; correlate with the hosting site's other activity.
indicators: A site displaying our trust seal/badge with no corresponding record in our partner/certification database
vectors: Copying badge image assets from our official marketing materials
rootCauses: Trust seals are simple static images with no built-in verification mechanism
mitreTechniques: T1036.005 Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
controls: Partner/certification registry verification tooling
Brand/content monitoring for badge misuse
ITID-22312.detection: External content monitoring and periodic partner-registry cross-checks.
metrics: Count of fraudulent trust-seal cases detected
ITID-22312.notes: Frequently found in combination with scam e-commerce sites (ITID-2214x); logged here when the trust-seal misuse itself is the primary finding.

playbook.name: Response: Fraudulent Trust Seal/Security Certification Badge Misuse
playbook.description: For a fraudulent use of this organization's trust seal, security certification, or accreditation badge on a third-party site to falsely imply endorsement, certification, or partnership.

steps.title: Confirm the badge is being used without authorization
steps.desc: Verify against the organization's records that the site displaying the badge is not an authorized licensee/partner.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized use confirmed with evidence captured (screenshot, site URL).

steps.title: Send a cease-and-desist / abuse notice to the site owner and hosting provider
steps.desc: Request immediate removal of the unauthorized badge, citing trademark/brand-misrepresentation grounds.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with legal counsel on the notice language.
steps.abort: Escalate to the hosting provider if the site owner is unresponsive.

steps.title: Confirm the badge is removed
steps.desc: Follow up until the unauthorized badge is confirmed removed from the site.

steps.title: Assess whether customer trust was misled and needs correction
steps.desc: If the false badge was used to sell products/services, evaluate whether affected customers need to be notified.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and any needed customer communication issued.

steps.title: Document the misuse and consider technical badge-verification measures
steps.desc: Record the case and evaluate whether a verification mechanism (e.g., a live badge-check API) would help detect future misuse faster.

steps.title: Identify the hosting provider and site owner
steps.desc: Determine where the site is hosted and, where possible, who owns/operates it.
steps.outcome: Hosting provider and site owner identified where possible.

ITID-22313.def: Unauthorized display of our logo/trademark within a marketplace product listing (e.g., in listing images or descriptions) to imply an affiliation or endorsement that does not exist, tracked distinctly from the underlying counterfeit-goods transaction risk.
ITID-22313.purpose: Captures unauthorized use of our logo in a product listing on a third-party marketplace, absent an actual counterfeit product transaction.
scopeIncludes: Marketplace listing images/descriptions using our logo without authorization for an unrelated or generic product
scopeExcludes: The counterfeit product-listing/storefront pattern already covered under ITID-22143 (Fake Marketplace Listing/Storefront on Legitimate Platform) — this leaf is reserved for logo misuse absent a full storefront-impersonation pattern
ITID-22313.escalation: Escalate to legal/brand protection for standard marketplace abuse reporting.
indicators: Listing using our logo image asset without an authorized seller relationship on file
vectors: Copying our logo asset into unrelated product listings to boost perceived credibility
rootCauses: Marketplace listing-content review gaps for unauthorized trademark use
mitreTechniques: T1036.005 Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
controls: Marketplace brand-registry/abuse reporting program
ITID-22313.response: Report listing to marketplace abuse program for correction/removal.
metrics: Count of unauthorized logo-use listings removed
ITID-22313.notes: Deliberately scoped narrower than ITID-22143 to avoid duplication: this leaf covers standalone logo misuse in a listing, not a full fake-storefront/seller-impersonation pattern.

playbook.name: Response: Unauthorized Logo Use in Third-Party Marketplace Product Listing
playbook.description: For unauthorized use of this organization's logo in a product listing on a legitimate third-party marketplace to falsely imply endorsement, compatibility, or affiliation.

steps.title: Confirm the logo use is unauthorized
steps.desc: Verify against licensing/partnership records that the seller is not authorized to use the logo, and capture the listing.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized use confirmed with evidence captured (listing URL, seller ID, screenshots).

steps.title: File a brand-abuse report with the marketplace's trust and safety team
steps.desc: Submit a report through the platform's brand-registry/intellectual-property program requesting listing removal.

steps.title: Confirm the listing is removed or corrected
steps.desc: Follow up with the marketplace until the listing is removed or the unauthorized logo is removed from it.

steps.title: Assess customer impact if the listing implied a compatibility/endorsement that was false
steps.desc: If customers purchased based on the false implication, evaluate whether a customer notice is warranted.

steps.title: Document the case and expand marketplace monitoring
steps.desc: Record the seller pattern and consider enrolling in or expanding the platform's automated brand-protection tools.

steps.title: Identify the marketplace platform and seller account
steps.desc: Record the platform and seller/listing ID.

ITID-22314.def: Unauthorized use of our logo or trademark in physical marketing collateral — flyers, brochures, signage, physical mailers — implying a nonexistent affiliation, sponsorship, or endorsement.
ITID-22314.purpose: Captures unauthorized use of our logo in print or other physical marketing materials.
scopeIncludes: Print flyers/mailers using our logo without authorization
Physical signage falsely implying sponsorship or partnership
scopeExcludes: Digital advertisement misuse of our logo (see ITID-22321-22325, Fraudulent Advertisements)
indicators: Physical marketing material reported by the public or found during field observation using our logo without authorization
vectors: Local/regional scams using our logo on printed materials to appear legitimate
rootCauses: Physical print materials are outside standard digital brand-monitoring coverage
controls: Trademark enforcement program
Public reporting channel for suspected brand misuse
ITID-22314.detection: Weak — relies almost entirely on public/customer reporting since this is a physical, non-digital channel.
ITID-22314.response: Cease-and-desist and, where relevant, local law enforcement referral for fraud.
metrics: Count of physical-materials misuse cases reported
ITID-22314.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK applicability given the non-digital nature of this leaf; included for taxonomy completeness.

playbook.name: Response: Logo Misuse in Print/Physical Marketing Materials
playbook.description: For unauthorized use of this organization's logo in a third party's print or physical marketing materials (flyers, brochures, signage, vehicle wraps) to falsely imply endorsement or affiliation.

steps.title: Confirm the logo use is unauthorized and document it
steps.desc: Verify against licensing/partnership records that the party is not authorized, and photograph/collect the physical material as evidence.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized use confirmed with physical evidence captured.

steps.title: Send a cease-and-desist notice to the responsible party
steps.desc: Request immediate removal/destruction of remaining materials, citing trademark/brand-misrepresentation grounds.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with legal counsel on the notice language.
steps.abort: Escalate to legal action if unresponsive.

steps.title: Confirm the materials are withdrawn from circulation
steps.desc: Follow up to confirm remaining physical materials are pulled from display/distribution.

steps.title: Assess local customer/public confusion and correct if needed
steps.desc: If the materials caused local confusion about affiliation, issue a local clarification through appropriate channels.

steps.title: Document the case for the brand-protection record
steps.desc: Record the party and materials involved for future reference, particularly if the same party reoffends.

steps.title: Identify the responsible party and their location/distribution scope
steps.desc: Determine who produced/distributed the materials and how widely they have been circulated.
steps.outcome: Responsible party and distribution scope identified.

ITID-22315.def: Unauthorized use of our logo/trademark, not yet matched to a more specific physical-goods/trust-seal/marketplace/print-materials leaf.
ITID-22315.purpose: Catch-all for logo misuse impersonating our brand that does not fit a more specific leaf.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered logo misuse cases pending classification
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-22311 through ITID-22314
ITID-22315.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; default Low-Medium.

steps.desc: Submit a brand-impersonation/scam-ad report requesting removal of the ad and suspension of the advertiser account.

steps.title: Identify the advertiser account and landing page infrastructure

steps.title: Report the content to the publisher and native-ad network
steps.desc: Submit a brand-impersonation/scam-content report to both the hosting publisher and the ad network that served the placement.
steps.outcome: Report submitted to publisher and ad network.

steps.title: Confirm the content is removed
steps.desc: Follow up until the sponsored content is confirmed removed.

steps.title: Support readers who engaged with the fake offer
steps.desc: For anyone known to have submitted payment or personal data, help them dispute charges or secure exposed data.

steps.title: Document the campaign and expand native-ad network monitoring
steps.desc: Record the publisher/network pattern to sharpen future detection.

steps.title: Identify the publisher, ad network, and landing page infrastructure
steps.desc: Determine which publisher hosts the content, which native-ad network served it, and the landing page's hosting/registrar if separately hosted.
steps.outcome: Publisher, ad network, and landing-page infrastructure identified.

steps.title: File a takedown report for the landing page if separately hosted
steps.desc: If the content drives to a separate scam site, submit a takedown request to its hosting provider and registrar.

ITID-22324.def: A malicious advertisement (on any ad network) specifically promoting a fake mobile application impersonating our brand for download, connecting the advertising vector to the malware-distribution outcome.
ITID-22324.purpose: Captures a fraudulent advertisement promoting a fake mobile app impersonating our brand.
scopeIncludes: An ad promoting download of a fake app impersonating our brand
scopeExcludes: The fake app artifact itself once installed/analyzed (see ITID-22123, Fake Mobile App Download Site)
ITID-22324.severity: High — combines ad-driven reach with mobile malware/data-theft outcomes.
ITID-22324.priority: P1 while the ad is active.
ITID-22324.escalation: Escalate to brand protection and mobile threat intel; report to both the ad network and, if applicable, the app store hosting the fake app.
indicators: Ad promoting a fake app under our brand name/icon
App analysis confirming malicious behavior
vectors: Ad campaigns driving install volume for a fake app before detection
rootCauses: Ad-network and app-store review gaps working independently rather than in a coordinated abuse pipeline
mitreTechniques: T1036.005 Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
controls: Ad-network and app-store abuse reporting relationships
Mobile threat intelligence monitoring
ITID-22324.detection: External ad-monitoring and mobile threat intel feeds.
ITID-22324.response: Report to both the ad network and app store; issue public advisory if install volume is high.
metrics: Count of fake-app-promoting ads removed
Estimated install volume before takedown
ITID-22324.notes: This leaf tracks the advertising vector specifically; the resulting fake app artifact is tracked under ITID-22123 to avoid duplicating the malware-distribution-site record.

playbook.name: Response: Fraudulent App Store Advertisement Promoting Fake App
playbook.description: For a fraudulent advertisement impersonating this organization to promote a fake mobile app listed in an official app store, luring users into installing malware or a data-harvesting app.

steps.title: Confirm both the ad and the promoted app are impersonating this organization
steps.desc: Confirm the ad's branding impersonates this organization and that the linked app store listing is not this organization's genuine app.
steps.outcome: Impersonation confirmed with evidence captured (ad screenshot, app store listing URL).

steps.title: Report the fraudulent ad to the ad platform
steps.desc: Submit a brand-impersonation/scam-ad report requesting removal of the ad and suspension of the advertiser account.

steps.title: Confirm the ad and fake app are removed
steps.desc: Follow up until both the ad and the app store listing are confirmed removed.

steps.title: Advise any known-affected users to remove the fake app
steps.desc: For any user confirmed to have installed the fake app, provide removal instructions and recommend a credential/session review.

steps.title: Document the campaign and monitor for repeat developer accounts
steps.desc: Record the developer account and ad pattern, since fake-app operators often reappear under new listings.

steps.title: Identify the advertiser account and app store developer account
steps.desc: Identify the advertiser account running the ad and the developer account behind the fake app listing.

steps.title: Report the fake app to the app store's trust and safety team
steps.desc: Submit a trademark/impersonation and malware report requesting removal of the fake app listing.

steps.title: Warn customers through official channels
steps.desc: Publish a notice clarifying the organization's genuine app listing and warning against the fake one.
steps.outcome: Customers warned and directed to the genuine app.

steps.title: Identify the advertiser account and landing page infrastructure

ITID-22331.def: A fraudulent email response impersonating our official customer support, inserted into or fabricated to resemble an ongoing email reply-chain with a customer, used to extract payment or personal data.
ITID-22331.purpose: Captures an adversary impersonating our customer support in an email reply-chain to a customer.
scopeIncludes: A fake support reply impersonating our brand sent to a customer, fabricating a plausible reply-chain context
Use of a lookalike support email address to continue a real or fabricated customer conversation
scopeExcludes: Reply-chain phishing that hijacks an internal employee's actual mailbox to target other employees (see ITID-11132, Reply-Chain Hijack Clone Phishing, under Attacks Against the Human)
ITID-22331.severity: High — direct financial/data harm to customers who trust an apparent continuation of real support contact.
ITID-22331.escalation: Escalate to brand protection and customer support leadership; notify affected customers.
indicators: Customer report of a suspicious 'support' reply from a lookalike email address
Email header analysis showing a spoofed or lookalike sender domain
vectors: Lookalike domain email spoofing customer support communications
Compromise of an actual customer support agent's mailbox (rare; see notes)
rootCauses: Customers unable to easily verify the authenticity of a support sender address
controls: Email authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) on our official support domain
Customer education on verifying official support channels
ITID-22331.detection: Customer reports and email-authentication failure monitoring on lookalike domains.
ITID-22331.response: Investigate, notify affected customers, and pursue takedown of the spoofing infrastructure.
metrics: Count of impersonated support email cases reported
detections: DMARC monitoring on our support domain
ITID-22331.notes: If the incident instead involves compromise of one of our actual support agent mailboxes used to attack other employees internally, route to ITID-11132 instead; this leaf covers customer-facing impersonation via spoofed/lookalike infrastructure.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Customer Support Email Reply-Chain Impersonation
playbook.description: For a fraudulent email impersonating this organization's customer support team, often inserted into or spoofing a plausible reply-chain to a genuine customer inquiry, to extract data or payment.

steps.title: Confirm the email is impersonating this organization's support team
steps.desc: Review the sending address, headers, and content to confirm it did not originate from this organization's real support systems.
steps.guidance: Check SPF/DKIM/DMARC results and the true sending domain.
steps.outcome: Confirmed impersonation with header evidence captured.

steps.title: Identify and report the sending domain/mailbox infrastructure
steps.desc: Identify the domain or mailbox used to send the fraudulent email and file an abuse report with its registrar/hosting provider or email provider.

steps.title: Confirm the sending infrastructure is taken down
steps.desc: Follow up until the domain/mailbox is confirmed suspended.

steps.title: Support any customer who submitted data or payment
steps.desc: For any customer who acted on the fraudulent email, help them secure accounts or dispute payments.

steps.title: Document the case and review support-channel authentication practices
steps.desc: Record the technique used and consider whether support communications need a stronger authenticity signal (e.g., ticket reference verification).

steps.title: Determine whether a genuine support ticket/thread was involved
steps.desc: Check whether the attacker had visibility into a real prior conversation (indicating a possible mailbox or ticketing-system compromise) or fabricated a plausible-looking new thread.
steps.outcome: Determined whether any real system/data was exposed to enable the impersonation.

steps.title: If a real support-system exposure enabled the impersonation, contain it
steps.desc: If investigation shows a support mailbox or ticketing system was compromised or leaked, secure that system (reset credentials, revoke sessions).

steps.title: Warn the affected customer(s) directly
steps.desc: Contact the customer(s) targeted to confirm they did not act on the fraudulent email and warn them it did not come from the organization.

ITID-22332.def: A fraudulent live chat interface embedded on a fake/cloned site impersonating our brand, used to interactively social-engineer visitors in real time (e.g., walking them through a fraudulent payment or remote-access session).
ITID-22332.purpose: Captures a fake live chat widget embedded on a cloned or fake website impersonating our customer support.
scopeIncludes: A live chat widget on a fake site that impersonates our support agents to extract payment or push malicious downloads
scopeExcludes: A static fake support page with no interactive chat element (see ITID-22131-22134, Fake Support Pages)
ITID-22332.severity: High — real-time interactive social engineering has a higher success rate than static content.
ITID-22332.escalation: Escalate to brand protection immediately given the active, interactive nature of the scam.
indicators: Fake site featuring a live chat widget staffed by a scam operator claiming to be our support
vectors: Embedding a generic live-chat widget service on a cloned site, staffed by human scam operators
rootCauses: Low cost of embedding third-party live-chat widgets on any site
controls: Brand/domain monitoring extended to interactive-element detection
ITID-22332.detection: External monitoring and customer reports; interactive nature makes automated detection harder than static content scanning.
ITID-22332.response: Rapid takedown given active, real-time victim engagement.
metrics: Count of fake live-chat impersonation cases detected
ITID-22332.notes: Differentiated from the Fake Support Pages leaves by interactivity: this leaf specifically covers a real-time chat-based scam layered on a fake site.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Live Chat Widget Impersonation (Embedded on Cloned/Fake Site)
playbook.description: For a fake live-chat widget embedded on a cloned or fake site, staffed by scammers impersonating this organization's support team to build trust and extract data or payment in real time.

steps.title: Confirm the site and chat widget are impersonating this organization
steps.desc: Confirm the site is a clone/fake and that the embedded chat widget is presenting itself as this organization's support, capturing a transcript if possible.
steps.outcome: Confirmed impersonation with evidence captured (site, chat transcript, chat vendor if identifiable).

steps.title: File a takedown report with the hosting provider and registrar
steps.desc: Submit a phishing/brand-impersonation takedown request for the fake site.

steps.title: Confirm the site is taken down
steps.desc: Follow up until the site is confirmed offline.

steps.title: Support any customer who chatted and disclosed data or paid
steps.desc: For any customer known to have interacted with the fake chat and disclosed data or paid, help them secure accounts or dispute payments.

steps.title: Document the campaign and update brand-monitoring rules
steps.desc: Record the site template and chat vendor pattern to sharpen future detection.

steps.title: Identify the hosting provider, registrar, and chat widget vendor
steps.desc: Determine where the fake site is hosted, where its domain is registered, and which third-party chat widget service is embedded.
steps.outcome: Hosting, registrar, and chat vendor identified.
steps.tool: WHOIS / passive DNS / page source inspection

steps.title: Report the chat widget account to its vendor
steps.desc: If the chat widget is a recognizable third-party service, report the account for abuse to have it suspended.

steps.title: Warn customers through official channels
steps.desc: Publish a notice warning customers that live chat only exists on the organization's genuine site.
steps.outcome: Customers warned against the fake chat.

ITID-22333.def: A fraudulent SMS/text message impersonating our brand's customer support, used to direct recipients to a phishing link, request sensitive information, or request a callback to a fraudulent number.
ITID-22333.purpose: Captures fraudulent SMS/text messages impersonating our customer support.
scopeIncludes: A smishing message impersonating our official support/notification sender ID
scopeExcludes: SMS-based phishing targeting our own employees (see the Multi-Channel Phishing leaves under ITID-11912, Email + SMS Coordinated Phishing, when the victim is internal)
ITID-22333.priority: P1 while an active campaign is confirmed.
ITID-22333.escalation: Escalate to brand protection and telecom/carrier abuse reporting where sender ID spoofing is confirmed.
indicators: Customer report of a suspicious SMS impersonating our support sender ID
Carrier abuse report confirming sender ID spoofing
vectors: SMS sender ID spoofing
Bulk SMS campaigns using leaked or purchased phone number lists
rootCauses: SMS sender ID verification gaps at the carrier/aggregator level
controls: Registered/verified sender ID for our official SMS communications
Carrier/aggregator abuse reporting relationship
ITID-22333.detection: Customer reports and carrier abuse-reporting channels.
ITID-22333.response: Report to carrier/aggregator and issue a customer advisory.
metrics: Count of smishing campaigns impersonating our support reported
ITID-22333.notes: Scoped to customer-facing smishing impersonating our brand; SMS phishing where the confirmed target is our own workforce remains under the ITID-11000 multi-channel phishing leaves.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Customer Support SMS/Text Impersonation
playbook.description: For a fraudulent SMS/text message impersonating this organization's customer support team (smishing) to extract data, credentials, or payment, or to drive victims to a fake site.

steps.title: Confirm the SMS is impersonating this organization
steps.desc: Review the sending number/short code and message content to confirm it did not originate from this organization's real messaging systems.
steps.outcome: Confirmed impersonation with evidence captured (sender ID, message text, any linked URL).

steps.title: Report the number/short code to the carrier or messaging aggregator
steps.desc: File an abuse report to have the sending number suspended.

steps.title: Confirm the number is suspended and any linked site taken down
steps.desc: Follow up until both actions are confirmed.
steps.outcome: Number suspended and site offline where applicable.

steps.title: Support any customer who responded or clicked the link
steps.desc: For any customer known to have disclosed data or paid, help them secure accounts or dispute payments.

steps.title: Document the campaign and update brand-monitoring rules
steps.desc: Record the sender pattern and message template to sharpen future detection.

steps.title: Identify the sending number/short code and any linked site

steps.outcome: Sending infrastructure and any linked site identified.

steps.title: File a takedown report for any linked site
steps.desc: If the SMS links to a fake site, submit a takedown request to its hosting provider and registrar.

steps.title: Warn customers through official channels
steps.desc: Publish a notice warning customers about the smishing campaign and how genuine organization texts are identified.
steps.outcome: Customers warned against the fake SMS.

ITID-22334.def: A fraudulent response to a customer's public review or complaint, impersonating our brand's official social media/review-management account, used to redirect the customer to a fraudulent 'resolution' channel.
ITID-22334.purpose: Captures a fake public review-response engagement impersonating our brand on a review platform or social media.
scopeIncludes: A fake reply to a public customer complaint, impersonating our official brand account, directing the customer to a fraudulent DM/link/phone number
scopeExcludes: A legitimate response from our actual, verified brand account
ITID-22334.severity: Medium — targets customers already primed to seek resolution, increasing susceptibility.
ITID-22334.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for high-volume or high-profile complaint threads.
ITID-22334.escalation: Escalate to brand protection and social media/community management teams.

Customer report of being redirected to an unofficial channel after a public complaint
vectors: Creation of a lookalike social media account mimicking our official handle to monitor and respond to public complaints
rootCauses: Public complaint threads create a visible, targetable list of frustrated customers
controls: Verified/badge-authenticated official social media accounts
Social listening for lookalike account activity
ITID-22334.detection: Social listening tools and customer reports.
ITID-22334.response: Report the impersonating account to the platform and issue a customer advisory.
metrics: Count of fake review-response impersonation accounts reported

playbook.name: Response: Fake Public Review-Response Engagement
playbook.description: For a fraudulent account impersonating this organization's official presence to publicly reply to customer reviews/comments on a review site or social platform, typically to redirect victims to a scam channel.

steps.title: Post a public clarification from the organization's verified account
steps.desc: Reply publicly from the genuine official account clarifying that the other account is not affiliated with the organization.

steps.title: Report the impersonating infrastructure/account to the responsible provider or platform
steps.desc: File an abuse report with the relevant registrar, hosting provider, carrier, or platform.

steps.title: Confirm the impersonating infrastructure/account is taken down
steps.desc: Follow up until the takedown/suspension is confirmed.

steps.title: Support any customer who engaged with the impersonating communication
steps.desc: For anyone known to have disclosed data or paid, help them secure accounts or dispute payments.

steps.title: Document the case and evaluate whether it fits an existing category going forward
steps.desc: Record the case to sharpen future detection and categorization.

steps.title: Identify the sending infrastructure or account
steps.desc: Identify the domain, number, or account used to impersonate the organization.

steps.title: Warn customers through official channels
steps.desc: Publish a notice warning customers about the fraudulent communication.

ITID-22411.def: An adversary gains control of a real executive's actual corporate mailbox and uses that genuine, authenticated identity to send fraudulent payment/data requests to external recipients such as customers, vendors, or partners.
ITID-22411.purpose: Captures a compromised legitimate executive mailbox at our organization used to defraud external recipients (customers, partners, financial counterparties).
scopeIncludes: A confirmed account takeover of a real executive mailbox used to send fraudulent requests to external parties
Fraudulent wire/payment instructions sent from the genuine, compromised mailbox to an external recipient
scopeExcludes: An external attacker impersonating an executive (via spoofing or a fabricated identity, not mailbox compromise) to defraud our own organization's internal staff (see ITID-53111, Executive Impersonation Fraud, BEC Context)

The underlying mailbox account-compromise incident itself, which is tracked as a security/credential-compromise incident under the relevant account-compromise ITID; this leaf tracks the external-fraud outcome and brand-trust impact
ITID-22411.severity: Critical — a genuine, authenticated executive identity carries maximum trust and bypasses most external recipient scrutiny.
ITID-22411.escalation: Escalate immediately to IR, legal, and executive leadership; notify all external parties who may have received fraudulent communications from the compromised mailbox.
indicators: Unusual sending patterns or financial requests from a genuine executive mailbox
External recipient report of a suspicious payment request that, on verification, came from the real executive address
vectors: Prior credential phishing or MFA-fatigue attack against the executive leading to mailbox takeover
Session token theft via an AiTM kit
rootCauses: Insufficient MFA/conditional-access hardening on executive accounts given their high external-fraud value
controls: Enhanced MFA/conditional access for executive accounts
Out-of-band verification requirement for payment/wire instruction changes
External partner advisory on verifying financial instruction changes
ITID-22411.detection: Moderate — mailbox-side anomaly detection (impossible travel, unusual send volume) plus external recipient reports; genuine mailbox use makes email-authentication-based detection ineffective.
ITID-22411.response: Immediate account lockdown/reset, forensic review of mailbox activity, and outreach to all potentially affected external recipients.
metrics: Time to detect and contain mailbox compromise
External parties notified per incident
sops: Business Email Compromise External Notification SOP
ITID-22411.notes: Direction is the key scope decision: this leaf covers our real executive being used (via compromise) to defraud external third parties, the mirror image of ITID-53111 where an external actor impersonates an executive to defraud us.

playbook.name: Response: BEC via Compromised Legitimate Executive Mailbox
playbook.description: For business email compromise where an attacker has gained control of a real executive's mailbox at this organization and uses it to send fraudulent payment/wire instructions.

steps.title: Confirm the mailbox is compromised and scope the attacker's access
