steps.desc: Review mailbox sign-in logs, mail-forwarding/rule changes, and sent items to confirm compromise and determine how long the attacker had access and what they viewed or sent.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with IT/security for log review.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed and scope of access/exfiltration documented.

steps.title: Lock down the compromised mailbox immediately
steps.desc: Force a password reset, revoke all active sessions and app passwords, remove any malicious forwarding/inbox rules, and re-enroll MFA.

steps.title: Confirm the mailbox is fully clean and no persistence remains
steps.desc: Verify no malicious rules, delegated access, or forwarding remain, and that credentials have been fully rotated.

steps.title: Track recovery of any transferred funds
steps.desc: Follow up with the bank/law enforcement on recall status until resolved.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered or loss confirmed and documented for finance/insurance purposes.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce payment-verification controls
steps.desc: Record the compromise vector and reinforce out-of-band verification requirements for any payment/wire-instruction change.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and control gap addressed.

steps.title: Identify all fraudulent messages sent and their recipients
steps.desc: Search sent mail and any hidden mailbox rules for fraudulent payment/wire-instruction messages and identify who received them.
steps.outcome: List of fraudulent messages and recipients compiled.

steps.title: Determine whether any payment was made based on the fraudulent instructions
steps.desc: Contact finance/AP to check whether any wire transfer or payment was executed in response to the fraudulent messages.
steps.abort: If no payment was made, proceed directly to notifying affected recipients.

steps.title: If a payment was made, initiate an emergency bank recall
steps.desc: Immediately contact the sending bank's fraud department to request a recall/hold on the transfer, and file a report with law enforcement (e.g., via the relevant financial-fraud reporting channel) as required for recovery eligibility.
steps.guidance: Speed is critical — recall success drops sharply after the first 24 hours.
steps.outcome: Recall request filed with the bank; law enforcement report filed.
steps.tool: Bank fraud department / law enforcement financial-fraud unit

steps.title: Notify all recipients of the fraudulent messages
steps.desc: Contact every internal and external recipient of the fraudulent messages to warn them not to act on the instructions.
steps.outcome: All recipients warned before further action is taken.

ITID-22412.def: An adversary sets an email display name to match a real executive's name, sending from an unrelated (often free webmail) address, to defraud external recipients who are relying on the visible display name rather than the underlying address.
ITID-22412.purpose: Captures display-name spoofing of a real executive (no mailbox or domain compromise) used to defraud external recipients.
scopeIncludes: Display-name spoofing of a named executive sent to external customers/partners/vendors from an unrelated address
Free-webmail-based impersonation of an executive's name targeting an external party
scopeExcludes: Display-name spoofing targeting our own internal employees (see ITID-11126, Spoofed Sender Identity Spear Phishing)
ITID-22412.escalation: Escalate to brand protection and notify affected external parties.
indicators: External recipient report of an email 'from' the executive's name but an unrelated email address
Free-webmail domain in the underlying sender address
vectors: Free webmail account creation with a matching display name
No email compromise required — purely a social engineering technique
rootCauses: External recipients trusting the visible display name without checking the underlying address
No DMARC/authentication signal to distinguish this from ITID-22411, since no domain is spoofed
controls: External partner education on verifying sender addresses, not just display names
Out-of-band verification for financial instruction changes
ITID-22412.detection: Weak on our side — this vector generally does not touch our infrastructure at all since it's sent from an unrelated address; primarily detected via external recipient reports.
ITID-22412.response: Issue advisory to known partners/customers and support any affected recipient's fraud investigation.
metrics: Count of reported display-name spoofing incidents
sops: Business Email Compromise External Notification SOP
ITID-22412.notes: Differentiated from ITID-22411 by mechanism: no compromise or domain infrastructure at all here, purely a spoofed display name; also distinguished from ITID-11126 by direction (external victim vs. internal).

playbook.name: Response: BEC via Display-Name Spoofing (No Domain Compromise)
playbook.description: For business email compromise where the attacker spoofs an executive's display name (e.g., "Jane Smith, CEO") from an unrelated external address, with no compromise of this organization's mail systems.

steps.title: Confirm the message is display-name spoofing, not a domain/mailbox compromise
steps.desc: Inspect the actual sending address and headers to confirm the executive's name is spoofed on an unrelated external mailbox, ruling out compromise of this organization's own systems.
steps.outcome: Confirmed display-name spoof with the true sending address identified.
steps.abort: If headers instead show the real executive mailbox or domain, redirect to the mailbox/domain-compromise BEC playbook.

steps.title: Block the sending address/domain at the email gateway
steps.desc: Add the true sending address and domain to the email security gateway's blocklist.
steps.outcome: Sender blocked from reaching further recipients.

steps.title: Confirm no further messages are reaching staff
steps.desc: Verify the blocklist is effective and no variant addresses are still getting through.

steps.title: Track recovery of any transferred funds
steps.desc: Follow up with the bank/law enforcement on recall status until resolved.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered or loss confirmed and documented.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce display-name-spoof awareness
steps.desc: Record the lure and reinforce staff training on checking the true sending address, not just the display name.

steps.title: Identify all recipients and requested actions
steps.desc: Determine who received the message and what action (payment, gift cards, data) was requested.

steps.title: Determine whether any payment was made based on the fraudulent instructions
steps.desc: Contact finance/AP to check whether any payment or gift-card purchase was made in response.
steps.abort: If no payment was made, proceed to notifying recipients.

steps.title: If a payment was made, initiate an emergency bank recall
steps.desc: Contact the sending bank's fraud department to request a recall/hold, and file a law enforcement report.
steps.guidance: Speed is critical for recall success.
steps.outcome: Recall request filed; law enforcement report filed.
steps.tool: Bank fraud department / law enforcement financial-fraud unit

steps.title: Notify all recipients of the fraudulent message
steps.desc: Warn everyone who received it not to act on the instructions.

ITID-22413.def: An adversary registers a lookalike domain of our organization and sends email as a named executive from that domain to defraud external recipients who do not scrutinize the domain closely.
ITID-22413.purpose: Captures use of a lookalike domain email (impersonating our corporate domain) carrying a real executive's identity to defraud external recipients.
scopeIncludes: Email sent from a typosquat/lookalike domain of ours, impersonating a named executive, to an external party
Lookalike-domain BEC confirmed via header/domain analysis
scopeExcludes: Lookalike domain BEC targeting our own internal employees (would fall under the equivalent ITID-10000 phishing/BEC leaves, e.g. ITID-11126)
ITID-22413.escalation: Escalate to brand protection for domain takedown and notify affected external parties.
indicators: Sender domain closely resembling but not matching our real domain
External recipient report of a suspicious payment/data request
vectors: Lookalike domain registration (cross-referenced with the Phishing Domains > Lookalike Domains leaves) paired with MX record setup for outbound email
rootCauses: No defensive registration of the specific lookalike variant used
controls: Proactive lookalike domain monitoring with MX-record change alerting
External partner education on verifying sender domains
ITID-22413.detection: Strong when correlated with domain-monitoring MX-record alerts; otherwise relies on external recipient reports.
ITID-22413.response: Domain takedown and outreach to affected external recipients.
metrics: Count of lookalike-domain BEC incidents
Mean time from MX activation to detection
sops: Business Email Compromise External Notification SOP
detections: Lookalike domain MX-record change alerting (cross-referenced with ITID-22214)
ITID-22413.notes: Directly ties to the domain-registration finding under ITID-22214 (pre-positioned lookalike domain) once that domain acquires MX records and is used in a BEC attempt.

playbook.name: Response: BEC via Lookalike Domain Email
playbook.description: For business email compromise sent from an attacker-registered lookalike domain (e.g., a typosquat or combosquat of this organization's real domain) impersonating an executive.

steps.title: Confirm the sending domain is a lookalike, not the real domain
steps.desc: Compare the sending domain character-by-character against this organization's real domain to confirm it is a distinct, attacker-registered lookalike.

steps.title: File a takedown report with the registrar and block the domain at the email gateway
steps.desc: Submit an abuse/trademark report to the registrar to suspend the domain, and immediately block the domain at the organization's own email security gateway.
steps.tool: Registrar abuse portal / Email security gateway

steps.title: Confirm the domain is taken down or suspended
steps.desc: Follow up until the registrar action results in the domain no longer being usable.

steps.title: Track recovery of any transferred funds
steps.desc: Follow up with the bank/law enforcement on recall status until resolved.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered or loss confirmed and documented.

steps.title: Document the domain pattern and tune email-security and monitoring rules
steps.desc: Record the lookalike pattern to sharpen future detection at both the domain-monitoring and email-gateway layers.

steps.title: Identify the registrar/hosting of the lookalike domain and all recipients
steps.desc: Determine where the domain is registered/hosted, and identify all recipients and the requested action.
steps.outcome: Domain infrastructure and recipient list documented.

steps.title: Determine whether any payment was made based on the fraudulent instructions
steps.desc: Contact finance/AP to check whether any payment was made in response.
steps.abort: If no payment was made, proceed to notifying recipients.

steps.title: If a payment was made, initiate an emergency bank recall
steps.desc: Contact the sending bank's fraud department to request a recall/hold, and file a law enforcement report.
steps.outcome: Recall request filed; law enforcement report filed.
steps.tool: Bank fraud department / law enforcement financial-fraud unit

steps.title: Notify all recipients of the fraudulent message
steps.desc: Warn everyone who received it not to act on the instructions.

ITID-22414.def: An adversary compromises the email account of one of our vendors or third parties, and uses the trusted relationship with our organization (impersonating our executives or referencing our real transactions) to defraud that vendor's other customers or our own shared counterparties.
ITID-22414.purpose: Captures BEC conducted via a compromised vendor or third-party email account, where our organization's executive identity or business relationship is leveraged to defraud a party downstream in the supply chain.
scopeIncludes: A compromised vendor mailbox used to send fraudulent communications referencing our organization/executives to defraud a shared customer or counterparty
Confirmed cases where our brand/relationship context is used as social proof in a vendor-mailbox BEC scheme
scopeExcludes: A compromised vendor mailbox used to defraud our own organization directly (see ITID-53121, Vendor Invoice Fraud, BEC Context)
ITID-22414.escalation: Escalate to brand protection and legal; coordinate with the affected vendor's incident response team.
indicators: A vendor/partner notifies us that their compromised mailbox referenced our organization in a fraud attempt against a third party
Shared customer/counterparty reports a fraudulent request citing our organization
vectors: Credential phishing against a vendor/partner employee leading to mailbox compromise
Reply-chain hijacking of genuine vendor-us correspondence to add a fraudulent third leg
rootCauses: Weak security posture at a third-party vendor outside our direct control, combined with a trusted three-way business relationship
controls: Vendor security requirements/due diligence program
Out-of-band verification requirement for financial instruction changes across the vendor relationship
ITID-22414.detection: Weak on our side — the compromise occurs in a third party's environment; detection relies on the vendor's own IR or a downstream victim's report.
ITID-22414.response: Coordinate with the vendor's IR team and notify any of our own counterparties who may have been targeted using our brand context.
metrics: Count of vendor-mailbox BEC cases referencing our brand
sops: Business Email Compromise External Notification SOP
ITID-22414.notes: Direction is the scope decision: this leaf covers our brand/relationship being weaponized from a compromised vendor mailbox against a third party, the mirror of ITID-53121 where a compromised vendor mailbox defrauds us directly.

playbook.name: Response: BEC via Compromised Vendor/Third-Party Email Account
playbook.description: For business email compromise where a genuine vendor or third-party partner's own email account has been compromised and used to send fraudulent invoice/payment-redirect instructions impersonating that vendor to this organization.

steps.title: Confirm the message came from the vendor's real (compromised) account
steps.desc: Review headers to confirm the message genuinely originated from the vendor's real mailbox/domain rather than a lookalike, indicating the vendor's own account is compromised.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the vendor's real account is compromised.
steps.abort: If the domain is instead a lookalike, redirect to the lookalike-domain BEC playbook.

steps.title: Notify the vendor that their email account is compromised
steps.desc: Contact the vendor through a verified out-of-band channel (a known phone number, not one from the suspicious email) to alert them their account has been compromised and is being used against this organization's staff.
steps.outcome: Vendor notified and engaged in securing their own account.

steps.title: Confirm the vendor's account has been secured
steps.desc: Follow up with the vendor to confirm they have reset credentials and removed any malicious forwarding rules.

steps.title: Track recovery of any transferred funds
steps.desc: Follow up with the bank/law enforcement on recall status until resolved.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered or loss confirmed and documented.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce vendor payment-change verification
steps.desc: Record the incident and reinforce a policy requiring out-of-band verification for any vendor bank-detail change.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and control gap addressed.

steps.title: Identify all recipients and the requested payment/account change
steps.desc: Determine who received the fraudulent instructions and what payment details or bank account change was requested.

steps.title: Determine whether any payment was made or bank details changed based on the fraudulent instructions
steps.desc: Contact finance/AP to check whether any payment was redirected or vendor bank details were updated.
steps.abort: If no payment was made, proceed to internal notification.

steps.title: If a payment was made, initiate an emergency bank recall
steps.desc: Contact the sending bank's fraud department to request a recall/hold, and file a law enforcement report.
steps.outcome: Recall request filed; law enforcement report filed.
steps.tool: Bank fraud department / law enforcement financial-fraud unit

steps.title: Revert any changed bank/payment details and notify internal staff
steps.desc: Restore the vendor's verified original payment details and warn accounts-payable staff not to act on the fraudulent instructions.

ITID-22415.def: A business email compromise incident leveraging our organization's brand or executive identity against an external party, not yet matched to a more specific mailbox-compromise/display-name/lookalike-domain/vendor-compromise leaf.
ITID-22415.purpose: Catch-all for BEC cases leveraging our brand/executive identity against external parties that do not fit a more specific leaf.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered BEC cases pending classification
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-22411 through ITID-22414
BEC where our own organization is the direct financial victim (see the ITID-53100-series)
ITID-22415.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; default High given the financial fraud potential.
ITID-22415.escalation: Reclassify once the specific mechanism is clarified; treat as active fraud until ruled out.
indicators: Report of unclear specific BEC mechanism referencing our brand
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Out-of-band verification requirement for financial instruction changes
ITID-22415.detection: Same telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-22415.response: Investigate and reclassify once confirmed; treat as active fraud in the interim.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-22415.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Business Email Compromise
playbook.description: For business email compromise impersonating an executive of this organization, where the specific vector (mailbox compromise, display-name spoof, lookalike domain, vendor compromise) does not fit an existing category.

steps.title: Determine the compromise vector
steps.desc: Inspect headers and the sending infrastructure to determine whether this is a mailbox compromise, display-name spoof, lookalike domain, or vendor compromise.
steps.abort: If a specific vector is identified, redirect to the matching dedicated playbook.

steps.title: Contain the sending infrastructure or account appropriate to the vector
steps.desc: Block, report, or lock down the sender as appropriate once the vector is known.

steps.title: Confirm the threat is fully contained
steps.desc: Verify no further fraudulent messages are reaching staff.

steps.title: Track recovery of any transferred funds
steps.desc: Follow up until resolved.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered or loss confirmed and documented.

steps.title: Document the incident and evaluate whether it fits an existing category going forward
steps.desc: Record the case to sharpen future detection and categorization.

steps.title: Identify all recipients and requested action
steps.desc: Determine who received the message and what action was requested.

steps.title: Determine whether any payment was made and pursue recall if so
steps.desc: Contact finance/AP to check for any payment made, and if so, contact the bank's fraud department immediately.
steps.outcome: Payment status determined and recall pursued if applicable.

ITID-22421.def: A fraudulent profile on a professional networking platform (e.g., LinkedIn) impersonating a named executive of our organization, used to build false credibility for connection requests, recruitment scams, or follow-on fraud.
ITID-22421.purpose: Captures a fake profile impersonating one of our executives on a professional networking platform.
scopeIncludes: A fake profile using an executive's name/photo/title on a professional networking platform
A fake profile used to send fraudulent connection requests or job offers referencing our organization
scopeExcludes: A compromised, genuine account belonging to the executive (a separate account-compromise incident, not an impersonation)
ITID-22421.severity: Medium, escalating to High if used for follow-on financial fraud or targeted social engineering against our staff/customers.
ITID-22421.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if linked to active fraud.
ITID-22421.escalation: Escalate to brand protection and the affected executive; report to the platform for removal.
indicators: Duplicate/near-duplicate profile of a named executive discovered via platform monitoring or reported by a connection
Fraudulent connection requests sent under the executive's identity
vectors: Scraping publicly available executive photos/bios to build a convincing fake profile
rootCauses: Low identity-verification barriers for profile creation on networking platforms
controls: Executive social media monitoring service
Platform impersonation-reporting relationship
ITID-22421.detection: External social media monitoring and network-connection reports.
ITID-22421.response: Report to the platform for takedown; advise the executive's real connections.
metrics: Count of fake executive profiles detected/removed

playbook.name: Response: Fake Executive Profile on Professional Networking Platform
playbook.description: For a fake profile impersonating an executive of this organization on a professional networking platform (e.g., LinkedIn), used for social engineering or fraud against employees, customers, or partners.

steps.title: Confirm the profile is impersonating the executive
steps.desc: Compare the profile against the executive's genuine account and confirm it is unauthorized, capturing the profile URL and content.

steps.title: Report the profile to the platform's impersonation/trust and safety team
steps.desc: Submit an impersonation report requesting profile removal.

steps.title: Confirm the profile is removed
steps.desc: Follow up until the platform confirms removal.

steps.title: Support anyone who engaged with the fake profile and disclosed data or funds
steps.desc: Help affected individuals secure accounts or dispute any resulting payments.

steps.title: Document the case and monitor for repeat impersonation
steps.desc: Record the profile and consider periodic searches for further executive impersonation.

steps.title: Assess how the profile is being used
steps.desc: Check whether the fake profile is being used to send connection requests, messages, or job offers, which indicates active social-engineering intent.

steps.title: Warn employees, customers, or partners if the profile has been actively messaging them
steps.desc: Notify anyone known to have been contacted by the fake profile.

ITID-22422.def: A fraudulent profile impersonating a named executive, used to post or privately send fabricated financial statements, forward-looking claims, or investment solicitations intended to manipulate investor or shareholder behavior.
ITID-22422.purpose: Captures a fake executive profile specifically used to manipulate investors or shareholders (e.g., pump-and-dump, fake financial announcements).
scopeIncludes: A fake executive profile posting fabricated earnings/financial claims
A fake executive account used to solicit fraudulent investment (e.g., crypto scam) citing our company
scopeExcludes: Legitimate executive commentary from a verified, genuine account
ITID-22422.severity: Critical — market/securities implications in addition to brand harm.
ITID-22422.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, investor relations, and executive leadership; consider securities-regulator notification depending on jurisdiction and materiality.
indicators: Fake profile posting financial claims attributed to the executive
Unusual trading activity correlated with a fake post's timing
vectors: Fake profile combined with a coordinated social media/forum posting campaign to maximize market impact
rootCauses: High market sensitivity to perceived executive statements, combined with low platform identity verification
controls: Executive/brand social media monitoring with market-sensitive keyword alerting
Investor relations rapid-response and public correction process
ITID-22422.detection: External social media monitoring; correlation with trading activity requires coordination with investor relations/legal.
ITID-22422.response: Immediate public correction, platform takedown request, and regulatory consultation as warranted.
metrics: Time to public correction
Count of investor-manipulation impersonation incidents
detections: Executive social media monitoring with market-sensitive alerting
ITID-22422.notes: Highest-severity leaf in this sibling group given securities/market implications; differentiated from ITID-22421 by intended harm (market manipulation vs. general credibility abuse).

playbook.name: Response: Fake Executive Profile Used for Investor/Shareholder Manipulation
playbook.description: For a fake profile impersonating an executive of this organization used to spread false statements to investors/shareholders, potentially affecting stock price or market perception.

steps.title: Confirm the profile and its false statements
steps.desc: Confirm the profile is unauthorized and document the specific statements made about the organization's financial position, deals, or outlook.
steps.outcome: Confirmed impersonation and statements captured verbatim.

steps.title: Report the profile to the platform's impersonation/trust and safety team
steps.desc: Submit an impersonation report requesting immediate profile removal, citing potential market-manipulation harm.
steps.outcome: Report submitted with expedited handling requested where available.

steps.title: Confirm the profile and false statements are removed
steps.desc: Follow up until the platform confirms removal.

steps.title: Monitor market/investor sentiment following the correction
steps.desc: Track investor and media reaction to confirm the correction is being received and the false narrative is not persisting.

steps.title: Document the incident for legal/compliance and IR records
steps.desc: Record the case, statements made, and response for the legal/compliance and investor-relations record.

steps.title: Assess market/investor exposure
steps.desc: Determine how widely the statements have circulated and whether there is any indication of market impact (unusual trading volume/price movement), looping in investor relations.

steps.title: Engage legal, investor relations, and compliance
steps.desc: Loop in legal/compliance to assess disclosure obligations and coordinate a public correction if the false statements are materially significant.
steps.outcome: Legal/compliance/IR engaged and a response plan agreed.

steps.title: Issue a public clarification through official channels
steps.desc: Publish an official statement correcting the record for investors/shareholders.
steps.guidance: Coordinate timing and wording with legal/IR.

ITID-22423.def: A fraudulent profile or post impersonating a named executive, used to falsely announce a resignation, termination, or leadership succession, intended to cause reputational, operational, or market disruption.
ITID-22423.purpose: Captures a fake executive profile used to falsely announce an executive's departure or a succession event.
scopeIncludes: A fake profile/post falsely announcing an executive's departure or replacement
Fabricated 'farewell' or succession-announcement content impersonating the executive
scopeExcludes: A genuine, authorized announcement from official corporate or verified executive channels
ITID-22423.severity: High — false leadership-change news can cause immediate reputational and market disruption.
ITID-22423.escalation: Escalate immediately to corporate communications, investor relations, and legal for rapid public correction.
indicators: Fake profile/post announcing a leadership change not corroborated by official channels
Media inquiries following an unverified succession claim
vectors: Fake profile timed around a period of genuine leadership speculation or corporate uncertainty to maximize believability
rootCauses: Public appetite for leadership-change news creates high viral potential for false claims
controls: Executive/brand social media monitoring
Rapid corporate communications correction process
ITID-22423.detection: External social media monitoring and media/analyst inbound inquiries.
ITID-22423.response: Immediate public correction via verified official channels and platform takedown request.
metrics: Time to public correction
ITID-22423.notes: No cross-domain overlap identified; distinguished from ITID-22422 by the nature of the false claim (leadership change vs. financial/investment manipulation).

playbook.name: Response: Fake Executive Profile Announcing False Departure/Succession
playbook.description: For a fake profile or post impersonating an executive of this organization to falsely announce their departure, resignation, or a leadership succession, risking reputational and market confusion.

steps.title: Confirm the profile/post and the false announcement
steps.desc: Confirm the profile is unauthorized and document the exact false announcement made.
steps.outcome: Confirmed impersonation and false statement captured verbatim.

steps.title: Report the profile/post to the platform's impersonation/trust and safety team
steps.desc: Submit an impersonation report requesting immediate removal.

steps.title: Confirm the profile/post is removed
steps.desc: Follow up until the platform confirms removal.

steps.title: Monitor media and investor reaction following the correction
steps.desc: Track coverage and sentiment to confirm the false narrative has been corrected.

steps.title: Document the incident for PR and IR records
steps.desc: Record the case and response for future reference, including response-time benchmarks.

steps.title: Assess spread and confirm with the real executive
steps.desc: Gauge how widely the false announcement has circulated, and confirm directly with the real executive that no genuine departure/succession is occurring (or clarify the actual facts if it partially overlaps a real event).
steps.outcome: Spread assessed and facts confirmed with the executive.

steps.title: Issue a public clarification through official channels
steps.desc: Coordinate with PR/communications and investor relations to publish an official statement correcting the record before the false narrative spreads further.

ITID-22431.def: A voice call, potentially using AI voice-cloning/deepfake technology, impersonating a named executive of our organization to instruct finance staff or an external party to execute an urgent, unauthorized wire transfer.
ITID-22431.purpose: Captures a phone call (potentially deepfake-voice) impersonating a real executive to authorize an urgent, fraudulent wire transfer.
scopeIncludes: A confirmed or suspected deepfake-voice call impersonating an executive to authorize a wire transfer
A traditional (non-deepfake) voice impersonation of an executive used for the same purpose
scopeExcludes: Generic vishing/CEO-fraud calls with no specific named-executive voice impersonation, targeting our own staff without leveraging a real executive identity (see ITID-11211, Impersonation Vishing Call)
ITID-22431.severity: Critical — direct, often irreversible financial loss potential.
ITID-22431.escalation: Escalate immediately to finance leadership, IR, and legal; attempt payment recall through the bank immediately upon detection.
indicators: Urgent wire request citing unusual secrecy/urgency, attributed to a call from the executive
Voice characteristics reported as slightly 'off' by the recipient (possible deepfake artifact)
vectors: AI voice cloning trained on publicly available executive audio (earnings calls, interviews, conference talks)
Combined with a supporting spoofed email or lookalike-domain follow-up for corroboration
rootCauses: Abundant public audio/video of executives available for voice-cloning training
Absence of a mandatory out-of-band verification step for wire authorization
controls: Mandatory out-of-band, pre-agreed verification (callback to a known number, code word) for any wire-transfer authorization
Finance team training on deepfake voice fraud indicators
ITID-22431.detection: Weak technical detection for the call itself; strongest control is a mandatory verification process rather than detection.
ITID-22431.response: Immediate payment recall attempt, IR engagement, and law enforcement notification.
metrics: Count of executive voice-impersonation fraud attempts
Recovery rate on attempted fraudulent transfers
sops: Business Email Compromise External Notification SOP
ITID-22431.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11211 by specificity: this leaf requires impersonation of a real, named executive's identity/voice, not a generic vishing pretext.

playbook.name: Response: Executive Impersonation Call Authorizing Urgent Wire Transfer
playbook.description: For a phone call (often AI-voice-cloned) impersonating an executive of this organization, pressuring an employee to urgently authorize a wire transfer outside normal approval channels.

steps.title: Confirm the call was fraudulent and capture details
steps.desc: Confirm with the employee the call's content, the number/caller ID used, and the urgency/pressure tactics applied, and rule out a genuine (if unusual) request from the real executive.
steps.guidance: Do not assume urgency alone proves fraud, but treat any off-process payment request as suspect by default.
steps.outcome: Call details documented and confirmed suspicious/fraudulent.

steps.title: Perform an urgent out-of-band verification callback to the real executive
steps.desc: Call the executive back on a known, independently sourced number (never a number provided during the suspicious call) to confirm whether they made the request.
steps.guidance: This step should happen in parallel with, not after, transfer-status checks.
steps.outcome: Request confirmed fraudulent via independent verification.
steps.abort: If the executive confirms the request was genuine, stand down the fraud response and close as a false positive.

steps.title: Identify and block the calling number if reused
steps.desc: Report the calling number to the carrier if it appears to be part of a targeted campaign, and confirm the incident is contained.
steps.outcome: Number reported where applicable; incident contained.

steps.title: Track recovery of any transferred funds
steps.desc: Follow up with the bank/law enforcement on recall status until resolved.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered or loss confirmed and documented.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce callback-verification policy for payment requests
steps.desc: Record the technique (including any AI voice-cloning indicators) and reinforce a mandatory out-of-band callback policy for any urgent payment request.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and control gap addressed.

steps.title: Determine whether a wire transfer was initiated or completed
steps.desc: Check with finance/treasury whether any transfer was initiated, and its current status (pending, sent, cleared).

steps.title: If a transfer was made, initiate an emergency bank recall
steps.desc: Immediately contact the sending bank's fraud department to request a recall/hold, and file a report with law enforcement's financial-fraud unit.
steps.guidance: Speed is critical — recall success drops sharply after the first 24 hours.
steps.outcome: Recall request filed; law enforcement report filed.
steps.tool: Bank fraud department / law enforcement financial-fraud unit

steps.title: Halt any further pending action tied to the call
steps.desc: Ensure no additional payments or actions proceed based on the impersonation call while the incident is investigated.
steps.outcome: No further action taken on the fraudulent request.

ITID-22432.def: A voice call impersonating a named executive of our organization, directed at our internal IT helpdesk, used to socially engineer a password reset, MFA reset, or access-elevation action.
ITID-22432.purpose: Captures a phone call impersonating a real executive directed at our own IT helpdesk to request a password or access reset.
scopeIncludes: A call impersonating a specific named executive targeting our IT helpdesk for a credential/access reset
scopeExcludes: A generic (non-named-executive) helpdesk-impersonation vishing call (see ITID-95121, Vishing Test Targeting Help Desk Impersonation Scenario, for the simulated/testing equivalent; live generic cases fall under the ITID-11000 vishing leaves)
ITID-22432.severity: Critical — a successful reset can grant an attacker executive-level account access.
ITID-22432.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT security and executive leadership; lock down the targeted account pending verification.
indicators: Helpdesk report of an urgent reset request citing executive authority with pressure to bypass standard verification
Call originating from a spoofed or unfamiliar number claiming to be the executive
vectors: Social engineering the helpdesk by invoking executive urgency/authority to bypass identity verification steps
rootCauses: Helpdesk verification procedures that can be overridden by perceived seniority/urgency
controls: Mandatory strong identity verification for helpdesk resets with no seniority-based exception
Callback verification to a known-good number before any executive-account reset
ITID-22432.detection: Weak technical detection; strongest control is a hardened, exception-free helpdesk verification procedure.
ITID-22432.response: Immediate account lockdown and verification if a reset was completed; helpdesk staff debrief and process review.
metrics: Count of executive-impersonation helpdesk social engineering attempts
Helpdesk verification bypass rate
ITID-22432.notes: This leaf specifically requires impersonation of a real named executive; a generic caller claiming to be 'IT support' or an unnamed employee falls under the ITID-11000 vishing leaves instead.

playbook.name: Response: Executive Impersonation Call to IT Helpdesk Requesting Password/Access Reset
playbook.description: For a phone call impersonating an executive of this organization to the IT helpdesk, pressuring staff to reset a password, MFA, or grant access outside normal identity-verification procedures.

steps.title: Confirm the call was fraudulent and capture details
steps.desc: Confirm with the helpdesk staff member the call's content, the number/caller ID used, and what was requested and/or granted.

steps.title: Perform an urgent out-of-band verification callback to the real executive
steps.desc: Call the executive back on a known, independently sourced number to confirm whether they made the request.
steps.outcome: Request confirmed fraudulent via independent verification.
steps.abort: If the executive confirms the request was genuine, stand down and close as a false positive.

steps.title: Confirm the account and any downstream systems are secure
steps.desc: Verify no persistence (forwarding rules, delegated access, new devices) remains from the exposure window.
steps.outcome: Account and downstream systems confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore normal account access for the legitimate user
steps.desc: Ensure the real executive/user has working, securely re-verified access.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce helpdesk identity-verification procedures
steps.desc: Record the technique and reinforce (or introduce) a mandatory callback/secondary-verification step for any credential or access reset requested by phone.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and control gap addressed.

steps.title: Determine whether any reset or access grant was completed
steps.desc: Check helpdesk/IAM logs to determine whether a password reset, MFA re-enrollment, or access grant was actually completed before verification.

steps.title: If any reset/access was granted, immediately revoke it and re-secure the account
steps.desc: Reverse any password reset, MFA change, or access grant made based on the fraudulent call, force a fresh reset through verified channels, and revoke active sessions.
steps.outcome: Account access restored to a secure, verified state.

steps.title: Check for any account activity during the exposure window
steps.desc: Review the account's activity between the fraudulent reset and its remediation for signs of unauthorized use.
steps.outcome: Exposure window activity reviewed; any unauthorized use identified.

ITID-22433.def: A voice call impersonating a named executive of our organization, directed at a board member or investor, used to extract confidential information, solicit an urgent decision, or authorize a fraudulent action under apparent executive authority.
ITID-22433.purpose: Captures a phone call impersonating a real executive directed at a board member or investor to extract information or authorize an action.
scopeIncludes: A call impersonating an executive targeting a board member for confidential information or an urgent decision
A call impersonating an executive targeting an investor for the same purpose
scopeExcludes: Calls targeting internal finance/helpdesk staff (see ITID-22431/22432)
ITID-22433.severity: Critical — board/investor targets often have access to highly sensitive strategic or financial information.
ITID-22433.escalation: Escalate immediately to the general counsel, board secretary, and investor relations.
indicators: Board member/investor report of an unusual call requesting confidential information or urgent action attributed to the executive
vectors: Voice impersonation combined with research on upcoming board matters (e.g., an anticipated deal) to add plausibility
rootCauses: Board members/investors often lack the same verification training as internal finance/helpdesk staff
controls: Board/investor briefing on executive-impersonation fraud and verification procedures
Pre-agreed out-of-band verification channel for sensitive board communications
ITID-22433.detection: Weak technical detection; relies on board/investor awareness and reporting.
ITID-22433.response: Immediate verification with the real executive and legal review of any information believed disclosed.
metrics: Count of board/investor-targeted executive impersonation attempts
ITID-22433.notes: No cross-domain overlap identified; differentiated from ITID-22431/22432 by target audience (board/investor vs. finance/helpdesk).

playbook.name: Response: Executive Impersonation Call to Board Member/Investor
playbook.description: For a phone call impersonating an executive of this organization to a board member or investor, seeking sensitive information, an urgent decision, or a wire transfer under false pretenses.

steps.title: Confirm the call was fraudulent and capture details
steps.desc: Confirm with the board member/investor the call's content, the number/caller ID used, and what was requested or disclosed.

steps.title: Perform an urgent out-of-band verification callback to the real executive
steps.desc: Call the executive back on a known, independently sourced number to confirm whether they made the request.
steps.outcome: Request confirmed fraudulent via independent verification.
steps.abort: If the executive confirms the request was genuine, stand down and close as a false positive.

steps.title: Confirm no further contact attempts are succeeding
steps.desc: Verify the board member/investor and others in similar roles are aware and the calling number is not reaching further targets.

steps.title: Track recovery of any transferred funds
steps.desc: Follow up with the bank/law enforcement on recall status until resolved.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered or loss confirmed and documented.

steps.title: Document the incident and brief the board on verification practices
steps.desc: Record the case and brief the board/investor relations on out-of-band verification practices for future contact.

steps.title: Determine whether any sensitive information was disclosed or funds transferred
steps.desc: Establish whether the board member/investor disclosed non-public information, made a decision, or transferred funds based on the call.

steps.title: If a transfer was made, initiate an emergency bank recall
steps.desc: Contact the sending bank's fraud department to request a recall/hold, and file a law enforcement report.
steps.outcome: Recall request filed; law enforcement report filed.
steps.tool: Bank fraud department / law enforcement financial-fraud unit

steps.title: If non-public information was disclosed, engage legal/compliance on insider-trading exposure
steps.desc: If the disclosed information was material non-public information, immediately involve legal/compliance to assess trading-restriction or disclosure obligations.
steps.outcome: Legal/compliance engaged and any necessary restrictions/disclosures actioned.

ITID-22434.def: A voice call impersonating a named executive of our organization, not yet matched to a more specific wire-transfer/helpdesk/board-investor leaf.
ITID-22434.purpose: Catch-all for executive call impersonation cases that do not fit a more specific leaf.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered executive call impersonation cases pending classification
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-22431 through ITID-22433
ITID-22434.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; default High given financial/reputational fraud potential.
ITID-22434.escalation: Reclassify once the specific target/purpose is clarified; treat as active fraud until ruled out.
indicators: Report of unclear specific call target/purpose
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Out-of-band verification requirement
ITID-22434.detection: Same telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-22434.response: Investigate and reclassify once confirmed; treat as active fraud in the interim.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-22434.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Executive Call Impersonation
playbook.description: For a phone call impersonating an executive of this organization, where the specific target (wire-transfer request, helpdesk reset, board/investor) does not fit an existing category.

steps.title: Confirm the call was fraudulent and capture details
steps.desc: Confirm with the recipient the call's content, the number/caller ID used, and exactly what was requested.

steps.title: Perform an urgent out-of-band verification callback to the real executive
steps.desc: Call the executive back on a known, independently sourced number to confirm whether they made the request.
steps.outcome: Request confirmed fraudulent via independent verification.
steps.abort: If the executive confirms the request was genuine, stand down and close as a false positive.

steps.title: Confirm no further contact attempts are succeeding
steps.desc: Verify the calling number is not reaching further targets and the incident is contained.

steps.title: Restore any affected access or track fund recovery
steps.desc: Follow up until any affected access is fully restored to a secure state or funds are recovered.

steps.title: Document the incident and evaluate whether it fits an existing category going forward
steps.desc: Record the case to sharpen future detection and categorization.

steps.title: Determine whether any action was taken based on the call
steps.desc: Establish whether any payment, access grant, or disclosure occurred as a result of the call.

steps.title: Reverse or halt any action taken and pursue recall/recovery if funds moved
steps.desc: Reverse any access grant, or if funds were transferred, immediately contact the bank's fraud department and file a law enforcement report.
steps.tool: Bank fraud department / law enforcement financial-fraud unit

ITID-22511.def: An adversary compromises the real account/domain of a vendor connected to our brand's business ecosystem and uses that genuine, trusted vendor identity to defraud our customers or partners in transactions that reference or rely on our relationship with that vendor.
ITID-22511.purpose: Captures a compromised real vendor account or domain within our extended partner ecosystem used to defraud our customers or other partners referencing our business relationship.
scopeIncludes: A compromised real vendor account used to send fraudulent invoices/instructions to our customers or partners, referencing the vendor's relationship with us
Confirmed vendor-domain compromise used to attack parties beyond our own organization
scopeExcludes: A compromised vendor account/domain used to defraud our own organization's accounts payable directly (see ITID-53121, Vendor Invoice Fraud, BEC Context) — that is the internal-victim mirror of this leaf
ITID-22511.escalation: Escalate to brand protection and legal; coordinate with the compromised vendor's IR team and notify affected customers/partners.
indicators: A customer/partner reports a fraudulent invoice referencing our vendor relationship, traced to a compromised vendor account
Vendor notifies us of a mailbox/domain compromise with evidence of external targeting beyond our own organization
vectors: Credential phishing against vendor staff leading to account/domain takeover
Reply-chain hijacking of genuine three-way vendor-us-customer correspondence
rootCauses: Weak security posture at a vendor outside our direct control, combined with a visible three-way trust relationship
controls: Vendor security due-diligence/requirements program
Out-of-band verification requirement for payment-detail changes across vendor-brokered transactions
ITID-22511.detection: Weak on our side — compromise occurs in the vendor's environment; relies on the vendor's IR or a downstream victim's report.
ITID-22511.response: Coordinate with the vendor's IR team and notify any customers/partners who may have been targeted using the vendor relationship.
metrics: Count of vendor-compromise cases targeting customers/partners
sops: Business Email Compromise External Notification SOP
ITID-22511.notes: Direction is the scope decision: this leaf covers a real vendor relationship being weaponized against our customers/partners, distinct from ITID-53121 where a compromised vendor account defrauds our own organization directly.

playbook.name: Response: Impersonation via Compromised Real Vendor Account/Domain
playbook.description: For fraudulent communications sent from a real vendor's genuine, but compromised, email account or domain, impersonating that vendor to request payment redirects or sensitive data from this organization.

steps.title: Confirm the message came from the vendor's real (compromised) account
steps.desc: Review headers to confirm the message genuinely originated from the vendor's real domain/mailbox, indicating their account is compromised rather than spoofed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the vendor's real account is compromised.

steps.title: Verify the request out-of-band directly with the vendor
steps.desc: Contact the vendor through a previously known, verified channel (not any contact info from the suspicious message) to confirm whether the request is genuine.
steps.outcome: Request confirmed fraudulent via independent verification, and vendor alerted their account is compromised.
steps.abort: If the vendor confirms the request was genuine, stand down and close as a false positive.

steps.title: Confirm the vendor's account has been secured
steps.desc: Follow up with the vendor to confirm they have reset credentials and removed any malicious mailbox rules.

steps.title: Track recovery of any transferred funds
steps.desc: Follow up with the bank/law enforcement on recall status until resolved.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered or loss confirmed and documented.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce vendor payment-change verification
steps.desc: Record the incident and reinforce a policy requiring out-of-band verification for any vendor payment-detail change.

steps.title: Identify what was requested and by whom it was received
steps.desc: Determine the specific request (payment redirect, data, credentials) and which staff received it.

steps.title: Determine whether any payment was made or data disclosed
steps.desc: Check with finance/relevant teams whether any payment was made or data disclosed based on the fraudulent request.

steps.title: If a payment was made, initiate an emergency bank recall
steps.desc: Contact the sending bank's fraud department to request a recall/hold, and file a law enforcement report.
steps.outcome: Recall request filed; law enforcement report filed.
steps.tool: Bank fraud department / law enforcement financial-fraud unit

steps.title: Notify internal staff and revert any changed payment details
steps.desc: Warn relevant staff not to act on the fraudulent request and restore any changed vendor payment details to the verified originals.

ITID-22512.def: An adversary invents a wholly fictitious vendor entity, falsely claiming a supply or service relationship with our organization, to defraud our customers or partners who believe the arrangement is genuine.
ITID-22512.purpose: Captures an entirely fabricated vendor identity (no real vendor exists) invented to defraud our customers or partners by falsely claiming a relationship with us.
scopeIncludes: A fake vendor entity with no real underlying business, claiming an authorized relationship with us, contacting our customers/partners
Fabricated vendor invoices/contracts referencing a nonexistent business relationship with us
scopeExcludes: Impersonation of an actual, existing vendor (see ITID-22511)
ITID-22512.escalation: Escalate to brand protection and legal for cease-and-desist and customer/partner notification.
indicators: Customer/partner inquiry about a vendor relationship we have no record of
Fabricated vendor documentation referencing our brand with no matching internal procurement record
vectors: Fabricated vendor website/domain and documentation citing our brand as a client to appear legitimate
rootCauses: Customers/partners have no easy way to verify our actual vendor relationships
controls: Published/verifiable list of authorized vendors where feasible
Customer/partner education on verifying vendor relationships directly with us
ITID-22512.detection: External reports from confused/defrauded customers or partners; weak proactive detection.
ITID-22512.response: Cease-and-desist, public advisory, and support for affected customers/partners.
metrics: Count of fabricated vendor identity cases reported
ITID-22512.notes: No cross-domain overlap identified; differentiated from ITID-22511 by the absence of any real underlying vendor relationship.

playbook.name: Response: Impersonation via Entirely Fabricated Vendor Identity
playbook.description: For fraud where an attacker fabricates an entirely fictitious vendor identity (no real vendor relationship exists) to submit fraudulent invoices or payment requests to this organization.

steps.title: Confirm no genuine vendor relationship exists
steps.desc: Check the organization's approved-vendor records and procurement history to confirm the named vendor is entirely fabricated or unrelated to any real engagement.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no genuine vendor relationship exists.
steps.abort: If a genuine (but perhaps mismanaged) relationship is found, redirect to the appropriate vendor-impersonation playbook.

steps.title: Halt any pending payment to the fabricated vendor
steps.desc: Immediately place a hold on any invoice or payment request associated with the fabricated identity.

steps.title: Confirm no further invoices from the fabricated identity are being processed
steps.desc: Verify the fabricated vendor record is blocked/flagged in the vendor-master system.

steps.title: Track recovery of any transferred funds
steps.desc: Follow up with the bank/law enforcement on recall status until resolved.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered or loss confirmed and documented.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce new-vendor verification controls
steps.desc: Record the incident and reinforce controls requiring verification of a vendor's existence/legitimacy before any invoice is paid.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and control gap addressed.

steps.title: Identify the fabricated identity's contact and payment details
steps.desc: Document the fake vendor name, contact information, and requested payment/bank details.

steps.title: Determine whether any payment was already made
steps.desc: Check whether a payment was already disbursed before the hold was placed.
steps.abort: If no payment was made, proceed to internal notification.

steps.title: If a payment was made, initiate an emergency bank recall
steps.desc: Contact the sending bank's fraud department to request a recall/hold, and file a law enforcement report.
steps.outcome: Recall request filed; law enforcement report filed.
steps.tool: Bank fraud department / law enforcement financial-fraud unit

steps.title: Notify accounts-payable and procurement staff
steps.desc: Warn relevant staff about the fabricated vendor to prevent any repeat invoice from being processed.
steps.outcome: Staff warned and vendor flagged as fraudulent in procurement systems.

ITID-22513.def: An adversary exploits the window of ambiguity around a newly onboarded or not-yet-widely-verified vendor relationship with our organization, impersonating that new vendor to defraud our customers or partners before the relationship's legitimate details are well established or easily verifiable.
ITID-22513.purpose: Captures vendor impersonation exploiting a newly onboarded or as-yet-unverified vendor relationship connected to our brand.
scopeIncludes: Impersonation of a newly announced vendor partnership before customers/partners have an established way to verify it
Fraud exploiting the ambiguity period immediately following a new vendor relationship announcement
scopeExcludes: Impersonation of a long-established, well-known vendor relationship (see ITID-22511)
ITID-22513.severity: Medium-High — elevated because the lack of established verification channels increases victim susceptibility.
ITID-22513.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for confirmed active campaigns.
ITID-22513.escalation: Escalate to brand protection; expedite publishing verified relationship details to close the ambiguity window.
indicators: Fraud reports appearing shortly after a new vendor relationship is publicly announced
Customer/partner confusion about how to verify the new relationship
vectors: Rapid exploitation of the announcement news cycle before official verification channels are established
rootCauses: Delay between announcing a new vendor relationship and publishing verifiable details/contact channels
controls: Rapid publication of verified contact/relationship details alongside any new vendor relationship announcement
ITID-22513.detection: External reports; timing correlation with announcement dates aids triage.
ITID-22513.response: Rapid public clarification and cease-and-desist against the impersonator.
metrics: Count of new-relationship impersonation cases per announcement
ITID-22513.notes: No cross-domain overlap identified; differentiated from ITID-22511 by relationship maturity/verifiability rather than by compromise mechanism.

playbook.name: Response: Impersonation via Newly Onboarded/Unverified Vendor Relationship
playbook.description: For fraud exploiting a newly onboarded vendor relationship that has not yet been fully verified, where an attacker impersonates the new vendor (or intercepts early communications) to redirect an initial payment.

steps.title: Confirm the vendor relationship's onboarding status
steps.desc: Check procurement records to confirm the vendor was recently onboarded and whether standard verification (site visit, reference check, verified banking details) was completed.
steps.outcome: Onboarding status and verification gaps documented.

steps.title: Verify the request out-of-band using an independently sourced contact
steps.desc: Since the relationship is new, obtain the vendor's contact details independently (their official website, a known business registry) rather than trusting any number/email from the request itself, and confirm whether the request is genuine.
steps.outcome: Request confirmed fraudulent via independent verification.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, complete standard vendor verification before proceeding.

steps.title: Complete full vendor verification before resuming payments
steps.desc: Ensure standard vendor-verification steps are completed and confirmed before any further payments proceed.
steps.outcome: Vendor fully verified or relationship terminated if fraudulent.

steps.title: Track recovery of any transferred funds
steps.desc: Follow up with the bank/law enforcement on recall status until resolved.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered or loss confirmed and documented.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce new-vendor onboarding verification
steps.desc: Record the gap in onboarding verification that was exploited and reinforce the standard process for all new vendor relationships.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and control gap addressed.

steps.title: Identify the suspicious request and its source
steps.desc: Document the payment/data request in question and the channel it arrived through.

steps.title: Halt any pending payment pending verification
steps.desc: Place a hold on the payment until the vendor relationship and request are fully verified.

steps.title: If a payment was already made, initiate an emergency bank recall
steps.desc: Contact the sending bank's fraud department to request a recall/hold, and file a law enforcement report.
steps.outcome: Recall request filed; law enforcement report filed.
steps.tool: Bank fraud department / law enforcement financial-fraud unit

ITID-22514.def: Vendor impersonation exploiting our organization's brand or business relationships, not yet matched to a more specific compromised-vendor/fabricated-vendor/new-relationship leaf.
ITID-22514.purpose: Catch-all for vendor impersonation cases connected to our brand that do not fit a more specific leaf.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered vendor impersonation cases pending classification
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-22511 through ITID-22513
ITID-22514.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; default High given financial fraud potential.
ITID-22514.escalation: Reclassify once the specific mechanism is clarified; treat as active fraud until ruled out.
indicators: Report of unclear specific vendor impersonation mechanism
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Out-of-band verification requirement for payment-detail changes
ITID-22514.detection: Same telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-22514.response: Investigate and reclassify once confirmed; treat as active fraud in the interim.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-22514.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Vendor Impersonation
playbook.description: For fraud impersonating a vendor of this organization, where the specific mechanism (compromised real account, fabricated identity, unverified new relationship) does not fit an existing category.

steps.title: Determine whether a genuine vendor relationship exists and its status
steps.desc: Check procurement/vendor-master records to determine whether the named vendor is real, fabricated, or newly onboarded.
steps.abort: If a specific scenario is identified, redirect to the matching dedicated playbook.

steps.title: Verify the request out-of-band with the real vendor
steps.desc: Contact the vendor through an independently sourced channel to confirm whether the request is genuine.
steps.outcome: Request confirmed fraudulent via independent verification.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, stand down and close as a false positive.

steps.title: Confirm the threat is contained
steps.desc: Verify no further fraudulent requests are being acted upon.

steps.title: Track recovery of any transferred funds
steps.desc: Follow up until resolved.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered or loss confirmed and documented.

steps.title: Document the incident and evaluate whether it fits an existing category going forward
steps.desc: Record the case to sharpen future detection and categorization.

steps.title: Identify the suspicious request
steps.desc: Document the specific request and the channel it arrived through.

steps.title: Halt any pending payment and pursue recall if funds were already sent
steps.desc: Place a hold on the payment, or if already sent, contact the bank's fraud department immediately and file a law enforcement report.

ITID-22521.def: An adversary impersonates one of our actual clients (via spoofed/lookalike email or a compromised client mailbox) to instruct our organization to redirect a payment, invoice, or refund to a fraudulent account.
ITID-22521.purpose: Captures an adversary impersonating a real client of ours to redirect a payment or invoice to a fraudulent account.
scopeIncludes: A spoofed or lookalike-domain email impersonating a real client requesting a payment/bank-detail change
A compromised client mailbox used to send a fraudulent redirect request to us
scopeExcludes: Our own executive being impersonated to instruct an external party to redirect payment (see ITID-22411-22414, which cover our own executive identity being weaponized outward)
ITID-22521.severity: High — direct financial loss risk to our organization.
ITID-22521.escalation: Escalate immediately to finance/AP leadership and IR; verify any pending payment before release.
indicators: Payment redirect request from a client contact citing an urgent bank-detail change
Sender domain/mailbox anomalies inconsistent with the client's known correspondence pattern
vectors: Lookalike domain email impersonating the client
Compromise of the actual client's mailbox (reply-chain hijack of genuine correspondence)
rootCauses: Accounts payable process lacking mandatory out-of-band verification for bank-detail changes
controls: Mandatory out-of-band verification (known phone number, not the one in the email) for any payment-detail change request
AP staff training on client-impersonation payment fraud
ITID-22521.detection: Moderate — email authentication checks on the sending domain plus AP process controls; a genuine compromised client mailbox evades authentication-based detection.
ITID-22521.response: Verify before any payment release; if funds already sent, initiate immediate bank recall and law enforcement notification.
metrics: Count of client-impersonation payment redirect attempts
Recovery rate on funds already sent
ITID-22521.notes: Direction is the scope decision: this leaf covers a client being impersonated to target our organization, the counterpart to the Executive Impersonation BEC leaves where our own executive is impersonated to target others.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Client Payment/Invoice Redirect Request
playbook.description: For a fraudulent communication impersonating a real client of this organization to request that an invoice payment or refund be redirected to a different bank account.

steps.title: Confirm the request is impersonating the client
steps.desc: Review the communication's sending address/channel and content to assess whether it is consistent with the real client or shows signs of impersonation (urgency, changed contact details, unusual channel).

steps.title: Verify the request out-of-band directly with the real client
steps.desc: Contact the client through a previously known, verified channel (not contact info from the suspicious request) to confirm whether the change is genuine.
steps.outcome: Request confirmed fraudulent via independent verification.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, proceed with the change through normal verified channels.

steps.title: Confirm no further fraudulent payment redirects are pending
steps.desc: Verify all payments to this client are reverted to and remain on the originally verified bank details.

steps.title: Track recovery of any transferred funds
steps.desc: Follow up with the bank/law enforcement on recall status until resolved.
steps.outcome: Funds recovered or loss confirmed and documented.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce payment-change verification
steps.desc: Record the incident and reinforce a policy requiring out-of-band verification for any client-requested bank-detail change.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and control gap addressed.

steps.title: Identify the requested change and who received it
steps.desc: Document the specific bank-detail change requested and which staff received the request.

steps.title: Halt any pending payment/refund to the new account
steps.desc: Place a hold on the payment or refund pending verification, and revert to the client's originally verified bank details.
steps.outcome: Payment halted; original verified details restored.

steps.title: If a payment was already made to the fraudulent account, initiate an emergency bank recall
steps.desc: Contact the sending bank's fraud department to request a recall/hold, and file a law enforcement report.
steps.outcome: Recall request filed; law enforcement report filed.
steps.tool: Bank fraud department / law enforcement financial-fraud unit

steps.title: Notify the real client that their identity is being used fraudulently
steps.desc: Inform the client so they are aware their name/identity is being impersonated to target this organization.

ITID-22522.def: An adversary impersonates one of our actual clients to request sensitive data, reports, or account information from our organization that would not normally be shared outside a verified request.
ITID-22522.purpose: Captures an adversary impersonating a real client of ours to request sensitive data or an internal report.
scopeIncludes: A spoofed/lookalike client email requesting sensitive account, financial, or personal data
A compromised client mailbox used to request internal reporting data
scopeExcludes: A legitimate, verified client data request through an established secure channel
ITID-22522.severity: High — potential data exposure in addition to trust exploitation.
ITID-22522.escalation: Escalate to data privacy/legal in addition to IR if any data was disclosed before detection.
indicators: Data/report request from a client contact via an unusual channel or with subtle sender anomalies
Request for data outside the normal scope of the client relationship
vectors: Lookalike domain or compromised client mailbox used to request data under false pretenses
rootCauses: Data-request verification process not requiring out-of-band confirmation for sensitive requests
controls: Mandatory verification for sensitive data requests via a known-good channel
Staff training on client-impersonation data-request fraud
ITID-22522.detection: Moderate — relies on staff recognizing anomalies and following verification procedure.
ITID-22522.response: Verify before releasing any data; if data was disclosed, assess breach-notification obligations.
metrics: Count of client-impersonation data-request attempts

playbook.name: Response: Fake Client Data/Report Request
playbook.description: For a fraudulent communication impersonating a real client of this organization to request sensitive data or reports the client would not normally be authorized to receive through that channel.

steps.title: Confirm the request is impersonating the client
steps.desc: Review the communication's sending address/channel and the nature of the data requested to assess whether it is consistent with the real client relationship or shows signs of impersonation.

steps.title: Verify the request out-of-band directly with the real client
steps.desc: Contact the client through a previously known, verified channel to confirm whether the request is genuine.
steps.outcome: Request confirmed fraudulent via independent verification.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, proceed with the client's standard authorized data-request process.

steps.title: Confirm no further fraudulent data requests are being acted on
steps.desc: Verify staff are aware and no additional data has been sent.

steps.title: Assess and remediate any data already disclosed
steps.desc: If any data was disclosed before detection, assess the sensitivity and notify affected parties per data-protection obligations if warranted.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce data-request verification
steps.desc: Record the incident and reinforce a policy requiring out-of-band verification for any client data/report request outside the normal channel.

steps.title: Determine whether any data was already disclosed
steps.desc: Check whether staff already responded to the request with any data before it was flagged as suspicious.

steps.title: Halt any further response and notify the real client
steps.desc: Ensure no further data is sent, and inform the real client that their identity is being used to solicit data fraudulently.

ITID-22523.def: An adversary impersonates one of our actual clients to request a change to account settings — contact details, authorized users, delivery/service configuration — that could facilitate further fraud or unauthorized access.
ITID-22523.purpose: Captures an adversary impersonating a real client of ours to request a change to the client's account settings.
scopeIncludes: A spoofed/lookalike client email requesting an authorized-contact or account-setting change
A compromised client mailbox used to add an unauthorized user to the account
scopeExcludes: A legitimate, verified account change request through an established secure channel
ITID-22523.severity: Medium-High — often a precursor step enabling further fraud (e.g., subsequent payment redirect).
ITID-22523.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if paired with a financial request.
ITID-22523.escalation: Escalate to account management and IR if the change appears designed to enable follow-on fraud.
indicators: Account-setting change request from a client contact with subtle sender anomalies
A new 'authorized contact' added shortly before an unusual request
vectors: Lookalike domain or compromised client mailbox requesting an account-setting change as a precursor to fraud
rootCauses: Account-change verification process not requiring out-of-band confirmation
controls: Mandatory verification for account-setting changes, especially additions of new authorized contacts
ITID-22523.detection: Moderate — relies on account management staff recognizing anomalies.
ITID-22523.response: Verify before applying any change; review recent account history if a change was already applied.
metrics: Count of client-impersonation account-change attempts
ITID-22523.notes: Often a precursor to ITID-22521 (payment redirect); track linkage between the two when both occur in sequence.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Client Account Change Request
playbook.description: For a fraudulent communication impersonating a real client of this organization to request a change to their account (contact details, authorized users, access permissions) that could facilitate further fraud.

steps.title: Confirm the request is impersonating the client
steps.desc: Review the communication's sending address/channel and the requested change to assess whether it is consistent with the real client or shows signs of impersonation.

steps.title: Verify the request out-of-band directly with the real client
steps.desc: Contact the client through a previously known, verified channel to confirm whether the requested change is genuine.
steps.outcome: Request confirmed fraudulent via independent verification.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, apply the change through the normal verified process.

steps.title: Confirm the account is fully restored and no further changes are pending
steps.desc: Verify the account reflects only verified, authorized details.

steps.title: Review the account for any activity during the exposure window
steps.desc: If the fraudulent change was live for any period, review account activity for signs of misuse.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce account-change verification
steps.desc: Record the incident and reinforce a policy requiring out-of-band verification for sensitive client account changes.

steps.title: Determine whether the account change was already made
steps.desc: Check account/CRM records to determine whether the requested change was already applied.

steps.title: Revert any unauthorized change and notify the real client
steps.desc: Restore the account to its prior verified state and inform the client that their identity is being used to attempt account changes fraudulently.

ITID-22524.def: An adversary impersonates one of our actual clients to submit a fraudulent contract renewal, purchase order, or procurement request, intended to extract payment, favorable terms, or sensitive commercial information under false pretenses.
ITID-22524.purpose: Captures an adversary impersonating a real client of ours to push a fraudulent contract renewal or procurement request.
scopeIncludes: A spoofed/lookalike client email submitting a fraudulent renewal or purchase order
A compromised client mailbox used to negotiate fraudulent contract terms
scopeExcludes: Legitimate contract renewal negotiations through an established account management relationship
ITID-22524.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if a payment or sensitive commercial term is involved.
ITID-22524.escalation: Escalate to sales/account management leadership and legal for contract-fraud review.
indicators: Renewal/procurement request from a client contact with subtle sender anomalies or unusual urgency
Terms inconsistent with the established commercial relationship
vectors: Lookalike domain or compromised client mailbox used to submit fraudulent commercial paperwork
rootCauses: Procurement/renewal verification process not requiring out-of-band confirmation for unusual terms
controls: Mandatory verification for renewal/procurement requests with unusual terms or urgency
ITID-22524.detection: Moderate — relies on account management staff recognizing anomalies against known relationship history.
ITID-22524.response: Verify before finalizing any renewal/procurement action.
metrics: Count of client-impersonation contract fraud attempts

playbook.name: Response: Fake Client Contract Renewal/Procurement Request
playbook.description: For a fraudulent communication impersonating a real client of this organization to push through a contract renewal, purchase order, or procurement action under false pretenses.

steps.title: Confirm the request is impersonating the client
steps.desc: Review the communication's sending address/channel and the requested contract/procurement action to assess whether it is consistent with the real client relationship or shows signs of impersonation.

steps.title: Verify the request out-of-band directly with the real client
