steps.desc: Contact the client's known point of contact through a previously verified channel to confirm whether the request is genuine.
steps.outcome: Request confirmed fraudulent via independent verification.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, proceed through the normal contract/procurement process.

steps.title: Confirm no fraudulent contract/order has been finalized
steps.desc: Verify with sales/legal/procurement that nothing was finalized based on the fraudulent request.

steps.title: Unwind any action already taken
steps.desc: If any contract or order was processed before detection, work with legal/procurement to unwind it.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce contract/procurement verification
steps.desc: Record the incident and reinforce a policy requiring out-of-band verification for client-initiated contract/procurement requests.

steps.title: Determine whether the contract/procurement action was already processed
steps.desc: Check with sales/legal/procurement whether any action was taken based on the request.

steps.title: Halt processing and notify the real client
steps.desc: Ensure no contract/procurement action proceeds based on the fraudulent request, and inform the client their identity is being used fraudulently.

ITID-22525.def: An adversary impersonates one of our actual clients to submit a fabricated support escalation or complaint, used to pressure staff into an unwarranted concession (refund, credit, account change) or to extract sensitive account information under the guise of complaint resolution.
ITID-22525.purpose: Captures an adversary impersonating a real client of ours to submit a fraudulent support escalation or complaint intended to extract concessions or sensitive information.
scopeIncludes: A spoofed/lookalike client email submitting a fabricated complaint demanding a refund/credit
A compromised client mailbox used to escalate a fake issue to extract information
scopeExcludes: A genuine client complaint or escalation
ITID-22525.escalation: Escalate to account management if the escalation includes unusual financial or data demands.
indicators: Complaint/escalation from a client contact with subtle sender anomalies
Unusual pressure/urgency paired with a financial or data demand
vectors: Lookalike domain or compromised client mailbox used to fabricate a complaint scenario
rootCauses: Support escalation process not requiring identity verification proportional to the concession requested
controls: Verification proportional to the size of any requested concession
Staff training on complaint-based social engineering
ITID-22525.detection: Moderate — relies on support staff recognizing anomalies.
ITID-22525.response: Verify before granting any concession or disclosing information.
metrics: Count of client-impersonation escalation fraud attempts

playbook.name: Response: Fake Client Support Escalation/Complaint Request
playbook.description: For a fraudulent communication impersonating a real client of this organization to escalate a fake complaint or support issue, typically as a pretext to extract data, refunds, or account access.

steps.title: Confirm the request is impersonating the client
steps.desc: Review the communication's sending address/channel and the nature of the escalation to assess whether it is consistent with the real client or shows signs of impersonation.

steps.title: Verify the request out-of-band directly with the real client
steps.desc: Contact the client through a previously known, verified channel to confirm whether the complaint/escalation is genuine.
steps.outcome: Request confirmed fraudulent via independent verification.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, handle through the normal support-escalation process.

steps.title: Confirm no fraudulent remedy has been granted
steps.desc: Verify with support/finance that nothing was disbursed or disclosed based on the fraudulent escalation.

steps.title: Unwind any refund/data already released
steps.desc: If a refund or data was released before detection, work with finance/legal to unwind or mitigate it.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce escalation-verification practices
steps.desc: Record the incident and reinforce a policy requiring identity verification before high-value refunds/data releases on escalated complaints.

steps.title: Determine what was requested as resolution (refund, data, access)
steps.desc: Document the specific remedy demanded and whether any action was already taken to resolve it.
steps.outcome: Requested remedy and action status documented.

steps.title: Halt any pending refund/data release and notify the real client
steps.desc: Ensure no refund, data, or access is granted based on the fraudulent escalation, and inform the client their identity is being used fraudulently.

ITID-22526.def: An incident of a real client being impersonated to target our organization, not yet matched to a more specific payment/data/account-change/contract/support-escalation leaf.
ITID-22526.purpose: Catch-all for client impersonation cases that do not fit a more specific leaf.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered client impersonation cases pending classification
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-22521 through ITID-22525
ITID-22526.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; default Medium-High.
ITID-22526.escalation: Reclassify once the specific request type is clarified; treat as potential active fraud until ruled out.
indicators: Report of unclear specific client impersonation request type
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Out-of-band verification requirement
ITID-22526.detection: Same telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-22526.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Client Impersonation
playbook.description: For a fraudulent communication impersonating a real client of this organization, where the specific request (payment redirect, data, account change, contract, complaint) does not fit an existing category.

steps.title: Confirm the request is impersonating the client
steps.desc: Review the communication's sending address/channel and content to assess whether it is consistent with the real client or shows signs of impersonation.

steps.title: Verify the request out-of-band directly with the real client
steps.desc: Contact the client through a previously known, verified channel to confirm whether the request is genuine.
steps.outcome: Request confirmed fraudulent via independent verification.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, proceed through the normal verified process.

steps.title: Confirm the threat is contained
steps.desc: Verify no further fraudulent action is being taken.

steps.title: Unwind any erroneous action and track fund recovery
steps.desc: Unwind any action taken based on the fraudulent request and follow up on any fund recovery.

steps.title: Document the incident and evaluate whether it fits an existing category going forward
steps.desc: Record the case to sharpen future detection and categorization.

steps.title: Determine what was requested and whether any action was already taken
steps.desc: Document the specific request and check whether staff already acted on it.

steps.title: Halt any pending action and pursue recall/recovery if funds moved
steps.desc: Halt any pending payment, data release, or account change; if funds were already transferred, contact the bank's fraud department immediately and file a law enforcement report.
steps.tool: Bank fraud department / law enforcement financial-fraud unit

steps.title: Notify the real client of the impersonation
steps.desc: Inform the client their identity is being used fraudulently against this organization.

ITID-22531.def: An adversary impersonates our organization's real, named outsourced or managed IT service provider (MSP) — via phone, email, or a fake portal — to socially engineer our own employees into granting access, resetting credentials, or installing remote-access tooling.
ITID-22531.purpose: Captures impersonation of our outsourced/managed IT service provider (MSP) to socially engineer our own staff.
scopeIncludes: A call/email impersonating our named MSP requesting credential reset or remote-access installation from our staff
A fake portal impersonating our MSP's real support/ticketing system
scopeExcludes: A generic, unnamed 'IT support' vishing pretext with no specific real MSP identity invoked (see the ITID-11000 vishing leaves)
ITID-22531.severity: High — MSP relationships typically carry broad privileged access, amplifying impact.
ITID-22531.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT security; verify directly with the MSP's known escalation contact before granting any access.
indicators: Staff report of a support contact claiming to be our MSP requesting unusual access
Sender/caller details inconsistent with our MSP's known contact channels
vectors: Research identifying our named MSP (e.g., via public vendor announcements or job postings) to add credibility to the pretext
rootCauses: Staff not trained to verify MSP contacts through a pre-established, independent channel
controls: Pre-established, independent verification channel for our MSP's identity
Staff training on MSP-impersonation social engineering
ITID-22531.detection: Weak technical detection; relies on staff verification discipline.
ITID-22531.response: Verify with the MSP through the known escalation contact before granting any access; review recent access grants if verification fails after the fact.
metrics: Count of MSP-impersonation social engineering attempts
ITID-22531.notes: Requires impersonation of our actual, named MSP; a generic unnamed IT-support pretext against our staff falls under the ITID-11000 vishing leaves instead.

playbook.name: Response: Impersonation of Outsourced/Managed IT Service Provider (MSP)
playbook.description: For an attacker impersonating this organization's outsourced/managed IT service provider (by phone, email, or remote-access tool prompt) to gain unauthorized access, credentials, or sensitive system information.

steps.title: Confirm the contact is impersonating the MSP
steps.desc: Review the contact channel, caller/sender identity, and content to assess whether it is consistent with the real MSP relationship or shows signs of impersonation.

steps.title: Verify the contact out-of-band directly with the real MSP
steps.desc: Contact the MSP through a previously known, verified channel (the organization's own MSP contract contact, not any number/email from the suspicious contact) to confirm whether the outreach is genuine.
steps.outcome: Contact confirmed fraudulent via independent verification.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, resume the normal support engagement.

steps.title: Audit systems accessed during the exposure window for compromise
steps.desc: Review any system the attacker accessed for signs of malware, data exfiltration, or persistence.

steps.title: Restore normal, verified MSP support access
steps.desc: Ensure the legitimate MSP's access channels remain intact and re-verify staff awareness of the correct engagement process.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce MSP-contact verification procedures
steps.desc: Record the technique and reinforce a policy requiring out-of-band verification before granting any remote access or credentials to an IT support contact.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and control gap addressed.

steps.title: Determine whether any access, credentials, or remote session was granted
steps.desc: Check with the employee contacted and relevant logs to determine whether remote access, credentials, or system information was already provided.
steps.abort: IAM / remote-access session logs

steps.title: Terminate any active remote-access session and revoke any granted access
steps.desc: Immediately disconnect any remote-access session and revoke any credentials or permissions provided during the fraudulent contact.

steps.title: Notify the real MSP that their identity is being used fraudulently
steps.desc: Inform the MSP so they are aware their brand/identity is being used to target their clients.

ITID-22532.def: An adversary impersonates the official support team of a SaaS platform we actually use, contacting our staff to socially engineer credential resets, OAuth consent grants, or account access.
ITID-22532.purpose: Captures impersonation of a SaaS vendor's official support team to socially engineer our own staff.
scopeIncludes: A call/email impersonating a real SaaS vendor's support team requesting credential reset or OAuth consent from our staff
A fake support portal impersonating a real SaaS vendor we use
scopeExcludes: OAuth/application consent spear phishing with a generic or fabricated application identity not tied to impersonating the SaaS vendor's actual support team (see ITID-11128, OAuth / Application Consent Spear Phishing)
ITID-22532.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT security; verify with the SaaS vendor's official support channel before taking any requested action.
indicators: Staff report of a support contact claiming to be a used SaaS vendor requesting unusual access or consent
Sender/caller details inconsistent with the vendor's known official support channels
vectors: Research identifying our actual SaaS vendor relationships (e.g., via job postings, case studies, or public integrations) to add credibility
rootCauses: Staff not trained to verify vendor support contacts through the vendor's own official channel
controls: Staff training on SaaS vendor support impersonation
Verification via the vendor's official support channel before granting access/consent
ITID-22532.detection: Weak technical detection; relies on staff verification discipline.
ITID-22532.response: Verify with the vendor's official channel; review recent OAuth grants/access changes if verification fails after the fact.
metrics: Count of SaaS vendor support impersonation attempts
ITID-22532.notes: Differentiated from ITID-11128 by specificity: this leaf requires impersonation of a real, named SaaS vendor's actual support identity, rather than a generic/fabricated application consent lure.

playbook.name: Response: Impersonation of SaaS Vendor's Official Support Team
playbook.description: For an attacker impersonating the official support team of a SaaS vendor used by this organization, to gain unauthorized account access, credentials, or sensitive configuration information.

steps.title: Confirm the contact is impersonating the SaaS vendor's support team
steps.desc: Review the contact channel, caller/sender identity, and content to assess whether it is consistent with the real SaaS vendor's known support process.

steps.title: Verify the contact out-of-band directly with the real SaaS vendor
steps.desc: Contact the vendor through their official support channel (from the vendor's own website, not any contact from the suspicious outreach) to confirm whether it is genuine.
steps.outcome: Contact confirmed fraudulent via independent verification.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, resume the normal support engagement.

steps.title: Audit the SaaS environment for unauthorized changes
steps.desc: Review the SaaS platform's audit logs for any configuration changes, new integrations, or data exports made during the exposure window.

steps.title: Restore normal, verified support access with the vendor
steps.desc: Confirm the legitimate support relationship remains functional and staff know the correct verification process.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce SaaS support-contact verification procedures
steps.desc: Record the technique and reinforce a policy requiring out-of-band verification before disclosing credentials or granting access to a support contact.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and control gap addressed.

steps.title: Determine whether any access, credentials, or configuration data was disclosed
steps.desc: Check with the employee contacted and relevant logs to determine whether account access, credentials, or sensitive configuration data was already provided.
steps.abort: SaaS admin console logs

steps.title: Revoke any granted access and rotate exposed credentials
steps.desc: Revoke any account access or API tokens shared, and rotate any credentials disclosed during the fraudulent contact.

steps.title: Notify the real SaaS vendor that their identity is being used fraudulently
steps.desc: Inform the vendor so they are aware their support brand is being impersonated to target their customers.

ITID-22533.def: An adversary impersonates the official support team of a hardware/equipment manufacturer whose products we actually use, contacting our staff to socially engineer physical or remote access, or to deliver malware disguised as a firmware/driver update.
ITID-22533.purpose: Captures impersonation of a hardware or equipment manufacturer's support team to socially engineer our own staff.
scopeIncludes: A call/email impersonating a real hardware vendor's support team requesting remote access or pushing a fake firmware update to our staff
scopeExcludes: A fake software vendor support page targeting the general public rather than our own staff (see ITID-22131, Fake Software Vendor Support Page)
ITID-22533.severity: High — hardware-level compromise can be difficult to detect and remediate.
ITID-22533.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT security; verify with the manufacturer's official support channel before installing any update or granting access.
indicators: Staff report of a support contact claiming to be a hardware vendor requesting remote access or an unscheduled firmware update
Update package/installer inconsistent with the vendor's official distribution channel
vectors: Research identifying our actual hardware vendor relationships to add credibility to the pretext
Fake firmware/driver packages bundled with malware
rootCauses: Staff not trained to verify hardware vendor support contacts through the vendor's own official channel
controls: Staff training on hardware vendor support impersonation
Firmware/driver updates sourced only from verified official channels
ITID-22533.detection: Weak technical detection; relies on staff verification discipline and endpoint monitoring for unauthorized firmware/driver changes.
ITID-22533.response: Verify with the manufacturer's official channel before any action; isolate and investigate any device where an unverified update was applied.
metrics: Count of hardware vendor support impersonation attempts
ITID-22533.notes: Differentiated from ITID-22131 by target: this leaf covers impersonation targeting our own internal staff, whereas ITID-22131 covers a public-facing fake support page targeting customers.

playbook.name: Response: Impersonation of Hardware/Equipment Manufacturer Support
playbook.description: For an attacker impersonating a hardware or equipment manufacturer's support team to gain physical or remote access, credentials, or sensitive system/network information under the guise of maintenance or troubleshooting.

steps.title: Confirm the contact is impersonating the manufacturer's support team
steps.desc: Review the contact channel, caller/technician identity, and requested access to assess whether it is consistent with the real manufacturer's known support/maintenance process.

steps.title: Verify the contact out-of-band directly with the real manufacturer
steps.desc: Contact the manufacturer through their official support channel (from the manufacturer's own documentation/website, not any contact from the suspicious outreach) to confirm whether the visit/contact is genuine.
steps.outcome: Contact confirmed fraudulent via independent verification.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, resume the normal support engagement.

steps.title: Inspect any equipment or systems the impersonator accessed
steps.desc: Physically and/or digitally inspect any equipment for tampering, added hardware, or malicious firmware/software changes.

steps.title: Restore normal, verified manufacturer support access
steps.desc: Confirm the legitimate support relationship remains functional and staff know the correct verification process for on-site or remote technician visits.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce technician-visit verification procedures
steps.desc: Record the technique and reinforce a policy requiring identity/appointment verification before granting any physical or remote access to a support technician.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and control gap addressed.

steps.title: Determine whether physical or remote access was already granted
steps.desc: Check with staff and physical/remote access logs whether the impersonator was granted site access, remote access, or system information.
steps.abort: Badge access logs / remote-access platform

steps.title: Revoke any physical or remote access granted
steps.desc: Terminate any remote-access session, revoke any temporary badge/site access, and secure any equipment the impersonator interacted with.

steps.title: Notify the real manufacturer that their identity is being used fraudulently
steps.desc: Inform the manufacturer so they are aware their support brand is being impersonated to target their customers.

ITID-22534.def: Impersonation of a real third-party support provider connected to our organization, not yet matched to a more specific MSP/SaaS-vendor/hardware-vendor leaf.
ITID-22534.purpose: Catch-all for third-party support impersonation cases that do not fit a more specific leaf.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered third-party support impersonation cases pending classification
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching ITID-22531 through ITID-22533
ITID-22534.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; default High.
ITID-22534.escalation: Reclassify once the specific provider type is clarified; treat as active social engineering until ruled out.
indicators: Report of unclear specific third-party support provider being impersonated
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Verification via the provider's official support channel
ITID-22534.detection: Same telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-22534.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Third-Party Support Impersonation
playbook.description: For an attacker impersonating a third-party support provider (MSP, SaaS vendor, hardware manufacturer, or otherwise) of this organization, where the specific provider type does not fit an existing category.

steps.title: Confirm the contact is impersonating a legitimate third-party support provider
steps.desc: Review the contact channel, identity claimed, and requested access to assess whether it is consistent with a known support relationship or shows signs of impersonation.

steps.title: Verify the contact out-of-band directly with the real provider
steps.desc: Contact the real provider through a previously known, verified channel to confirm whether the outreach is genuine.
steps.outcome: Contact confirmed fraudulent via independent verification.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine, resume the normal support engagement.

steps.title: Audit any systems or access points touched during the exposure window
steps.desc: Review logs for any changes or misuse during the fraudulent contact.

steps.title: Restore normal, verified support access
steps.desc: Confirm the legitimate support relationship remains functional and staff know the correct verification process.

steps.title: Document the incident and evaluate whether it fits an existing category going forward
steps.desc: Record the case to sharpen future detection and categorization.

steps.title: Determine whether any access, credentials, or data was disclosed

steps.title: Notify the real provider that their identity is being used fraudulently
steps.desc: Inform the provider so they are aware their support brand is being impersonated.

ITID-23111.def: An incident in which customer personal or financial data is exfiltrated from a company-owned and -operated database through direct technical compromise (SQL injection, exploited vulnerability, stolen application credentials), and the exposure becomes known to customers, regulators, or the public.
ITID-23111.purpose: Captures the public disclosure and brand/regulatory fallout when customer data is confirmed stolen from a company-operated database via direct compromise.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed exfiltration of customer records from a first-party database
Public disclosure, regulator notification, or media reporting of the breach
Customer notification and credit-monitoring obligations triggered by the exposure
scopeExcludes: The underlying database intrusion technique itself (tracked under the relevant external-attack ITID domain)
Exposure via a misconfigured cloud storage bucket rather than an active database compromise (ITID-23112)
Exposure sourced from a third-party processor's own breach (ITID-23113)
ITID-23111.severity: High to Critical, scaling with record volume and data sensitivity (financial/health data raises severity).
ITID-23111.priority: P1 once exfiltration and customer data scope are confirmed.
ITID-23111.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, privacy/DPO, and executive communications; regulatory notification clocks (e.g., 72-hour GDPR) start at confirmed knowledge.
indicators: Anomalous bulk database query or export activity
Threat actor claim or leak-site posting referencing company customer data
Regulator or journalist inquiry citing specific customer records
vectors: SQL injection against a customer-facing application
Exploitation of an unpatched database server vulnerability
Use of stolen application or service-account credentials to query the database directly
rootCauses: Unpatched database or application vulnerability
Insufficient database access segmentation/least privilege
Lack of anomalous-query detection on production databases
controls: Database activity monitoring/DAM
Web application firewall
Data loss prevention on egress channels
Least-privilege database access controls
ITID-23111.detection: Database audit logs and DLP/egress monitoring provide strong technical detection once exfiltration is underway; earlier-stage intrusion detection lives with the source vulnerability's own ITID.
ITID-23111.response: Confirm scope of exfiltrated records, contain the compromised access path, engage legal/privacy for notification obligations, and coordinate public/customer communications.
metrics: Time from exfiltration to detection
Number of customer records confirmed exposed
Time to regulatory notification
detections: DLP egress alerting on bulk customer-record transfer
ITID-23111.notes: Scoped to the disclosure and brand-impact side of the breach. The technical database intrusion vector is tracked under the corresponding external-attack ITID; this leaf begins once customer data has been confirmed exfiltrated and disclosure/notification obligations are in play.

playbook.name: Response: Customer Data Breach via Compromised Database
playbook.description: For customer data exposed as a result of unauthorized access to a production database (e.g. stolen credentials, SQL injection, or exploited vulnerability granting direct DB access).

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized database access and identify the entry vector
steps.desc: Review database audit logs, WAF logs, and application logs to confirm access occurred and determine how (compromised credentials, injection, exposed admin interface, etc.).
steps.outcome: Access confirmed with a working theory of the entry vector.
steps.abort: If no evidence of actual access is found, downgrade and continue monitoring rather than declaring a breach.

steps.title: Revoke the compromised access path immediately
steps.desc: Disable the compromised account/credential, patch the exploited vulnerability, or close the exposed access point, then force-terminate any active malicious sessions.
steps.guidance: Coordinate timing with DBAs to avoid unnecessary production outage where possible, but prioritize stopping ongoing access.
steps.outcome: Attacker access path closed; no active unauthorized sessions remain.

steps.title: Close the root-cause vulnerability
steps.desc: Patch the exploited software vulnerability, fix the injection flaw, or remediate the misconfiguration that allowed the compromise.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated and verified by re-test.

steps.title: Execute regulatory and customer notification per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications on the legally mandated timeline once scope is confirmed.

steps.title: Document the incident and implement preventive guardrails
steps.desc: Record the root cause, timeline, and scope; recommend controls (e.g. WAF rules, least-privilege DB access, query monitoring) to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; preventive controls proposed and tracked.

steps.title: Scope exactly which tables/records were queried or exfiltrated
steps.desc: Reconstruct query history or network egress logs to determine which customer records and data fields were accessed, and estimate the affected record count.
steps.guidance: Distinguish between data merely accessible and data actually queried/exfiltrated where logs allow.
steps.outcome: Documented scope: data categories, approximate record count, and confidence level in that scope.
steps.tool: Database audit logs / DLP / network flow logs

steps.title: Rotate all credentials with access to the affected database
steps.desc: Rotate database service accounts, application connection strings, and any admin credentials that may have been exposed.

steps.title: Sweep for additional footholds
steps.desc: Check for webshells, added database accounts, or other persistence the attacker may have planted while inside.

steps.title: Determine whether the access is ongoing
steps.desc: Check for active sessions, persistence mechanisms, or scheduled jobs using the compromised access path.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the intrusion is contained or still live.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Privacy immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Privacy given likely breach-notification obligations for exposed customer data.
steps.guidance: Do this in parallel with technical containment, not after.
steps.outcome: Legal/Privacy engaged and assessing notification obligations.

ITID-23112.def: An incident in which customer data stored in a cloud object-storage bucket (e.g., S3, Azure Blob, GCS) is left publicly accessible due to misconfiguration and is discovered by a researcher, journalist, or threat actor, triggering public disclosure.
ITID-23112.purpose: Captures the public disclosure and brand fallout when customer data is found exposed due to a misconfigured cloud storage bucket rather than an active intrusion.
scopeIncludes: Publicly readable/listable bucket containing customer records discovered by an external party
Security researcher or journalist responsible-disclosure report of an open bucket
Public disclosure/notification obligations triggered by confirmed unauthorized access or download
scopeExcludes: Active database compromise via exploitation (ITID-23111)
Exposure originating from a third-party vendor's own cloud misconfiguration (ITID-23113)
The cloud configuration-management control failure itself, tracked as an infrastructure-security ITID
ITID-23112.severity: High, escalating to Critical if evidence shows the bucket was actually accessed/downloaded by unauthorized parties rather than merely exposed.
ITID-23112.priority: P1 upon confirmation of public accessibility to customer data; P2 if exposure is found and remediated before evidence of external access.
ITID-23112.escalation: Escalate to cloud security, legal/privacy, and communications; determine access logs to establish whether exposure was merely possible or actually exploited.
indicators: Researcher or journalist notification of an open bucket
Cloud provider security alert on public-read ACL
Access logs showing downloads from unrecognized external IP ranges
vectors: Publicly readable bucket ACL/policy left open
Bucket enumeration via public scanning services
Shared/forgotten pre-signed URL circulated beyond intended recipients
rootCauses: Absence of automated cloud configuration/posture scanning
Manual bucket policy change bypassing review
No default-deny baseline for new storage resources
controls: Cloud security posture management (CSPM)
Default-deny public-access bucket policies
Automated public-exposure scanning
ITID-23112.detection: Cloud provider access logging and CSPM tooling give reliable technical signal on public exposure and, where enabled, on actual access events.
ITID-23112.response: Immediately restrict access, review access logs for evidence of external download, and route to legal/privacy for notification assessment.
metrics: Time bucket was publicly exposed before detection
Number of records within the exposed bucket
Time to remediation after discovery
detections: Cloud storage access log anomaly detection
ITID-23112.notes: Scoped to the disclosure and brand-impact side of a cloud misconfiguration exposure. The underlying cloud configuration control gap is tracked under the relevant infrastructure-security ITID; this leaf covers the moment exposure becomes known externally and disclosure obligations begin.

playbook.name: Response: Customer Data Exposure via Misconfigured Cloud Storage Bucket
playbook.description: For customer data discovered publicly exposed due to a misconfigured cloud storage bucket (e.g. a public S3 bucket).

steps.title: Confirm the exposure and secure access immediately
steps.desc: Verify the bucket is genuinely public and belongs to this organization, and immediately restrict access.
steps.guidance: Don't wait for full scoping before restricting access — every hour public is more exposure.
steps.outcome: Bucket access restricted to authorized principals only.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Privacy immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Privacy given likely breach-notification obligations.
steps.guidance: Do this in parallel with technical containment, not after.
steps.outcome: Legal/Privacy engaged and assessing notification obligations.

steps.title: Fix the root-cause configuration/process gap
steps.desc: Correct the misconfiguration and, if applicable, the process/template that allowed it (e.g. a default-public bucket policy in an IaC template).
steps.outcome: Root cause closed, not just the one bucket.

steps.title: Execute regulatory and customer notification per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications on the legally mandated timeline once scope is confirmed.

steps.title: Document the incident and implement preventive guardrails
steps.desc: Record the root cause and recommend an automated guardrail (e.g. a policy preventing public bucket creation) to prevent recurrence.

steps.title: Determine exactly what data was in the bucket
steps.desc: Inventory the exposed files/records to determine data types and volume (PII, payment data, etc.).
steps.outcome: Full scope of exposed data categories and record count established.

steps.title: Audit for other similarly-misconfigured resources
steps.desc: Check whether the same misconfiguration pattern exists elsewhere in the cloud environment.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no other public-exposed resources of the same kind.

steps.title: Determine if the bucket was actually accessed by anyone other than the organization
steps.desc: Review cloud access logs for the exposure window to determine if external parties accessed the data.
steps.guidance: Access logs may not always be enabled — note this limitation if so.
steps.outcome: Confirmed access history, or confirmed logging gap.

ITID-23113.def: An incident in which a third-party vendor, contractor, or data processor entrusted with company customer data suffers its own breach, resulting in exposure of the company's customer data and requiring the company to manage disclosure despite not controlling the compromised system.
ITID-23113.purpose: Captures the brand and disclosure impact on the company when a third-party vendor or data processor holding customer data is breached.
scopeIncludes: Vendor/processor breach confirmed to include company customer data
Company-side notification, customer communication, and reputational management following a vendor breach
Contractual/legal review of vendor liability and data-processing agreement obligations
scopeExcludes: Breach of a company-owned and -operated system (ITID-23111)
The vendor's own internal incident response and root-cause investigation (owned by the vendor, referenced but not duplicated here)
Vendor breach limited to employee data rather than customer data (ITID-23123)
ITID-23113.severity: High, driven by volume/sensitivity of exposed customer data regardless of fault location.
ITID-23113.priority: P1 once vendor confirms company customer data was included in the breach.
ITID-23113.escalation: Escalate to vendor management, legal, and privacy immediately upon vendor notification; do not wait for the vendor's full investigation to begin customer-facing risk assessment.
indicators: Vendor breach notification naming the company as an affected customer
Public reporting of a vendor breach that references the company by name
Customer data appearing in a leak associated with a known vendor incident
vectors: Compromise of the vendor's own infrastructure or applications
Vendor employee or contractor negligence/insider action
Compromise of a sub-processor further downstream in the vendor's supply chain
rootCauses: Insufficient vendor security due-diligence or ongoing assessment
Data processing agreement lacking timely breach-notification requirements
Excessive data sharing with vendor beyond minimum necessary
controls: Vendor security risk assessment program
Data processing agreements with breach-notification SLAs
Data minimization in vendor data-sharing arrangements
ITID-23113.detection: Detection is largely dependent on vendor self-reporting or third-party breach-monitoring services; the company has limited direct technical visibility into the vendor's environment.
ITID-23113.response: Confirm scope of company data involved, activate vendor incident-response clause, and manage independent customer/regulatory notification obligations.
metrics: Time from vendor notification to company customer notification
Number of vendor breaches affecting company data per year
detections: Third-party breach monitoring/threat intelligence feed alerting
ITID-23113.notes: Scoped to the company's own disclosure and brand-management obligations arising from a vendor's breach; the vendor's internal compromise investigation is out of scope and owned by the vendor.

playbook.name: Response: Customer Data Exposure via Third-Party/Vendor Data Processor Breach
playbook.description: For customer data exposed because a third-party vendor or data processor entrusted with that data was breached.

steps.title: Obtain confirmation and details from the vendor
steps.desc: Contact the vendor's security/incident response contact to confirm the breach, its timeline, and what data of ours was in scope.
steps.guidance: Vendors may be slow or incomplete in initial disclosure — request written confirmation and follow up formally via the contract's security-incident clause.
steps.outcome: Written vendor confirmation with initial scope and timeline.
steps.tool: Vendor incident notification / contract escalation contacts

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Privacy immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Privacy given likely breach-notification obligations, and confirm contractual obligations the vendor owes us (DPA/BAA terms).
steps.outcome: Legal/Privacy engaged, vendor contract obligations reviewed.

steps.title: Verify vendor remediation before resuming normal data sharing
steps.desc: Review evidence that the vendor has closed the root cause of their breach before resuming full data sharing.
steps.outcome: Vendor remediation verified or data sharing arrangement revised/terminated.

steps.title: Execute regulatory and customer notification per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications on the legally mandated timeline once scope is confirmed, coordinating messaging with the vendor where appropriate.

steps.title: Reassess vendor risk posture and contractual controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and evaluate whether the vendor relationship, DPA terms, or vendor risk tiering need to change.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; vendor risk review completed.

steps.title: Determine which of our customers' data was processed by the affected vendor
steps.desc: Cross-reference internal records of what data was shared with or processed by this vendor to independently scope exposure, rather than relying solely on the vendor's account.
steps.outcome: Independent scope of affected customer data and record count.

steps.title: Suspend or restrict further data sharing with the vendor pending assessment
steps.desc: Pause new data transfers to the affected vendor until their remediation and our risk assessment are complete.
steps.outcome: Data flow to vendor paused or restricted.

ITID-23114.def: An incident in which a malicious insider steals customer data and the theft results in public disclosure, regulatory notification, or reputational impact — distinct from the insider's motivation and internal handling, which is tracked elsewhere.
ITID-23114.purpose: Captures the public disclosure and brand fallout when customer data theft by a malicious insider becomes externally known.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed insider theft of customer records that has become known to customers, regulators, media, or the public
Customer notification and regulatory disclosure obligations triggered by insider-sourced customer data theft
scopeExcludes: The insider's motivation, method of theft, and internal HR/investigative handling (ITID-13111 Insider Theft of Customer PII/Financial Records)
Insider theft that remains internally contained with no external disclosure obligation (tracked solely under ITID-13111)
ITID-23114.severity: High, driven by data volume/sensitivity; insider provenance does not reduce severity for affected customers.
ITID-23114.priority: P1 once external disclosure or notification obligations are confirmed.
ITID-23114.escalation: Escalate to legal, privacy, and communications in parallel with the HR/insider-threat investigation tracked under ITID-13111.
indicators: Insider-sourced customer data appearing in a public leak or for sale
Regulator or media inquiry referencing insider involvement
Customer complaints tracing to data an insider was known to have accessed
vectors: Insider bulk export of customer records to personal storage or email
Insider sale of stolen customer data to a third party who later leaks it
rootCauses: Insufficient monitoring of legitimate-access bulk data exports
Excessive standing access to customer data beyond role requirements
controls: Data loss prevention on privileged user egress
User and entity behavior analytics (UEBA)
ITID-23114.detection: Depends on DLP/UEBA coverage of privileged internal access; often first detected via external disclosure rather than internal telemetry.
ITID-23114.response: Coordinate with the insider-threat investigation team while independently managing customer notification, regulatory obligations, and public communications.
metrics: Time from public disclosure to customer notification
Number of insider-sourced data exposure incidents per year
ITID-23114.notes: Deliberately narrow: this leaf covers only the public disclosure and brand-impact consequence of an insider theft of customer data. The theft itself — motivation, method, internal handling — is owned by ITID-13111 (Insider Theft of Customer PII/Financial Records) and is not re-described here to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Customer Data Exposure via Insider Data Theft
playbook.description: For customer data deliberately exfiltrated by an insider (employee or contractor) with legitimate access.

steps.title: Identify the insider and the access used
steps.desc: Review DLP alerts, access logs, and export/download activity to identify who exfiltrated data and through what access path.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR and Legal before taking any employee-facing action.
steps.outcome: Identified individual and confirmed access path used.

steps.title: Suspend the insider's access
steps.desc: Immediately suspend account access and physical access for the individual, coordinated with HR and Legal.
steps.guidance: Preserve devices and accounts for forensic collection rather than wiping them.

steps.title: Attempt to recover or confirm destruction of exfiltrated data
steps.desc: Where legally and technically possible, pursue recovery of the exfiltrated data (e.g. via legal hold, device return, or third-party takedown).
steps.outcome: Data recovered, destroyed under legal process, or scope of irrecoverable exposure confirmed.

steps.title: Execute regulatory and customer notification per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications on the legally mandated timeline once scope is confirmed.

steps.title: Review access controls and insider-threat detection gaps
steps.desc: Document the incident and evaluate whether access scoping, DLP coverage, or offboarding controls need improvement.

steps.title: Scope exactly what customer data was exfiltrated
steps.desc: Reconstruct the export/download/transfer activity to determine data categories and record volume taken.

steps.title: Loop in Legal, HR, and Privacy immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal, HR, and Privacy given both employment-action and breach-notification implications.

ITID-23115.def: An incident in which a ransomware group, having exfiltrated customer data as part of a double- or triple-extortion attack, publicly posts or threatens to post that data on a leak site, triggering brand, regulatory, and customer-notification consequences.
ITID-23115.purpose: Captures the public disclosure and brand fallout when a ransomware group publishes or threatens to publish stolen customer data on a leak site.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed or threatened posting of company customer data on a ransomware group's leak site
Public/media/customer reaction and regulatory notification triggered by such a posting
scopeExcludes: The ransomware intrusion, encryption, and exfiltration mechanics themselves (ITID-31131 through ITID-31144, the double-extortion ransomware ITID family)
Extortion communications that do not involve confirmed customer data (ITID-23611 through ITID-23615, the general ransomware extortion-threat leaves)
ITID-23115.severity: Critical once customer data is confirmed posted publicly; High while only threatened.
ITID-23115.priority: P1 immediately upon leak-site posting or credible threat naming the company.
ITID-23115.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership, legal, privacy, law enforcement liaison, and communications; align with the ransomware incident's own command structure rather than running a parallel response.
indicators: Company name/data appearing on a known ransomware leak site
Ransom note or negotiation channel referencing planned publication of customer data
Dark-web monitoring alert matching company data samples
vectors: Data staged and exfiltrated prior to encryption by a ransomware affiliate
Publication via the group's dedicated leak-site infrastructure
rootCauses: Successful ransomware intrusion and exfiltration (root cause owned by the ransomware ITID family)
Failure to negotiate or pay before the group's disclosure deadline
controls: Dark-web/leak-site monitoring
Pre-negotiated incident response retainer with ransomware negotiation expertise
ITID-23115.detection: Leak-site monitoring services provide the primary external detection signal for this leaf; internal telemetry is owned by the underlying ransomware ITIDs.
ITID-23115.response: Confirm data scope and authenticity from leak-site samples, engage legal and communications for coordinated disclosure, and support the broader ransomware incident response.
metrics: Time from leak-site posting to customer/regulatory notification
Volume of customer records confirmed posted
ITID-23115.notes: Scoped strictly to the disclosure and brand-impact side of a ransomware group's data leak. The intrusion, encryption, and exfiltration techniques belong to the double-extortion ransomware ITID family (ITID-31131 through ITID-31144); this leaf begins once customer data is posted or credibly threatened for publication.

playbook.name: Response: Customer Data Breach via Ransomware Group Data Exfiltration/Leak
playbook.description: For customer data exfiltrated and published/threatened by a ransomware group as part of a double-extortion attack.

steps.title: Confirm the leak site posting and verify authenticity
steps.desc: Locate the ransomware group's leak site listing/sample and verify it corresponds to real, current organizational data rather than recycled or fabricated data.
steps.guidance: Use threat intel resources and out-of-band access to avoid interacting directly with attacker infrastructure from corporate assets.
steps.outcome: Authenticity of the claimed leak confirmed or refuted.
steps.abort: If data cannot be verified as ours, treat as an unverified claim and continue monitoring.
steps.tool: Threat intelligence platform / dark web monitoring

steps.title: Loop in Legal, Privacy, and Law Enforcement
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Privacy given breach-notification obligations, and coordinate with law enforcement per standard ransomware engagement protocol.
steps.guidance: Standard guidance is against paying extortion demands; any negotiation decision is Legal/Executive-level, not SOC-level.

steps.title: Coordinate takedown requests where feasible
steps.desc: Pursue takedown or delisting requests for the leak site posting through Legal and threat intel partners where jurisdictionally possible.
steps.outcome: Takedown pursued; outcome documented regardless of success likelihood.

steps.title: Execute regulatory and customer notification per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications on the legally mandated timeline once scope is confirmed.

steps.title: Document the incident and feed findings into ransomware readiness improvements
steps.desc: Record the root cause of the underlying intrusion and recommend controls to reduce future ransomware/exfiltration risk.

steps.title: Correlate with the known intrusion and scope exfiltrated customer data
steps.desc: Cross-reference the leaked sample against forensic findings from the underlying ransomware intrusion to determine full scope of customer data taken.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of exfiltrated customer data tied to the confirmed intrusion.

steps.title: Confirm the underlying intrusion is fully contained
steps.desc: Verify with the IR team handling the ransomware intrusion that attacker access has been eradicated, not just that encryption has stopped.
steps.outcome: Confirmed containment of the source intrusion.

ITID-23116.def: A confirmed or suspected exposure of customer data that has not yet been attributed to a specific vector (compromised database, cloud misconfiguration, vendor breach, insider theft, or ransomware leak).
ITID-23116.purpose: Catch-all for customer data exposure incidents that do not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to attribute a specific exposure vector
Ambiguous or multi-vector customer data exposure reports
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf (ITID-23111 through ITID-23115)
ITID-23116.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High pending scoping given customer data sensitivity.
ITID-23116.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 upon confirmation of a specific exposure vector or scale.
ITID-23116.escalation: Escalate to legal/privacy for preliminary risk assessment while investigation continues; reclassify once the specific pattern is clarified.
indicators: Customer complaint or external report of unclear origin
Fragmentary evidence of customer data appearing outside authorized systems
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
ITID-23116.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-23116.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed; begin preliminary legal/privacy risk assessment in parallel.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
Average time to reclassification
ITID-23116.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one; reclassify to ITID-23111 through ITID-23115 as soon as the exposure vector is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Customer Data Exposure
playbook.description: For customer data exposure incidents that do not clearly fit a more specific category; establishes baseline scoping and notification handling pending clearer classification.

steps.title: Establish the exposure mechanism
steps.desc: Determine how the customer data became exposed (system compromise, misconfiguration, third party, insider, or unclear) to enable reclassification to a more specific playbook if warranted.
steps.outcome: Exposure mechanism identified or confirmed as genuinely unclear.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Privacy immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Privacy given likely breach-notification obligations for any customer data exposure.

steps.title: Address root cause once mechanism is confirmed
steps.desc: Once the exposure mechanism is clear, remediate its root cause; reclassify to a specific ITID playbook if one now clearly applies.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated or incident reclassified.

steps.title: Execute regulatory and customer notification per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications on the legally mandated timeline once scope is confirmed.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the exposure mechanism, scope, and response actions for future reference and classification refinement.

steps.title: Scope the exposed customer data
steps.desc: Determine what data categories and approximate volume of customer records are affected.

steps.title: Close the exposure vector
steps.desc: Take whatever technical or procedural action is needed to stop ongoing exposure once the mechanism is understood.

ITID-23121.def: An incident in which employee personal identifiable information or HR records (SSNs, addresses, benefits enrollment, performance data) are exfiltrated from a company-operated HR system through direct technical compromise, and the exposure becomes known internally or externally.
ITID-23121.purpose: Captures the public disclosure and brand fallout when employee PII or HR records are breached from company-owned HR systems.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed exfiltration of employee PII/HR records from a first-party HR system
Employee notification and regulatory disclosure obligations triggered by the exposure
scopeExcludes: Payroll/compensation-specific data exposure (ITID-23122)
Exposure via a third-party HR/benefits platform breach (ITID-23123)
Exposure via insider theft (ITID-23124)
ITID-23121.severity: High, driven by data sensitivity (SSNs, health data) and employee population size affected.
ITID-23121.priority: P1 once exfiltration and employee data scope are confirmed.
ITID-23121.escalation: Escalate to HR leadership, legal, and privacy; internal workforce communications must be coordinated to avoid rumor and confusion ahead of formal notification.
indicators: Anomalous bulk export from HRIS/HR database
Employee reports of identity theft or fraud correlating with company employment
Threat actor claim referencing internal HR data
vectors: Exploitation of an HRIS application vulnerability
Compromise of HR administrator credentials
Direct database compromise of the HR system
rootCauses: Unpatched HRIS application or underlying database
Excessive standing access to HR records beyond role requirements
controls: HRIS access controls and least privilege
Database activity monitoring on HR systems
ITID-23121.detection: HRIS audit logs and DLP on HR-system egress provide the primary technical detection surface.
ITID-23121.response: Confirm scope of exposed employee records, contain the compromised access path, and coordinate employee notification with HR and legal.
metrics: Number of employee records confirmed exposed
Time to employee notification
ITID-23121.notes: Scoped to direct compromise of first-party HR systems; adjacent leaves cover payroll-specific data, third-party HR platforms, and insider-sourced theft to avoid overlap.

playbook.name: Response: Employee PII/HR Records Data Breach
playbook.description: For a breach exposing employee personal or HR records (e.g. SSNs, addresses, performance reviews, background checks).

steps.title: Confirm the breach and identify the affected HR system or data store
steps.desc: Verify the breach and identify which HR/HRIS system, file share, or export was involved.
steps.outcome: Confirmed breach with identified source system.

steps.title: Loop in Legal, Privacy, and HR immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Privacy/HR given likely breach-notification obligations and employee-relations sensitivity.
steps.guidance: Employee-data breaches carry both regulatory and workplace-trust implications; HR must be part of the communications plan.

steps.title: Remediate root cause and audit HR system access controls
steps.desc: Fix the underlying vulnerability/misconfiguration and review who has access to sensitive HR data more broadly.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated; access controls reviewed.

steps.title: Execute regulatory and employee notification per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications to regulators and affected employees on the legally mandated timeline, coordinated with HR communications.
steps.guidance: Consider offering credit monitoring where SSNs or financial data were exposed, per Legal's guidance.

steps.title: Document the incident and implement preventive guardrails
steps.desc: Record root cause and recommend controls to better protect employee data going forward.

steps.title: Scope exactly which employee records and data fields were exposed
steps.desc: Determine the specific employee population affected and which sensitive fields (SSN, banking, health, disciplinary records) were included.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of affected employees and data fields.

steps.title: Close the exposure vector
steps.desc: Revoke compromised access, fix the misconfiguration, or otherwise stop ongoing exposure of the HR data.

ITID-23122.def: An incident in which payroll, salary, bonus, or equity compensation data is exposed or leaked, creating distinct risks around employee financial fraud, internal pay-equity fallout, and competitive intelligence exposure.
ITID-23122.purpose: Captures the public disclosure and brand fallout specific to payroll or compensation data exposure, distinct from broader HR record breaches.
scopeIncludes: Exposure of payroll processing data, direct-deposit/bank details, or compensation bands/statements
Internal fallout from leaked comparative salary/compensation data (pay-equity disputes)
scopeExcludes: General HR/PII exposure not specific to compensation (ITID-23121)
Payroll exposure sourced from a third-party payroll platform breach (ITID-23123)
ITID-23122.severity: High; direct-deposit/bank detail exposure warrants Critical due to fraud risk.
ITID-23122.priority: P1 once payroll data with financial fraud potential is confirmed exposed.
ITID-23122.escalation: Escalate to finance/payroll operations, legal, and HR simultaneously; direct-deposit exposure requires urgent fraud-prevention outreach to employees.
indicators: Anomalous access to payroll processing system
Employee reports of fraudulent direct-deposit changes
Compensation spreadsheet found circulating outside authorized distribution
vectors: Compromise of payroll system credentials
Business email compromise targeting payroll change requests
Unauthorized internal access to compensation records
rootCauses: Weak authentication on payroll change workflows
Compensation data stored/shared beyond minimum necessary access
controls: Multi-factor verification for payroll/direct-deposit changes
Access restriction on compensation data to HR/finance leadership
ITID-23122.detection: Payroll system audit logs and finance fraud-monitoring provide the primary detection surface.
ITID-23122.response: Freeze/verify any pending payroll changes, notify affected employees of fraud risk, and coordinate with finance on financial-loss containment.
metrics: Number of employees with exposed direct-deposit/bank data
Financial loss from resulting payroll fraud
ITID-23122.notes: Differentiated from ITID-23121 by its compensation-specific scope and the added financial-fraud and pay-equity dimensions unique to payroll data.

playbook.name: Response: Payroll/Compensation Data Exposure
playbook.description: For exposure of employee payroll or compensation data (salaries, bonuses, bank account/direct-deposit details).

steps.title: Confirm the exposure and identify the payroll system or process involved
steps.desc: Verify the exposure and identify the specific payroll platform, report, or export affected.

steps.title: Loop in Legal, Privacy, HR, and Finance immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Privacy/HR/Finance given breach-notification obligations and risk of direct-deposit fraud.

steps.title: Remediate root cause
steps.desc: Fix the underlying vulnerability or process gap that allowed the exposure.

steps.title: Execute regulatory and employee notification per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications on the legally mandated timeline, including guidance to affected employees on monitoring their accounts.

steps.title: Document the incident and implement preventive guardrails
steps.desc: Record root cause and recommend controls (e.g. MFA on direct-deposit changes) to prevent recurrence and follow-on fraud.

steps.title: Scope the affected employees and compensation data fields
steps.desc: Determine which employees' compensation and banking details were exposed.

steps.title: Flag affected accounts for direct-deposit fraud monitoring
steps.desc: Coordinate with Payroll/Finance to monitor for unauthorized direct-deposit change requests on affected employees during the exposure window.
steps.guidance: Direct-deposit redirection fraud is a common follow-on attack after payroll data exposure.
steps.outcome: Monitoring in place for fraudulent deposit changes.

ITID-23123.def: An incident in which a third-party HR, payroll, or benefits administration platform used by the company suffers its own breach, exposing company employee data and requiring the company to manage disclosure despite not controlling the compromised system.
ITID-23123.purpose: Captures the brand and disclosure impact on the company when a third-party HR or benefits platform holding employee data is breached.
scopeIncludes: Vendor/platform breach confirmed to include company employee data
Company-side employee notification and communication following a vendor breach
Contractual review of vendor liability under the data-processing agreement
scopeExcludes: Breach of a company-owned and -operated HR system (ITID-23121)
Vendor breach limited to customer rather than employee data (ITID-23113)
ITID-23123.severity: High, driven by volume/sensitivity of exposed employee data regardless of fault location.
ITID-23123.priority: P1 once the vendor confirms company employee data was included in the breach.
ITID-23123.escalation: Escalate to HR, vendor management, and legal immediately upon vendor notification.
indicators: Vendor breach notification naming the company as an affected customer
Public reporting of a benefits/payroll platform breach affecting multiple client organizations
vectors: Compromise of the vendor's own infrastructure or applications
Vendor insider or contractor negligence
rootCauses: Insufficient vendor security due-diligence
Data processing agreement lacking timely breach-notification requirements
controls: Vendor security risk assessment program
Data processing agreements with breach-notification SLAs
ITID-23123.detection: Detection is largely dependent on vendor self-reporting or third-party breach-monitoring services.
ITID-23123.response: Confirm scope of company employee data involved, activate vendor incident-response clause, and manage independent employee notification obligations.
metrics: Time from vendor notification to employee notification
Number of vendor breaches affecting employee data per year
detections: Third-party breach monitoring/threat intelligence feed alerting
ITID-23123.notes: Mirrors ITID-23113 but scoped to employee rather than customer data, reflecting the distinct notification and workforce-relations obligations involved.

playbook.name: Response: Employee Data Exposure via Third-Party HR/Benefits Platform Breach
playbook.description: For employee data exposed because a third-party HR, payroll, or benefits platform vendor was breached.

steps.title: Obtain confirmation and details from the vendor
steps.desc: Contact the vendor's incident response contact to confirm the breach, timeline, and what employee data was in scope.
steps.guidance: Escalate via the contract's security-incident clause if the vendor is slow to respond.
steps.outcome: Written vendor confirmation with initial scope.

steps.title: Loop in Legal, Privacy, and HR immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Privacy/HR given breach-notification obligations and confirm vendor contractual obligations (DPA/BAA terms).
steps.outcome: Relevant teams engaged; vendor obligations reviewed.

steps.title: Verify vendor remediation before resuming normal data sharing
steps.desc: Review evidence the vendor has closed the root cause before resuming full data sharing.
steps.outcome: Vendor remediation verified or arrangement revised.

steps.title: Execute regulatory and employee notification per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications on the legally mandated timeline, coordinated with the vendor where appropriate.

steps.title: Reassess vendor risk posture and contractual controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and evaluate whether the vendor relationship or DPA terms need to change.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; vendor risk review completed.

steps.title: Independently determine which employees' data was held by the vendor
steps.desc: Cross-reference internal records of what employee data was shared with the vendor to independently verify scope.
steps.outcome: Independent scope of affected employee population.

steps.title: Suspend further data sharing with the vendor pending assessment
steps.desc: Pause new employee data transfers to the affected vendor until remediation is verified.

ITID-23124.def: An incident in which a malicious insider steals employee data and the theft results in public disclosure, regulatory notification, or reputational impact — distinct from the insider's motivation and internal handling, which is tracked elsewhere.
ITID-23124.purpose: Captures the public disclosure and brand fallout when employee data theft by a malicious insider becomes externally known.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed insider theft of employee records that has become known externally or to affected employees at scale
Employee notification and disclosure obligations triggered by insider-sourced employee data theft
scopeExcludes: The insider's motivation, method of theft, and internal HR/investigative handling (ITID-13113 Insider Theft of Employee/HR Records)
Insider theft that remains internally contained with no external disclosure obligation
ITID-23124.severity: High, driven by data volume/sensitivity; insider provenance does not reduce severity for affected employees.
ITID-23124.priority: P1 once external disclosure or notification obligations are confirmed.
ITID-23124.escalation: Escalate to legal, privacy, and HR communications in parallel with the insider-threat investigation tracked under ITID-13113.
indicators: Insider-sourced employee data appearing in a public leak or for sale
Employee complaints of identity theft tracing to internal data an insider was known to have accessed
vectors: Insider bulk export of employee records to personal storage or email
Insider sale of stolen employee data to a third party who later leaks it
rootCauses: Insufficient monitoring of legitimate-access bulk data exports
Excessive standing access to employee data beyond role requirements
controls: Data loss prevention on privileged user egress
User and entity behavior analytics (UEBA)
ITID-23124.detection: Depends on DLP/UEBA coverage of privileged internal access; often first detected via external disclosure rather than internal telemetry.
ITID-23124.response: Coordinate with the insider-threat investigation team while independently managing employee notification and public communications.
metrics: Time from public disclosure to employee notification
Number of insider-sourced employee data exposure incidents per year
ITID-23124.notes: Deliberately narrow: this leaf covers only the public disclosure and brand-impact consequence of an insider theft of employee data. The theft itself is owned by ITID-13113 (Insider Theft of Employee/HR Records) and is not re-described here to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Employee Data Exposure via Insider Data Theft
playbook.description: For employee personal/HR data deliberately exfiltrated by an insider with legitimate access.

steps.title: Identify the insider and the access used
steps.desc: Review DLP alerts and HR system access/export logs to identify who exfiltrated employee data and through what access path.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR and Legal before taking any employee-facing action; this may involve HR staff themselves given system access, requiring extra care in the investigation team's composition.
steps.outcome: Identified individual and confirmed access path.

steps.title: Suspend the insider's access
steps.desc: Immediately suspend account and physical access for the individual, coordinated with HR and Legal.
steps.guidance: Preserve devices and accounts for forensic collection.

steps.title: Attempt to recover or confirm destruction of exfiltrated data
steps.desc: Where legally and technically possible, pursue recovery of the exfiltrated data via legal hold, device return, or third-party takedown.
steps.outcome: Data recovered, destroyed under legal process, or irrecoverable exposure confirmed.

steps.title: Execute regulatory and employee notification per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications on the legally mandated timeline once scope is confirmed.

steps.title: Review HR data access controls and insider-threat detection gaps
steps.desc: Document the incident and evaluate whether access scoping, DLP coverage, or HR system audit controls need improvement.

steps.title: Scope exactly what employee data was exfiltrated
steps.desc: Reconstruct export/download activity to determine data categories and affected employee population.

steps.title: Loop in Legal, HR leadership, and Privacy immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal, senior HR leadership (outside the implicated individual's chain if relevant), and Privacy.

ITID-23125.def: A confirmed or suspected exposure of employee data that has not yet been attributed to a specific vector (direct HR system compromise, payroll-specific exposure, third-party HR/benefits platform breach, or insider theft).
ITID-23125.purpose: Catch-all for employee data exposure incidents that do not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to attribute a specific exposure vector
Ambiguous or multi-vector employee data exposure reports
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf (ITID-23121 through ITID-23124)
ITID-23125.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High pending scoping given employee data sensitivity.
ITID-23125.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 upon confirmation of a specific exposure vector or scale.
ITID-23125.escalation: Escalate to HR and legal/privacy for preliminary risk assessment while investigation continues; reclassify once the specific pattern is clarified.
indicators: Employee complaint or external report of unclear origin
Fragmentary evidence of employee data appearing outside authorized systems
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
ITID-23125.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-23125.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed; begin preliminary HR/legal risk assessment in parallel.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
Average time to reclassification
ITID-23125.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one; reclassify to ITID-23121 through ITID-23124 as soon as the exposure vector is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Employee Data Exposure
playbook.description: For employee data exposure incidents that do not clearly fit a more specific category; establishes baseline scoping and notification handling pending clearer classification.

steps.title: Establish the exposure mechanism
steps.desc: Determine how the employee data became exposed (system compromise, misconfiguration, third party, insider, or unclear) to enable reclassification if warranted.
steps.outcome: Exposure mechanism identified or confirmed as genuinely unclear.

steps.title: Loop in Legal, Privacy, and HR immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Privacy/HR given likely breach-notification obligations for any employee data exposure.

steps.title: Address root cause once mechanism is confirmed
steps.desc: Once the exposure mechanism is clear, remediate its root cause; reclassify to a specific ITID playbook if one now clearly applies.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated or incident reclassified.

steps.title: Execute regulatory and employee notification per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications on the legally mandated timeline once scope is confirmed.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the exposure mechanism, scope, and response actions for future reference and classification refinement.

steps.title: Scope the exposed employee data
steps.desc: Determine which employees and what data fields are affected.

steps.title: Close the exposure vector
steps.desc: Take whatever technical or procedural action is needed to stop ongoing exposure once the mechanism is understood.

ITID-23131.def: An incident in which company source code is discovered publicly accessible via a misconfigured public code repository (e.g., a private GitHub/GitLab repo accidentally made public, or code pushed to a public repo), and the exposure becomes known to researchers, competitors, or the public.
ITID-23131.purpose: Captures the public disclosure and brand fallout when proprietary source code is found exposed in a publicly accessible code repository.
scopeIncludes: Public discovery of company source code in a misconfigured public repository
Researcher/journalist responsible-disclosure report of exposed source code
Assessment and disclosure of any secrets/credentials embedded in the exposed code
scopeExcludes: Source code stolen via deliberate insider exfiltration (ITID-23132)
Source code obtained via a compromised CI/build pipeline (ITID-23133)
Any hardcoded credential found within the exposed code itself, which is tracked under the credential-leakage domain (ITID-12512 Hardcoded Credential in Public Code Repository)
ITID-23131.severity: High, escalating to Critical if the exposed code contains embedded secrets, security architecture detail, or core proprietary algorithms.
ITID-23131.priority: P1 upon confirmation of public exposure of production source code.
ITID-23131.escalation: Escalate to engineering leadership, security, and legal; rotate any embedded secrets immediately and assess competitive/security exposure.
indicators: Researcher or automated scanner notification of a public repository containing company code
Repository fork/star activity spike indicating external discovery
Code snippet referencing internal systems appearing in public forums
vectors: Repository visibility misconfigured from private to public
Code pushed to a personal or public fork by mistake
Public repository search/scanning by researchers or threat actors
rootCauses: Absence of repository visibility governance/scanning
No pre-commit secret-scanning or review gate
controls: Repository visibility governance and automated scanning
Pre-commit and CI secret-scanning
ITID-23131.detection: Automated public-repository scanning services provide strong detection coverage for this exposure pattern.
ITID-23131.response: Immediately restrict repository visibility, rotate exposed secrets, and assess whether proprietary logic disclosed creates competitive or security risk.
metrics: Time repository was publicly exposed before detection
Number of secrets rotated as a result
ITID-23131.notes: Any embedded credential found in the exposed repository is tracked separately under ITID-12512 (Hardcoded Credential in Public Code Repository) to avoid duplicating the credential-leakage domain; this leaf covers the source-code and IP disclosure impact itself.

playbook.name: Response: Source Code Leak via Misconfigured Public Code Repository
playbook.description: For source code discovered publicly exposed due to a misconfigured repository visibility setting (e.g. a private repo accidentally set to public, or a public fork retaining private history).

steps.title: Confirm exposure and set the repository private immediately
steps.desc: Verify the repository is genuinely public and belongs to the organization, and immediately restrict visibility.
steps.guidance: Restricting visibility does not undo any cloning/scraping that already happened — treat as already-exposed for scoping purposes.

steps.title: Rotate every credential/secret found in the code or history
steps.desc: Rotate all API keys, passwords, tokens, and certificates discovered in the exposed repository, regardless of whether misuse has been confirmed.
steps.guidance: Treat any found secret as compromised — do not wait for evidence of misuse.

steps.title: Fix the root-cause process/policy gap
steps.desc: Correct the org-level default visibility settings or approval process that allowed a private repo to be made public.
steps.outcome: Root cause closed at the org-policy level.

steps.title: Assess and communicate business impact
steps.desc: Assess whether the exposed code reveals exploitable vulnerabilities in production systems and coordinate any needed hardening or customer communication with Legal/PR.

steps.title: Document the incident and implement preventive guardrails
steps.desc: Record root cause and recommend automated guardrails (e.g. secret-scanning pre-commit hooks, default-private repo policy).

steps.title: Scope what the repository contained
steps.desc: Review the repository contents and full commit history for hardcoded secrets, credentials, API keys, customer data, or other sensitive material — not just the current state.
