steps.guidance: Secrets committed and later removed still exist in git history and must be treated as exposed.
steps.outcome: Full inventory of sensitive material ever present in the repo.

steps.title: Audit for other similarly-misconfigured repositories
steps.desc: Check the organization's other repositories for the same visibility misconfiguration.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no other publicly-exposed private repositories.

steps.title: Determine if the repository was cloned, forked, or indexed by anyone external
steps.desc: Check hosting platform analytics/logs, search engine caches, and code-scraping archive sites for evidence of external access.
steps.outcome: Confirmed access history, or confirmed inability to determine it.

ITID-23132.def: An incident in which a malicious insider deliberately exfiltrates company source code and it subsequently becomes publicly known, sold, or leaked — distinct from the insider's motivation and internal handling, which is tracked elsewhere.
ITID-23132.purpose: Captures the public disclosure and brand/competitive fallout when a malicious insider exfiltrates and leaks proprietary source code.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed insider exfiltration of source code that has become known externally (leaked, sold, or published)
Public/competitive-impact assessment and disclosure decisions following such a leak
scopeExcludes: The insider's motivation, method of exfiltration, and internal HR/investigative handling (ITID-13112 Insider Theft of Proprietary Source Code or Trade Secrets)
Insider exfiltration that remains internally contained with no external disclosure or discovery
ITID-23132.severity: High to Critical depending on the strategic value of the leaked code (core product vs. peripheral tooling).
ITID-23132.priority: P1 once external disclosure or leak of the code is confirmed.
ITID-23132.escalation: Escalate to legal, engineering leadership, and communications in parallel with the insider-threat investigation tracked under ITID-13112.
indicators: Company source code appearing on a public repository, forum, or dark-web listing
Competitor product suddenly mirroring proprietary implementation details
vectors: Insider upload of source code to personal cloud storage or public repository
Insider sale of source code to a competitor or broker who later leaks it
rootCauses: Insufficient monitoring of source-code repository export/clone activity by privileged developers
controls: Source-code repository DLP and export monitoring
Code repository access reviews for departing/high-risk personnel
ITID-23132.detection: Depends on repository-level DLP and export monitoring; often first detected via external discovery rather than internal telemetry.
ITID-23132.response: Coordinate with the insider-threat investigation while independently assessing competitive exposure and any public statement needs.
metrics: Time from public discovery to internal confirmation
Estimated competitive/IP value of leaked code
ITID-23132.notes: Deliberately narrow: this leaf covers only the public disclosure and brand/competitive-impact consequence of an insider's source-code theft. The theft itself is owned by ITID-13112 and is not re-described here to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Source Code Leak via Insider Exfiltration
playbook.description: For source code deliberately exfiltrated by an insider (employee or contractor) with legitimate repository access.

steps.title: Identify the insider and the access used
steps.desc: Review repository audit logs, DLP alerts, and clone/download activity to identify who exfiltrated code and how.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR and Legal before taking any employee-facing action.
steps.outcome: Identified individual and confirmed access path.

steps.title: Suspend the insider's access
steps.desc: Immediately suspend repository, VPN, and physical access for the individual, coordinated with HR and Legal.
steps.guidance: Preserve devices and accounts for forensic collection.

steps.title: Rotate any secrets present in the exfiltrated code
steps.desc: Rotate credentials, keys, or certificates present in the exfiltrated codebase.

steps.title: Pursue legal remedies and recovery where applicable
steps.desc: Work with Legal on options such as legal hold, cease-and-desist, or civil action depending on destination and use of the code.
steps.outcome: Legal course of action determined and pursued.

steps.title: Review repository access controls and insider-threat detection gaps
steps.desc: Document the incident and evaluate whether repository access scoping, DLP coverage, or offboarding controls need improvement.

steps.title: Scope exactly which repositories/code was exfiltrated
steps.desc: Reconstruct clone/export activity to determine which repositories and what proportion of the codebase was taken.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and HR immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal and HR given employment-action and potential IP-theft/litigation implications.

ITID-23133.def: An incident in which an attacker compromises a build server, CI/CD pipeline, or associated artifact repository to exfiltrate proprietary source code, and the resulting leak or theft becomes publicly known.
ITID-23133.purpose: Captures the public disclosure and brand fallout when source code is stolen via compromise of the build or CI/CD pipeline.
scopeIncludes: Source code exfiltrated through compromise of build/CI infrastructure and subsequently disclosed or leaked
Public/competitive-impact assessment following such a leak
scopeExcludes: The technical compromise of the CI/CD pipeline itself, including any supply-chain tampering with build artifacts (tracked under the relevant software-supply-chain-security ITID)
Source code exposure via a simple public-repository misconfiguration with no pipeline compromise (ITID-23131)
ITID-23133.severity: Critical, given that pipeline compromise can also indicate broader software-supply-chain risk beyond the code leak itself.
ITID-23133.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation of pipeline compromise with code exfiltration.
ITID-23133.escalation: Escalate to engineering, security, and legal; coordinate closely with the software-supply-chain-security incident response given shared root cause.
indicators: Anomalous access or artifact download from build/CI infrastructure
Leaked code sample matching an internal build artifact rather than the version-control source
vectors: Compromised CI/CD service account or API token
Exploited vulnerability in build-server software
Malicious pipeline configuration change granting exfiltration access
rootCauses: Insufficient hardening/monitoring of CI/CD infrastructure
Excessive standing permissions on build-pipeline service accounts
controls: CI/CD access hardening and monitoring
Build artifact integrity verification
ITID-23133.detection: CI/CD audit logging and artifact-integrity monitoring provide the primary technical detection surface, owned jointly with the supply-chain-security domain.
ITID-23133.response: Contain the compromised pipeline, rotate pipeline credentials, and assess both the code-leak brand impact and broader supply-chain integrity risk.
metrics: Time from pipeline compromise to code-leak detection
Number of build artifacts affected
ITID-23133.notes: The pipeline compromise mechanics are jointly owned with the software-supply-chain-security ITID domain; this leaf focuses on the resulting source-code disclosure and its brand impact.

playbook.name: Response: Source Code Leak via Compromised Build/CI Pipeline
playbook.description: For source code leaked as a result of a compromised CI/CD pipeline, build server, or associated credentials.

steps.title: Confirm the compromise and identify the affected pipeline/stage
steps.desc: Review CI/CD logs, build artifacts, and pipeline configuration changes to confirm compromise and identify the affected stage (source checkout, build, artifact storage, deployment).
steps.outcome: Confirmed compromise with identified pipeline stage.

steps.title: Isolate and disable the compromised pipeline
steps.desc: Disable the affected pipeline/runner immediately and revoke its credentials to stop further access.
steps.outcome: Pipeline isolated; no further attacker access.

steps.title: Audit build artifacts and past releases for tampering
steps.desc: Verify that no malicious code was injected into build artifacts or released software during the compromise window (supply-chain check).
steps.outcome: Confirmed no tampered artifacts shipped, or tampering identified and addressed.

steps.title: Re-sign and re-release affected artifacts if tampering occurred
steps.desc: If tampered artifacts were found to have shipped, coordinate a clean re-release and customer communication as needed.
steps.outcome: Clean artifacts released; customers informed if warranted.

steps.title: Document the incident and harden the CI/CD pipeline
steps.desc: Record root cause and recommend hardening (e.g. least-privilege pipeline secrets, artifact signing verification).

steps.title: Scope which source code and secrets the pipeline had access to
steps.desc: Determine which repositories, build secrets, and signing keys the compromised pipeline could access, and whether they were exfiltrated.
steps.guidance: CI systems often hold broad secrets access — treat scope generously.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of exposed code and secrets.

steps.title: Rotate all secrets and signing keys accessible to the pipeline
steps.desc: Rotate build/deploy credentials, API keys, and code-signing certificates the pipeline could reach.

steps.title: Fix the root-cause pipeline vulnerability
steps.desc: Patch the vulnerability or misconfiguration that allowed pipeline compromise.

ITID-23134.def: An incident in which a third-party contractor or vendor with legitimate access to company source code (for development, integration, or support purposes) leaks or loses control of that code, resulting in public disclosure.
ITID-23134.purpose: Captures the brand and disclosure impact when source code is leaked via a third-party contractor or vendor's authorized access.
scopeIncludes: Source code leaked or exposed via a contractor/vendor's own systems, devices, or negligence
Company-side disclosure and vendor-liability management following such a leak
scopeExcludes: Source code leaked by a company employee/insider (ITID-23132)
Source code stolen via direct compromise of company-owned build infrastructure (ITID-23133)
ITID-23134.severity: High to Critical depending on the strategic value of the leaked code.
ITID-23134.priority: P1 once vendor/contractor-sourced code leak is confirmed.
ITID-23134.escalation: Escalate to vendor management, engineering leadership, and legal; review contractor access scope and NDA/contract enforcement options.
indicators: Source code appearing publicly traceable to a contractor's own repository or device
Vendor notification of their own security incident referencing company code access
vectors: Contractor's personal or unmanaged device compromised or lost
Contractor's own repository misconfigured to public
Contractor negligence in handling code under NDA
rootCauses: Insufficient access scoping/least privilege for contractor code access
Lack of contractual security requirements or audit rights over contractor environments
controls: Contractor access scoping and time-limited credentials
Vendor security requirements in contracts/NDAs
ITID-23134.detection: Detection is largely dependent on external discovery or contractor self-reporting; limited direct technical visibility into contractor environments.
ITID-23134.response: Revoke contractor access, assess leak scope, and pursue contractual/legal remedies alongside brand-impact management.
metrics: Number of contractor-sourced code leaks per year
Time from discovery to contractor access revocation
ITID-23134.notes: Differentiated from ITID-23132 (insider) and ITID-23133 (pipeline compromise) by the third-party/contractual access vector, which drives distinct vendor-liability and contract-enforcement response steps.

playbook.name: Response: Source Code Leak via Third-Party Contractor/Vendor Access
playbook.description: For source code leaked through a third-party contractor or vendor who was granted legitimate repository access.

steps.title: Confirm the leak and identify the contractor/vendor involved
steps.desc: Review repository access grants and audit logs to confirm which contractor/vendor account was the source.
steps.outcome: Confirmed leak with identified third-party account.

steps.title: Revoke the third party's access immediately
steps.desc: Suspend the contractor/vendor's repository and system access pending investigation.

steps.title: Rotate any secrets the third party had access to
steps.desc: Rotate credentials or keys accessible to the third-party account.

steps.title: Pursue contractual/legal remedies as determined by Legal
steps.desc: Execute on Legal's determined course of action against the third party (e.g. breach-of-contract claim, takedown demand).

steps.title: Review third-party access provisioning practices
steps.desc: Document the incident and evaluate whether third-party access scoping, review cadence, or offboarding processes need improvement.

steps.title: Scope what code and access the third party had
steps.desc: Determine the full extent of repository access granted to the contractor/vendor and what was actually accessed or downloaded.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of access and exposure.

steps.title: Loop in Legal to review the contractor/vendor agreement
steps.desc: Notify Legal to review the applicable NDA/contract terms and determine liability and remedy options.

ITID-23135.def: A confirmed or suspected leak of proprietary source code that has not yet been attributed to a specific vector (public repository misconfiguration, insider exfiltration, pipeline compromise, or contractor/vendor access).
ITID-23135.purpose: Catch-all for source code leak incidents that do not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to attribute a specific leak vector
Ambiguous or multi-vector source code leak reports
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf (ITID-23131 through ITID-23134)
ITID-23135.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High pending scoping.
ITID-23135.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 upon confirmation of a specific leak vector or scale.
ITID-23135.escalation: Escalate to engineering and legal for preliminary risk assessment while investigation continues; reclassify once the specific pattern is clarified.
indicators: Report of exposed source code of unclear origin
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
ITID-23135.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-23135.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-23135.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one; reclassify to ITID-23131 through ITID-23134 as soon as the leak vector is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Source Code Leak
playbook.description: For source code leak incidents that do not clearly fit a more specific category; establishes baseline scoping and remediation pending clearer classification.

steps.title: Establish the leak mechanism
steps.desc: Determine how the source code became exposed (misconfiguration, insider, compromised pipeline, third party, or unclear) to enable reclassification if warranted.
steps.outcome: Leak mechanism identified or confirmed as genuinely unclear.

steps.title: Rotate any discovered secrets and close the exposure vector
steps.desc: Rotate any credentials found in the exposed code and take whatever action is needed to stop ongoing exposure.

steps.title: Address root cause once mechanism is confirmed
steps.desc: Once the leak mechanism is clear, remediate its root cause; reclassify to a specific ITID playbook if one now clearly applies.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated or incident reclassified.

steps.title: Assess and address business impact
steps.desc: Assess whether the exposed code reveals exploitable vulnerabilities and coordinate any needed hardening.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the leak mechanism, scope, and response actions for future reference and classification refinement.

steps.title: Scope what code and secrets were exposed
steps.desc: Determine which repositories were affected and scan for hardcoded secrets or sensitive material.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of exposed code and secrets.

steps.title: Loop in Legal
steps.desc: Notify Legal given potential IP-protection and disclosure obligations.

ITID-23211.def: An incident in which material, non-public financial results (quarterly earnings, revenue figures, guidance) are disclosed to the media, market, or public before the company's official announcement.
ITID-23211.purpose: Captures the market and disclosure impact when unpublished earnings or financial results leak ahead of official announcement.
scopeIncludes: Premature disclosure of earnings figures, guidance, or financial results to media or market participants
Trading-halt, disclosure-controls, and investor-relations response to a premature leak
scopeExcludes: Leaks specifically tied to M&A/deal activity (ITID-23212)
Leaks resulting from a confirmed compromise of a finance system (ITID-23213)
Leaks motivated by insider trading intent (ITID-23214)
ITID-23211.severity: Critical, given securities-law implications (Reg FD) and potential market manipulation.
ITID-23211.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation that non-public financial data has reached external parties.
ITID-23211.escalation: Escalate immediately to the CFO, general counsel, and investor relations; assess Reg FD obligations for simultaneous public disclosure.
indicators: Financial figures reported by media ahead of the scheduled earnings release
Unusual pre-announcement trading volume/price movement
Analyst questions referencing specific unpublished figures
vectors: Leak by an individual with legitimate pre-release access to draft financials
Unsecured distribution of draft earnings materials (e.g., email, shared drive) reaching unauthorized recipients
rootCauses: Overly broad internal distribution of draft financial results prior to release
Insufficient information-barrier controls around the earnings process
controls: Restricted distribution list for pre-release financial materials
Disclosure controls and procedures under SOX/Reg FD
ITID-23211.detection: Primarily a governance/process control area; technical telemetry (document access logs, email DLP) supplements but does not replace disclosure-control review.
ITID-23211.response: Issue an immediate corrective public disclosure under Reg FD if warranted, and investigate the internal source of the leak.
metrics: Time from leak detection to corrective public disclosure
Number of individuals with pre-release access to leaked material
detections: Email DLP on draft financial documents
Document access logging on earnings materials
ITID-23211.notes: Scoped to premature disclosure of routine earnings/financial results; M&A-specific leaks, system-compromise-driven leaks, and insider-trading-motivated leaks are tracked in dedicated sibling leaves to keep the differentiating axis (leak channel/motive) clean.

playbook.name: Response: Pre-Announcement Earnings/Financial Results Leak
playbook.description: For unreleased earnings or financial results data leaked prior to official public announcement.

steps.title: Confirm the leaked content matches actual unreleased financial data
steps.desc: Verify the leaked figures/documents correspond to genuine, current internal financial data rather than outdated or fabricated figures.
steps.abort: If the leaked content cannot be verified as genuine and current, treat as unverified and continue monitoring rather than escalating market-moving actions.

steps.title: Loop in Legal, Investor Relations, and Compliance immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/IR/Compliance given securities-law implications of a material non-public information leak — this may trigger disclosure obligations under Reg FD or equivalent.
steps.guidance: Timing of any corrective public disclosure is a Legal/IR decision, not SOC-level.
steps.outcome: Legal/IR/Compliance engaged and assessing disclosure obligations.

steps.title: Identify and address the root-cause handling gap
steps.desc: Determine whether the leak stemmed from a process gap (e.g. overly broad pre-release distribution list) and correct it.

steps.title: Execute corrective public disclosure if required
steps.desc: If Legal/IR determine a Reg FD or equivalent disclosure obligation applies, issue the corrective public disclosure on the required timeline.

steps.title: Document the incident and tighten pre-release financial data controls
steps.desc: Record root cause and recommend controls (e.g. tighter distribution lists, watermarking, embargo enforcement) for future earnings cycles.

steps.title: Trace the leak's source and distribution path
steps.desc: Determine how the data left the organization (email, document sharing, insider disclosure) and how widely it has circulated.
steps.outcome: Source and distribution scope identified where possible.

steps.title: Restrict further internal distribution of the pre-announcement data
steps.desc: Revoke access to the source document/system and remind relevant personnel of confidentiality obligations.

ITID-23212.def: An incident in which non-public information about a pending merger, acquisition, divestiture, or other material deal is disclosed to media, market participants, or the public ahead of the official announcement.
ITID-23212.purpose: Captures the market and disclosure impact when confidential merger, acquisition, or deal financial data leaks before public announcement.
scopeIncludes: Premature disclosure of deal terms, valuation, target/counterparty identity, or deal timing
Response to leaks occurring during active due diligence or negotiation
scopeExcludes: Leaks of routine earnings/financial results not tied to a specific deal (ITID-23211)
Board governance document leaks that happen to reference a deal but are not primarily financial-data leaks (ITID-23233)
ITID-23212.severity: Critical, given securities-law implications, deal risk (walk-away rights, renegotiation), and market manipulation potential.
ITID-23212.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation that non-public deal information has reached external parties.
ITID-23212.escalation: Escalate immediately to general counsel, deal team leadership, and investor relations; assess counterparty notification obligations under the deal agreement.
indicators: Media reporting of deal terms or counterparty identity ahead of announcement
Unusual trading activity in the target or acquirer's securities
Counterparty inquiry about a suspected leak on their own side
vectors: Leak by an individual on the deal team with legitimate access to diligence materials
Compromise of a deal data room or virtual data room platform
Leak by an external advisor (bank, law firm, consultant) involved in the deal
rootCauses: Overly broad access to the deal data room beyond need-to-know
Insufficient confidentiality controls with external deal advisors
controls: Deal data room access controls and watermarking
NDA enforcement with all deal participants and advisors
ITID-23212.detection: Data room access logging provides useful technical signal; much of the exposure surface sits with external counterparties and advisors outside company telemetry.
ITID-23212.response: Assess deal-risk implications with legal, consider accelerated public announcement, and investigate the source of the leak including external parties.
metrics: Time from leak to accelerated public disclosure (if pursued)
Number of parties with data room access at time of leak
ITID-23212.notes: Distinguished from ITID-23211 by its deal-specific scope, which introduces external-advisor exposure surfaces and deal-risk (not just disclosure-timing) consequences not present in routine earnings leaks.

playbook.name: Response: M&A/Deal Financial Data Disclosure
playbook.description: For confidential merger, acquisition, or deal financial data disclosed prior to public announcement.

steps.title: Confirm the leaked content matches genuine deal data
steps.desc: Verify the leaked material corresponds to a genuine, current deal rather than speculative or outdated information.

steps.title: Loop in Legal, Compliance, and the deal team lead immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Compliance given securities-law implications (insider trading risk, Reg FD) and inform deal leadership.

steps.title: Address the root-cause handling gap
steps.desc: Determine whether the leak stemmed from a process gap (e.g. overly broad data room access) and correct it.

steps.title: Execute corrective disclosure or deal communications per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Issue any required corrective public disclosure or manage counterparty communications per Legal's guidance.

steps.title: Document the incident and tighten deal-room access controls
steps.desc: Record root cause and recommend controls for future deal processes.

steps.title: Trace the leak's source among the deal team and advisors
steps.desc: Determine how the data left the deal team's control — internal personnel, external advisors (bankers, lawyers, auditors), or a compromised system.
steps.guidance: Deal leaks often originate outside the organization's direct control (advisors, counterparties) — scope accordingly.
steps.outcome: Source and distribution scope identified where possible.

steps.title: Restrict further access to deal-room materials
steps.desc: Tighten access to the virtual data room and deal documents pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Access restricted to essential personnel only.

ITID-23213.def: An incident in which an attacker gains unauthorized technical access to a finance system (ERP, financial reporting platform, treasury system) and exfiltrates confidential financial data that subsequently becomes known externally.
ITID-23213.purpose: Captures the disclosure impact when confidential financial data is exposed through a direct technical compromise of a finance system.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed exfiltration of financial data from a compromised finance system, followed by external disclosure or threat-actor claim
Assessment of securities-law and market-disclosure obligations triggered by such a compromise
scopeExcludes: The technical intrusion technique and finance-system compromise investigation itself (tracked under the relevant external-attack ITID domain)
Leaks arising from authorized personnel misusing legitimate access for insider trading purposes (ITID-23214)
ITID-23213.severity: Critical, given both securities-disclosure and financial-fraud risk from a compromised finance system.
ITID-23213.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation of exfiltration from a finance system.
ITID-23213.escalation: Escalate to CFO, general counsel, security, and investor relations in parallel; assess whether attacker access enables ongoing financial fraud beyond the data leak itself.
indicators: Anomalous access or export activity from ERP/financial reporting systems
Threat actor claim or leak-site posting referencing internal financial data
Regulator or media inquiry citing specific unpublished financial figures
vectors: Exploited vulnerability or stolen credentials granting access to a finance system
Business email compromise targeting finance personnel with system access
rootCauses: Insufficient segmentation/monitoring of finance systems from general corporate network
Excessive standing access to financial reporting data
controls: Finance system network segmentation
Privileged access monitoring on finance/ERP systems
ITID-23213.detection: Finance system audit logs and DLP on egress provide the primary technical detection surface; upstream intrusion detection is owned by the source-vulnerability ITID.
ITID-23213.response: Contain the compromised access path, assess disclosure obligations with legal/IR, and coordinate any required corrective public disclosure.
metrics: Time from exfiltration to detection
Time to corrective public disclosure where required
ITID-23213.notes: Scoped to the disclosure/brand-impact side of a finance-system compromise; the technical intrusion itself is tracked under the relevant external-attack ITID domain.

playbook.name: Response: Financial Data Disclosure via Compromised Finance System
playbook.description: For confidential financial data disclosed as a result of unauthorized access to a finance system (ERP, accounting platform, treasury system).

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized access and identify the entry vector
steps.desc: Review finance system audit logs and SIEM data to confirm access occurred and determine how.
steps.outcome: Access confirmed with a working theory of entry vector.

steps.title: Revoke the compromised access path and rotate credentials
steps.desc: Disable the compromised account, close the exploited vulnerability, and rotate affected finance system credentials.

steps.title: Close the root-cause vulnerability and sweep for persistence
steps.desc: Patch the exploited vulnerability and check for additional footholds or unauthorized changes to financial records.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated; no persistence found; financial data integrity confirmed.

steps.title: Execute disclosure obligations per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send any required regulatory or market disclosures on the legally mandated timeline once scope is confirmed.

steps.title: Document the incident and harden finance system access controls
steps.desc: Record root cause and recommend controls to prevent recurrence.

steps.title: Scope exactly which financial data was accessed or exfiltrated
steps.desc: Determine which reports, ledgers, or records were accessed and whether data left the environment.

steps.title: Loop in Legal, Compliance, and Finance leadership immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Compliance/Finance given securities-law and financial-integrity implications.

ITID-23214.def: An incident in which an individual with legitimate access to material non-public financial information leaks or tips that information to a third party (or trades on it directly) for the purpose of enabling securities trading ahead of public disclosure.
ITID-23214.purpose: Captures the disclosure and legal impact when confidential financial data is leaked specifically to facilitate insider trading.
scopeIncludes: Leak of financial data with evidence or allegation of trading-motivated intent (tipping, front-running)
Securities-law investigation and disclosure obligations triggered by suspected insider trading
scopeExcludes: Leaks without evidence of trading motive (ITID-23211, ITID-23212)
Leaks resulting from external system compromise rather than an insider's deliberate tip (ITID-23213)
ITID-23214.severity: Critical, given direct securities-fraud and regulatory-enforcement exposure (SEC, insider trading statutes).
ITID-23214.priority: P1 immediately upon suspicion of trading-motivated leak.
ITID-23214.escalation: Escalate immediately to general counsel and outside securities counsel; preserve all relevant records for regulatory investigation before any remediation that could affect evidence.
indicators: Unusual trading activity by an individual or associated party ahead of a material announcement
Whistleblower report alleging a specific tip
Regulatory inquiry (SEC) referencing suspicious trading patterns
vectors: Deliberate tip by an insider with legitimate access to material non-public information
Direct trading by the insider or a closely associated party
rootCauses: Insufficient insider-trading policy enforcement or trading-window controls
Inadequate monitoring of trading activity by personnel with access to material non-public information
controls: Insider trading policy and blackout-window enforcement
Restricted trading list monitoring for personnel with MNPI access
ITID-23214.detection: Primarily a compliance/surveillance area; trading-activity surveillance and whistleblower channels are the main detection surface, not technical telemetry.
ITID-23214.response: Preserve evidence, cooperate with regulatory investigation, and take employment action consistent with legal guidance once findings are confirmed.
metrics: Number of suspected insider-trading leak cases investigated per year
detections: Trading surveillance system alerting on restricted-list personnel
ITID-23214.notes: Differentiated from other financial-disclosure leaves by trading motive rather than leak channel; this is the axis most relevant to securities-law response obligations.

playbook.name: Response: Financial Data Disclosure via Insider Trading-Motivated Leak
playbook.description: For confidential financial data leaked by an insider apparently motivated by facilitating insider trading.

steps.title: Identify the insider and the access used
steps.desc: Review access logs and DLP alerts to identify who disclosed the data and through what access path.
steps.guidance: Do not confront the individual before Legal/Compliance are engaged — securities-law matters require careful handling to preserve any enforcement action.
steps.outcome: Identified individual and confirmed access path.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal and Compliance as mandatory, immediate priority
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Compliance immediately given securities-law implications; this is a mandatory escalation, not optional, given potential SEC/regulator involvement.
steps.guidance: Legal/Compliance will likely need to coordinate with external counsel and potentially self-report to regulators.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance engaged and directing next steps.

steps.title: Preserve all relevant evidence under legal hold
steps.desc: Place all relevant systems, communications, and logs under legal hold per Legal's direction.

steps.title: Support regulatory engagement as directed by Legal
steps.desc: Provide technical support for any regulatory inquiry or self-report Legal/Compliance initiates.

steps.title: Review insider-trading control environment
steps.desc: Document the incident and evaluate whether information barriers, access controls, or trading blackout enforcement need improvement.

steps.title: Scope exactly what financial data was disclosed and to whom
steps.desc: Determine what specific material non-public information was disclosed and identify, if possible, the recipient(s).
steps.outcome: Documented scope of disclosed data and known recipients.

steps.title: Suspend the insider's access pending Legal's direction
steps.desc: Suspend account/system access for the individual only as directed by Legal, to avoid compromising any investigation.
steps.guidance: Do not act unilaterally — Legal may want evidence preserved in a specific way before any account action.
steps.outcome: Access suspended per Legal's direction; evidence preserved.

ITID-23215.def: A confirmed or suspected premature disclosure of confidential financial data that has not yet been attributed to a specific vector (routine earnings leak, deal-specific leak, system compromise, or trading-motivated leak).
ITID-23215.purpose: Catch-all for financial data disclosure incidents that do not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to attribute a specific leak vector or motive
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf (ITID-23211 through ITID-23214)
ITID-23215.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Critical by default given securities-disclosure risk.
ITID-23215.priority: P1 by default pending scoping, given potential Reg FD/securities-law exposure.
ITID-23215.escalation: Escalate to legal and investor relations immediately for preliminary risk assessment; reclassify once the specific pattern is clarified.
indicators: Report of leaked financial data of unclear origin or motive
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
ITID-23215.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-23215.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-23215.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one; reclassify to ITID-23211 through ITID-23214 as soon as the leak vector/motive is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Financial Data Disclosure
playbook.description: For confidential financial data disclosure incidents that do not clearly fit a more specific category.

steps.title: Establish the disclosure mechanism
steps.desc: Determine how the financial data was disclosed (pre-announcement leak, deal data, compromised system, insider trading motive, or unclear) to enable reclassification if warranted.
steps.outcome: Disclosure mechanism identified or confirmed as genuinely unclear.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Compliance immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Compliance given potential securities-law implications of any material non-public financial information disclosure.

steps.title: Address root cause once mechanism is confirmed
steps.desc: Remediate the root cause once clear; reclassify to a specific ITID playbook if one now clearly applies.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated or incident reclassified.

steps.title: Execute disclosure obligations per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Complete any required regulatory or market disclosure on the legally mandated timeline.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the disclosure mechanism, scope, and response actions for future reference.

steps.title: Scope what financial data was disclosed
steps.desc: Determine the specific data and its materiality/sensitivity.

steps.title: Restrict further distribution
steps.desc: Take action to stop further internal or external spread of the data pending investigation.

ITID-23221.def: An incident in which a trade secret, proprietary manufacturing process, or other protected business methodology is disclosed to competitors, media, or the public, undermining the company's competitive advantage.
ITID-23221.purpose: Captures the competitive and brand impact when a trade secret or proprietary business process is disclosed publicly.
scopeIncludes: Disclosure of a formally designated trade secret or proprietary process
Legal assessment of trade-secret protection status following disclosure
scopeExcludes: Patent-pending invention disclosures specifically (ITID-23222)
Unreleased product/roadmap leaks that are not process/trade-secret in nature (ITID-23223)
The mechanism of theft when carried out by a departing employee (ITID-23225)
ITID-23221.severity: High to Critical depending on the competitive value and remaining trade-secret protection life of the disclosed process.
ITID-23221.priority: P1 upon confirmation that a designated trade secret has reached a competitor or the public.
ITID-23221.escalation: Escalate to legal (IP counsel) and executive leadership; assess trade-secret litigation options (e.g., under the Defend Trade Secrets Act) promptly, as delay can weaken legal standing.
indicators: Competitor product or process suddenly mirroring a proprietary methodology
Trade-secret document found circulating outside authorized distribution
Former employee or contractor identified with unauthorized possession of the material
vectors: Unauthorized copying/removal of trade-secret documentation by personnel with legitimate access
Compromise of a system storing trade-secret documentation
rootCauses: Insufficient marking/classification of trade-secret material
Overly broad internal access to proprietary process documentation
controls: Trade-secret classification and access-marking program
Least-privilege access to proprietary process documentation
ITID-23221.detection: Detection is primarily driven by external market observation and legal monitoring rather than internal technical telemetry.
ITID-23221.response: Engage IP counsel promptly, assess litigation options, and review access controls around the disclosed material.
metrics: Time from disclosure to legal assessment
Number of trade-secret disclosure incidents per year
detections: DLP alerting on classified trade-secret document movement
ITID-23221.notes: Scoped to the disclosure event and its competitive/legal impact; where a departing employee is the confirmed vector, the theft mechanism is tracked under ITID-23225 to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Trade Secret/Proprietary Process Leak
playbook.description: For disclosure of a trade secret or proprietary manufacturing/business process outside the organization.

steps.title: Determine the leak's source
steps.desc: Investigate whether the disclosure originated from an insider, a compromised system, or a third party (e.g. a partner or supplier), and trace exactly what was disclosed.
steps.outcome: Source and content of the disclosure identified.

steps.title: Loop in Legal immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal given IP-protection implications and potential need for injunctive relief.

steps.title: Tighten access controls around the proprietary information
steps.desc: Review and restrict who has access to the trade secret going forward.
steps.outcome: Access scope reduced to essential personnel.

steps.title: Pursue legal remedies as directed by Legal
steps.desc: Execute on Legal's determined course of action (cease-and-desist, injunction, litigation).

steps.title: Document the incident and strengthen trade-secret protections
steps.desc: Record root cause and recommend controls (e.g. compartmentalization, NDAs, access review cadence).

steps.title: Confirm trade-secret status and assess competitive exposure
steps.desc: Work with Legal to confirm the disclosed material meets trade-secret protection criteria and assess the competitive damage.
steps.outcome: Trade-secret status confirmed; competitive exposure assessed.

steps.title: Revoke access for the identified source
steps.desc: Suspend the responsible insider's or third party's access to the proprietary information.
steps.outcome: Further access to the source material revoked.

ITID-23222.def: An incident in which details of an invention that has not yet been filed for patent protection, or is in a pending/unpublished patent application state, are disclosed publicly — potentially jeopardizing patentability due to prior-art or public-disclosure rules.
ITID-23222.purpose: Captures the impact when an unfiled or patent-pending invention disclosure leaks before formal patent protection is secured.
scopeIncludes: Disclosure of invention details prior to patent filing or during the unpublished pendency period
Legal assessment of patentability impact (grace periods, prior-art bars) following disclosure
scopeExcludes: Disclosure of a trade secret not intended for patenting (ITID-23221)
General product roadmap leaks without specific patentable-invention detail (ITID-23223)
ITID-23222.severity: Critical if disclosure occurs before filing and jeopardizes patentability in relevant jurisdictions; High if a grace period still applies.
ITID-23222.priority: P1 immediately upon disclosure, given time-sensitive filing deadlines.
ITID-23222.escalation: Escalate immediately to IP/patent counsel to assess emergency filing options and jurisdiction-specific grace-period eligibility.
indicators: Invention details appearing in a public forum, publication, or competitor filing before the company's own patent application
Inventor or engineer report of unauthorized disclosure of unfiled invention material
vectors: Premature disclosure by an inventor or engineer (e.g., conference talk, publication, social media)
Leak of invention disclosure forms or R&D notebooks prior to filing
rootCauses: Insufficient invention-disclosure and pre-filing confidentiality controls
Lack of awareness among engineers/researchers of public-disclosure patent risk
controls: Invention disclosure and pre-filing confidentiality process
Employee training on public-disclosure patent risk
ITID-23222.detection: Primarily a legal/process control area; detection relies on IP counsel monitoring of publications and competitor filings rather than technical telemetry.
ITID-23222.response: File an emergency patent application where a grace period allows, and document the disclosure circumstances for legal record.
metrics: Number of pre-filing disclosure incidents per year
Number of inventions impacted by lost patentability
sops: Invention Disclosure and Pre-Filing Confidentiality SOP
ITID-23222.notes: Distinguished from ITID-23221 by the time-sensitive patentability consequence, which drives an emergency-filing response distinct from general trade-secret handling.

playbook.name: Response: Patent-Pending/Unfiled Invention Disclosure Leak
playbook.description: For disclosure of an invention that is unfiled or has a pending patent application, which can jeopardize patentability.

steps.title: Determine the leak's source and disclosure scope
steps.desc: Investigate the source of the disclosure and determine exactly what invention details were revealed and how publicly.
steps.guidance: Public disclosure before filing can jeopardize patent rights in many jurisdictions — timing is critical.
steps.outcome: Source and scope of disclosure identified.

steps.title: Loop in Legal/IP counsel immediately as top priority
steps.desc: Notify Legal/IP counsel immediately given time-sensitive patentability implications — expedited filing may be needed.
steps.guidance: This is a time-critical escalation; delay can permanently forfeit patent rights.
steps.outcome: Legal/IP counsel engaged and acting on filing urgency.

steps.title: Identify and address the root-cause handling gap
steps.desc: Determine how the disclosure occurred and correct the underlying process or access gap.

steps.title: Complete expedited filing or alternative protection per Legal's direction
steps.desc: Execute Legal/IP counsel's determined course of action to preserve whatever protection remains available.
steps.outcome: Filing completed or alternative protection pursued.

steps.title: Document the incident and review pre-filing confidentiality practices
steps.desc: Record root cause and recommend controls for handling unfiled inventions going forward.

steps.title: Determine patent filing status and urgency
steps.desc: Confirm with Legal/IP counsel the current filing status and whether any grace period applies.
steps.outcome: Filing status and any applicable grace period confirmed.

steps.title: Restrict further disclosure of invention details
steps.desc: Revoke access to related documentation and remind relevant personnel of confidentiality obligations.

ITID-23223.def: An incident in which details of an unreleased product, feature, or forward-looking product roadmap are disclosed to media, competitors, or the public before the company's planned announcement.
ITID-23223.purpose: Captures the competitive and market impact when an unreleased product or product roadmap leaks ahead of official announcement.
scopeIncludes: Leak of unreleased product specifications, launch timing, or roadmap priorities
Marketing/communications response to a premature product leak
scopeExcludes: Disclosure of a specific patentable invention with patent-filing implications (ITID-23222)
Disclosure of the underlying trade secret/process behind a product rather than the product plan itself (ITID-23221)
ITID-23223.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High if the leak materially disrupts a planned launch or competitive positioning.
ITID-23223.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 for flagship product leaks close to launch.
ITID-23223.escalation: Escalate to product leadership and communications; assess whether the leak requires accelerating the announcement timeline.
indicators: Media or influencer coverage of unreleased product details
Roadmap document found circulating outside authorized distribution
Competitor messaging that appears to react to the leaked plan
vectors: Leak by an employee, contractor, or partner with legitimate pre-release access
Compromise of a product-management or design-collaboration tool
rootCauses: Overly broad internal/partner distribution of pre-release product materials
Insufficient access controls on product-management collaboration tools
controls: Access restriction on pre-release product materials
NDA enforcement with launch partners
ITID-23223.detection: Detection is primarily driven by external media/social monitoring; internal DLP on product-management tools provides secondary signal.
ITID-23223.response: Assess launch-timeline impact with product leadership, and consider accelerated or reactive public communications.
metrics: Time from leak to public/media coverage
Number of pre-release leak incidents per product cycle
detections: Social/media monitoring for pre-release product mentions
ITID-23223.notes: Scoped to the product-plan/roadmap disclosure itself; a leak that also reveals a proprietary process or unfiled invention is cross-referenced to ITID-23221/ITID-23222 rather than duplicated here.

playbook.name: Response: Product Roadmap/Unreleased Product Leak
playbook.description: For disclosure of unreleased product plans, roadmap details, or pre-launch product information.

steps.title: Determine the leak's source and what was disclosed
steps.desc: Investigate whether the leak originated from an insider, compromised system, or third party, and determine exactly what roadmap/product details were revealed.
steps.outcome: Source and content of the disclosure identified.

steps.title: Revoke access for the identified source
steps.desc: Suspend the responsible insider's or third party's access to roadmap materials.

steps.title: Tighten access controls around pre-release materials
steps.desc: Review and restrict who has access to unreleased roadmap/product information going forward.
steps.outcome: Access scope reduced to essential personnel.

steps.title: Execute agreed public/customer communications if warranted
steps.desc: Issue any agreed public statement or adjust launch communications per the PR/Comms plan.

steps.title: Document the incident and strengthen pre-launch confidentiality practices
steps.desc: Record root cause and recommend controls (e.g. compartmentalized roadmap access, NDA reminders).

steps.title: Assess competitive and launch-strategy impact
steps.desc: Work with Product and Marketing to assess how the leak affects competitive positioning and launch timing/messaging.

steps.title: Coordinate with PR/Comms on public response
steps.desc: Loop in PR/Comms to determine whether a public statement or launch-timeline adjustment is warranted.
steps.outcome: PR/Comms engaged and response plan agreed.

ITID-23224.def: An incident in which an attacker gains unauthorized technical access to a research and development system or repository and exfiltrates confidential R&D data, which subsequently becomes publicly known.
ITID-23224.purpose: Captures the disclosure impact when R&D or research data is leaked through direct technical compromise of a research system.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed exfiltration of R&D/research data from a compromised system, followed by external disclosure or threat-actor claim
scopeExcludes: The technical intrusion technique and R&D-system compromise investigation itself (tracked under the relevant external-attack ITID domain)
R&D data theft carried out by a departing employee (ITID-23225)
ITID-23224.severity: High to Critical depending on the competitive/scientific value of the exfiltrated research data.
ITID-23224.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation of exfiltration from an R&D system.
ITID-23224.escalation: Escalate to R&D leadership, IP counsel, and security; assess whether attacker access enables ongoing monitoring of future research activity.
indicators: Anomalous access or export activity from R&D data repositories
Threat actor claim or leak-site posting referencing internal research data
Competitor research suddenly mirroring unpublished company findings
vectors: Exploited vulnerability or stolen credentials granting access to an R&D system
Spear-phishing targeting research personnel with system access
rootCauses: Insufficient segmentation/monitoring of R&D systems from general corporate network
Excessive standing access to sensitive research repositories
controls: R&D system network segmentation
Privileged access monitoring on research repositories
ITID-23224.detection: R&D system audit logs and DLP on egress provide the primary technical detection surface; upstream intrusion detection is owned by the source-vulnerability ITID.
ITID-23224.response: Contain the compromised access path, assess IP/competitive impact with legal, and determine notification needs for research partners if applicable.
metrics: Time from exfiltration to detection
Estimated competitive value of exfiltrated research data
ITID-23224.notes: Scoped to the disclosure/brand-impact side of an R&D-system compromise; the technical intrusion itself is tracked under the relevant external-attack ITID domain.

playbook.name: Response: R&D Data/Research Leak via Compromised System
playbook.description: For confidential research and development data leaked as a result of unauthorized access to an R&D system or repository.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized access and identify the entry vector
steps.desc: Review system audit logs and SIEM data to confirm access occurred and determine how.
steps.outcome: Access confirmed with a working theory of entry vector.

steps.title: Revoke the compromised access path and rotate credentials
steps.desc: Disable the compromised account, close the exploited vulnerability, and rotate affected credentials.

steps.title: Close the root-cause vulnerability and sweep for persistence
steps.desc: Patch the exploited vulnerability and check for additional footholds.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated; no persistence found.

steps.title: Assess competitive impact and pursue remedies as needed
steps.desc: Assess impact on competitive position and pursue any legal remedies Legal recommends.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed; remedies pursued as applicable.

steps.title: Document the incident and harden R&D system access controls
steps.desc: Record root cause and recommend controls to prevent recurrence.

steps.title: Scope exactly which R&D data was accessed or exfiltrated
steps.desc: Determine which research datasets, formulas, or findings were accessed and whether data left the environment.

steps.title: Loop in Legal given IP-protection implications
steps.desc: Notify Legal given trade-secret and potential patentability implications of the exposed research data.

ITID-23225.def: An incident in which an employee, in the process of leaving the company (resignation, termination, or move to a competitor), takes proprietary intellectual property — trade secrets, research data, product plans — and it subsequently becomes known externally or is used by a competitor.
ITID-23225.purpose: Captures the disclosure and competitive impact when a departing employee steals intellectual property before or after their exit.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed IP theft by a departing employee that results in external disclosure, competitor use, or litigation
Public/competitive-impact assessment and any resulting trade-secret litigation
scopeExcludes: The departing employee's internal offboarding investigation and access-revocation handling, and general insider theft not tied to departure (ITID-13112 Insider Theft of Proprietary Source Code or Trade Secrets)
IP disclosure via a current, non-departing insider (ITID-23132 for source code; ITID-23221 for trade secrets generally)
ITID-23225.severity: High to Critical depending on the competitive value of the stolen IP and whether the employee has moved to a direct competitor.
ITID-23225.priority: P1 once departure-linked IP theft is confirmed, particularly where the employee has joined a competitor.
ITID-23225.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal for injunctive relief consideration; time is critical to prevent competitive use of the stolen IP.
indicators: Departing employee's bulk download/export activity in the weeks before resignation
Former employee's new employer (a competitor) releasing suspiciously similar IP shortly after hire
Exit interview or forensic review revealing unauthorized data transfer
vectors: Bulk download of documents/code to personal cloud storage or removable media before departure
Emailing proprietary material to a personal account ahead of resignation
rootCauses: Insufficient offboarding data-loss-prevention controls during the notice period
Lack of enhanced monitoring for employees identified as flight risks
controls: Departure-triggered DLP monitoring and access review
Exit interview and IP-return attestation process
ITID-23225.detection: DLP on egress channels in the pre-departure window provides the primary technical detection surface.
ITID-23225.response: Preserve forensic evidence of the exfiltration, pursue legal remedies (cease-and-desist, injunction) promptly, and coordinate with the new employer where appropriate.
metrics: Number of departure-linked IP theft cases per year
Time from departure to detection of exfiltration
ITID-23225.notes: Distinguished from the general insider-theft ITIDs (ITID-13112) by the departure-timing axis, which drives distinct time-critical legal remedies (injunctive relief); underlying access-monitoring mechanics are shared with, not duplicated from, the insider-threat domain.

playbook.name: Response: IP Leak via Departing Employee Theft
playbook.description: For intellectual property stolen by an employee at or near their departure from the organization.

steps.title: Review the departing employee's recent access and export activity
steps.desc: Audit the departing employee's file access, downloads, email forwarding, and USB/cloud transfer activity in the weeks preceding departure.
steps.guidance: This review should be a standard part of the offboarding process for any employee with access to sensitive IP, triggered before final access is cut.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether anomalous export activity occurred.
steps.abort: If no anomalous activity is found, close the review as part of standard offboarding.

steps.title: Suspend remaining access and secure devices immediately
steps.desc: Cut off all remaining access and retrieve/preserve company devices before or at separation.
steps.guidance: Preserve devices and accounts for forensic collection rather than wiping/reissuing them.

steps.title: Attempt to recover or confirm destruction of the taken IP
steps.desc: Where legally possible, pursue recovery or certified destruction of the exfiltrated IP.
steps.outcome: IP recovered, destroyed under legal process, or irrecoverable exposure confirmed.

steps.title: Pursue legal remedies as directed by Legal
steps.desc: Execute Legal's determined course of action (cease-and-desist, injunction against new employer use, litigation).

steps.title: Strengthen offboarding IP-protection procedures
steps.desc: Document the incident and recommend standard pre-departure export monitoring for employees with sensitive IP access.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; offboarding process improvements proposed.

steps.title: Scope exactly what IP was taken
steps.desc: Determine which documents, code, designs, or datasets were exfiltrated.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and HR immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal and HR given potential need for a cease-and-desist, especially if the employee is joining a competitor.

ITID-23226.def: A confirmed or suspected leak of intellectual property that has not yet been attributed to a specific vector (trade secret, patent-pending invention, product roadmap, R&D system compromise, or departing employee theft).
ITID-23226.purpose: Catch-all for intellectual property leak incidents that do not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to attribute a specific IP leak vector
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf (ITID-23221 through ITID-23225)
ITID-23226.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High pending scoping.
ITID-23226.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 upon confirmation of a specific leak vector or competitive impact.
ITID-23226.escalation: Escalate to IP counsel for preliminary risk assessment while investigation continues; reclassify once the specific pattern is clarified.
indicators: Report of leaked proprietary information of unclear origin
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
ITID-23226.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-23226.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-23226.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one; reclassify to ITID-23221 through ITID-23225 as soon as the leak vector is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Intellectual Property Leak
playbook.description: For IP leak incidents that do not clearly fit a more specific category.

steps.title: Establish the leak mechanism and what IP was disclosed
steps.desc: Determine how the IP became exposed (insider, compromised system, third party, departing employee, or unclear) and what specifically was disclosed.
steps.outcome: Leak mechanism and content identified or confirmed as genuinely unclear.

steps.title: Loop in Legal immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal given IP-protection implications.

steps.title: Address root cause once mechanism is confirmed
steps.desc: Remediate the root cause; reclassify to a specific ITID playbook if one now clearly applies.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated or incident reclassified.

steps.title: Pursue remedies as directed by Legal
steps.desc: Execute Legal's determined course of action.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the leak mechanism, scope, and response actions for future reference.

steps.title: Assess IP protection status and materiality
steps.desc: Work with Legal to confirm the disclosed material's protection status (trade secret, patent-pending, copyrighted) and business materiality.

steps.title: Restrict further access/distribution
steps.desc: Take action to stop further spread once the mechanism is understood.

ITID-23231.def: An incident in which confidential documents related to active or contemplated litigation — legal strategy memos, privileged correspondence, discovery materials — are disclosed to media, opposing counsel improperly, or the public.
ITID-23231.purpose: Captures the disclosure and legal-strategy impact when confidential litigation or legal case documents are leaked publicly.
scopeIncludes: Leak of litigation strategy, privileged attorney-client materials, or discovery documents
Assessment of privilege-waiver risk and litigation-strategy impact following disclosure
scopeExcludes: Leak of contracts or NDAs not tied to active litigation (ITID-23232)
Leak of regulatory investigation documents specifically (ITID-23234)
ITID-23231.severity: Critical if attorney-client privilege is compromised or litigation strategy is exposed to an adverse party; High otherwise.
ITID-23231.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation that privileged litigation material has reached an unauthorized party.
ITID-23231.escalation: Escalate immediately to general counsel and outside litigation counsel; assess privilege-waiver exposure and whether protective court orders have been violated.
indicators: Litigation document found in media reporting or on a public forum
Opposing counsel referencing internal strategy details not disclosed through formal discovery
Law firm notification of a suspected leak from their own systems
vectors: Leak by personnel with legitimate access to litigation materials
Compromise of an outside law firm's document management system
Improper handling of documents subject to a protective order
rootCauses: Insufficient access restriction on privileged litigation materials
Inadequate security requirements for outside counsel handling sensitive case documents
controls: Privileged-document access restriction and marking
Outside counsel security requirements for case document handling
ITID-23231.detection: Detection is primarily driven by legal-team monitoring of media/court filings rather than internal technical telemetry.
ITID-23231.response: Engage litigation counsel immediately to assess privilege and protective-order implications, and pursue court remedies where a protective order was violated.
metrics: Number of litigation document leak incidents per year
ITID-23231.notes: Scoped to active litigation materials specifically, distinguishing it from general contract leaks (ITID-23232) and regulatory investigation leaks (ITID-23234) given the distinct privilege and protective-order considerations.

playbook.name: Response: Litigation/Legal Case Document Leak
playbook.description: For disclosure of confidential litigation documents (e.g. privileged communications, case strategy, discovery materials).

steps.title: Determine the leak's source and what was disclosed
steps.desc: Investigate how the litigation documents were disclosed and determine exactly which documents and case details were revealed.
steps.outcome: Source and content of the disclosure identified.

steps.title: Loop in Legal/outside counsel immediately as top priority
steps.desc: Notify Legal and outside counsel immediately given the case-strategy and privilege implications.
steps.outcome: Legal engaged and directing next steps.

steps.title: Address the root-cause access or handling gap
steps.desc: Determine how the disclosure occurred and correct the underlying process or access gap.

steps.title: Pursue court remedies as directed by Legal
steps.desc: Execute Legal's determined course of action, which may include seeking a protective order or notifying the court.

steps.title: Document the incident and strengthen litigation document controls
steps.desc: Record root cause and recommend controls (e.g. privileged-document access restrictions, secure case management platform).

steps.title: Assess whether attorney-client privilege was compromised
steps.desc: Work with outside/in-house counsel to determine if privileged material was disclosed and whether privilege has been waived.

steps.title: Restrict further access to case materials
steps.desc: Tighten access to the litigation document repository pending investigation.

ITID-23232.def: An incident in which a confidential commercial contract, partnership agreement, or non-disclosure agreement is disclosed to media, competitors, or the public, revealing terms both parties intended to keep private.
ITID-23232.purpose: Captures the disclosure and counterparty-relationship impact when a confidential contract or NDA is leaked publicly.
scopeIncludes: Leak of contract terms, pricing, or partnership arrangements protected by confidentiality provisions
Counterparty notification and relationship-management response following a leak
scopeExcludes: Leaks of litigation-specific materials (ITID-23231)
Leaks of board governance documents that happen to reference a contract but are primarily governance in nature (ITID-23233)
ITID-23232.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High if the leak breaches a counterparty's confidentiality expectations and creates legal liability toward that counterparty.
ITID-23232.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 where the leaked contract involves a major partner or creates immediate legal exposure.
ITID-23232.escalation: Escalate to legal and the relevant business relationship owner; notify the counterparty promptly to preserve the relationship and assess mutual legal exposure.
indicators: Contract terms appearing in media reporting or on a public forum
Counterparty inquiry about a suspected leak on their own or the company's side
vectors: Leak by personnel with legitimate access to the contract
Compromise of a contract management/e-signature platform
rootCauses: Insufficient access restriction on contract repositories
Lack of confidentiality-breach monitoring for high-value agreements
controls: Contract management system access controls
Confidentiality clause enforcement and counterparty notification protocols
ITID-23232.detection: Detection is primarily driven by counterparty notification or media monitoring rather than internal technical telemetry.
ITID-23232.response: Notify the affected counterparty, assess mutual legal exposure, and review access controls around the contract repository.
metrics: Number of contract/NDA leak incidents per year
ITID-23232.notes: Scoped to commercial contracts/NDAs specifically, distinct from litigation materials (ITID-23231) and board governance documents (ITID-23233).

playbook.name: Response: Contract/NDA Leak
playbook.description: For disclosure of a confidential contract or NDA-protected agreement outside authorized parties.

steps.title: Determine the leak's source and identify the affected agreement(s)
steps.desc: Investigate how the contract/NDA was disclosed and identify which agreement(s) and counterparties are affected.

steps.title: Loop in Legal immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal given contractual breach and counterparty relationship implications.

steps.title: Address the root-cause access or handling gap
steps.desc: Determine how the disclosure occurred and correct the underlying process or access gap.

steps.title: Notify the counterparty and manage the relationship per Legal's guidance
steps.desc: Notify the affected counterparty if required and manage the relationship impact per Legal's direction.
steps.outcome: Counterparty notified as required; relationship managed.

steps.title: Document the incident and strengthen contract/NDA document controls
steps.desc: Record root cause and recommend controls for handling confidential agreements going forward.

steps.title: Review the confidentiality terms of the affected agreement
steps.desc: Work with Legal to review the specific confidentiality/NDA terms breached and any notification obligations to the counterparty.

steps.title: Restrict further access/distribution
steps.desc: Take action to stop further spread pending investigation.

ITID-23233.def: An incident in which board meeting minutes, board deck materials, or other corporate governance documents are disclosed to media, shareholders outside proper channels, or the public.
ITID-23233.purpose: Captures the governance and disclosure impact when confidential board meeting minutes or governance documents are leaked publicly.
scopeIncludes: Leak of board minutes, board presentation decks, or governance-committee materials
Board-level and investor-relations response to a governance document leak
scopeExcludes: Contract/NDA leaks not tied to board materials (ITID-23232)
Financial results leaks that happen to appear in board materials but are primarily earnings-disclosure events (ITID-23211)
ITID-23233.severity: High to Critical, given potential securities-disclosure implications and governance/shareholder-relations impact.
ITID-23233.priority: P1 upon confirmation that board-level confidential material has reached external parties.
ITID-23233.escalation: Escalate immediately to the corporate secretary, general counsel, and board chair; assess whether the leak reveals material non-public information triggering disclosure obligations.
indicators: Board minutes or deck content appearing in media reporting
Shareholder or activist investor referencing specific unpublished board discussion
Board member or executive assistant identified with unauthorized document distribution
vectors: Leak by a board member, executive, or support staff with legitimate access to board materials
Compromise of the board portal/document management platform
rootCauses: Insufficient access restriction on the board document portal
Lack of confidentiality reinforcement for board members and support staff
controls: Board portal access controls and document watermarking
Board confidentiality policy and periodic reinforcement
ITID-23233.detection: Detection is primarily driven by media monitoring and internal governance-team awareness rather than technical telemetry.
ITID-23233.response: Assess securities-disclosure implications with legal, and review board-portal access controls and distribution practices.
metrics: Number of governance document leak incidents per year
ITID-23233.notes: Scoped to board/governance-specific materials; overlapping financial-results content is cross-referenced to ITID-23211 rather than duplicated here.

playbook.name: Response: Board Meeting Minutes/Governance Document Leak
playbook.description: For disclosure of confidential board meeting minutes or corporate governance documents.

steps.title: Determine the leak's source and what was disclosed
steps.desc: Investigate how the board materials were disclosed and determine exactly which minutes/documents and discussion topics were revealed.
steps.outcome: Source and content of the disclosure identified.

steps.title: Loop in Legal, Compliance, and the Corporate Secretary immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Compliance/Corporate Secretary given governance and potential securities-law implications.

steps.title: Address the root-cause access or handling gap
steps.desc: Determine how the disclosure occurred and correct the underlying process or access gap.

steps.title: Execute disclosure obligations per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Complete any required regulatory or market disclosure if material non-public information was involved.

steps.title: Document the incident and strengthen board document controls
steps.desc: Record root cause and recommend controls (e.g. board portal access review, watermarking).

steps.title: Assess governance and securities-law sensitivity
steps.desc: Work with Legal/Compliance/Corporate Secretary to assess whether the disclosed content includes material non-public information.

steps.title: Restrict further access to board materials
steps.desc: Tighten access to the board portal/document repository pending investigation.

ITID-23234.def: An incident in which confidential documents related to an active or contemplated regulatory investigation (subpoenas, information requests, internal investigative findings, regulator correspondence) are disclosed to media or the public.
ITID-23234.purpose: Captures the disclosure impact when documents from a confidential regulatory investigation are leaked publicly.
scopeIncludes: Leak of regulatory investigation correspondence, subpoena responses, or internal investigative findings
Assessment of regulatory-relationship and legal-strategy impact following disclosure
scopeExcludes: Leaks of litigation-specific materials not tied to a regulatory investigation (ITID-23231)
Whistleblower disclosures made directly to a regulator, which are the regulator's own receipt of a report rather than a leak of investigation documents (ITID-23311 through ITID-23315)
ITID-23234.severity: Critical, given potential to damage the regulatory relationship and complicate the investigation's resolution.
ITID-23234.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation that regulatory investigation material has reached an unauthorized party.
ITID-23234.escalation: Escalate immediately to general counsel and the regulatory-relationship lead; assess whether the leak violates any confidentiality order tied to the investigation.
indicators: Regulatory investigation details appearing in media reporting
Regulator inquiry about a suspected leak on the company's side
Internal investigative report found circulating outside authorized distribution
vectors: Leak by personnel with legitimate access to the investigation file
Compromise of outside counsel's or a compliance consultant's systems handling investigation materials
rootCauses: Insufficient access restriction on regulatory investigation materials
Inadequate security requirements for external counsel/consultants supporting the investigation
controls: Regulatory investigation document access restriction
External counsel/consultant security requirements
ITID-23234.detection: Detection is primarily driven by legal-team monitoring of media and regulator communications rather than technical telemetry.
ITID-23234.response: Engage legal immediately to assess regulatory-relationship impact, and notify the regulator proactively if appropriate to preserve credibility.
metrics: Number of regulatory investigation leak incidents per year
ITID-23234.notes: Scoped to leaks of investigation documents themselves; a whistleblower's direct report to a regulator is a distinct disclosure channel tracked under the Regulatory Disclosures Type (ITID-23311 through ITID-23315).

playbook.name: Response: Regulatory Investigation Document Leak
playbook.description: For disclosure of confidential documents related to an active or pending regulatory investigation of the organization.

steps.title: Determine the leak's source and what was disclosed
steps.desc: Investigate how the investigation-related documents were disclosed and determine exactly which documents and details were revealed.
steps.outcome: Source and content of the disclosure identified.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Compliance immediately as top priority
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Compliance immediately given the active regulatory matter — this may require notifying the regulator itself.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance engaged and directing next steps.

steps.title: Address the root-cause access or handling gap
steps.desc: Determine how the disclosure occurred and correct the underlying process or access gap.

steps.title: Notify the regulator if required and manage the matter per Legal's guidance
steps.desc: Complete any required notification to the regulator and manage ongoing engagement per Legal's direction.

steps.title: Document the incident and strengthen investigation document controls
steps.desc: Record root cause and recommend controls for handling sensitive regulatory matter documents going forward.

steps.title: Assess impact on the regulatory matter
steps.desc: Work with Legal/Compliance to assess whether the leak compromises the organization's position in the regulatory matter or triggers reporting obligations to the regulator.
steps.outcome: Impact on the regulatory matter assessed.

steps.title: Restrict further access to investigation materials
steps.desc: Tighten access to the investigation document repository pending review.

ITID-23235.def: A confirmed or suspected leak of confidential legal documents that has not yet been attributed to a specific vector (litigation materials, contracts/NDAs, board governance documents, or regulatory investigation documents).
ITID-23235.purpose: Catch-all for legal document leak incidents that do not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to attribute a specific legal document leak vector
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf (ITID-23231 through ITID-23234)
ITID-23235.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High pending scoping.
ITID-23235.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 upon confirmation of a specific leak vector or legal sensitivity.
