ITID-23235.escalation: Escalate to legal for preliminary risk assessment while investigation continues; reclassify once the specific pattern is clarified.
indicators: Report of leaked legal document of unclear origin or category
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
ITID-23235.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-23235.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-23235.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one; reclassify to ITID-23231 through ITID-23234 as soon as the leak vector is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Legal Document Leak
playbook.description: For legal document leak incidents that do not clearly fit a more specific category.

steps.title: Establish the leak mechanism and what was disclosed
steps.desc: Determine how the legal document became exposed and what specifically was disclosed.
steps.outcome: Leak mechanism and content identified or confirmed as genuinely unclear.

steps.title: Loop in Legal immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal given the legal-document nature of the disclosure.

steps.title: Address root cause once mechanism is confirmed
steps.desc: Remediate the root cause; reclassify to a specific ITID playbook if one now clearly applies.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated or incident reclassified.

steps.title: Pursue remedies as directed by Legal
steps.desc: Execute Legal's determined course of action.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the leak mechanism, scope, and response actions for future reference.

steps.title: Assess privilege and sensitivity
steps.desc: Work with Legal to determine if attorney-client privilege or other legal protection was compromised.

steps.title: Restrict further access/distribution
steps.desc: Take action to stop further spread pending investigation.

ITID-23311.def: An incident in which a current or former employee submits a whistleblower report to the SEC or another financial regulator alleging securities-law violations, accounting fraud, or financial misconduct by the company.
ITID-23311.purpose: Captures the brand and regulatory-relationship impact when an employee files a whistleblower disclosure with the SEC or another financial regulator.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed or suspected SEC/financial-regulator whistleblower submission naming the company
Company response to a resulting regulatory inquiry or investigation, and any related market/investor communications
scopeExcludes: Safety, environmental, or data-privacy regulator whistleblower disclosures (ITID-23312, ITID-23313, ITID-23314)
Internal-only ethics hotline reports that are not escalated to an external regulator (ITID-23324, unless later leaked externally)
ITID-23311.severity: Critical, given potential for SEC investigation, market impact, and executive liability.
ITID-23311.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation of a regulator inquiry referencing a whistleblower submission.
ITID-23311.escalation: Escalate immediately to general counsel, the audit committee, and outside securities counsel; preserve all potentially relevant records under litigation hold.
indicators: SEC or regulator inquiry letter referencing a whistleblower tip
Employee's own confirmation of having filed an SEC whistleblower complaint
Media reporting of a securities-related whistleblower case
rootCauses: Underlying accounting or securities-compliance failure motivating the disclosure
Ineffective internal reporting channels causing the employee to bypass them
controls: Whistleblower non-retaliation policy and program
Internal audit and disclosure-controls testing
ITID-23311.detection: Not a technical detection domain; awareness typically comes via direct regulator contact or employee disclosure rather than security telemetry.
ITID-23311.response: Cooperate fully with the regulatory inquiry, ensure strict non-retaliation against the whistleblower, and assess underlying control failures.
metrics: Number of financial-regulator whistleblower cases per year
Time to regulator response/cooperation milestones
ITID-23311.notes: This is a non-technical, human-driven disclosure; no adversary technique applies. Scoped narrowly to SEC/financial-regulator channel to keep the differentiating axis (which regulator) clean across this Type.

playbook.name: Response: SEC/Financial Regulator Whistleblower Disclosure
playbook.description: For an unauthorized disclosure of internal information to the SEC or a comparable financial regulator by an employee raising a concern. Handle as protected whistleblower activity, not as a security incident to be punished.

steps.title: Understand what was disclosed and to whom
steps.desc: Determine what information was shared with the regulator and confirm the disclosure channel, without attempting to unmask an anonymous discloser.
steps.guidance: Do not treat this as an insider-threat investigation aimed at identifying or confronting the discloser — the goal is understanding scope, not attribution.
steps.outcome: Nature and scope of the disclosed information understood.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Compliance immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Compliance given whistleblower-protection law implications (e.g. Dodd-Frank, Sarbanes-Oxley anti-retaliation provisions) and any regulator engagement requirements.
steps.guidance: Legal must ensure no retaliatory action is taken against any identified or suspected discloser.
steps.outcome: Legal/Compliance engaged and anti-retaliation safeguards confirmed.

steps.title: Remediate the underlying issue if the concern is valid
steps.desc: If the concern is substantiated, address the underlying compliance gap or misconduct that prompted the disclosure.
steps.abort: If the concern is not substantiated, document the basis for that conclusion.

steps.title: Cooperate with the regulator per Legal's direction
steps.desc: Respond to any regulator inquiry cooperatively and transparently as directed by Legal.
steps.outcome: Regulatory engagement handled per Legal's direction.

steps.title: Review internal reporting channels and strengthen protections
steps.desc: Document the incident and assess whether internal reporting channels need improvement so future concerns can be raised internally with confidence.
steps.guidance: Frame findings around improving trust in internal channels, not around preventing future external disclosures.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; internal channel improvements proposed.

steps.title: Assess the validity of the underlying concern
steps.desc: Work with Legal/Compliance to independently assess whether the concern raised has merit, regardless of how it was disclosed.
steps.guidance: The validity assessment is the primary substantive task here — the disclosure channel is secondary to whether the concern is real.

steps.title: Ensure no retaliatory action occurs against the discloser
steps.desc: Explicitly confirm with HR/Legal that no adverse employment action is taken against any individual connected to the disclosure while the matter is reviewed.
steps.guidance: This step exists to actively prevent a punitive response, not merely to note the risk.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no retaliatory action has occurred or is planned.

ITID-23312.def: An incident in which a current or former employee submits a whistleblower report to OSHA or another workplace-safety regulator alleging unsafe working conditions or safety-law violations by the company.
ITID-23312.purpose: Captures the brand and regulatory-relationship impact when an employee files a whistleblower disclosure with OSHA or another workplace-safety regulator.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed or suspected OSHA/safety-regulator whistleblower submission naming the company
Company response to a resulting safety inquiry, inspection, or investigation
scopeExcludes: Financial, environmental, or data-privacy regulator whistleblower disclosures (ITID-23311, ITID-23313, ITID-23314)
ITID-23312.severity: High to Critical, escalating if the underlying safety concern involves imminent risk to life or health.
ITID-23312.priority: P1 upon confirmation of a regulator inspection or inquiry tied to the whistleblower report.
ITID-23312.escalation: Escalate to EHS (environmental health and safety) leadership, legal, and operations; ensure strict non-retaliation and remediate any confirmed safety hazard immediately.
indicators: OSHA inspection or inquiry referencing a whistleblower complaint
Employee's own confirmation of having filed a safety-related whistleblower complaint
Media reporting of a workplace-safety whistleblower case
rootCauses: Underlying workplace-safety control failure motivating the disclosure
Ineffective internal safety-reporting channels causing the employee to bypass them
controls: Whistleblower non-retaliation policy and program
Workplace safety incident reporting and remediation program
ITID-23312.detection: Not a technical detection domain; awareness typically comes via direct regulator contact or employee disclosure.
ITID-23312.response: Cooperate fully with the safety inspection, remediate any confirmed hazard, and ensure strict non-retaliation against the whistleblower.
metrics: Number of safety-regulator whistleblower cases per year
Time to hazard remediation
ITID-23312.notes: Non-technical, human-driven disclosure; no adversary technique applies.

playbook.name: Response: Safety/OSHA Regulatory Whistleblower Disclosure
playbook.description: For an unauthorized disclosure of internal safety information to OSHA or a comparable safety regulator by an employee raising a concern. Handle as protected whistleblower activity, not as a security incident to be punished.

steps.title: Understand what was disclosed and to whom
steps.desc: Determine what safety-related information was shared with the regulator and confirm the disclosure channel, without attempting to unmask an anonymous discloser.
steps.guidance: Do not treat this as an insider-threat investigation aimed at identifying or confronting the discloser.
steps.outcome: Nature and scope of the disclosed information understood.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and EHS immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/EHS given whistleblower-protection law implications (e.g. OSH Act Section 11(c) anti-retaliation) and any regulator engagement requirements.
steps.outcome: Legal/EHS engaged and anti-retaliation safeguards confirmed.

steps.title: Remediate the underlying safety issue if the concern is valid
steps.desc: If the concern is substantiated, address the underlying safety hazard or process gap.

steps.title: Cooperate with the regulator per Legal's direction
steps.desc: Respond to any OSHA inquiry or inspection cooperatively as directed by Legal.
steps.outcome: Regulatory engagement handled per Legal's direction.

steps.title: Review internal safety reporting channels and strengthen protections
steps.desc: Document the incident and assess whether internal safety reporting channels need improvement.
steps.guidance: Frame findings around improving trust in internal channels, not around preventing future external disclosures.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; internal channel improvements proposed.

steps.title: Assess the validity of the underlying safety concern
steps.desc: Work with EHS/Legal to independently assess whether the safety concern raised has merit.

steps.title: Ensure no retaliatory action occurs against the discloser
steps.desc: Explicitly confirm with HR/Legal that no adverse employment action is taken against any individual connected to the disclosure.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no retaliatory action has occurred or is planned.

ITID-23411.def: An incident in which company privileged or administrator account credentials are discovered listed for sale on a dark web marketplace or forum, triggering organizational response to the discovery itself, distinct from how the credentials were originally obtained.
ITID-23411.purpose: Captures the brand and incident-response impact when the organization discovers its own privileged/administrator credentials listed for sale on a dark web marketplace.
scopeIncludes: Organizational discovery, triage, and response to a confirmed dark-web listing of company privileged credentials
Decision-making on forced credential rotation, scope assessment, and any customer/board notification
scopeExcludes: The technical mechanics of how the credential was originally exposed, phished, or leaked (tracked under the credential-leakage domain, e.g., ITID-12521 through ITID-12529)
Listings of non-privileged/standard user credentials without administrator scope (ITID-23414)
ITID-23411.severity: Critical, given the elevated access privileged/admin credentials would grant if used.
ITID-23411.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation of a verified privileged-credential listing referencing the company.
ITID-23411.escalation: Escalate immediately to security operations and IT leadership for emergency credential rotation; escalate to legal/communications if public disclosure becomes likely.

Initial Access Broker listing specifically advertising administrator-level access

rootCauses: Underlying credential-exposure event (root cause owned by the credential-leakage domain)

ITID-23411.detection: Dark-web monitoring and threat intelligence feeds are the primary detection surface for this leaf; the original exposure detection lives with the credential-leakage domain.
ITID-23411.response: Immediately rotate and verify revocation of the listed credential, assess for signs of prior unauthorized use, and determine whether the listing itself warrants disclosure.

ITID-23411.notes: Deliberately scoped to the organization's response to discovering the listing and its brand/security-posture consequences; the underlying exposure/harvesting mechanism is owned by the ITID-12500 credential-leakage domain and is cross-referenced here rather than re-described.

playbook.description: For discovery of a dark web listing offering privileged or administrator credentials belonging to the organization for sale.

steps.title: Discover and verify the listing's authenticity and scope
steps.desc: Locate the listing via threat-intel monitoring and assess whether the offered credentials are genuine and current, checking any provided samples against known account identifiers.
steps.guidance: Use isolated/out-of-band research tools rather than corporate assets to investigate dark web listings.
steps.abort: If the listing cannot be verified as genuine, treat as unverified and continue monitoring rather than force-rotating broadly.
steps.tool: Threat intelligence platform / dark web monitoring

steps.title: Force credential rotation for all confirmed and suspected exposed privileged accounts
steps.desc: Immediately rotate credentials and, where applicable, revoke active sessions for the implicated privileged accounts.
steps.guidance: Given the elevated access level, err toward rotating broadly among plausible candidates rather than narrowly.
steps.outcome: Implicated privileged credentials rotated; sessions revoked.

steps.title: Determine and close the credential-theft source
steps.desc: Investigate how the credentials were originally obtained (phishing, infostealer malware, prior breach) and remediate that root cause.
steps.outcome: Credential-theft source identified and closed where possible.

steps.title: Enforce MFA and review privileged access policy
steps.desc: Confirm MFA is enforced on all privileged accounts and review whether privileged access scope can be reduced.

steps.title: Document the incident and strengthen credential-theft detection
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend improved dark web monitoring coverage and credential-theft detection controls.

steps.title: Identify which specific accounts are implicated
steps.desc: Determine, as precisely as possible, which privileged/admin accounts the listing refers to.
steps.outcome: Implicated accounts identified or narrowed to a credible set.

steps.title: Check for signs the credentials have already been used
steps.desc: Review authentication and privileged-action logs for anomalous use of the implicated accounts.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no unauthorized use, or unauthorized use identified and escalated as an active intrusion.

ITID-23412.def: An incident in which credentials granting access to a company cloud infrastructure tenant (AWS, Azure, GCP) or a critical SaaS platform are discovered listed for sale on a dark web marketplace, triggering organizational response to the discovery itself.
ITID-23412.purpose: Captures the brand and incident-response impact when the organization discovers its own cloud/SaaS tenant credentials listed for sale on a dark web marketplace.
scopeIncludes: Organizational discovery, triage, and response to a confirmed dark-web listing of company cloud/SaaS tenant access
Decision-making on forced credential/session rotation and tenant-wide security review
scopeExcludes: The technical mechanics of how the credential was originally exposed or phished (ITID-12500 credential-leakage domain)
Listings of on-premises administrator credentials rather than cloud/SaaS tenant access (ITID-23411)
ITID-23412.severity: Critical, given the potential for full cloud-tenant compromise if the access is used.
ITID-23412.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation of a verified cloud/SaaS tenant access listing referencing the company.
ITID-23412.escalation: Escalate immediately to cloud security/IT leadership for emergency credential and session rotation across the affected tenant.
indicators: Dark-web monitoring alert matching company cloud tenant identifiers
Initial Access Broker listing specifically advertising cloud/SaaS tenant access
Threat intelligence vendor notification of verified tenant-access sale
rootCauses: Underlying credential-exposure event (root cause owned by the credential-leakage domain)
Insufficient dark-web monitoring coverage for cloud-specific identifiers
controls: Dark-web/credential marketplace monitoring
Cloud tenant conditional access and session revocation capability
Multi-factor authentication on all cloud/SaaS administrator accounts
ITID-23412.detection: Dark-web monitoring and threat intelligence feeds are the primary detection surface; cloud provider anomaly detection provides secondary signal if the access is used.
ITID-23412.response: Immediately rotate credentials and revoke active sessions across the affected tenant, and audit for signs of prior unauthorized use.
metrics: Time from listing discovery to credential/session rotation
Number of cloud/SaaS tenant listings discovered per year
sops: Emergency Cloud Tenant Access Rotation SOP
ITID-23412.notes: Scoped to the organization's response to a cloud/SaaS-specific listing and its brand impact; the underlying exposure mechanism remains owned by the ITID-12500 credential-leakage domain.

steps.desc: Locate the listing via threat-intel monitoring and assess whether the offered credentials are genuine and current.
steps.abort: If unverified, continue monitoring rather than force-rotating broadly.
steps.tool: Threat intelligence platform / dark web monitoring

steps.title: Force credential rotation and session revocation for implicated accounts
steps.desc: Immediately rotate credentials and revoke active sessions/tokens for the implicated cloud/SaaS accounts.

steps.title: Determine and close the credential-theft source
steps.desc: Investigate how the credentials were originally obtained and remediate that root cause.
steps.outcome: Credential-theft source identified and closed where possible.

steps.title: Enforce MFA and conditional access policies
steps.desc: Confirm MFA and conditional access policies are enforced across the affected tenant(s).

steps.title: Document the incident and strengthen credential-theft detection
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend improved dark web monitoring and credential-theft detection controls.

steps.title: Identify which cloud/SaaS tenants and accounts are implicated
steps.desc: Determine which specific tenant(s) and user accounts the listing refers to.
steps.outcome: Implicated tenants/accounts identified or narrowed to a credible set.

steps.title: Check for signs the credentials have already been used
steps.desc: Review the cloud/SaaS platform's sign-in and activity logs for anomalous access from the implicated accounts.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no unauthorized use, or unauthorized use identified and escalated as an active intrusion.

ITID-23413.def: An incident in which credentials granting access to a company financial or banking account (treasury, corporate card administration, banking portal) are discovered listed for sale on a dark web marketplace, triggering organizational response to prevent financial fraud.
ITID-23413.purpose: Captures the brand and financial-fraud response impact when the organization discovers its financial/banking account credentials listed for sale on a dark web marketplace.
scopeIncludes: Organizational discovery, triage, and response to a confirmed dark-web listing of company financial/banking account access
Coordination with the bank/financial institution to freeze or monitor the affected account
scopeExcludes: The technical mechanics of how the credential was originally exposed or phished (ITID-12500 credential-leakage domain)
Listings of non-financial administrator or cloud/SaaS credentials (ITID-23411, ITID-23412)
ITID-23413.severity: Critical, given direct and immediate financial-fraud risk.
ITID-23413.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation of a verified financial-account credential listing referencing the company.
ITID-23413.escalation: Escalate immediately to finance/treasury leadership and the banking relationship team to freeze or heighten monitoring on the affected account.
indicators: Dark-web monitoring alert matching company banking/treasury account identifiers
Bank fraud-monitoring alert coinciding with a known dark-web listing
rootCauses: Underlying credential-exposure event (root cause owned by the credential-leakage domain)
Insufficient dark-web monitoring coverage for financial-system-specific identifiers
controls: Dark-web/credential marketplace monitoring
Banking portal multi-factor authentication and transaction limits
Bank-side fraud monitoring and account freeze capability
ITID-23413.detection: Dark-web monitoring and bank fraud-monitoring alerts are the primary detection surface for this leaf.
ITID-23413.response: Immediately rotate credentials, coordinate with the bank to freeze or restrict the account, and audit for signs of fraudulent transactions.
metrics: Time from listing discovery to account restriction
Financial loss prevented or incurred
sops: Emergency Financial Account Credential Rotation SOP
ITID-23413.notes: Scoped to the organization's response to a financial-account-specific listing and its fraud/brand impact; the underlying exposure mechanism remains owned by the ITID-12500 credential-leakage domain.

steps.desc: Record findings and recommend controls (e.g. multi-approval for transfers, dedicated banking MFA hardware) to reduce future risk.

steps.desc: Determine which bank or financial platform accounts the listing refers to.

steps.title: Rotate credentials and review recent transaction history

ITID-23414.def: A confirmed or suspected dark-web listing of company credentials for sale that has not yet been attributed to a specific access category (privileged/admin, cloud/SaaS tenant, or financial/banking).
ITID-23414.purpose: Catch-all for credentials-for-sale incidents that do not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to attribute the specific access category of the listed credential
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf (ITID-23411 through ITID-23413)
ITID-23414.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High pending scoping.
ITID-23414.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 upon confirmation of the specific access category and its privilege level.
ITID-23414.escalation: Escalate to security operations for preliminary rotation/triage while investigation continues; reclassify once the specific access category is clarified.
indicators: Dark-web listing referencing company credentials of unclear scope
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
ITID-23414.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-23414.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed; rotate the credential immediately regardless of classification.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-23414.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one; reclassify to ITID-23411 through ITID-23413 as soon as the access category is confirmed.

ITID-23421.def: An incident in which a database of stolen company customer records is discovered listed for sale on a dark web marketplace or breach forum, triggering organizational response to the listing's discovery and any resulting disclosure obligations.
ITID-23421.purpose: Captures the brand and disclosure impact when a stolen customer database is discovered listed for sale on a dark web marketplace.
scopeIncludes: Organizational discovery, verification, and response to a confirmed dark-web listing of stolen customer data
Sample-data verification to confirm authenticity and scope of the listed dataset
scopeExcludes: The original breach/theft mechanism that produced the stolen dataset (ITID-23111 through ITID-23115, the Customer Data Exposure Type)
Listings of source code, internal documents, or employee data rather than customer records (ITID-23422, ITID-23423, ITID-23424)
ITID-23421.severity: Critical once the listing's authenticity and scope are confirmed.
ITID-23421.priority: P1 immediately upon discovery of a credible listing referencing company customer data.
ITID-23421.escalation: Escalate to legal, privacy, and communications for coordinated verification and notification planning.
indicators: Breach forum or marketplace listing naming the company with sample customer records attached
Dark-web monitoring alert matching company customer data patterns
rootCauses: The underlying breach that produced the dataset (root cause owned by the relevant Customer Data Exposure leaf)
controls: Dark-web/breach-forum monitoring
Pre-negotiated legal/communications rapid-response process for confirmed listings
ITID-23421.detection: Dark-web and breach-forum monitoring services are the primary detection surface for this leaf.
ITID-23421.response: Verify sample data authenticity, confirm scope with the underlying breach investigation, and coordinate customer/regulatory notification.
metrics: Time from listing discovery to authenticity verification
Time to customer/regulatory notification
ITID-23421.notes: Scoped to the discovery and disclosure response to the dark-web listing itself; the originating theft/breach is tracked under the appropriate Customer Data Exposure leaf (ITID-23111 through ITID-23115) and is cross-referenced rather than re-described.

playbook.name: Response: Stolen Customer Database Listing for Sale
playbook.description: For discovery of a dark web listing offering the organization's stolen customer database for sale.

steps.title: Discover and verify the listing's authenticity and scope
steps.desc: Locate the listing and assess the provided sample data against known customer records to verify authenticity and estimate scope.
steps.outcome: Listing authenticity and approximate scope assessed.
steps.abort: If the sample cannot be verified as genuine organizational data, treat as unverified and continue monitoring.
steps.tool: Threat intelligence platform / dark web monitoring

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Privacy immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Privacy given likely breach-notification obligations for exposed customer data.

steps.title: Force rotation of any credentials present in the exposed dataset
steps.desc: Rotate any customer or system credentials contained in the exposed dataset.

steps.title: Execute regulatory and customer notification per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications on the legally mandated timeline once scope is confirmed.

steps.title: Document the incident and strengthen detection/prevention controls
steps.desc: Record root cause and recommend controls to prevent recurrence.

steps.title: Correlate with any known intrusion to determine the exfiltration source
steps.desc: Cross-reference the listing against any known or suspected prior intrusion to identify how the data was obtained.
steps.outcome: Exfiltration source identified or investigation opened if none is currently known.

steps.title: Close the exfiltration source if still active
steps.desc: If the source system/access path is still exploitable, close it immediately.
steps.outcome: Exfiltration path closed if still active.

ITID-23422.purpose: Captures the brand and competitive impact when stolen source code or intellectual property is discovered listed for sale on a dark web marketplace.
scopeIncludes: Organizational discovery, verification, and response to a confirmed dark-web listing of stolen source code/IP
Sample-data verification to confirm authenticity and scope of the listed material
scopeExcludes: The original theft/leak mechanism that produced the dataset (ITID-23131 through ITID-23135, the Source Code Leaks Type; ITID-23221 through ITID-23226, the IP Leaks Type)
Listings of customer, employee, or general document data rather than code/IP (ITID-23421, ITID-23423, ITID-23424)
ITID-23422.severity: Critical for core product code or high-value IP; High for peripheral/tooling code.
ITID-23422.priority: P1 immediately upon discovery of a credible listing referencing company source code or IP.
ITID-23422.escalation: Escalate to engineering leadership, IP counsel, and security for verification and competitive-risk assessment.
indicators: Marketplace or forum listing naming the company with sample code/IP attached
Dark-web monitoring alert matching company code repository identifiers
rootCauses: The underlying theft/leak that produced the material (root cause owned by the relevant Source Code Leaks or IP Leaks leaf)
controls: Dark-web/specialized forum monitoring
Code/IP watermarking to aid authenticity verification
ITID-23422.detection: Dark-web and forum monitoring services are the primary detection surface for this leaf.
ITID-23422.response: Verify sample authenticity, assess competitive/security exposure, and coordinate any needed legal or public response.
metrics: Time from listing discovery to authenticity verification
Estimated competitive value of listed material
ITID-23422.notes: Scoped to the discovery and response to the dark-web listing itself; the originating theft/leak is tracked under the appropriate Source Code Leaks or IP Leaks leaf and is cross-referenced rather than re-described.

ITID-23431.def: An incident in which a ransomware group publishes a public countdown, deadline, or extortion announcement on its leak site or communication channel naming the company, intended to pressure payment through public visibility ahead of confirmed data publication.
ITID-23431.purpose: Captures the brand and crisis-response impact when a ransomware group publicly announces an extortion deadline/countdown naming the company.
scopeIncludes: Public leak-site countdown/announcement naming the company prior to any confirmed data posting
Crisis-communications response to media inquiries generated by the public announcement
scopeExcludes: Confirmed posting/publication of actual stolen data (ITID-23611 through ITID-23615, the Ransomware Data Exposure Type; ITID-23115 for customer-data-specific postings)
The underlying ransomware intrusion and encryption mechanics (ITID-31131 through ITID-31144)
ITID-23431.severity: High, escalating to Critical as the countdown deadline approaches without resolution.
ITID-23431.priority: P1 immediately upon discovery of a public announcement naming the company.
ITID-23431.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership, legal, law enforcement liaison, and communications; align messaging with the broader ransomware incident response team.
indicators: Company name appearing on a ransomware group's public leak-site countdown page
Media inquiry referencing a public ransomware group announcement about the company
rootCauses: Successful ransomware intrusion (root cause owned by the ransomware ITID family)
Lack of resolution/negotiation progress before the group's self-imposed deadline
controls: Dark-web/leak-site monitoring
Pre-negotiated crisis communications plan for ransomware scenarios
ITID-23431.detection: Leak-site monitoring services provide the primary detection signal for this leaf.
ITID-23431.response: Prepare a holding public statement, monitor the countdown for evidence of actual publication, and support the broader ransomware incident response.
metrics: Time from announcement to resolution or data publication
Media inquiry volume during the countdown period
ITID-23431.notes: Scoped to the pre-publication public announcement/countdown stage; actual data publication is tracked under the Ransomware Data Exposure Type (ITID-23611 through ITID-23615) to avoid duplicating the same incident twice.

playbook.name: Response: Ransomware Group Extortion/Countdown Announcement
playbook.description: For a public announcement by a ransomware group posting a countdown/extortion threat against the organization on a leak site.

steps.title: Urgent triage: determine if this correlates with a known active intrusion
steps.desc: Immediately check whether SOC/IR has any open ransomware, encryption, or exfiltration incident that this announcement could correspond to.
steps.guidance: This determination should happen within the first hour — it drives whether this is a live crisis or an opportunistic/false claim.
steps.outcome: Correlation with a known active intrusion confirmed or ruled out.
steps.abort: If no correlating intrusion is found after reasonable investigation, treat as unverified pending further evidence, but continue monitoring the countdown.

steps.title: Loop in Legal, Executive leadership, and Law Enforcement immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Executives/Law Enforcement given the extortion nature and time pressure of the countdown.
steps.guidance: Standard guidance is against paying extortion demands; negotiation decisions are Legal/Executive-level.
steps.outcome: Relevant leadership and law enforcement engaged.

steps.title: Eradicate the intrusion and close the root cause
steps.desc: Complete full eradication of attacker presence and remediate the initial access vector.
steps.outcome: Attacker presence eradicated; root cause closed.

steps.title: Execute regulatory, customer, and public communications per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications and coordinate any public statement on the legally mandated and PR-appropriate timeline.
steps.outcome: Notifications and communications executed as required.

steps.title: Document the incident and update ransomware playbook readiness
steps.desc: Record the timeline and response effectiveness; recommend improvements to detection and leak-site monitoring.

steps.title: Verify authenticity and scope of any claimed data
steps.desc: Assess any sample data posted by the group against known organizational data to verify authenticity and estimate scope.

steps.title: Contain the underlying intrusion if confirmed
steps.desc: If correlated with an active intrusion, execute standard ransomware containment (isolate affected systems, disable compromised accounts).

ITID-23432.def: An incident in which a hacktivist group publicly posts a claim of responsibility for an attack (defacement, DDoS, data theft, or other action) against the company, typically framed around an ideological, political, or social cause.
ITID-23432.purpose: Captures the brand and crisis-response impact when a hacktivist group publicly claims responsibility for an attack against the company.
scopeIncludes: Public hacktivist claim-of-responsibility posting naming the company
Crisis-communications response addressing the claim, including verifying its accuracy
scopeExcludes: The underlying technical attack the claim refers to (tracked under its own relevant ITID, e.g., DDoS, defacement, or data-breach domains)
Unverified or exaggerated claims not attributable to a credible hacktivist group (ITID-23433)
ITID-23432.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High if the claim is verified accurate or gains significant media traction.
ITID-23432.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 if the claim proves accurate or drives significant public attention.
ITID-23432.escalation: Escalate to security operations to verify the claim's accuracy against internal telemetry, and to communications for public response preparation.
indicators: Hacktivist group social media or forum post claiming responsibility for an attack on the company
Media coverage referencing the hacktivist claim
rootCauses: The underlying attack the claim refers to (root cause owned by the corresponding technical ITID)
Ideological/political grievance motivating the hacktivist group's targeting of the company
controls: Social/dark-web monitoring for hacktivist claims
Cross-functional verification process linking claims to internal incident telemetry
ITID-23432.detection: Social media and dark-web monitoring are the primary detection surface; internal telemetry from the referenced attack (if any) provides verification.
ITID-23432.response: Verify the claim's accuracy promptly, and issue a factual public statement to prevent unverified claims from shaping the narrative unchallenged.
metrics: Time from claim posting to internal verification
Media pickup volume of the claim
detections: Social/dark-web monitoring alerting for brand mentions
ITID-23432.notes: Scoped to the public claim itself and the company's verification/response; the underlying technical attack, if verified, is tracked under its own dedicated ITID rather than duplicated here.

playbook.name: Response: Hacktivist Claim-of-Responsibility Announcement
playbook.description: For a public claim-of-responsibility announcement by a hacktivist group alleging a breach or attack against the organization.

steps.title: Urgent triage: determine if this correlates with a known active intrusion
steps.desc: Immediately check whether SOC/IR has any open incident that this claim could correspond to.
steps.guidance: Hacktivist claims are frequently exaggerated or entirely false for attention; verify before reacting publicly.
steps.outcome: Correlation with a known active intrusion confirmed or ruled out.
steps.abort: If no correlating intrusion is found, treat as unverified/likely opportunistic pending further evidence.

steps.title: Loop in PR/Comms and Legal
steps.desc: Notify PR/Comms and Legal to prepare a measured public response and assess any confirmed exposure's implications.

steps.title: Close the confirmed vulnerability if applicable
steps.desc: Remediate any confirmed vulnerability exploited, regardless of whether the broader claim is verified.

steps.title: Issue a fact-based public statement if warranted
steps.desc: Coordinate with PR/Comms to issue a fact-based correction or acknowledgment as appropriate to the verified facts.

steps.title: Document the incident and the claim's veracity outcome
steps.desc: Record findings on whether the claim was substantiated and any lessons for detection or monitoring.

steps.title: Verify authenticity and scope of any claimed data or access
steps.desc: Assess any sample data or proof posted by the group against known organizational data to verify authenticity.

steps.title: Contain the underlying intrusion if confirmed
steps.desc: If correlated with a confirmed intrusion, execute standard containment for the access vector used.

ITID-23433.def: An incident in which a threat actor or unknown party publicly claims a data breach or compromise of the company that cannot be verified against internal evidence, or is confirmed to be false, exaggerated, or recycled from an unrelated prior incident.
ITID-23433.purpose: Captures the brand and crisis-response impact when an unverified or exaggerated breach claim about the company circulates publicly.
scopeIncludes: Public claims of compromise that investigation shows to be false, unverifiable, or substantially exaggerated relative to internal evidence
Public correction/clarification response to such claims
scopeExcludes: Claims later verified as accurate, which should be reclassified to the appropriate specific leaf (e.g., ITID-23431, ITID-23432, or the relevant data-exposure leaf)
ITID-23433.severity: Medium, escalating to High if the false claim gains significant media traction or causes market/customer impact despite being inaccurate.
ITID-23433.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 if the claim drives material stock or customer-confidence impact before it can be corrected.
ITID-23433.escalation: Escalate to security operations for rapid internal verification, and to communications and legal for a factual public correction.
indicators: Breach claim posted on a forum or social media with no corroborating evidence matching internal telemetry
Sample data attached to a claim that proves to be recycled from an unrelated, previously disclosed breach
Discrepancies between claimed scope and confirmed internal data holdings
rootCauses: Threat actor reputation-building or extortion attempt using a fabricated or exaggerated claim
Recycled data from an unrelated breach misattributed to the company
controls: Rapid internal verification process for external breach claims
Dark-web/forum monitoring for company-name mentions
ITID-23433.detection: Detection relies on monitoring plus rapid internal telemetry cross-check; there is no adversary technique to detect since no confirmed compromise exists.
ITID-23433.response: Verify rapidly against internal evidence, and issue a clear, fact-based public correction to limit reputational damage from the false claim.
metrics: Time from claim to internal verification/correction
Media pickup volume of the false claim
detections: Dark-web/forum monitoring alerting for brand mentions
ITID-23433.notes: This leaf exists specifically for claims that investigation shows are false or exaggerated; a confirmed claim should be reclassified into the matching sibling leaf rather than remaining here.

playbook.name: Response: Unverified/Exaggerated Breach Claim Announcement
playbook.description: For a threat-actor announcement claiming a breach that appears unverified, exaggerated, or potentially fabricated.

steps.title: Urgent triage: determine if this correlates with a known active intrusion
steps.desc: Immediately check whether SOC/IR has any open incident that this claim could correspond to, to rule out an active but undetected intrusion.
steps.guidance: Do not dismiss the claim purely because it seems exaggerated — verify before concluding it is false.
steps.outcome: Correlation with a known active intrusion confirmed or ruled out.

steps.title: Loop in PR/Comms and Legal for a measured stance
steps.desc: Notify PR/Comms and Legal so any public inquiry can be met with a fact-based, measured response rather than silence or overreaction.
steps.outcome: PR/Comms and Legal engaged and aligned on response stance.

steps.title: Close any confirmed vulnerability found during triage
steps.desc: If triage surfaced any real, even if minor, security gap, remediate it regardless of the overall claim's veracity.

steps.title: Issue a fact-based public statement if warranted
steps.desc: Coordinate with PR/Comms to issue a fact-based correction if the claim is gaining public traction and is assessed as false or exaggerated.

steps.title: Document the incident and the claim's veracity outcome
steps.desc: Record findings on the claim's veracity for future reference and threat-actor pattern tracking.

steps.title: Assess any provided evidence for authenticity
steps.desc: Evaluate any sample data or proof against known organizational data and check for signs of fabrication (recycled data from other breaches, inconsistent formatting).
steps.outcome: Evidence assessed as genuine, fabricated, or inconclusive.

steps.title: Continue monitoring for corroborating evidence
steps.desc: Keep the claim under threat-intel monitoring in case further evidence emerges that changes the assessment.

ITID-23434.def: An incident in which a threat actor posts a pre-sale teaser or auction announcement referencing stolen company data, without yet publishing the full listing or sample data, intended to build buyer interest or increase extortion pressure.
ITID-23434.purpose: Captures the brand impact when a threat actor publicly teases an upcoming sale or auction of stolen company data ahead of the full listing.
scopeIncludes: Public teaser/auction announcement naming the company ahead of a full data listing
Monitoring and response as the teaser transitions toward a full listing or sale
scopeExcludes: A full proprietary-data-for-sale listing with sample data already attached (ITID-23421 through ITID-23425, the Proprietary Data for Sale Type)
A ransomware-specific countdown announcement (ITID-23431)
ITID-23434.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High as the teaser approaches its stated auction/sale date.
ITID-23434.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 as the sale date nears or bidding activity is observed.
ITID-23434.escalation: Escalate to security operations for dark-web monitoring intensification, and to legal for evidence preservation ahead of a potential full listing.
indicators: Marketplace or forum post teasing an upcoming auction referencing the company without full sample data
Observed bidding or buyer-interest activity on the teaser listing
rootCauses: An underlying, not-yet-fully-disclosed theft of company data (root cause to be confirmed as the teaser develops)
controls: Dark-web/marketplace monitoring for pre-sale teaser activity
ITID-23434.detection: Dark-web and marketplace monitoring services are the primary detection surface for this leaf.
ITID-23434.response: Intensify monitoring as the teaser develops, and prepare a response plan in anticipation of a full listing under ITID-23421 through ITID-23425.
metrics: Time from teaser to full listing (if it occurs)
Observed bidding/buyer-interest activity
ITID-23434.notes: This leaf covers the pre-sale teaser stage specifically; once a full listing with sample data appears, the incident should be reclassified into the matching Proprietary Data for Sale leaf to avoid tracking the same event twice.

playbook.name: Response: Threat Actor Sale/Auction Announcement (Pre-Sale Teaser)
playbook.description: For a threat-actor announcement teasing an upcoming sale or auction of allegedly stolen organizational data, prior to the full listing going live.

steps.title: Urgent triage: determine if this correlates with a known active intrusion
steps.desc: Immediately check whether SOC/IR has any open incident that this teaser could correspond to.
steps.outcome: Correlation with a known active intrusion confirmed or ruled out.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Executive leadership
steps.desc: Notify Legal/Executives given the escalation risk if the auction proceeds and to prepare a response plan proactively.
steps.outcome: Legal/Executives engaged and response plan prepared.

steps.title: Close the root-cause vulnerability if confirmed
steps.desc: Remediate any confirmed exploited vulnerability.

steps.title: Prepare regulatory/customer notification materials proactively
steps.desc: Prepare draft notifications in advance in case the full listing confirms a genuine breach, so response is fast if it materializes.

steps.title: Document the incident and monitoring outcome
steps.desc: Record whether the full listing materialized and what it confirmed, for future reference.

steps.title: Assess any teaser sample for authenticity and monitor for the full listing
steps.desc: Evaluate any sample data in the teaser and set up monitoring to capture the full listing when/if it goes live.
steps.outcome: Teaser assessed; monitoring in place for the full listing.
steps.tool: Threat intelligence platform / dark web monitoring

steps.title: Contain the underlying intrusion if confirmed
steps.desc: If correlated with a confirmed intrusion, execute standard containment before the full listing potentially goes live.

ITID-23435.def: A confirmed or suspected public threat actor announcement referencing the company that has not yet been attributed to a specific category (ransomware countdown, hacktivist claim, unverified/exaggerated claim, or sale/auction teaser).
ITID-23435.purpose: Catch-all for threat actor announcement incidents that do not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to attribute the specific announcement category
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf (ITID-23431 through ITID-23434)
ITID-23435.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Medium-High pending scoping.
ITID-23435.priority: P2 by default, escalating upon confirmation of the specific announcement category and its credibility.
ITID-23435.escalation: Escalate to security operations for preliminary verification while investigation continues; reclassify once the specific pattern is clarified.
indicators: Public announcement referencing the company of unclear category or credibility
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
ITID-23435.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-23435.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-23435.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one; reclassify to ITID-23431 through ITID-23434 as soon as the announcement category is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Threat Actor Announcement
playbook.description: For a threat-actor public announcement that does not clearly fit a specific category (ransomware countdown, hacktivist claim, exaggerated claim, or sale teaser).

steps.title: Urgent triage: determine if this correlates with a known active intrusion
steps.desc: Immediately check whether SOC/IR has any open incident that this announcement could correspond to versus being an opportunistic/false claim.
steps.outcome: Correlation with a known active intrusion confirmed or ruled out.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and PR/Comms
steps.desc: Notify Legal/PR/Comms given the public nature of the announcement.

steps.title: Close the root-cause vulnerability if confirmed
steps.desc: Remediate any confirmed exploited vulnerability; reclassify to a specific ITID playbook if warranted.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated or incident reclassified.

steps.title: Execute notifications/communications per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send any required notifications or public communications based on what is confirmed.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings for future reference and classification refinement.

steps.title: Verify authenticity and classify the announcement type
steps.desc: Assess any evidence provided and determine which more specific category (ransomware, hacktivist, exaggerated claim, sale teaser) best applies, to enable reclassification.

steps.title: Contain the underlying intrusion if confirmed
steps.desc: If correlated with a confirmed intrusion, execute standard containment.

ITID-23511.def: An incident in which a network of automated or semi-automated social media bot accounts coordinates to spread false or misleading claims about the company, its products, or its leadership, at a scale and pattern indicating inauthentic coordination rather than organic public sentiment.
ITID-23511.purpose: Captures the brand impact of a coordinated misinformation campaign against the company driven primarily by automated bot networks.
scopeIncludes: Bot-network-driven spread of false or misleading claims about the company
Platform reporting and public-correction response to bot-amplified misinformation
scopeExcludes: State-sponsored disinformation operations, even if bot networks are used as a tool within them (ITID-23512)
Competitor-sponsored misinformation campaigns (ITID-23513)
Organic (non-bot) negative press amplification by real users (ITID-23522, ITID-23524)
ITID-23511.severity: Medium, escalating to High if the campaign achieves significant reach or is picked up by mainstream media as if genuine.
ITID-23511.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 if the campaign materially affects stock price, sales, or public trust.
ITID-23511.escalation: Escalate to communications and social media/brand monitoring; report inauthentic accounts to platforms for takedown.
indicators: Coordinated posting patterns (near-identical timing/content) across many low-history accounts
Platform-level bot/inauthentic-behavior signals flagged by social media analytics tools
Unnatural spike in negative mentions inconsistent with organic engagement patterns
vectors: Bot network amplification of a fabricated claim or manipulated content
Coordinated inauthentic account creation to simulate grassroots sentiment
rootCauses: Absence of proactive social-listening/bot-detection monitoring
Low platform friction for creating and operating inauthentic accounts at scale
controls: Social media/brand monitoring with bot-detection analytics
Platform reporting and takedown request process
ITID-23511.detection: Social listening and bot-detection analytics tools provide the primary detection surface; there is no adversary network-intrusion technique involved.
ITID-23511.response: Document and report inauthentic accounts to platforms, issue factual public corrections, and monitor for campaign evolution.
metrics: Reach/impression volume of the campaign
Number of inauthentic accounts identified and reported
Time to platform takedown
ITID-23511.notes: This is a communications/PR event with no adversary network-intrusion technique; MITRE mapping is intentionally empty. Distinguished from ITID-23512/23513 by absence of confirmed state or competitor sponsorship.

playbook.name: Response: Bot Network-Driven Misinformation Campaign
playbook.description: For a coordinated misinformation campaign against the organization driven by an automated bot network.

steps.title: Identify the false claims and assess the bot network's scale
steps.desc: Catalog the specific false claims being spread and assess the scale and platforms of the bot network amplifying them.
steps.outcome: False claims cataloged; bot network scale assessed.

steps.title: Report the bot accounts/content to the platforms
steps.desc: File coordinated inauthentic behavior reports with the relevant social media platforms.

steps.title: Publish fact-based corrective content
steps.desc: Issue clear, fact-based corrections through official channels to counter the false claims.
steps.guidance: Avoid amplifying the false claims further by over-engaging directly with bot accounts.

steps.title: Monitor for continued spread and adjust response
steps.desc: Continue monitoring sentiment and spread to determine if further correction or platform escalation is needed.
steps.outcome: Spread trend confirmed declining or further action taken.

steps.title: Document the incident and update misinformation response playbook
steps.desc: Record the campaign's tactics and response effectiveness for future reference.

steps.title: Assess actual reach and business impact
steps.desc: Determine how far the misinformation has spread and whether it is affecting customer trust, stock price, or media coverage.

steps.title: Loop in PR/Comms immediately
steps.desc: Notify PR/Comms to prepare a fact-based correction and coordinate response messaging.

ITID-23512.def: An incident in which a nation-state or state-affiliated actor conducts a coordinated disinformation campaign against the company, typically tied to geopolitical tensions, sanctions, or the company's operations in a particular region.
ITID-23512.purpose: Captures the brand and geopolitical-risk impact of a state-sponsored disinformation campaign targeting the company.
scopeIncludes: Disinformation campaign attributed with reasonable confidence to a state or state-affiliated actor
Coordination with geopolitical-risk, legal, and government-affairs functions in response
scopeExcludes: Bot-driven misinformation without state attribution (ITID-23511)
Competitor-sponsored misinformation (ITID-23513)
ITID-23512.severity: High to Critical, given the resourcing and persistence typical of state-sponsored operations and potential geopolitical escalation.
ITID-23512.priority: P1 upon reasonable-confidence attribution to a state actor.
ITID-23512.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership, government affairs/geopolitical risk, legal, and communications; consider coordination with relevant government or industry-sharing bodies.
indicators: Disinformation content matching known state-actor messaging themes or infrastructure
Threat intelligence attribution linking the campaign to a known state-sponsored influence operation
Coordinated cross-platform, multi-language amplification consistent with state-level resourcing
vectors: State-operated media outlet or state-linked account network amplification
Coordinated multi-platform disinformation campaign with sustained resourcing
rootCauses: Company operations, statements, or positioning perceived as adverse to the state actor's interests
controls: Threat intelligence monitoring for state-sponsored influence operations
Government-affairs and geopolitical-risk engagement process
ITID-23512.detection: Detection relies on threat intelligence attribution and social listening rather than internal technical telemetry; there is no adversary network-intrusion technique involved.
ITID-23512.response: Coordinate a measured, fact-based public response while engaging geopolitical-risk and government-affairs functions on broader strategic implications.
metrics: Reach/impression volume of the campaign
Time to attribution confidence
ITID-23512.notes: This is a communications/geopolitical event with no adversary network-intrusion technique; MITRE mapping is intentionally empty. Distinguished from sibling leaves by confirmed or reasonably-confident state attribution.

playbook.name: Response: State-Sponsored Disinformation Campaign
playbook.description: For a coordinated disinformation campaign against the organization assessed as state-sponsored.

steps.title: Identify the false claims and assess attribution indicators
steps.desc: Catalog the specific false claims and work with threat intelligence to assess indicators suggesting state-sponsored origin.
steps.guidance: Attribution to a specific state actor should be treated cautiously and left to qualified threat intel analysis.
steps.outcome: False claims cataloged; attribution indicators assessed.
steps.tool: Threat intelligence platform / social media monitoring

steps.title: Loop in Legal, PR/Comms, and Executive leadership immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/PR/Comms/Executives given the elevated sensitivity of a suspected state-sponsored campaign, which may warrant government/law-enforcement coordination.

steps.title: Publish fact-based corrective content
steps.desc: Issue clear, fact-based corrections through official channels.

steps.title: Coordinate with relevant government/industry bodies if appropriate
steps.desc: Where Legal/Executives determine appropriate, share findings with relevant government cybersecurity or industry information-sharing bodies.

steps.title: Document the incident and update misinformation response playbook
steps.desc: Record the campaign's tactics, attribution assessment, and response effectiveness.

steps.title: Assess actual reach and business/geopolitical impact
steps.desc: Determine how far the disinformation has spread and whether it carries geopolitical or regulatory implications.

steps.title: Report the coordinated inauthentic content to the platforms
steps.desc: File coordinated inauthentic behavior reports with the relevant platforms.

ITID-23513.def: An incident in which a competitor is found to be directly or indirectly sponsoring a coordinated misinformation campaign against the company, typically to damage market perception or influence a competitive deal/procurement decision.
ITID-23513.purpose: Captures the brand and competitive-intelligence impact of a misinformation campaign against the company sponsored by a competitor.
scopeIncludes: Misinformation campaign attributed with reasonable confidence to a competitor's direct or indirect sponsorship
Legal assessment of unfair-competition/defamation remedies
scopeExcludes: State-sponsored disinformation (ITID-23512)
Bot-driven misinformation without confirmed competitor sponsorship (ITID-23511)
ITID-23513.severity: High, given potential for direct competitive/sales impact and available legal remedies.
ITID-23513.priority: P1 upon reasonable-confidence attribution to a competitor.
ITID-23513.escalation: Escalate to legal (unfair competition/defamation counsel), sales leadership, and communications.
indicators: Misinformation content traceable to a competitor's marketing agency, employee, or affiliated third party
Content specifically targeting a competitive deal/procurement decision with false claims about the company
Whistleblower or investigative reporting linking the campaign to a competitor
vectors: Sponsored/paid content placement disparaging the company through an intermediary agency
Coordinated sales-team talking points based on fabricated claims traced back to a competitor
rootCauses: Competitive pressure in an active sales cycle or market-positioning battle
controls: Legal monitoring for unfair-competition/defamation exposure
Sales-team competitive-intelligence rebuttal process
ITID-23513.detection: Detection relies on social listening, sales-team field reporting, and investigative/legal discovery rather than technical telemetry.
ITID-23513.response: Pursue legal remedies where attribution is solid, equip sales teams with factual rebuttals, and issue public correction where warranted.
metrics: Number of deals/customers impacted by the campaign
Time to legal response where pursued
ITID-23513.notes: This is a communications/competitive event with no adversary network-intrusion technique; MITRE mapping is intentionally empty. Distinguished from sibling leaves by confirmed or reasonably-confident competitor sponsorship.

playbook.name: Response: Competitor-Sponsored Misinformation Campaign
playbook.description: For a coordinated misinformation campaign against the organization assessed as sponsored by a competitor.

steps.title: Identify the false claims and assess evidence of competitor involvement
steps.desc: Catalog the specific false claims and gather any evidence suggesting competitor sponsorship, handling attribution carefully.
steps.guidance: Attribution claims against a named competitor carry legal risk if wrong — corroborate before acting on this theory.
steps.outcome: False claims cataloged; competitor-involvement evidence assessed.

steps.title: Loop in Legal immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal given potential defamation, unfair-competition, or trade-practices claims if competitor sponsorship is substantiated.

steps.title: Publish fact-based corrective content
steps.desc: Issue clear, fact-based corrections through official channels, coordinated with PR/Comms.

steps.title: Pursue legal remedies if competitor sponsorship is substantiated
steps.desc: Execute Legal's determined course of action if evidence sufficiently substantiates competitor involvement.

steps.title: Document the incident and update misinformation response playbook
steps.desc: Record the campaign's tactics and response effectiveness.

steps.title: Assess actual reach and business impact
steps.desc: Determine how far the misinformation has spread and its effect on customer trust or market position.

steps.title: Report the coordinated inauthentic content to the platforms
steps.desc: File coordinated inauthentic behavior reports with the relevant platforms.

ITID-23514.def: An incident in which AI-generated synthetic media (deepfake video, cloned voice audio, or fabricated imagery) depicting a company executive or representing the company is used to spread false statements or claims, and is disseminated as if genuine.
ITID-23514.purpose: Captures the brand impact of a misinformation campaign against the company using AI-generated deepfake audio, video, or imagery.
scopeIncludes: Deepfake/synthetic media falsely depicting a company executive or representing the company, disseminated to deceive
Public correction and platform takedown response to the synthetic media
scopeExcludes: Traditional (non-AI-generated) misinformation, even if bot-amplified (ITID-23511)
Deepfake content used specifically to compromise an influencer's account or reputation rather than the company's (ITID-23532)
ITID-23514.severity: High to Critical, given the difficulty of debunking convincing synthetic media quickly and its potential to move markets or damage executive credibility.
ITID-23514.priority: P1 immediately upon discovery of circulating deepfake content depicting the company or its executives.
ITID-23514.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership, legal, and communications immediately; engage platform trust-and-safety teams for expedited takedown.
indicators: Video/audio content depicting an executive making statements they did not make
Forensic analysis identifying synthetic-media artifacts (inconsistent lip-sync, audio artifacts)
Rapid unexplained spread of a video/audio clip inconsistent with any real event
vectors: AI voice-cloning of an executive for a fabricated statement or scam
AI video generation depicting an executive in a fabricated scenario
rootCauses: Increasing accessibility of generative AI tools lowering the barrier to convincing synthetic media
Abundant public audio/video source material of executives enabling voice/likeness cloning
controls: Deepfake detection/forensic analysis capability
Rapid public-debunking and platform-takedown process
Executive digital-likeness monitoring
ITID-23514.detection: Detection relies on social listening plus deepfake-forensic analysis tools rather than network/endpoint telemetry; there is no adversary intrusion technique involved.
ITID-23514.response: Obtain forensic confirmation of the synthetic nature of the media, issue a rapid public debunking, and pursue platform takedown and legal action where identifiable.
metrics: Time from discovery to public debunking
Reach/impression volume before takedown
ITID-23514.notes: This is a communications/PR event with no adversary network-intrusion technique; MITRE mapping is intentionally empty even though the content itself is AI-generated. Distinguished from ITID-23532 by targeting the company/executive directly rather than compromising an influencer's own account.

playbook.name: Response: AI-Generated Deepfake Misinformation Campaign
playbook.description: For a coordinated misinformation campaign against the organization using AI-generated deepfake video, audio, or imagery.

steps.title: Confirm the content is fabricated and catalog the false claims it makes
steps.desc: Technically analyze the suspect media to confirm it is AI-generated/fabricated and document what false claims or statements it depicts.
steps.guidance: Use forensic media analysis tools; do not assume fabrication without technical verification.
steps.outcome: Fabrication confirmed and false content documented.
steps.abort: If the content cannot be conclusively shown as fabricated, treat cautiously and consult Legal before public denial.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and PR/Comms immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/PR/Comms given reputational and potential defamation/impersonation legal implications.

steps.title: Publish a clear, fact-based public denial with technical evidence
steps.desc: Issue a public statement clearly identifying the content as fabricated, supported by the forensic analysis where appropriate.

steps.title: Support any affected individuals depicted in the deepfake
steps.desc: Provide support to any executive or employee falsely depicted, including legal and communications support.

steps.title: Document the incident and update deepfake detection readiness
steps.desc: Record the campaign's tactics and recommend improved monitoring for synthetic media impersonation.

steps.title: Assess actual reach and business impact
steps.desc: Determine how far the deepfake has spread and its effect on customer trust, executives' reputations, or stock price.

steps.title: Report the deepfake content to platforms for takedown
steps.desc: File takedown requests with the relevant platforms citing their synthetic/manipulated media policies.

ITID-23515.def: A confirmed or suspected coordinated misinformation campaign against the company that has not yet been attributed to a specific driver (bot network, state sponsorship, competitor sponsorship, or AI-generated deepfake content).
ITID-23515.purpose: Catch-all for coordinated misinformation campaign incidents that do not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to attribute the specific campaign driver
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf (ITID-23511 through ITID-23514)
ITID-23515.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Medium-High pending scoping.
ITID-23515.priority: P2 by default, escalating upon confirmation of the specific driver and its reach.
ITID-23515.escalation: Escalate to communications for preliminary assessment while investigation continues; reclassify once the specific pattern is clarified.
indicators: Coordinated false content about the company of unclear origin
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
ITID-23515.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-23515.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-23515.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one; reclassify to ITID-23511 through ITID-23514 as soon as the campaign driver is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Coordinated Misinformation Campaign
playbook.description: For a coordinated misinformation campaign against the organization that does not clearly fit a specific origin category (bot network, state-sponsored, competitor, deepfake).

steps.title: Identify the false claims and assess origin indicators
steps.desc: Catalog the specific false claims being spread and gather any evidence of the campaign's origin to enable reclassification if warranted.
steps.outcome: False claims cataloged; origin indicators assessed.

steps.title: Report the content to the platforms
steps.desc: File appropriate reports with the relevant social media/content platforms.

steps.title: Publish fact-based corrective content
steps.desc: Issue clear, fact-based corrections through official channels; reclassify to a specific ITID playbook if origin becomes clear.
steps.outcome: Corrective content published or incident reclassified.

steps.title: Monitor for continued spread and adjust response
steps.desc: Continue monitoring sentiment and spread to determine if further correction is needed.
steps.outcome: Spread trend confirmed declining or further action taken.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the campaign's tactics and response effectiveness for future reference.

steps.title: Assess actual reach and business impact
steps.desc: Determine how far the misinformation has spread and its effect on customer trust or reputation.

steps.title: Loop in PR/Comms and Legal
steps.desc: Notify PR/Comms/Legal to prepare a fact-based correction and assess any legal implications once origin is clearer.

ITID-23521.def: An incident in which genuine (not fabricated) negative press coverage of the company is artificially amplified beyond its organic reach through paid bot networks or click-farm services, distorting the apparent scale of public reaction.
ITID-23521.purpose: Captures the brand impact when negative press coverage of the company is artificially amplified using paid bots or click-farms.
scopeIncludes: Artificial amplification (shares, clicks, engagement) of genuinely published negative press via paid bot/click-farm services
Assessment of whether amplified engagement is materially distorting business or investor perception
scopeExcludes: Fabrication of false content itself, which is a misinformation campaign (ITID-23511 through ITID-23515)
Coordinated inauthentic sharing that is unpaid/organic-appearing rather than a paid click-farm service (ITID-23522)
ITID-23521.severity: Medium, escalating to High if amplification materially affects stock price or search-result prominence.
ITID-23521.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 for material business impact.
ITID-23521.escalation: Escalate to communications and social media/brand monitoring; report identified inauthentic amplification to platforms.
indicators: Engagement metrics on a negative article inconsistent with organic reach patterns (e.g., disproportionate shares relative to actual readership)
Analytics tooling identifying click-farm traffic signatures
vectors: Paid click-farm/bot service engaged to boost engagement metrics on existing negative coverage
rootCauses: Underlying negative event that generated the genuine press coverage being amplified
Low-cost availability of click-farm/bot amplification services
controls: Social/brand monitoring with bot-detection analytics
Platform reporting process for inauthentic engagement
ITID-23521.detection: Social listening and bot-detection analytics tools provide the primary detection surface; there is no adversary network-intrusion technique involved.
ITID-23521.response: Report inauthentic amplification to platforms, and address the underlying negative story on its merits rather than only the amplification.
metrics: Engagement volume attributable to identified inauthentic amplification
Time to platform action on reported inauthentic activity
ITID-23521.notes: Distinguished from the Coordinated Misinformation Campaign Type by amplifying genuinely true/published content rather than fabricating false claims.

playbook.name: Response: Paid Bot/Click-Farm Amplification of Negative Story
playbook.description: For a negative story about the organization being artificially amplified via paid bots or a click-farm operation.

steps.title: Identify the negative story and assess evidence of artificial amplification
steps.desc: Catalog the story's claims and gather evidence (engagement pattern anomalies, account age/behavior clustering) indicating bot/click-farm amplification versus organic spread.
steps.outcome: Story cataloged; artificial amplification evidence assessed.

steps.title: Report the coordinated inauthentic activity to the platforms
steps.desc: File coordinated inauthentic behavior reports with the relevant platforms.

steps.title: Publish a fact-based response
steps.desc: If the story is false/exaggerated, issue a factual correction; if accurate, address the underlying issue rather than only the amplification.

steps.title: Monitor for continued amplification
steps.desc: Continue monitoring to confirm the artificial amplification has subsided.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings and response effectiveness for future reference.

steps.title: Assess the underlying story's factual accuracy
steps.desc: Independently determine whether the negative story itself is factually accurate, exaggerated, or false, separate from how it's being amplified.
steps.guidance: Artificial amplification does not mean the underlying story is false — verify both independently.
steps.outcome: Factual accuracy of the underlying story assessed.

steps.title: Loop in PR/Comms
steps.desc: Notify PR/Comms to prepare a response appropriate to whether the underlying story is accurate or not.

ITID-23522.def: An incident in which a coordinated network of accounts, designed to appear as genuine individual users rather than obvious bots, shares and amplifies negative press coverage of the company in a synchronized pattern indicating central coordination.
ITID-23522.purpose: Captures the brand impact when negative press is amplified through coordinated inauthentic social sharing by a network of accounts posing as genuine users.
scopeIncludes: Coordinated, synchronized sharing of negative press by accounts designed to mimic authentic individual users
Platform reporting and investigation into the coordination network
scopeExcludes: Amplification via an overtly automated bot/click-farm service (ITID-23521)
Fabrication of false content itself (ITID-23511 through ITID-23515)
ITID-23522.severity: Medium, escalating to High if the coordination is large-scale or materially shapes public/media narrative.
ITID-23522.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 for material business or narrative impact.
ITID-23522.escalation: Escalate to communications and social media/brand monitoring; provide platform trust-and-safety teams with coordination evidence for investigation.
indicators: Synchronized posting timing and near-identical phrasing across many accounts with genuine-looking profiles
Platform coordinated-inauthentic-behavior (CIB) detection flagging the network
vectors: Sock-puppet account network activated to synchronize sharing of a negative story
rootCauses: Underlying negative event that generated the story being amplified
Availability of sock-puppet account networks for hire
controls: Social/brand monitoring with coordinated-inauthentic-behavior detection
Platform reporting process for CIB networks
ITID-23522.detection: Platform CIB-detection tooling and social listening provide the primary detection surface; there is no adversary network-intrusion technique involved.
ITID-23522.response: Report the coordination network to platforms for investigation, and address the underlying story on its merits.
metrics: Number of accounts identified in the coordination network
Reach/impression volume of the amplified story
ITID-23522.notes: Distinguished from ITID-23521 by the sock-puppet/genuine-appearing account pattern rather than an overt paid click-farm/bot signature.

playbook.name: Response: Coordinated Inauthentic Social Sharing of Negative Story
playbook.description: For a negative story about the organization being spread via a coordinated network of inauthentic social media accounts (as distinct from automated bots or paid click-farms).

steps.title: Identify the negative story and map the sharing network
steps.desc: Catalog the story's claims and analyze the account network sharing it for signs of coordination (shared creation dates, identical posting timing, network structure).

steps.title: Report the coordinated inauthentic network to the platforms
steps.desc: File coordinated inauthentic behavior reports with the relevant platforms.

steps.title: Publish a fact-based response
steps.desc: If the story is false/exaggerated, issue a factual correction; if accurate, address the underlying issue.

steps.title: Monitor for continued spread
steps.desc: Continue monitoring to confirm the coordinated sharing has subsided.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings and response effectiveness for future reference.
