steps.title: Assess the underlying story's factual accuracy
steps.desc: Independently determine whether the negative story is factually accurate, exaggerated, or false.

steps.title: Loop in PR/Comms
steps.desc: Notify PR/Comms to prepare an appropriate response.

ITID-23523.def: An incident in which a party manipulates search engine ranking signals (SEO manipulation, negative SEO, review/link farms) to increase the visibility and ranking of negative press content about the company in search results.
ITID-23523.purpose: Captures the brand impact when search engine results are manipulated to surface negative press about the company more prominently.
scopeIncludes: Deliberate manipulation of search ranking signals to elevate negative content's visibility
Positive-SEO/reputation-management response to counter the manipulation
scopeExcludes: Amplification via direct social sharing rather than search-ranking manipulation (ITID-23521, ITID-23522)
Review-specific manipulation on a review platform rather than general search results (ITID-23524)
ITID-23523.severity: Medium, escalating to High if the manipulated negative content dominates first-page results for company-name searches over a sustained period.
ITID-23523.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 for sustained first-page dominance affecting sales/recruiting/investor perception.
ITID-23523.escalation: Escalate to communications/digital marketing for SEO countermeasures; report clearly abusive link-farm manipulation to the search engine.
indicators: Unusual backlink pattern pointing to negative content from low-quality/farm sites
Sudden, unexplained ranking jump for negative content inconsistent with organic SEO signals
vectors: Negative SEO campaign building manipulative backlinks to negative content
Link-farm network used to artificially boost negative content ranking
rootCauses: Underlying negative event that generated the content being promoted
Insufficient proactive SEO/reputation-management investment in owned positive content
controls: SEO/reputation monitoring for company-name search results
Proactive positive-content SEO investment as a resilience measure
ITID-23523.detection: SEO monitoring tools and search-ranking analytics provide the primary detection surface; there is no adversary network-intrusion technique involved.
ITID-23523.response: Deploy legitimate SEO countermeasures, report clear manipulation to the search engine, and address the underlying negative story on its merits.
metrics: Search ranking position for company-name queries over time
Time to countermeasure effectiveness
ITID-23523.notes: Distinguished from other amplification leaves by the search-ranking-manipulation mechanism specifically, which requires SEO-specific rather than social-platform countermeasures.

playbook.name: Response: Search Engine Result Manipulation to Surface Negative Press
playbook.description: For manipulation of search engine results (SEO manipulation, negative SEO attacks) designed to surface negative press about the organization more prominently.

steps.title: Identify the manipulated search results and the technique used
steps.desc: Document which search queries/results are affected and investigate the manipulation technique (link spam, fake reviews feeding search ranking, negative SEO).

steps.title: Report manipulation to the search engine
steps.desc: File a report with the search engine's spam/manipulation reporting channel with supporting evidence.

steps.title: Publish authoritative, fact-based content
steps.desc: Publish clear, authoritative content addressing the topic to help legitimate information rank appropriately, coordinated with Marketing.

steps.title: Monitor search result changes
steps.desc: Continue monitoring the affected search queries to confirm results normalize.
steps.outcome: Search results confirmed normalized or improved.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings and response effectiveness for future reference.

steps.title: Assess the underlying content's factual accuracy
steps.desc: Independently determine whether the surfaced negative press is factually accurate, exaggerated, or false.

steps.title: Loop in PR/Comms and Marketing/SEO team
steps.desc: Notify PR/Comms and the Marketing/SEO team to coordinate response and any legitimate SEO countermeasures.

ITID-23524.def: An incident in which a coordinated group posts a large volume of negative reviews or ratings against the company on a review platform (app stores, Glassdoor, Google/Yelp, etc.) within a short period, disproportionate to genuine customer/employee sentiment, typically in reaction to a specific triggering event.
ITID-23524.purpose: Captures the brand impact when the company is targeted by a coordinated review-bombing campaign on a review or ratings platform.
scopeIncludes: Coordinated bulk negative-review posting in a short timeframe disproportionate to normal review volume
Platform reporting and dispute process for identified inauthentic reviews
scopeExcludes: General search-ranking manipulation not specific to a review platform (ITID-23523)
Genuine, organically distributed negative reviews reflecting real customer/employee sentiment, even at elevated volume, which are a business/product-quality matter rather than a security incident
ITID-23524.severity: Medium, escalating to High if the campaign materially depresses the company's review score or app-store ranking over a sustained period.
ITID-23524.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 for material sales/recruiting impact.
ITID-23524.escalation: Escalate to communications and the relevant platform-relationship owner (app store, review site) to file a coordinated-abuse report.
indicators: Sudden spike in negative reviews within a short window, often coinciding with a specific triggering event (news story, social media call-to-action)
Reviews with near-identical phrasing or clearly fabricated details inconsistent with genuine use of the product/employment
vectors: Organized online community coordinating a mass negative-review posting campaign
Bot/fake-account network posting reviews without genuine underlying interaction with the company
rootCauses: A specific triggering event (news story, controversy) galvanizing coordinated review activity
Insufficient review-platform anti-abuse controls allowing bulk fake review posting
controls: Review-platform monitoring for volume/sentiment anomalies
Platform dispute/reporting process for identified fake reviews
ITID-23524.detection: Review-platform monitoring and sentiment-analytics tools provide the primary detection surface; there is no adversary network-intrusion technique involved.
ITID-23524.response: File dispute/abuse reports with the platform for clearly inauthentic reviews, and address the underlying triggering event through normal communications channels.
metrics: Review volume and average rating during the campaign window versus baseline
Number of reviews successfully removed via platform dispute
ITID-23524.notes: Scoped strictly to coordinated, inauthentic review-bombing; a wave of genuine negative reviews reflecting real dissatisfaction is a product/business matter, not a security incident, and is explicitly excluded.

playbook.name: Response: Review Bombing Campaign
playbook.description: For a coordinated campaign of negative reviews (review bombing) targeting the organization's products/services on review platforms.

steps.title: Identify the affected platforms and assess coordination evidence
steps.desc: Catalog which review platforms are affected and gather evidence of coordination (review timing clustering, similar wording, reviewer account patterns).
steps.outcome: Affected platforms identified; coordination evidence assessed.

steps.title: Report the coordinated reviews to the platforms
steps.desc: File reports with the relevant review platforms citing their policies against coordinated/inauthentic reviews.

steps.title: Address any genuine underlying issues identified
steps.desc: If genuine issues were surfaced, address them and communicate the fix, separate from the review-bombing response.

steps.title: Monitor review score recovery
steps.desc: Continue monitoring review platforms to confirm scores normalize after platform action.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings and response effectiveness for future reference.

steps.title: Assess whether any reviews reflect genuine underlying issues
steps.desc: Separate genuine customer complaints from coordinated inauthentic reviews to ensure legitimate feedback is not dismissed.
steps.outcome: Genuine issues, if any, identified separately from the coordinated campaign.

steps.title: Loop in PR/Comms and Customer Success
steps.desc: Notify PR/Comms and Customer Success to coordinate response and address any genuine customer concerns identified.

ITID-23525.def: A confirmed or suspected artificial amplification of negative press about the company that has not yet been attributed to a specific mechanism (paid bot/click-farm, coordinated inauthentic sharing, search engine manipulation, or review bombing).
ITID-23525.purpose: Catch-all for negative press amplification incidents that do not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to attribute the specific amplification mechanism
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf (ITID-23521 through ITID-23524)
ITID-23525.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Medium pending scoping.
ITID-23525.priority: P2 by default, escalating upon confirmation of the specific mechanism and its reach.
ITID-23525.escalation: Escalate to communications for preliminary assessment while investigation continues; reclassify once the specific pattern is clarified.
indicators: Unusual amplification of negative content of unclear mechanism
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
ITID-23525.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-23525.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-23525.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one; reclassify to ITID-23521 through ITID-23524 as soon as the amplification mechanism is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Negative Press Amplification
playbook.description: For a negative press amplification incident that does not clearly fit a specific mechanism category (bot/click-farm, coordinated sharing, SEO manipulation, review bombing).

steps.title: Identify the negative content and the amplification mechanism
steps.desc: Catalog the negative content and investigate how it is being amplified, to enable reclassification if a more specific category applies.

steps.title: Report to relevant platforms
steps.desc: File appropriate reports with the relevant platforms based on the amplification mechanism.

steps.title: Publish a fact-based response
steps.desc: Issue a factual correction or address the underlying issue as appropriate; reclassify to a specific ITID playbook if the mechanism becomes clear.
steps.outcome: Appropriate response published or incident reclassified.

steps.title: Monitor for continued amplification
steps.desc: Continue monitoring to confirm the amplification has subsided.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings for future reference and classification refinement.

steps.title: Assess the underlying content's factual accuracy
steps.desc: Independently determine whether the negative content is factually accurate, exaggerated, or false.

steps.title: Loop in PR/Comms
steps.desc: Notify PR/Comms to coordinate response.

ITID-23531.def: An incident in which an influencer is paid (directly or through an intermediary, potentially including a competitor or hostile actor) to post disinformation or unfairly negative content about the company without disclosing the paid/sponsored nature of the post, violating advertising-disclosure norms.
ITID-23531.purpose: Captures the brand and regulatory (FTC disclosure) impact when a paid influencer disseminates disinformation about the company without disclosing sponsorship.
scopeIncludes: Paid influencer content spreading false or misleading claims about the company without sponsorship disclosure
Assessment and reporting of advertising-disclosure violations to relevant platforms/regulators
scopeExcludes: An influencer's account being compromised and used without their knowledge or consent (ITID-23532)
An influencer coerced/blackmailed into posting against their will (ITID-23533)
ITID-23531.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High if the influencer has substantial reach or the campaign appears linked to a competitor.
ITID-23531.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 for high-reach influencers or confirmed competitor sponsorship.
ITID-23531.escalation: Escalate to communications and legal; consider referring clear non-disclosure violations to the relevant advertising-standards regulator (e.g., FTC).
indicators: Influencer post containing false claims about the company with no sponsorship disclosure
Evidence of payment or coordination linking the influencer to an undisclosed sponsor
vectors: Paid content placement through an intermediary agency obscuring the true sponsor
rootCauses: Competitive or ideological motivation of the undisclosed sponsor
Weak enforcement of influencer disclosure requirements on the hosting platform
controls: Social/influencer monitoring for undisclosed sponsored negative content
Legal referral process for advertising-disclosure violations
ITID-23531.detection: Detection relies on social listening and investigative/legal discovery rather than technical telemetry.
ITID-23531.response: Document the non-disclosure violation, pursue platform/regulatory reporting, and issue a factual public correction.
metrics: Reach of the influencer content
Time to platform/regulatory reporting
ITID-23531.notes: This is a communications/advertising-compliance event with no adversary network-intrusion technique; MITRE mapping is intentionally empty.

playbook.name: Response: Paid Influencer Disinformation Campaign (Undisclosed Sponsorship)
playbook.description: For an influencer spreading negative or false claims about the organization as part of an undisclosed paid campaign, likely sponsored by a competitor or other adversarial party.

steps.title: Identify the influencer content and assess evidence of undisclosed sponsorship
steps.desc: Catalog the specific claims made and gather evidence suggesting paid, undisclosed sponsorship (e.g. sudden coordinated posting across multiple influencers, disclosure law violations).

steps.title: Loop in Legal and PR/Comms
steps.desc: Notify Legal/PR/Comms given potential advertising-disclosure law violations (e.g. FTC endorsement guidelines) and defamation considerations.

steps.title: Publish a fact-based correction
steps.desc: Issue a factual correction addressing the false or misleading claims through official channels.

steps.title: Pursue legal remedies as directed by Legal
steps.desc: Execute Legal's determined course of action if the campaign is substantiated as sponsored disinformation.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings and response effectiveness for future reference.

steps.title: Assess the underlying claims' factual accuracy
steps.desc: Independently determine whether the claims made are factually accurate, exaggerated, or false.

steps.title: Report non-disclosure violations to the platform/regulator as appropriate
steps.desc: File reports with the relevant platform or advertising regulator regarding undisclosed sponsorship where evidence supports it.

ITID-23532.def: An incident in which an attacker gains unauthorized technical access to an influencer's social media account and uses it to post fabricated negative content about the company, without the influencer's knowledge or consent.
ITID-23532.purpose: Captures the brand impact when an influencer's own account is compromised by an attacker and used to post negative content about the company.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed account takeover of an influencer used to post negative content about the company
Coordination with the influencer and platform to remove the unauthorized content and restore the account
scopeExcludes: Content posted willingly by a paid, undisclosed-sponsorship influencer (ITID-23531)
Content posted by an influencer under coercion/blackmail while still in control of their own account (ITID-23533)
ITID-23532.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High for influencers with substantial reach or if the compromised content spreads rapidly before removal.
ITID-23532.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 for high-reach influencers or rapid content spread.
ITID-23532.escalation: Escalate to communications and the influencer's own security/platform-support contacts; coordinate rapid content removal and public clarification.
indicators: Influencer reports being locked out of their own account after the negative post appeared
Post content and tone inconsistent with the influencer's normal voice/style
Influencer's own public statement disavowing the post as unauthorized
vectors: Phishing of the influencer's account credentials
Credential stuffing or reused-password compromise of the influencer's account
SIM-swap attack enabling account-recovery takeover
rootCauses: Influencer's own weak account security (no MFA, reused passwords)
Platform account-recovery process vulnerable to social engineering
controls: Coordination with influencer/partner accounts to require MFA
Rapid content-takedown coordination process with platforms
ITID-23532.detection: Detection relies primarily on the influencer's own account-security telemetry (outside company control) plus social listening for anomalous content.
ITID-23532.response: Coordinate with the influencer and platform for rapid takedown, issue a factual public clarification, and support the influencer's account-recovery process.
metrics: Time from compromised post to takedown
Reach of the compromised content before removal
ITID-23532.notes: This is the one leaf in its sibling group with a genuine adversary account-compromise technique, since it involves an actual unauthorized technical takeover rather than a willing or coerced post.

playbook.name: Response: Influencer Account Compromise for Negative Content Posting
playbook.description: For an influencer's social media account being compromised and used to post negative content about the organization.

steps.title: Confirm the account compromise and identify the posted content
steps.desc: Contact the influencer or their management to confirm the account was compromised (not a genuine post) and catalog the posted negative content.
steps.guidance: Approach the influencer collaboratively — they are a victim of the compromise, not the source of the negative content.
steps.abort: If the influencer confirms the post was genuine, this is not an account compromise — treat under a different ITID.

steps.title: Support the influencer in regaining account control
steps.desc: Assist the influencer/their team with the platform's account-recovery process where appropriate.
steps.outcome: Support provided to regain account control.

steps.title: Request removal of the compromised posts
steps.desc: Work with the influencer and platform to have the unauthorized posts removed.

steps.title: Publish a clarifying statement
steps.desc: Issue a statement clarifying that the negative content did not reflect the influencer's genuine views and resulted from a security compromise.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings and response effectiveness, and consider advising key influencer partners on account security best practices.

steps.title: Assess reach and business impact
steps.desc: Determine how far the false content spread before removal and its impact on brand perception.

steps.title: Loop in PR/Comms
steps.desc: Notify PR/Comms to prepare a clarifying statement noting the content resulted from a compromised account, not the influencer's genuine views.

ITID-23533.def: An incident in which a third party coerces or blackmails an influencer — using their own account, under their own knowing control — into posting fabricated or unfairly negative content about the company.
ITID-23533.purpose: Captures the brand impact when an influencer is coerced or blackmailed into posting negative content about the company against their will.
scopeIncludes: Negative content posted by an influencer under confirmed coercion or blackmail, with the influencer's own knowing (if unwilling) involvement
Support for the influencer in reporting the coercion and removing the content
scopeExcludes: Account takeover without the influencer's knowledge or consent (ITID-23532)
Paid, willingly undisclosed-sponsorship posting (ITID-23531)
ITID-23533.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High for influencers with substantial reach.
ITID-23533.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 for high-reach influencers or evidence of a broader coercion campaign against multiple influencers.
ITID-23533.escalation: Escalate to communications and legal; support the influencer in law enforcement reporting of the coercion/blackmail where they are willing.
indicators: Influencer's own disclosure of having been coerced or blackmailed into posting
Post content inconsistent with the influencer's prior public positions, later followed by an apology or explanation
vectors: Blackmail using compromising personal material to compel the influencer's cooperation
Threats against the influencer or their associates to compel a negative post
rootCauses: The coercing party's motivation (competitive, ideological, or personal grievance) against the company
controls: Support resources/legal referral for influencers reporting coercion
Social listening for content inconsistent with an influencer's established pattern
ITID-23533.detection: Detection relies primarily on the influencer's own disclosure rather than technical telemetry.
ITID-23533.response: Support the influencer's disclosure and law enforcement reporting, issue a factual public clarification, and avoid publicly blaming the coerced influencer.
metrics: Reach of the coerced content
Time to public clarification
ITID-23533.notes: This is a human coercion event with no adversary network-intrusion technique; MITRE mapping is intentionally empty. Distinguished from ITID-23532 by the influencer's own knowing (if unwilling) control of their account throughout.

playbook.name: Response: Coerced/Blackmailed Influencer Negative Content Campaign
playbook.description: For an influencer posting negative content about the organization because they have been coerced or blackmailed by a third party into doing so.

steps.title: Understand the situation and confirm coercion
steps.desc: If the influencer or their representative discloses coercion, gather what details they are willing to share about the threat and content they were forced to post.
steps.guidance: Approach the influencer with support and confidentiality, not suspicion — they are a victim in this scenario.
steps.outcome: Coercion understood to the extent the influencer is willing to disclose.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and offer the influencer support resources
steps.desc: Notify Legal given the blackmail/extortion dimension, and offer the influencer access to support resources (legal referral, law enforcement contact) alongside the organization's own response.
steps.guidance: Providing support to the coerced influencer is a required part of the response, not optional.

steps.title: Address the false claims in the content
steps.desc: Publish a fact-based correction addressing any false claims in the coerced content, without placing blame on the influencer.

steps.title: Continue supporting the influencer through resolution
steps.desc: Maintain support for the influencer as the situation resolves, including any needed PR support for them.

steps.title: Document the incident with appropriate confidentiality
steps.desc: Record findings while protecting the influencer's privacy regarding the coercion details.

steps.title: Assess reach and business impact of the posted content
steps.desc: Determine how far the coerced content spread and its impact on brand perception.

steps.title: Coordinate with law enforcement if the influencer consents
steps.desc: With the influencer's consent, coordinate with law enforcement regarding the blackmail/coercion.
steps.outcome: Law enforcement engaged if the influencer consents.

ITID-23534.def: An incident in which a third party deceives an influencer — through a false pretext, fabricated documents, or a misleading briefing — into believing false claims about the company are true, leading the influencer to unknowingly and in good faith produce negative coverage.
ITID-23534.purpose: Captures the brand impact when an influencer is deceived through a false pretext into producing negative coverage of the company.
scopeIncludes: Negative influencer content produced in good faith based on a confirmed false pretext or fabricated briefing supplied by a third party
Corrective outreach to the deceived influencer with accurate information
scopeExcludes: Knowing, paid participation in spreading disinformation (ITID-23531)
Coercion/blackmail of an influencer who knows the claims are false (ITID-23533)
ITID-23534.severity: Medium, escalating to High if the influencer has substantial reach and is slow to correct once informed.
ITID-23534.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 for high-reach influencers or slow correction after outreach.
ITID-23534.escalation: Escalate to communications for direct, good-faith outreach to the influencer with corrective information and evidence.
indicators: Influencer content citing a specific fabricated document, briefing, or claim not matching company records
Influencer's own account of having received a specific outreach or pitch containing the false claims
vectors: Fabricated press release, document, or briefing provided to the influencer under a false pretext
rootCauses: The deceiving party's motivation (competitive, ideological, or personal grievance) against the company
Insufficient fact-checking by the influencer before publishing
controls: Proactive media/influencer relations to establish trusted fact-checking channels
Rapid corrective-information outreach process for good-faith deceived parties
ITID-23534.detection: Detection relies on social listening and direct engagement with the influencer rather than technical telemetry.
ITID-23534.response: Provide the deceived influencer with clear corrective evidence promptly and in good faith, expecting cooperative correction once informed.
metrics: Time from outreach to influencer correction/retraction
Reach of the original content versus the correction
ITID-23534.notes: This is a deception/PR event with no adversary network-intrusion technique; MITRE mapping is intentionally empty. Distinguished from ITID-23531 by the influencer's good-faith, unknowing participation.

playbook.name: Response: Deceptive Influencer Outreach (False Pretext for Negative Coverage)
playbook.description: For an individual posing as a journalist, partner, or other legitimate contact to deceptively obtain material later used to produce negative influencer coverage of the organization.

steps.title: Identify the deceptive outreach and what was obtained
steps.desc: Determine who was contacted under false pretenses, what information or material was provided to the deceptive party, and how it was subsequently used.
steps.outcome: Deceptive outreach and obtained material identified.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and PR/Comms
steps.desc: Notify Legal/PR/Comms given potential fraud/deceptive-practices implications and to prepare a response.

steps.title: Publish a fact-based response addressing misrepresentation
steps.desc: Issue a factual correction addressing how the material was misrepresented, without escalating into a broader dispute.

steps.title: Pursue remedies as directed by Legal
steps.desc: Execute Legal's determined course of action if the deceptive outreach and its use rise to an actionable level.

steps.title: Document the incident and update media-inquiry handling guidance
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend improved verification procedures for media/partner outreach.

steps.title: Assess the resulting negative coverage's accuracy
steps.desc: Independently determine whether the resulting coverage misrepresents the obtained material or organization's position.

steps.title: Alert relevant personnel about the deceptive outreach pattern
steps.desc: Warn employees (especially those handling media/partner inquiries) about the specific pretext used, to prevent further deceptive outreach from succeeding.

ITID-23535.def: A confirmed or suspected instance of influencer-driven negative content about the company that has not yet been attributed to a specific mechanism (undisclosed paid sponsorship, account compromise, coercion, or deceptive pretext).
ITID-23535.purpose: Catch-all for targeted influencer manipulation incidents that do not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to attribute the specific mechanism
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf (ITID-23531 through ITID-23534)
ITID-23535.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Medium pending scoping.
ITID-23535.priority: P2 by default, escalating upon confirmation of the specific mechanism and reach.
ITID-23535.escalation: Escalate to communications for preliminary assessment while investigation continues; reclassify once the specific pattern is clarified.
indicators: Negative influencer content of unclear origin or mechanism
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
ITID-23535.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-23535.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-23535.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one; reclassify to ITID-23531 through ITID-23534 as soon as the mechanism is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Targeted Influencer Manipulation
playbook.description: For a targeted influencer manipulation incident that does not clearly fit a specific mechanism category (paid disinformation, account compromise, coercion, deceptive outreach).

steps.title: Identify the influencer content and the manipulation mechanism
steps.desc: Catalog the negative content and investigate how the influencer was manipulated into producing/posting it, to enable reclassification if a more specific category applies.
steps.guidance: Approach the influencer collaboratively where contact is possible — they may be a victim rather than a willing participant.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and PR/Comms
steps.desc: Notify Legal/PR/Comms to assess implications and coordinate response.

steps.title: Publish a fact-based response
steps.desc: Issue a factual correction addressing false claims; reclassify to a specific ITID playbook if the mechanism becomes clear.
steps.outcome: Corrective content published or incident reclassified.

steps.title: Monitor for continued impact
steps.desc: Continue monitoring to confirm the situation has resolved.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings for future reference and classification refinement.

steps.title: Assess reach and business impact
steps.desc: Determine how far the content spread and its impact on brand perception.

steps.title: Support the influencer as appropriate
steps.desc: Offer support to the influencer if they appear to be a victim of the manipulation rather than a willing participant.

ITID-23611.def: An incident in which a ransomware group's ransom note — discovered on encrypted systems at the moment of attack — explicitly threatens to publish stolen data if payment demands are not met, distinct from any later direct extortion communication channel or confirmed data publication.
ITID-23611.purpose: Captures the brand and negotiation-response impact of the ransom note itself, left on encrypted systems, threatening future publication of stolen data.
scopeIncludes: The initial ransom note content and its data-publication threat, discovered on company systems
Immediate triage of the threat's credibility and initial negotiation-team activation
scopeExcludes: The ransomware intrusion and encryption mechanics themselves (ITID-31131 through ITID-31144)
Subsequent direct communication via a dedicated extortion email/negotiation portal (ITID-23612)
Confirmed publication or sample-data proof of the threatened data (ITID-23613, ITID-23115)
ITID-23611.severity: Critical, given the combined encryption and data-publication threat.
ITID-23611.priority: P1 immediately upon discovery of the ransom note.
ITID-23611.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive leadership, legal, law enforcement liaison, and the ransomware incident response team as a whole.
indicators: Ransom note file discovered on encrypted endpoints referencing data theft and publication threat
Note directing the victim to a negotiation portal or communication channel
vectors: Ransom note dropped as part of the encryption payload's final-stage execution
rootCauses: Successful ransomware intrusion and encryption (root cause owned by the ransomware ITID family)
controls: Endpoint detection and response with ransomware-note detection signatures
Pre-negotiated ransomware incident response retainer
ITID-23611.detection: Endpoint detection tooling reliably surfaces ransom note artifacts once encryption has occurred.
ITID-23611.response: Activate the full ransomware incident response process, assess the credibility of the data-theft claim, and begin parallel technical containment and negotiation-strategy planning.
metrics: Time from note discovery to full incident response activation
ITID-23611.notes: Scoped to the discovery and immediate triage of the ransom note's data-publication threat specifically; the encryption/intrusion mechanics belong to the ransomware ITID family, and confirmed data publication is tracked under sibling leaves to avoid double-counting the same incident at multiple stages.

playbook.name: Response: Ransom Note Left on Encrypted Systems Threatening Data Publication
playbook.description: For a ransomware incident where the ransom note left on encrypted systems explicitly threatens to publish exfiltrated data if the ransom is not paid.

steps.title: Verify the threat's credibility — is there actual evidence of data access?
steps.desc: Work with the IR team handling the underlying ransomware intrusion to determine whether attacker access to sensitive data can be confirmed (via forensic evidence of exfiltration) or whether the exposure threat may be a bluff.
steps.guidance: Many ransomware groups claim exfiltration as a bluff to increase pressure — do not assume the threat is credible without forensic corroboration.
steps.outcome: Threat credibility assessed based on available forensic evidence.
steps.tool: IR forensics findings / network egress logs

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Law Enforcement immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal and Law Enforcement per standard ransomware engagement protocol.
steps.guidance: Standard guidance is against paying extortion demands; any negotiation decision is Legal/Executive-level, not SOC-level.

steps.title: Complete full eradication and remediate the initial access vector
steps.desc: Ensure attacker presence is fully eradicated and the initial access vector is closed.
steps.outcome: Attacker presence eradicated; root cause closed.

steps.title: Execute regulatory and customer notification per Legal's determination
steps.desc: If exfiltration is confirmed, send required notifications on the legally mandated timeline.

steps.title: Document the incident and update ransomware readiness
steps.desc: Record the timeline, threat credibility assessment, and response effectiveness for future ransomware readiness.

steps.title: Scope what data may have been exfiltrated if the threat is credible
steps.desc: If evidence supports exfiltration, determine what data categories and volume are at risk of publication.

steps.title: Confirm the underlying intrusion is fully contained
steps.desc: Verify with the IR team that attacker access has been eradicated, not just that encryption has stopped.
steps.outcome: Confirmed containment of the source intrusion.

ITID-23612.def: An incident in which a threat actor establishes a direct communication channel (email address, dedicated negotiation portal/website) to negotiate payment under threat of publishing stolen data, distinct from the initial ransom note or confirmed publication itself.
ITID-23612.purpose: Captures the negotiation-response impact of direct extortion communication via a dedicated email address or negotiation portal threatening data publication.
scopeIncludes: Ongoing negotiation communications via a dedicated extortion channel
Assessment of communication authenticity and negotiation-strategy decisions
scopeExcludes: The initial ransom note discovery (ITID-23611)
Sample data proof attached to the communication as leverage (ITID-23613)
ITID-23612.severity: Critical while active negotiation is underway with a credible data-publication threat.
ITID-23612.priority: P1 for the duration of active negotiation.
ITID-23612.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership, legal, and law enforcement liaison; ensure a single authorized negotiation channel to avoid conflicting communications with the threat actor.
indicators: Email or portal communication from a threat actor referencing stolen data and payment demands
Negotiation portal accessible via credentials provided in the ransom note
vectors: Dedicated negotiation infrastructure (portal, anonymous email) operated by the threat actor
rootCauses: Successful ransomware intrusion and exfiltration preceding the negotiation (root cause owned by the ransomware ITID family)
controls: Pre-negotiated ransomware negotiation expertise/retainer
Single-channel negotiation communication discipline
ITID-23612.detection: Detection relies on the communication itself rather than technical telemetry; negotiation-portal access can be logged if company-side tooling permits.
ITID-23612.response: Maintain a single authorized negotiation channel, document all communications for legal/law-enforcement record, and coordinate strategy with executive leadership.
metrics: Duration of active negotiation
Number of communications exchanged
ITID-23612.notes: Scoped to the ongoing negotiation-communication stage specifically, distinct from the initial note discovery and any later data-publication confirmation, to keep each stage of the same incident separately trackable without duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Direct Extortion Email/Portal Threatening Data Publication
playbook.description: For a direct extortion communication (email or dedicated extortion portal) threatening to publish organizational data unless a demand is met, without an accompanying ransomware/encryption event.

steps.title: Verify the threat's credibility — is there actual proof of data access?
steps.desc: Examine any sample data or proof provided in the communication against known organizational data to assess whether the claim is genuine or a bluff.
steps.guidance: Do not engage directly with the extortionist to 'test' their claims — verify independently first.
steps.abort: If no credible evidence of data access is found, treat as an unverified/likely bluff extortion attempt.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Law Enforcement immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal and Law Enforcement; standard guidance is against paying extortion demands, and law enforcement engagement is important regardless of payment decision.
steps.guidance: Do not respond to the extortionist without Legal's guidance.

steps.title: Close any confirmed access vector
steps.desc: If a corroborating intrusion is found, close the access vector and remediate the root cause.

steps.title: Execute notifications per Legal's determination if data exposure is confirmed
steps.desc: Send required regulatory/customer notifications if the threat is substantiated.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the timeline, threat credibility assessment, and response effectiveness.

steps.title: Investigate for a corresponding intrusion
steps.desc: Check for any evidence of unauthorized access or exfiltration that would corroborate the extortion claim.
steps.outcome: Corroborating intrusion evidence found or ruled out.

steps.title: Preserve the extortion communication as evidence
steps.desc: Preserve the original email/portal communication, headers, and any artifacts for law enforcement and forensic use.

ITID-23613.def: An incident in which a threat actor provides a sample of the stolen data (a small file set or screenshot cache) as proof of the theft, to substantiate a double-extortion threat and increase pressure to pay.
ITID-23613.purpose: Captures the brand and disclosure impact when a ransomware group attaches sample stolen data as proof to strengthen a double-extortion threat.
scopeIncludes: Provision of verifiable sample data as extortion leverage, and the company's forensic verification of its authenticity and scope
Assessment of disclosure obligations triggered by confirmed data-theft proof
scopeExcludes: The ransom note or negotiation communication without attached proof (ITID-23611, ITID-23612)
Full data publication on a leak site (ITID-23115, ITID-23611 through ITID-23615's Unclassified catch-all for confirmed exposure)
ITID-23613.severity: Critical, since verified sample data materially raises confidence that a real breach occurred and disclosure obligations likely apply.
ITID-23613.priority: P1 immediately upon receipt of sample data proof.
ITID-23613.escalation: Escalate to legal and privacy for disclosure-obligation assessment as soon as sample authenticity is confirmed, in parallel with continued negotiation.
indicators: Sample data file or screenshot cache provided by the threat actor matching known internal document formats/content
Forensic confirmation that sample data originates from company systems
vectors: Pre-encryption data staging and exfiltration by the ransomware affiliate, with a subset released as proof
rootCauses: Successful ransomware intrusion and exfiltration preceding the extortion (root cause owned by the ransomware ITID family)
controls: Forensic sample-verification process
Pre-negotiated legal/privacy rapid-response for confirmed data-theft proof
ITID-23613.detection: Forensic verification of the sample against internal records provides the primary confirmation signal for this leaf.
ITID-23613.response: Verify sample authenticity and scope promptly, and begin disclosure-obligation assessment in parallel with continued negotiation.
metrics: Time from sample receipt to authenticity confirmation
Time to disclosure-obligation determination
ITID-23613.notes: Scoped to the sample-proof stage specifically, which is the point at which disclosure obligations typically become clear even before full publication; kept distinct from the note/negotiation stage and from confirmed full publication.

playbook.name: Response: Double-Extortion Threat with Sample Data Proof Attached
playbook.description: For a double-extortion threat (ransomware or standalone extortion) that includes attached sample data as proof of access, elevating the credibility of the claim.

steps.title: Verify the attached sample data's authenticity
steps.desc: Confirm the attached sample corresponds to genuine, current organizational data rather than recycled data from another source or a fabricated sample.
steps.guidance: Given a sample is attached, credibility assessment should move quickly but must still be rigorous.
steps.abort: If the sample cannot be verified as genuine, treat with appropriate caution but do not fully dismiss given the elevated credibility of a sample-backed claim.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Law Enforcement immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal and Law Enforcement given the elevated credibility of the threat; standard guidance is against paying extortion demands.

steps.title: Complete full eradication and remediate the initial access vector
steps.desc: Ensure attacker presence is fully eradicated and the initial access vector is closed.
steps.outcome: Attacker presence eradicated; root cause closed.

steps.title: Execute regulatory and customer notification per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications on the legally mandated timeline given the credible evidence of exfiltration.

steps.title: Document the incident and update ransomware/extortion readiness
steps.desc: Record the timeline and response effectiveness for future readiness.

steps.title: Scope what data the sample suggests was fully exfiltrated
steps.desc: Use the sample and any corroborating forensic evidence to estimate the full scope of data likely taken.
steps.outcome: Scope of likely exfiltrated data estimated.

steps.title: Confirm the underlying intrusion is fully contained
steps.desc: Verify that attacker access has been eradicated, not just that any encryption has stopped.
steps.outcome: Confirmed containment of the source intrusion.

ITID-23614.def: An incident in which a threat actor combines the standard data-publication extortion threat with an active or threatened distributed denial-of-service attack and a threat to directly notify the company's customers, partners, or regulators, compounding pressure across three simultaneous vectors.
ITID-23614.purpose: Captures the brand and operational impact when a ransomware group escalates to triple extortion, combining data exposure threats with DDoS and third-party notification threats.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed or credibly threatened combination of data-exposure threat, DDoS action/threat, and third-party notification threat as a single coordinated extortion campaign
Cross-functional response spanning security operations (DDoS), legal/privacy (notification threat), and negotiation (data threat)
scopeExcludes: A data-publication threat without the additional DDoS or notification-threat components (ITID-23611 through ITID-23613)
A standalone DDoS extortion incident with no data-theft component (tracked under the relevant DDoS/RDoS ITID)
ITID-23614.severity: Critical, given the compounding operational, brand, and regulatory pressure across three simultaneous vectors.
ITID-23614.priority: P1 for the duration of the active triple-extortion campaign.
ITID-23614.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership, legal, security operations, and communications simultaneously; coordinate a unified response spanning all three threat vectors rather than treating them separately.
indicators: Extortion communication explicitly threatening DDoS and third-party notification in addition to data publication
Observed DDoS activity coinciding with an active data-extortion negotiation
Threat actor providing evidence of drafted notification messages intended for customers/regulators
vectors: Coordinated use of a DDoS-for-hire service alongside data-theft extortion by the same actor or affiliate group
rootCauses: Successful ransomware/data-theft intrusion preceding the extortion (root cause owned by the ransomware ITID family)
Availability of low-cost DDoS-for-hire services as an additional pressure tool
controls: DDoS mitigation/scrubbing service
Pre-negotiated legal/privacy rapid-response for notification threats
Ransomware negotiation expertise/retainer
ITID-23614.detection: Network-layer DDoS monitoring plus the extortion communication itself provide the combined detection surface for this leaf.
ITID-23614.response: Activate DDoS mitigation, verify the credibility of the notification threat with legal, and manage negotiation strategy across all three vectors in a unified incident command structure.
metrics: Duration of the triple-extortion campaign
DDoS mitigation effectiveness (uptime maintained during the campaign)
ITID-23614.notes: Scoped to the compounded, multi-vector extortion pattern specifically; a standalone DDoS-only extortion incident with no data-theft component is tracked under the relevant DDoS/RDoS ITID rather than here.

playbook.name: Response: Triple-Extortion Threat (Data Exposure + DDoS + Notification Threat)
playbook.description: For a triple-extortion threat combining a data exposure threat, an active or threatened DDoS attack, and a threat to notify regulators/customers/media directly if the demand is unmet.

steps.title: Verify the data exposure threat's credibility
steps.desc: Assess any provided sample data or corroborating forensic evidence to determine whether the data-access claim is genuine.

steps.title: Stand up cross-team coordination spanning SOC, PR, and Legal
steps.desc: Establish a coordinated response bridging SOC (handling the DDoS threat), and PR/Legal (handling the exposure and notification threat) so all three fronts are managed together rather than in silos.
steps.guidance: This cross-team coordination is essential given the multi-pronged nature of triple extortion — each team should have visibility into the others' status.
steps.outcome: Cross-team coordination established with clear ownership of each threat vector.

steps.title: Close any confirmed data-access vector
steps.desc: If a corroborating intrusion is found, close the access vector and remediate the root cause.

steps.title: Execute coordinated notifications per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required regulatory/customer notifications and any needed public statement, coordinated across Legal and PR, particularly given the attacker's own notification threat.
steps.outcome: Notifications sent as required, ahead of any attacker-driven disclosure where possible.

steps.title: Document the incident and update multi-vector extortion readiness
steps.desc: Record the timeline, cross-team coordination effectiveness, and response outcomes; recommend improvements to DDoS capacity and extortion playbooks.

steps.title: Confirm and characterize the DDoS component
steps.desc: Determine whether a DDoS attack is already underway or merely threatened, and assess its potential scale against current infrastructure capacity.
steps.outcome: DDoS status and potential impact characterized.

steps.title: Activate DDoS mitigation and confirm/preserve data exposure evidence
steps.desc: Engage DDoS mitigation services/capacity if an attack is active or imminent, while Legal preserves the extortion communications as evidence.
steps.guidance: Standard guidance is against paying extortion demands; Law Enforcement should also be engaged.

ITID-23615.def: A confirmed or suspected ransomware-linked threat to expose stolen data that has not yet been attributed to a specific stage (initial ransom note, direct negotiation communication, sample-proof provision, or triple-extortion escalation).
ITID-23615.purpose: Catch-all for ransomware data exposure threat incidents that do not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to attribute the specific stage of the extortion threat
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf (ITID-23611 through ITID-23614)
ITID-23615.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Critical by default given the ransomware context.
ITID-23615.priority: P1 by default pending scoping, given the ransomware context.
ITID-23615.escalation: Escalate to the full ransomware incident response team immediately; reclassify once the specific stage is clarified.
indicators: Ransomware-linked data-exposure threat of unclear stage
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
ITID-23615.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-23615.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed; treat as an active ransomware incident regardless of classification.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-23615.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one; reclassify to ITID-23611 through ITID-23614 as soon as the extortion stage is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Ransomware Data Exposure Threat
playbook.description: For a ransomware-related data exposure threat that does not clearly fit a specific category (ransom note, direct extortion, sample-backed threat, triple extortion).

steps.title: Verify the threat's credibility
steps.desc: Assess any provided evidence and corroborating forensic findings to determine whether the data-exposure claim is genuine or a bluff.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Law Enforcement immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal and Law Enforcement; standard guidance is against paying extortion demands.

steps.title: Complete eradication once mechanism is confirmed
steps.desc: Remediate the root cause; reclassify to a specific ITID playbook if one now clearly applies.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated or incident reclassified.

steps.title: Execute notifications per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications if data exposure is substantiated.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings for future reference and classification refinement.

steps.title: Determine the specific threat pattern to enable reclassification
steps.desc: Determine whether this matches a ransom note, direct extortion, sample-backed threat, or triple-extortion pattern.

steps.title: Confirm containment of any underlying intrusion
steps.desc: Verify with the IR team that any underlying intrusion is contained.

ITID-23621.def: An incident in which a threat actor obtains company data through means other than a ransomware/encryption attack (e.g., exploiting a vulnerability, database compromise, or purchasing stolen data from another source) and directly demands payment to prevent its publication, without any encryption having occurred.
ITID-23621.purpose: Captures the brand and disclosure impact of a pure data-blackmail extortion attempt against the company that involves no ransomware or encryption component.
scopeIncludes: Direct extortion demand tied to threatened publication of company data, with no ransomware/encryption event involved
Negotiation and disclosure-obligation response distinct from the ransomware-specific playbook
scopeExcludes: Any extortion threat following a confirmed ransomware/encryption event (ITID-23611 through ITID-23615)
Blackmail specifically targeting an individual executive's personal data (ITID-23622)
ITID-23621.severity: Critical, given the data-publication threat and associated disclosure obligations, independent of any encryption impact.
ITID-23621.priority: P1 immediately upon receipt of a credible extortion demand tied to company data.
ITID-23621.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership, legal, and law enforcement liaison; verify data authenticity before determining response and disclosure strategy.
indicators: Extortion communication demanding payment with no accompanying encryption/ransomware indicators
Sample data attached to substantiate the threat, sourced independently of any ransomware attack
vectors: Direct exploitation of a vulnerability to steal data followed by extortion demand
Purchase of previously stolen/leaked data by an opportunistic extortionist
rootCauses: The underlying data-theft vector (varies by case; verify and reference the applicable data-exposure ITID once known)
Absence of encryption capability/intent distinguishing this from a ransomware operation
controls: Forensic sample-verification process
Pre-negotiated legal/privacy rapid-response for extortion demands
ITID-23621.detection: Detection relies on the extortion communication itself plus forensic verification against internal records.
ITID-23621.response: Verify data authenticity, assess disclosure obligations with legal, and determine negotiation strategy independent of any ransomware playbook.
metrics: Time from demand receipt to authenticity verification
Time to disclosure-obligation determination
ITID-23621.notes: Explicitly scoped to exclude any ransomware/encryption component, distinguishing it from the Ransomware Data Exposure Type; if a ransomware event is later confirmed, reclassify to the appropriate ITID-2361x leaf.

playbook.name: Response: Corporate Data Blackmail (No Ransomware/Encryption Involved)
playbook.description: For blackmail threatening to publish stolen corporate data, where no ransomware or encryption event is involved (e.g. data obtained via a standalone breach or insider).

steps.title: Verify the threat's credibility — is there actual proof of data access?
steps.desc: Examine any sample data or proof provided against known organizational data to assess whether the claim is genuine.
steps.abort: If no credible evidence is found, treat as an unverified/likely bluff.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Law Enforcement immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal and Law Enforcement; standard guidance is against paying extortion demands.

steps.title: Close any confirmed access vector
steps.desc: If a corroborating access path is found, close it and remediate the root cause.

steps.title: Execute notifications per Legal's determination if data exposure is confirmed
steps.desc: Send required regulatory/customer notifications if the threat is substantiated.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the timeline, threat credibility assessment, and response effectiveness.

steps.title: Investigate how the data may have been obtained
steps.desc: Investigate for evidence of a breach, insider theft, or other access path that would corroborate the claim.
steps.outcome: Potential access path identified or ruled out.

steps.title: Preserve the blackmail communication as evidence
steps.desc: Preserve the original communication and any artifacts for law enforcement and forensic use.

ITID-23622.def: An incident in which a threat actor obtains an executive's or other individual's personal data (not general corporate data) and threatens to publish it, with the threat framed to pressure the company (e.g., reputational damage to the individual's public company role) rather than the company's systems or corporate data directly.
ITID-23622.purpose: Captures the brand and personal-safety impact when an executive or other individual is personally blackmailed using their own leaked personal data, in a way that implicates the company.
scopeIncludes: Personal-data blackmail targeting an executive or individual where the threat is framed to affect the company's reputation or the individual's company role
Coordination between personal legal counsel, company legal, and executive protection
scopeExcludes: Corporate data blackmail with no individual-personal-data component (ITID-23621)
Blackmail specifically threatening regulatory/customer notification of a corporate breach (ITID-23623)
ITID-23622.severity: Critical, given the personal-safety and reputational dimensions combined with potential corporate brand impact.
ITID-23622.priority: P1 immediately upon receipt of a credible personal-data blackmail threat referencing a company executive.
ITID-23622.escalation: Escalate to executive protection, legal, HR, and communications simultaneously; treat the affected individual's safety and well-being as the immediate priority alongside brand-risk assessment.
indicators: Blackmail communication targeting a named executive using personal data/material
Sample personal data or material provided to substantiate the threat
vectors: Compromise of the executive's personal accounts/devices (outside typical corporate IT boundary)
Physical or social engineering targeting of the executive's personal information
rootCauses: Insufficient personal digital-security support/training for high-profile executives
controls: Executive digital-security and personal-account protection program
Executive protection/personal-safety coordination process
ITID-23622.detection: Detection relies on the executive's own disclosure and the blackmail communication itself rather than corporate technical telemetry.
ITID-23622.response: Prioritize the individual's safety and well-being, engage law enforcement where appropriate, and manage brand risk separately from personal legal support.
metrics: Number of executive personal-data blackmail incidents per year
ITID-23622.notes: Distinguished from ITID-23621 by the personal (not corporate) data target and the added personal-safety dimension requiring executive-protection involvement.

playbook.name: Response: Executive/Individual Personal Data Blackmail
playbook.description: For blackmail targeting a specific executive or individual using their personal data (obtained via a breach of corporate or personal systems), threatening exposure unless a demand is met.

steps.title: Verify the threat's credibility with the affected individual's cooperation
steps.desc: With the affected individual's involvement, assess any provided proof to determine whether the claim is genuine.
steps.guidance: Handle with discretion and support for the targeted individual throughout.

steps.title: Loop in Legal, HR/Executive Protection, and Law Enforcement immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal, HR/Executive Protection, and Law Enforcement; standard guidance is against paying extortion demands.
steps.outcome: Relevant teams engaged; support provided to the individual.

steps.title: Close any confirmed corporate access vector
steps.desc: If the data was obtained via a corporate system, close the access vector and remediate the root cause.

steps.title: Support the individual through resolution and manage disclosure per Legal's guidance
steps.desc: Continue supporting the individual and manage any needed organizational disclosure per Legal's direction.

steps.title: Document the incident with appropriate confidentiality
steps.desc: Record findings while protecting the individual's privacy, and review executive personal-security protections.

steps.title: Investigate how the personal data may have been obtained
steps.desc: Determine whether the data came from a corporate system breach, a personal account compromise, or another source.

steps.title: Secure the individual's accounts and preserve evidence
steps.desc: Assist the individual in securing personal/corporate accounts and preserve the blackmail communication as evidence.

ITID-23623.def: An incident in which a threat actor's primary extortion leverage is not the data publication itself but the threat to directly notify regulators or customers of a breach ahead of or instead of the company's own controlled disclosure process, aiming to maximize reputational and regulatory pressure.
ITID-23623.purpose: Captures the brand impact when a threat actor's extortion leverage is specifically the threat to force a regulatory or customer notification the company would otherwise not yet be required to make.
scopeIncludes: Extortion demand where the stated or implied threat is direct third-party (regulator/customer) notification by the threat actor
Assessment of whether the actor's threatened notification would be more damaging than the company's own controlled disclosure, and adjustment of disclosure timeline accordingly
scopeExcludes: General data-publication threats without a specific notification-timing angle (ITID-23621)
Personal blackmail of an individual executive (ITID-23622)
ITID-23623.severity: Critical, given the direct pressure on the company's disclosure timeline and control over its own narrative.
ITID-23623.priority: P1 immediately upon receipt of a threat specifically invoking regulator/customer notification.
ITID-23623.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal and privacy to accelerate the company's own disclosure assessment; consider proactively notifying regulators/customers ahead of the actor to retain narrative control.
indicators: Extortion communication explicitly threatening to notify regulators or customers directly
Threat actor referencing specific regulatory notification deadlines (e.g., GDPR 72-hour window) as leverage
vectors: Data theft (mechanism to be confirmed and cross-referenced to the relevant data-exposure ITID) followed by notification-timing-focused extortion
rootCauses: The underlying data-theft vector (varies by case)
Threat actor's understanding of regulatory notification deadlines as an additional pressure lever
controls: Accelerated disclosure-decision process for extortion scenarios
Pre-negotiated legal/privacy rapid-response for notification-timing threats
ITID-23623.detection: Detection relies on the extortion communication itself plus forensic verification against internal records.
ITID-23623.response: Accelerate the company's own disclosure assessment and consider proactive notification to retain control of the narrative ahead of the threat actor.
metrics: Time from threat receipt to disclosure decision
Whether company notification preceded or followed any actor-initiated notification
ITID-23623.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves by the specific notification-timing extortion angle, which drives an accelerated-disclosure response distinct from standard negotiation.

playbook.name: Response: Blackmail Threatening Regulatory/Customer Notification Disclosure
playbook.description: For blackmail that threatens to notify regulators or customers directly about a data exposure unless a demand is met, using the organization's own notification obligations as leverage.

steps.title: Verify the threat's credibility — is there actual proof of data access?
steps.desc: Examine any sample data or proof provided to assess whether the underlying exposure claim is genuine.
steps.abort: If no credible evidence is found, treat as an unverified/likely bluff, though the notification threat itself should still be tracked.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Law Enforcement immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal and Law Enforcement; standard guidance is against paying extortion demands, and the notification threat should not change that guidance.
steps.guidance: Do not let the notification threat pressure a payment decision — proceed with the standard non-payment stance and prepare for the notification regardless.

steps.title: Close any confirmed access vector
steps.desc: If a corroborating access path is found, close it and remediate the root cause.

steps.title: Proactively execute the organization's own notification ahead of the attacker's threat
steps.desc: If notification is independently warranted, execute it on the organization's own timeline per Legal's determination, rather than waiting to be forced by the attacker.
steps.guidance: Getting ahead of the attacker's threatened disclosure is generally preferable from a trust and narrative-control standpoint.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the timeline, threat credibility assessment, and response effectiveness.

steps.title: Determine whether notification would be independently required regardless of the threat
steps.desc: Work with Legal/Privacy to assess whether the underlying exposure, if genuine, would trigger notification obligations on its own merits.

steps.title: Preserve the blackmail communication as evidence
steps.desc: Preserve the original communication and any artifacts for law enforcement and forensic use.

ITID-23624.def: A confirmed or suspected blackmail attempt using leaked or stolen company-related data that has not yet been attributed to a specific pattern (pure corporate blackmail, executive personal-data blackmail, or notification-timing-focused blackmail).
ITID-23624.purpose: Catch-all for blackmail-with-leaked-data incidents that do not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to attribute the specific blackmail pattern
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf (ITID-23621 through ITID-23623)
ITID-23624.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Critical by default given the blackmail context.
ITID-23624.escalation: Escalate to legal immediately for preliminary risk assessment; reclassify once the specific pattern is clarified.
indicators: Blackmail communication of unclear target or leverage pattern
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
ITID-23624.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-23624.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-23624.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one; reclassify to ITID-23621 through ITID-23623 as soon as the blackmail pattern is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Blackmail with Leaked Data
playbook.description: For a blackmail-with-leaked-data incident that does not clearly fit a specific category (corporate blackmail, executive/personal blackmail, notification-threat blackmail).

steps.title: Verify the threat's credibility
steps.desc: Assess any provided evidence to determine whether the data-access claim is genuine.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Law Enforcement immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal and Law Enforcement; standard guidance is against paying extortion demands.

steps.title: Close any confirmed access vector once mechanism is understood
steps.desc: Remediate the root cause; reclassify to a specific ITID playbook if one now clearly applies.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated or incident reclassified.

steps.title: Execute notifications per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications if data exposure is substantiated.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings for future reference and classification refinement.

steps.title: Determine the specific blackmail pattern to enable reclassification
steps.desc: Determine whether this matches corporate blackmail, executive/personal blackmail, or notification-threat blackmail.

steps.title: Preserve the blackmail communication as evidence
steps.desc: Preserve the original communication and any artifacts for law enforcement and forensic use.

ITID-23631.def: An incident in which a threat actor conducts a sustained, public social media campaign making threats against the company (operational disruption, further attacks, reputational harm) intended to intimidate or extort, without necessarily holding stolen data as leverage.
ITID-23631.purpose: Captures the brand impact of a public threat campaign conducted openly via social media against the organization, without a targeted data-blackmail component.
scopeIncludes: Sustained public social media threat campaign against the company, visible to the general public
Communications and security-operations response to assess credibility and public exposure
scopeExcludes: Threats made via direct private communication to customers or employees rather than public posting (ITID-23632)
Threats made specifically through press/media outreach rather than the actor's own social media presence (ITID-23633)
Threats where stolen data is the primary leverage (ITID-23611 through ITID-23624)
ITID-23631.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High if the campaign includes specific, credible operational threats or gains significant public attention.
ITID-23631.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 for credible operational threats or high public visibility.
ITID-23631.escalation: Escalate to security operations for credibility assessment, and to communications for public response planning.
indicators: Threat actor social media account publicly posting threats against the company
Escalating public post frequency or specificity of threats over a sustained period
rootCauses: Threat actor's ideological, financial, or personal grievance motivation against the company
controls: Social/dark-web monitoring for brand-directed threats
Threat credibility assessment process involving security and legal
ITID-23631.detection: Social listening and dark-web monitoring provide the primary detection surface for this leaf; there is no adversary network-intrusion technique unless a technical compromise is separately confirmed.
ITID-23631.response: Assess threat credibility, involve law enforcement for credible threats, and prepare a measured public response.
metrics: Duration and reach of the public threat campaign
Time to credibility assessment
detections: Social/dark-web monitoring alerting for brand-directed threats
ITID-23631.notes: Scoped to public, non-data-leverage threat campaigns; if stolen data becomes the primary leverage, reclassify to the appropriate Ransomware Data Exposure or Blackmail leaf.

playbook.name: Response: Public Social Media Threat Campaign Against Organization
playbook.description: For a public threat campaign conducted openly on social media against the organization (as distinct from a private extortion demand), such as public threats of harm, data exposure, or disruption.

steps.title: Catalog the threats and assess credibility
steps.desc: Document the specific threats being made publicly and assess their credibility, including whether the actor has demonstrated capability (e.g. prior verified attacks) or appears to be making empty threats.
steps.tool: Social media monitoring tool / threat intelligence platform

steps.title: Loop in Legal, PR/Comms, and Physical Security/Law Enforcement as applicable
steps.desc: Notify Legal/PR/Comms and, if any physical safety component exists, Physical Security and Law Enforcement.

steps.title: Address any underlying vulnerability referenced in the threats
steps.desc: If the threats reference specific vulnerabilities or access, investigate and remediate if substantiated.

steps.title: Issue a measured public/employee communication if warranted
steps.desc: Coordinate with PR/Comms and HR to issue any needed reassurance communication to employees or the public.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings and response effectiveness for future reference.

steps.title: Assess whether the threat corresponds to any physical safety risk
steps.desc: Determine whether the threats include any physical safety component (e.g. threats against facilities or personnel) requiring immediate physical security involvement.

steps.title: Report the threatening content to the platform
steps.desc: File reports with the relevant social media platform citing their threats/violence policies.

ITID-23632.def: An incident in which a threat actor directly contacts company customers or employees (via email, text, or phone) with threats intended to intimidate, extort, or damage the company's relationship with those individuals.
ITID-23632.purpose: Captures the brand and safety impact when a threat actor sends threat communications directly to the company's customers or employees rather than posting publicly.
scopeIncludes: Direct threat communications sent to customers or employees referencing the company
Coordination of customer/employee notification and safety response
scopeExcludes: Public social media threat campaigns not directly targeting individual customers/employees (ITID-23631)
Press/media outreach threatening exposure (ITID-23633)
ITID-23632.severity: High to Critical, given the direct personal-safety and customer-trust dimensions of threats reaching individuals directly.
ITID-23632.priority: P1 upon confirmation of direct threat communications reaching customers or employees at scale, or any threat involving physical safety.
ITID-23632.escalation: Escalate immediately to security, legal, HR/customer support, and law enforcement liaison; prioritize physical-safety assessment for any threat with a safety dimension.
indicators: Customer or employee reports of receiving threatening communications referencing the company
Pattern of similar threat messages sent to multiple individuals, indicating a coordinated campaign
vectors: Use of a stolen or leaked customer/employee contact list to distribute threat communications at scale
Direct targeted contact using data obtained from a prior breach
rootCauses: An underlying data exposure providing the contact list used for targeting (cross-reference the relevant Customer or Employee Data Exposure leaf)
controls: Customer/employee incident communication and support process
Coordination with law enforcement for threats involving physical safety
ITID-23632.detection: Detection relies on customer/employee self-reporting rather than internal technical telemetry, unless the contact list itself was obtained via a confirmed breach.
ITID-23632.response: Notify and support affected customers/employees promptly, involve law enforcement for safety-related threats, and cross-reference any underlying data breach that supplied contact information.
metrics: Number of individuals reporting receipt of threat communications
Time to notification/support response
ITID-23632.notes: Where the threat actor used a stolen contact list from a confirmed data breach, that breach is tracked under its own Customer/Employee Data Exposure leaf and cross-referenced rather than re-described here.

playbook.name: Response: Direct Threat Communication to Customers/Employees
playbook.description: For threats communicated directly to the organization's customers or employees (rather than made publicly), such as threatening emails referencing stolen data or intended harm.

steps.title: Collect and assess the direct threat communications
steps.desc: Gather reports from affected customers/employees and assess the threats' content, scope of recipients, and credibility.
steps.outcome: Threat communications collected; scope and credibility assessed.

steps.title: Loop in Legal, HR, Customer Success, and Law Enforcement as applicable
steps.desc: Notify Legal/HR/Customer Success and, if the threats are credible or involve safety risk, Law Enforcement.

steps.title: Investigate and close any confirmed data-access vector
steps.desc: If genuine stolen data is confirmed, investigate the source breach and remediate.

steps.title: Execute notifications per Legal's determination if a breach is confirmed
steps.desc: Send required regulatory/customer notifications if the underlying data theft is substantiated.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings and response effectiveness for future reference.

steps.title: Determine if the threats reference genuine stolen data
steps.desc: Assess whether any data referenced in the threats (e.g. personal details used to lend credibility) is genuine, indicating an actual prior breach.

steps.title: Notify affected customers/employees with guidance
steps.desc: Provide affected recipients with guidance on the threats and available support/reporting channels.

ITID-23633.def: An incident in which a threat actor reaches out to journalists or media outlets directly, threatening to provide them with damaging information about the company unless demands are met, using media exposure itself as the extortion lever.
ITID-23633.purpose: Captures the brand impact when a threat actor contacts press or media outlets directly, threatening to expose the company as leverage.
scopeIncludes: Threat actor outreach to media/journalists threatening exposure as extortion leverage
Coordination with communications to manage media relationships and prepare for potential coverage
scopeExcludes: Public social media threat campaigns not specifically directed at media outlets (ITID-23631)
Direct threats to customers/employees rather than the press (ITID-23632)
