ITID-23633.severity: High, given the risk of the threat actor successfully placing damaging coverage regardless of whether demands are met.
ITID-23633.priority: P1 upon confirmation that a threat actor has contacted media with an exposure threat.
ITID-23633.escalation: Escalate immediately to communications and legal; proactively engage relevant journalists with factual context to reduce the risk of one-sided coverage.
indicators: Journalist inquiry referencing an unsolicited tip from a threat actor threatening exposure
Threat actor's own communication referencing plans to contact media if demands are unmet
vectors: Threat actor directly emailing or contacting journalists with claims and sample material
rootCauses: An underlying data theft or compromise providing the material used as leverage (cross-reference the relevant data-exposure ITID)
controls: Proactive media relations and rapid-response communications process
Journalist relationship management to enable early factual engagement
ITID-23633.detection: Detection relies on journalist outreach for comment or the threat actor's own communication rather than technical telemetry.
ITID-23633.response: Engage proactively with contacted journalists to provide accurate context, and prepare a public statement in anticipation of potential coverage.
metrics: Time from threat-actor media outreach to company awareness
Whether coverage was published and its accuracy relative to company-provided context
ITID-23633.notes: Where the threat actor's leverage material originates from a confirmed data theft, that theft is tracked under its own data-exposure ITID and cross-referenced rather than re-described here.

playbook.name: Response: Press/Media Outreach Threatening Exposure
playbook.description: For a threat actor contacting press or media outlets directly, threatening to expose stolen data or damaging information to force the organization's hand.

steps.title: Confirm the media outreach and assess what was threatened
steps.desc: Determine which media outlet(s) were contacted and what specifically the threat actor claims to have and threatens to expose.
steps.guidance: Media contacts sometimes voluntarily inform the subject organization of such outreach — leverage any such relationship for early warning.

steps.title: Loop in Legal, PR/Comms, and Law Enforcement immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal/PR/Comms/Law Enforcement given the imminent media exposure risk; standard guidance is against paying extortion demands.

steps.title: Close any confirmed access vector
steps.desc: If a corroborating intrusion or leak source is found, close it and remediate the root cause.

steps.title: Execute proactive notification and press engagement per Legal's determination
steps.desc: If the claim is substantiated, proactively notify regulators/customers and engage transparently with the press rather than waiting to be forced.
steps.outcome: Notifications and press engagement executed as required.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the timeline, threat credibility assessment, and response effectiveness.

steps.title: Verify the threat's credibility
steps.desc: Assess any evidence provided to the media or to the organization to determine whether the underlying data-access claim is genuine.

steps.title: Prepare proactive media statement materials
steps.desc: Prepare a factual holding statement and, if the claim is substantiated, a fuller response in case the media outlet proceeds with publication.

ITID-23634.def: A confirmed or suspected public threat campaign against the company that has not yet been attributed to a specific channel (public social media, direct customer/employee communication, or press/media outreach).
ITID-23634.purpose: Catch-all for public threat campaign incidents that do not fit a more specific leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to attribute the specific threat-communication channel
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf (ITID-23631 through ITID-23633)
ITID-23634.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High pending scoping given the threat context.
ITID-23634.priority: P2 by default, escalating to P1 upon confirmation of a credible threat or safety dimension.
ITID-23634.escalation: Escalate to security and legal for preliminary credibility assessment while investigation continues; reclassify once the specific channel is clarified.
indicators: Threat communication against the company of unclear channel
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
ITID-23634.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-23634.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-23634.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one; reclassify to ITID-23631 through ITID-23633 as soon as the threat-communication channel is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Public Threat Campaign
playbook.description: For a public threat campaign incident that does not clearly fit a specific category (social media threat campaign, direct communication to customers/employees, press/media outreach).

steps.title: Catalog the threats and identify the channel used
steps.desc: Document the specific threats and how they were communicated, to enable reclassification if a more specific category applies.

steps.title: Loop in Legal and Law Enforcement immediately
steps.desc: Notify Legal and Law Enforcement; standard guidance is against paying extortion demands.

steps.title: Close any confirmed access vector once mechanism is understood
steps.desc: Remediate the root cause; reclassify to a specific ITID playbook if one now clearly applies.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated or incident reclassified.

steps.title: Execute notifications per Legal's determination
steps.desc: Send required notifications if the underlying claim is substantiated.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings for future reference and classification refinement.

steps.title: Verify the threat's credibility
steps.desc: Assess any evidence provided to determine whether the underlying claim is genuine.

steps.title: Preserve threat communications as evidence
steps.desc: Preserve the original communications and any artifacts for law enforcement and forensic use.

ITID-24111.def: A deliberate campaign in which a network of automated or fabricated accounts (no real purchase/usage history) floods a review platform with negative reviews of the organization's product or service to depress its rating and visibility.
ITID-24111.purpose: Captures a coordinated negative-review attack carried out through a network of bot or fake/sockpuppet accounts posting near-simultaneous negative reviews.
scopeIncludes: Multiple newly-created or sockpuppet accounts posting negative reviews within a compressed time window
Accounts sharing infrastructure fingerprints (IP ranges, device fingerprints, registration patterns) with no legitimate purchase/order record
scopeExcludes: Genuine but coordinated customer complaints following an actual product/service failure
ITID-23524 Review Bombing Campaign (press-narrative-driven review bombing following a media story, tracked under Public Relations Disruption)
Paid human click-farm workers (ITID-24112)
Compromised/purchased verified accounts used for the same purpose (ITID-24113)
ITID-24111.severity: Medium, escalating to High if the campaign meaningfully moves the aggregate public rating or triggers marketplace/app-store enforcement action against the organization.
ITID-24111.priority: P3, escalating to P2 for sustained multi-day campaigns or ones affecting a flagship listing.
ITID-24111.escalation: Escalate to brand/communications and the platform-relations team for takedown reporting; loop in legal if defamatory claims are embedded in the reviews.
indicators: Spike in negative reviews far exceeding normal review velocity
Reviewer accounts with no verified purchase, near-identical creation dates, or templated phrasing
Shared IP ranges/device fingerprints across many reviewer accounts
vectors: Bot-operated or scripted account creation at scale on the review platform
Sockpuppet accounts pre-seeded and aged to appear legitimate
rootCauses: No automated anomaly detection on review velocity/sentiment
No standing relationship with the platform's trust-and-safety team for expedited reporting
controls: Review-platform monitoring and sentiment/velocity anomaly alerting
Established platform abuse-reporting relationship with expedited escalation path
ITID-24111.detection: Detected via brand-monitoring/social-listening tools and platform-provided fake-engagement signals, not network telemetry; account-creation-pattern analysis is the closest technical signal available.
ITID-24111.response: Capture evidence (screenshots, account IDs, timestamps, fingerprint overlaps), submit a bulk policy-violation report to the platform, and brief communications on any external messaging needed.
metrics: Review-velocity anomaly count per quarter
Platform takedown success rate and time-to-removal
ITID-24111.notes: Differentiated from ITID-23524 (press-narrative-driven bombing under Public Relations Disruption) by mechanism: this leaf is scoped strictly to bot/sockpuppet account infrastructure on review platforms, not a press-triggered public backlash. Differentiated from sibling 24112/24113 by actor mechanism (automated fake accounts vs. paid humans vs. compromised/purchased verified accounts).

playbook.name: Response: Bot/Fake Account Network Negative Review Campaign
playbook.description: For a surge of negative reviews originating from a coordinated network of bot or fake accounts, rather than genuine dissatisfied customers.

steps.title: Quantify the review surge and pull the raw account list
steps.desc: Export the flagged reviews with timestamps, account handles, and any platform metadata available (account creation date, profile completeness, review history).
steps.outcome: Dataset of suspect reviews assembled for pattern analysis.

steps.title: Submit a bulk inauthentic-activity report to the platform(s)
steps.desc: File a report identifying the account network as fake/bot activity, with the evidence package from identification.
steps.guidance: Use the platform's dedicated fraudulent-review or fake-account reporting channel rather than disputing reviews individually.
steps.outcome: Report accepted and under platform review.

steps.title: Pursue removal through platform enforcement
steps.desc: Follow up on the report until the reviews/accounts are actioned; escalate through account management contacts if the platform is unresponsive.
steps.outcome: Fake reviews and/or accounts removed or annotated by the platform.
steps.abort: If the platform declines to act, document the decision and rating impact for ongoing monitoring.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence and rating recovery
steps.desc: Track overall rating trend and watch for a repeat wave from the same or a related account network.
steps.outcome: Rating stabilizes; no repeat activity from the same network.

steps.title: Document the bot pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the account signatures, timing pattern, and platform response time to speed up detection and reporting on any repeat campaign.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and shared with brand-protection stakeholders.

steps.title: Distinguish coordinated inauthenticity from a genuine viral complaint
steps.desc: Check for bot signatures: near-identical wording across reviews, unnatural posting velocity, accounts with no other activity, reviews posted in a tight time cluster, generic profile photos.
steps.guidance: This distinction is critical — if the underlying complaint is real and simply spreading organically, the correct response is a genuine customer-service fix, not a platform takedown request.
steps.outcome: Confident determination that the reviews are inauthentic and coordinated, with supporting evidence.
steps.abort: If the complaint reflects a real, verifiable issue, close this incident and route to Customer Service/Product for remediation instead.

steps.title: Flag the affected reviews internally and pause automated responses
steps.desc: Mark the suspect reviews in internal tracking so Customer Service does not respond to them as if genuine, avoiding wasted effort or accidental legitimization.
steps.outcome: Internal teams aware and not engaging with fake reviews individually.

steps.title: Map the scale and platform spread
steps.desc: Determine which platforms are affected and how many accounts/reviews are involved to size the response.
steps.outcome: Scope documented across all affected platforms.

ITID-24112.def: A campaign in which a paid human workforce (a click-farm or gig-labor pool) is directed to post negative reviews of the organization's product or service, typically via instructions distributed through a task-marketplace or messaging group.
ITID-24112.purpose: Captures a coordinated negative-review attack carried out by paid human click-farm workers rather than automated bots.
scopeIncludes: Reviews traceable to known click-farm labor pools or task-marketplace campaigns
Reviewer accounts with real human variability in phrasing but no genuine purchase/usage history
scopeExcludes: Automated bot/sockpuppet account campaigns (ITID-24111)
Compromised/purchased verified accounts (ITID-24113)
ITID-23524 Review Bombing Campaign (press-narrative-driven, different Tier-3 branch)
ITID-24112.severity: Medium, escalating to High for sustained campaigns affecting a flagship listing or triggering platform enforcement.
ITID-24112.priority: P3, escalating to P2 for high-volume or prolonged campaigns.
ITID-24112.escalation: Escalate to brand/communications and platform-relations for takedown; involve legal if the campaign can be traced to a specific paying party for potential civil action.
indicators: Batches of negative reviews with human-variable but similarly-structured phrasing
Reviewer accounts geographically clustered in known click-farm labor markets
Leaked or discovered task-marketplace job postings soliciting negative reviews
vectors: Task-marketplace gig postings soliciting paid negative reviews
Messaging-app group coordination of paid reviewers
rootCauses: No monitoring of reviewer geographic/behavioral clustering
No proactive scanning of task-marketplace platforms for campaigns targeting the brand
controls: Review-platform monitoring and sentiment-anomaly alerting
Periodic scanning of task-marketplace/gig platforms for brand-targeting job postings
ITID-24112.detection: Relies on brand-monitoring tools and manual investigation of reviewer clustering; no network/technical detection surface since paid humans, not malware or bots, are executing the posts.
ITID-24112.response: Document reviewer clustering evidence, report to the platform, and where a task-marketplace posting is discovered, report it to that marketplace's abuse team as well.
metrics: Count of click-farm-attributed reviews identified per quarter
Platform takedown success rate
ITID-24112.notes: No MITRE mapping applies — paid human labor, not adversary infrastructure or malware. Differentiated from sibling 24111 (bots) and 24113 (compromised/purchased verified accounts) by the human-labor-market mechanism.

playbook.name: Response: Paid Click-Farm Negative Review Campaign
playbook.description: For negative reviews traced to a paid click-farm — workers hired at scale to post reviews on demand rather than automated bots.

steps.title: Collect the suspect reviews and behavioral evidence
steps.desc: Export reviews showing click-farm indicators: shared IP ranges/geolocation clustering, similar device fingerprints if available, reviews posted in short bursts by accounts with sparse but real-looking profiles.
steps.outcome: Evidence set assembled distinguishing this from a single disgruntled customer or bot script.

steps.title: Report the account cluster to the platform
steps.desc: Submit a fake-review report highlighting the shared behavioral/technical patterns identified.
steps.outcome: Report filed and acknowledged by the platform.

steps.title: Pursue takedown and consider terms-of-service/legal follow-up
steps.desc: Track the platform's removal action; if the click-farm operator is identifiable, consider a cease-and-desist for violating the platform's terms of service.
steps.guidance: Loop in Legal before any direct contact with the suspected operator.
steps.outcome: Reviews removed and, where warranted, formal notice sent to the operator.

steps.title: Monitor rating recovery and recurrence
steps.desc: Track whether the rating stabilizes and whether the same click-farm resurfaces under new accounts.
steps.outcome: No further activity from the identified cluster.

steps.title: Document detection signatures for future speed
steps.desc: Record the technical/behavioral indicators that identified this as a click-farm to accelerate detection of similar future campaigns.

steps.title: Distinguish coordinated paid activity from a genuine complaint spike
steps.desc: Confirm the reviews lack specific, verifiable order/interaction details consistent with real customers.
steps.guidance: If several reviews independently describe a real, checkable incident, treat this as a genuine service issue rather than a click-farm campaign.
steps.outcome: Confirmed inauthentic origin with supporting rationale.
steps.abort: If evidence points to a genuine complaint, redirect to Customer Service for remediation.

steps.title: Preserve evidence before it disappears
steps.desc: Screenshot all flagged reviews and account profiles in case the platform or the operators remove them before action is taken.
steps.outcome: Evidence archive preserved independent of platform state.

ITID-24113.def: A campaign in which previously legitimate, verified reviewer accounts — obtained through account takeover or purchased on black-market forums — are used to post negative reviews that appear more credible than obviously-fake accounts.
ITID-24113.purpose: Captures a coordinated negative-review attack carried out through compromised or black-market-purchased verified reviewer accounts, which carry more platform credibility than fresh or bot accounts.
scopeIncludes: Negative reviews posted from accounts with a real purchase/verification history unrelated to the reviewer's apparent new posting behavior
Accounts flagged by the platform's own account-takeover detection coinciding with a negative review of the organization
scopeExcludes: Fresh bot/sockpuppet accounts (ITID-24111)
Paid click-farm human labor on new accounts (ITID-24112)
Account takeover of the organization's own corporate/social accounts (a distinct identity-compromise ITID elsewhere in the taxonomy)
ITID-24113.severity: Medium-High; verified-account credibility gives this variant more reputational weight than sibling leaves.
ITID-24113.priority: P2, given the elevated credibility and harder detectability of verified-account-sourced negative reviews.
ITID-24113.escalation: Escalate to brand/communications and platform trust-and-safety; the platform's own account-security team is the primary remediation path since the underlying issue is account compromise, not organic sentiment.
indicators: A previously dormant or unrelated-history verified account suddenly posting a negative review of the organization
Platform account-takeover flags coinciding with the review timing
Review content inconsistent with the account's established purchase category history
vectors: Purchase of compromised verified accounts on black-market/underground forums
Credential-stuffing or phishing to take over legitimate reviewer accounts
rootCauses: No monitoring for anomalous account-history mismatches in incoming negative reviews
No standing escalation channel to the platform's account-security team distinct from its content-moderation team
controls: Review-content-history anomaly monitoring
Escalation relationship with the platform's account-security/trust-and-safety team
ITID-24113.detection: Detection depends on the platform's own account-takeover telemetry combined with content/behavior-mismatch analysis; the organization has no direct technical visibility into the compromised account itself.
ITID-24113.response: Report the specific accounts to the platform's account-security team (not just content moderation), request the review be removed as originating from a compromised account, and document the pattern for the brand-abuse record.
metrics: Count of compromised-account-sourced reviews identified per quarter
Platform account-security escalation response time
ITID-24113.notes: This is the one leaf in its sibling group with a genuine adversary-infrastructure mechanism (compromised/purchased accounts), warranting the T1586 mapping under Resource Development.

playbook.name: Response: Review Platform Manipulation via Compromised/Purchased Verified Accounts
playbook.description: For negative reviews posted through legitimate, verified accounts that have been compromised or purchased for the purpose of the campaign, giving the reviews unwarranted credibility.

steps.title: Identify which reviews originate from verified accounts and gather evidence of compromise
steps.desc: Cross-reference the flagged reviews against verified-account status; look for signs the account was hijacked or resold (sudden change in posting topic/language, activity gap followed by an off-topic burst).
steps.outcome: List of implicated verified accounts with supporting compromise indicators.

steps.title: Report the compromised accounts to the platform's account-security team
steps.desc: Submit a report specifically flagging account takeover/resale, which most platforms treat with higher urgency than generic fake-review reports.
steps.tool: Platform trust & safety / account security portal

steps.title: Pursue removal and account restoration
steps.desc: Track the platform's remediation — removal of the fraudulent reviews and restoration/lockdown of the compromised accounts.
steps.outcome: Reviews removed; accounts secured or disabled.

steps.title: Monitor for reappearance under newly compromised accounts
steps.desc: Watch for a repeat pattern suggesting the same actor is cycling through compromised accounts.

steps.title: Document the compromise pattern
steps.desc: Record how the compromised/purchased accounts were identified, for faster detection of future verified-account abuse.

steps.title: Assess reputational risk from the verified-status credibility boost
steps.desc: Because these reviews carry a 'verified' badge, weigh the added visibility/trust impact relative to a standard fake-review case.
steps.guidance: Loop in PR/Comms given verified reviews are more likely to be believed and shared.

steps.title: Notify affected genuine account holders where identifiable
steps.desc: If any compromised accounts belong to identifiable real customers, notify them that their account may have been hijacked so they can secure it.
steps.outcome: Affected users informed and directed to the platform's account-recovery process.

ITID-24114.def: A coordinated negative-review incident awaiting further investigation to determine its specific mechanism (bot network, paid click-farm, or compromised/purchased accounts) before reclassification to the appropriate sibling ITID.
ITID-24114.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for a coordinated negative-review campaign that does not yet clearly fit the bot-network, click-farm, or compromised-account mechanisms.
scopeIncludes: Newly-detected coordinated negative-review spikes not yet triaged to a specific mechanism
Ambiguous or mixed-mechanism campaigns pending further evidence
scopeExcludes: Any campaign for which the mechanism has been confirmed and should be reclassified to ITID-24111, ITID-24112, or ITID-24113
Single, isolated negative reviews with no coordination pattern (not an incident)
ITID-24114.severity: Medium pending triage; reassess once the mechanism is confirmed and reclassify accordingly.
ITID-24114.escalation: Escalate to the brand/reputation analyst on triage duty; reclassify to a specific sibling ITID as soon as evidence supports it rather than leaving the incident here.
indicators: An unexplained spike in negative reviews without yet-established source attribution
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial evidence to attribute mechanism at time of intake
controls: Review-platform monitoring and sentiment-anomaly alerting
ITID-24114.detection: Same brand-monitoring/social-listening detection surface as sibling leaves, pending mechanism attribution.
ITID-24114.response: Triage promptly, gather account/fingerprint evidence, and reclassify to the specific sibling ITID once the mechanism is clear.
metrics: Count of incidents held in this bucket beyond 5 business days without reclassification
ITID-24114.notes: Intake/triage bucket only, not a terminal classification — every incident here should be reclassified to a specific sibling leaf once the mechanism is known.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Coordinated Negative Reviews
playbook.description: General-purpose response for a coordinated negative review campaign that does not fit a more specific known pattern (bots, click-farms, or compromised accounts).

steps.title: Collect and characterize the suspect reviews
steps.desc: Export the flagged reviews with all available metadata and look for any coordination signal — timing clusters, wording overlap, account patterns.

steps.title: Report the campaign to the relevant platform(s)
steps.desc: File an inauthentic-activity report with the assembled evidence.

steps.title: Pursue takedown through platform enforcement
steps.desc: Follow through on the report until resolved, escalating as needed.

steps.title: Monitor rating and sentiment recovery
steps.desc: Track whether rating and sentiment return to baseline.

steps.title: Document the incident pattern
steps.desc: Record what type of coordination this turned out to be, to refine future classification and detection.

steps.title: Distinguish inauthentic coordination from a genuine viral complaint
steps.desc: Assess whether the reviews describe a real, verifiable service issue versus generic or implausible complaints.
steps.guidance: This distinction is critical — a genuine underlying issue calls for a customer-service fix, not a takedown request.
steps.abort: If the complaint is genuine, redirect to Customer Service.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and brief internal stakeholders
steps.desc: Archive screenshots and brief Customer Service/PR so responses are coordinated.

ITID-24121.def: A campaign in which an identifiable competitor organization (or its employees/agents acting on its direction) directly authors or commissions fake negative reviews of the organization's product or service.
ITID-24121.purpose: Captures a negative-review campaign directly sponsored and operated by an identified competitor, as opposed to an outsourced reputation-attack vendor.
scopeIncludes: Negative reviews traceable to a competitor's employees, contractors, or corporate IP ranges
Internal evidence (leaked emails, whistleblower reports) showing a competitor directed the campaign
scopeExcludes: Campaigns run through an outsourced third-party reputation-attack service where the paying competitor is not directly operating the campaign (ITID-24122)
Generic bot/click-farm campaigns with no identified sponsor (ITID-24111/24112)
ITID-24121.severity: High; direct competitor sponsorship raises legal (unfair competition, defamation) and business-risk stakes beyond a generic anonymous campaign.
ITID-24121.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if attribution is strong enough to support legal action or public disclosure.
ITID-24121.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal and executive leadership given the potential for an unfair-competition claim; involve communications for any public response.
indicators: Reviews originating from IP ranges or accounts traceable to a named competitor
Internal whistleblower or leaked-communication evidence of competitor direction
Reviews referencing internal, non-public competitor talking points
vectors: Competitor employees or contractors posting or directing fake negative reviews
Competitor marketing/growth teams tasked with reputation attacks
rootCauses: No legal deterrence framework in place for competitor-sponsored attacks
No forensic capability to trace review-account infrastructure to a corporate origin
controls: Legal monitoring for unfair-competition indicators
Forensic account/infrastructure attribution capability
ITID-24121.detection: Attribution relies on forensic investigation of account infrastructure combined with legal discovery/whistleblower evidence — not a technical detection surface.
ITID-24121.response: Build an evidentiary record sufficient for legal review, pursue platform takedown, and evaluate a cease-and-desist or civil claim with legal counsel.
metrics: Count of confirmed competitor-attributed campaigns per year
Legal action outcomes
sops: Legal Escalation SOP for Unfair Competition
ITID-24121.notes: Differentiated from sibling ITID-24122 by sponsorship structure: this leaf is the competitor acting directly, not through an outsourced third-party vendor.

playbook.name: Response: Direct Competitor-Sponsored Fake Negative Review Campaign
playbook.description: For a negative review campaign directly traceable to a competitor sponsoring or orchestrating fake reviews against the company.

steps.title: Collect the suspect reviews and behavioral evidence
steps.desc: Export flagged reviews with timestamps, account patterns, and any content that references competitor products/offers.

steps.title: Report the fake reviews to the platform without naming the competitor publicly
steps.desc: Submit a standard inauthentic-activity report to the platform; keep any competitor attribution internal/legal at this stage.

steps.title: Pursue platform takedown and, if warranted, formal legal action against the competitor
steps.desc: Follow through on platform removal; where evidence is strong, Legal may pursue a cease-and-desist or other formal action against the competitor.
steps.outcome: Reviews removed; formal action initiated if warranted.

steps.title: Monitor rating recovery and competitor activity
steps.desc: Track rating trend and watch for continued or escalating activity from the same source.

steps.title: Document the evidentiary process for future competitor-attribution cases
steps.desc: Record what evidence was sufficient (or insufficient) to establish the competitor link, to speed up and de-risk future cases.

steps.title: Establish the competitor link with verifiable evidence before any public claim
steps.desc: Build a documented chain of evidence connecting the review activity to the competitor — e.g. accounts also promoting the competitor's products, shared origin infrastructure, or a leaked/reported instruction to staff or contractors.
steps.guidance: This step is mandatory before any public statement or accusation. Loop in Legal early; an unsubstantiated public accusation against a named competitor carries real legal and reputational risk to the company.
steps.outcome: Documented, defensible evidence trail establishing the competitor link, or a determination that the link cannot be substantiated.
steps.abort: If the competitor link cannot be substantiated to a defensible standard, treat this as a standard coordinated-review incident and do not name or imply the competitor publicly.

steps.title: Brief Legal and Executive leadership on the evidence
steps.desc: Present the substantiated evidence trail to Legal and relevant executives before deciding on any direct or public response to the competitor.
steps.outcome: Leadership aligned on response strategy (platform-only vs. legal action vs. public statement).

ITID-24122.def: A campaign in which a competitor hires an independent third-party service (a 'black hat' reputation-management or review-manipulation vendor) to execute a negative-review campaign, obscuring the competitor's direct involvement.
ITID-24122.purpose: Captures a negative-review campaign a competitor commissions from an outsourced third-party reputation-attack vendor, distancing the competitor from direct attribution.
scopeIncludes: Campaigns traceable to a known third-party review-manipulation vendor's infrastructure or service signature
Cases where a vendor's marketing/sales material explicitly advertises negative-review campaign services
scopeExcludes: A competitor's own employees or contractors directly operating the campaign (ITID-24121)
Generic anonymous bot/click-farm campaigns with no vendor attribution (ITID-24111/24112)
ITID-24122.severity: High; comparable business risk to direct competitor sponsorship, but harder to attribute and legally pursue.
ITID-24122.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the vendor and paying competitor can both be identified.
ITID-24122.escalation: Escalate to legal for potential action against the vendor directly (many jurisdictions have anti-fake-review statutes targeting the service provider) and to communications for brand response.
indicators: Review infrastructure signatures matching a known reputation-attack vendor's prior campaigns against other brands
Reviews appearing shortly after a competitor engagement or marketing push
vectors: Third-party reputation-attack or 'black hat SEO/reviews' vendor services
Vendor-operated bot/account networks reused across multiple paying clients
rootCauses: No threat-intelligence tracking of known review-manipulation vendors and their infrastructure signatures
No legal framework addressing vendor-side liability for fake-review services
controls: Threat-intelligence tracking of known review-manipulation vendor infrastructure
Legal engagement on vendor-side anti-fake-review statutes where applicable
ITID-24122.detection: Relies on cross-campaign infrastructure-signature correlation (often via brand-monitoring vendor threat intelligence) rather than direct technical telemetry.
ITID-24122.response: Correlate infrastructure signatures against known vendor patterns, report to the platform, and pursue legal action against the vendor and/or the paying party where attribution supports it.
metrics: Count of vendor-attributed campaigns identified per year
sops: Legal Escalation SOP for Unfair Competition
ITID-24122.notes: Differentiated from sibling ITID-24121 by the outsourced-vendor structure, which changes both the attribution difficulty and the available legal remedies.

playbook.name: Response: Competitor-Hired Third-Party Reputation Attack Service
playbook.description: For a negative review campaign carried out by a third-party 'reputation attack' service hired by a competitor, adding a layer of separation between the competitor and the activity.

steps.title: Collect the suspect reviews and identify the operating service pattern
steps.desc: Export flagged reviews and look for signatures common to commercial reputation-attack services (templated review structures, cross-client account reuse, pricing-page evidence if the service is found publicly).
steps.outcome: Evidence set assembled, with the third-party service pattern identified where possible.

steps.title: Report the reviews and account network to the platform
steps.desc: Submit an inauthentic-activity report describing the coordinated pattern.

steps.title: Pursue takedown and consider action against the service and/or competitor
steps.desc: Track platform removal; where the competitor link is substantiated, Legal may pursue further action.
steps.outcome: Reviews removed; further action taken if warranted.

steps.title: Monitor rating recovery and recurrence
steps.desc: Track whether the same service resurfaces against the company.

steps.title: Document the service's signature for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the templated patterns and any identifying details of the service used, to recognize it faster if reused against the company.

steps.title: Establish the competitor link before any public claim
steps.desc: Attempt to trace payment, referral, or communication evidence connecting the hired service back to the competitor, recognizing the deliberate layer of separation makes this harder than a direct campaign.
steps.guidance: Loop in Legal early. If the competitor link cannot be established, the incident should still be pursued against the service itself without naming a competitor.
steps.outcome: Evidence trail assessed for strength; competitor link confirmed, inconclusive, or absent.
steps.abort: If no competitor link can be substantiated, proceed against the fake-review service alone and do not imply competitor involvement publicly.

steps.title: Brief Legal on findings and any competitor evidence
steps.desc: Share the evidence trail with Legal to decide next steps, including whether the platform's own vendor-abuse policies can be invoked against the paid service.

ITID-24123.def: A suspected competitor-sponsored negative-review incident awaiting further investigation to determine sponsorship structure before reclassification to a specific sibling ITID.
ITID-24123.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for a suspected competitor-led review campaign pending confirmation of whether the competitor acted directly or through a third-party vendor.
scopeIncludes: Suspected competitor involvement without yet-confirmed direct-vs-vendor attribution
scopeExcludes: Any campaign for which sponsorship structure has been confirmed and should be reclassified to ITID-24121 or ITID-24122
Campaigns with no competitor-attribution evidence at all (belongs under Coordinated Negative Reviews instead)
ITID-24123.priority: P2 during initial triage given the potential legal stakes.
ITID-24123.escalation: Escalate to legal and the brand/reputation analyst on triage duty; reclassify once attribution evidence is gathered.
indicators: Circumstantial evidence suggesting competitor involvement without full attribution
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial evidence to attribute sponsorship structure at time of intake
controls: Forensic account/infrastructure attribution capability
ITID-24123.detection: Same detection surface as sibling leaves, pending attribution.
ITID-24123.response: Gather attribution evidence promptly and reclassify to the specific sibling ITID once sponsorship structure is clear.
metrics: Count of incidents held in this bucket beyond 5 business days without reclassification
ITID-24123.notes: Intake/triage bucket only, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Competitor-Led Review Campaign
playbook.description: General-purpose response for a suspected competitor-led fake review campaign that does not fit a more specific known pattern.

steps.title: Collect the suspect reviews and any competitor-referencing signals
steps.desc: Export flagged reviews and note any content, timing, or account behavior suggesting competitor involvement.

steps.title: Report the reviews to the platform
steps.desc: Submit a standard inauthentic-activity report.

steps.title: Pursue takedown and further action as warranted
steps.desc: Follow through on platform removal and any legal follow-up Legal determines is appropriate.

steps.title: Monitor rating recovery
steps.desc: Track rating trend back to baseline.

steps.title: Document the incident and evidentiary approach
steps.desc: Record what was found and how the competitor-attribution question was resolved.

steps.title: Establish the competitor link with verifiable evidence before any public claim
steps.desc: Build a documented, defensible evidence trail before treating this as competitor-attributed.
steps.guidance: Loop in Legal early — never make or imply a public accusation without substantiated evidence.
steps.outcome: Competitor link confirmed, inconclusive, or ruled out.
steps.abort: If unsubstantiated, treat as a standard coordinated-review incident with no competitor attribution.

steps.title: Brief Legal and leadership on findings
steps.desc: Share the evidence trail internally before any external response is considered.

ITID-24131.def: A spike in negative reviews caused by a social media post (often a single viral complaint, video, or thread) that drives real users, not fabricated accounts, to leave negative reviews en masse — an organically-triggered pile-on rather than a manufactured campaign.
ITID-24131.purpose: Captures organic-origin negative-review surges driven by a viral social media post, distinct from a deliberately orchestrated bot or paid campaign.
scopeIncludes: Negative-review surges directly traceable to a single identifiable viral post or thread
Reviews from apparently real accounts referencing the viral content
scopeExcludes: Bot/fake-account-driven campaigns with no organic viral trigger (ITID-24111)
Influencer-directed call-to-action campaigns, where a creator explicitly instructs followers to leave reviews (ITID-24132)
ITID-23524 Review Bombing Campaign (press-narrative-driven, different Tier-3 branch)
ITID-24131.severity: Medium, escalating to High if the viral post reaches mass reach (millions of views) or trends nationally.
ITID-24131.priority: P2 during an active viral spike given the speed of reputational damage; de-escalate to P3 once the post's reach plateaus.
ITID-24131.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR immediately for rapid response messaging; loop in the product/service team if the viral complaint reflects a genuine underlying issue.
indicators: A single social media post's engagement metrics correlating with the timing of the review spike
Reviews referencing or quoting the viral post's specific claims
Real-looking, individually-varied review accounts (not templated)
vectors: Organic virality of a genuine or exaggerated customer complaint post
rootCauses: No real-time social-listening alerting tied to review-platform monitoring
Slow or absent public response to the underlying complaint allowing the narrative to spread unchecked
controls: Real-time social-listening and review-velocity correlation alerting
Rapid-response communications playbook for viral complaints
ITID-24131.detection: Detected via social-listening tools correlating viral-post metrics with review-platform velocity; no technical/network detection surface since accounts and reviews are largely genuine.
ITID-24131.response: Assess whether the underlying complaint is genuine (and if so, address it publicly and operationally) versus exaggerated/false, then issue a proportionate public response and monitor for de-escalation.
metrics: Time from viral-post detection to communications response
Review-velocity return-to-baseline time
ITID-24131.notes: Differentiated from sibling 24132 by the absence of directed influencer instruction — this is organic follower-driven amplification. Also distinct from ITID-23524, which is press-narrative-driven rather than social-post-driven.

playbook.name: Response: Viral Social Media Post Driving Mass Negative Review Influx
playbook.description: For a surge of negative reviews triggered by a viral social media post, where reviewers may be genuine members of the public reacting to the post rather than a coordinated fake-account campaign.

steps.title: Trace the influx back to its originating post(s)
steps.desc: Identify the specific social media post(s) driving the review surge and gauge its reach (shares, views, comment sentiment).

steps.title: Report reviews found to be inauthentic to the platform(s)
steps.desc: For reviews confirmed as fake/bot rather than organic reaction, file a standard inauthentic-activity report.
steps.outcome: Report filed for the inauthentic subset.

steps.title: Pursue removal of confirmed-fake reviews only
steps.desc: Follow through on platform action for the inauthentic subset; do not attempt to suppress genuine reviews.
steps.outcome: Fake reviews removed; genuine reviews left in place.

steps.title: Publish a factual correction where warranted and monitor sentiment
steps.desc: If the original post was misleading, publish a clear factual correction; track sentiment recovery either way.
steps.outcome: Correction published if needed; sentiment trend tracked back to baseline.

steps.title: Document the viral trigger and response timeline
steps.desc: Record how quickly the source post was identified and fact-checked, to improve response speed next time.

steps.title: Distinguish genuine viral reaction from inauthentic coordination
steps.desc: Assess whether the resulting reviews come from distinct, real-looking accounts reacting organically versus a bot/coordinated pattern layered on top of the viral moment.
steps.guidance: This distinction matters — if the underlying claim in the viral post is true, the correct response is a genuine fix and public correction, not a mass takedown request.
steps.outcome: Determination made on authenticity of the resulting reviews.
steps.abort: If the viral post's claim is factually accurate, redirect to standard PR crisis handling and Customer Service remediation rather than this playbook.

steps.title: Coordinate a factual response with PR/Comms
steps.desc: For the genuine-reaction portion, prepare a factual public response addressing the claim rather than pursuing takedowns.
steps.outcome: Response drafted and approved by PR/Comms.

steps.title: Fact-check the claim in the originating post
steps.desc: Determine whether the post's underlying claim about the company is true, exaggerated, or fabricated.
steps.guidance: Loop in the relevant business unit to confirm facts quickly.
steps.outcome: Factual basis of the viral claim established.

ITID-24132.def: A campaign in which an influencer or content creator explicitly calls on their audience to go leave negative reviews of the organization's product or service, converting follower engagement into a directed review-bombing action.
ITID-24132.purpose: Captures a negative-review surge explicitly directed by an influencer or content creator instructing their audience to leave reviews, as opposed to organic viral spread.
scopeIncludes: Posts containing an explicit call-to-action directing followers to leave a negative review, with a measurable review-volume response
Coordinated hashtag or comment instructions linking directly to the review platform
scopeExcludes: Organic viral spread with no explicit call-to-action (ITID-24131)
Paid/sponsored competitor-directed influencer campaigns (tracked under Fake Influencer Reviews, Tier-3 branch, e.g. ITID-24511)
ITID-24132.severity: Medium-High, scaling with the influencer's follower count and engagement rate.
ITID-24132.priority: P2 while the call-to-action is actively driving review volume.
ITID-24132.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR for direct engagement strategy; consider direct outreach to the influencer to understand and potentially address the underlying grievance.
indicators: An identifiable post or video containing an explicit call-to-action to leave a negative review
Review-volume spike timed to the post's publication and engagement curve
Reviews echoing specific phrases from the influencer's content
vectors: Influencer/creator content explicitly directing audience review-bombing
rootCauses: No proactive influencer-relations monitoring for brand-critical content
No rapid-response protocol for direct creator engagement
controls: Social-listening monitoring for influencer content referencing the brand
Rapid-response communications and influencer-engagement protocol
ITID-24132.detection: Detected via social-listening tools tracking influencer content and correlated review-velocity spikes; not a technical detection surface.
ITID-24132.response: Assess the legitimacy of the underlying grievance, consider direct outreach to the influencer, and issue a proportionate public response while monitoring review-platform impact.
metrics: Review-volume spike magnitude correlated to influencer reach
Time to direct influencer engagement
ITID-24132.notes: Differentiated from sibling 24131 by the presence of an explicit, directed call-to-action rather than organic spread. Paid/sponsored variants of influencer-driven negativity are tracked separately under the Fake Influencer Reviews Tier-3 branch.

playbook.name: Response: Influencer-Driven Negative Review Call-to-Action
playbook.description: For an influencer explicitly urging their audience to leave negative reviews of the company, whether based on a genuine grievance or not.

steps.title: Identify the influencer, the call-to-action content, and audience reach
steps.desc: Locate the specific post/video and quantify the influencer's following and engagement to size potential impact.

steps.title: Report reviews that are demonstrably fabricated or from non-customers
steps.desc: Where resulting reviews come from accounts with no purchase/interaction history and repeat the influencer's talking points verbatim, file a platform report.
steps.outcome: Report filed for the fabricated subset.

steps.title: Pursue removal of fabricated reviews
steps.desc: Follow through on platform action for reviews confirmed as fabricated or from non-customers.

steps.title: Monitor influencer content spread and rating trend
steps.desc: Track whether the call-to-action continues to drive activity and whether the rating stabilizes.

steps.title: Document the incident and influencer-relations approach
steps.desc: Record what worked in engaging (or not engaging) with the influencer for future reference.

steps.title: Assess the legitimacy of the influencer's underlying grievance
steps.desc: Determine whether the influencer's complaint reflects a real, verifiable experience with the company.
steps.guidance: If the grievance is genuine, this is a customer-service and PR matter, not a fake-review takedown case.
steps.outcome: Grievance assessed as genuine, exaggerated, or fabricated.
steps.abort: If genuine, redirect to Customer Service and PR for direct resolution with the influencer.

steps.title: Consider direct outreach to the influencer
steps.desc: If the grievance is genuine or partly genuine, PR/Comms may reach out directly to resolve the underlying issue and reduce further amplification.
steps.guidance: Handle with care — a defensive-sounding outreach can escalate the situation.

ITID-24133.def: A campaign or organic pattern in which negative reviews (real or fabricated) are screenshotted and re-shared across multiple social media platforms, amplifying reputational reach well beyond the original review site's audience.
ITID-24133.purpose: Captures negative-review content amplified across multiple social platforms via screenshots, extending its reach beyond the original review platform.
scopeIncludes: Screenshots of negative reviews circulating and gaining engagement across platforms distinct from the original review site
Compilation posts or threads aggregating multiple negative reviews as screenshots
scopeExcludes: The original negative review itself on the source platform (tracked under the applicable Coordinated Negative Reviews leaf if fabricated)
A single viral post driving new reviews to be written (ITID-24131), as opposed to re-sharing existing ones
ITID-24133.severity: Medium, escalating to High if the screenshot compilation reaches viral cross-platform distribution.
ITID-24133.priority: P2 during active cross-platform spread; monitor for plateau.
ITID-24133.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR for cross-platform response coordination; verify authenticity of screenshotted content, since screenshots are trivially fabricable.
indicators: Identical review screenshots appearing across multiple unrelated social platforms within a short window
Screenshot compilations with edited or cropped context altering the review's meaning
vectors: Screenshot re-sharing and compilation posts across social platforms
Selectively cropped or doctored review screenshots
rootCauses: No cross-platform social-listening coverage beyond the primary review platform
No process to verify screenshot authenticity against the platform's actual review record
controls: Cross-platform social-listening monitoring
Screenshot-authenticity verification process against source platform records
ITID-24133.detection: Detected via cross-platform social-listening tools tracking image/screenshot re-circulation; no technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24133.response: Verify the screenshot against the platform's actual review record, flag any doctoring publicly if found, and coordinate a cross-platform communications response.
metrics: Cross-platform screenshot circulation volume
Rate of doctored/fabricated screenshots identified
ITID-24133.notes: Scoped specifically to the cross-platform re-sharing mechanism, distinguishing it from the original review posting (sibling leaves) and from organic new-review-driving virality (ITID-24131).

playbook.name: Response: Cross-Platform Review Screenshot Amplification Campaign
playbook.description: For screenshots of negative reviews (real or fabricated) being circulated and amplified across multiple social platforms beyond the review platform itself.

steps.title: Locate the original review(s) behind the circulating screenshots
steps.desc: Find the source review on the originating platform to verify whether the screenshot is authentic, altered, or entirely fabricated.
steps.outcome: Screenshot authenticity determined against the original source.

steps.title: Report altered or fabricated screenshots to each hosting platform
steps.desc: Where the screenshot is confirmed altered or fake, file a report on each platform where it is circulating.

steps.title: Pursue removal of fabricated/altered content
steps.desc: Follow through on takedown requests for confirmed fake or altered screenshots.
steps.outcome: Fabricated content removed where policy violations are confirmed.

steps.title: Monitor continued spread and publish a correction if needed
steps.desc: Track whether the amplification subsides; publish a factual clarification if a fabricated version is still circulating widely.
steps.outcome: Spread contained; correction reaching relevant audience if published.

steps.title: Document the amplification pattern
steps.desc: Record which platforms served as amplification vectors and how quickly authenticity was verified, to speed up future response.

steps.title: Map the amplification spread across platforms
steps.desc: Track which platforms and accounts are driving the spread and estimate total reach.

steps.title: If the underlying review is genuine, coordinate a real response rather than a takedown
steps.desc: For an authentic underlying review, route to Customer Service for a genuine resolution and have PR/Comms prepare a factual response to the amplification.

ITID-24134.def: A social-media-amplified negative-review incident awaiting further investigation to determine its specific amplification mechanism before reclassification to the appropriate sibling ITID.
ITID-24134.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for a social-media-amplified negative-review incident not yet triaged to the viral-post, influencer-directed, or cross-platform-screenshot mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Newly-detected social-media-driven review spikes not yet triaged to a specific mechanism
scopeExcludes: Any incident for which the mechanism has been confirmed and should be reclassified to ITID-24131, ITID-24132, or ITID-24133
ITID-24134.priority: P3 during initial triage; escalate per the confirmed mechanism once known.
ITID-24134.escalation: Escalate to the brand/reputation analyst on triage duty; reclassify promptly once the amplification mechanism is identified.
indicators: An unexplained social-media-correlated review spike without yet-established mechanism attribution
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial evidence to attribute mechanism at time of intake
controls: Social-listening and review-velocity correlation alerting
ITID-24134.detection: Same detection surface as sibling leaves, pending mechanism attribution.
ITID-24134.response: Triage promptly and reclassify to the specific sibling ITID once the mechanism is clear.
metrics: Count of incidents held in this bucket beyond 5 business days without reclassification
ITID-24134.notes: Intake/triage bucket only, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Social Media Amplified Reviews
playbook.description: General-purpose response for a negative review campaign amplified via social media that does not fit a more specific known pattern (viral post, influencer call-to-action, or screenshot amplification).

steps.title: Trace the amplification back to its source
steps.desc: Identify the social media content and accounts driving the review surge, and gauge reach.

steps.title: Report confirmed-inauthentic reviews to the platform(s)
steps.desc: File an inauthentic-activity report for any reviews confirmed as fake/bot.

steps.title: Pursue removal of confirmed-fake reviews
steps.desc: Follow through on platform action for the inauthentic subset only.
steps.outcome: Fake reviews removed; genuine reviews left in place.

steps.title: Monitor sentiment and rating recovery
steps.desc: Track whether rating and sentiment return to baseline.

steps.title: Document the amplification pattern
steps.desc: Record the source and mechanism of amplification for faster future detection.

steps.title: Distinguish genuine amplified reaction from inauthentic coordination
steps.desc: Assess whether the resulting reviews look like organic public reaction versus a bot/coordinated pattern.
steps.guidance: If the underlying complaint is real, the correct response is a genuine customer-service fix, not a takedown request.
steps.abort: If the underlying issue is genuine, redirect to Customer Service for remediation.

steps.title: Coordinate a factual public response where warranted
steps.desc: If the amplifying content contains inaccuracies, prepare a factual response with PR/Comms.

ITID-24211.def: A campaign in which automated or fabricated accounts post fake positive reviews for a competing product/service, framed comparatively to disadvantage the organization's standing (e.g., reviews explicitly contrasting favorably against the organization).
ITID-24211.purpose: Captures the use of a bot account network to inflate a competitor's ratings with fake positive reviews, as a comparative disparagement tactic against the organization.
scopeIncludes: Fake positive reviews for a competitor posted by bot/fabricated accounts with no genuine purchase history
Reviews explicitly naming or comparing unfavorably against the organization
scopeExcludes: Paid human reviewer rings performing the same function (ITID-24212)
Astroturfed grassroots-style praise campaigns without bot infrastructure (ITID-24213)
Genuine organic competitor reviews with no comparative disparagement
ITID-24211.severity: Low-to-Medium; primarily a comparative-market-perception harm rather than a direct attack on the organization's own listings.
ITID-24211.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if the pattern is part of a broader coordinated campaign also including direct negative reviews of the organization.
ITID-24211.escalation: Escalate to brand/competitive-intelligence for awareness; loop in legal only if the comparative claims are factually false and defamatory.
indicators: A competitor's reviews showing an anomalous positive-sentiment spike with comparative language against the organization
Reviewer accounts bearing bot-network fingerprints similar to those seen in direct attacks on the organization
vectors: Bot-operated account networks posting comparative fake praise for a competitor
rootCauses: No monitoring of competitor review sentiment for comparative disparagement patterns
controls: Competitive review-sentiment monitoring for comparative disparagement patterns
ITID-24211.detection: Detected via brand/competitive-monitoring tools tracking sentiment and comparative-language patterns on competitor listings; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24211.response: Document the pattern for competitive-intelligence awareness; escalate to legal only where factually false comparative claims rise to defamation.
metrics: Count of comparative-disparagement patterns identified per quarter
ITID-24211.notes: Differentiated from sibling 24212 (paid human ring) and 24213 (astroturfed grassroots praise) by the bot-network infrastructure mechanism, which justifies the Resource Development mapping.

playbook.name: Response: Bot Network-Generated Fake Positive Reviews for Competitor
playbook.description: A bot/fake-account network is posting a volume of positive reviews for a competitor in a manner that references or disparages this organization (e.g., 'better than [org]', comparison call-outs), skewing the competitive landscape at this organization's expense.

steps.title: Confirm the competitor reviews show signs of inauthentic bot activity
steps.desc: Analyze the flagged reviews on the competitor's listing for shared bot signatures — near-identical phrasing, clustered account-creation dates, unnatural posting-time clustering, low or no genuine purchase/activity history.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with brand-monitoring/social-listening tooling to pull the full set of flagged reviews for pattern analysis.
steps.outcome: Documented evidence of coordinated/inauthentic activity, or a determination that the reviews are organic (in which case this is a competitive-marketing matter, not a security incident).
steps.abort: If the reviews appear genuine on review, hand off to marketing/competitive-intelligence rather than treating as an attack.

steps.title: Report the inauthentic review network to each affected platform
steps.desc: Submit a formal inauthentic-activity/fake-engagement report with supporting evidence to each platform's review-integrity or trust-and-safety team, noting the bot network is being used to disparage this organization.
steps.guidance: Most major review and marketplace platforms have a dedicated inauthentic-activity reporting channel distinct from a normal dispute process.
steps.outcome: Report(s) submitted with evidence package attached.

steps.title: Follow up until the platform removes or labels the confirmed-inauthentic reviews
steps.desc: Track each platform's response and escalate if the initial report doesn't result in removal or a fake-engagement label within a reasonable window.
steps.outcome: Inauthentic reviews removed, or their effect on the competitor's rating corrected/flagged.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence or a shifted campaign
steps.desc: Watch the same platforms and adjacent ones for a resumed or relocated version of the bot campaign over the following weeks.
steps.outcome: No renewed campaign observed, or a new instance caught early.

steps.title: Document the bot signature and disparagement pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the specific inauthenticity signatures and comparison-attack language observed to speed up identification of similar future campaigns.
steps.outcome: Finding logged in the incident knowledge base.

steps.title: Determine scale, platforms, and the specific claims made about this organization
steps.desc: Catalog every platform where the bot network is active and record the exact language used to disparage or unfavorably compare this organization, for later evidentiary use.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the campaign and a documented set of the specific claims made.

steps.title: Loop in legal/brand-protection if the claims are false and defamatory
steps.desc: Where the disparaging comparison claims about this organization are factually false (not merely opinion), assess with legal counsel whether a defamation or unfair-competition claim against the competitor or campaign operator is warranted.
steps.outcome: Decision recorded on whether legal action is pursued.
steps.abort: If claims are opinion-based rather than factually false, legal escalation is unlikely to apply.

ITID-24212.def: A campaign in which a paid ring of human reviewers posts fake positive reviews for a competing product/service, often with comparative language disadvantaging the organization's standing.
ITID-24212.purpose: Captures the use of a paid human reviewer ring to inflate a competitor's ratings comparatively against the organization.
scopeIncludes: Fake positive reviews for a competitor traceable to a known paid reviewer ring or task-marketplace campaign
Reviews with human-variable phrasing but no genuine purchase history
scopeExcludes: Bot-network-generated reviews (ITID-24211)
Astroturfed grassroots-style campaigns without a paid-ring structure (ITID-24213)
ITID-24212.severity: Low-to-Medium; a comparative-market-perception harm rather than a direct attack on the organization's own listings.
ITID-24212.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if part of a broader coordinated campaign.
ITID-24212.escalation: Escalate to brand/competitive-intelligence for awareness; legal only where comparative claims are factually false and defamatory.
indicators: A competitor's reviews showing human-authored but templated praise with comparative language
Reviewer accounts geographically clustered in known paid-reviewer labor markets
vectors: Paid reviewer ring or task-marketplace campaign generating fake competitor praise
rootCauses: No monitoring of competitor review sentiment for reviewer-clustering patterns indicative of paid rings
controls: Competitive review-sentiment and reviewer-clustering monitoring
ITID-24212.detection: Relies on brand/competitive-monitoring tools and reviewer-clustering analysis; no technical/network detection surface since paid humans execute the posts.
ITID-24212.response: Document the pattern for competitive-intelligence awareness; escalate to legal only where factually false comparative claims rise to defamation.
metrics: Count of paid-ring-attributed comparative campaigns identified per quarter
ITID-24212.notes: No MITRE mapping applies — paid human labor, not adversary infrastructure. Differentiated from sibling 24211 (bots) and 24213 (astroturfed grassroots) by the paid-ring labor mechanism.

playbook.name: Response: Paid Reviewer Ring Boosting Competitor Ratings
playbook.description: A paid human reviewer ring (as opposed to a bot network) is posting positive reviews for a competitor, in a coordinated fashion that disparages or unfavorably compares this organization.

steps.title: Confirm the pattern indicates a paid reviewer ring rather than organic praise
steps.desc: Analyze reviewer accounts for cross-platform review-farm indicators — reviewers who consistently review the same narrow set of businesses, reciprocal review patterns, reviewer profiles matching known review-exchange/gig-marketplace activity.
steps.guidance: Paid-ring reviews tend to read as more varied and human than bot text but share suspicious reviewer-account overlap; cross-check reviewer handles against known review-exchange groups where possible.
steps.outcome: Documented evidence the reviews originate from a paid ring, or a determination the reviews are genuine.
steps.abort: If evidence of a paid ring cannot be established, treat as ordinary competitive activity and stand down.

steps.title: Report the paid reviewer ring to each affected platform
steps.desc: Submit a formal paid/incentivized-review violation report with the supporting reviewer-pattern evidence to each platform's review-integrity team; most platforms explicitly prohibit undisclosed paid reviews.

steps.title: Follow up until the platform removes the confirmed paid reviews
steps.desc: Track the platform's enforcement action and escalate if removal doesn't occur within a reasonable window.
steps.outcome: Paid reviews removed or the competitor's rating corrected.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Watch for the ring resuming activity on the same or other platforms.
steps.outcome: No renewed activity observed, or caught early.

steps.title: Document the ring's pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the reviewer-overlap and language signatures observed to speed detection of future paid-ring campaigns.

steps.title: Determine scale, platforms, and the specific unfavorable claims about this organization
steps.desc: Catalog every platform where the ring is active and record the exact disparaging or comparative language used against this organization.

steps.title: Assess legal exposure for false comparative claims
steps.desc: Where the ring's reviews make false, factual (not opinion) unfavorable claims about this organization, consult legal on unfair-competition or defamation exposure.

ITID-24213.def: A campaign designed to look like organic, independent grassroots enthusiasm for a competitor's product/service, which includes unfavorable references to the organization, but which is in fact orchestrated (e.g., by a marketing team or PR firm) rather than genuinely organic.
ITID-24213.purpose: Captures a grassroots-styled astroturfing campaign praising a competitor while unfavorably referencing the organization, without the paid-ring or bot-network infrastructure of sibling leaves.
scopeIncludes: Coordinated posting patterns across seemingly independent accounts/blogs praising a competitor and disparaging the organization, with evidence of central orchestration (shared talking points, coordinated timing)
Sock-puppet 'independent enthusiast' blog or forum content traceable to a marketing/PR operation
scopeExcludes: Bot-network-generated reviews (ITID-24211)
Paid human reviewer rings (ITID-24212)
Genuine organic grassroots enthusiasm for a competitor with no orchestration evidence
ITID-24213.severity: Low-to-Medium; a comparative-market-perception harm rather than a direct attack on the organization's own listings.
ITID-24213.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if part of a broader coordinated campaign.
ITID-24213.escalation: Escalate to brand/competitive-intelligence for awareness; legal only where comparative claims are factually false and defamatory.
indicators: Identical or near-identical talking points appearing across supposedly independent accounts/blogs
Coordinated timing of 'organic' posts around a competitor product launch
vectors: Orchestrated astroturfing via a marketing/PR firm simulating grassroots enthusiasm
rootCauses: No monitoring of competitor-favorable content for orchestration/talking-point overlap patterns
controls: Competitive content monitoring for talking-point overlap and coordination patterns
ITID-24213.detection: Relies on content-similarity and coordination-pattern analysis via brand/competitive-monitoring tools; no technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24213.response: Document the pattern for competitive-intelligence awareness; escalate to legal only where factually false comparative claims rise to defamation.
metrics: Count of astroturfing patterns identified per quarter
ITID-24213.notes: No MITRE mapping applies — purely social/behavioral orchestration, not adversary infrastructure. Differentiated from sibling 24211/24212 by the absence of bot or paid-ring infrastructure; this is simulated-grassroots orchestration.

playbook.name: Response: Astroturfed Competitor Praise Campaign Referencing Organization Unfavorably
playbook.description: An orchestrated astroturfing campaign (fabricated grassroots appearance, e.g. coordinated social posts, seeded forum threads, fake blog testimonials) praises a competitor while unfavorably referencing this organization.

steps.title: Establish that the campaign is astroturfed rather than genuine grassroots sentiment
steps.desc: Trace the origin and spread of the praise content across platforms — look for near-simultaneous posting, shared templated language, accounts with no history predating the campaign, or a common seeding source (e.g. a single forum thread or PR firm).
steps.outcome: Documented evidence of coordination/fabricated origin, or a determination the sentiment is organic.
steps.abort: If genuine, redirect to competitive-intelligence/marketing rather than treating as an attack.

steps.title: Report the coordinated inauthentic content to each affected platform
steps.desc: File coordinated-inauthentic-behavior reports with each platform's trust-and-safety team, providing the cross-account evidence of coordination.

steps.title: Follow up until platforms take enforcement action
steps.desc: Track each platform's response and escalate if content isn't removed or labeled within a reasonable window.

steps.title: Monitor for a resumed or shifted campaign
steps.desc: Watch for the same operators re-seeding the narrative on new platforms.
steps.outcome: No renewed campaign, or caught early.

steps.title: Document the astroturfing pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the coordination signatures and seeding methods observed to speed detection of future astroturfing campaigns.

steps.title: Map the full campaign footprint and the specific claims made about this organization
steps.desc: Identify every platform, publication, and account involved, and document the exact unfavorable statements about this organization for evidentiary use.
steps.outcome: Complete campaign map and documented claims.

steps.title: Assess legal exposure for false unfavorable claims
steps.desc: Consult legal where the astroturfed content makes false factual claims about this organization, to evaluate defamation or unfair-competition options.

ITID-24214.def: A suspected fake-positive-review-for-competitor incident awaiting further investigation to determine its specific mechanism before reclassification to the appropriate sibling ITID.
ITID-24214.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for a suspected fake-positive-review-for-competitor incident not yet triaged to the bot-network, paid-ring, or astroturfing mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Newly-detected comparative-praise patterns not yet triaged to a specific mechanism
scopeExcludes: Any incident for which the mechanism has been confirmed and should be reclassified to ITID-24211, ITID-24212, or ITID-24213
ITID-24214.escalation: Escalate to the brand/competitive-intelligence analyst on triage duty; reclassify once the mechanism is clear.
indicators: An unexplained comparative-praise pattern favoring a competitor without yet-established mechanism attribution
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial evidence to attribute mechanism at time of intake
controls: Competitive review-sentiment monitoring
ITID-24214.detection: Same detection surface as sibling leaves, pending mechanism attribution.
ITID-24214.response: Triage promptly and reclassify to the specific sibling ITID once the mechanism is clear.
metrics: Count of incidents held in this bucket beyond 5 business days without reclassification
ITID-24214.notes: Intake/triage bucket only, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General False Positive Reviews for Competitor
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for a false positive review campaign benefiting a competitor at this organization's expense that does not fit the bot-network, paid-ring, or astroturfing sub-patterns.

steps.title: Characterize the review pattern and determine inauthenticity
steps.desc: Analyze the flagged reviews for whatever inauthenticity signals are present (account patterns, timing, language, incentive structure) and classify the mechanism if possible.
steps.outcome: Documented evidence of inauthenticity and, where possible, a refined classification into a more specific sub-pattern.
steps.abort: If the reviews appear genuine, redirect to marketing/competitive-intelligence.

steps.title: Report the inauthentic reviews to each affected platform
steps.desc: Submit an inauthentic-activity report with supporting evidence to each platform's review-integrity team.

steps.title: Follow up until the platform takes enforcement action
steps.desc: Track the platform's response and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Watch for the campaign resuming or shifting platforms.
steps.outcome: No renewed campaign, or caught early.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record observed signatures to speed detection of future incidents in this category.

steps.title: Determine scale, platforms, and specific claims about this organization
steps.desc: Catalog affected platforms and document any disparaging or comparative claims made about this organization.

steps.title: Assess legal exposure for false claims
steps.desc: Consult legal where false factual claims about this organization are involved.

ITID-24221.def: A campaign in which fake positive reviews are posted to a counterfeit product listing impersonating or trading on the organization's brand, to make the fraudulent listing appear trustworthy to buyers.
ITID-24221.purpose: Captures fake positive reviews used to legitimize a counterfeit product listing that trades on the organization's brand.
scopeIncludes: Fake positive reviews on a listing selling counterfeit goods under the organization's brand name/trademark
Reviews praising product attributes inconsistent with the organization's actual genuine product
scopeExcludes: Fake positive reviews supporting a scam storefront not selling counterfeit branded goods specifically (ITID-24222)
Fake positive reviews supporting a fraudulent app listing (ITID-24223)
The counterfeit listing itself, which is tracked under brand/trademark-infringement ITIDs elsewhere in the taxonomy — this leaf covers only the review-manipulation layer supporting it
ITID-24221.severity: High; directly enables customer harm (receiving counterfeit goods) and trademark dilution under the organization's name.
ITID-24221.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for high-volume marketplace exposure or documented consumer harm/complaints.
ITID-24221.escalation: Escalate to legal (trademark/brand protection) and the marketplace's counterfeit-reporting channel immediately; loop in customer support if consumer complaints are being misdirected to the organization.
indicators: Fake positive reviews on a listing using the organization's brand imagery/trademark without authorization
Product description or reviews inconsistent with the organization's actual product specifications
Customer complaints reaching the organization about a product it did not sell
vectors: Counterfeit listing creation paired with fake-review seeding to build apparent trust
rootCauses: No proactive marketplace scanning for unauthorized listings using the organization's brand assets
No standing relationship with major marketplaces' counterfeit/brand-protection reporting programs
controls: Marketplace brand-protection scanning for unauthorized listings
Established counterfeit-reporting relationship with major marketplaces
ITID-24221.detection: Detected via brand-protection/marketplace-scanning tools; not a technical/network detection surface, though the counterfeit-goods harm itself can trigger customer-support signal.
ITID-24221.response: Report the listing to the marketplace's counterfeit/brand-protection program for takedown, redirect misdirected customer complaints, and coordinate with legal on trademark enforcement.
metrics: Counterfeit listing takedown volume and time-to-removal
Misdirected customer complaint volume
ITID-24221.notes: Scoped to the review-manipulation layer only; the underlying counterfeit listing itself is tracked under a separate brand/trademark-infringement ITID elsewhere in the taxonomy to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Positive Reviews Supporting Counterfeit Product Listing
