playbook.description: Fake positive reviews are propping up a counterfeit product listing that falsely bears this organization's brand, misleading buyers into believing they are purchasing a genuine product.

steps.title: Confirm the listing is counterfeit and the reviews are inauthentic
steps.desc: Compare the listed product against genuine SKUs (packaging, imagery, model/serial conventions, seller identity) to confirm counterfeit status, and analyze the reviews for bot/incentivized-review signatures propping up its rating.
steps.guidance: Involve brand-protection/product teams to make the counterfeit determination authoritatively.
steps.outcome: Documented confirmation the product is counterfeit and the supporting reviews are inauthentic.
steps.abort: If the product is genuine (e.g. an authorized reseller) and reviews are organic, stand down.

steps.title: Report the fake reviews and the counterfeit listing together to the marketplace
steps.desc: Submit a combined inauthentic-review report and brand/counterfeit-infringement report to the marketplace's trust-and-safety and IP-enforcement channels.
steps.guidance: Most marketplaces (e.g. Amazon Brand Registry, eBay VeRO) have a dedicated counterfeit-reporting program separate from generic review disputes — use it for faster action.

steps.title: Confirm removal of both the counterfeit listing and its fake reviews
steps.desc: Track the marketplace's response and escalate if the listing or reviews remain live beyond a reasonable window.
steps.outcome: Listing and its supporting fake reviews removed.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence and consider a customer advisory
steps.desc: Continue monitoring the marketplace and, if the counterfeit had meaningful reach, consider publishing guidance for customers on how to identify genuine products.
steps.outcome: No renewed listing, or customers informed.

steps.title: Document the counterfeit and fake-review pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the listing/seller signatures and review-inauthenticity indicators to speed detection of similar future counterfeit listings.

steps.title: Capture evidence of the listing, seller, and reviews
steps.desc: Screenshot the listing, seller profile, and flagged reviews, and record the marketplace, listing ID, and seller ID for the takedown submission.

steps.title: Engage legal/brand-protection on the counterfeit listing itself
steps.desc: Hand the listing and seller details to legal/brand-protection to pursue takedown under trademark/IP enforcement, independent of the review-report track.
steps.outcome: Legal/brand-protection engaged and pursuing the IP-enforcement route in parallel.

steps.title: Search for duplicate or relisted counterfeit listings
steps.desc: Sellers of counterfeit goods commonly relist under new seller IDs after a takedown; search the marketplace and other channels for reappearance.
steps.outcome: No active duplicate listings found, or newly found listings reported.

ITID-24222.def: A campaign in which fake positive reviews are posted on a standalone scam e-commerce storefront (a dedicated fraudulent website, not a marketplace listing) that impersonates the organization's brand to build purchaser trust before defrauding customers.
ITID-24222.purpose: Captures fake positive reviews used to legitimize a scam e-commerce storefront impersonating the organization, distinct from a counterfeit-goods marketplace listing.
scopeIncludes: Fake positive reviews/testimonials embedded on a standalone fraudulent storefront website impersonating the organization
Fabricated review widgets or trust badges on the scam site
scopeExcludes: Fake positive reviews on a legitimate marketplace's counterfeit listing (ITID-24221)
Fake positive reviews supporting a fraudulent app listing (ITID-24223)
The scam storefront/domain itself, tracked under a separate phishing/brand-impersonation ITID elsewhere in the taxonomy — this leaf covers only the embedded review-manipulation layer
ITID-24222.severity: High; directly enables financial fraud against customers under the organization's brand.
ITID-24222.priority: P1 given active financial fraud risk to customers.
ITID-24222.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, fraud/customer-protection, and the domain registrar/hosting provider for takedown; notify customer support to prepare for inbound fraud-victim inquiries.
indicators: A domain impersonating the organization's brand hosting fake reviews/testimonials
Customer reports of purchases never received from a look-alike site
Fabricated review counts/star ratings not backed by any real review platform
vectors: Fake review widgets and fabricated testimonials embedded directly on a scam storefront
rootCauses: No proactive domain-monitoring for brand-impersonating storefronts
No rapid takedown relationship with hosting providers/registrars
controls: Brand-impersonation domain monitoring
Rapid takedown relationship with hosting providers/registrars
ITID-24222.detection: Detected via domain/brand-monitoring tools and customer fraud reports; not a technical/network detection surface for the review content itself.
ITID-24222.response: Initiate rapid domain takedown, issue a customer-facing fraud warning, and coordinate with legal and fraud teams on affected-customer remediation.
metrics: Scam storefront takedown time
Customer fraud-report volume
ITID-24222.notes: Scoped to the embedded fake-review/testimonial layer only; the underlying scam domain/storefront itself is tracked under a separate brand-impersonation/phishing ITID elsewhere in the taxonomy to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Positive Reviews Supporting Scam E-Commerce Storefront
playbook.description: Fake positive reviews are propping up a scam e-commerce storefront (a site or marketplace store, often never fulfilling orders or shipping counterfeit/nonexistent goods) that falsely uses this organization's brand.

steps.title: Confirm the storefront is fraudulent and impersonates this organization's brand
steps.desc: Assess the storefront for scam indicators (unofficial domain, no verifiable business registration, unrealistic pricing, no genuine fulfillment) and confirm unauthorized use of this organization's brand/trademarks.
steps.outcome: Documented confirmation the storefront is fraudulent and brand-infringing.
steps.abort: If the storefront is a legitimate authorized reseller, stand down.

steps.title: Report the storefront and its fake reviews to the hosting platform/marketplace and registrar
steps.desc: Submit a fraud/brand-impersonation report to the hosting platform or marketplace, and a separate abuse report to the domain registrar if the storefront is an independent site.
steps.outcome: Reports submitted to all relevant parties.

steps.title: Confirm the storefront and its reviews are taken down
steps.desc: Track host/registrar/platform response and escalate if action isn't taken within a reasonable window.
steps.outcome: Storefront taken offline or removed from the marketplace.

steps.title: Publish a factual advisory if customer harm is likely
steps.desc: Where customers may have been defrauded, publish guidance on official channels for identifying genuine storefronts and reporting the fraud.

steps.title: Document the storefront and review pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the fraudulent-storefront and fake-review signatures observed to speed detection of similar future scams.

steps.title: Capture evidence of the storefront, hosting/registrar, and supporting reviews
steps.desc: Screenshot the storefront, note its domain/registrar or marketplace host, and document the fake reviews propping up its credibility.

steps.title: Engage legal/brand-protection for takedown and warn affected customers if identifiable
steps.desc: Hand the case to legal/brand-protection to pursue formal takedown, and coordinate with customer-support to warn any customers who may have engaged with the storefront.
steps.outcome: Legal/brand-protection engaged; affected customers alerted where identifiable.

ITID-24223.def: A campaign in which fake positive reviews are posted on an app-store listing for a fraudulent application impersonating the organization's brand, to drive installs before delivering malware or defrauding users.
ITID-24223.purpose: Captures fake positive reviews used to legitimize a fraudulent mobile-app listing impersonating the organization's brand.
scopeIncludes: Fake positive reviews on an app-store listing using the organization's brand name/icon without authorization
Reviews praising features that do not match the organization's actual legitimate app
scopeExcludes: Fake positive reviews on a counterfeit marketplace listing (ITID-24221)
Fake positive reviews on a scam website storefront (ITID-24222)
The fraudulent app itself and any malware it delivers, tracked under a separate mobile-app-impersonation/malware ITID elsewhere in the taxonomy — this leaf covers only the review-manipulation layer
ITID-24223.severity: High; directly enables malware distribution or fraud against users under the organization's brand.
ITID-24223.priority: P1 given potential malware-distribution risk to end users.
ITID-24223.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, security/threat-intel (to assess malware payload if present), and the app store's fraudulent-listing reporting channel.
indicators: Fake positive reviews on an app-store listing using unauthorized organization branding
App permissions or behavior inconsistent with the organization's legitimate app
User reports of the fraudulent app requesting excessive permissions or exhibiting malicious behavior
vectors: Fraudulent app listing paired with fake-review seeding to drive install volume and app-store ranking
rootCauses: No proactive app-store monitoring for unauthorized listings using the organization's brand assets
No standing relationship with major app stores' fraudulent-app reporting programs
controls: App-store brand-protection monitoring
Established fraudulent-app reporting relationship with app store platforms
ITID-24223.detection: Detected via app-store brand-monitoring tools and user complaint signal; malware analysis of the app itself (if obtained) is a separate technical detection surface owned by security/threat-intel, not this review-manipulation leaf.
ITID-24223.response: Report the listing to the app store for expedited takedown, coordinate with security/threat-intel if malware is suspected, and issue a customer-facing warning if install volume is significant.
metrics: Fraudulent app-listing takedown time
Estimated affected-install volume
ITID-24223.notes: Scoped to the review-manipulation layer only; the underlying fraudulent app and any malware payload are tracked under a separate mobile-app-impersonation ITID elsewhere in the taxonomy to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Positive Reviews Supporting Fraudulent App Listing
playbook.description: Fake positive reviews are propping up a fraudulent mobile-app listing that impersonates this organization's brand (e.g. a fake 'official app' clone) in an app store.

steps.title: Confirm the app listing is fraudulent/impersonating and reviews are inauthentic
steps.desc: Compare the listing's developer identity, icon, screenshots, and permissions against the genuine app; analyze the flagged reviews for bot/incentivized-review signatures inflating its rating.
steps.guidance: Involve mobile/security engineering to assess whether the app itself is malicious (e.g. credential harvesting) in addition to being a brand impersonation.
steps.outcome: Documented confirmation of impersonation and inauthentic reviews.
steps.abort: If the listing is a legitimate third-party integration, stand down.

steps.title: Report the fraudulent app and its fake reviews to the app store operator
steps.desc: Submit a brand-impersonation and inauthentic-review report through the app store's developer/IP-enforcement and trust-and-safety channels, flagging any security risk found.
steps.guidance: App stores typically prioritize takedown when a security or malware risk is documented.

steps.title: Confirm the app listing and its fake reviews are removed
steps.desc: Track the app store's response and escalate if the listing remains live beyond a reasonable window.
steps.outcome: App listing removed from the store.

steps.title: Monitor app stores for relisting under a new developer account
steps.desc: Fraudulent app operators commonly resubmit under new accounts; monitor for reappearance.
steps.outcome: No new impersonating listing found, or newly found listings reported.

steps.title: Document the impersonation and review pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the app-listing and fake-review signatures observed to speed detection of similar future fraudulent app listings.

steps.title: Capture evidence and assess whether the app poses a security risk to installers
steps.desc: Screenshot the listing and reviews, note the developer account and app ID, and, if feasible, have security engineering assess the app package for malicious behavior.
steps.outcome: Evidence package assembled; risk to installers assessed.

steps.title: Warn users/customers if the app poses a credential or data risk
steps.desc: If the fraudulent app was found to harvest credentials or data, coordinate with security and communications to warn affected or potentially affected users.

ITID-24224.def: A suspected fake-positive-review incident supporting an as-yet-unclassified fake product/service offering, awaiting further investigation before reclassification to the appropriate sibling ITID.
ITID-24224.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for a suspected fake-positive-review-for-fake-product/service incident not yet triaged to the counterfeit-listing, scam-storefront, or fraudulent-app mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Newly-detected fake-review patterns supporting an unidentified fraudulent offering type
scopeExcludes: Any incident for which the offering type has been confirmed and should be reclassified to ITID-24221, ITID-24222, or ITID-24223
ITID-24224.severity: Medium-High pending triage given the general fraud-risk profile of this group.
ITID-24224.escalation: Escalate to legal/brand-protection on triage duty; reclassify promptly once the offering type is confirmed.
indicators: Fake reviews supporting an unidentified fraudulent product/service offering
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial evidence to classify offering type at time of intake
controls: Marketplace/domain/app-store brand-protection monitoring
ITID-24224.detection: Same detection surface as sibling leaves, pending offering-type attribution.
ITID-24224.response: Triage promptly and reclassify to the specific sibling ITID once the offering type is clear.
metrics: Count of incidents held in this bucket beyond 5 business days without reclassification
ITID-24224.notes: Intake/triage bucket only, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Positive Reviews of Fake Product/Service
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for fake positive reviews propping up a fraudulent product or service listing bearing this organization's brand that does not fit the counterfeit-product, scam-storefront, or fraudulent-app sub-patterns.

steps.title: Confirm the listing is fraudulent/brand-infringing and the reviews are inauthentic
steps.desc: Assess the listing for indicators it is not a genuine, authorized offering of this organization, and analyze the supporting reviews for inauthenticity signatures.
steps.outcome: Documented confirmation of fraud/infringement and inauthentic reviews.
steps.abort: If the listing is legitimate, stand down.

steps.title: Report the listing and its fake reviews to the hosting platform
steps.desc: Submit a combined brand-infringement and inauthentic-review report to the platform's relevant enforcement channel.

steps.title: Confirm removal of the listing and its fake reviews
steps.desc: Track the platform's response and escalate if action isn't taken within a reasonable window.

steps.title: Monitor for relisting or recurrence
steps.desc: Watch for the same or a similar fraudulent listing reappearing.
steps.outcome: No renewed listing, or caught early.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record observed signatures to speed detection of future incidents in this category.

steps.title: Capture evidence of the listing and reviews
steps.desc: Screenshot the listing, seller/operator details, and flagged reviews for the takedown submission.

steps.title: Engage legal/brand-protection on the underlying fraudulent listing
steps.desc: Hand the case to legal/brand-protection to pursue takedown independent of the review-report track.

ITID-24231.def: The use of fraudulent (fake or bot-driven) upvotes/likes to artificially boost the visibility and perceived legitimacy of scam or fraudulent content — such as phishing posts, fake giveaways, or counterfeit promotions — that misuses the organization's brand.
ITID-24231.purpose: Captures fraudulent upvoting used to boost the visibility of scam or fraudulent content that trades on or targets the organization's brand.
scopeIncludes: Fraudulent upvoting of posts, comments, or listings that are themselves scam/fraudulent content misusing the organization's brand
Bot-driven engagement inflating the apparent popularity of a phishing or fake-giveaway post
scopeExcludes: Fraudulent upvoting used to suppress legitimate negative feedback about the organization (ITID-24232)
Fraudulent upvoting via a dedicated bot network as the defining mechanism, tracked separately when the network itself (not the content boosted) is the salient feature (ITID-24233)
The underlying scam content itself, tracked under a separate phishing/brand-impersonation ITID elsewhere in the taxonomy
ITID-24231.severity: Medium-High; boosted scam content directly increases the likelihood of customer victimization.
ITID-24231.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the boosted content is an active phishing or financial-fraud vector.
ITID-24231.escalation: Escalate to security/threat-intel if the content is phishing, and to the platform's fraud/trust-and-safety team for content and engagement takedown.
indicators: A scam/phishing post with engagement metrics far exceeding what its actual reach/audience would organically generate
Engagement traceable to fake or bot accounts with no genuine interaction history
vectors: Bot or fake-account upvoting/liking to boost a scam post's algorithmic visibility
rootCauses: No monitoring for brand-impersonating content with anomalous engagement-to-reach ratios
controls: Brand-impersonation content monitoring with engagement-anomaly detection
ITID-24231.detection: Detected via social-listening/brand-monitoring tools tracking engagement-to-reach anomalies on brand-referencing content; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24231.response: Report the content and its fraudulent engagement to the platform for takedown, and alert customers if the scam is actively soliciting sensitive information or payment.
metrics: Count of fraudulently-boosted scam posts identified per quarter
Takedown time
ITID-24231.notes: Scoped to upvoting that boosts external scam content; the scam content itself is tracked under a separate phishing/brand-impersonation ITID elsewhere in the taxonomy to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Fraudulent Upvoting of Scam/Fraudulent Content
playbook.description: Fraudulent (bot or paid) upvoting is being used to boost the visibility/credibility of scam or fraudulent content that targets this organization's customers or misuses its brand (e.g. an upvoted phishing link disguised as a deal, a fraudulent giveaway post).

steps.title: Confirm the content is fraudulent and the upvotes are inauthentic
steps.desc: Assess the underlying content for scam/fraud indicators, and analyze the voting pattern for bot signatures — vote velocity spikes, low-karma/new voter accounts, coordinated timing.
steps.outcome: Documented confirmation the content is fraudulent and the upvoting is inauthentic.
steps.abort: If the content is legitimate and organically popular, stand down.

steps.title: Report the fraudulent content and the vote manipulation to the platform
steps.desc: Submit both a fraud/scam-content report and a vote-manipulation report to the platform's trust-and-safety team.

steps.title: Confirm the content is removed and vote manipulation addressed
steps.desc: Track the platform's response and escalate if the content remains visible beyond a reasonable window.
steps.outcome: Content removed or its ranking corrected.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence of similar fraudulent content
steps.desc: Watch for repost or variant scam content targeting the same audience.
steps.outcome: No renewed content, or caught early.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the vote-manipulation and content signatures observed to speed detection of future incidents.

steps.title: Determine reach and whether customers have already been harmed
steps.desc: Estimate how many users likely saw or engaged with the fraudulent content given its artificially boosted visibility, and check support/fraud channels for reports of harm.

steps.title: Warn potentially affected customers
steps.desc: If the fraudulent content targeted customers directly (e.g. a fake giveaway or phishing link), issue a warning via official channels.

ITID-24232.def: The use of fraudulent (fake or bot-driven) downvotes/reports against a legitimate negative review, or upvotes on unrelated content, to push genuine negative feedback out of visibility on a platform's ranking algorithm.
ITID-24232.purpose: Captures fraudulent upvoting used to bury or suppress the visibility of legitimate, genuine negative feedback about the organization.
scopeIncludes: Fraudulent mass-downvoting or mass-reporting of a genuine negative review to suppress its visibility or trigger its removal
Fraudulent upvoting of other content specifically timed to bury a genuine negative review in ranking order
scopeExcludes: Fraudulent upvoting boosting external scam content (ITID-24231)
Legitimate use of a platform's dispute/appeal process to contest a review that violates platform policy (e.g., a fake review being legitimately reported)
ITID-24232.severity: Medium; this is a self-serving suppression tactic rather than an attack, but still constitutes platform-policy violation and ethical/reputational risk if discovered.
ITID-24232.priority: P3 for monitoring/awareness; treat as an internal-conduct risk requiring immediate escalation if traced to organization-affiliated actors.
ITID-24232.escalation: If traced to an organization-affiliated actor (employee, agency, or vendor), escalate immediately to legal, ethics/compliance, and executive leadership given the reputational and platform-policy risk of being caught suppressing genuine feedback.
indicators: A genuine negative review disappearing or losing visibility shortly after an anomalous downvote/report spike
Suppression activity traceable to accounts or infrastructure associated with the organization or its agents
vectors: Fraudulent mass-downvoting or mass-reporting of genuine negative feedback
rootCauses: No internal policy or oversight preventing marketing/PR teams from engaging in review-suppression tactics
No monitoring to detect if organization-affiliated actors are engaging in this conduct
controls: Internal policy prohibiting review-suppression tactics
Monitoring for organization-affiliated involvement in suppression activity
ITID-24232.detection: Detected via anomaly monitoring on review visibility/ranking changes; attribution to organization-affiliated actors requires internal investigation, not a technical detection surface.
ITID-24232.response: If traced to an external attacker suppressing feedback for unrelated reasons, treat as a platform-integrity report; if traced to an organization-affiliated actor, treat as an internal-conduct investigation with legal/ethics involvement.
metrics: Count of suppression-pattern incidents identified per quarter
Count attributed to internal vs. external actors
ITID-24232.notes: This leaf uniquely covers the risk of the organization's OWN agents engaging in suppression tactics, not just external attackers — internal attribution triggers ethics/compliance rather than pure brand-defense response.

playbook.name: Response: Fraudulent Upvoting to Suppress Legitimate Negative Feedback
playbook.description: Fraudulent upvoting/downvoting is being used to bury or suppress genuine, legitimate negative feedback about this organization (e.g. mass-downvoting a valid complaint thread, upvoting distracting or off-topic content to push it off the front page).

steps.title: Confirm the vote manipulation and identify the legitimate feedback being suppressed
steps.desc: Analyze the voting pattern on the affected thread(s) for bot/coordination signatures, and confirm whether the negative feedback being suppressed is itself legitimate and factually grounded.
steps.guidance: This step matters because the underlying feedback being suppressed may be a real issue this organization needs to address on its own merits, independent of the vote manipulation.
steps.outcome: Documented confirmation of vote manipulation, and a determination of whether the underlying complaint is valid.
steps.abort: If no vote manipulation is evident, treat the negative feedback as ordinary customer sentiment and route to the appropriate business owner.

steps.title: Report the vote manipulation to the platform
steps.desc: Submit a vote-manipulation report to the platform's trust-and-safety team, noting that manipulation is suppressing legitimate discourse rather than promoting inauthentic content.

steps.title: Confirm the platform restores visibility of the legitimate feedback or corrects the manipulated ranking
steps.desc: Track the platform's response and escalate if the manipulation isn't addressed within a reasonable window.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence and for public perception that the organization was trying to hide the complaint
steps.desc: Watch for renewed manipulation and for any narrative suggesting the organization itself suppressed the feedback, which would require a transparency response.
steps.outcome: No renewed manipulation and no adverse perception issue, or issues caught early.

steps.title: Document the pattern and the underlying complaint's resolution for future reference
steps.desc: Record the manipulation signature and confirm the underlying legitimate issue was tracked to resolution, not just the manipulation.

steps.title: Determine who benefits from the suppression
steps.desc: Assess whether the suppression appears self-inflicted (e.g. an overzealous internal or agency actor) versus a third party trying to hide a legitimate issue from public view — this affects containment and disclosure decisions.

steps.title: Address the legitimate underlying complaint through normal channels regardless of the manipulation finding
steps.desc: Route the underlying valid complaint to customer support/product/PR for a genuine response, independent of whether the platform acts on the vote-manipulation report.
steps.guidance: Suppressing awareness of a real problem is not remediation; the organization should still respond to the substance.
steps.outcome: Underlying issue acknowledged and being addressed on its own track.

ITID-24233.def: Fraudulent upvoting/engagement activity attributable to a specific, identifiable bot network whose infrastructure (account clusters, automation signatures) is reused across multiple targets, distinguishing it from a one-off or purpose-built engagement-boosting effort.
ITID-24233.purpose: Captures fraudulent upvoting executed via a dedicated, identifiable bot network, where the network infrastructure itself (reusable across targets) is the defining and most actionable characteristic.
scopeIncludes: Fraudulent upvoting traceable to a bot network with a known, reusable infrastructure signature seen targeting multiple unrelated posts/brands
Cases where the bot network itself, not the specific content boosted or suppressed, is the primary investigative lead
scopeExcludes: Fraudulent upvoting boosting scam content where the content is the primary concern rather than the network (ITID-24231)
Fraudulent downvoting/suppression of genuine feedback (ITID-24232)
ITID-24233.severity: Medium; severity depends more on what the network is used for in a given instance than the network's existence alone.
ITID-24233.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if the same network is found actively engaged with the organization's brand on multiple occasions.
ITID-24233.escalation: Escalate to threat-intel/brand-protection to track the network's infrastructure signature over time; report to the platform's trust-and-safety team for network-level takedown.
indicators: Engagement activity matching a known bot-network infrastructure signature (shared registration patterns, automation fingerprints)
The same network signature observed engaging with multiple unrelated brands/targets
vectors: Reusable commercial or underground bot-network infrastructure sold/rented for engagement fraud
rootCauses: No threat-intelligence tracking of known bot-network infrastructure signatures relevant to the brand's platforms
controls: Threat-intelligence tracking of known bot-network infrastructure signatures
Platform-level network takedown reporting relationship
ITID-24233.detection: Detected via infrastructure-signature correlation using brand-monitoring/threat-intel tooling; the closest thing to a technical detection surface in this sibling group given the reusable, fingerprint-able network infrastructure.
ITID-24233.response: Report the network signature to the platform for network-level takedown, and track the network across future incidents via threat-intel.
metrics: Count of incidents attributed to tracked bot networks per quarter
ITID-24233.notes: This is the one leaf in its sibling group with a genuine reusable adversary-infrastructure mechanism, warranting the Resource Development/T1585 mapping, distinguishing it from content-specific siblings 24231/24232.

playbook.name: Response: Fraudulent Upvoting via Bot Network
playbook.description: A confirmed bot network (as opposed to a manual brigade or unclear actor) is fraudulently upvoting content in a way that affects this organization's public perception — either boosting harmful content or suppressing legitimate discourse.

steps.title: Confirm the vote pattern is bot-driven and characterize the affected content
steps.desc: Analyze vote velocity, timing, and voter-account characteristics (creation date, activity history, device/IP clustering where visible) to confirm bot involvement, and determine whether the boosted content is harmful or the suppressed content is legitimate.
steps.outcome: Documented confirmation of bot-driven voting and a clear picture of its effect (promotion vs. suppression).
steps.abort: If the pattern does not hold up as bot-driven, stand down or reclassify.

steps.title: Report the bot network to the platform
steps.desc: Submit a vote-manipulation/bot-network report with the supporting technical evidence to the platform's trust-and-safety or anti-abuse team.

steps.title: Confirm the platform removes the bot votes and corrects the affected ranking
steps.desc: Track the platform's response and escalate if action isn't taken within a reasonable window.
steps.outcome: Bot votes removed and content ranking corrected.

steps.title: Monitor for the bot network resuming activity
steps.desc: Watch for the same network fingerprint reappearing on this or other platforms.
steps.outcome: No renewed activity, or caught early.

steps.title: Document the bot network's fingerprint for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the technical signatures observed (timing, account patterns) to speed detection of this network's future activity.

steps.title: Determine scale and whether the same network is active elsewhere
steps.desc: Check whether the identified bot network has fingerprints matching activity on other platforms or against other content involving this organization.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the bot network's activity established.

steps.title: Escalate for expedited review if content is actively harmful
steps.desc: Where the boosted content poses active harm (scam, safety, or reputational risk) rather than routine manipulation, request expedited platform review.

ITID-24234.def: A suspected fraudulent-upvoting incident awaiting further investigation to determine its specific mechanism and target before reclassification to the appropriate sibling ITID.
ITID-24234.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for a suspected fraudulent-upvoting incident not yet triaged to the scam-boosting, suppression, or bot-network mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Newly-detected engagement-fraud patterns not yet triaged to a specific mechanism
scopeExcludes: Any incident for which the mechanism has been confirmed and should be reclassified to ITID-24231, ITID-24232, or ITID-24233
ITID-24234.escalation: Escalate to the brand/reputation analyst on triage duty; reclassify promptly once the mechanism is clear.
indicators: An unexplained engagement-fraud pattern without yet-established mechanism attribution
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial evidence to attribute mechanism at time of intake
controls: Brand-monitoring engagement-anomaly detection
ITID-24234.detection: Same detection surface as sibling leaves, pending mechanism attribution.
ITID-24234.response: Triage promptly and reclassify to the specific sibling ITID once the mechanism is clear.
metrics: Count of incidents held in this bucket beyond 5 business days without reclassification
ITID-24234.notes: Intake/triage bucket only, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Fraudulent Upvoting
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for fraudulent upvoting/vote-manipulation activity affecting this organization's public perception that does not fit the scam-content, suppression, or bot-network sub-patterns.

steps.title: Confirm the vote manipulation and characterize its effect
steps.desc: Analyze the voting pattern for manipulation signatures and determine whether it is promoting harmful content or suppressing legitimate content concerning this organization.
steps.outcome: Documented confirmation of manipulation and its effect.
steps.abort: If no manipulation is evident, stand down.

steps.title: Report the vote manipulation to the platform
steps.desc: Submit a vote-manipulation report with supporting evidence to the platform's trust-and-safety team.

steps.title: Confirm the platform corrects the manipulated ranking
steps.desc: Track the platform's response and escalate if unresolved beyond a reasonable window.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Watch for renewed manipulation.
steps.outcome: No renewed activity, or caught early.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record observed signatures to speed detection of future incidents in this category.

steps.title: Determine scale and platforms affected
steps.desc: Check for the same or similar manipulation occurring on other platforms.

steps.title: Address any underlying legitimate issue independently
steps.desc: If suppressed content reflects a genuine concern, route it to the appropriate business owner regardless of the platform's response to the manipulation report.
steps.outcome: Underlying issue tracked separately where applicable.

ITID-24311.def: A social media post or thread falsely claiming the organization's product has a safety defect, contamination issue, or an active/pending recall, when no such issue or recall exists.
ITID-24311.purpose: Captures a social media misinformation post fabricating a product safety issue or recall that never occurred, aimed at damaging consumer trust in the organization's products.
scopeIncludes: Posts fabricating a specific safety defect, contamination, or recall claim with no basis in the organization's actual quality/recall records
Fabricated 'leaked' recall notices or safety-agency documents
scopeExcludes: Genuine customer safety complaints about an actual product issue (a product-quality/customer-escalation matter, not this ITID)
Fabricated executive-scandal claims (ITID-24312)
Fabricated data-breach/security claims (ITID-24313)
ITID-24311.severity: High; false safety/recall claims can trigger genuine consumer panic, regulatory inquiries, and rapid sales impact.
ITID-24311.priority: P1 given the potential for regulatory attention and rapid viral spread.
ITID-24311.escalation: Escalate immediately to communications/PR, legal, and regulatory-affairs (in case a real regulator inquires based on the false claim); issue a factual public correction as quickly as possible.
indicators: A viral post referencing a specific alleged defect/recall with no corroborating record in the organization's actual quality or regulatory filings
Fabricated or doctored 'official' recall documents circulating
vectors: Fabricated safety/recall claims posted for virality, financial manipulation (e.g., short-selling), or malicious brand attack
rootCauses: No rapid-response fact-check protocol for viral safety/recall misinformation
No proactive monitoring for the organization's brand name paired with 'recall' or 'safety' keywords
controls: Keyword-based social-listening for brand+safety/recall term combinations
Rapid-response fact-check and correction protocol coordinated with regulatory-affairs
ITID-24311.detection: Detected via social-listening/keyword-monitoring tools; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24311.response: Verify against actual quality/recall records within hours, issue a clear public correction citing facts, and coordinate with regulatory-affairs if a real regulator inquiry results from the false claim.
metrics: Time from post detection to public correction
Viral reach at time of correction
ITID-24311.notes: Differentiated from siblings 24312/24313 by subject matter (product safety/recall specifically); no MITRE mapping applies since this is social-platform misinformation, not a network-intrusion technique.

playbook.name: Response: Misinformation Post Fabricating Product Safety/Recall Claim
playbook.description: For a social media post fabricating a specific false claim that the company's product is unsafe or subject to a recall that has not actually occurred.

steps.title: Locate and preserve the originating post
steps.desc: Capture the exact claim, wording, and any fabricated supporting 'evidence' (fake images, doctored documents) along with reach metrics.
steps.outcome: Post captured with reach and content documented.

steps.title: Report the post as misinformation to the hosting platform(s)
steps.desc: Submit a report citing the platform's health/safety misinformation policy where applicable.

steps.title: Publish a full factual correction and pursue platform takedown
steps.desc: Release a complete correction with supporting facts, and pursue removal of the fabricated post where it violates platform policy.

steps.title: Monitor sentiment, sales impact, and spread of the correction
steps.desc: Track whether panic subsides and the correction reaches a meaningful share of the original audience.
steps.outcome: Sentiment and sales trend back to baseline.

steps.title: Document the incident and response speed
steps.desc: Record how quickly the claim was verified and corrected, to speed up any future fabricated safety claim.

steps.title: Urgently verify against actual product safety/recall records
steps.desc: Confirm with Product Safety/Quality and Legal, within hours, that no such recall or safety issue exists (or identify the real issue if the claim has any basis).
steps.guidance: This is time-critical — a fabricated safety/recall claim can cause real customer panic and even purchase avoidance within hours of going viral.
steps.outcome: Ground truth established and documented, with a timestamp showing rapid verification.
steps.abort: If an actual safety issue is uncovered during verification, immediately redirect to the real product-recall/safety-incident process instead of this playbook.

steps.title: Issue an urgent factual holding statement
steps.desc: Publish a brief, fast factual statement confirming no recall/safety issue exists (or the real status) while the fuller correction is prepared.
steps.guidance: Coordinate wording tightly with Legal and PR/Comms given the urgency.

ITID-24312.def: A social media post or thread falsely claiming an executive engaged in misconduct, fraud, or scandal that did not occur, or grossly misrepresenting an actual minor event as major misconduct.
ITID-24312.purpose: Captures a social media misinformation post fabricating a scandal involving an organization executive, aimed at damaging leadership credibility and brand trust.
scopeIncludes: Fabricated claims of executive misconduct, fraud, or scandal with no factual basis
Grossly distorted misrepresentation of a real but minor/unrelated event framed as major misconduct
scopeExcludes: Fabricated product safety/recall claims (ITID-24311)
Fabricated data-breach/security claims (ITID-24313)
Genuine, factually accurate reporting on actual executive misconduct (not misinformation, a legal/HR matter instead)
ITID-24312.severity: High; executive-scandal misinformation can move stock price, trigger board/investor inquiries, and cause lasting reputational harm even after correction.
ITID-24312.priority: P1 given the speed and severity of reputational and potentially market impact.
ITID-24312.escalation: Escalate immediately to communications/PR, legal, executive leadership, investor relations (if publicly traded), and HR to confirm facts before responding.
indicators: A viral post making specific misconduct allegations against a named executive with no corroborating evidence
Anonymous or newly-created accounts as the sole originating source of the claim
vectors: Fabricated executive-scandal claims for virality, activist short-selling, or malicious brand/personal attack
rootCauses: No rapid-response fact-check protocol for viral executive-misconduct misinformation
No proactive monitoring for named-executive-plus-scandal keyword combinations
controls: Keyword-based social-listening for executive names paired with scandal/misconduct terms
Rapid-response fact-check and correction protocol coordinated with legal and investor relations
ITID-24312.detection: Detected via social-listening/keyword-monitoring tools; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24312.response: Confirm facts internally within hours, issue a clear public correction or statement, and coordinate with investor relations and legal on any market or defamation implications.
metrics: Time from post detection to public response
Viral reach at time of correction
ITID-24312.notes: Differentiated from siblings 24311/24313 by subject matter (executive scandal specifically); no MITRE mapping applies since this is social-platform misinformation, not a network-intrusion technique.

playbook.name: Response: Misinformation Post Fabricating Executive Scandal Claim
playbook.description: For a social media post fabricating a specific false scandal claim about a named company executive.

steps.title: Locate and preserve the originating post
steps.desc: Capture the exact claim, any fabricated 'evidence', and reach metrics.

steps.title: Report the post as misinformation/defamation to the hosting platform(s)
steps.desc: Submit a report citing fabricated content about a real, named individual.

steps.title: Publish a factual correction and pursue removal, escalating to legal action if warranted
steps.desc: Release a clear correction; where the claim is defamatory and the source identifiable, Legal may pursue a cease-and-desist.
steps.guidance: Coordinate timing and wording with PR/Comms and the executive.
steps.outcome: Correction published; removal pursued; legal action considered where warranted.

steps.title: Monitor sentiment and spread of the correction
steps.desc: Track whether the correction is reaching the original audience and whether the executive continues to face targeted harassment.
steps.outcome: Sentiment trend improving; executive's wellbeing monitored.

steps.title: Document the incident and response process
steps.desc: Record the verification and support process for future fabricated executive claims.

steps.title: Urgently verify the claim with the executive and Legal/HR
steps.desc: Confirm directly with the named executive, Legal, and HR, within hours, whether any part of the claim has factual basis.
steps.guidance: This is time-critical — a fabricated executive scandal claim can cause real reputational and personal harm to a named individual very quickly.
steps.outcome: Ground truth established; executive informed and supported.
steps.abort: If any part of the claim is substantiated, redirect to the appropriate HR/Legal/crisis-management process instead of this playbook.

steps.title: Support the named executive directly
steps.desc: Notify and support the executive personally — offer Legal and Comms support and coordinate on any personal statement they wish to make.

ITID-24313.def: A social media post or thread falsely claiming the organization suffered a data breach, ransomware attack, or security compromise that did not actually occur, or grossly exaggerating a minor/unrelated event as a major breach.
ITID-24313.purpose: Captures a social media misinformation post fabricating a data breach or security incident that never occurred, aimed at damaging customer trust in the organization's security posture.
scopeIncludes: Fabricated claims of a data breach/security incident with no basis in actual security/incident-response records
Fabricated 'leaked data' samples falsely attributed to the organization
scopeExcludes: Fabricated product safety/recall claims (ITID-24311)
Fabricated executive-scandal claims (ITID-24312)
An actual confirmed data breach or security incident (tracked under the organization's real incident-response ITIDs, not this misinformation leaf)
ITID-24313.severity: High; false breach claims can trigger genuine customer panic, regulatory inquiries, and require the security team to divert resources to prove a negative.
ITID-24313.priority: P1 given the need for rapid, credible technical verification and correction.
ITID-24313.escalation: Escalate immediately to security/incident-response (to definitively confirm no actual breach occurred), communications/PR, and legal; coordinate a technically-credible public statement.
indicators: A viral post claiming a breach with no corroborating alert, log evidence, or IR case in the organization's actual security systems
Fabricated or recycled 'leaked data' samples (often reused from unrelated real breaches) falsely attributed to the organization
vectors: Fabricated breach claims for extortion leverage, virality, or malicious brand attack
Recycled data from an unrelated real breach falsely relabeled as belonging to the organization
rootCauses: No rapid-response protocol coordinating security/IR verification with communications for breach-misinformation claims
No proactive monitoring for brand name paired with 'breach'/'hacked'/'leaked' keywords
controls: Keyword-based social-listening for brand+breach/hack/leak term combinations
Rapid-response protocol jointly owned by security/IR and communications
ITID-24313.detection: Detected via social-listening/keyword-monitoring tools combined with a definitive internal security/IR verification check; the verification step is the one genuinely technical component in this sibling group.
ITID-24313.response: Security/IR must definitively confirm no actual breach occurred, and communications must issue a clear, technically-credible public correction quickly to prevent panic and misinformed regulatory attention.
metrics: Time from post detection to internal security verification
Time from verification to public correction
detections: Internal security/IR log review confirming absence of an actual breach
ITID-24313.notes: Differentiated from siblings 24311/24312 by subject matter (data breach/security specifically) and requires positive internal security verification rather than pure communications judgment. No MITRE mapping applies since the misinformation itself is social-platform content, not a network-intrusion technique — an actual confirmed breach is tracked separately under the organization's real IR ITIDs.

playbook.name: Response: Misinformation Post Fabricating Data Breach/Security Claim
playbook.description: For a social media post fabricating a specific false claim that the company suffered a data breach or security incident that did not actually occur.

steps.title: Locate and preserve the originating post
steps.desc: Capture the exact claim, any fabricated 'leaked data' samples, and reach metrics.

steps.title: Report the post as misinformation to the hosting platform(s)
steps.desc: Submit a report citing fabricated security/breach claims where the platform's policy covers it.

steps.title: Publish a full factual correction and pursue platform takedown
steps.desc: Release a complete correction with supporting facts and pursue removal of the fabricated post.

steps.title: Monitor sentiment, support-channel volume, and spread of the correction
steps.desc: Track whether customer concern subsides and the correction reaches the original audience.
steps.outcome: Sentiment and support volume back to baseline.

steps.title: Document the incident and response speed
steps.desc: Record how quickly the claim was verified and corrected, to speed up response to any future fabricated breach claim.

steps.title: Urgently verify against actual security incident records
steps.desc: Confirm with Security/IT, within hours, whether any breach or incident matching the claim actually occurred.
steps.guidance: This is time-critical — a fabricated breach claim can cause real customer panic (password changes, churn, support-line overload) within hours.
steps.outcome: Ground truth established and documented, with a rapid-verification timestamp.
steps.abort: If a real security incident is uncovered, immediately redirect to the actual security-incident-response process instead of this playbook.

steps.title: Issue an urgent factual holding statement
steps.desc: Publish a brief factual statement confirming no breach occurred (or the real status) while a fuller correction is prepared.
steps.guidance: Coordinate tightly with Security, Legal, and PR/Comms given the urgency and customer-trust stakes.

ITID-24314.def: A suspected fabricated social media misinformation post about the organization awaiting further investigation to determine its subject matter before reclassification to the appropriate sibling ITID.
ITID-24314.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for a suspected social media misinformation post not yet triaged to the product-safety, executive-scandal, or data-breach subject matter.
scopeIncludes: Newly-detected fabricated misinformation posts not yet triaged to a specific subject matter
scopeExcludes: Any post for which subject matter has been confirmed and should be reclassified to ITID-24311, ITID-24312, or ITID-24313
ITID-24314.severity: Medium-High pending triage given the general risk profile of viral misinformation.
ITID-24314.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR on triage duty; reclassify promptly once subject matter is confirmed.
indicators: An unclassified fabricated claim about the organization circulating on social media
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial evidence to classify subject matter at time of intake
controls: Keyword-based social-listening for brand-related misinformation
ITID-24314.detection: Same detection surface as sibling leaves, pending subject-matter attribution.
ITID-24314.response: Triage promptly and reclassify to the specific sibling ITID once subject matter is clear.
metrics: Count of incidents held in this bucket beyond 5 business days without reclassification
ITID-24314.notes: Intake/triage bucket only, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Misinformation Post
playbook.description: General-purpose response for a social media post fabricating a false claim about the company that does not fit a more specific known category (product safety, executive scandal, or data breach).

steps.title: Locate and preserve the originating post
steps.desc: Capture the exact claim, any fabricated supporting material, and reach metrics.

steps.title: Report the post as misinformation to the hosting platform(s)
steps.desc: Submit a report citing the platform's misinformation policy where applicable.

steps.title: Publish a full factual correction and pursue platform takedown
steps.desc: Release a complete correction and pursue removal of the fabricated post.

steps.title: Monitor sentiment and spread of the correction
steps.desc: Track whether the correction reaches the original audience and sentiment stabilizes.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the claim, verification process, and response speed for future reference.

steps.title: Urgently verify the claim against the facts
steps.desc: Confirm with the relevant internal team, promptly, whether any part of the claim has factual basis.
steps.guidance: Fabricated claims that could cause panic or reputational harm should be treated as time-critical.
steps.abort: If the claim is substantiated, redirect to the appropriate incident-response process for that underlying issue instead of this playbook.

steps.title: Prepare a factual holding statement if urgency warrants it
steps.desc: For claims with potential for rapid spread or panic, issue a brief factual statement pending the fuller correction.

ITID-24321.def: A campaign publishing video content presenting paid actors, stock footage, or fabricated scenarios as genuine, unpaid customer testimonials about the organization's product or service.
ITID-24321.purpose: Captures a fabricated customer testimonial video campaign using actors or fabricated footage presented as genuine customer experiences.
scopeIncludes: Video testimonials using actors or stock footage without disclosure, presented as genuine customers
Fabricated or staged 'customer' scenarios misrepresenting real product usage
scopeExcludes: Fake employee/culture testimonial campaigns (ITID-24322)
Fake influencer-style single-post testimonials (ITID-24323)
Legitimate, disclosed customer-testimonial marketing produced by the organization's own authorized marketing team
ITID-24321.severity: Medium-High; discovery of fabrication causes significant trust damage and potential advertising-standards/regulatory exposure (e.g., FTC endorsement guidelines).
ITID-24321.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if regulatory (advertising-standards) attention results.
ITID-24321.escalation: Escalate to legal/compliance (advertising standards) and marketing leadership immediately; determine whether the campaign was internally authorized or is a third-party/rogue-agency attack.
indicators: Testimonial video 'customers' traceable to stock-footage libraries or acting-casting platforms
Inconsistent or reused footage across supposedly distinct customer stories
vectors: Use of stock actors/footage marketed as genuine testimonials, either by a rogue internal marketing effort or an external attacker fabricating content to later discredit the brand
rootCauses: No internal compliance review process for testimonial-based marketing content
No monitoring for externally-fabricated testimonial content falsely attributed to the organization
controls: Internal compliance/advertising-standards review of testimonial marketing content
Monitoring for externally-fabricated testimonial content misattributed to the organization
ITID-24321.detection: Detected via reverse-image/video search against stock-footage and casting-platform sources, plus internal compliance review; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24321.response: If internally sourced, immediately pull the content and remediate compliance process; if externally fabricated to attack the brand, pursue platform takedown and public correction.
metrics: Count of fabricated-testimonial incidents identified per quarter
Time to content takedown/correction
ITID-24321.notes: Differentiated from siblings 24322 (employee/culture) and 24323 (influencer-style single post) by the video-testimonial-of-customer-experience format specifically.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Customer Testimonial Video Campaign
playbook.description: For a video campaign featuring fabricated customer testimonials — actors or stock footage presented as real customers, or genuine customers' likenesses used without consent to endorse the company falsely.

steps.title: Locate the video(s) and identify the individuals depicted
steps.desc: Collect the video content and determine whether the people shown are stock actors, unrelated individuals, or real customers whose likeness was used without consent.
steps.outcome: Video content and depicted individuals identified.

steps.title: Report the video to the hosting platform(s) for fake/misleading endorsement content
steps.desc: Submit a platform report citing fabricated testimonial/endorsement policy violations.

steps.title: Pursue takedown and, where a real person's likeness was misused without consent, pursue appropriate legal remedies
steps.desc: Follow through on platform removal; Legal may pursue further action for unauthorized use of likeness.
steps.outcome: Video removed; legal follow-up pursued if warranted.

steps.title: Monitor for re-upload or spread of the video
steps.desc: Track whether the video resurfaces on other platforms or accounts.

steps.title: Document the incident and detection method
steps.desc: Record how the fabricated video was identified, to speed up detection of similar campaigns.

steps.title: Confirm fabrication with the depicted individual(s) where identifiable
steps.desc: Where a real person can be identified, contact them to confirm whether they gave the testimonial or consented to its use.
steps.outcome: Fabrication confirmed, or genuine consent issue identified.

steps.title: Notify and support any real person whose likeness was misused
steps.desc: If a real customer's identity or likeness was used without consent, notify them, apologize as appropriate, and support any personal correction they wish to make.

ITID-24322.def: A campaign publishing content presenting fabricated or paid actors as genuine employees, misrepresenting the organization's actual workplace culture, benefits, or conditions — either overly positive (astroturfed employer branding) or falsely negative (a discrediting attack).
ITID-24322.purpose: Captures a fabricated employee testimonial or company-culture campaign misrepresenting the organization's actual workplace conditions.
scopeIncludes: Fabricated 'employee' testimonials (positive or negative) not traceable to any actual current or former employee
Paid-actor content misrepresenting workplace culture in either direction
scopeExcludes: Fake customer testimonial videos (ITID-24321)
Genuine employee reviews on legitimate employer-review platforms (e.g., real Glassdoor reviews), even if unflattering
Fake influencer-style testimonials (ITID-24323)
ITID-24322.severity: Medium; affects employer brand and recruiting/retention perception rather than direct customer trust.
ITID-24322.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if the campaign meaningfully affects recruiting pipeline or triggers employee-relations concern.
ITID-24322.escalation: Escalate to HR/employer-branding and communications; legal if a specific real employee's identity is being impersonated without consent.
indicators: 'Employee' testimonials with no matching record in HR systems
Content traceable to stock actors or an external PR/attack campaign rather than genuine staff
vectors: Fabricated employer-branding content (astroturfed positive) or a discrediting attack using fake 'employee' voices (fabricated negative)
rootCauses: No internal compliance review for employer-branding testimonial content
No monitoring for externally-fabricated 'employee' content misattributed to the organization
controls: Internal HR/compliance review of employer-branding testimonial content
Monitoring for externally-fabricated 'employee' content
ITID-24322.detection: Detected via HR-record cross-checking and reverse-image/casting-platform search; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24322.response: Verify against actual HR employment records, and either correct internally-sourced fabricated content or pursue takedown/correction for externally-fabricated attacks.
metrics: Count of fabricated-employee-testimonial incidents identified per quarter
ITID-24322.notes: Differentiated from sibling 24321 (customer testimonials) by subject matter (employees/culture specifically) and covers both fabricated-positive (employer-branding astroturfing) and fabricated-negative (discrediting attack) directions.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Employee Testimonial/Culture Campaign
playbook.description: For content presenting fabricated 'employee' testimonials or company-culture claims from people who are not actual employees, misrepresenting the company's workplace.

steps.title: Locate the content and check claimed employment against HR records
steps.desc: Identify the individual(s) presented as employees and verify with HR whether they have ever been employed by the company.
steps.outcome: Employment status verified against HR records.

steps.title: Report the content to the hosting platform(s)
steps.desc: Submit a report citing fabricated/misleading content where the platform's policy covers it.

steps.title: Pursue takedown and publish a factual correction on company culture where needed
steps.desc: Follow through on platform removal; if the claims gained traction, publish a factual response about actual workplace practices.
steps.outcome: Content removed; correction published if warranted.

steps.title: Monitor sentiment among current employees and the public
steps.desc: Track internal and external sentiment for lingering effects.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record how the fabrication was identified and verified, for future reference.

steps.title: Confirm the fabrication and assess intent
steps.desc: Determine whether this is a deliberate fabrication (e.g. a competitor or activist group) versus a former employee misrepresenting their status.
steps.outcome: Nature and likely source of the fabrication understood.

steps.title: Brief HR and PR/Comms internally
steps.desc: Ensure HR and PR/Comms are aligned on messaging, particularly if current employees ask about the claims.

ITID-24323.def: A single fabricated or impersonated social media post styled to look like an influencer's organic testimonial about the organization's product, where the influencer either does not exist, did not actually make the post, or is being impersonated.
ITID-24323.purpose: Captures a single fabricated social media post styled as an influencer's genuine testimonial, distinct from a broader coordinated video campaign.
scopeIncludes: A single post falsely attributed to a real influencer who never made it (impersonation)
A single post from a fabricated persona designed to appear as an independent influencer
scopeExcludes: Fake customer testimonial video campaigns (ITID-24321)
Fake employee/culture testimonial campaigns (ITID-24322)
Genuinely sponsored/paid influencer content with proper disclosure (a marketing-compliance matter, not misinformation)
Undisclosed paid positive reviews from real influencers, tracked under the Fake Influencer Reviews Tier-3 branch (e.g., ITID-24511)
ITID-24323.severity: Medium, escalating to High if the impersonated influencer has a large following and the post goes viral before correction.
ITID-24323.priority: P2 while the post is actively circulating; escalate for large-follower impersonation targets.
ITID-24323.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR and, where a real influencer is impersonated without consent, coordinate with that influencer's team on a joint correction and platform report.
indicators: A post attributed to a known influencer that does not appear on their verified official accounts
Stylistic or factual inconsistencies with the influencer's established voice/content history
vectors: Impersonation account posing as a real influencer
Fabricated persona designed to simulate an independent influencer voice
rootCauses: No monitoring for impersonation accounts referencing the organization's brand
No verification-liaison relationship with known influencers relevant to the brand
controls: Impersonation-account monitoring referencing the brand
Verification-liaison relationships with relevant real influencers
ITID-24323.detection: Detected via social-listening tools and direct verification against the influencer's official channels; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24323.response: Verify directly with the influencer (or their team) whether the post is genuine, report impersonation accounts to the platform, and issue a correction if the fabrication gained meaningful reach.
metrics: Count of impersonation/fabrication incidents identified per quarter
Time to verification and correction
ITID-24323.notes: Differentiated from siblings 24321/24322 by format (a single social post, not a produced video campaign) and from the Fake Influencer Reviews Tier-3 branch, which covers real influencers being paid without disclosure rather than impersonation/fabrication.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Influencer-Style Testimonial Post
playbook.description: For a social media post styled as an influencer endorsement that is entirely fabricated — no genuine relationship, payment, or product use behind the claimed endorsement.

steps.title: Locate the post and identify the purported influencer
steps.desc: Capture the content and identify the account presenting the endorsement.

steps.title: Report the post to the hosting platform for fake endorsement/impersonation
steps.desc: Submit a report citing fabricated endorsement or impersonation policy violations as applicable.

steps.title: Pursue takedown of the fabricated post
steps.desc: Follow through on platform removal.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence under new accounts
steps.desc: Track whether similar fake endorsement posts reappear.

steps.title: Document the incident and verification approach
steps.desc: Record how quickly the fabrication was confirmed with the influencer, for future reference.

steps.title: Confirm with the purported influencer (or their agency) that no genuine relationship exists
steps.desc: Contact the influencer or their representation to confirm whether any partnership, payment, or product interaction actually occurred.
steps.outcome: Fabrication confirmed with the influencer's cooperation, or a genuine undisclosed relationship uncovered.

steps.title: Coordinate with the genuine influencer on a public clarification if they are willing
steps.desc: If the influencer is willing, a joint or independent clarification from them carries more credibility than a company statement alone.
steps.outcome: Clarification coordinated where the influencer agrees.

ITID-24324.def: A suspected fake testimonial incident awaiting further investigation to determine its specific format before reclassification to the appropriate sibling ITID.
ITID-24324.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for a suspected fake testimonial incident not yet triaged to the customer-video, employee-culture, or influencer-style-post format.
scopeIncludes: Newly-detected fabricated testimonial content not yet triaged to a specific format
scopeExcludes: Any incident for which format has been confirmed and should be reclassified to ITID-24321, ITID-24322, or ITID-24323
ITID-24324.escalation: Escalate to the brand/reputation analyst on triage duty; reclassify promptly once format is confirmed.
indicators: An unclassified fabricated testimonial referencing the organization
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial evidence to classify format at time of intake
controls: Social-listening monitoring for fabricated testimonial content
ITID-24324.detection: Same detection surface as sibling leaves, pending format attribution.
ITID-24324.response: Triage promptly and reclassify to the specific sibling ITID once format is clear.
metrics: Count of incidents held in this bucket beyond 5 business days without reclassification
ITID-24324.notes: Intake/triage bucket only, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Fake Testimonial Campaign
playbook.description: General-purpose response for a fabricated testimonial campaign that does not fit a more specific known pattern (customer video, employee/culture, or influencer-style post).

steps.title: Locate the content and identify who is depicted
steps.desc: Capture the testimonial content and determine who is presented as giving it.

steps.title: Report the content to the hosting platform(s)
steps.desc: Submit a report citing fabricated testimonial/endorsement content.

steps.title: Pursue takedown of the fabricated content
steps.desc: Follow through on platform removal.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Track whether similar fabricated testimonials reappear.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the pattern for faster future detection.

steps.title: Confirm fabrication with the depicted individual(s) where identifiable
steps.desc: Contact the real person or organization depicted, where identifiable, to confirm the testimonial is fabricated.

steps.title: Notify and support any real person misrepresented
steps.desc: If a real identifiable person was misrepresented, notify and support them.

ITID-24331.def: A viral social media hashtag campaign explicitly organized to call on consumers to boycott the organization's products or services, whether triggered by a genuine grievance or a fabricated/exaggerated one.
ITID-24331.purpose: Captures a hashtag campaign specifically organized to call for a consumer boycott of the organization.
scopeIncludes: A trending hashtag whose explicit call-to-action is a boycott of the organization
Coordinated posting explicitly urging followers to stop purchasing from or using the organization
scopeExcludes: Scandal-framing hashtags that do not explicitly call for a boycott (ITID-24332)
Hijacking of the organization's own branded hashtag for negative messaging (ITID-24333)
ITID-24331.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High if the hashtag trends nationally or is picked up by mainstream media.
ITID-24331.priority: P2 during active trending; de-escalate to P3 once engagement plateaus.
ITID-24331.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR and executive leadership; assess whether the underlying grievance (if genuine) requires a substantive operational response, not just a messaging one.
indicators: A branded boycott hashtag trending with rapidly increasing volume
Explicit boycott language and calls-to-action within the hashtag's top posts
vectors: Organic or orchestrated grassroots boycott hashtag campaign
rootCauses: No real-time social-listening alerting for boycott-related hashtag trends referencing the brand
Slow or dismissive initial public response allowing the narrative to harden
controls: Real-time hashtag-trend social-listening alerting
Rapid-response communications playbook for boycott campaigns
ITID-24331.detection: Detected via social-listening/hashtag-trend monitoring tools; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24331.response: Assess the legitimacy and scale of the underlying grievance, respond with substantive action where warranted, and issue a proportionate public statement while monitoring for de-escalation or further spread.
metrics: Hashtag volume/trend trajectory
Time to substantive public response
ITID-24331.notes: Differentiated from sibling 24332 by the explicit boycott call-to-action, distinguishing it from scandal-framing hashtags that damage reputation without directly calling for a boycott.

playbook.name: Response: Boycott Hashtag Campaign
playbook.description: For a hashtag campaign calling for a boycott of the company, which may be rooted in a genuine grievance, a misunderstanding, or a fabricated pretext.

steps.title: Identify the hashtag, its origin, and its reach
steps.desc: Determine who started the hashtag, what specific grievance or claim it is based on, and how far it has spread.

steps.title: Report demonstrably fabricated claims fueling the hashtag to relevant platforms
steps.desc: Where specific fabricated claims are driving the hashtag, report those individual posts under the platform's misinformation policy.

steps.title: Execute the chosen response and pursue removal of fabricated content
steps.desc: Carry out the agreed response (correction, direct engagement, or genuine remediation) and pursue takedown of any confirmed fabricated posts.
steps.outcome: Response executed; fabricated content actioned where applicable.

steps.title: Monitor hashtag volume and sentiment trend
steps.desc: Track whether the hashtag's volume and negative sentiment subside.

steps.title: Document the incident and engagement decision rationale
steps.desc: Record why the chosen engagement strategy was selected and how effective it was, for future hashtag-crisis decisions.

steps.title: Assess the legitimacy of the underlying grievance
steps.desc: Determine whether the boycott is grounded in a real, verifiable company action or a false/exaggerated pretext.
steps.guidance: If the grievance is genuine, this is a PR/Customer-Service matter requiring a real response, not a misinformation takedown.
steps.outcome: Grievance assessed as genuine, exaggerated, or fabricated.
steps.abort: If the grievance is genuine, redirect to Customer Service/PR for a substantive response addressing the real issue.

steps.title: Decide on engagement strategy with PR/Comms
steps.desc: Determine whether to respond publicly, respond privately to key voices, or stay quiet, since visible engagement can sometimes amplify a hashtag further.
steps.guidance: Document the reasoning for whichever approach is chosen.

ITID-24332.def: A viral social media hashtag campaign that frames the organization as the subject of a scandal (e.g., '#[BrandName]Exposed' style framing), generating reputational damage through narrative association rather than an explicit boycott call-to-action.
ITID-24332.purpose: Captures a hashtag campaign that frames the organization within a scandal narrative without necessarily calling for a boycott.
scopeIncludes: A trending hashtag framing the organization within a scandal narrative without an explicit boycott ask
Hashtags built around an exposé-style narrative (real, exaggerated, or fabricated)
scopeExcludes: Explicit boycott-call hashtag campaigns (ITID-24331)
Hijacking of the organization's own branded hashtag (ITID-24333)
ITID-24332.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High if picked up by mainstream media or if the underlying scandal claim is fabricated and defamatory.
ITID-24332.priority: P2 during active trending; de-escalate to P3 once engagement plateaus.
ITID-24332.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR and legal (if claims are fabricated/defamatory); verify the factual basis of the scandal framing before responding.
indicators: A scandal-framed hashtag trending with rapidly increasing volume
Content mixing genuine grievances with exaggerated or fabricated claims under a unifying scandal narrative
vectors: Organic or orchestrated scandal-framing hashtag campaign
rootCauses: No real-time social-listening alerting for scandal-narrative hashtag trends referencing the brand
No rapid fact-verification protocol to distinguish genuine from fabricated elements of the narrative
controls: Real-time hashtag-trend social-listening alerting
Rapid fact-verification protocol for scandal-narrative claims
ITID-24332.detection: Detected via social-listening/hashtag-trend monitoring tools; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24332.response: Verify the factual basis of the scandal claims, issue a fact-based correction for fabricated elements, and address genuine elements substantively.
metrics: Hashtag volume/trend trajectory
Time to fact-verification and public response
ITID-24332.notes: Differentiated from sibling 24331 by the absence of an explicit boycott call-to-action — this is narrative/scandal framing rather than a direct consumer-action ask.

playbook.name: Response: Scandal-Framing Hashtag Campaign
playbook.description: For a hashtag campaign framing the company around an alleged scandal, which may reflect a real issue, an exaggeration, or a fabricated pretext.

steps.title: Identify the hashtag, the specific scandal claim, and its reach
steps.desc: Determine the exact allegation the hashtag is built around, who originated it, and how far it has spread.

steps.title: Report demonstrably fabricated content fueling the hashtag
steps.desc: Where specific posts contain fabricated claims, report them under the platform's misinformation policy.

steps.title: Execute the chosen response and pursue removal of fabricated content
steps.desc: Carry out the agreed response and pursue takedown of confirmed fabricated posts.
steps.outcome: Response executed; fabricated content actioned where applicable.

steps.title: Monitor hashtag volume and sentiment trend
steps.desc: Track whether the hashtag's volume and negative sentiment subside.

steps.title: Document the incident and engagement rationale
steps.desc: Record why the chosen engagement strategy was selected and its effectiveness for future reference.

steps.title: Verify the underlying scandal claim against the facts
steps.desc: Confirm with the relevant internal team (Legal, HR, Security, or Product as applicable) whether the alleged scandal has any factual basis.
steps.abort: If the claim is substantiated, redirect to the appropriate real incident-response process (Legal, HR, security, etc.) instead of this playbook.

steps.title: Decide on public engagement strategy with PR/Comms
steps.desc: Determine whether to respond publicly, engage selectively, or hold back, since a visible response can sometimes amplify the hashtag further.
steps.guidance: Document the reasoning for the chosen approach.

ITID-24333.def: An attack in which the organization's own established, legitimate marketing hashtag is flooded with negative, critical, or mocking content by outside actors, subverting the hashtag's intended positive purpose.
ITID-24333.purpose: Captures the hijacking of the organization's own legitimate branded hashtag by attackers to flood it with negative content.
scopeIncludes: Coordinated or organic flooding of the organization's own branded/campaign hashtag with negative content
Cases where a marketing hashtag intended for positive engagement becomes dominated by critical/mocking posts
scopeExcludes: Independently-created boycott hashtags (ITID-24331)
Independently-created scandal-framing hashtags (ITID-24332)
ITID-24333.severity: Medium-High; particularly damaging because it subverts an active marketing investment and is highly visible to the campaign's intended audience.
ITID-24333.priority: P2 during active hijacking, especially if the hashtag is part of a paid or high-visibility marketing push.
ITID-24333.escalation: Escalate to marketing (to pause or adjust the campaign using the hijacked hashtag) and communications/PR for response messaging.
