indicators: A marketing-owned hashtag showing a sudden shift from campaign-aligned content to negative/mocking content
Volume of negative posts exceeding the campaign's own promotional posting activity
vectors: Coordinated or organic piggybacking on an existing branded hashtag to subvert its purpose
rootCauses: No real-time monitoring of the organization's own active marketing hashtags for sentiment shifts
No contingency plan for pausing/adjusting a campaign whose hashtag has been hijacked
controls: Real-time sentiment monitoring of active owned marketing hashtags
Campaign contingency plan for hashtag hijacking
ITID-24333.detection: Detected via social-listening/hashtag-sentiment monitoring tools specifically tracking the organization's own active campaigns; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24333.response: Assess whether to pause the campaign, adjust messaging, or lean into transparent engagement with the criticism, in coordination with marketing and communications.
metrics: Sentiment shift magnitude on the owned hashtag
Time to campaign response decision
ITID-24333.notes: Differentiated from siblings 24331/24332 by targeting the organization's OWN branded hashtag infrastructure rather than an independently-created attack hashtag.

playbook.name: Response: Hashtag Hijacking of Legitimate Branded Hashtag
playbook.description: For a company's own branded hashtag being hijacked by critics or bad actors and flooded with negative or off-topic content, subverting its original purpose.

steps.title: Confirm the hijacking and characterize the hijacking content
steps.desc: Review the branded hashtag's recent activity to confirm it has been overtaken by negative/off-topic posts rather than its intended use.

steps.title: Decide whether to engage with the hijacked hashtag at all
steps.desc: Weigh whether responding, correcting, or continuing to use the hashtag will help or will simply amplify the hijacking further by drawing more attention to it.
steps.guidance: This is a genuine judgment call — sometimes the lowest-risk response is to quietly retire or pause use of the hashtag rather than engage. Document the reasoning either way with PR/Comms.
steps.outcome: A documented decision: engage, stay silent, or retire the hashtag.

steps.title: Execute the chosen strategy
steps.desc: Follow through on whatever was decided — continued monitoring, a factual response, or retiring the hashtag from future campaigns.

steps.title: Monitor whether the hijack subsides and reassess hashtag usability
steps.desc: Track hashtag volume and sentiment; decide whether the hashtag is safe to use again in future campaigns.
steps.outcome: Hijack activity subsides; future usability assessed.

steps.title: Document the engagement decision and its outcome
steps.desc: Record whether the chosen engagement approach helped or amplified the hijack, to guide the next hijacking judgment call.

steps.title: Assess scale and whether the hijack is organic or coordinated
steps.desc: Determine how many accounts are involved and whether there are signs of coordination versus organic pile-on.
steps.outcome: Scale and nature of the hijack documented.

steps.title: Report clearly abusive or policy-violating posts using the hashtag
steps.desc: Where individual posts violate the platform's harassment, spam, or misinformation policies, report them individually rather than the hashtag itself.

ITID-24334.def: A suspected viral negative hashtag incident awaiting further investigation to determine its specific mechanism before reclassification to the appropriate sibling ITID.
ITID-24334.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for a suspected viral negative hashtag incident not yet triaged to the boycott, scandal-framing, or hijacking mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Newly-detected negative hashtag trends referencing the organization not yet triaged to a specific mechanism
scopeExcludes: Any incident for which the mechanism has been confirmed and should be reclassified to ITID-24331, ITID-24332, or ITID-24333
ITID-24334.priority: P3 during initial triage; escalate per the confirmed mechanism once known.
ITID-24334.escalation: Escalate to the brand/reputation analyst on triage duty; reclassify promptly once the mechanism is identified.
indicators: An unclassified negative hashtag trend referencing the organization
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial evidence to attribute mechanism at time of intake
controls: Real-time hashtag-trend social-listening alerting
ITID-24334.detection: Same detection surface as sibling leaves, pending mechanism attribution.
ITID-24334.response: Triage promptly and reclassify to the specific sibling ITID once the mechanism is clear.
metrics: Count of incidents held in this bucket beyond 5 business days without reclassification
ITID-24334.notes: Intake/triage bucket only, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Viral Negative Hashtag Campaign
playbook.description: General-purpose response for a viral negative hashtag campaign that does not fit a more specific known pattern (boycott call, scandal-framing, or hijacking of a branded hashtag).

steps.title: Identify the hashtag, its basis, and reach
steps.desc: Determine what claim or grievance the hashtag is built around, who originated it, and how far it has spread.

steps.title: Report demonstrably fabricated content fueling the hashtag
steps.desc: Report individual posts containing fabricated claims under the platform's misinformation policy.

steps.title: Execute the chosen response
steps.desc: Carry out the agreed response and pursue takedown of any confirmed fabricated content.

steps.title: Monitor hashtag volume and sentiment trend
steps.desc: Track whether volume and negative sentiment subside.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the pattern and engagement outcome for future reference.

steps.title: Assess whether the underlying basis is genuine, exaggerated, or fabricated
steps.desc: Confirm with the relevant internal team whether the hashtag's premise has factual basis.
steps.abort: If genuine, redirect to the appropriate real incident-response process instead of this playbook.

steps.title: Decide on engagement strategy with PR/Comms
steps.desc: Determine whether responding will help or amplify the hashtag further, and document the reasoning.

ITID-24411.def: Review-platform abuse in which large numbers of freshly-created, disposable accounts (no aging, no purchase history, minimal profile completion) are used to post reviews, prioritizing volume and speed over evading detection.
ITID-24411.purpose: Captures review-platform spam using freshly, mass-created disposable accounts with no attempt to appear aged or established.
scopeIncludes: Reviews from accounts created in immediate temporal proximity to the review posting, with minimal or templated profile information
Batches of accounts sharing registration-time infrastructure (email domain patterns, IP ranges)
scopeExcludes: Stolen or purchased aged/established accounts (ITID-24412)
Cross-platform spam networks reused across multiple platforms (ITID-24413)
ITID-24411.severity: Low-to-Medium; disposable accounts are typically the easiest variant for platforms to detect and remove.
ITID-24411.priority: P3, escalating to P2 for high-volume campaigns overwhelming manual moderation capacity.
ITID-24411.escalation: Escalate to the platform's automated trust-and-safety detection channel, which is typically well-equipped to catch this pattern; internal escalation is mainly for tracking volume trends.
indicators: Reviewer accounts created within minutes/hours of posting
Minimal profile completion (no photo, generic username patterns)
High volume of reviews from a narrow account-creation time window
vectors: Mass automated account registration immediately followed by review posting
rootCauses: No baseline monitoring of account-age-to-review-posting-time ratios
controls: Account-age/review-timing anomaly monitoring
Reliance on platform-native fake-account detection systems
ITID-24411.detection: Detected primarily via the review platform's own account-age and registration-pattern signals; a straightforward technical detection surface given the disposable-account mechanism.
ITID-24411.response: Report the batch to the platform for removal; this pattern is typically handled efficiently by the platform's existing anti-spam systems with organizational reporting as a supplement.
metrics: Volume of disposable-account reviews identified and removed per quarter
ITID-24411.notes: Differentiated from sibling 24412 (aged/stolen accounts) by the disposable, freshly-created nature of the accounts used, which makes this variant comparatively easier to detect than its siblings.

playbook.name: Response: Mass-Created Disposable Account Review Spam
playbook.description: For negative reviews posted from a large number of newly created, disposable accounts with no meaningful history — a common low-effort review-manipulation pattern.

steps.title: Pull account-age and activity data for the flagged reviews
steps.desc: Export account creation dates, review counts, and profile completeness for each flagged reviewer.

steps.title: Submit a bulk fake-account report via the platform's trust & safety portal/API
steps.desc: Most review platforms provide a bulk-reporting mechanism for confirmed inauthentic account networks — use it rather than reporting reviews one at a time.
steps.tool: Platform trust & safety portal / bulk-report API

steps.title: Pursue removal through platform enforcement
steps.desc: Follow up until the reviews and accounts are actioned by the platform.
steps.outcome: Reviews and accounts removed or annotated.

steps.title: Monitor rating recovery and recurrence
steps.desc: Track rating trend and watch for a new wave of disposable accounts.

steps.title: Document the detection signature for faster future bulk reporting
steps.desc: Record the specific account-age/velocity thresholds that identified this batch, to speed up detection and bulk-reporting next time.

steps.title: Confirm the disposable-account signature
steps.desc: Check for the technical/behavioral signature: accounts created shortly before posting, single-review histories, generic or missing profile details, and posting-velocity clustering in a short window.
steps.outcome: Disposable-account pattern confirmed with supporting data.
steps.abort: If accounts show established, varied review histories, this is not a disposable-account pattern — reassess as a different manipulation type or a genuine complaint.

steps.title: Flag the account list internally for ongoing monitoring
steps.desc: Retain the identified account list to recognize reuse of the same disposable accounts in future campaigns.

ITID-24412.def: Review-platform abuse using accounts that have genuine age and prior activity history — either stolen via account takeover or purchased on black-market forums — making the resulting reviews harder to distinguish from genuine activity than freshly-created accounts.
ITID-24412.purpose: Captures review-platform spam using stolen or black-market-purchased aged accounts, which evade detection better than freshly-created disposable accounts.
scopeIncludes: Reviews from accounts with established registration dates and prior unrelated activity history inconsistent with a sudden review-posting pattern
Accounts flagged by the platform's account-takeover detection coinciding with review posting
scopeExcludes: Freshly-created disposable accounts (ITID-24411)
Cross-platform spam networks reused across multiple platforms (ITID-24413)
ITID-24412.severity: Medium-High; aged-account credibility makes this variant harder to detect and more damaging per-review than disposable-account spam.
ITID-24412.priority: P2 given the elevated credibility and detection difficulty relative to sibling 24411.
ITID-24412.escalation: Escalate to the platform's account-security team specifically (not just content moderation), since the underlying issue is account compromise or black-market trafficking.
indicators: An account's established history showing an abrupt, inconsistent shift to review-posting activity
Platform account-takeover flags coinciding with review timing
vectors: Black-market purchase of aged/established accounts
Credential-stuffing or phishing to take over legitimate dormant accounts
rootCauses: No monitoring for anomalous behavioral-history shifts in reviewer accounts
No escalation channel to the platform's account-security team distinct from content moderation
controls: Behavioral-history anomaly monitoring on reviewer accounts
Escalation relationship with the platform's account-security team
ITID-24412.detection: Detection depends on the platform's account-takeover telemetry and behavioral-history-mismatch analysis; harder technical detection surface than sibling 24411 given the accounts' genuine aging.
ITID-24412.response: Report specific accounts to the platform's account-security team, request review removal as originating from a compromised/trafficked account, and document for the brand-abuse record.
metrics: Count of aged-account-sourced reviews identified per quarter
Platform account-security escalation response time
ITID-24412.notes: Differentiated from sibling 24411 by account aging/legitimacy, which materially increases both credibility and detection difficulty; warrants the Compromise Accounts mapping given the genuine account-takeover/trafficking mechanism.

playbook.name: Response: Stolen/Purchased Aged Account Review Spam
playbook.description: For negative reviews posted through older, established accounts that have been stolen or purchased specifically to lend false credibility to the review manipulation.

steps.title: Pull account history data for the flagged reviews
steps.desc: Export account age, prior review topics/categories, and any sudden shift in posting behavior for each flagged account.

steps.title: Submit a report to the platform's account-security and trust & safety teams
steps.desc: Flag both the fraudulent reviews and the likely account compromise/resale, which platforms often prioritize over standard fake-review reports.
steps.tool: Platform trust & safety / account security portal

steps.title: Pursue removal and account restoration
steps.desc: Track the platform's remediation — review removal and restoration/lockdown of the affected accounts.

steps.title: Monitor for reappearance under newly acquired aged accounts
steps.desc: Watch for a repeat pattern suggesting continued cycling through purchased/stolen accounts.

steps.title: Document the detection signature
steps.desc: Record how the aged-account mismatch was identified, to speed up detection of future occurrences.

steps.title: Confirm the aged-account compromise/purchase signature
steps.desc: Look for a mismatch between an account's long-standing history (e.g. years of unrelated reviews) and a sudden, out-of-character negative review, often alongside other accounts showing the same pattern in the same timeframe.
steps.outcome: Compromise/purchase pattern confirmed with supporting evidence.
steps.abort: If the review is consistent with the account's established history and interests, treat it as a potentially genuine review rather than manipulation.

steps.title: Preserve evidence of the pattern across accounts
steps.desc: Archive the account list and behavioral evidence before the platform or operator can alter or delete it.

ITID-24413.def: Review-platform manipulation carried out by an account network whose infrastructure (registration patterns, automation signatures) is observed being reused across multiple, distinct platforms (e.g., the same underlying network posting fake reviews, fake social engagement, and fake app ratings), indicating a commercial engagement-fraud-as-a-service operation.
ITID-24413.purpose: Captures review-platform spam executed by a network of accounts that is reused across multiple, unrelated platforms rather than being dedicated to a single review site.
scopeIncludes: Review-manipulation activity traceable to an account network with a known infrastructure signature also seen operating on unrelated platforms
Cases where the network's commercial 'service' nature (sold/rented to multiple paying clients) is the salient investigative lead
scopeExcludes: A single-platform disposable-account spam campaign (ITID-24411)
A single-platform aged/stolen-account campaign (ITID-24412)
ITID-24413.severity: Medium; comparable to sibling leaves per-incident, but the cross-platform reuse indicates a persistent, ongoing threat actor worth sustained tracking.
ITID-24413.priority: P2 if the network is newly identified and actively engaging with the organization's platforms; P3 for routine monitoring once tracked.
ITID-24413.escalation: Escalate to threat-intel/brand-protection to track the network's infrastructure signature over time across all platforms where the brand has a presence.
indicators: Account infrastructure signatures matching a network previously observed on unrelated platforms
Evidence the network is commercially available (e.g., advertised on underground forums as an engagement-fraud service)
vectors: Commercial engagement-fraud-as-a-service networks rented to multiple paying clients across platforms
rootCauses: No threat-intelligence tracking of cross-platform account-network infrastructure signatures relevant to the brand
controls: Cross-platform threat-intelligence tracking of account-network infrastructure signatures
ITID-24413.detection: Detected via infrastructure-signature correlation using threat-intel tooling across platforms; a genuine technical detection surface given the network's reusable, fingerprint-able infrastructure.
ITID-24413.response: Report the network signature to each affected platform, and maintain an ongoing threat-intel watch on the network across the brand's full platform footprint.
metrics: Count of platforms where the tracked network has been observed targeting the brand
ITID-24413.notes: Differentiated from siblings 24411/24412 by the cross-platform, commercial-service nature of the network, warranting sustained threat-intel tracking rather than one-off incident handling.

playbook.name: Response: Cross-Platform Spam Account Network Reused for Reviews
playbook.description: For a spam account network previously used for other abuse (e.g. social media spam, fake follows) that has been redeployed to post reviews against the company.

steps.title: Identify the account network and cross-reference known spam signatures
steps.desc: Check the flagged accounts against known spam-network indicators — shared naming conventions, near-identical bios, cross-posting of unrelated spam content on the same accounts.
steps.outcome: Network identified and cross-referenced against known spam patterns.
steps.tool: Review platform dashboard / social listening tool

steps.title: Submit a bulk report identifying the network as reused spam infrastructure
steps.desc: Provide the platform's trust & safety team with the cross-platform evidence, which strengthens the case for network-wide action rather than individual review removal.
steps.tool: Platform trust & safety portal / bulk-report API

steps.title: Pursue network-wide removal through platform enforcement
steps.desc: Follow up until the platform actions the full account network, not just the individual flagged reviews.

steps.title: Monitor for redeployment of the network
steps.desc: Watch for the same network resurfacing under new account names.

steps.title: Document the network's signature for faster future recognition
steps.desc: Record identifying characteristics of the network to recognize it faster if redeployed again.

steps.title: Confirm the cross-platform reuse pattern
steps.desc: Establish that the same accounts or account cluster are active with similar spam behavior on other platforms, indicating a reused network rather than a one-off campaign.
steps.outcome: Cross-platform reuse confirmed with supporting evidence.

steps.title: Share threat-intelligence with other affected platforms where appropriate
steps.desc: If the same network is known to be active elsewhere, consider sharing non-sensitive indicators with the other platform's trust & safety team.

ITID-24414.def: A suspected spam-account review-manipulation incident awaiting further investigation to determine its specific account mechanism before reclassification to the appropriate sibling ITID.
ITID-24414.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for a suspected spam-account review-manipulation incident not yet triaged to the disposable, aged, or cross-platform-network mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Newly-detected spam-account review activity not yet triaged to a specific mechanism
scopeExcludes: Any incident for which the mechanism has been confirmed and should be reclassified to ITID-24411, ITID-24412, or ITID-24413
ITID-24414.escalation: Escalate to the brand/reputation analyst on triage duty; reclassify promptly once the mechanism is clear.
indicators: An unexplained spam-account review pattern without yet-established mechanism attribution
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial evidence to attribute mechanism at time of intake
controls: Account-age/review-timing anomaly monitoring
ITID-24414.detection: Same detection surface as sibling leaves, pending mechanism attribution.
ITID-24414.response: Triage promptly and reclassify to the specific sibling ITID once the mechanism is clear.
metrics: Count of incidents held in this bucket beyond 5 business days without reclassification
ITID-24414.notes: Intake/triage bucket only, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Spam Account Review Manipulation
playbook.description: General-purpose response for review manipulation via spam accounts that does not fit a more specific known pattern (mass-created disposable, stolen/purchased aged, or cross-platform reused accounts).

steps.title: Pull account data for the flagged reviews
steps.desc: Export account age, history, and posting-behavior data for each flagged account.

steps.title: Submit a bulk report to the platform's trust & safety team
steps.desc: Use the platform's bulk-reporting mechanism where available rather than reporting reviews individually.
steps.tool: Platform trust & safety portal / bulk-report API

steps.title: Pursue removal through platform enforcement
steps.desc: Follow up until the reviews/accounts are actioned by the platform.
steps.outcome: Reviews and accounts removed or annotated.

steps.title: Monitor rating recovery and recurrence
steps.desc: Track rating trend and watch for a repeat wave.

steps.title: Document the detection signature
steps.desc: Record the pattern that identified this batch for faster future detection.

steps.title: Confirm the spam-account signature
steps.desc: Look for behavioral/technical indicators of inauthenticity — unnatural velocity, sparse or mismatched history, clustering with other flagged accounts.
steps.outcome: Spam-account pattern confirmed with supporting evidence.
steps.abort: If the accounts show genuine, consistent activity, reassess whether this is truly a spam network.

steps.title: Preserve evidence of the account pattern
steps.desc: Archive the account list and supporting evidence.

ITID-24421.def: Exploitation of a review platform's internal review-sorting or ranking logic (such as 'most helpful' voting weight or recency weighting) to artificially surface favorable reviews or bury unfavorable ones, independent of the reviews' actual content authenticity.
ITID-24421.purpose: Captures manipulation of a review platform's own internal sorting/ranking algorithm (e.g., 'most helpful' or default sort order) to bury or surface specific reviews.
scopeIncludes: Gaming a platform's 'helpful' vote weighting to push specific reviews to the top or bottom of the default sort
Exploiting recency or verified-purchase sort-weighting logic to disproportionately surface/bury specific reviews
scopeExcludes: Manipulation of an external search engine's ranking of review-related results (ITID-24422)
Manipulation of a platform's product/service recommendation engine rather than its review sort order (ITID-24423)
ITID-24421.severity: Medium; the reviews themselves may be genuine, but the sort-order manipulation misrepresents overall sentiment to browsing customers.
ITID-24421.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if the manipulation is sustained and materially distorts the visible rating/sentiment for the listing.
ITID-24421.escalation: Escalate to the platform's trust-and-safety/algorithm-integrity team, since remediation requires the platform's own ranking-logic intervention.
indicators: A statistically improbable concentration of 'helpful' votes on specific reviews within a short window
A visible sort-order pattern inconsistent with the platform's stated ranking methodology
vectors: Coordinated 'helpful' vote-gaming via bot or paid-human networks targeting the sort algorithm specifically
rootCauses: No monitoring of anomalous helpful-vote concentration patterns on the organization's own listings
controls: Helpful-vote-concentration anomaly monitoring on owned listings
Escalation relationship with the platform's algorithm-integrity team
ITID-24421.detection: Detected via statistical anomaly analysis of vote/sort patterns on the organization's own listings; a moderate technical detection surface given the platform's own vote-metadata visibility.
ITID-24421.response: Report the anomalous voting pattern to the platform's algorithm-integrity team and request a ranking-logic review/reset for the affected listing.
metrics: Count of sort-order manipulation incidents identified per quarter
ITID-24421.notes: Differentiated from siblings 24422 (search-engine ranking) and 24423 (recommendation engine) by targeting the review platform's own internal sort/ranking logic specifically.

playbook.name: Response: Review Sorting/Ranking Algorithm Manipulation
playbook.description: For an attempt to manipulate the review platform's own sorting or ranking algorithm — e.g. coordinated 'helpful' votes, timing exploits, or engagement-farming to push negative reviews to the top or bury positive ones.

steps.title: Identify the specific ranking signal being gamed
steps.desc: Determine which mechanism is being exploited — helpful-vote brigading, coordinated timing, engagement farming, or another platform-specific ranking input.

steps.title: Report the manipulation to the platform via its integrity/abuse-reporting channel
steps.desc: Most platforms have a dedicated channel, separate from individual content reports, for reporting engagement or ranking-signal manipulation — use that channel with the technical evidence package.
steps.outcome: Report submitted to the appropriate platform integrity team.
steps.tool: Platform integrity/abuse reporting portal or API

steps.title: Pursue correction of the ranking and removal of the manipulating activity
steps.desc: Follow up until the platform corrects the affected rankings and actions the accounts/votes responsible.

steps.title: Monitor ranking stability and recurrence
steps.desc: Track whether rankings stabilize and watch for renewed manipulation attempts.

steps.title: Document the exploit mechanism for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the specific ranking signal and manipulation technique used, since platform-specific exploits are often reused.

steps.title: Gather technical/behavioral evidence of the manipulation
steps.desc: Collect data showing the anomalous pattern — e.g. a spike in 'helpful' votes from newly created or clustered accounts on specific reviews, occurring in a tight timeframe.
steps.outcome: Evidence package assembled showing the manipulation pattern.
steps.abort: If the ranking shift is explainable by genuine organic engagement, this is not an algorithm-exploit incident.

steps.title: Flag the affected reviews/rankings internally
steps.desc: Note which reviews are artificially ranked so internal teams understand the true standing while the platform investigates.

ITID-24422.def: Exploitation of an external search engine's ranking algorithm using review-related signals (e.g., review-schema markup abuse, fabricated star-rating rich snippets, or review-farm-linked SEO tactics) to distort search-result visibility or star-rating display for the organization's listings.
ITID-24422.purpose: Captures manipulation of an external search engine's ranking signals via review-related content to distort search visibility for the organization or its listings.
scopeIncludes: Fabricated or manipulated review-schema markup producing misleading star-rating rich snippets in search results
SEO campaigns using review-farm content specifically to manipulate search ranking signals
scopeExcludes: Manipulation confined to a review platform's own internal sort order (ITID-24421)
Manipulation of a platform's product recommendation engine (ITID-24423)
ITID-24422.severity: Medium-High; search-result-level manipulation affects visibility far beyond the review platform itself, reaching all potential customers using search.
ITID-24422.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the manipulation is being used against the organization by an attacker (e.g., suppressing its search visibility) rather than in its favor.
ITID-24422.escalation: Escalate to SEO/digital-marketing and the search engine's webmaster/spam-reporting channel; legal if the manipulation constitutes a targeted attack rather than the organization's own (improper) practice.
indicators: Star-rating rich snippets inconsistent with the actual aggregate rating on the source review platform
Anomalous review-farm-linked backlink or schema-markup patterns detected in SEO audits
vectors: Fabricated review-schema markup abuse
Review-farm-linked SEO/backlink manipulation targeting search ranking
rootCauses: No SEO integrity monitoring for review-schema markup discrepancies
No search-engine spam-reporting relationship for third-party manipulation targeting the brand
controls: SEO integrity monitoring for review-schema markup discrepancies
Search-engine spam-reporting relationship
ITID-24422.detection: Detected via SEO-audit tooling comparing displayed search-result ratings against source-platform ratings; a moderate technical detection surface.
ITID-24422.response: Verify the schema-markup discrepancy, correct it if it originated internally, or report to the search engine's spam-reporting channel if externally manipulated against the organization.
metrics: Count of schema-markup/search-ranking discrepancies identified per quarter
ITID-24422.notes: Differentiated from sibling 24421 by targeting external search-engine ranking signals rather than the review platform's own internal sort logic.

playbook.name: Response: Search Result Ranking Manipulation via Review Signal Gaming
playbook.description: For manipulation of a third-party search engine or marketplace's ranking algorithm by gaming review-related signals it uses (e.g. review velocity, review-response rate, or keyword-stuffed review content).

steps.title: Identify which review-related search-ranking signal is being gamed
steps.desc: Determine the specific signal being targeted — e.g. artificial review velocity, keyword-stuffed review text designed to game search relevance, or fabricated review-response patterns.

steps.title: Report the manipulation to the platform's search-integrity/webmaster abuse channel
steps.desc: Search platforms and marketplaces typically have a dedicated spam/manipulation reporting channel separate from content moderation — use the technical evidence package there.
steps.outcome: Report submitted to the appropriate integrity team.

steps.title: Pursue correction of the ranking and removal of the gaming content
steps.desc: Follow up until the platform demotes/removes the manipulating content and corrects the ranking impact.

steps.title: Monitor ranking stability and recurrence
steps.desc: Track whether rankings stabilize and watch for renewed gaming attempts.

steps.title: Document the gaming technique for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the specific signal and technique used, to recognize similar gaming attempts sooner.

steps.title: Gather technical evidence of the gaming pattern
steps.desc: Collect data showing the anomalous pattern in review timing, content, or structure that is designed to manipulate ranking rather than reflect genuine feedback.
steps.abort: If the pattern is explainable by a legitimate marketing campaign or organic surge, this is not a gaming incident.

steps.title: Flag the affected rankings internally
steps.desc: Note the artificially influenced rankings so internal Marketing/SEO teams do not mistake them for organic performance.

ITID-24423.def: Exploitation of a platform's recommendation engine (e.g., 'customers also liked', personalized recommendation feeds) using manipulated review signals to suppress the organization's products from recommendation surfaces or to inject a competitor's products in their place.
ITID-24423.purpose: Captures manipulation of a platform's product/service recommendation engine using review signals, distinct from review sort order or external search ranking.
scopeIncludes: Manipulated review-sentiment signals used specifically to suppress the organization's listings from a platform's recommendation feed
Fabricated negative-review signal injection timed to degrade recommendation-engine standing
scopeExcludes: Manipulation of the review platform's own sort/ranking of reviews (ITID-24421)
Manipulation of external search-engine ranking (ITID-24422)
ITID-24423.severity: Medium-High; recommendation-engine suppression can materially reduce organic discovery and sales on the affected platform.
ITID-24423.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if a sustained, measurable sales-impact is confirmed.
ITID-24423.escalation: Escalate to the platform's algorithm-integrity/trust-and-safety team and to the organization's own platform-relations/marketplace-management function.
indicators: A measurable drop in recommendation-feed placement inconsistent with actual rating/sentiment trends
Review-sentiment signal anomalies correlating with the recommendation-placement drop
vectors: Coordinated fake-negative-review injection specifically timed and weighted to influence recommendation-engine inputs
rootCauses: No monitoring of recommendation-feed placement trends relative to actual review-sentiment trends
controls: Recommendation-feed placement monitoring relative to review-sentiment trends
Escalation relationship with the platform's algorithm-integrity team
ITID-24423.detection: Detected via platform-analytics monitoring of recommendation placement versus underlying sentiment trends; a moderate technical detection surface given typical platform seller-analytics visibility.
ITID-24423.response: Report the anomaly to the platform's algorithm-integrity team with supporting analytics, and request an investigation into the recommendation-engine's input weighting for the affected listing.
metrics: Recommendation-feed placement trend versus sentiment trend divergence
ITID-24423.notes: Differentiated from siblings 24421/24422 by targeting the platform's recommendation/discovery engine specifically, rather than review sort order or external search ranking.

playbook.name: Response: Platform Recommendation Engine Gaming
playbook.description: For manipulation of a platform's recommendation engine (e.g. 'similar products,' 'people also viewed,' or personalized feed placement) using review-related or engagement signals to suppress the company's visibility or promote a competitor's.

steps.title: Identify the recommendation surface and signal being gamed
steps.desc: Determine which recommendation feature is affected and what signal (reviews, click patterns, co-engagement) appears to be manipulated.

steps.title: Report the manipulation to the platform's integrity/abuse team
steps.desc: Submit the technical evidence package through the platform's dedicated integrity-abuse reporting channel.

steps.title: Pursue correction of the recommendation placement
steps.desc: Follow up until the platform corrects the placement and actions the responsible activity.

steps.title: Monitor placement stability and recurrence
steps.desc: Track whether the recommendation placement stabilizes and watch for renewed gaming attempts.

steps.title: Document the gaming technique
steps.desc: Record the specific signal and mechanism used, to recognize similar attempts sooner.

steps.title: Gather technical evidence of the gaming pattern
steps.desc: Collect data showing anomalous engagement or review patterns coinciding with the recommendation shift.
steps.abort: If the shift is explainable by a legitimate change in genuine customer behavior, this is not a gaming incident.

steps.title: Flag the affected recommendation placements internally
steps.desc: Note the artificially influenced placements so Marketing/Category teams understand the true picture.

ITID-24424.def: A suspected review-platform algorithm exploit awaiting further investigation to determine its specific target mechanism before reclassification to the appropriate sibling ITID.
ITID-24424.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for a suspected review-platform algorithm exploit not yet triaged to the sort-order, search-ranking, or recommendation-engine mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Newly-detected algorithmic manipulation patterns not yet triaged to a specific mechanism
scopeExcludes: Any incident for which the mechanism has been confirmed and should be reclassified to ITID-24421, ITID-24422, or ITID-24423
ITID-24424.escalation: Escalate to the brand/reputation analyst on triage duty; reclassify promptly once the mechanism is clear.
indicators: An unexplained algorithmic-visibility anomaly without yet-established mechanism attribution
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial evidence to attribute mechanism at time of intake
controls: General algorithmic-visibility anomaly monitoring
ITID-24424.detection: Same detection surface as sibling leaves, pending mechanism attribution.
ITID-24424.response: Triage promptly and reclassify to the specific sibling ITID once the mechanism is clear.
metrics: Count of incidents held in this bucket beyond 5 business days without reclassification
ITID-24424.notes: Intake/triage bucket only, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Review Platform Algorithm Exploit
playbook.description: General-purpose response for a review-platform algorithm exploit that does not fit a more specific known pattern (review sorting/ranking, search ranking, or recommendation engine gaming).

steps.title: Identify the specific mechanism being exploited
steps.desc: Determine which platform algorithm or ranking signal appears to be manipulated.

steps.title: Report the exploit to the platform's integrity/abuse team
steps.desc: Submit the technical evidence package through the platform's dedicated integrity-abuse reporting channel.

steps.title: Pursue correction and removal of the manipulating activity
steps.desc: Follow up until the platform corrects the impact and actions the responsible activity.

steps.title: Monitor for stability and recurrence
steps.desc: Track whether the affected metric stabilizes and watch for renewed exploitation.

steps.title: Document the exploit technique
steps.desc: Record the mechanism and technique used, to recognize similar exploits sooner.

steps.title: Gather technical/behavioral evidence of the exploit
steps.desc: Collect data showing the anomalous pattern responsible for the ranking or visibility shift.
steps.abort: If the shift is explainable by genuine organic activity, this is not an exploit incident.

steps.title: Flag the affected rankings/placements internally
steps.desc: Note the artificially influenced outcomes so internal teams understand the true picture.

ITID-24431.def: A campaign using traditional scripted/automated bots to post reviews at scale, relying on fixed or lightly-varied templated text rather than generative-AI text production or advanced anti-bot evasion.
ITID-24431.purpose: Captures a review-posting campaign executed by traditional scripted automation (fixed-template bots) rather than AI-generated text or CAPTCHA-evasion technology.
scopeIncludes: Reviews posted via scripted automation using templated or lightly-varied fixed text patterns
Bot farms detectable via repeated exact or near-exact phrase matching across many reviews
scopeExcludes: AI-generated unique review text at scale (ITID-24432)
Bot networks specifically engineered to bypass CAPTCHA/anti-bot verification as their defining feature (ITID-24433)
ITID-24431.severity: Medium; the most detectable variant in this sibling group due to repeated/templated text patterns.
ITID-24431.priority: P3, escalating to P2 for high-volume campaigns.
ITID-24431.escalation: Escalate to the platform's automated anti-spam detection channel, which typically catches repeated-text patterns efficiently.
indicators: Exact or near-exact repeated phrases across many reviews
Reviews posted at machine-consistent intervals inconsistent with human posting behavior
vectors: Scripted bot farms using template-based text generation for review posting
rootCauses: No text-similarity monitoring across incoming reviews for the organization's listings
controls: Text-similarity/duplicate-phrase monitoring across incoming reviews
Reliance on platform-native bot detection
ITID-24431.detection: Detected via text-similarity analysis and posting-interval regularity, a straightforward technical detection surface given the templated nature of the content.
ITID-24431.response: Report the batch and its text-similarity evidence to the platform for removal.
metrics: Volume of templated-text bot reviews identified and removed per quarter
ITID-24431.notes: Differentiated from sibling 24432 (AI-generated unique text) by the templated/repeated nature of the text, and from sibling 24433 by the absence of CAPTCHA-evasion as a defining feature.

playbook.name: Response: Automated Scripted Review-Posting Bot Farm
playbook.description: For negative reviews posted by an automated script/bot farm operating at scale against the company, rather than manually operated fake accounts.

steps.title: Detect the automation signature
steps.desc: Analyze posting timestamps, intervals, and request patterns for machine-like regularity inconsistent with human posting behavior.
steps.outcome: Automation signature identified with supporting data.

steps.title: Submit a bulk-report identifying the confirmed bot network via the platform's API/portal
steps.desc: Most review platforms provide a bulk-reporting mechanism or API specifically for confirmed automated abuse — use it with the full evidence package rather than reporting reviews individually.
steps.tool: Platform trust & safety portal / bulk-report API

steps.title: Pursue removal through platform enforcement
steps.desc: Follow up until the platform actions the bot network and its output.
steps.outcome: Bot network and reviews removed or annotated.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence under a modified script
steps.desc: Watch for the same or a modified automation pattern reappearing.

steps.title: Document the automation signature for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the specific timing/pattern indicators that identified this bot farm.

steps.title: Quantify scale and confirm coordination
steps.desc: Determine the number of accounts/reviews involved and confirm they trace to a single scripted operation rather than independent actors.
steps.abort: If posting patterns are irregular and human-consistent, reassess as a manually operated campaign instead.

steps.title: Preserve technical evidence of the automation pattern
steps.desc: Archive timing/pattern data before the operator can alter behavior to evade detection.

ITID-24432.def: A campaign using generative-AI language models to produce large volumes of unique, non-templated fake review text, deliberately evading the text-similarity detection that catches traditional scripted bot campaigns.
ITID-24432.purpose: Captures a review-posting campaign using generative-AI text production to create unique, non-repeating fake review content at scale, evading simple text-similarity detection.
scopeIncludes: Fake reviews with no repeated/templated phrasing but detectable AI-generation stylistic markers (e.g., unnaturally consistent tone, generic specificity, AI-detector tool flags)
High-volume review batches where per-review text similarity is low but posting-account/infrastructure patterns still indicate coordination
scopeExcludes: Traditional scripted/templated bot campaigns (ITID-24431)
CAPTCHA-bypass-focused bot networks (ITID-24433)
ITID-24432.severity: Medium-High; harder to detect via simple text-similarity methods than templated bot campaigns, requiring more sophisticated AI-content-detection tooling.
ITID-24432.priority: P2 given the elevated detection difficulty and this being an emerging, growing attack pattern.
ITID-24432.escalation: Escalate to the platform's trust-and-safety team with AI-content-detection evidence, since standard text-duplication filters will not catch this pattern.
indicators: Reviews flagged by AI-content-detection tooling despite low text-similarity to each other
Coordinated account/infrastructure patterns despite individually unique review text
Generic, oddly-consistent stylistic patterns typical of LLM-generated content
vectors: Generative-AI text production integrated into a review-posting bot pipeline
rootCauses: No AI-content-detection tooling applied to incoming review monitoring; reliance on legacy text-similarity methods alone
controls: AI-generated-content detection tooling applied to incoming review monitoring
Account/infrastructure-pattern correlation independent of text similarity
ITID-24432.detection: Requires AI-content-detection tooling and infrastructure/account-pattern correlation rather than simple text-duplication analysis; a meaningfully harder technical detection surface than sibling 24431.
ITID-24432.response: Apply AI-content-detection tooling and account-infrastructure correlation to build an evidentiary case, then report the batch to the platform.
metrics: Volume of AI-generated fake reviews identified per quarter
AI-content-detection tool flag rate on incoming reviews
ITID-24432.notes: Differentiated from sibling 24431 by the use of generative AI to produce unique text specifically to evade text-similarity detection — an emerging and increasingly common variant.

playbook.name: Response: AI-Generated Fake Review Text at Scale
playbook.description: For a wave of fake reviews using AI-generated text at scale, designed to appear varied and human-written while actually being produced by a language model.

steps.title: Collect the suspect reviews for text analysis
steps.desc: Export the flagged reviews' full text alongside account metadata.

steps.title: Submit a bulk report to the platform identifying the AI-generated review cluster
steps.desc: Use the platform's bulk-reporting mechanism or API, including the text-similarity evidence, since this is often more persuasive than reporting reviews individually.
steps.tool: Platform trust & safety portal / bulk-report API

steps.title: Pursue removal through platform enforcement
steps.desc: Follow up until the platform actions the identified review cluster and associated accounts.
steps.outcome: Reviews and accounts removed or annotated.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence with regenerated text
steps.desc: Watch for a new wave using differently generated but similarly patterned text.

steps.title: Document the detection method for faster future analysis
steps.desc: Record which text-similarity/AI-detection approach worked, to speed up future analysis of similar campaigns.

steps.title: Run text-similarity/AI-generation detection analysis
steps.desc: Apply text-similarity clustering and AI-text-detection signals to identify reviews that share underlying structure, phrasing patterns, or generation artifacts despite surface-level rewording.
steps.outcome: AI-generated pattern confirmed across a cluster of reviews, with supporting analysis.
steps.abort: If the reviews show genuine stylistic diversity and no generation artifacts, reassess as a different manipulation type or genuine feedback.

steps.title: Preserve the text-analysis evidence
steps.desc: Archive the similarity/detection analysis output before the reviews are altered or removed.

ITID-24433.def: A review-posting bot network whose defining and most technically significant characteristic is its capability to defeat CAPTCHA and other anti-automation verification challenges on the review platform, regardless of whether the review text itself is templated or AI-generated.
ITID-24433.purpose: Captures a review-posting bot network specifically engineered to bypass CAPTCHA and other anti-bot verification mechanisms, distinguishing it by its evasion capability rather than its text-generation method.
scopeIncludes: Bot activity confirmed to be bypassing the platform's CAPTCHA or anti-bot challenge mechanisms
Cases where the CAPTCHA-bypass technique itself (e.g., CAPTCHA-solving services, browser-automation fingerprint spoofing) is the primary investigative and remediation focus
scopeExcludes: Scripted/templated bot campaigns not specifically engineered around CAPTCHA evasion (ITID-24431)
AI-text-generation-focused campaigns where CAPTCHA evasion is not the distinguishing feature (ITID-24432)
ITID-24433.severity: High; successful CAPTCHA bypass indicates a more sophisticated, well-resourced adversary and undermines the platform's core anti-abuse defense layer.
ITID-24433.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the bypass technique is novel and not yet known to the platform's security team.
ITID-24433.escalation: Escalate immediately to the platform's security/anti-abuse engineering team, since this represents a defeat of their core automated-abuse defense requiring an engineering-level fix, not just content moderation.
indicators: Confirmed automated posting activity that successfully passed CAPTCHA/anti-bot challenges
Browser-automation fingerprint anomalies (headless-browser signatures, timing patterns) in posting behavior
vectors: Commercial CAPTCHA-solving services (human-relay or AI-based)
Browser-automation fingerprint spoofing to mimic genuine human interaction patterns
rootCauses: Platform anti-bot verification mechanism has a known or emerging bypass vulnerability
controls: Browser-automation fingerprint anomaly detection
Escalation relationship with the platform's security/anti-abuse engineering team
ITID-24433.detection: Requires the platform's own security telemetry (browser fingerprinting, behavioral biometrics) to detect; the most technically sophisticated detection challenge in this sibling group.
ITID-24433.response: Report the CAPTCHA-bypass evidence directly to the platform's security/anti-abuse engineering team for a defense-layer fix, in addition to standard content removal.
metrics: Count of confirmed CAPTCHA-bypass incidents identified per quarter
ITID-24433.notes: Differentiated from siblings 24431/24432 by the CAPTCHA-bypass mechanism being the defining characteristic, regardless of the review text-generation method used.

playbook.name: Response: CAPTCHA-Bypass Automated Review Bot Network
playbook.description: For an automated review bot network specifically engineered to bypass the platform's CAPTCHA or other anti-automation defenses in order to post at scale.

steps.title: Detect the automation signature despite CAPTCHA bypass
steps.desc: Analyze posting timestamps, account creation velocity, and behavioral patterns for machine-like regularity, since the bypass defeats the platform's front-line automation defense but not behavioral analysis.
steps.outcome: Automation signature identified with supporting data.

steps.title: Submit a bulk report to the platform's trust & safety and security engineering teams
steps.desc: Given the CAPTCHA-bypass sophistication, flag this to both trust & safety (for content removal) and, where a contact exists, security engineering (since it indicates a platform defense gap), using the platform's bulk-report API/portal.
steps.outcome: Report submitted and acknowledged by relevant teams.
steps.tool: Platform trust & safety portal / bulk-report API

steps.title: Pursue removal through platform enforcement
steps.desc: Follow up until the platform actions the bot network and its output.
steps.outcome: Bot network and reviews removed or annotated.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence with an adapted bypass technique
steps.desc: Watch for the same actor returning with a modified bypass method.

steps.title: Document the bypass technique and detection signature
steps.desc: Record the automation and bypass indicators observed, for faster detection and to inform the platform's defense improvements.

steps.title: Quantify scale and assess the sophistication of the bypass
steps.desc: Determine the number of accounts/reviews involved and note any details about the bypass method that would help the platform harden its defenses.

steps.title: Preserve technical evidence of the automation and bypass pattern
steps.desc: Archive timing/pattern data and any observable bypass indicators before the operator can adapt.

ITID-24434.def: A suspected paid review bot campaign awaiting further investigation to determine its specific mechanism before reclassification to the appropriate sibling ITID.
ITID-24434.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for a suspected paid review bot campaign not yet triaged to the scripted-template, AI-generated-text, or CAPTCHA-bypass mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Newly-detected bot-driven review activity not yet triaged to a specific mechanism
scopeExcludes: Any incident for which the mechanism has been confirmed and should be reclassified to ITID-24431, ITID-24432, or ITID-24433
ITID-24434.escalation: Escalate to the brand/reputation analyst on triage duty; reclassify promptly once the mechanism is clear.
indicators: An unexplained bot-driven review pattern without yet-established mechanism attribution
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial evidence to attribute mechanism at time of intake
controls: General bot-activity monitoring on review platforms
ITID-24434.detection: Same detection surface as sibling leaves, pending mechanism attribution.
ITID-24434.response: Triage promptly and reclassify to the specific sibling ITID once the mechanism is clear.
metrics: Count of incidents held in this bucket beyond 5 business days without reclassification
ITID-24434.notes: Intake/triage bucket only, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Paid Review Bot Campaign
playbook.description: General-purpose response for a paid review bot campaign that does not fit a more specific known pattern (scripted bot farm, AI-generated text, or CAPTCHA-bypass network).

steps.title: Detect the automation/bot signature
steps.desc: Analyze posting timestamps, account patterns, and content for indicators of automated or bot-driven posting.
steps.outcome: Automation signature identified with supporting data.

steps.title: Submit a bulk report to the platform via its trust & safety portal/API
steps.desc: Use the platform's bulk-reporting mechanism for confirmed automated abuse.
steps.tool: Platform trust & safety portal / bulk-report API

steps.title: Pursue removal through platform enforcement
steps.desc: Follow up until the platform actions the network and its output.
steps.outcome: Network and reviews removed or annotated.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Watch for a new wave from the same or a related operation.

steps.title: Document the detection signature
steps.desc: Record the pattern that identified this campaign for faster future detection.

steps.title: Quantify scale and confirm the pattern
steps.desc: Determine the number of accounts/reviews involved and confirm the bot/automated origin.
steps.abort: If the pattern is not confirmed as automated, reassess as a different manipulation type.

steps.title: Preserve evidence of the pattern
steps.desc: Archive the supporting data before the operator can adapt.

ITID-24511.def: An influencer publishes a positive review or endorsement of a competitor's legitimate product/service without disclosing that they were paid to do so, in violation of advertising-disclosure regulations (e.g., FTC endorsement guidelines), potentially drawing customers away from the organization under false pretenses of organic endorsement.
ITID-24511.purpose: Captures an influencer posting an undisclosed paid positive review for a legitimate competitor product, violating disclosure regulations and misleading the organization's prospective customers.
scopeIncludes: An identifiable influencer post promoting a competitor's product with no #ad/#sponsored disclosure, where payment can be confirmed or reasonably inferred
Cases explicitly or implicitly framing the endorsement as an independent, unpaid opinion
scopeExcludes: Undisclosed paid promotion of a counterfeit/scam product rather than a legitimate competitor (ITID-24512)
Sponsored content misrepresenting comparative test/benchmark results (ITID-24513)
Properly disclosed sponsored content (a compliant marketing practice, not an incident)
ITID-24511.severity: Low-to-Medium; primarily a competitive/regulatory-compliance concern for the competitor and influencer rather than a direct attack on the organization.
ITID-24511.priority: P3 for monitoring/awareness; escalate only if the organization intends to file a regulatory complaint.
ITID-24511.escalation: Escalate to legal/competitive-intelligence for awareness; a regulatory complaint (e.g., to the FTC) is a legal-team decision, not an automatic escalation.
indicators: An influencer post promoting a competitor with no sponsorship disclosure
Evidence of a paid partnership (e.g., a leaked contract, an affiliate link revealing compensation) despite no on-post disclosure
vectors: Undisclosed influencer marketing partnerships by a competitor
rootCauses: No monitoring of competitor-favorable influencer content for disclosure-compliance gaps
controls: Competitive influencer-content monitoring for disclosure-compliance gaps
ITID-24511.detection: Detected via social-listening/competitive-monitoring tools tracking influencer content and disclosure compliance; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24511.response: Document the pattern for competitive-intelligence awareness; refer to legal for a potential regulatory complaint if the organization elects to pursue one.
metrics: Count of undisclosed-sponsorship patterns identified per quarter
ITID-24511.notes: Differentiated from sibling 24512 by the target being a legitimate competitor product rather than a counterfeit/scam offering, which materially changes the severity and response.

playbook.name: Response: Undisclosed Paid Positive Review for Competitor Product
playbook.description: An influencer has posted an undisclosed paid positive review for a competitor's product, in a way that unfavorably references or compares against this organization, violating disclosure requirements (e.g. FTC endorsement guidelines).

steps.title: Trace the sponsorship/payment relationship behind the content
steps.desc: Gather evidence that the review was paid or otherwise materially incentivized and not disclosed — check for prior sponsorship history with the competitor, affiliate links, discount codes, or direct claims/leaks of a paid arrangement.
steps.guidance: Public brand-deal databases, affiliate-link patterns, and the influencer's disclosure history on other posts are useful signals.
steps.outcome: Documented evidence of an undisclosed material connection, or a determination the content is a genuine unpaid opinion.
steps.abort: If no paid relationship can be established, treat as ordinary competitive commentary rather than an incident.

steps.title: Report the disclosure violation to the platform
steps.desc: Submit an undisclosed-paid-promotion report to the platform's advertising/branded-content policy team, citing the evidence of a material connection.

steps.title: Follow up until the content is labeled, corrected, or removed
steps.desc: Track the platform's and/or regulator's response and escalate if no action is taken within a reasonable window.
steps.outcome: Content properly disclosed, corrected, or removed.

steps.title: Monitor for a pattern of repeat undisclosed content from the same influencer
steps.desc: Watch for further undisclosed paid content from the same source targeting this organization.

steps.title: Document the case for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the sponsorship-tracing method and outcome to speed handling of similar future cases.

steps.title: Document the specific unfavorable claims made about this organization
steps.desc: Record the exact comparative or disparaging statements about this organization made in the content for evidentiary use.

steps.title: Consider a regulatory complaint where warranted
steps.desc: Where the disclosure failure is clear-cut and material, consult legal on filing a complaint with the relevant advertising-standards or consumer-protection regulator (e.g. FTC in the US).
steps.abort: If evidence is thin, a regulatory complaint may not be actionable.

ITID-24512.def: An influencer publishes an undisclosed paid positive review or endorsement of a counterfeit or scam product/service (as opposed to a legitimate competitor), directly exposing their audience to fraud while also drawing customers away from the organization.
ITID-24512.purpose: Captures an influencer posting an undisclosed paid positive review for a counterfeit or scam product trading on or competing unfairly against the organization's brand, creating direct consumer-harm risk.
scopeIncludes: An identifiable influencer post promoting a confirmed counterfeit or scam product with no sponsorship disclosure
Cases where the influencer's audience is directed to a scam storefront or counterfeit listing via the review
scopeExcludes: Undisclosed paid promotion of a legitimate competitor product (ITID-24511)
Sponsored content misrepresenting comparative test/benchmark results for a legitimate product (ITID-24513)
ITID-24512.severity: High; directly exposes consumers to fraud/counterfeit-goods harm, well beyond a simple competitive-disclosure issue.
ITID-24512.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, fraud/customer-protection, and the platform's influencer-policy enforcement team; consider a public consumer-warning if the influencer's reach is significant.
indicators: An influencer post promoting a product later confirmed to be counterfeit/scam, with no sponsorship disclosure
Audience complaints reaching the organization about a fraudulent product they discovered via an influencer post
vectors: Scam/counterfeit product operators paying influencers, often through anonymized affiliate networks, to legitimize fraudulent offerings
rootCauses: No monitoring for influencer content promoting confirmed counterfeit/scam products referencing or competing with the organization
No rapid consumer-warning protocol for influencer-driven scam exposure
controls: Influencer-content monitoring cross-referenced with known counterfeit/scam listings
Rapid consumer-warning communications protocol
ITID-24512.detection: Detected via social-listening/brand-protection tools cross-referencing influencer content against confirmed counterfeit/scam listings; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24512.response: Issue a public consumer warning where reach is significant, report the influencer to the platform's policy-enforcement and advertising-standards channels, and coordinate with fraud/customer-protection on affected-consumer support.
metrics: Count of counterfeit/scam-promoting influencer incidents identified per quarter
Time to consumer warning
ITID-24512.notes: Differentiated from sibling 24511 by the fraudulent/counterfeit nature of the promoted product, which elevates severity to direct consumer-harm rather than a purely competitive-disclosure issue.

playbook.name: Response: Undisclosed Paid Positive Review for Counterfeit/Scam Product
playbook.description: An influencer has posted an undisclosed paid positive review promoting a counterfeit or scam product that falsely bears this organization's brand, driving followers toward a fraudulent purchase.

steps.title: Confirm the promoted product is counterfeit/scam and trace the payment relationship
steps.desc: Confirm with brand-protection that the promoted product/listing is counterfeit or fraudulent, and gather evidence the influencer was paid (affiliate link, discount code, direct sponsorship) without disclosure.
steps.outcome: Documented confirmation of both the counterfeit/scam nature of the product and the undisclosed payment.
steps.abort: If the product is genuine (authorized reseller), redirect to standard marketing channels.

steps.title: Report both the counterfeit promotion and the disclosure violation to the platform
steps.desc: Submit a combined brand-infringement/counterfeit-promotion report and an undisclosed-paid-promotion report to the platform.
steps.tool: Platform brand/IP enforcement and advertising-policy reporting channels

steps.title: Confirm the content and the underlying counterfeit listing are both taken down
steps.desc: Track both response tracks and escalate if either remains unresolved beyond a reasonable window.
steps.outcome: Content removed and counterfeit listing taken down.

steps.title: Publish a customer advisory if exposure was significant
steps.desc: Where reach was significant, publish guidance for customers on identifying genuine products and reporting suspected fraud.

steps.title: Document the case for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the combination of signals (counterfeit indicators plus undisclosed sponsorship) that led to detection.

steps.title: Assess the scale of consumer exposure
steps.desc: Estimate the influencer's reach and engagement on the content to gauge how many customers may have been exposed to the fraudulent product.

steps.title: Engage legal/brand-protection on the underlying counterfeit listing
steps.desc: Pursue the counterfeit listing itself through legal/brand-protection channels in parallel with the influencer-content report.

ITID-24513.def: Sponsored influencer content presenting fabricated, cherry-picked, or methodologically-biased product test/comparison results that unfairly disadvantage the organization's product relative to the sponsoring competitor's, while the sponsorship or methodology bias is undisclosed.
ITID-24513.purpose: Captures sponsored influencer content that misrepresents product test, comparison, or benchmark results to unfairly disadvantage the organization's product against a sponsor's product.
scopeIncludes: Sponsored 'independent' product comparison/test content with fabricated or methodologically-biased results disadvantaging the organization
Undisclosed sponsorship combined with a claimed-objective testing methodology that is not actually objective
scopeExcludes: Undisclosed paid positive reviews with no comparative testing claim (ITID-24511, ITID-24512)
Genuine, methodologically-sound independent comparison content that happens to favor a competitor (not misinformation)
ITID-24513.severity: Medium-High; the veneer of 'objective testing' gives this variant more persuasive credibility and potential for lasting misinformed purchase decisions than a simple endorsement.
ITID-24513.priority: P2 given the elevated credibility and potential regulatory (advertising-standards) exposure.
ITID-24513.escalation: Escalate to legal/competitive-intelligence and consider a public technical rebuttal if the test methodology can be shown to be flawed or fabricated.
indicators: A 'test' or 'comparison' methodology that cannot be independently reproduced or verified
Test conditions or metrics conspicuously favoring the sponsor's product in ways inconsistent with real-world usage
No sponsorship disclosure despite a demonstrable financial relationship
vectors: Sponsored 'independent test' content with fabricated or biased methodology
rootCauses: No monitoring of comparative-testing content referencing the organization's product for methodology red flags
controls: Competitive comparison-content monitoring for methodology red flags
Technical rebuttal capability for flawed comparative claims
ITID-24513.detection: Detected via competitive-monitoring tools and technical/product-team methodology review; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24513.response: Have the product team assess the methodology's validity, prepare a technical rebuttal if warranted, and refer to legal for a potential advertising-standards complaint.
metrics: Count of biased-comparison-content incidents identified per quarter
ITID-24513.notes: Differentiated from siblings 24511/24512 by the comparative-testing/benchmark framing specifically, which carries more persuasive weight than a simple endorsement.

playbook.name: Response: Sponsored Content Misrepresenting Product Test/Comparison Results
playbook.description: Sponsored influencer content misrepresents the results of a product test or comparison involving this organization's product — e.g. rigged/staged testing conditions, fabricated data, or a comparison that omits material context — in a way that is materially misleading.

steps.title: Independently verify the disputed test/comparison claim
steps.desc: Have the relevant product/technical team review the claimed test methodology and results against known product performance to determine whether the comparison is factually misleading or merely an unflattering but fair test.
steps.guidance: Document the specific factual discrepancy precisely — vague objections to unfavorable-but-fair results will not support a takedown request.
steps.outcome: Documented technical determination of whether the content is materially misleading.
steps.abort: If the test appears methodologically fair even though unflattering, no incident response is warranted — this is normal competitive scrutiny.

steps.title: Report the misleading sponsored content to the platform
steps.desc: Submit a misleading-advertising/branded-content report to the platform, including the technical rebuttal evidence.

steps.title: Follow up until a correction is issued or the content is removed/labeled
steps.desc: Track the platform's and/or influencer's response and escalate if no action is taken within a reasonable window.
steps.outcome: Correction issued, or content removed/labeled misleading.

steps.title: Publish the accurate test data if the misleading claim gained traction
steps.desc: Where the misleading comparison spread meaningfully, publish accurate, independently verifiable test data through official channels.

steps.title: Document the case for faster future detection and rebuttal
steps.desc: Record the disputed claim, the technical rebuttal, and resolution for reuse against similar future claims.

steps.title: Trace the sponsorship relationship and document the misleading claims
steps.desc: Confirm the content is sponsored/paid and record the specific misrepresented claims for evidentiary use.

steps.title: Consider direct outreach requesting a correction
steps.desc: Where appropriate, have PR/communications reach out to the influencer or their agency directly with the technical rebuttal and request a correction or follow-up post.

ITID-24514.def: A suspected sponsored-misinformation influencer incident awaiting further investigation to determine its specific target/format before reclassification to the appropriate sibling ITID.
ITID-24514.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for suspected sponsored-misinformation influencer content not yet triaged to the competitor-product, counterfeit-product, or comparison-content variant.
scopeIncludes: Newly-detected undisclosed-sponsorship influencer content not yet triaged to a specific target/format
scopeExcludes: Any incident for which target/format has been confirmed and should be reclassified to ITID-24511, ITID-24512, or ITID-24513
ITID-24514.escalation: Escalate to legal/competitive-intelligence on triage duty; reclassify promptly once target/format is confirmed.
indicators: An unclassified undisclosed-sponsorship influencer post referencing the organization or its competitive landscape
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial evidence to classify target/format at time of intake
controls: Competitive influencer-content monitoring
ITID-24514.detection: Same detection surface as sibling leaves, pending target/format attribution.
ITID-24514.response: Triage promptly and reclassify to the specific sibling ITID once target/format is clear.
metrics: Count of incidents held in this bucket beyond 5 business days without reclassification
ITID-24514.notes: Intake/triage bucket only, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Sponsored Misinformation
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for sponsored influencer misinformation involving this organization that does not fit the competitor-review, counterfeit-promotion, or test-misrepresentation sub-patterns.

steps.title: Verify the disputed claim and trace the sponsorship relationship
steps.desc: Determine whether the content contains a factually false or materially misleading claim about this organization, and confirm whether it is paid/sponsored and undisclosed.
steps.outcome: Documented determination of falsity and sponsorship status.
steps.abort: If the claim is accurate or is genuine opinion, stand down.

steps.title: Report the misinformation/disclosure violation to the platform
steps.desc: Submit the appropriate report (misinformation, undisclosed promotion, or both) to the platform's relevant policy team.

steps.title: Follow up until the platform or influencer takes action
steps.desc: Track response and escalate if unresolved beyond a reasonable window.

steps.title: Publish a factual correction if warranted
steps.desc: Where the misinformation spread significantly, publish a factual correction through official channels.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record observed signatures and resolution to speed handling of future incidents in this category.

steps.title: Assess reach and platforms affected
steps.desc: Determine the influencer's reach and whether the content has spread to other platforms.

steps.title: Consider direct outreach for a correction
steps.desc: Have PR/communications reach out where appropriate to request a correction.

ITID-24521.def: An influencer purchases or otherwise fraudulently inflates follower counts, likes, views, or comments to misrepresent their genuine audience size and engagement, which misleads marketing/partnership decisions and audiences evaluating the influencer's credibility.
ITID-24521.purpose: Captures an influencer fraudulently inflating their follower or engagement metrics to appear more influential than they genuinely are, misleading the organization or others relying on those metrics.
scopeIncludes: Fraudulently purchased followers/engagement on an influencer's account discovered during due diligence for a marketing partnership
Fake-engagement inflation discovered after the fact on an existing influencer partner's content
scopeExcludes: Identity/credential fabrication about the influencer's expertise or qualifications (ITID-24522)
Undisclosed financial conflicts of interest in a specific review (ITID-24523)
ITID-24521.severity: Low-to-Medium; primarily a marketing-due-diligence and wasted-spend concern rather than a direct reputational attack, unless the organization itself paid for the inflated reach.
ITID-24521.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if the organization has an active or planned paid partnership with the influencer in question.
ITID-24521.escalation: Escalate to marketing/influencer-relations to reassess or terminate any active partnership; involve legal/finance if contractual remedies (clawback) apply.
indicators: Follower/engagement ratios statistically inconsistent with genuine audience patterns
Third-party fake-follower audit tools flagging the account
Sudden, unexplained follower spikes inconsistent with content/posting activity
vectors: Purchase of fake followers/engagement from click-farm or bot-follower services
rootCauses: No fake-follower/engagement audit step in the influencer-partnership due-diligence process
controls: Fake-follower/engagement audit as a standard influencer due-diligence step
Contractual clawback provisions for fraudulent metrics
ITID-24521.detection: Detected via third-party influencer-audit tooling analyzing follower/engagement authenticity; not a technical/network detection surface for the organization directly.
ITID-24521.response: Reassess the partnership's value and legitimacy, pursue contractual remedies if a paid engagement is affected, and update due-diligence process to catch this earlier for future partnerships.
metrics: Count of influencer-fraud audit findings per quarter
Contractual clawback recovery amount
ITID-24521.notes: Differentiated from siblings 24522/24523 by the specific fraud type (fabricated audience metrics) rather than fabricated expertise or undisclosed financial conflicts.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Follower/Engagement Purchase Fraud
playbook.description: An influencer partnered with or referencing this organization has been found to have purchased fake followers or engagement, undermining the credibility of campaigns run through them and potentially constituting marketing fraud against this organization if metrics were used to justify payment.

steps.title: Confirm the follower/engagement fraud with an audit tool
steps.desc: Run the influencer's account through follower-authenticity analysis (audience-quality tools) to quantify the proportion of fake/bot followers and engagement.
steps.outcome: Documented quantitative finding on the extent of fake followers/engagement.
steps.abort: If the account passes authenticity checks within normal tolerances, no incident response is warranted.

steps.title: Pause any active or planned campaigns with the influencer
steps.desc: Suspend current sponsorship activity with the influencer pending resolution, to avoid further exposure.

steps.title: Resolve the contractual/financial matter
steps.desc: Follow through on the agreed remedy (renegotiation, repayment, or termination) and document closure.

steps.title: Review and tighten influencer vetting for future partnerships
steps.desc: Update the partnerships/marketing vetting process to include authenticity audits before future engagements.

steps.title: Document the case to inform future influencer vetting
steps.desc: Record the detection method and outcome for reuse in vetting future influencer partnerships.

steps.title: Determine financial exposure if this organization paid based on inflated metrics
steps.desc: Check marketing/partnerships records for any payments made to this influencer that were based on follower count or engagement metrics now shown to be inflated.
steps.outcome: Financial exposure quantified, or determined not applicable.

steps.title: Engage the influencer/agency and, if warranted, legal on contract remedies
steps.desc: Raise the findings with the influencer or their agency and, where a contract with performance representations was breached, consult legal on remedies (repayment, contract termination).
steps.outcome: Contractual issue raised and remedy path determined.
