ITID-24522.def: An influencer falsely claims professional credentials, expertise, or qualifications (e.g., a fabricated medical, technical, or industry credential) they do not actually hold, to lend unearned authority to reviews or claims made about the organization's or a competitor's products.
ITID-24522.purpose: Captures an influencer fabricating credentials, expertise, or professional qualifications to lend false authority to their reviews or endorsements.
scopeIncludes: An influencer falsely claiming a professional credential or expertise relevant to the authority of their product claims
Cases where the fabricated expertise is used to make a review appear more authoritative or trustworthy than warranted
scopeExcludes: Fake follower/engagement metric inflation (ITID-24521)
Undisclosed financial conflicts of interest where the influencer's actual credentials are genuine (ITID-24523)
ITID-24522.severity: Medium-High; fabricated expertise claims can materially mislead consumers making decisions based on perceived authority (e.g., a fabricated 'certified technician' claim about product safety).
ITID-24522.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the fabricated expertise relates to safety, health, or financial claims about the organization's product.
ITID-24522.escalation: Escalate to legal and, where the fabricated credential involves a licensed profession, consider referring the matter to the relevant licensing/professional body.
indicators: An influencer's claimed credential not verifiable against any licensing/certification database
Reviews or claims framed with an authority the influencer does not actually possess
Discrepancies between the influencer's claimed background and publicly-verifiable history
vectors: Fabricated professional credentials or expertise claims used to lend authority to a review or endorsement
rootCauses: No credential-verification step in influencer-partnership due diligence
No monitoring for fabricated-expertise claims in third-party content referencing the organization's product
controls: Credential-verification step in influencer-partnership due diligence
Monitoring for fabricated-expertise claims in third-party product content
ITID-24522.detection: Detected via credential/license-database verification and background research; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24522.response: Verify the claimed credential, publicly correct the record if the claim is fabricated and materially misleading, and refer to the relevant licensing body if applicable.
metrics: Count of fabricated-credential incidents identified per quarter
ITID-24522.notes: Differentiated from sibling 24521 by the specific fraud type (fabricated expertise/credentials rather than fabricated audience size).

playbook.name: Response: Influencer Identity/Credential Fabrication (Fake Expertise Claims)
playbook.description: An influencer commenting on this organization's products/services has fabricated professional credentials or expertise claims (e.g. falsely claiming to be a licensed expert, doctor, engineer) to lend undue authority to negative or misleading claims.

steps.title: Verify the claimed credentials
steps.desc: Check the claimed credential/license/qualification against the relevant professional body or public record to confirm whether it is fabricated.
steps.outcome: Documented confirmation the credential claim is false, or that it is genuine (in which case this is not an incident).
steps.abort: If the credential is genuine, the influencer's opinion — however unfavorable — is not fraudulent and should not be treated as an incident.

steps.title: Report the credential fabrication and resulting misinformation to the platform
steps.desc: Submit a report to the platform citing both the fabricated-credential evidence and the misleading claims made under that false authority.

steps.title: Follow up until the platform takes action
steps.desc: Track the platform's response and escalate if unresolved beyond a reasonable window.

steps.title: Monitor for continued use of the fabricated credential
steps.desc: Watch for the same individual continuing to use the false credential in future content about this organization.

steps.title: Document the case for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the verification method and outcome for reuse against similar future claims.

steps.title: Document the specific claims made using the fabricated authority
steps.desc: Record the exact statements about this organization that relied on the fabricated credential for added credibility.

steps.title: Publicize the verification finding through official channels where appropriate
steps.desc: Where the fabricated-expert claim gained meaningful traction, have PR issue a factual statement noting the credential could not be verified.
steps.guidance: Word this carefully and factually — state what was and wasn't verified rather than making unproven counter-accusations.

ITID-24523.def: An influencer publishes a review or endorsement without disclosing a material financial conflict of interest beyond standard sponsorship — such as holding an equity stake in a competitor, a short position benefiting from the organization's stock decline, or a referral-fee arrangement not disclosed as such — that would reasonably affect audience trust in the review's objectivity.
ITID-24523.purpose: Captures an influencer failing to disclose a direct financial conflict of interest (beyond simple sponsorship, e.g., an equity stake or short position) affecting the credibility of a specific review.
scopeIncludes: A review where the influencer holds an undisclosed equity/financial stake in a competitor discussed favorably
A review timed to benefit an undisclosed short position or other financial interest tied to the organization's stock or market standing
scopeExcludes: Simple undisclosed paid-sponsorship arrangements without a deeper financial stake (ITID-24511, ITID-24512)
Fabricated credentials/expertise with no financial-conflict element (ITID-24522)
ITID-24523.severity: High, particularly where a publicly-traded organization is involved, given potential market-manipulation and securities-disclosure implications.
ITID-24523.priority: P1 if the conflict involves market-moving content about a publicly-traded organization; P2 otherwise.
ITID-24523.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, investor relations (if publicly traded), and compliance; potential referral to securities regulators if market-manipulation elements are present.
indicators: Discoverable financial holdings (equity, short positions) inconsistent with the influencer's claimed independence
Review timing correlating suspiciously with market events or the influencer's disclosed/discoverable trading activity
vectors: Undisclosed equity stakes, short positions, or referral-fee arrangements influencing review content
rootCauses: No monitoring for financial-conflict-of-interest red flags in high-impact influencer content about the organization
controls: Financial-conflict-of-interest monitoring for high-impact influencer content
Legal/compliance escalation protocol for securities-relevant disclosures
ITID-24523.detection: Detected via financial-disclosure research and, where publicly-traded, correlation with trading-activity and market-event timing; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24523.response: Investigate the financial-conflict evidence thoroughly, involve legal/investor-relations/compliance immediately, and consider a securities-regulator referral if warranted.
metrics: Count of undisclosed-financial-conflict incidents identified per year
sops: Legal Escalation SOP for Unfair Competition
ITID-24523.notes: Differentiated from siblings 24521/24522 by the deeper financial-conflict element (equity/short positions) rather than fake metrics or fabricated credentials; carries the highest severity in this sibling group given potential securities implications.

playbook.name: Response: Undisclosed Financial Conflict of Interest in Review
playbook.description: An influencer or reviewer with an undisclosed financial conflict of interest (e.g. an investor in, or on the payroll of, a direct competitor) has published a review or commentary about this organization without disclosing that relationship.

steps.title: Establish the undisclosed financial relationship
steps.desc: Gather public or credible evidence of the reviewer's financial interest (investment, employment, advisory role, equity) in a competitor or other party benefiting from the negative commentary.
steps.guidance: Corporate filings, LinkedIn history, and public disclosures of investment portfolios are useful sources; ensure evidence is solid before proceeding, as this claim itself is sensitive to assert publicly.
steps.outcome: Documented evidence of the undisclosed conflict, or a determination it cannot be substantiated.
steps.abort: If the relationship cannot be credibly substantiated, do not proceed with a conflict-of-interest report — pursue only the substance of any factual disputes instead.

steps.title: Report the disclosure violation to the platform
steps.desc: Submit an undisclosed-conflict-of-interest/paid-promotion report to the platform with the supporting evidence.

steps.title: Follow up until the platform requires disclosure or takes down the content
steps.desc: Track the platform's response and escalate if unresolved beyond a reasonable window.

steps.title: Monitor for continued undisclosed activity from the same reviewer
steps.desc: Watch for further undisclosed content from the same source.

steps.title: Document the case for future reference
steps.desc: Record the evidence-gathering approach and legal review outcome for reuse in similar future cases.

steps.title: Document the specific claims made and their materiality
steps.desc: Record the reviewer's claims about this organization and assess whether the undisclosed conflict is material to how a reasonable audience would weigh them.

steps.title: Consult legal before any public statement naming the conflict
steps.desc: Given the sensitivity of publicly alleging an undisclosed financial conflict, have legal review any planned public statement before release.
steps.outcome: Legal review completed before any public statement.

ITID-24524.def: A suspected influencer-fraud incident awaiting further investigation to determine its specific fraud type before reclassification to the appropriate sibling ITID.
ITID-24524.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for a suspected influencer-fraud incident not yet triaged to the fake-engagement, fabricated-credential, or financial-conflict-of-interest variant.
scopeIncludes: Newly-detected influencer-fraud indicators not yet triaged to a specific fraud type
scopeExcludes: Any incident for which the fraud type has been confirmed and should be reclassified to ITID-24521, ITID-24522, or ITID-24523
ITID-24524.escalation: Escalate to marketing/influencer-relations on triage duty; reclassify promptly once the fraud type is confirmed.
indicators: An unclassified influencer-fraud indicator during partnership due diligence or ongoing monitoring
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial evidence to classify fraud type at time of intake
controls: Influencer partnership due-diligence monitoring
ITID-24524.detection: Same detection surface as sibling leaves, pending fraud-type attribution.
ITID-24524.response: Triage promptly and reclassify to the specific sibling ITID once the fraud type is clear.
metrics: Count of incidents held in this bucket beyond 5 business days without reclassification
ITID-24524.notes: Intake/triage bucket only, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Influencer Fraud
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for influencer fraud affecting this organization that does not fit the fake-follower, fabricated-credential, or undisclosed-conflict sub-patterns.

steps.title: Establish the specific nature of the fraud
steps.desc: Gather evidence to characterize the fraudulent behavior (e.g. fabricated claims, undisclosed relationships, manipulated metrics) and confirm it is substantiated.
steps.outcome: Documented evidence of the fraud, or a determination it cannot be substantiated.
steps.abort: If the evidence does not hold up, stand down.

steps.title: Report the fraud to the relevant platform
steps.desc: Submit the appropriate policy report to the platform with supporting evidence.

steps.title: Follow up until the matter is resolved
steps.desc: Track the platform's and/or influencer's response and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Review vetting processes for future partnerships
steps.desc: Update influencer-vetting practices based on lessons from this case.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record observed signatures and resolution to speed handling of future incidents.

steps.title: Assess reach and any financial exposure to this organization
steps.desc: Determine the influencer's reach and whether this organization has any financial relationship with them affected by the fraud.

steps.title: Pause any active partnership pending resolution
steps.desc: If this organization has an active relationship with the influencer, pause it pending resolution.

ITID-24531.def: A campaign in which multiple, otherwise-unconnected influencers publish negative content about the organization using strikingly similar or identical talking points, phrases, or claims within a short window — evidence of a centrally-supplied briefing or script rather than independently-formed organic opinions.
ITID-24531.purpose: Captures multiple influencers independently publishing coordinated negative content using the same talking points, indicating a centrally-supplied attack narrative rather than organic parallel criticism.
scopeIncludes: Multiple influencers using near-identical phrasing or claims about the organization within a compressed timeframe
Evidence of a shared briefing document, script, or talking-points sheet distributed to the influencers
scopeExcludes: Timed-simultaneous posting by a single coordinated influencer network without necessarily sharing identical talking points (ITID-24532)
Independent organic criticism by multiple influencers that happens to overlap in substance without evidence of coordination
ITID-24531.severity: High; centrally-coordinated multi-influencer attacks carry outsized reach and an appearance of independent consensus that is especially damaging and hard to rebut.
ITID-24531.priority: P1 given the reach and credibility-multiplying effect of coordinated independent-seeming voices.
ITID-24531.escalation: Escalate immediately to communications/PR, legal, and executive leadership; attempt to identify and expose the common source/sponsor of the talking points as part of the response.
indicators: Near-identical or templated phrasing appearing across multiple unrelated influencer accounts within a short window
A leaked or discovered briefing document/script matching the observed talking points
vectors: A centrally-organized briefing/script distributed to multiple influencers, often via a PR firm or sponsor obscuring the ultimate source
rootCauses: No monitoring for cross-influencer talking-point similarity as a coordination signal
No rapid-response protocol for identifying and countering a centrally-sourced attack narrative
controls: Cross-influencer content-similarity monitoring for coordination signals
Rapid-response protocol for centrally-sourced attack narratives
ITID-24531.detection: Detected via social-listening tools performing cross-account content-similarity analysis; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24531.response: Document the talking-point overlap as evidence of coordination, issue a fact-based public rebuttal, and investigate/expose the common source if identifiable.
metrics: Count of confirmed coordinated multi-influencer campaigns identified per year
Time to public rebuttal
ITID-24531.notes: Differentiated from sibling 24532 by the defining evidence being shared talking points/content rather than merely coordinated timing.

playbook.name: Response: Multi-Influencer Coordinated Negative Campaign (Same Talking Points)
playbook.description: Multiple, seemingly independent influencers have posted near-identical negative talking points about this organization within a short window, indicating a coordinated attack rather than organic, independent criticism.

steps.title: Correlate the multiple influencer accounts to establish coordination
steps.desc: Compare the wording, imagery, timing, and hashtags used across the flagged influencer posts to establish that the talking points are shared/scripted rather than independently arrived at, and check for a common source (brief, briefing document, shared handler/agency).
steps.guidance: This correlation evidence is the core of the platform report — without it, each post looks like ordinary (if unfavorable) independent commentary.
steps.outcome: Documented evidence of coordination across the accounts, or a determination the similarity is coincidental/organic.
steps.abort: If no coordination can be established, treat each post as independent commentary and respond (if at all) through normal PR channels rather than as a security incident.

steps.title: Report the coordinated inauthentic campaign to each platform
steps.desc: Submit a coordinated-inauthentic-behavior report to each affected platform's trust-and-safety team, including the cross-account correlation evidence.

steps.title: Follow up until platforms take enforcement action
steps.desc: Track each platform's response and escalate if content isn't labeled or removed within a reasonable window.

steps.title: Publish the factual rebuttal if the campaign gained meaningful traction
steps.desc: Release the prepared factual correction through official channels if warranted by reach.

steps.title: Document the coordination signature for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the correlation method and findings to speed detection of future coordinated influencer campaigns.

steps.title: Document the specific false or misleading claims being repeated
steps.desc: Record the exact shared talking points and assess which, if any, are factually false versus merely unfavorable opinion.

steps.title: Prepare a factual rebuttal for any false claims
steps.desc: Have PR/communications prepare a factual rebuttal document addressing the false claims, for use regardless of platform action.

steps.title: Attempt to identify the common source or coordinator
steps.desc: Investigate whether the campaign traces to a competitor, PR/opposition-research firm, or other identifiable coordinator.
steps.outcome: Likely source identified where possible, or noted as unattributed.

ITID-24532.def: A campaign in which a coordinated network of influencers is directed to publish negative content about the organization at deliberately synchronized times (rather than sharing identical talking points), designed to maximize algorithmic trending/visibility through simultaneous posting volume.
ITID-24532.purpose: Captures a network of influencers posting negative content about the organization at deliberately synchronized times, maximizing algorithmic visibility even when talking points are not identical.
scopeIncludes: Multiple influencers posting negative content within a tightly synchronized time window as the primary coordination evidence
Cases where posting-time synchronization, not content similarity, is the defining coordination signal
scopeExcludes: Multi-influencer campaigns defined by shared talking points regardless of timing (ITID-24531)
A single influencer's content being cross-platform amplified (ITID-24533)
ITID-24532.severity: High; synchronized posting is specifically designed to trigger platform trending algorithms, amplifying reach beyond what the individual influencers' audiences alone would achieve.
ITID-24532.priority: P1 given the amplification effect of trending-algorithm exploitation.
ITID-24532.escalation: Escalate immediately to communications/PR and legal; alert the platform's trust-and-safety team to the synchronized-posting pattern as evidence of inauthentic coordination.
indicators: Multiple influencer posts about the organization published within an implausibly narrow time window
A resulting trending/algorithmic-visibility spike disproportionate to the influencers' combined organic reach
vectors: Centrally-organized scheduling of influencer posting times to exploit trending algorithms
rootCauses: No monitoring for cross-influencer posting-time synchronization as a coordination signal
No escalation relationship with platforms for reporting inauthentic-coordination patterns
controls: Cross-influencer posting-time synchronization monitoring
Escalation relationship with platforms for inauthentic-coordination reporting
ITID-24532.detection: Detected via social-listening tools analyzing posting-time clustering across accounts; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24532.response: Document the timing-synchronization evidence, report the inauthentic-coordination pattern to the platform, and issue a public rebuttal addressing the substance of the claims.
metrics: Count of confirmed synchronized-posting campaigns identified per year
ITID-24532.notes: Differentiated from sibling 24531 by the coordination evidence being posting-time synchronization rather than shared talking points.

playbook.name: Response: Influencer Network Timed Simultaneous Posting Campaign
playbook.description: A network of influencers has posted negative content about this organization within an implausibly tight time window, indicating deliberate, synchronized timing rather than independent, organic reaction.

steps.title: Correlate posting timestamps across the network to establish synchronization
steps.desc: Compile precise posting timestamps across the flagged accounts and assess whether the clustering is statistically implausible for independent, organic posting.
steps.outcome: Documented evidence of synchronized timing, or a determination the clustering is explainable (e.g. reaction to a shared genuine news event).
steps.abort: If the timing is explainable by a genuine shared trigger event, treat as organic reaction rather than a coordinated attack.

steps.title: Report the coordinated campaign to each affected platform
steps.desc: Submit a coordinated-inauthentic-behavior report with the timing-correlation evidence to each platform's trust-and-safety team.

steps.title: Follow up until platforms take enforcement action
steps.desc: Track each platform's response and escalate if unresolved beyond a reasonable window.

steps.title: Publish the rebuttal if warranted and monitor for a repeat synchronized wave
steps.desc: Release the prepared correction if reach was significant, and watch for the network repeating the tactic.
steps.outcome: Correction published where warranted; no renewed wave, or caught early.

steps.title: Document the network's timing signature for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the timing-correlation method and the network's fingerprint for reuse against future campaigns.

steps.title: Document the shared content/claims and identify the network's scope
steps.desc: Catalog every account involved and the specific claims made, and check for prior instances of this same network acting in concert.

steps.title: Prepare a factual rebuttal for any false claims
steps.desc: Have PR/communications prepare a rebuttal addressing false claims, ready for release independent of platform action.

ITID-24533.def: A campaign in which a single originating influencer's negative content about the organization is deliberately re-posted, translated, clipped, or re-shared across multiple additional platforms by a coordinated network of secondary accounts, extending the narrative's reach well beyond the original influencer's own audience.
ITID-24533.purpose: Captures a single influencer's negative content about the organization being deliberately re-amplified across multiple platforms by a coordinated support network, extending its reach beyond its original audience.
scopeIncludes: A single original piece of negative influencer content being systematically re-distributed across multiple platforms by a coordinated secondary-account network
Clipped/translated/re-edited versions of the original content circulating in coordination
scopeExcludes: Multiple independent influencers originating content with shared talking points (ITID-24531)
Multiple independent influencers posting original content at synchronized times (ITID-24532)
ITID-24533.severity: High; cross-platform amplification can expose the negative narrative to audiences the original influencer would never have reached organically.
ITID-24533.priority: P1 given the multiplied reach across platform audiences.
ITID-24533.escalation: Escalate immediately to communications/PR for a cross-platform coordinated response; report the secondary amplification network to each platform where it is active.
indicators: A single original content piece being re-posted/clipped/translated across many platforms in a coordinated pattern
Secondary amplifier accounts with infrastructure or timing patterns indicating coordination rather than organic re-sharing
vectors: A coordinated secondary-account network systematically re-distributing a single piece of originating content across platforms
rootCauses: No cross-platform social-listening coverage tracking a single narrative's spread across platform boundaries
No coordinated cross-platform communications response capability
controls: Cross-platform social-listening tracking narrative spread across platform boundaries
Coordinated cross-platform communications response capability
ITID-24533.detection: Detected via cross-platform social-listening tools tracking content re-circulation and secondary-account coordination patterns; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24533.response: Track the narrative's spread across all affected platforms, issue a consistent cross-platform response, and report the secondary amplification network where its coordination can be demonstrated.
metrics: Number of platforms reached by the amplified narrative
Time to coordinated cross-platform response
ITID-24533.notes: Differentiated from siblings 24531/24532 by the single-origin-content, multi-platform-amplification mechanism, as opposed to multiple influencers originating their own content.

playbook.name: Response: Cross-Platform Influencer Amplification of Single Attack Narrative
playbook.description: A single false or misleading attack narrative about this organization is being deliberately amplified by multiple influencers across different platforms (e.g. the same claim relayed from video to short-form to blog), extending reach beyond what any single post would achieve.

steps.title: Trace the narrative's origin and cross-platform amplification path
steps.desc: Identify the original source of the narrative and map how it has been relayed and amplified by influencers across each platform, establishing this is a deliberate amplification effort rather than independent organic pickup.
steps.outcome: Documented amplification map and origin point, or a determination the spread is organic.
steps.abort: If the spread appears to be genuine organic interest in a real news story, respond through normal PR channels rather than as a coordinated-attack incident.

steps.title: Report the amplification campaign to each affected platform
steps.desc: Submit coordinated-inauthentic-behavior or misinformation reports to each platform involved, referencing the cross-platform amplification evidence.
steps.outcome: Report(s) submitted to all affected platforms.

steps.title: Follow up on each platform until enforcement action is taken
steps.desc: Track responses from every affected platform and escalate as needed.
steps.outcome: Content labeled inauthentic or removed across affected platforms.

steps.title: Publish the unified rebuttal and monitor for a second amplification wave
steps.desc: Release the prepared rebuttal across channels and watch for the narrative resurfacing.
steps.outcome: Rebuttal published; no renewed wave, or caught early.

steps.title: Document the amplification pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the amplification map and detection method to speed handling of future cross-platform campaigns.

steps.title: Fact-check the narrative and document the specific false claims
steps.desc: Determine which elements of the narrative are factually false versus accurate but unfavorable.

steps.title: Prepare and coordinate a unified factual rebuttal across all affected platforms
steps.desc: Given the narrative's cross-platform reach, prepare a single factual rebuttal that communications can publish consistently across every affected channel.
steps.outcome: Unified rebuttal prepared for multi-channel release.

ITID-24534.def: A suspected coordinated-influencer-attack incident awaiting further investigation to determine its specific coordination mechanism before reclassification to the appropriate sibling ITID.
ITID-24534.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for a suspected coordinated-influencer-attack incident not yet triaged to the shared-talking-points, synchronized-timing, or cross-platform-amplification mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Newly-detected multi-influencer negative-content patterns not yet triaged to a specific coordination mechanism
scopeExcludes: Any incident for which the mechanism has been confirmed and should be reclassified to ITID-24531, ITID-24532, or ITID-24533
ITID-24534.severity: Medium-High pending triage given the general severity profile of this sibling group.
ITID-24534.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR on triage duty; reclassify promptly once the coordination mechanism is confirmed.
indicators: An unclassified multi-influencer negative-content pattern without yet-established coordination-mechanism attribution
vectors: Unknown pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial evidence to attribute coordination mechanism at time of intake
controls: Cross-influencer content and timing-pattern monitoring
ITID-24534.detection: Same detection surface as sibling leaves, pending mechanism attribution.
ITID-24534.response: Triage promptly and reclassify to the specific sibling ITID once the coordination mechanism is clear.
metrics: Count of incidents held in this bucket beyond 5 business days without reclassification
ITID-24534.notes: Intake/triage bucket only, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Coordinated Influencer Attack
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for a coordinated influencer attack against this organization that does not fit the shared-talking-points, synchronized-timing, or cross-platform-amplification sub-patterns.

steps.title: Correlate the involved accounts to establish coordination
steps.desc: Gather whatever evidence is available (shared content, timing, cross-platform spread, common source) to establish coordination among the influencer accounts involved.
steps.outcome: Documented evidence of coordination, or a determination the activity is independent/organic.
steps.abort: If coordination cannot be established, respond (if at all) through normal PR channels.

steps.title: Report the coordinated campaign to each affected platform
steps.desc: Submit coordinated-inauthentic-behavior reports with supporting evidence to each platform involved.

steps.title: Follow up until platforms take enforcement action
steps.desc: Track responses and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Publish the rebuttal if warranted and monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Release the correction if reach was significant, and watch for a repeat campaign.
steps.outcome: Correction published where warranted; no recurrence, or caught early.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the coordination signature and resolution for reuse against future campaigns.

steps.title: Document the claims made and fact-check them
steps.desc: Catalog the claims made across the campaign and determine which are factually false.

steps.title: Prepare a factual rebuttal
steps.desc: Have PR/communications prepare a rebuttal addressing false claims.

ITID-24611.def: A coordinated campaign in which multiple actors publish their own negative blog posts about the company within a compressed timeframe or with shared fabricated talking points, intended to simulate a groundswell of independent criticism.
ITID-24611.purpose: Captures organized publication of independent, negative blog posts across multiple blogs/sites aimed at damaging the company's reputation.
scopeIncludes: Multiple unaffiliated-looking blogs publishing near-identical negative claims about the company within a short window
Evidence of shared talking points, templates, or coordination (e.g. a leaked brief) behind ostensibly independent bloggers
Cross-linking between the negative posts to boost search visibility
scopeExcludes: A single blog's genuine, unsolicited negative opinion piece (not an incident)
Flooding the comment sections of third-party blogs rather than publishing original posts (ITID-24612)
Paid/sponsored placements arranged to appear independent (ITID-24613)
ITID-24611.severity: Low-to-Medium; escalates to Medium-High if the campaign gains significant search/social traction.
ITID-24611.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if the coordinated posts begin ranking prominently for brand-name search terms.
ITID-24611.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR and SEO teams; escalate to legal if any post contains verifiably false, defamatory factual claims.
indicators: Multiple low-authority blogs publishing similar negative content about the company within days of each other
Near-identical phrasing or structure across posts from different authors
Coordinated social sharing amplifying the posts simultaneously
vectors: Third-party blog publishing platforms (WordPress, Medium, Blogger)
Paid click farms or partisan blog networks distributing a shared narrative
rootCauses: No proactive brand/search monitoring for coordinated negative content
No established rapid factual-rebuttal process for blog-based claims
controls: Brand and search-result monitoring (social listening)
SEO monitoring for coordinated negative-content ranking spikes
Pre-established crisis communications playbook
ITID-24611.detection: Relies on social-listening and SEO-monitoring tools; no technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24611.response: Verify factual accuracy of the claims, issue a factual correction through official channels, and pursue platform reporting or legal options for demonstrably false and defamatory content.
metrics: Count of coordinated blog-campaign incidents per quarter
Time from detection to public correction
Search-ranking impact of the negative content
ITID-24611.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is content-based reputational manipulation, not a network-intrusion technique. Differentiated from sibling leaves by scope: original, independently-published blog posts (vs. comment flooding or paid placements).

playbook.name: Response: Coordinated Negative Blog Post Campaign
playbook.description: A coordinated set of negative blog posts about this organization has been published across multiple blogs/sites within a short window, indicating an orchestrated campaign rather than independent commentary.

steps.title: Correlate the posts to establish coordination
steps.desc: Compare the posts for shared language, structure, publication timing, and authorship/hosting patterns to establish coordination rather than independent commentary.
steps.outcome: Documented evidence of coordination, or a determination the posts are independent.
steps.abort: If independent, respond (if at all) through normal PR/content channels rather than as a coordinated-attack incident.

steps.title: Report false/defamatory posts to the hosting platforms
steps.desc: Where posts are hosted on a blogging platform (rather than a self-hosted site), submit a content-policy or defamation report to the platform.

steps.title: Follow up until posts are corrected or removed
steps.desc: Track responses from platforms, site owners, and hosting providers, escalating as needed.

steps.title: Publish a factual correction if the campaign gained meaningful reach
steps.desc: Release a factual rebuttal through official channels where warranted.

steps.title: Document the campaign pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the coordination signature and resolution for reuse against future campaigns.

steps.title: Fact-check the claims made across the posts
steps.desc: Determine which claims are factually false versus unfavorable opinion.

steps.title: Engage legal for self-hosted sites carrying false, defamatory claims
steps.desc: For posts on independently hosted sites outside platform reporting reach, have legal send a cease-and-desist or pursue a hosting-provider abuse complaint where claims are false and defamatory.

ITID-24612.def: A coordinated effort to fill the comment sections of third-party blogs (relevant to the company's industry, products, or news coverage) with fabricated negative claims, designed to shape reader perception at the point of consumption.
ITID-24612.purpose: Captures coordinated flooding of blog comment sections with fabricated negative claims about the company, distinct from publishing original posts.
scopeIncludes: Coordinated posting of near-identical negative comments across multiple unrelated blogs
Use of multiple accounts/personas to simulate independent grassroots criticism in comment threads
Comment content containing fabricated factual claims about the company

New or low-history commenting accounts driving the volume
Comment content matching a shared script or talking-point set

Coordinated volunteer or paid commenter networks
rootCauses: No brand monitoring covering third-party blog comment sections
No established relationship with blog platforms/moderators for abuse reporting
controls: Brand/comment monitoring across key industry blogs
Platform abuse-reporting relationships
Pre-established crisis communications playbook
ITID-24612.detection: Relies on manual or tool-assisted monitoring of third-party comment sections; not a technical/network detection surface.

playbook.name: Response: Blog Comment Section Flooding with Negative Content
playbook.description: A coordinated group or bot network is flooding blog comment sections (on this organization's own blog or third-party coverage of it) with negative, often repetitive or off-topic, content.

steps.title: Confirm the comments show signs of coordinated/inauthentic flooding
steps.desc: Analyze the flagged comments for shared language, posting-time clustering, and commenter-account patterns indicating coordination rather than genuine independent reader reaction.
steps.outcome: Documented evidence of coordinated flooding, or a determination the comments reflect genuine reader sentiment.
steps.abort: If comments reflect genuine sentiment (even if critical), treat as legitimate feedback rather than an attack.

steps.title: Moderate/remove the flooding comments on owned properties
steps.desc: If on this organization's own blog, apply comment moderation (removal, rate-limiting, CAPTCHA) directly.
steps.outcome: Flooding comments removed on owned properties.

steps.title: Confirm the flooding has stopped and comments are cleaned up
steps.desc: Verify removal on owned properties and follow up with third parties as needed.
steps.outcome: Flooding comments removed across affected properties.

steps.title: Consider stronger comment controls if flooding recurs
steps.desc: If the flooding is recurring, implement stronger moderation controls (registration requirements, rate limits) on owned properties.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the flooding signature and resolution for reuse against future incidents.

steps.title: Determine whether this organization's own blog or third-party coverage is affected
steps.desc: Establish which is affected, since the containment path differs — this organization controls moderation on its own blog but must request action from a third party otherwise.

steps.title: Request moderation action from third-party site owners where applicable
steps.desc: For third-party coverage, contact the site's moderation team with evidence of the coordinated flooding and request action.

ITID-24613.def: An attacker arranges for negative or misleading content about the company to be published on a legitimate blog through a guest-post submission or paid sponsored-content placement, exploiting the host blog's credibility while concealing the placement's true source or intent.
ITID-24613.purpose: Captures negative content placed on legitimate, higher-authority blogs via guest-post or sponsored-content channels while appearing to be independent editorial content.
scopeIncludes: Submitting a guest post under a false or misleading byline that contains fabricated negative claims
Paying for sponsored content designed to look like independent editorial criticism
Concealing sponsorship/compensation disclosure to make the piece appear organic
scopeExcludes: Organic, unsolicited negative posts from independent bloggers (ITID-24611)
Legitimate, properly disclosed sponsored content that is merely unfavorable but factually accurate
ITID-24613.severity: Medium; the borrowed credibility of a legitimate host blog increases believability and reach.
ITID-24613.priority: P2, given the reputational leverage a credible host site provides to fabricated claims.
ITID-24613.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR and legal immediately; contact the host blog's editorial team to request correction, disclosure, or takedown.
indicators: A guest/sponsored post with fabricated or unverifiable claims appearing on an otherwise reputable blog
Byline or sponsorship disclosure inconsistent with the actual author/funder
Host blog unaware of the true source or intent behind the submission
vectors: Guest-post submission programs on industry blogs
Native/sponsored content marketplaces with weak vetting
rootCauses: Host blogs with weak editorial vetting of guest contributors
No monitoring of sponsored-content networks for brand mentions
controls: Brand monitoring across sponsored-content and guest-post networks
Direct relationships with key industry publications for rapid correction requests
Pre-established crisis communications playbook
ITID-24613.detection: Relies on brand/content monitoring; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24613.response: Contact the host publication with evidence of the fabrication, request correction or takedown and proper sponsorship disclosure, and issue a public correction if the piece has gained traction.
metrics: Count of fake guest-post/sponsored placement incidents per quarter
Time to host-publication takedown or correction
ITID-24613.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies. Differentiated from ITID-24611 by the mechanism: content is placed through a legitimate blog's own guest/sponsored channel rather than published independently.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Guest Post/Sponsored Blog Negative Placement

steps.outcome: Documented findings on the article's true origin and disclosure status.
steps.abort: If the article is a genuine independent guest contribution, respond (if at all) through normal PR channels.

steps.title: Contact the publishing site with the disclosure/factual findings
steps.desc: Reach out to the blog's editorial or advertising team with evidence of the undisclosed sponsorship and/or factual inaccuracies, requesting correction, disclosure, or removal.

steps.title: Follow up until the site corrects, discloses, or removes the article
steps.desc: Track the site's response and escalate (hosting provider, legal) if it does not cooperate.

steps.title: Publish a factual correction if the article gained meaningful reach
steps.desc: Release a rebuttal through official channels where warranted.

steps.title: Document the case for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the tracing method and outcome for reuse against similar future placements.

steps.title: Fact-check the article's claims

Cross-promotion between the videos to boost algorithmic reach
scopeExcludes: A single creator's genuine, unsolicited negative review (not an incident)

ITID-24622.purpose: Captures a single, highly-produced video styled as investigative journalism that presents fabricated or distorted claims about the company as a credible exposé.
scopeIncludes: A single video using investigative-journalism production techniques to present unverified or fabricated claims as fact
Use of fabricated or misrepresented 'evidence' (documents, anonymous testimony, doctored screenshots) within the video
The video being positioned/marketed as an independent exposé rather than opinion commentary
scopeExcludes: Coordinated campaigns of multiple ordinary negative review videos (ITID-24621)
Genuine investigative journalism by an established, accountable news outlet, even if unfavorable
Manipulated photo/video specifically fabricating an association with a controversial figure (ITID-24732)
ITID-24622.severity: Medium-High; the exposé framing is designed to maximize perceived credibility and viral spread.
ITID-24622.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the video gains mainstream media pickup or viral distribution.
ITID-24622.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR and legal immediately to assess defamation exposure and platform takedown options.

Use of anonymous or uncredited 'sources' and unverifiable documents as evidence
Rapid viral spread disproportionate to the channel's normal audience size
vectors: Video platforms with algorithmic amplification (YouTube, TikTok)
Cross-posting to social media to accelerate virality

Absence of a rapid-response fact-check and correction process
controls: Video-platform brand/social-listening monitoring
Legal review process for defamation assessment
Platform takedown-request relationships
Pre-established crisis communications playbook
ITID-24622.detection: Relies on social-listening and media-monitoring tools; not a technical/network detection surface.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Exposé/Investigation-Style Attack Video
playbook.description: A video styled as an independent investigative exposé makes serious, misleading, or fabricated claims about this organization, borrowing the credibility of investigative journalism without its rigor.

steps.title: Fact-check every substantive claim in the video against verifiable evidence
steps.desc: Have the relevant subject-matter teams (legal, product, HR, finance as applicable) review each claim made in the video against internal records and public facts to determine what is false, misleading, or missing context.
steps.guidance: Serious exposé-style claims often mix a kernel of truth with exaggeration or fabrication — document precisely which parts are false versus merely unflattering.
steps.abort: If the video's core claims hold up as substantially accurate, this is a legitimate criticism to be addressed on the merits, not a security incident.

steps.title: Report factually false claims to the platform

steps.title: Follow up until the platform or creator takes corrective action

steps.title: Publish the fact-check rebuttal through official channels
steps.desc: Release the claim-by-claim rebuttal publicly given the seriousness of the original claims, regardless of platform action.

steps.title: Document the case for faster future detection and legal reference
steps.desc: Record the fact-check process, legal assessment, and outcome for reuse in similar future cases.

steps.title: Assess the video's reach and source credibility
steps.desc: Determine the channel's size, history, and any indication of who commissioned or is behind the video.

steps.title: Consult legal on defamation exposure and response options
steps.desc: Given the serious nature of exposé-style claims, have legal assess defamation exposure and whether a cease-and-desist or correction demand is warranted before any public response.
steps.outcome: Legal guidance obtained before public response.

Comment content matching a shared script or talking-point set
vectors: Video-platform comment systems
Coordinated bot or paid-commenter networks
rootCauses: No monitoring of comment sentiment on high-visibility brand-relevant videos

ITID-24631.def: A coordinated campaign in which multiple actors post negative threads or replies about the company across general-purpose discussion forums, using shared talking points to simulate broad organic criticism.

ITID-24632.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR; report the sockpuppet network to forum moderators/trust and safety for platform-policy enforcement.
indicators: Multiple accounts with correlated registration dates, writing style, or posting cadence reinforcing the same narrative
Accounts with minimal posting history outside the target thread
Rapid, mutually-reinforcing replies within the same thread from newly active accounts
vectors: Forum account creation at scale
Coordinated manual or semi-automated posting from a shared actor group
rootCauses: No monitoring for sockpuppet behavioral patterns on brand-relevant threads
No established relationship with forum trust and safety teams
controls: Forum sentiment/behavioral-pattern monitoring
Platform abuse-reporting relationships for coordinated inauthentic behavior
Pre-established crisis communications playbook
ITID-24632.detection: Relies on behavioral-pattern analysis of forum accounts; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24632.response: Document the behavioral evidence of coordination, report the sockpuppet network to platform moderators, and issue a factual correction where the manufactured consensus has gained visible traction.
metrics: Count of confirmed sockpuppet pile-on incidents per quarter
Number of accounts identified as part of the same network
ITID-24632.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies. Differentiated from ITID-24631 by the mechanism: a single actor/small group operating multiple fake accounts within one thread, rather than genuinely distributed multi-actor coordination across forums.

playbook.name: Response: Sockpuppet-Driven Forum Pile-On Campaign
playbook.description: A single actor or small group operating multiple sockpuppet accounts is creating the appearance of a large, organic pile-on against this organization within a forum.

steps.title: Establish evidence of sockpuppetry
steps.desc: Analyze account-creation dates, writing style/voice similarity, posting-time overlap, and any technical signals (where available, e.g. shared IP flags from forum admins) across the piling-on accounts to establish they are operated by the same actor(s).
steps.guidance: Forum administrators typically hold technical evidence (IP/device data) that this organization cannot access directly — request their assistance rather than trying to prove sockpuppetry purely from public behavior.
steps.outcome: Documented evidence of sockpuppetry, or a determination the accounts are independent.
steps.abort: If accounts appear independent, treat as a genuine (if negative) pile-on and respond through normal channels rather than as an inauthenticity incident.

steps.title: Report the sockpuppet network to forum administrators
steps.desc: Submit a sockpuppetry/ban-evasion report to the forum's administrators with the behavioral evidence, requesting they check technical signals available to them.

steps.title: Follow up until administrators take action against the sockpuppet accounts
steps.desc: Track the forum's response and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Monitor for the same actor creating new accounts
steps.desc: Watch for the pattern recurring under new account identities.
steps.outcome: No renewed activity, or caught early.

steps.title: Document the sockpuppet signature for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the behavioral fingerprint observed to speed detection of this actor's future activity.

steps.title: Document the claims made and their spread across the pile-on
steps.desc: Catalog the claims repeated across the sockpuppet accounts for evidentiary use.

steps.title: Prepare a factual rebuttal for the underlying claims
steps.desc: Have PR/communications prepare a rebuttal addressing any false claims, independent of the sockpuppetry finding.

ITID-24633.def: A campaign that specifically targets a niche online community, subreddit, or specialized forum whose membership overlaps heavily with the company's actual customers or industry stakeholders, exploiting the community's credibility and influence within that specific audience.
ITID-24633.purpose: Captures targeted negative campaigns directed at a specific niche online community or subreddit closely tied to the company's industry or customer base.
scopeIncludes: Negative content deliberately seeded into a niche community whose membership significantly overlaps with the company's customer base or industry peers
Exploitation of the niche community's internal credibility/trust dynamics to lend the content outsized weight
Targeting selected specifically because of its influence over a defined customer or stakeholder segment
scopeExcludes: Broad, undifferentiated posting across general-purpose forums (ITID-24631)
Sockpuppet pile-ons where the defining feature is fake-account use rather than community targeting (ITID-24632)
ITID-24633.severity: Medium; the concentrated, trusted audience of a niche community can produce outsized influence on purchasing or stakeholder decisions.
ITID-24633.priority: P2, given the direct overlap with the company's actual customer or stakeholder base.
ITID-24633.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR and the relevant business unit (e.g. customer success, industry relations) given the direct audience overlap.
indicators: Negative content appearing specifically within a community known to overlap with the company's customer/industry base
Community members flagging the content as inconsistent with known facts
Disproportionate campaign focus on this single community versus broader forums
vectors: Niche subreddits, specialized industry forums, professional community platforms
rootCauses: No monitoring of niche communities directly relevant to the customer base
No established relationships or presence within key industry communities to enable rapid rebuttal
controls: Monitoring of identified high-relevance niche communities
Established company presence/relationships within key industry communities
Pre-established crisis communications playbook
ITID-24633.detection: Relies on targeted community monitoring; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24633.response: Engage directly and transparently within the community with factual corrections, leveraging any established company presence, and coordinate with community moderators where content violates rules.
metrics: Count of niche-community targeted incidents per quarter
Estimated customer/stakeholder overlap reached
ITID-24633.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies. Differentiated from sibling leaves by the targeting axis: a specific niche community with direct customer/industry overlap, rather than general forums (ITID-24631) or the sockpuppet mechanism (ITID-24632).

playbook.name: Response: Niche Community/Subreddit Targeted Attack Campaign
playbook.description: A targeted attack campaign against this organization is being run within a specific niche online community or subreddit whose culture and moderation norms differ from mainstream platforms, requiring a community-appropriate response.

steps.title: Understand the community's norms and confirm the activity is an orchestrated attack
steps.desc: Research the specific community's culture, moderation policies, and typical discourse norms, then assess whether the flagged activity is coordinated/inauthentic or reflects genuine community sentiment (which may look different from mainstream platform norms).
steps.guidance: Niche communities often have norms (heavy sarcasm, brigading rules, specific vernacular) that can look like an attack to an outsider but are ordinary discourse — get this read right before acting.
steps.outcome: Documented determination of whether this is a genuine orchestrated attack, with community context factored in.
steps.abort: If the activity reflects genuine community sentiment or norms, do not treat it as an attack — engaging as though it were can backfire badly in a niche community.

steps.title: Engage the community's moderators through appropriate channels
steps.desc: Contact the subreddit/community's moderator team, respecting their specific reporting process and norms, with evidence of coordination and any rule violations.

steps.title: Follow up until moderators take action on rule-violating content
steps.desc: Track the moderator team's response and escalate through the platform (e.g. Reddit admin reporting) if community moderation is insufficient.

steps.title: Monitor the community for recurrence
steps.desc: Watch for renewed activity within the same or related communities.
steps.outcome: No renewed campaign, or caught early.

steps.title: Document the community context and pattern for faster future handling
steps.desc: Record the community's norms and the campaign's signature to inform faster, better-calibrated future responses in this or similar communities.

steps.title: Document the specific claims and their spread within the community
steps.desc: Catalog the claims made and how far they have spread within and beyond the community.

steps.title: Decide whether a direct organizational response within the community is appropriate
steps.desc: Given the community's culture, decide whether an official, transparent response posted within the community would help or backfire, in consultation with PR/community management.

ITID-24634.def: A catch-all classification for coordinated forum-based activity targeting the company's reputation that does not match a more specific sibling ITID under Forum-based Attacks, pending clearer categorization or reclassification.
ITID-24634.purpose: Intake bucket for forum-based reputation attacks that do not clearly fit the defined sibling leaves.
scopeIncludes: Forum-based reputation attacks with a novel or mixed mechanism not covered by the sibling leaves
Ambiguous cases pending investigation to determine the correct specific classification
scopeExcludes: Any activity clearly matching Coordinated Negative Thread/Post Campaign (ITID-24631), Sockpuppet Pile-On (ITID-24632), or Niche Community Targeted Attack (ITID-24633) — reclassify once determined
ITID-24634.severity: Assess case-by-case; default to Low-to-Medium pending clarification.
ITID-24634.priority: P3 by default; re-prioritize once the specific mechanism is identified and reclassified.
ITID-24634.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR for triage; reclassify to a specific sibling ITID as soon as the mechanism is clear.
indicators: Forum-based reputation activity that does not cleanly match an existing sibling pattern
vectors: Varies; any forum-based reputation attack mechanism not yet catalogued
rootCauses: Novel or hybrid attack technique not yet reflected in the taxonomy
Insufficient information at time of triage to classify precisely
controls: Forum/social-listening brand monitoring
Triage process to reclassify into a specific sibling ITID
ITID-24634.detection: Relies on the same social-listening/brand-monitoring tooling as sibling leaves.
ITID-24634.response: Investigate to determine the specific mechanism, reclassify under the appropriate sibling ITID, and follow that leaf's response guidance.
metrics: Count of unclassified forum incidents pending reclassification
Average time to reclassification
ITID-24634.notes: This is the standard 'Unclassified / General' catch-all leaf for the Forum-based Attacks group, following the taxonomy's established intake-bucket pattern.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Forum-Based Attack
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for a forum-based attack campaign against this organization that does not fit the coordinated-thread, sockpuppet, or niche-community sub-patterns.

steps.title: Confirm the activity is coordinated or otherwise inauthentic
steps.desc: Gather evidence establishing that the forum activity is orchestrated or inauthentic rather than genuine independent commentary.
steps.outcome: Documented evidence of coordination/inauthenticity, or a determination it is organic.
steps.abort: If organic, respond through normal PR/support channels.

steps.title: Report to forum moderators/administrators
steps.desc: Submit a report with supporting evidence to the forum's moderation team.

steps.title: Follow up until moderators take action
steps.desc: Track responses and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Watch for the campaign resuming.
steps.outcome: No renewed campaign, or caught early.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record observed signatures for reuse against future incidents.

steps.title: Fact-check the claims and document scope
steps.desc: Catalog affected threads and determine which claims are factually false.

steps.title: Prepare a factual rebuttal
steps.desc: Have PR/communications prepare a rebuttal addressing false claims.

ITID-24711.def: An actor creates content (a review, statement, or social post) falsely attributed to a real, named journalist or critic who did not write it, exploiting that individual's established public credibility to lend false authority to negative claims about the company.
ITID-24711.purpose: Captures impersonation of a specific, identifiable journalist or critic to post a fake review or statement attributed to that real person.
scopeIncludes: Content falsely attributed to a specific, named, identifiable journalist or critic
Fake social media accounts or fabricated statements impersonating a real media figure
Use of the impersonated figure's known reputation/beat to lend credibility to the fabricated content
scopeExcludes: Impersonation of an anonymous/pseudonymous verified platform reviewer account without a real-world public identity (ITID-24712)
Fabricated reviews attributed to an actual real customer rather than a public media figure (ITID-24713)
ITID-24711.severity: Medium-High; borrowed credibility from a recognized journalist/critic significantly increases believability.
ITID-24711.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the impersonated figure has a large following or the content gains rapid traction.
ITID-24711.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR and legal immediately; notify the impersonated individual/their outlet, and pursue platform takedown for the impersonating account/content.
indicators: A review or statement attributed to a named journalist/critic that they did not actually publish
The named individual publicly denying authorship
A fake account impersonating the individual's name/likeness on a review or social platform
vectors: Fake social media accounts impersonating public figures
Fabricated screenshots or quotes attributed to a real journalist/critic
rootCauses: No monitoring for impersonation of key media figures relevant to the company's coverage
No established rapid-verification relationship with the outlets/individuals typically covering the company
controls: Impersonation/brand monitoring covering key journalists and critics
Platform impersonation-reporting relationships
Pre-established crisis communications playbook
ITID-24711.detection: Relies on social-listening and impersonation-monitoring tools; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24711.response: Confirm the impersonation directly with the named individual/outlet, request platform takedown of the fake account/content, and issue a public correction identifying the content as fabricated.
metrics: Count of journalist/critic impersonation incidents per quarter
Time from detection to platform takedown
ITID-24711.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is identity/content fabrication targeting public perception, not a network-intrusion technique. Differentiated from siblings by target identity: a real, named public media figure.

playbook.name: Response: Impersonation of Known Journalist/Critic Posting Fake Review
playbook.description: For a fake review or post created under the impersonated identity of a real, known journalist or critic, lending false credibility to a fabricated negative assessment.

steps.title: Locate the impersonating content and compare against the real person's known accounts/publications
steps.desc: Identify the fake account or post and cross-check it against the journalist/critic's verified accounts and publication history.

steps.title: Report the impersonating account/content to the platform
steps.desc: Submit an impersonation report, which most platforms treat with priority given it involves a real, identifiable individual.

steps.title: Pursue takedown of the impersonating content
steps.desc: Follow through on platform removal of the fake account/content.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence or re-creation of the impersonating account
steps.desc: Track whether the impersonation reappears under a new account.

steps.title: Document the incident and the verification/cooperation process
steps.desc: Record how the real person was reached and how quickly cooperation was secured, for future impersonation cases.

steps.title: Confirm the impersonation directly with the real journalist/critic or their publication
steps.desc: Contact the individual or their publication's editorial team to confirm they did not create the content and to establish their willingness to help correct it.
steps.outcome: Impersonation confirmed by the real person/publication, with their input on next steps.

steps.title: Coordinate with the real journalist/critic or their publication on a public clarification
steps.desc: Where the person or publication is willing, a clarification issued or co-issued by them carries far more credibility than a company statement alone.
steps.outcome: Clarification coordinated where the individual/publication agrees.

ITID-24712.def: An actor takes over, spoofs, or closely mimics a verified or otherwise high-trust reviewer account on a specific review platform (e.g. a 'Top Reviewer'-badged account) to post a fabricated negative review, exploiting the platform's own trust signals.
ITID-24712.purpose: Captures impersonation or compromise of a verified/high-trust reviewer account on a specific platform to post a fabricated review.
scopeIncludes: Compromise or account takeover of a legitimate high-trust/verified reviewer account to post fabricated content
Creation of a lookalike account closely mimicking a verified reviewer's handle, photo, and badge presentation
Exploitation of platform-specific trust indicators (verified badges, review counts, 'top reviewer' status) to increase believability
scopeExcludes: Impersonation of a named public journalist/critic outside the review-platform trust-badge context (ITID-24711)
Fabricated review attributed to an actual real, non-verified customer (ITID-24713)
ITID-24712.severity: Medium; platform trust signals materially increase reader confidence in the fabricated review.
ITID-24712.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if account takeover (rather than lookalike spoofing) is confirmed, given the account-security implication.
ITID-24712.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR; where account takeover (not just lookalike spoofing) is confirmed, also notify the platform's trust and safety/security team, since a real user's account has been compromised.
indicators: A verified/high-trust reviewer account posting content inconsistent with its prior review history or the account owner's public statements
The legitimate account owner reporting they did not write the review
A near-identical lookalike account mimicking a verified account's handle and badge
vectors: Account takeover via credential compromise
Lookalike account creation mimicking verified reviewer presentation
rootCauses: Weak account security on high-trust reviewer accounts (outside the company's control)
No monitoring for anomalous activity on verified accounts frequently reviewing the company
controls: Review-platform monitoring for anomalous verified-account activity
Platform reporting relationships for account takeover/impersonation
Pre-established crisis communications playbook
ITID-24712.detection: Relies on platform-side account monitoring outside the company's direct visibility; company-side detection is limited to content/pattern anomaly review.
ITID-24712.response: Report the suspected takeover/impersonation to the platform for investigation and content removal, and issue a factual correction where the fabricated review has gained visible traction.
metrics: Count of verified-reviewer impersonation/takeover incidents per quarter
Time to platform removal of the fabricated content
ITID-24712.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies by default; where a genuine account-takeover mechanism (not just visual lookalike spoofing) is confirmed, this may warrant a light-touch reference to account-compromise concepts, but the primary harm remains reputational content fabrication.

playbook.name: Response: Impersonation of Verified Platform Reviewer Account
playbook.description: For a fake review posted by impersonating a verified reviewer account on the platform itself, exploiting the credibility of the 'verified' badge.

steps.title: Compare the suspect review's account against the genuine verified account
steps.desc: Determine whether the review comes from a spoofed/lookalike account or an actual compromise of the genuine verified account.

steps.title: Report the impersonation/compromise to the platform's trust & safety and account-security teams
steps.desc: Flag both the fake review and the underlying impersonation or account compromise, which platforms typically prioritize.
steps.tool: Platform trust & safety / account security portal

steps.title: Pursue takedown and account restoration
steps.desc: Follow up until the fake review is removed and the genuine account is secured or the spoofed account is removed.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Watch for repeat impersonation of the same or other verified accounts.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record how the impersonation was identified and resolved, for future reference.

steps.title: Confirm with the real verified reviewer where identifiable
steps.desc: Contact the genuine account holder, if identifiable and reachable, to confirm they did not post the review and were not compromised (or to help them secure their account if they were).
steps.outcome: Impersonation or compromise confirmed with the real account holder's input where possible.

steps.title: Support the genuine reviewer if their account was compromised
steps.desc: If the real account was compromised rather than spoofed, help direct the account holder to the platform's account-recovery process.

ITID-24713.def: An actor fabricates review content and falsely attributes it to a real, identifiable customer of the company, who did not actually write or authorize the statement, in order to lend the fabricated claim the credibility of a genuine customer voice.
ITID-24713.purpose: Captures fabrication of a review or statement falsely attributed to a real, identifiable customer who did not actually write it.
scopeIncludes: Content falsely attributed to a real, named or otherwise identifiable customer who did not write it
The real customer subsequently disputing or being unaware of the attributed statement
Use of a real customer's likeness, name, or account details without consent to author the fabricated review
scopeExcludes: Impersonation of a named public journalist/critic (ITID-24711)
Impersonation of a verified platform reviewer account/badge as the defining mechanism (ITID-24712)
A genuine customer's real, unaltered negative review
ITID-24713.severity: Medium-High; also raises a potential harm/consent issue for the real, misappropriated customer.
ITID-24713.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the affected customer is a known or influential figure, or if legal exposure for misappropriation is significant.
ITID-24713.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR and legal; proactively contact the misappropriated customer to confirm the fabrication and offer support/correction.
indicators: A review attributed to a real, identifiable customer who denies writing it
Content inconsistent with the actual customer's known purchase history or documented interactions
The customer proactively reporting misuse of their name/identity
vectors: Fabricated review submissions using a real customer's name/details without consent
Doctored screenshots presenting a fabricated statement as coming from a real customer
rootCauses: No process to verify customer identity claims on disputed reviews
No established outreach process to support customers whose identity has been misappropriated
controls: Review-authenticity verification process for disputed reviews
Direct customer outreach/support process for misappropriation cases
Pre-established crisis communications playbook
ITID-24713.detection: Relies on customer-reported disputes and manual verification against purchase/interaction records; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24713.response: Verify the fabrication with the real customer, request platform removal of the fabricated content, support the affected customer, and issue a factual correction where appropriate.
metrics: Count of fabricated-attribution incidents per quarter
Time to platform removal after verification
ITID-24713.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies. Differentiated from siblings by the misappropriated identity being a real, ordinary customer rather than a public media figure (ITID-24711) or a platform's own verified-badge account (ITID-24712).

playbook.name: Response: Fabricated Review Falsely Attributed to Real Customer
playbook.description: For a fabricated review falsely presented as coming from a specific, real, identifiable customer who did not actually write it.

steps.title: Identify the real customer named/implied and cross-check against actual purchase/interaction records
steps.desc: Determine who is being falsely attributed and check internal records for any genuine interaction matching the review's claims.

steps.title: Report the fabricated review to the platform
steps.desc: Submit a report citing false attribution to a real, identifiable individual, which most platforms treat with priority.

steps.title: Pursue takedown of the fabricated review
steps.desc: Follow through on platform removal.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence and confirm customer satisfaction with the resolution
steps.desc: Track whether similar fabricated reviews reappear and check back with the customer.
steps.outcome: No recurrence; customer confirms satisfactory resolution.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record how the fabrication was identified and resolved, for future reference.

steps.title: Confirm the fabrication directly with the real customer
steps.desc: Contact the customer to confirm they did not write the review and to learn how they would like the situation handled.
steps.outcome: Fabrication confirmed with the customer's input and preferences noted.

steps.title: Support the misrepresented customer
steps.desc: Apologize as appropriate, keep them informed of progress, and offer any reasonable support given the false attribution.

ITID-24714.def: A catch-all classification for impersonation of a legitimate reviewer targeting the company's reputation that does not match a more specific sibling ITID under Impersonation of Legitimate Reviewers, pending clearer categorization or reclassification.
ITID-24714.purpose: Intake bucket for impersonation-of-reviewer activity that does not clearly fit the defined sibling leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reviewer-impersonation activity with a novel or mixed mechanism not covered by the sibling leaves
Ambiguous cases pending investigation to determine the correct specific classification
scopeExcludes: Any activity clearly matching Journalist/Critic Impersonation (ITID-24711), Verified Reviewer Account Impersonation (ITID-24712), or Fabricated Review Attributed to Real Customer (ITID-24713) — reclassify once determined
ITID-24714.severity: Assess case-by-case; default to Medium pending clarification given the impersonation element.
ITID-24714.priority: P3 by default; re-prioritize once the specific mechanism is identified and reclassified.
ITID-24714.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR for triage; reclassify to a specific sibling ITID as soon as the mechanism is clear.
indicators: Reviewer-impersonation activity that does not cleanly match an existing sibling pattern
vectors: Varies; any reviewer-impersonation mechanism not yet catalogued
rootCauses: Novel or hybrid attack technique not yet reflected in the taxonomy
Insufficient information at time of triage to classify precisely
controls: Impersonation/brand monitoring
Triage process to reclassify into a specific sibling ITID
ITID-24714.detection: Relies on the same social-listening/brand-monitoring tooling as sibling leaves.
ITID-24714.response: Investigate to determine the specific mechanism, reclassify under the appropriate sibling ITID, and follow that leaf's response guidance.
metrics: Count of unclassified impersonation incidents pending reclassification
Average time to reclassification
ITID-24714.notes: This is the standard 'Unclassified / General' catch-all leaf for the Impersonation of Legitimate Reviewers group, following the taxonomy's established intake-bucket pattern.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Impersonation of Legitimate Reviewer
playbook.description: General-purpose response for impersonation of a legitimate reviewer that does not fit a more specific known pattern (journalist/critic, verified platform account, or a specific real customer).

steps.title: Locate the impersonating content and identify the real person/entity being impersonated
steps.desc: Identify the fake account or content and determine who it purports to be.

steps.title: Report the impersonating content to the platform
steps.desc: Submit an impersonation report.

steps.title: Pursue takedown of the impersonating content
steps.desc: Follow through on platform removal.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Track whether the impersonation reappears.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record how the impersonation was identified and resolved, for future reference.

steps.title: Confirm the impersonation directly with the real person or entity where identifiable
steps.desc: Contact the real individual/entity to confirm the content is fabricated and learn their preferences for handling it.
steps.outcome: Impersonation confirmed with the real party's input where possible.

steps.title: Coordinate with the real person/entity on next steps where possible
steps.desc: Where the real party is willing, their cooperation on a correction is more credible than a company statement alone.

ITID-24721.def: An actor takes a real, verifiable quote actually spoken or written by a company executive and deliberately removes surrounding context, edits, or truncates it so that the presented meaning materially differs from the original statement's intent.
