ITID-24721.purpose: Captures a genuine statement made by a company executive that is deliberately edited, cropped, or presented without context to distort its meaning.
scopeIncludes: A genuinely-spoken/written executive quote presented with material context removed to alter its meaning
Selective editing of audio/video/text of a real statement to change its apparent meaning
The distorted version circulating with the original context unavailable or suppressed
scopeExcludes: A quote entirely invented that the executive never said at all (ITID-24722)
A real quote from an unrelated third party falsely attributed to the company/executive (ITID-24723)
ITID-24721.severity: Medium; the underlying quote's authenticity can make the distortion harder to immediately rebut.
ITID-24721.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for high-visibility executives or rapid viral spread.
ITID-24721.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR immediately to publish the full original context; escalate to legal if the distortion causes material reputational or financial harm.
indicators: A widely-shared quote missing verifiable surrounding context (source recording, transcript, publication date)
The full original source, when located, materially changing the apparent meaning
Rapid spread of the truncated version disproportionate to the original statement's visibility
vectors: Selective video/audio editing
Screenshot cropping of interviews, transcripts, or social posts
rootCauses: No practice of publishing full transcripts/recordings of executive public statements
No proactive monitoring for out-of-context quote circulation
controls: Brand/quote monitoring (social listening)
Standard practice of publishing full context (transcripts/recordings) for executive statements
Pre-established crisis communications playbook
ITID-24721.detection: Relies on social-listening tools and manual verification against original source material; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24721.response: Locate and publish the full original context/source, issue a factual correction clarifying the intended meaning, and request platform correction/removal where warranted.
metrics: Count of out-of-context quote incidents per quarter
Time from detection to publishing full context
ITID-24721.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies. Differentiated from siblings by the quote being genuinely spoken but stripped of context, rather than wholly invented (ITID-24722) or attributed from an unrelated source (ITID-24723).

playbook.name: Response: Fabricated Executive Quote Taken Out of Context
playbook.description: For a case where a real executive quote is circulated stripped of context in a way that misrepresents what they actually said or meant.

steps.title: Locate the original, full-context source of the quote
steps.desc: Find the original interview/speech/document the quote was pulled from.

steps.title: Report the out-of-context post to the hosting platform(s) if it violates their misinformation policy
steps.desc: Submit a platform report where applicable.
steps.outcome: Report submitted; may or may not result in removal since 'context' claims are often not enforced quickly by platforms.

steps.title: Publish the full context publicly
steps.desc: Release the full quote/transcript alongside a clear statement of what was omitted.
steps.guidance: Coordinate timing and wording with PR/Comms — a defensive-sounding correction can sometimes amplify the story further.
steps.outcome: Full context is publicly available and discoverable.

steps.title: Monitor sentiment and spread following the correction
steps.desc: Track whether the correction is gaining traction relative to the original distorted version.
steps.outcome: Correction reaching a meaningful share of the original audience.

steps.title: Document the incident and review executive-communications practices
steps.desc: Record how the quote was taken and whether clearer original framing (e.g., a fuller press release quote) could reduce this risk in future.

steps.title: Assess how the out-of-context version differs materially from the original meaning
steps.desc: Determine specifically what was omitted or reframed that changes the apparent meaning.
steps.guidance: Loop in Legal/PR to assess reputational and, if relevant, legal exposure.
steps.outcome: Clear articulation of the distortion, ready to support a correction.
steps.abort: If the quote is actually accurately represented, this isn't a hijacking incident — redirect to normal PR crisis handling instead.

ITID-24722.def: An actor invents a statement in its entirety and attributes it to a company executive or spokesperson who never said or wrote anything resembling it, fabricating the quote from nothing rather than distorting an existing statement.
ITID-24722.purpose: Captures a quote wholly invented and falsely attributed to a company executive or spokesperson, with no basis in anything actually said.
scopeIncludes: A quote with no corresponding original statement whatsoever, attributed to a named company executive/spokesperson
Fabricated quote graphics, screenshots, or 'leaked' text presenting the invented statement as authentic
The named individual explicitly denying ever making the statement
scopeExcludes: A genuine quote edited/cropped to change its meaning (ITID-24721)
A real quote said by someone else entirely, falsely attributed to the executive (ITID-24723)
ITID-24722.severity: Medium-High; wholly fabricated quotes attributed to leadership can cause significant, rapid reputational and even market impact.
ITID-24722.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for quotes attributed to the CEO/senior leadership or those touching on sensitive topics (safety, discrimination, financial guidance).
ITID-24722.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR and legal immediately; issue an explicit denial from the named individual and pursue platform takedown and defamation options.
indicators: A viral quote with no locatable original source, interview, or recording
The named executive/spokesperson explicitly denying the statement
A fabricated 'screenshot' or graphic with no corresponding verifiable original post
vectors: Fabricated quote graphics/memes
Fake 'leaked' internal communications or screenshots
rootCauses: No proactive monitoring for fabricated quotes attributed to leadership
No rapid-denial process established for executive misquote incidents
controls: Brand/quote monitoring (social listening)
Rapid-denial and correction process for leadership misquotes
Legal review for defamation assessment
ITID-24722.detection: Relies on social-listening tools and direct verification with the named individual; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24722.response: Obtain and publish an explicit denial from the named individual, issue a factual correction, and pursue platform takedown and legal action for clearly fabricated and damaging content.
metrics: Count of wholly-fabricated quote incidents per quarter
Time from detection to public denial
ITID-24722.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies. Differentiated from ITID-24721 by there being no underlying real statement at all, and from ITID-24723 by the (fictional) source being the company's own executive rather than an unrelated third party.

playbook.name: Response: Entirely Fabricated Quote Never Actually Said
playbook.description: For a quote attributed to a company executive or spokesperson that was never actually said, entirely invented rather than taken out of context.

steps.title: Locate the circulating quote and confirm no matching source exists
steps.desc: Search for any interview, speech, or document that could be the source; confirm none exists that supports the quote.
steps.outcome: Absence of any real source confirmed.

steps.title: Report the fabricated quote to the hosting platform(s)
steps.desc: Submit a report citing fabricated content/misinformation about a real, named individual.

steps.title: Publish a clear public denial and pursue takedown, escalating to legal action if warranted
steps.desc: Issue a direct statement that the quote is entirely fabricated; pursue removal, and where the source is identifiable, Legal may pursue formal action.
steps.outcome: Denial published; takedown pursued; legal action considered where warranted.

steps.title: Monitor sentiment and spread of the denial
steps.desc: Track whether the denial reaches the original audience and sentiment stabilizes.

steps.title: Document the incident and response process
steps.desc: Record the verification and response process for future fabricated-quote cases.

steps.title: Confirm directly with the named individual that the quote was never said
steps.desc: Have the named executive/spokesperson personally confirm they never made the statement, and loop in Legal to assess exposure.
steps.guidance: This is a clear fabrication case, distinct from a merely decontextualized real quote — treat with appropriate urgency given the direct falsehood.
steps.outcome: Fabrication confirmed by the named individual, with Legal's input on next steps.
steps.abort: If some version of the statement was in fact made, this is actually a misattributed/out-of-context case — redirect accordingly.

steps.title: Support the named individual directly
steps.desc: Notify and support the executive/spokesperson personally, offering Legal and Comms support.

ITID-24723.def: An actor takes a real quote genuinely spoken or written by an unrelated third party (not the company or its executives) and falsely re-attributes it to the company or one of its executives, borrowing the emotional impact of a real statement while misdirecting its source.
ITID-24723.purpose: Captures a genuine quote actually said by an unrelated third party that is falsely re-attributed to the company or one of its executives.
scopeIncludes: A verifiably real quote from an identifiable unrelated third party, falsely presented as coming from the company/executive
Fabricated attribution graphics pairing a real quote with the company's branding or an executive's name/photo
The actual original speaker being identifiable and unconnected to the company
scopeExcludes: A genuine company executive quote edited out of context (ITID-24721)
A quote wholly invented with no real original speaker (ITID-24722)
ITID-24723.severity: Medium; can be rapidly and definitively rebutted once the real original source is identified.
ITID-24723.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the quote is inflammatory or touches on sensitive social/political topics.
ITID-24723.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR to publish the correct original source and attribution; escalate to legal if the misattribution is being used for demonstrably defamatory purposes.
indicators: A quote circulating with the company's branding/executive name attached, findable as originating from an unrelated identifiable source
The real original speaker or their representatives confirming authorship
Reverse-search of the quote/image revealing an unrelated original context
vectors: Quote-attribution graphics/memes swapping speaker identity
Cross-posting a real quote with fabricated company branding
rootCauses: No proactive monitoring for misattributed quote circulation
No established rapid fact-check/source-verification process
controls: Brand/quote monitoring (social listening)
Rapid source-verification and correction process
Pre-established crisis communications playbook
ITID-24723.detection: Relies on social-listening tools and reverse-source verification; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24723.response: Identify and publish the correct original source, issue a factual correction clarifying the misattribution, and request platform correction where warranted.
metrics: Count of misattributed-quote incidents per quarter
Time from detection to public correction
ITID-24723.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies. Differentiated from siblings by the quote being real but sourced from an unrelated third party, distinct from a genuine executive quote (ITID-24721) or a wholly invented one (ITID-24722).

playbook.name: Response: Misattributed Quote from Unrelated Third Party
playbook.description: For a real quote, actually said by an unrelated third party, that has been falsely attributed to the company or one of its executives.

steps.title: Trace the quote back to its actual, real source
steps.desc: Identify who actually said the quote and in what original context.

steps.title: Report the misattributed content to the hosting platform(s)
steps.desc: Submit a report citing misattributed/fabricated content.

steps.title: Publish a factual correction identifying the real source and pursue takedown
steps.desc: Release a correction clarifying the quote's true origin; pursue removal of the misattributed version.

steps.title: Monitor sentiment and spread of the correction
steps.desc: Track whether the correction reaches the original audience.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record how the true source was traced and the correction process, for future reference.

steps.title: Confirm the misattribution with the actual source where identifiable
steps.desc: Where the real speaker is identifiable and reachable, confirm the misattribution with them and gauge their willingness to help correct it publicly.
steps.outcome: Misattribution confirmed, with the real source's input where possible.

steps.title: Coordinate with the actual source on a joint or independent correction where possible
steps.desc: A correction acknowledged by the real speaker is more credible than a company statement alone.
steps.outcome: Coordination established where the real source is willing.

ITID-24724.def: A catch-all classification for misattributed-quote activity targeting the company's reputation that does not match a more specific sibling ITID under Misattributed Quotes, pending clearer categorization or reclassification.
ITID-24724.purpose: Intake bucket for misattributed-quote activity that does not clearly fit the defined sibling leaves.
scopeIncludes: Misattributed-quote activity with a novel or mixed mechanism not covered by the sibling leaves
Ambiguous cases pending investigation to determine the correct specific classification
scopeExcludes: Any activity clearly matching Out-of-Context Executive Quote (ITID-24721), Entirely Fabricated Quote (ITID-24722), or Misattributed Third-Party Quote (ITID-24723) — reclassify once determined
ITID-24724.severity: Assess case-by-case; default to Low-to-Medium pending clarification.
ITID-24724.priority: P3 by default; re-prioritize once the specific mechanism is identified and reclassified.
ITID-24724.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR for triage; reclassify to a specific sibling ITID as soon as the mechanism is clear.
indicators: Misattributed-quote activity that does not cleanly match an existing sibling pattern
vectors: Varies; any misattributed-quote mechanism not yet catalogued
rootCauses: Novel or hybrid attack technique not yet reflected in the taxonomy
Insufficient information at time of triage to classify precisely
controls: Brand/quote monitoring
Triage process to reclassify into a specific sibling ITID
ITID-24724.detection: Relies on the same social-listening/brand-monitoring tooling as sibling leaves.
ITID-24724.response: Investigate to determine the specific mechanism, reclassify under the appropriate sibling ITID, and follow that leaf's response guidance.
metrics: Count of unclassified misattributed-quote incidents pending reclassification
Average time to reclassification
ITID-24724.notes: This is the standard 'Unclassified / General' catch-all leaf for the Misattributed Quotes group, following the taxonomy's established intake-bucket pattern.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Misattributed Quote
playbook.description: General-purpose response for a misattributed quote incident that does not fit a more specific known pattern (out-of-context executive quote, entirely fabricated quote, or a quote misattributed from an unrelated third party).

steps.title: Locate the original source, if any, and compare it to the circulating version
steps.desc: Determine whether the quote has any real source and how the circulating version differs.

steps.title: Report the content to the hosting platform(s)
steps.desc: Submit a report citing fabricated/misattributed content where applicable.

steps.title: Publish a factual correction and pursue takedown
steps.desc: Release a correction addressing the specific issue and pursue removal of the problematic content.

steps.title: Monitor sentiment and spread of the correction
steps.desc: Track whether the correction reaches the original audience.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the facts and resolution process for future reference.

steps.title: Confirm the nature of the issue with the relevant real person(s) where identifiable
steps.desc: Contact any identifiable real person involved (the person quoted, or falsely attributed) to confirm the facts and their preferences for correction.
steps.guidance: Loop in Legal to assess exposure.

steps.title: Coordinate with any involved real person on a correction where possible
steps.desc: Their cooperation strengthens the credibility of any correction.

ITID-24731.def: An actor fabricates and circulates a claim (written or verbal, without accompanying doctored visual evidence) asserting that the company has partnered with, sponsored, endorsed, or been endorsed by a controversial public figure, when no such relationship exists.
ITID-24731.purpose: Captures a fabricated textual or verbal claim asserting a false partnership, sponsorship, or endorsement relationship between the company and a controversial figure.
scopeIncludes: A written or verbal claim of partnership/sponsorship/endorsement with a controversial figure that has no factual basis
Fabricated press-release-style announcements or social posts asserting the false relationship
The claim circulating without a doctored photo/video as its primary evidence (see ITID-24732 for that variant)
scopeExcludes: Manipulated photo/video fabricating the appearance of the association (ITID-24732)
A real historical connection resurfaced without current context (ITID-24733)
A genuine, disclosed partnership that later becomes controversial due to the partner's subsequent conduct (a business/PR decision, not a fabrication incident)
ITID-24731.severity: Medium-High; false association claims can trigger rapid public backlash before verification occurs.
ITID-24731.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for high-visibility controversial figures or rapid viral spread.
ITID-24731.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR and legal immediately to issue a categorical denial and assess defamation/takedown options.
indicators: A partnership/endorsement claim with no corresponding official announcement, contract, or public record
The controversial figure's own representatives denying any relationship
Rapid viral spread of the claim disproportionate to any verifiable source
vectors: Fabricated social media posts or fake press releases
Fake 'leaked' partnership documents or announcements
rootCauses: No proactive monitoring for false association claims
No rapid-denial process established for fabricated partnership claims
controls: Brand/association monitoring (social listening)
Rapid public-denial and correction process
Legal review for defamation assessment
ITID-24731.detection: Relies on social-listening tools and verification against actual partnership records; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24731.response: Issue an immediate, categorical public denial with supporting documentation, and pursue platform takedown or legal action for content causing material harm.
metrics: Count of fabricated-association-claim incidents per quarter
Time from detection to public denial
ITID-24731.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies. Differentiated from ITID-24732 by evidence type: a textual/verbal claim rather than doctored visual media, and from ITID-24733 by having no genuine historical basis at all.

playbook.name: Response: Fabricated Endorsement/Partnership Claim with Controversial Figure
playbook.description: For a false claim that the company endorses, partners with, or is otherwise associated with a controversial public figure, when no such relationship exists.

steps.title: Locate the claim and identify the specific controversial figure and alleged relationship
steps.desc: Capture the exact claim (endorsement, partnership, sponsorship, etc.) and its reach.

steps.title: Report the fabricated claim to the hosting platform(s)
steps.desc: Submit a report citing fabricated content where the platform's misinformation policy applies.

steps.title: Publish the denial and pursue takedown of the fabricated claim
steps.desc: Release the statement and pursue removal of the fabricated content.

steps.title: Monitor sentiment and spread of the denial
steps.desc: Track whether the denial is reaching the original audience and whether the false claim continues to circulate.
steps.outcome: Sentiment trend improving; spread of the false claim declining.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the claim and response process for future reference.

steps.title: Confirm with internal records that no such relationship exists
steps.desc: Check with Partnerships/Marketing/Legal to confirm definitively that no endorsement, partnership, or association of any kind exists or ever existed with the named figure.
steps.outcome: Absence of any relationship confirmed and documented.
steps.abort: If some limited or historical relationship is found to actually exist, redirect to a factual clarification of its scope rather than a flat denial.

steps.title: Prepare a clear, factual denial with PR/Comms and Legal
steps.desc: Draft a concise public statement denying the claim, coordinated to avoid amplifying the controversial figure's profile unnecessarily.

ITID-24732.def: An actor creates or alters visual media (a photo or video, including digitally composited or AI-generated imagery) to falsely depict the company, its branding, or its executives in association with a controversial figure, in order to make the fabricated association visually convincing.
ITID-24732.purpose: Captures a manipulated (doctored) photo or video fabricated to visually depict a false association between the company and a controversial figure.
scopeIncludes: Digitally composited, edited, or AI-generated (deepfake-style) imagery/video falsely depicting association with a controversial figure
Doctored event/venue photos inserting company branding or executives into unrelated footage
The visual media serving as the primary claimed 'evidence' for the false association
scopeExcludes: A false association claim made only in text/verbal form without doctored visual evidence (ITID-24731)
A genuine, undoctored historical photo resurfaced without current context (ITID-24733)
ITID-24732.severity: High; doctored visual media is disproportionately persuasive and harder to rapidly disprove to a general audience.
ITID-24732.priority: P1, given the high credibility and virality risk of convincing fabricated visual evidence.
ITID-24732.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR and legal immediately; engage digital forensics resources to document the manipulation and pursue urgent platform takedown.
indicators: A photo/video depicting an association with no corresponding real event on record
Forensic/technical analysis revealing digital compositing or generative-AI artifacts
Inconsistencies in lighting, shadows, resolution, or metadata indicating manipulation
vectors: Photo/video editing and compositing tools
Generative AI image/video synthesis (deepfakes)
rootCauses: No proactive monitoring for manipulated visual media referencing the company
No established forensic-verification capability or relationship for rapid authentication
controls: Visual-media/brand monitoring (social listening, reverse image search)
Digital forensics/authentication capability or vendor relationship
Legal review for defamation and platform-takedown escalation
ITID-24732.detection: Relies on reverse-image search and digital forensic analysis; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24732.response: Commission forensic analysis to document the manipulation, issue an immediate public denial with supporting evidence, and pursue urgent platform takedown given the higher credibility risk of visual media.
metrics: Count of manipulated-media association incidents per quarter
Time from detection to platform takedown
ITID-24732.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies — this is content fabrication (deepfake/photo manipulation), not a network-intrusion technique. Differentiated from ITID-24731 by the presence of doctored visual media as the primary evidence.

playbook.name: Response: Manipulated Photo/Video Falsely Depicting Association
playbook.description: For a manipulated or fabricated photo or video falsely depicting the company, its branding, or its executives in association with a controversial figure or event.

steps.title: Obtain and preserve the manipulated media
steps.desc: Capture the exact image/video circulating, along with reach metrics.

steps.title: Report the manipulated media to the hosting platform(s)
steps.desc: Submit a report citing manipulated media/misinformation policy violations.

steps.title: Publish the statement and pursue takedown of the manipulated media
steps.desc: Release the statement and pursue removal wherever the media is hosted.
steps.outcome: Statement published; takedown pursued across platforms.

steps.title: Monitor for re-upload and spread of the manipulated media
steps.desc: Track whether the media resurfaces on other platforms or accounts.

steps.title: Document the incident and forensic process
steps.desc: Record the forensic method used to confirm manipulation, for faster response to future cases.

steps.title: Conduct forensic verification that the media is manipulated
steps.desc: Analyze the media (reverse image search, metadata review, or forensic tools) to establish it is manipulated or fabricated rather than genuine.
steps.guidance: Engage a digital-forensics specialist for high-profile or highly convincing cases.
steps.outcome: Manipulation confirmed with supporting technical evidence.
steps.abort: If the media is confirmed genuine, this is not a fabrication case — reassess as a factual association matter requiring a different response.
steps.tool: Reverse image search / media forensics tool

steps.title: Prepare a factual statement with the forensic evidence
steps.desc: Draft a public statement identifying the media as manipulated, supported by the forensic findings, coordinated with PR/Comms and Legal.

ITID-24733.def: An actor resurfaces a factually real but historical, minor, or since-resolved connection between the company and a controversial figure or entity, deliberately omitting timeline, resolution, or context so that it appears to be a current or more significant association than it actually is.
ITID-24733.purpose: Captures the resurfacing of a genuine but old, minor, or resolved historical connection, presented without current context to imply an ongoing or more significant present-day association.
scopeIncludes: A genuine historical fact/connection presented without dates, resolution status, or context that would show it is outdated or minor
Recirculation of old, previously-addressed news framed as breaking or ongoing
Omission of material facts (e.g. the relationship ended years ago, or was a minor/incidental transaction) to imply present-day significance
scopeExcludes: A wholly fabricated claim of association with no factual basis (ITID-24731)
A manipulated photo/video with no genuine underlying historical event (ITID-24732)
ITID-24733.severity: Medium; the factual kernel makes the claim harder to categorically deny, requiring contextual correction rather than outright denial.
ITID-24733.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the resurfaced connection touches on a highly sensitive current controversy.
ITID-24733.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR to publish full context and timeline promptly; escalate to legal only if the omission is being used in a demonstrably defamatory manner.
indicators: A historical fact being circulated with dates or resolution status omitted
The connection having been previously publicly addressed or resolved by the company
Framing language implying present-day relevance for a dated event
vectors: Selective recirculation of old news articles or records
Framing/captioning that omits timeline context
rootCauses: No readily accessible public record of how/when past associations were addressed or resolved
No proactive monitoring for recirculation of old company history
controls: Brand/history monitoring (social listening)
Maintained public record/FAQ addressing past resolved associations
Pre-established crisis communications playbook
ITID-24733.detection: Relies on social-listening tools and historical-record verification; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24733.response: Publish the full timeline and resolution context promptly, correcting the misleading omission without denying the underlying factual event.
metrics: Count of misleading-historical-resurfacing incidents per quarter
Time from detection to contextual correction
ITID-24733.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies. Differentiated from siblings by having a genuine factual basis, unlike the wholly fabricated (ITID-24731) or visually doctored (ITID-24732) variants — the harm here is misleading omission of context, not invention.

playbook.name: Response: Misleading Historical Connection Resurfaced Out of Context
playbook.description: For a genuine but old, resolved, or otherwise non-representative historical connection to a controversial figure or event being resurfaced and framed misleadingly as current or more significant than it actually was.

steps.title: Establish the full, accurate history of the connection
steps.desc: Gather the complete factual record of the historical connection — dates, scope, and any subsequent actions the company took (e.g. ending a relationship, public distancing).

steps.title: Report the misleading post to the hosting platform(s) if it violates their misinformation policy
steps.desc: Submit a platform report where applicable.
steps.outcome: Report submitted; removal not guaranteed since 'missing context' claims are often not swiftly enforced.

steps.title: Publish the full factual timeline publicly
steps.desc: Release the complete history alongside a clear statement of what the resurfaced framing omitted.
steps.guidance: Coordinate timing and wording carefully — a defensive-sounding correction can sometimes amplify the story further.
steps.outcome: Full context publicly available and discoverable.

steps.title: Monitor sentiment and spread following the correction
steps.desc: Track whether the correction is gaining traction relative to the misleading framing.
steps.outcome: Correction reaching a meaningful share of the original audience.

steps.title: Document the incident and review historical-relationship disclosure practices
steps.desc: Record whether clearer proactive disclosure of the resolved history could reduce this risk in future.

steps.title: Assess specifically how the resurfaced framing is misleading
steps.desc: Determine what the current framing omits or distorts relative to the full history — e.g. presenting a decade-old, brief, already-terminated relationship as current and central.
steps.guidance: Loop in Legal/PR to assess reputational exposure.
steps.outcome: Clear articulation of the misleading framing, ready to support a correction.
steps.abort: If the current framing is in fact an accurate representation of an ongoing or unresolved connection, this is not a hijacking case — redirect to substantive PR crisis handling instead.

steps.title: Prepare a factual timeline for public release
steps.desc: Draft a clear, factual timeline of the connection and its resolution, coordinated with PR/Comms and Legal.

ITID-24734.def: A catch-all classification for false-association activity targeting the company's reputation that does not match a more specific sibling ITID under Association with Controversial Figures, pending clearer categorization or reclassification.
ITID-24734.purpose: Intake bucket for false-association-with-controversial-figure activity that does not clearly fit the defined sibling leaves.
scopeIncludes: False-association activity with a novel or mixed mechanism not covered by the sibling leaves
Ambiguous cases pending investigation to determine the correct specific classification
scopeExcludes: Any activity clearly matching Fabricated Endorsement Claim (ITID-24731), Manipulated Photo/Video (ITID-24732), or Misleading Historical Connection (ITID-24733) — reclassify once determined
ITID-24734.severity: Assess case-by-case; default to Medium pending clarification given the association-with-controversy element.
ITID-24734.priority: P3 by default; re-prioritize once the specific mechanism is identified and reclassified.
ITID-24734.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR for triage; reclassify to a specific sibling ITID as soon as the mechanism is clear.
indicators: False-association activity that does not cleanly match an existing sibling pattern
vectors: Varies; any false-association mechanism not yet catalogued
rootCauses: Novel or hybrid attack technique not yet reflected in the taxonomy
Insufficient information at time of triage to classify precisely
controls: Brand/association monitoring
Triage process to reclassify into a specific sibling ITID
ITID-24734.detection: Relies on the same social-listening/brand-monitoring tooling as sibling leaves.
ITID-24734.response: Investigate to determine the specific mechanism, reclassify under the appropriate sibling ITID, and follow that leaf's response guidance.
metrics: Count of unclassified false-association incidents pending reclassification
Average time to reclassification
ITID-24734.notes: This is the standard 'Unclassified / General' catch-all leaf for the Association with Controversial Figures group, following the taxonomy's established intake-bucket pattern.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General False Association with Controversial Figure
playbook.description: General-purpose response for a false-association incident that does not fit a more specific known pattern (fabricated endorsement, manipulated media, or a misleadingly resurfaced historical connection).

steps.title: Locate the claim and establish the actual facts of any relationship
steps.desc: Capture the exact claim and check internal records for any real relationship, past or present, with the named figure.

steps.title: Report the content to the hosting platform(s) where applicable
steps.desc: Submit a report citing the relevant platform policy (misinformation, manipulated media, etc.).

steps.title: Publish the statement and pursue takedown of the false content
steps.desc: Release the statement and pursue removal wherever the content is hosted.

steps.title: Monitor sentiment and spread following the correction
steps.desc: Track whether the correction reaches the original audience.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record the facts and resolution process for future reference.

steps.title: Assess whether the claim is fabricated, manipulated, or misleadingly framed
steps.desc: Determine the specific nature of the falsehood before deciding on a response, looping in Legal/PR as needed.
steps.abort: If a genuine, currently relevant relationship is confirmed, redirect to substantive PR crisis handling instead of this playbook.

steps.title: Prepare a factual statement with PR/Comms and Legal
steps.desc: Draft a public statement addressing the specific falsehood.

ITID-24811.def: An actor fabricates a product recall notice and presents it as an official communication from a genuine regulatory agency (e.g. a consumer safety, food/drug, or transport authority), impersonating that agency's identity, formatting, or channels to make the fake recall appear legally and factually authoritative.
ITID-24811.purpose: Captures a fabricated product recall notice presented as an official communication from a real regulatory agency to lend it false authority.
scopeIncludes: A fabricated recall notice styled to mimic a real regulatory agency's official format, letterhead, or branding
Distribution of the fake notice via channels impersonating the agency (fake agency social account, spoofed agency website/press page)
The notice asserting a specific, actionable-sounding recall event (affected product, batch, safety hazard) rather than general critical commentary
scopeExcludes: A fake recall distributed via a spoofed press-release wire service rather than agency impersonation (ITID-24812)
A fake recall sent directly to customers via fabricated company email (ITID-24813)

Broad, non-specific misinformation about product safety with no claimed regulatory action (ITID-24311, Misinformation Post Fabricating Product Safety/Recall Claim) or general coordinated misinformation campaigns (ITID-2351x) — this leaf is scoped specifically to a fabricated recall event impersonating a real regulator's official communication
ITID-24811.severity: High; impersonation of a real regulatory agency can trigger genuine consumer panic, retailer action, and regulatory confusion before it is debunked.
ITID-24811.priority: P1, given the potential for immediate operational and consumer-safety-perception impact.
ITID-24811.escalation: Escalate immediately to communications/PR, legal, and regulatory affairs; contact the impersonated agency directly to confirm the notice is fraudulent and request a joint public correction.
indicators: A recall notice that does not appear on the actual regulatory agency's official recall database/site
The agency confirming, upon direct contact, that it issued no such notice
Formatting or branding inconsistencies versus the agency's genuine communications
vectors: Fabricated agency letterhead/document templates
Spoofed agency social media accounts or lookalike websites
T1656 Impersonation of a real regulatory agency's identity/communications
rootCauses: No established rapid-verification channel with key regulatory agencies
No public-facing single source of truth for actual recall status that customers can quickly check
controls: Direct rapid-verification relationship with relevant regulatory agencies
Public, authoritative recall-status page maintained by the company
Pre-established crisis communications playbook for fake recall scenarios
ITID-24811.detection: Relies on regulatory-agency confirmation and brand monitoring; not a technical/network detection surface, though the impersonation mechanism itself has a narrow, real-world identity-fraud component.
ITID-24811.response: Confirm falsity with the impersonated agency immediately, publish a joint or company-issued public correction directing customers to the authoritative recall-status page, and pursue takedown of the fraudulent notice/accounts.
metrics: Count of fake regulatory-recall incidents per quarter
Time from detection to joint/company public correction
ITID-24811.notes: Scope decision: distinguished from general product-safety misinformation (ITID-24311) and coordinated misinformation campaigns (ITID-2351x) by requiring a specific, actionable-sounding fabricated recall event impersonating a real regulator — not broad narrative claims. Narrow MITRE mapping (T1656) applies here because a real regulatory agency's identity/communications are being impersonated, unlike most leaves in this domain.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Recall Notice via Fabricated Regulatory Agency Communication
playbook.description: A fabricated recall notice, falsely attributed to a regulatory agency (e.g. a consumer safety commission or health authority), is circulating and claims this organization has recalled a product it has not actually recalled.

steps.title: Verify directly with the named regulatory agency whether any recall exists
steps.desc: Contact the actual regulatory agency named in the notice (or check its official public recall database) to confirm no genuine recall has been issued, and obtain the agency's confirmation in writing where possible.
steps.guidance: Do this before any public denial — an authoritative third-party confirmation strengthens the response considerably.
steps.outcome: Written or documented confirmation from the actual agency that no such recall exists.
steps.abort: If a genuine recall does in fact exist, this is not a fake-crisis incident — route immediately to the organization's real product-recall/regulatory-compliance process instead.

steps.title: Report the fabricated notice to each platform where it is circulating
steps.desc: Submit a misinformation/impersonation report to each platform, including the agency's confirmation that no recall exists.

steps.title: Follow up until the fabricated notice is removed across all channels
steps.desc: Track each platform's response and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Publish an official statement confirming no recall exists
steps.desc: Issue a clear, factual public statement (with the agency's confirmation referenced where possible) reassuring customers no recall has occurred.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the fabrication method and response for reuse against future fake-recall incidents.

steps.title: Trace the notice's origin and distribution channels
steps.desc: Identify where the fabricated notice originated (social media, email, spoofed press release) and how widely it has spread.

steps.title: Notify the impersonated regulatory agency and law enforcement if warranted
steps.desc: Inform the agency that its identity was used to fabricate the notice, and consult legal on whether a law-enforcement report is warranted given the impersonation of a government body.

ITID-24812.def: An actor fabricates a product recall announcement and distributes it through a spoofed or compromised press-release wire/distribution channel, exploiting the perceived legitimacy of newswire distribution to make the fake recall appear to be officially released company or media news.
ITID-24812.purpose: Captures a fabricated product recall notice distributed through a spoofed press-release wire service to appear as legitimate news distribution.
scopeIncludes: A fabricated recall announcement formatted as a press release and distributed via a spoofed or compromised newswire channel
Use of a lookalike wire-service domain or compromised legitimate wire account to distribute the fake release
The release asserting a specific, actionable-sounding recall event
scopeExcludes: A fake recall notice impersonating a regulatory agency directly (ITID-24811)
A fake recall sent directly to customers via fabricated email (ITID-24813)
ITID-24812.severity: High; wire-service distribution can cause automated pickup by news aggregators and financial data feeds before verification.
ITID-24812.priority: P1, given the risk of automated media/financial pickup amplifying the fabricated release before correction.
ITID-24812.escalation: Escalate immediately to communications/PR, investor relations (given potential market impact), and legal; contact the wire service to confirm the release is fraudulent and request retraction.
indicators: A press release not present in the company's actual distribution history or PR archive
The wire service confirming no legitimate submission was made
Automated news aggregators or trading algorithms reacting to the fabricated release
vectors: Spoofed or lookalike wire-service domains
Compromised legitimate wire-service publisher accounts
Fake press-release submission via weakly-vetted distribution platforms
rootCauses: No monitoring of newswire distribution for unauthorized releases referencing the company
No established rapid-verification relationship with the wire services the company legitimately uses
controls: Newswire monitoring for unauthorized company-referencing releases
Rapid-verification relationship with legitimate wire services
Pre-established crisis communications playbook including investor relations coordination
ITID-24812.detection: Relies on media/wire monitoring and direct wire-service confirmation; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24812.response: Confirm falsity with the wire service, request immediate retraction, issue a public correction, and coordinate with investor relations if any market reaction has occurred.
metrics: Count of fake wire-distributed recall incidents per quarter
Time from detection to wire retraction
ITID-24812.notes: Scope decision: distinguished from ITID-24811 by distribution mechanism (newswire spoofing vs. direct regulatory-agency impersonation) and from general misinformation campaigns by the specific, actionable-sounding fabricated recall event.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Recall Notice Distributed via Spoofed Press Release Wire
playbook.description: A fabricated recall notice has been distributed as though issued through a legitimate press-release wire service, lending it false credibility with media outlets.

steps.title: Verify with the wire service whether it actually distributed the release
steps.desc: Contact the named press-release wire service directly to confirm whether it distributed the release, and if not, how the spoofing occurred (compromised account, look-alike domain, forged formatting).
steps.outcome: Confirmation from the wire service that the release was not legitimately distributed, and how the spoof occurred.
steps.abort: If the wire service confirms it did distribute the release, verify whether it originated from a compromised internal account — this may become a separate access-compromise incident.

steps.title: Notify media outlets that picked up the release with a correction request
steps.desc: Contact each identified outlet directly with evidence the release was fabricated/spoofed and request a correction or retraction.

steps.title: Follow up until media corrections/retractions are published
steps.desc: Track each outlet's response and escalate (e.g. via a formal correction request or the outlet's standards editor) as needed.

steps.title: Publish an official statement confirming no recall exists
steps.desc: Issue a clear public statement through verified organizational channels reassuring customers and media that no recall occurred.

steps.title: Document the spoofing method for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record how the wire spoof was executed and detected to speed future response and inform any authentication improvements with the wire service.

steps.title: Identify which media outlets picked up the fabricated release
steps.desc: Search for news coverage or republication of the fake release to determine outbound reach.
steps.outcome: List of outlets that picked up the release.

steps.title: Report the spoofing to the wire service and consider law enforcement
steps.desc: File a report with the wire service's security/abuse team and consult legal on a law-enforcement report given the impersonation involved.
steps.outcome: Wire service notified; law-enforcement engagement decided.

ITID-24813.def: An actor fabricates a product recall notice and sends it directly to customers via email designed to impersonate the company's own communications, exploiting the appearance of a direct company-to-customer channel to make the fake recall appear authoritative and urgent.
ITID-24813.purpose: Captures a fabricated recall notice sent directly to customers via a fraudulent email designed to look like it comes from the company.
scopeIncludes: A fabricated recall email spoofing or closely mimicking the company's sender domain, branding, and communication style
Direct distribution to customers claiming to be an official company recall notice
The notice asserting a specific, actionable-sounding recall event, potentially including a call to action (e.g. a fraudulent link or return process)
scopeExcludes: A fake recall impersonating a regulatory agency (ITID-24811)
A fake recall distributed via newswire (ITID-24812)

A phishing campaign whose primary goal is credential/payment theft rather than reputational/crisis fabrication (a distinct email-based-threat ITID elsewhere in the taxonomy) — this leaf is scoped to the reputational/crisis-fabrication intent even where a fraudulent link is present
ITID-24813.severity: High; direct customer targeting combined with company impersonation can cause both reputational harm and downstream customer confusion or fraud exposure.
ITID-24813.priority: P1, given direct customer impact and potential secondary fraud risk (e.g. malicious links).
ITID-24813.escalation: Escalate immediately to communications/PR, legal, and IT security (given the email-impersonation/phishing-adjacent mechanism and any embedded links); notify affected customers with a factual correction.
indicators: Customer reports of a recall email inconsistent with the company's actual communications
Spoofed or lookalike sender domain rather than the company's verified domain
Embedded links directing to non-company-controlled infrastructure
vectors: Email domain spoofing
Lookalike domains mimicking the company's official domain
T1656 Impersonation of the company's own identity/communications
T1585/T1586 Establish or Compromise Accounts to send from a plausible-looking sender
rootCauses: Weak email-authentication posture (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) making spoofing easier for recipients' mail systems to miss
No established rapid customer-notification channel to counter fraudulent emails
controls: Email authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) monitoring and enforcement
Rapid customer-notification/correction channel
IT security coordination for takedown of malicious sending infrastructure and links
Pre-established crisis communications playbook
ITID-24813.detection: Combines customer-reported phishing-style indicators with brand monitoring; has a genuine technical detection surface via email-authentication and infrastructure takedown, unlike most leaves in this domain.
ITID-24813.response: Confirm the email is fraudulent, coordinate with IT security to pursue takedown of the sending infrastructure/links, and issue a rapid factual correction to customers through verified channels.
metrics: Count of fake recall email incidents per quarter
Time from detection to customer correction notice
Number of customers reached by the fraudulent email
detections: Email-authentication failure alerting for lookalike domains
ITID-24813.notes: Scope decision: distinguished from ITID-24811/24812 by the impersonated identity being the company itself via direct email, and from credential-theft-focused phishing ITIDs elsewhere in the taxonomy by primary intent (reputational crisis fabrication, not credential/payment harvesting) — a dual-intent incident should be co-classified with the relevant phishing ITID if credential theft is also confirmed. Narrow MITRE mapping applies given the real technical impersonation/infrastructure mechanism.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Recall Notice via Fabricated Email to Customers
playbook.description: A fraudulent email impersonating this organization has been sent directly to customers claiming a product recall, potentially also serving as a phishing vector.

steps.title: Confirm no genuine recall exists and assess whether the email is also a phishing attempt
steps.desc: Confirm internally that no genuine recall has been issued, and have security review the fake email's headers, links, and any requested actions to determine whether it is also being used to phish credentials or payment information from customers.
steps.guidance: This is often simultaneously a brand-impersonation incident and a phishing/fraud incident — coordinate with the security/fraud team, not just brand-protection.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no genuine recall exists; phishing/fraud risk assessed.
steps.abort: If a genuine recall does exist, route to the real recall process instead.

steps.title: Report the fraudulent email to hosting/email providers and anti-phishing services
steps.desc: Submit abuse reports to the sending domain's host/registrar and to relevant anti-phishing services (e.g. browser safe-browsing feeds) to get the email/domain blocked.
steps.tool: Domain registrar/host abuse channel; anti-phishing reporting services

steps.title: Confirm the fraudulent sending infrastructure is taken down
steps.desc: Track the host/registrar response and escalate if the infrastructure remains active beyond a reasonable window.
steps.outcome: Sending domain/infrastructure taken down or blocklisted.

steps.title: Monitor for customer reports of fraud stemming from the email
steps.desc: Coordinate with customer support and fraud teams to track any reports of harm and assist affected customers.
steps.outcome: Affected customers identified and assisted, or none found.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the email infrastructure signature and response for reuse against future impersonation/phishing incidents.

steps.title: Identify the sending infrastructure and estimate customer exposure
steps.desc: Analyze the sending domain/infrastructure and estimate how many customers may have received the fraudulent email, using any available distribution indicators.

steps.title: Warn customers directly through verified channels
steps.desc: Send a warning to customers through this organization's own verified email/notification channels and website, describing the fake email and how to identify it.

ITID-24814.def: A catch-all classification for fake recall announcement activity targeting the company's reputation that does not match a more specific sibling ITID under Fake Recall Announcements, pending clearer categorization or reclassification.
ITID-24814.purpose: Intake bucket for fake recall announcement activity that does not clearly fit the defined sibling leaves.
scopeIncludes: Fake recall activity with a novel or mixed distribution mechanism not covered by the sibling leaves
Ambiguous cases pending investigation to determine the correct specific classification
scopeExcludes: Any activity clearly matching Regulatory Agency Impersonation (ITID-24811), Spoofed Wire Distribution (ITID-24812), or Fabricated Customer Email (ITID-24813) — reclassify once determined
ITID-24814.severity: Assess case-by-case; default to High pending clarification, given the general severity of fake recall events.
ITID-24814.priority: P2 by default; re-prioritize once the specific mechanism is identified and reclassified.
ITID-24814.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR and legal for triage; reclassify to a specific sibling ITID as soon as the mechanism is clear.
indicators: Fake recall activity that does not cleanly match an existing sibling pattern
vectors: Varies; any fake-recall distribution mechanism not yet catalogued
rootCauses: Novel or hybrid attack technique not yet reflected in the taxonomy
Insufficient information at time of triage to classify precisely
controls: Brand/crisis monitoring
Triage process to reclassify into a specific sibling ITID
ITID-24814.detection: Relies on the same monitoring tooling as sibling leaves.
ITID-24814.response: Investigate to determine the specific mechanism, reclassify under the appropriate sibling ITID, and follow that leaf's response guidance.
metrics: Count of unclassified fake-recall incidents pending reclassification
Average time to reclassification
ITID-24814.notes: This is the standard 'Unclassified / General' catch-all leaf for the Fake Recall Announcements group, following the taxonomy's established intake-bucket pattern.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Fake Recall Announcement
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for a fake recall announcement about this organization that does not fit the fabricated-agency-communication, spoofed-wire, or fabricated-customer-email sub-patterns.

steps.title: Confirm no genuine recall exists and trace the fake notice's origin
steps.desc: Confirm internally (and with any regulatory agency referenced) that no genuine recall exists, and trace how the fake notice originated and spread.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no genuine recall; origin documented.
steps.abort: If a genuine recall exists, route to the real recall process instead.

steps.title: Report the fake notice to each relevant platform/host
steps.desc: Submit misinformation/impersonation reports to each platform or infrastructure provider involved.

steps.title: Follow up until the fake notice is removed
steps.desc: Track responses and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Publish an official statement confirming no recall exists
steps.desc: Issue a factual public statement through verified channels.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the fabrication method and response for reuse against future incidents.

steps.title: Assess distribution channels and reach
steps.desc: Determine every channel the fake notice has appeared on and the likely reach.

steps.title: Notify any impersonated third party
steps.desc: If a third party (agency, wire service, etc.) was impersonated, notify them directly.

ITID-24821.def: An actor orchestrates the filing of numerous fabricated consumer complaints with a regulatory body or consumer-protection organization (e.g. the Better Business Bureau, a consumer protection agency), intended to manufacture the appearance of widespread, officially-documented consumer grievance against the company.
ITID-24821.purpose: Captures a fabricated mass consumer complaint campaign filed with regulators or consumer-protection bodies to manufacture the appearance of widespread official grievance.
scopeIncludes: Coordinated filing of fabricated or exaggerated complaints with a regulator or recognized consumer-protection body
Use of fake or coerced identities to file complaints at scale
The complaints being filed through the body's official intake/case-filing process rather than posted on an open review platform
scopeExcludes: Fake complaints posted directly to an open consumer advocacy review platform rather than a formal regulatory/BBB filing process (ITID-24822)
Flooding of the company's own customer service channels directly (ITID-24823)
ITID-24821.severity: High; a spike in official regulatory/BBB case filings can trigger genuine regulatory scrutiny independent of the underlying claims' truth.
ITID-24821.priority: P1, given the risk of triggering real regulatory inquiry based on fabricated volume.
ITID-24821.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal and regulatory affairs to respond formally to the filing body; escalate to communications/PR for any public-facing narrative.
indicators: A sudden spike in formal complaint filings inconsistent with actual customer service contact volume or known issues
Filed complaints containing fabricated or templated language across multiple filers
The regulatory/BBB body itself flagging unusual filing patterns
vectors: Mass submission of complaints through official regulator/BBB online intake forms
Use of fake or coerced consumer identities to file complaints
rootCauses: No monitoring of complaint-filing volume trends with key regulatory/consumer bodies
No established rapid-response relationship with those bodies to flag anomalous filing patterns
controls: Complaint-volume trend monitoring with key regulatory/consumer-protection bodies
Established relationship with those bodies for anomaly reporting
Legal/regulatory-affairs rapid-response process
ITID-24821.detection: Relies on complaint-volume trend analysis and direct coordination with the filing body; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24821.response: Respond formally to the filing body documenting the fabrication pattern, request investigation of the anomalous filing spike, and coordinate a factual public response if the volume becomes publicly visible.
metrics: Count of fabricated mass-filing incidents per quarter
Volume of anomalous filings identified per incident
ITID-24821.notes: Scope decision: differentiated from Public Relations Disruption / Coordinated Misinformation Campaign leaves (ITID-2351x) by fabricating a specific, actionable-sounding crisis event (a formal complaint filing at scale) rather than broader narrative-shaping content; differentiated from ITID-24822 by the formal regulatory/BBB filing channel rather than an open review platform.

playbook.name: Response: Fabricated Mass Consumer Complaint Campaign (Regulatory/BBB Filing)
playbook.description: A coordinated campaign is filing fabricated or exaggerated consumer complaints against this organization with regulatory bodies or consumer-advocacy organizations (e.g. Better Business Bureau) to manufacture the appearance of widespread genuine consumer harm.

steps.title: Review the filed complaints for authenticity and coordination signatures
steps.desc: Pull the actual complaint filings (via the regulator's/BBB's response process) and cross-reference complainant details, timing, and language against customer/order records to determine whether complaints are fabricated, exaggerated, or duplicated, and whether they show signs of coordination.
steps.guidance: Some complaints in a batch may be genuine even if the campaign as a whole is manufactured — assess each on its merits rather than dismissing all of them.
steps.outcome: Documented findings distinguishing fabricated/coordinated complaints from any genuine ones.
steps.abort: If complaints substantially reflect genuine customer experiences, this is a real customer-service/quality issue, not a fabrication incident.
steps.tool: Regulator/BBB complaint response portal; CRM/order records

steps.title: Respond formally to the regulator/BBB with evidence rebutting fabricated complaints
steps.desc: Submit the organization's formal response to each complaint through the regulator's/BBB's official response process, including the evidence establishing which complaints are unsubstantiated or fabricated.

steps.title: Follow up until the regulator/BBB closes or dismisses the fabricated filings
steps.desc: Track the regulator's/BBB's determination and escalate (e.g. request formal dismissal, appeal a rating impact) as needed.
steps.outcome: Fabricated filings closed/dismissed or the organization's rating protected.

steps.title: Monitor for a renewed filing campaign
steps.desc: Watch for further coordinated filings from the same or a related source.
steps.outcome: No renewed campaign, or caught early.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the fabrication/coordination signature and resolution for reuse against future filing campaigns.

steps.title: Determine the scale and any identifiable coordinating source
steps.desc: Assess how many complaints are involved and whether a common source (e.g. a competitor, activist group, or paid campaign) can be identified.
steps.outcome: Scale documented; source identified where possible.

steps.title: Address any genuine complaints found through normal customer-service channels
steps.desc: Route any complaints found to be genuine to the appropriate customer-service/quality team for real resolution, independent of the fabrication finding for the rest.
steps.outcome: Genuine complaints resolved through standard process.

ITID-24822.def: An actor posts a fabricated or materially exaggerated complaint directly onto an open consumer advocacy or complaint-aggregation platform (e.g. a public complaints board or consumer-review site), exploiting the platform's public visibility and search-engine indexing to spread the false claim.
ITID-24822.purpose: Captures a fabricated complaint posted to an open consumer advocacy or complaint-aggregation platform, distinct from a formal regulatory filing.
scopeIncludes: A fabricated or materially exaggerated complaint posted to an open, publicly-viewable consumer advocacy/complaints platform
Complaint content designed for search-engine visibility (using the company's name/products prominently) rather than formal case resolution
Possible coordination across multiple such platforms with similar fabricated claims
scopeExcludes: Formal complaint filings with a regulator or BBB-style body through an official case-intake process (ITID-24821)
Direct flooding of the company's own customer service channels (ITID-24823)
ITID-24822.severity: Medium; primarily an SEO/visibility and trust harm rather than triggering formal regulatory process.
ITID-24822.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if the complaint ranks prominently for brand-name searches or is picked up by media.
ITID-24822.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR; request platform correction/removal where the complaint is demonstrably fabricated, and escalate to legal for clearly defamatory content.
indicators: A complaint on a public platform containing claims inconsistent with actual company records
The platform post appearing prominently in brand-name search results
No corresponding real customer/transaction record matching the complaint details
vectors: Public consumer complaint/review aggregation platforms
SEO-oriented posting to maximize search visibility of the fabricated complaint
rootCauses: No monitoring of consumer advocacy/complaint platforms for brand mentions
No established process to respond publicly to platform-posted complaints
controls: Brand/complaint-platform monitoring (social listening, SEO tracking)
Public response process for platform-posted complaints
Platform abuse-reporting relationships
ITID-24822.detection: Relies on social-listening and SEO-monitoring tools; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24822.response: Verify the claim against internal records, post a factual public response through the platform where supported, and request removal for demonstrably fabricated content.
metrics: Count of fake platform-complaint incidents per quarter
Search-ranking visibility of the fabricated complaint
ITID-24822.notes: Scope decision: differentiated from ITID-24821 by channel (open public platform vs. formal regulatory/BBB filing) and from Coordinated Misinformation Campaign leaves (ITID-2351x) by fabricating a specific, actionable-sounding complaint event rather than broad narrative content.

playbook.name: Response: Fake Complaint Posted to Consumer Advocacy Platform
playbook.description: A fake or fabricated complaint about this organization has been posted to a public consumer-advocacy platform (e.g. a complaint-board website), which typically publishes complaints with limited verification and can rank prominently in search results.

steps.title: Verify the complaint against customer/order records
steps.desc: Cross-reference the complaint's details (name, order/account reference, described interaction) against actual customer and order records to determine whether it corresponds to a real customer interaction or is fabricated.
steps.outcome: Documented determination that the complaint is fabricated (no matching record) or reflects a real, addressable customer issue.
steps.abort: If the complaint matches a real customer issue, route to customer service for genuine resolution rather than treating as fabrication.

steps.title: Submit a formal dispute/response through the platform's business-response process
steps.desc: Most consumer-advocacy platforms allow a business to formally respond to or dispute a complaint; submit evidence that no matching customer record exists.

steps.title: Follow up until the complaint is removed or a business response is prominently attached
steps.desc: Track the platform's response and escalate as needed.
steps.outcome: Complaint removed, or the organization's rebuttal prominently attached.

steps.title: Monitor for similar fabricated complaints on the same or other platforms
steps.desc: Watch for recurrence.
steps.outcome: No renewed complaint, or caught early.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the verification process and outcome for reuse against future fabricated complaints.

steps.title: Assess the complaint's visibility and search ranking impact
steps.desc: Check how prominently the complaint ranks in search results for this organization's name, since these platforms often rank highly.

steps.title: Consult legal on removal options if the platform's dispute process is insufficient
steps.desc: Where the platform does not remove clearly fabricated content, consult legal on further options (e.g. a formal legal request to the platform, or defamation options if state law applies).

ITID-24823.def: An actor coordinates a high volume of fabricated complaint submissions directly into the company's own customer service channels (phone lines, email, live chat, support tickets), intended to overwhelm operational capacity and/or manufacture internal metrics suggesting a widespread genuine issue.
ITID-24823.purpose: Captures coordinated flooding of the company's own customer service channels (phone, email, chat) with fabricated complaints, distinct from public posting.
scopeIncludes: Coordinated high-volume submission of fabricated complaints directly to company-owned customer service channels
Complaint content inconsistent with any actual product/service issue on record
Potential secondary operational-disruption effect from the volume overwhelming genuine customer service capacity
scopeExcludes: Complaints filed with an external regulator/BBB body (ITID-24821)
Complaints posted to an external public advocacy platform (ITID-24822)
A genuine surge in real customer complaints following an actual product/service failure
ITID-24823.severity: Medium-High; combines reputational fabrication with a real operational-disruption risk to customer service capacity.
ITID-24823.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the volume materially degrades service to genuine customers.
ITID-24823.escalation: Escalate to customer service operations leadership and communications/PR; escalate to IT/security if channel flooding is automated (bot-driven) rather than manually coordinated.
indicators: A sudden spike in complaint volume with fabricated or templated content across submissions
Submissions clustered in a short time window inconsistent with organic complaint patterns
No corresponding real product/service incident to explain the volume
vectors: Coordinated manual submission via phone/email/chat
Automated or scripted submission (bot-driven) of complaint forms/tickets
rootCauses: No anomaly detection on customer service channel volume/content patterns
No rate-limiting or verification controls on public-facing complaint intake forms
controls: Customer service channel volume/anomaly monitoring
Rate-limiting and basic verification on public complaint intake forms
Pre-established surge-response process for customer service operations
ITID-24823.detection: Customer service volume/pattern monitoring provides a partial operational detection signal; broader narrative verification is not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24823.response: Verify the fabricated nature of the surge, apply operational mitigations (rate-limiting, triage) to protect service to genuine customers, and issue an internal/external communication if the disruption is visible.
metrics: Count of channel-flooding incidents per quarter
Peak volume increase versus baseline
Impact on genuine customer service response times
detections: Customer service channel volume anomaly alerting
ITID-24823.notes: Scope decision: differentiated from ITID-24821/24822 by the complaints being directed at the company's own internal channels rather than an external regulator or public platform, and differentiated from a genuine customer service capacity/DDoS-style ITID by the fabricated-content dimension being primary.

playbook.name: Response: Coordinated Fake Complaint Flooding of Customer Service Channels
playbook.description: A coordinated campaign is flooding this organization's own customer-service channels (phone, chat, email, social support) with fake or fabricated complaints, aiming to overwhelm support capacity and/or manufacture the appearance of a widespread service failure.

steps.title: Confirm the complaint volume is coordinated/fabricated rather than a genuine service issue
steps.desc: Analyze incoming complaint volume, timing, and content for coordination signatures (near-identical scripts, contact patterns not matching real customer/order records, volume spikes disproportionate to any actual service disruption), while confirming there is in fact no real underlying service failure driving the volume.
steps.guidance: This step is critical — a real outage or service failure can also produce a complaint spike; do not dismiss the volume as fake without first ruling out a genuine cause.
steps.outcome: Documented determination that the flood is fabricated/coordinated, or confirmation of a genuine underlying issue (in which case route to incident/service management instead).
steps.abort: If a genuine service issue is found, treat this as an operational incident, not a fake-complaint campaign.

steps.title: Apply channel-level controls to filter or triage the fabricated volume
steps.desc: Work with the customer-service platform/operations team to apply rate-limiting, CAPTCHA, pattern-based filtering, or manual triage to separate fabricated contacts from genuine ones without degrading service to real customers.
steps.outcome: Controls applied; genuine customer contacts prioritized.

steps.title: Confirm support channel capacity and response times return to normal
steps.desc: Track channel metrics until the fabricated volume subsides and normal service levels are restored.

steps.title: Review and retain effective filtering controls for future resilience
steps.desc: Assess whether the triage/filtering controls applied should remain in place to guard against a recurrence.
steps.outcome: Controls retained or adjusted as appropriate.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection and response
steps.desc: Record the flooding signature and effective mitigations for reuse against future campaigns.

steps.title: Assess operational impact on support capacity
steps.desc: Determine the extent to which the flood is degrading response times or availability for genuine customers.

steps.title: Report the coordinated campaign to relevant platforms if it originated from or is being amplified on social/public channels
steps.desc: If the flooding is being organized or amplified via a public platform, submit a coordinated-inauthentic-behavior report there as well.

ITID-24824.def: A catch-all classification for fake customer complaint campaign activity targeting the company's reputation that does not match a more specific sibling ITID under Fake Customer Complaints, pending clearer categorization or reclassification.
ITID-24824.purpose: Intake bucket for fake customer complaint campaign activity that does not clearly fit the defined sibling leaves.
scopeIncludes: Fake complaint activity with a novel or mixed channel/mechanism not covered by the sibling leaves
Ambiguous cases pending investigation to determine the correct specific classification
scopeExcludes: Any activity clearly matching Mass Regulatory/BBB Filing (ITID-24821), Fake Advocacy Platform Complaint (ITID-24822), or Customer Service Channel Flooding (ITID-24823) — reclassify once determined
ITID-24824.severity: Assess case-by-case; default to Medium pending clarification.
ITID-24824.priority: P3 by default; re-prioritize once the specific mechanism is identified and reclassified.
ITID-24824.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR for triage; reclassify to a specific sibling ITID as soon as the mechanism is clear.
indicators: Fake complaint activity that does not cleanly match an existing sibling pattern
vectors: Varies; any fake-complaint mechanism not yet catalogued
rootCauses: Novel or hybrid attack technique not yet reflected in the taxonomy
Insufficient information at time of triage to classify precisely
controls: Brand/complaint monitoring
Triage process to reclassify into a specific sibling ITID
ITID-24824.detection: Relies on the same monitoring tooling as sibling leaves.
ITID-24824.response: Investigate to determine the specific mechanism, reclassify under the appropriate sibling ITID, and follow that leaf's response guidance.
metrics: Count of unclassified fake-complaint incidents pending reclassification
Average time to reclassification
ITID-24824.notes: This is the standard 'Unclassified / General' catch-all leaf for the Fake Customer Complaints group, following the taxonomy's established intake-bucket pattern.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Fake Customer Complaint Campaign
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for a fake customer complaint campaign against this organization that does not fit the regulatory-filing, consumer-advocacy-platform, or support-channel-flooding sub-patterns.

steps.title: Verify the complaints against genuine customer/order records
steps.desc: Cross-reference the complaints against actual customer and order records to determine whether they are fabricated or reflect real customer issues.
steps.abort: If genuine, route to customer service for real resolution.

steps.title: Submit a formal dispute/response to the relevant channel or platform
steps.desc: Submit evidence rebutting the fabricated complaints through whatever formal response process the affected channel provides.

steps.title: Follow up until the complaints are resolved, dismissed, or removed
steps.desc: Track responses and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Watch for a renewed campaign.
steps.outcome: No renewed campaign, or caught early.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record observed signatures for reuse against future incidents.

steps.title: Determine scale and channels affected
steps.desc: Catalog every channel/platform where the fake complaints have appeared.

steps.title: Consult legal where warranted
steps.desc: Consult legal on removal or other options where the platform's own dispute process is insufficient.

ITID-24831.def: An actor fabricates and circulates a claim describing a specific workplace safety incident (an injury, unsafe condition, or safety-violation event) at a named company facility, when no such incident actually occurred as described.
ITID-24831.purpose: Captures a fabricated claim asserting a specific workplace safety incident occurred at a company facility when it did not.
scopeIncludes: A fabricated claim describing a specific, actionable-sounding workplace safety incident tied to a named facility, date, or department
Fabricated supporting 'evidence' (photos, alleged internal documents, purported witness accounts) attached to the claim
The claim being specific enough to suggest a real, investigable incident occurred
scopeExcludes: Fabricated service outage/failure claims (ITID-24832)
Fabricated environmental/public health incident claims (ITID-24833)
A genuine workplace safety incident that is separately reported and investigated through normal EHS/incident-management processes
ITID-24831.severity: High; workplace safety claims can trigger regulatory (OSHA-equivalent) inquiry and internal workforce concern independent of veracity.
ITID-24831.priority: P1, given potential regulatory, legal, and employee-relations exposure.
ITID-24831.escalation: Escalate immediately to Environmental Health & Safety (EHS), legal, HR, and communications/PR to jointly verify and respond.
indicators: A specific safety-incident claim with no corresponding record in the facility's actual incident log
