Fabricated or unverifiable supporting photos/documents
No corroborating report from actual on-site employees when discreetly checked
vectors: Fabricated incident reports or photos
Anonymous social media posts or tips claiming insider knowledge of a fabricated incident
rootCauses: No rapid-verification process to cross-check external safety claims against internal EHS incident logs
No established rapid-response coordination between EHS, legal, and communications for external safety claims
controls: Cross-check process against internal EHS incident logs for any externally-reported claim
Coordinated EHS/legal/communications rapid-response process
Pre-established crisis communications playbook
ITID-24831.detection: Relies on internal record cross-checking and social-listening; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24831.response: Verify against internal EHS records within hours, issue a factual public correction if the claim is confirmed fabricated, and coordinate with regulatory affairs if any inquiry is triggered.
metrics: Count of fabricated safety-incident-claim events per quarter
Time from claim to internal verification
ITID-24831.notes: Scope decision: differentiated from sibling leaves by subject matter (workplace safety specifically) and from Coordinated Misinformation Campaign leaves (ITID-2351x) by fabricating a specific, named, actionable-sounding incident rather than broad narrative content.

playbook.name: Response: Fabricated Workplace Safety Incident Claim
playbook.description: A false claim is circulating that a serious workplace safety incident (e.g. an injury, unsafe condition) occurred at this organization's facility, when no such incident actually took place.

steps.title: Verify with EHS/facilities whether any such incident occurred
steps.desc: Check with the organization's Environmental Health & Safety and facilities/site management teams whether any incident matching the claim's description occurred at the named location and time.
steps.outcome: Documented confirmation no such incident occurred, or confirmation that a real (possibly differently characterized) incident did occur.
steps.abort: If a real safety incident did occur, this is not a fabrication case — route immediately to the organization's real incident-response/EHS process, and any public-facing correction must reflect the true facts, not a blanket denial.

steps.title: Report the false claim to platforms where it is circulating
steps.desc: Submit misinformation reports to relevant platforms with the EHS confirmation that no such incident occurred.

steps.title: Follow up until the false claim is corrected or removed across channels
steps.desc: Track platform and media responses and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Publish a factual statement confirming the true facts
steps.desc: Issue a clear, factual public statement addressing the claim, coordinated with HR/legal/communications.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the fabrication method and response for reuse against future safety-claim incidents.

steps.title: Trace the claim's origin and distribution
steps.desc: Identify where the false claim originated and how it is spreading (social media, local news, employee-relations forums).

steps.title: Coordinate with HR/legal given the sensitivity of safety claims
steps.desc: Given that safety claims can implicate employees or trigger regulatory attention (e.g. OSHA), coordinate closely with HR and legal before any public response.
steps.outcome: HR/legal engaged and aligned on response.

ITID-24832.def: An actor fabricates and circulates a claim asserting that a specific, actionable-sounding service outage, system failure, or product malfunction has occurred, when no such outage/failure is actually taking place, intended to trigger customer alarm or operational confusion.
ITID-24832.purpose: Captures a fabricated claim asserting a specific service outage or product failure occurred when it did not.
scopeIncludes: A fabricated claim of a specific service outage/product failure with no corresponding entry in actual system status/incident logs
Fabricated supporting 'evidence' (fake status-page screenshots, fabricated error messages) attached to the claim
The claim being specific and timed to maximize customer confusion or panic (e.g. during a high-traffic period)
scopeExcludes: Fabricated workplace safety incident claims (ITID-24831)
Fabricated environmental/public health incident claims (ITID-24833)

A genuine service outage/failure, even if its severity is separately exaggerated by unrelated misinformation (which would be assessed as coordinated misinformation, ITID-2351x, rather than a wholly fabricated event)
ITID-24832.severity: Medium-High; can trigger real customer support load and stock/market sensitivity for publicly-traded companies even though no actual outage exists.
ITID-24832.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the fabricated claim triggers market reaction or significant customer support surge.
ITID-24832.escalation: Escalate to IT operations (to confirm actual system status), communications/PR, and investor relations if market-sensitive.
indicators: A claimed outage/failure with no corresponding entry on the company's actual status page or monitoring systems
Fabricated screenshots inconsistent with the real product UI/status page design
Customer support volume spike driven by the fabricated claim rather than a genuine technical issue
vectors: Fabricated status-page screenshots or error messages
Social media posts falsely claiming personal experience of an outage
rootCauses: No rapid public-facing confirmation process to counter false outage claims with real-time status data
No monitoring for fabricated status-page/error-message imagery circulating online
controls: Real-time public status page as an authoritative rapid-rebuttal source
IT operations coordination for rapid status confirmation
Pre-established crisis communications playbook
ITID-24832.detection: IT operations' actual monitoring/status systems provide a fast, authoritative rebuttal source; the fabrication detection itself relies on social listening, not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24832.response: Confirm actual system status immediately via IT operations, publish a rapid public correction directing customers to the authoritative status page, and coordinate with investor relations if market-sensitive.
metrics: Count of fabricated outage-claim incidents per quarter
Time from claim to public correction via status page
ITID-24832.notes: Scope decision: differentiated from sibling leaves by subject matter (service/product technical failure specifically) and from general Coordinated Misinformation Campaign leaves (ITID-2351x) by fabricating a specific, actionable-sounding outage event rather than broad narrative content.

playbook.name: Response: Fabricated Service Outage/Failure Claim
playbook.description: A false claim is circulating that this organization's service or product suffered a major outage or failure, when no such outage or failure actually occurred.

steps.title: Verify with engineering/operations whether any outage or failure occurred
steps.desc: Check service-status dashboards, monitoring/alerting systems, and the engineering/operations team's incident log for the claimed time window to confirm whether any actual outage or failure occurred.
steps.outcome: Documented confirmation no such outage occurred, or confirmation a real (possibly smaller-scale) issue did occur.
steps.abort: If a real outage did occur, this is not a fabrication case — route to the organization's real incident-response process, and any correction must reflect the true scope rather than a blanket denial.

steps.title: Report the false claim to platforms where it is circulating
steps.desc: Submit misinformation reports with the monitoring-data confirmation to relevant platforms.

steps.title: Follow up until the false claim is corrected or removed across channels
steps.desc: Track platform and media responses and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Publish the factual status statement
steps.desc: Release the prepared statement through the organization's status page and communications channels.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the fabrication method and response for reuse against future outage-claim incidents.

steps.title: Trace the claim's origin and distribution
steps.desc: Identify where the false claim originated and how it is spreading (social media, tech press, forums).

steps.title: Prepare a factual status statement
steps.desc: Have communications/engineering prepare a clear factual statement citing actual service-status data.

ITID-24833.def: An actor fabricates and circulates a claim describing a specific, actionable-sounding environmental incident (e.g. a spill, contamination, emissions violation) or public health incident (e.g. a contamination or illness outbreak) attributed to the company, when no such incident actually occurred as described.
ITID-24833.purpose: Captures a fabricated claim asserting a specific environmental or public health incident tied to the company occurred when it did not.
scopeIncludes: A fabricated claim describing a specific environmental or public health incident tied to a named facility, product, or location
Fabricated supporting 'evidence' (photos, purported test results, alleged internal reports) attached to the claim
The claim being specific enough to suggest a real, investigable incident (a location, date, substance, or affected population)
scopeExcludes: Fabricated workplace safety incident claims (ITID-24831)
Fabricated service outage/failure claims (ITID-24832)
A genuine environmental/public health incident reported and investigated through normal environmental compliance/regulatory processes
ITID-24833.severity: High; environmental/public health claims can trigger regulatory inquiry, public health authority involvement, and significant public alarm independent of veracity.
ITID-24833.priority: P1, given potential regulatory, public health, and legal exposure.
ITID-24833.escalation: Escalate immediately to environmental compliance/EHS, legal, regulatory affairs, and communications/PR to jointly verify and respond; loop in public health authorities proactively if the claim has public traction.
indicators: A specific environmental/health-incident claim with no corresponding record in actual environmental monitoring/compliance logs
Fabricated or unverifiable test results, photos, or documents
No corroborating reports from regulatory bodies or affected communities when checked
vectors: Fabricated test results, lab reports, or environmental monitoring data
Fabricated photos of alleged spills/contamination
Anonymous claims of insider knowledge
rootCauses: No rapid-verification process to cross-check external environmental/health claims against actual compliance monitoring data
No established rapid-response coordination between environmental compliance, regulatory affairs, and communications
controls: Cross-check process against actual environmental monitoring/compliance records
Coordinated environmental compliance/regulatory affairs/communications rapid-response process
Pre-established crisis communications playbook
ITID-24833.detection: Relies on internal compliance-record cross-checking and social listening; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24833.response: Verify against actual environmental/compliance monitoring data promptly, issue a factual public correction with supporting data if the claim is confirmed fabricated, and proactively engage regulators/public health authorities where the claim has gained public traction.
metrics: Count of fabricated environmental/health incident-claim events per quarter
Time from claim to internal verification
ITID-24833.notes: Scope decision: differentiated from sibling leaves by subject matter (environmental/public health specifically) and from Coordinated Misinformation Campaign leaves (ITID-2351x) by fabricating a specific, named, actionable-sounding incident rather than broad narrative content.

playbook.name: Response: Fabricated Environmental/Public Health Incident Claim
playbook.description: A false claim is circulating that this organization caused an environmental or public health incident (e.g. a contamination, spill, or hazard), when no such incident actually occurred.

steps.title: Verify with EHS/compliance and, where relevant, external testing whether any incident occurred
steps.desc: Check with the organization's Environmental Health & Safety/compliance team and, where feasible, commission independent testing or data review relevant to the specific claim (e.g. water/air/soil testing) to confirm whether the claimed environmental or health impact actually occurred.
steps.guidance: Given the public-health sensitivity, prioritize speed but do not skip independent verification — a rushed denial that is later contradicted by real data would cause far greater damage.
steps.outcome: Documented, ideally independently verifiable, confirmation no such incident occurred, or confirmation a real incident did occur.
steps.abort: If a real environmental/health incident did occur, this is not a fabrication case — route immediately to the organization's real environmental-incident/crisis-response process and regulatory-notification obligations.

steps.title: Report the false claim to platforms and notify relevant regulators proactively
steps.desc: Submit misinformation reports to platforms, and proactively notify any relevant environmental/health regulator of the false claim and the verification evidence, to get ahead of a regulatory inquiry.
steps.outcome: Reports submitted; regulator notified where applicable.
steps.tool: Platform misinformation reporting channel; regulator contact

steps.title: Follow up until the false claim is corrected or removed across channels
steps.desc: Track platform, media, and regulatory responses and escalate as needed.
steps.outcome: False claim corrected or removed; regulatory concern resolved.

steps.title: Publish the verified factual findings publicly
steps.desc: Release the independent verification results (or a summary) publicly to reassure the community and stakeholders.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection and response readiness
steps.desc: Record the verification process, regulatory coordination, and outcome for reuse against future environmental/health claim incidents.

steps.title: Trace the claim's origin and assess regulatory/media attention
steps.desc: Identify where the claim originated and whether it has drawn attention from regulators, media, or advocacy groups.

steps.title: Coordinate a unified legal/communications response given the reputational and regulatory stakes
steps.desc: Given the potential regulatory and public-health stakes, ensure legal and communications jointly review and approve all public statements before release.
steps.outcome: Legal/communications alignment achieved before any public statement.

ITID-24834.def: A catch-all classification for coordinated fabricated incident-claim activity targeting the company's reputation that does not match a more specific sibling ITID under Coordinated Incident Claims, pending clearer categorization or reclassification.
ITID-24834.purpose: Intake bucket for coordinated fabricated incident-claim activity that does not clearly fit the defined sibling leaves.
scopeIncludes: Fabricated incident-claim activity with a novel subject matter not covered by the sibling leaves (e.g. not safety, service, or environmental/health)
Ambiguous cases pending investigation to determine the correct specific classification
scopeExcludes: Any activity clearly matching Fabricated Workplace Safety Incident Claim (ITID-24831), Fabricated Service Outage/Failure Claim (ITID-24832), or Fabricated Environmental/Public Health Incident Claim (ITID-24833) — reclassify once determined
ITID-24834.severity: Assess case-by-case; default to Medium-High pending clarification given the general severity of fabricated incident claims.
ITID-24834.priority: P2 by default; re-prioritize once the specific mechanism/subject matter is identified and reclassified.
ITID-24834.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR and legal for triage; reclassify to a specific sibling ITID as soon as the subject matter is clear.
indicators: Fabricated incident-claim activity that does not cleanly match an existing sibling subject-matter pattern
vectors: Varies; any fabricated-incident-claim mechanism not yet catalogued
rootCauses: Novel or hybrid attack technique not yet reflected in the taxonomy
Insufficient information at time of triage to classify precisely
controls: Brand/incident-claim monitoring
Triage process to reclassify into a specific sibling ITID
ITID-24834.detection: Relies on the same monitoring tooling as sibling leaves.
ITID-24834.response: Investigate to determine the specific subject matter and mechanism, reclassify under the appropriate sibling ITID, and follow that leaf's response guidance.
metrics: Count of unclassified fabricated-incident-claim events pending reclassification
Average time to reclassification
ITID-24834.notes: This is the standard 'Unclassified / General' catch-all leaf for the Coordinated Incident Claims group, following the taxonomy's established intake-bucket pattern.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Coordinated Incident Claim
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for a fabricated crisis-style incident claim about this organization that does not fit the workplace-safety, service-outage, or environmental/public-health sub-patterns.

steps.title: Verify with the relevant internal team whether any such incident occurred
steps.desc: Check with the appropriate internal function (operations, HR, facilities, etc., depending on the claim's subject matter) to confirm whether the claimed incident actually occurred.
steps.outcome: Documented confirmation of whether the incident occurred.
steps.abort: If a real incident occurred, route to the organization's real incident-response process for that domain.

steps.title: Report the false claim to platforms where it is circulating
steps.desc: Submit misinformation reports with supporting verification evidence.

steps.title: Follow up until the false claim is corrected or removed
steps.desc: Track responses and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Publish a factual statement
steps.desc: Release a clear factual correction through official channels.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the fabrication method and response for reuse against future incidents.

steps.title: Trace the claim's origin and distribution
steps.desc: Identify where the claim originated and how it is spreading.

steps.title: Coordinate with the relevant internal function and legal before any public statement
steps.desc: Ensure the subject-matter team and legal review and approve any public response.

ITID-24911.def: A campaign, assessed with reasonable confidence to be sponsored or directed by a nation-state actor, that fabricates and disseminates false narratives about the company specifically tailored to and distributed within a particular country or region, typically tied to the company's market presence, geopolitical tensions, or local regulatory interests in that region.
ITID-24911.purpose: Captures a state-sponsored disinformation campaign specifically targeting the company's reputation within a particular country or region.
scopeIncludes: Disinformation content specifically tailored to and distributed within a defined country/region's media and social ecosystem
Attribution indicators consistent with state-sponsored origin (e.g. known state media amplification, linked influence-operation infrastructure)
Content tied to the company's specific market presence, operations, or geopolitical positioning in that region
scopeExcludes: General, non-region-specific state-sponsored disinformation (ITID-23512, State-Sponsored Disinformation Campaign, under Public Relations Disruption) — this leaf is scoped specifically to campaigns tailored to and distributed within a defined region/market
Locally-driven competitor attacks without state involvement (ITID-24912)
Campaigns primarily targeting regional regulators/politicians rather than the general public (ITID-24913)
ITID-24911.severity: High; state-sponsored campaigns typically bring greater resourcing, sophistication, and persistence than other actor types.
ITID-24911.priority: P1, given the resourcing and persistence typically associated with state-sponsored operations.
ITID-24911.escalation: Escalate immediately to communications/PR, legal, government affairs, and executive leadership given the geopolitical dimension; consider coordination with threat intelligence and, where appropriate, government partners.
indicators: Coordinated amplification via known or suspected state-linked media/social accounts
Narrative content aligned with the sponsoring state's broader geopolitical interests regarding the company's market or industry
Distribution concentrated in the target region's language and platforms
vectors: State-linked media outlets and social media amplification networks
Region-specific social platforms and messaging apps
rootCauses: Limited regional threat-intelligence/monitoring coverage in high-risk markets
No established government-affairs relationship in the region to support rapid response
controls: Regional social-listening/threat-intelligence monitoring
Government affairs relationship in key regional markets
Pre-established multi-region crisis communications playbook
ITID-24911.detection: Relies on regional social-listening and threat-intelligence sources for attribution; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24911.response: Coordinate a region-appropriate factual response through local channels, engage government affairs where geopolitically sensitive, and avoid response actions that could inadvertently escalate the geopolitical dimension.
metrics: Count of state-sponsored regional disinformation incidents per quarter
Number of regions actively monitored for this pattern
ITID-24911.notes: Scope decision: differentiated from ITID-23512 (general, non-region-specific state-sponsored disinformation under Public Relations Disruption) by requiring content specifically tailored to and distributed within a defined region tied to the company's market/geopolitical presence there; general state-sponsored disinformation without this regional-targeting specificity should remain classified under ITID-23512.

playbook.name: Response: State-Sponsored Regional Disinformation Campaign
playbook.description: A disinformation campaign targeting this organization's reputation in a specific region shows indicators of state sponsorship (e.g. coordination consistent with known state-linked influence operations, geopolitical motive).

steps.title: Confirm the claims are false in the actual regional/cultural context
steps.desc: Have native-language speakers and regional subject-matter reviewers assess the claims in their full local context to confirm they are factually false or materially misleading, rather than a genuine cultural or political grievance expressed in unfamiliar terms.
steps.guidance: This verification step is essential before escalating a claim of state-sponsored disinformation, given the geopolitical sensitivity of the assertion.
steps.outcome: Documented, regionally-informed confirmation the claims are false, or a determination that a genuine underlying grievance exists.
steps.abort: If the underlying concern is genuine, treat this as a legitimate regional issue to be addressed on its merits, not a disinformation incident.

steps.title: Route the response through the region-specific PR/legal team
steps.desc: Engage the organization's region-specific PR and legal teams to lead the response, rather than routing through a single global process — regional context, language, and regulatory considerations differ materially.
steps.outcome: Regional team engaged and leading response.

steps.title: Follow up until platforms take enforcement action
steps.desc: Track platform responses and escalate as needed, coordinating with the regional team on any local regulatory engagement.

steps.title: Publish a regionally-appropriate factual correction
steps.desc: Have the regional PR team publish a correction in the local language and cultural context, rather than a translated global statement.

steps.title: Document the campaign and regional response for faster future handling
steps.desc: Record the disinformation pattern, indicators, and the regional response process for reuse against future campaigns in this or other regions.

steps.title: Assess and document indicators consistent with state sponsorship
steps.desc: Gather indicators (coordination pattern, infrastructure, narrative alignment with known state interests) suggesting state involvement, without overstating attribution confidence.
steps.guidance: Attribution to a specific state actor is difficult and sensitive — document indicators and confidence level honestly rather than asserting certainty.
steps.outcome: Documented indicators and an honest confidence assessment.

steps.title: Report the campaign to platforms' coordinated-inauthentic-behavior / state-actor teams
steps.desc: Submit a report to each affected platform's dedicated team for state-linked influence operations, where such a channel exists, in addition to standard misinformation reporting.

ITID-24912.def: A local or regional competitor, operating without state sponsorship, fabricates and disseminates false or misleading narratives about the company specifically within a defined regional market, exploiting local market conditions, cultural context, or competitive positioning to damage the company's regional standing.
ITID-24912.purpose: Captures a regional reputation attack driven by a local competitor exploiting regional market dynamics, distinct from state-sponsored activity.
scopeIncludes: Disinformation/misleading content specifically tailored to a defined regional market, attributable or reasonably suspected to originate from a local competitor
Content exploiting local market conditions, competitive dynamics, or the company's specific regional entry/expansion
Evidence connecting the campaign to a specific competitor's regional interests
scopeExcludes: State-sponsored regional disinformation (ITID-24911)
Campaigns targeting regional regulators/politicians rather than the general regional market (ITID-24913)

Generic Competitor-Sponsored Misinformation Campaign (ITID-23513) with no defined regional targeting — this leaf is scoped specifically to competitor attacks tailored to and distributed within a defined regional market
ITID-24912.severity: Medium-High; can directly affect regional market share and customer trust.
ITID-24912.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for campaigns materially affecting regional revenue or a strategically important market entry.
ITID-24912.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR, regional business leadership, and legal (for potential unfair-competition or defamation claims against the competitor).
indicators: Misleading claims specifically tailored to the regional market appearing shortly after a competitive event (product launch, market entry, pricing change)
Content traceable to accounts, agencies, or infrastructure linked to a known local competitor
Narrative themes closely mirroring the competitor's own marketing positioning
vectors: Regional social media and local media outlets
Local influencer or PR agency networks engaged by the competitor
rootCauses: Limited regional competitive-intelligence/brand monitoring
No established legal relationship/process for pursuing unfair-competition claims in the region
controls: Regional brand and competitive-intelligence monitoring
Legal process for unfair-competition/defamation claims
Regional crisis communications playbook
ITID-24912.detection: Relies on regional social-listening and competitive-intelligence monitoring; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24912.response: Verify the competitor linkage with evidence, respond with a factual regional correction, and pursue legal action for unfair competition or defamation where warranted.
metrics: Count of competitor-driven regional attack incidents per quarter
Estimated regional market impact
ITID-24912.notes: Scope decision: differentiated from the generic Competitor-Sponsored Misinformation Campaign (ITID-23513) by requiring content specifically tailored to and distributed within a defined regional market, and from ITID-24911 by the absence of state sponsorship.

playbook.name: Response: Local Competitor-Driven Regional Reputation Attack
playbook.description: A local or regional competitor is driving a reputation attack against this organization within a specific regional market, exploiting local context this organization's global teams may not fully understand.

steps.title: Confirm the claim is false within the actual regional/cultural and competitive context
steps.desc: Have native-language, in-region reviewers assess the claims in local market context to confirm they are factually false or misleading, rather than a legitimate local competitive or regulatory point.
steps.outcome: Documented, regionally-informed confirmation of falsity, or a determination the concern is legitimate.
steps.abort: If the concern is legitimate, address it as a genuine local market issue rather than an attack.

steps.title: Route the response through the region-specific PR/legal team
steps.desc: Have the regional team lead the response given their familiarity with local platforms, media, and regulatory norms.
steps.outcome: Regional team engaged and leading response.

steps.title: Follow up until local platforms/outlets take action
steps.desc: Track responses and escalate through local legal channels if warranted (e.g. unfair-competition law where applicable in the region).

steps.title: Publish a regionally-appropriate factual correction
steps.desc: Have the regional team publish a correction tailored to the local market and language.

steps.title: Document the regional competitive pattern for faster future handling
steps.desc: Record the competitor, tactic, and regional response for reuse against future local attacks.

steps.title: Identify the competitor and assess the local competitive dynamics at play
steps.desc: Determine the likely local competitor source and understand the local market dynamics motivating the attack.

steps.title: Report the false claims to relevant local platforms
steps.desc: Submit misinformation/unfair-competition reports to the platforms and outlets local to the affected market.

ITID-24913.def: A campaign that fabricates or disseminates misleading narratives about the company specifically targeted at regional regulators, legislators, or political figures, intended to influence a pending regulatory decision, policy outcome, or political relationship affecting the company's operations in that region.
ITID-24913.purpose: Captures a regional reputation attack specifically aimed at influencing local regulators or political figures rather than the general public.
scopeIncludes: Misleading content specifically crafted for or delivered to regional regulatory/political audiences (e.g. targeted lobbying-adjacent misinformation, briefing materials, or letters to officials)
Timing tied to a specific pending regulatory decision, hearing, or legislative action affecting the company
Distribution channels aimed at officials and policy-influencers rather than the general public
scopeExcludes: Broad, public-facing regional disinformation aimed at consumers/the general public (ITID-24911/24912)
Legitimate, transparent lobbying or advocacy activity by competitors or advocacy groups presenting accurate information unfavorable to the company (not an incident)
ITID-24913.severity: High; a successful regulatory/political targeting campaign can directly affect the company's license to operate in the region.
ITID-24913.priority: P1, given direct regulatory/operational risk to the region's business.
ITID-24913.escalation: Escalate immediately to government affairs, regulatory affairs, legal, and executive leadership given the direct policy/regulatory stakes.
indicators: Misleading materials specifically circulating among regulators/legislators ahead of a relevant decision
Officials referencing fabricated or unverifiable claims in public statements or hearings
Timing closely aligned with a specific regulatory or legislative milestone
vectors: Targeted briefing materials or letters sent directly to officials
Coordinated op-eds or testimony citing fabricated claims
Astroturfed public comment submissions to regulatory dockets
rootCauses: No established government-affairs monitoring of regulatory/political narratives about the company in the region
No rapid-rebuttal relationship with key regional officials/regulatory bodies
controls: Government affairs monitoring of regional regulatory/political narratives
Established relationship with key regional officials/regulatory bodies for rapid rebuttal
Legal review of factual claims made in regulatory proceedings
ITID-24913.detection: Relies on government-affairs monitoring and direct relationships; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24913.response: Provide regulators/officials with factual rebuttal documentation promptly, coordinate a formal response through government affairs and legal channels, and correct the record in any relevant regulatory proceeding.
metrics: Count of regulatory/political targeting incidents per quarter
Regulatory/legislative outcomes potentially affected
ITID-24913.notes: Scope decision: differentiated from ITID-24911/24912 by audience — targeted at regulators/political figures specifically, rather than the general public — reflecting a distinct response pathway (government affairs) rather than public communications.

playbook.name: Response: Regional Regulatory/Political Targeting Campaign
playbook.description: A reputation attack against this organization within a specific region is being driven or amplified by regulatory or political actors, raising the stakes and complexity beyond a typical consumer-facing dispute.

steps.title: Confirm the underlying claims are false within the actual regional/political context
steps.desc: Have native-language, in-region reviewers and, where relevant, local regulatory-affairs staff assess the claims to confirm they are factually false or misleading, rather than a legitimate regulatory concern or genuine political critique.
steps.guidance: Distinguishing a bad-faith political attack from a legitimate regulatory concern is critical — treating a genuine regulatory issue as a mere reputation attack would be a serious misstep.
steps.outcome: Documented, regionally-informed confirmation of falsity, or a determination that a genuine regulatory/political concern exists.
steps.abort: If the concern is legitimate, route to regulatory-affairs/legal for a substantive response rather than treating this as a reputation-attack incident.

steps.title: Route the response through the region-specific PR/legal/government-affairs team
steps.desc: Given the political/regulatory dimension, ensure the region's government-affairs function leads or closely co-leads the response alongside regional PR/legal.
steps.outcome: Regional government-affairs, PR, and legal teams engaged and aligned.

steps.title: Pursue resolution through the appropriate regulatory/diplomatic channel
steps.desc: Work through the region's regulatory or, where applicable, diplomatic/industry-association channels to address the false claims at their source.
steps.outcome: Matter addressed through the appropriate formal channel.

steps.title: Publish a regionally and politically calibrated factual statement
steps.desc: Have the regional team, with government-affairs input, publish a carefully calibrated factual correction appropriate to the local political context.

steps.title: Document the case for faster future handling of regulatory/political targeting
steps.desc: Record the actors, tactics, and response for reuse against future regulatory/political campaigns in this or other regions.

steps.title: Assess the political/regulatory actors involved and the stakes
steps.desc: Identify who is driving the campaign (political figure, party, regulator, aligned media) and assess the potential regulatory or political consequences.

steps.title: Report clearly false claims to relevant local platforms while avoiding actions that could be seen as suppressing legitimate political speech
steps.desc: Submit misinformation reports only for claims established as factually false, taking care not to over-report legitimate political criticism, which could itself become a reputational issue.

ITID-24914.def: A catch-all classification for region-specific reputation campaign activity that does not match a more specific sibling ITID under Region-Specific Campaigns, pending clearer categorization or reclassification.
ITID-24914.purpose: Intake bucket for region-specific reputation campaign activity that does not clearly fit the defined sibling leaves.
scopeIncludes: Region-specific reputation attacks with an unclear or mixed actor type/target audience not covered by the sibling leaves
Ambiguous cases pending investigation to determine the correct specific classification
scopeExcludes: Any activity clearly matching State-Sponsored Regional Disinformation (ITID-24911), Local Competitor-Driven Attack (ITID-24912), or Regulatory/Political Targeting (ITID-24913) — reclassify once determined
ITID-24914.severity: Assess case-by-case; default to Medium pending clarification.
ITID-24914.priority: P3 by default; re-prioritize once the specific actor type and target audience are identified and reclassified.
ITID-24914.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR and regional business leadership for triage; reclassify to a specific sibling ITID as soon as the mechanism is clear.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Region-Specific Reputation Campaign
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for a region-specific reputation attack against this organization that does not fit the state-sponsored, local-competitor, or regulatory/political-targeting sub-patterns.

steps.title: Confirm the claims are false within the actual regional/cultural context
steps.desc: Have native-language, in-region reviewers assess the claims in local context to confirm they are factually false, rather than a genuine local concern.
steps.outcome: Documented, regionally-informed confirmation of falsity, or a determination the concern is legitimate.
steps.abort: If legitimate, address as a genuine regional issue rather than an attack.

steps.title: Route the response through the region-specific PR/legal team
steps.desc: Have the regional team lead the response given local familiarity with platforms, media, and norms.
steps.outcome: Regional team engaged and leading response.

steps.title: Follow up until local platforms/outlets take action
steps.desc: Track responses and escalate through local legal channels if warranted.

steps.title: Publish a regionally-appropriate factual correction
steps.desc: Have the regional team publish a correction tailored to the local market and language.

steps.title: Document the pattern for faster future handling
steps.desc: Record the tactic and regional response for reuse against future campaigns.

steps.title: Identify the likely source and scale of the campaign
steps.desc: Determine who is behind the campaign and how widely it has spread.

steps.title: Report the false claims to relevant local platforms

ITID-24921.def: An actor fabricates or materially distorts a claim that the company, its products, marketing, or representatives displayed cultural insensitivity or gave offense within a specific cultural context, in order to provoke public backlash within that market or community.
ITID-24921.purpose: Captures a fabricated claim that the company acted with cultural insensitivity or gave offense in a specific market, when the underlying claim is false or materially distorted.
scopeIncludes: A fabricated or materially distorted claim of cultural insensitivity with no basis, or a distorted basis, in the company's actual conduct/materials
Claims specifically tied to cultural norms, symbols, or sensitivities of a defined community or market
Deliberate mischaracterization of legitimate company content as culturally offensive
scopeExcludes: Fabricated religious offense claims specifically (ITID-24922)
A genuine cultural misstep by the company (an actual product/marketing decision needing a real corporate response, not a fabrication incident)
Deliberately mistranslated official statements as the primary mechanism (ITID-24931)
ITID-24921.severity: Medium-High; cultural offense claims can spread rapidly within tightly-networked communities before verification.
ITID-24921.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for claims gaining rapid traction within an economically or strategically important market.
ITID-24921.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR (with regional/cultural expertise) and legal; engage local cultural consultants to assess and respond appropriately.
indicators: A claim of cultural offense inconsistent with the company's actual published materials/conduct when checked against the original source
Rapid amplification within a specific cultural or linguistic community
The claim relying on a mistranslated, cropped, or decontextualized version of the original content
vectors: Selective/mistranslated excerpting of company marketing or statements
Fabricated screenshots or claims with no locatable original source
rootCauses: No proactive review of marketing/communications for cultural sensitivity in each target market
No established local cultural-consultant relationship for rapid, credible response
controls: Cultural-sensitivity review process for market-specific marketing/communications
Local cultural-consultant relationships for rapid response
Pre-established crisis communications playbook with regional variants
ITID-24921.detection: Relies on regional social-listening and direct verification against original source materials; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24921.response: Verify against the original source materials, engage local cultural expertise to craft a culturally appropriate factual correction, and issue the correction through channels trusted within that community.
metrics: Count of fabricated cultural-offense-claim incidents per quarter
Time from detection to culturally-appropriate correction
ITID-24921.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies. Differentiated from ITID-24922 (religious offense specifically) and from ITID-24931 (mistranslation as the primary mechanism) by scope: general cultural-norm-based offense claims not centered on religion or translation distortion.

playbook.name: Response: Fabricated Cultural Insensitivity/Offense Claim
playbook.description: A claim is circulating that this organization committed a cultural insensitivity or offense in a specific region, when the underlying content or action was not, in fact, culturally offensive or was misrepresented.

steps.title: Obtain native-language, in-culture review to confirm whether the claim is a genuine misstep or a false/exaggerated claim
steps.desc: Have native-language speakers with genuine cultural fluency in the specific region and context review the original content/action and the claim against it, to determine honestly whether a real cultural misstep occurred or whether the offense claim is fabricated, exaggerated, or misrepresents the original context.
steps.guidance: This is the single most important step — an organization that dismisses a genuine cultural misstep as a 'fake claim' will compound the damage severely. Be rigorous and honest here before proceeding.
steps.outcome: A documented, culturally-informed, honest determination of whether the claim is genuine or false.
steps.abort: If a genuine cultural misstep did occur, this is not a security incident — route to communications/regional leadership for a sincere, appropriate response and corrective action, not a defensive rebuttal.

steps.title: Route the response through the region-specific PR/legal team
steps.desc: Have the regional team, with the cultural review findings, lead the response.
steps.outcome: Regional team engaged and leading response.

steps.title: Follow up until the false claim is corrected or removed
steps.desc: Track responses and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Publish a culturally-informed, regionally-appropriate factual correction
steps.desc: Have the regional team, with cultural review input, publish a correction that is sensitive to local context and does not come across as dismissive.

steps.title: Document the case, including the cultural review process, for faster future handling
steps.desc: Record the claim, the cultural verification process, and the outcome for reuse and to sharpen future cultural-context review capability.

steps.title: Trace the false claim's origin and spread, if confirmed false
steps.desc: Once genuinely confirmed false, identify where the claim originated and how it is spreading.

steps.title: Report the confirmed-false claim to relevant platforms
steps.desc: Submit misinformation reports to platforms where the false claim is circulating, referencing the cultural review findings.

ITID-24922.def: An actor fabricates or materially distorts a claim that the company, its products, marketing, or representatives displayed religious insensitivity or gave offense to a specific faith community, in order to provoke public backlash within that community.
ITID-24922.purpose: Captures a fabricated claim that the company acted with religious insensitivity or gave religious offense, when the underlying claim is false or materially distorted.
scopeIncludes: A fabricated or materially distorted claim of religious offense with no basis, or a distorted basis, in the company's actual conduct/materials
Claims specifically tied to the practices, symbols, or sensitivities of a defined faith community
Deliberate mischaracterization of legitimate company content as religiously offensive
scopeExcludes: General (non-religious) fabricated cultural insensitivity claims (ITID-24921)
A genuine religious-sensitivity misstep by the company requiring a real corporate response (not a fabrication incident)
ITID-24922.severity: High; religious offense claims carry heightened potential for rapid, intense, and sometimes safety-relevant backlash.
ITID-24922.priority: P1, given the elevated intensity and safety considerations often associated with religious offense controversies.
ITID-24922.escalation: Escalate immediately to communications/PR, legal, security (for any safety-relevant escalation risk to personnel/facilities in the affected market), and local religious/cultural advisors.
indicators: A claim of religious offense inconsistent with the company's actual published materials/conduct when checked against the original source
Rapid, intense amplification within a specific faith community's networks
Calls for boycotts or protests referencing the fabricated claim
vectors: Selective/mistranslated excerpting of company marketing or statements
Fabricated screenshots or claims with no locatable original source
rootCauses: No proactive religious-sensitivity review of marketing/communications for markets with significant faith-community presence
No established relationship with local religious/community leaders for rapid, credible response
controls: Religious-sensitivity review process for market-specific marketing/communications
Local religious/community leader relationships for rapid response
Physical security coordination for any safety-relevant escalation
Pre-established crisis communications playbook with regional variants
ITID-24922.detection: Relies on regional social-listening and direct verification against original source materials; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24922.response: Verify against the original source materials immediately, engage local religious/community leaders to craft a respectful and factual correction, coordinate with physical security if any safety escalation risk is present, and issue the correction promptly.
metrics: Count of fabricated religious-offense-claim incidents per quarter
Time from detection to respectful, factual correction
ITID-24922.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies. Differentiated from ITID-24921 by the specific subject matter of religious (rather than general cultural) offense, given its distinct escalation profile and potential safety dimension.

playbook.name: Response: Fabricated Religious Offense Claim
playbook.description: A claim is circulating that this organization committed a religious offense in a specific region or community, when the underlying content or action did not, in fact, constitute a genuine religious offense or has been misrepresented.

steps.title: Obtain review from individuals with genuine religious/cultural expertise to confirm whether the claim is genuine or false
steps.desc: Have reviewers with authentic expertise in the specific religious tradition and regional context assess the original content/action and the claim against it, to make an honest determination of whether a genuine religious offense occurred or the claim is fabricated or exaggerated.
steps.guidance: Religious-offense claims carry particularly high stakes and sensitivity; move deliberately and involve genuinely qualified reviewers rather than assuming the claim is false.
steps.outcome: A documented, expert-informed, honest determination of whether the claim is genuine or false.
steps.abort: If a genuine offense did occur, this is not a security incident — route to communications/regional leadership for a sincere, appropriate response, not a defensive rebuttal.

steps.title: Route the response through the region-specific PR/legal team with expert input
steps.desc: Have the regional team lead the response, incorporating the expert review findings and exercising particular care given the sensitivity.
steps.outcome: Regional team engaged and leading a carefully calibrated response.

steps.title: Follow up until the false claim is corrected or removed
steps.desc: Track responses and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Publish a carefully-calibrated, expert-reviewed factual correction
steps.desc: Have the regional team publish a correction reviewed by the religious/cultural expert to ensure it is respectful and accurate.

steps.title: Document the case, including the expert review process, for faster future handling
steps.desc: Record the claim, the verification process, and the outcome for reuse and to strengthen future response readiness for religious-sensitivity claims.

steps.title: Trace the false claim's origin and spread, if confirmed false
steps.desc: Once genuinely confirmed false, identify where the claim originated and how it is spreading.

steps.title: Report the confirmed-false claim to relevant platforms
steps.desc: Submit misinformation reports to platforms where the false claim is circulating.

ITID-24923.def: An actor misrepresents or fabricates claims about how the company conducts business in a specific local market (e.g. labor practices, supplier relationships, pricing, or local partnership arrangements), framing legitimate or misunderstood practices as exploitative, unethical, or non-compliant with local norms/law.
ITID-24923.purpose: Captures a misrepresentation of the company's local business practices in a specific market, framed to appear as exploitative, unethical, or non-compliant conduct.
scopeIncludes: Claims mischaracterizing an actual, legitimate local business practice as exploitative or non-compliant
Fabricated claims about business practices with no basis in the company's actual local operations
Content exploiting local cultural expectations around fair business conduct to maximize outrage
scopeExcludes: Fabricated cultural insensitivity claims not tied to business practices specifically (ITID-24921)
Fabricated religious offense claims (ITID-24922)
A genuine local business-practice failing requiring real corporate remediation (a compliance/ethics matter, not a fabrication incident)
ITID-24923.severity: Medium-High; claims touching on labor or ethics can trigger both consumer backlash and regulatory/NGO scrutiny.
ITID-24923.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the claim triggers formal regulatory, NGO, or investor (ESG) scrutiny.
ITID-24923.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR, legal, compliance/ethics, and investor relations (given potential ESG scrutiny); engage local business/legal expertise to verify actual practices.
indicators: A claim about local business practices inconsistent with the company's actual documented practices/contracts when checked
The claim citing practices not reflected in actual supplier/labor audit records
Amplification by local advocacy groups or media based on the unverified claim
vectors: Fabricated or selectively-edited claims about labor/supplier practices
Misrepresented pricing or partnership terms presented without accurate context
rootCauses: No readily accessible, verifiable public record of actual local business practices/compliance audits
No established local compliance/legal relationship to rapidly verify and rebut claims
controls: Maintained, verifiable public record of compliance/audit practices in key markets
Local compliance/legal relationship for rapid claim verification
Pre-established crisis communications playbook with ESG/investor-relations coordination
ITID-24923.detection: Relies on regional social-listening and internal compliance-record verification; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24923.response: Verify the claim against actual compliance/audit records, publish a factual correction with supporting documentation, and coordinate with investor relations if ESG scrutiny results.
metrics: Count of misrepresented-business-practice-claim incidents per quarter
Time from detection to documented correction
ITID-24923.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies. Differentiated from ITID-24921/24922 by subject matter: business-practice/ethics claims specifically, rather than general cultural or religious offense.

playbook.name: Response: Misrepresented Local Business Practice Claim
playbook.description: A claim is circulating that this organization's local business practices in a specific region are improper or offensive, when the practices have in fact been misrepresented or taken out of local context.

steps.title: Have local business/legal experts assess whether the practice is genuinely improper or has been misrepresented
steps.desc: Have in-region business and legal/compliance staff review the actual practice against the claim, and against local law, custom, and industry norms, to make an honest determination of whether the practice is genuinely improper or the claim misrepresents it.
steps.guidance: Business-practice claims sometimes reveal a genuine compliance or cultural-fit gap even when framed inaccurately — separate the framing issue from any real underlying practice issue.
steps.abort: If the practice is genuinely improper, this is not a security incident — route to regional compliance/leadership to correct the practice, not merely to rebut the claim.

steps.title: Route the response through the region-specific PR/legal team
steps.desc: Have the regional team lead the response, given their understanding of local business norms and expectations.
steps.outcome: Regional team engaged and leading response.

steps.title: Follow up until the claim is corrected or removed
steps.desc: Track responses and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Publish a regionally-appropriate factual correction explaining the practice's actual local context
steps.desc: Have the regional team publish a correction that accurately explains the practice within its true local context.

steps.title: Document the case for faster future handling
steps.desc: Record the practice, the claim, and the resolution for reuse and to inform any needed practice or communication adjustments.

steps.title: Trace the false claim's origin and spread, if confirmed misrepresented
steps.desc: Once genuinely confirmed to be a misrepresentation, identify where the claim originated and how it is spreading.

steps.title: Report the confirmed misrepresentation to relevant local platforms
steps.desc: Submit misinformation reports to platforms where the misrepresentation is circulating.

ITID-24924.def: A catch-all classification for cultural misinformation activity targeting the company's reputation that does not match a more specific sibling ITID under Cultural Misinformation, pending clearer categorization or reclassification.
ITID-24924.purpose: Intake bucket for cultural misinformation activity that does not clearly fit the defined sibling leaves.
scopeIncludes: Cultural misinformation activity with a novel or mixed subject matter not covered by the sibling leaves
Ambiguous cases pending investigation to determine the correct specific classification

ITID-24924.priority: P3 by default; re-prioritize once the specific subject matter is identified and reclassified.
ITID-24924.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR for triage, with local cultural expertise engaged as needed; reclassify to a specific sibling ITID as soon as the mechanism is clear.
indicators: Cultural misinformation activity that does not cleanly match an existing sibling pattern
vectors: Varies; any cultural-misinformation mechanism not yet catalogued
rootCauses: Novel or hybrid attack technique not yet reflected in the taxonomy
Insufficient information at time of triage to classify precisely
controls: Regional/cultural social-listening monitoring
Triage process to reclassify into a specific sibling ITID
ITID-24924.detection: Relies on the same regional monitoring tooling as sibling leaves.
ITID-24924.response: Investigate to determine the specific subject matter, reclassify under the appropriate sibling ITID, and follow that leaf's response guidance.

Average time to reclassification

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Cultural Misinformation
playbook.description: General-purpose playbook for a cultural-misinformation attack against this organization that does not fit the cultural-insensitivity, religious-offense, or business-practice-misrepresentation sub-patterns.

steps.title: Obtain native-language/in-culture review to confirm whether the claim is genuine or false
steps.desc: Have reviewers with genuine cultural/regional fluency assess the claim honestly to determine whether it reflects a real issue or is fabricated/exaggerated/misrepresented.
steps.abort: If genuine, route to communications/regional leadership for a sincere response, not a defensive rebuttal.

steps.title: Route the response through the region-specific PR/legal team
steps.desc: Have the regional team lead the response.
steps.outcome: Regional team engaged and leading response.

steps.title: Follow up until the false claim is corrected or removed
steps.desc: Track responses and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Publish a culturally-appropriate factual correction
steps.desc: Have the regional team publish a correction sensitive to local context.

steps.title: Document the case for faster future handling
steps.desc: Record the claim and resolution for reuse against future cultural-misinformation incidents.

steps.title: Trace the false claim's origin and spread, if confirmed false
steps.desc: Identify where the claim originated and how it is spreading.

steps.title: Report the confirmed-false claim to relevant platforms
steps.desc: Submit misinformation reports to platforms where the claim is circulating.

ITID-24931.def: An actor deliberately mistranslates a genuine, verifiable official company statement (a press release, public statement, or executive remarks) into another language in a way that materially changes its meaning, and circulates the mistranslated version within that language's market as though it were the company's actual position.
ITID-24931.purpose: Captures deliberate mistranslation of a genuine official company statement to alter its meaning within a specific language market.
scopeIncludes: A genuinely-issued official statement that is deliberately mistranslated to alter its material meaning
The mistranslated version circulating as though it were the company's authentic localized statement
Deliberate (not merely erroneous/automated) mistranslation intended to mislead
scopeExcludes: A wholly fabricated localized page/announcement with no genuine original statement behind it (ITID-24932)
Distortion arising from genuine machine-translation error later exploited, rather than deliberately produced by the attacker (ITID-24933)
ITID-24931.severity: Medium-High; the genuine source statement makes the mistranslated version appear authoritative within the target-language market.
ITID-24931.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the mistranslation touches on a sensitive or high-stakes topic (safety, legal position, executive commitment).
ITID-24931.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR (with native-language review capability) and legal; publish the accurate localized translation promptly through official channels.
indicators: A circulating translated statement that, upon professional retranslation, materially diverges from the original-language source
The divergence concentrated in ways that alter meaning rather than simple idiomatic variance
The mistranslated version distributed through channels not controlled by the company's official localization process
vectors: Manual deliberate mistranslation of an official statement
Distribution via unofficial local news outlets or social accounts presenting the mistranslation as authentic
rootCauses: No official, company-controlled localized version of key public statements published promptly in each key market language
No native-language review capability to rapidly verify translation accuracy of circulating content
controls: Official localization process for key public statements in priority market languages
Native-language review capability for rapid verification
Pre-established crisis communications playbook with regional/language variants
ITID-24931.detection: Relies on native-language review and social-listening monitoring in the target market; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24931.response: Publish the accurate official translation through verified company channels promptly, and issue a factual correction identifying the circulating version as a deliberate mistranslation.
metrics: Count of deliberate-mistranslation incidents per quarter
Time from detection to publishing the accurate official translation
ITID-24931.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies. Differentiated from ITID-24932 by requiring a genuine underlying official statement (vs. a wholly fabricated localized page) and from ITID-24933 by the mistranslation being deliberately crafted rather than an exploited genuine machine-translation error.

playbook.name: Response: Deliberately Mistranslated Official Statement
playbook.description: An official statement from this organization has been deliberately mistranslated into a local language, altering its meaning in a way that damages the organization's reputation in that region.

steps.title: Obtain an accurate independent translation and compare against the circulating version
steps.desc: Have qualified native-language translators independently translate the original official statement and compare it word-for-word against the circulating mistranslation to precisely identify the distortions.
steps.outcome: A documented, precise comparison showing exactly how the circulating translation distorts the original.
steps.abort: If the circulating translation is a fair, if imperfect, rendering of the original, this is a translation-quality issue rather than a deliberate-manipulation incident — correct it through routine channels.

steps.title: Report the mistranslated content to relevant local platforms
steps.desc: Submit misinformation reports to platforms where the mistranslation is circulating, including the accurate-translation comparison as evidence.

steps.title: Follow up until platforms/outlets correct or remove the mistranslated content
steps.desc: Track responses and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Publish the accurate, verified translation as the correction
steps.desc: Release the independently-verified accurate translation of the original statement through official regional channels as the authoritative correction.

steps.title: Document the case and consider a verified-translation process for future official statements
steps.desc: Record the mistranslation and outcome, and consider establishing a standing process for publishing verified translations of official statements in key regional languages proactively.

steps.title: Trace where the mistranslation originated and how it has spread
steps.desc: Identify the source of the mistranslated version and its distribution across regional media and platforms.

steps.title: Route the response through the region-specific PR/legal team
steps.desc: Have the regional team lead outreach to local media/outlets that carried the mistranslation.
steps.outcome: Regional team engaged and conducting outreach.

ITID-24932.def: An actor fabricates an entire localized piece of content (a webpage, advertisement, or announcement) styled to appear as the company's official content in a local language, when no such genuine content or statement actually exists, exploiting the target market's reliance on localized (rather than original-language) sources.
ITID-24932.purpose: Captures a wholly fabricated localized version of legitimate company content (e.g. a fake local-language page or ad) with no genuine official statement behind it.
scopeIncludes: A wholly fabricated localized page, ad, or announcement with no corresponding genuine original-language source
Content styled to closely mimic the company's actual branding, design, and localization conventions
Distribution specifically targeting a market that relies primarily on localized content and may not cross-check the original language
scopeExcludes: Deliberate mistranslation of a genuine official statement that does exist (ITID-24931)
Exploitation of a genuine machine-translation distortion of real content (ITID-24933)
ITID-24932.severity: Medium-High; markets relying primarily on localized content have fewer opportunities to cross-check against an authoritative original.
ITID-24932.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the fabricated localized content includes actionable claims (pricing, safety, legal commitments) likely to cause direct customer harm.
ITID-24932.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR (local market team) and legal; verify against the actual absence of any original-language source and issue a public denial in the local language.
indicators: Localized content with no findable original-language equivalent in the company's official archive
Branding/design inconsistencies versus the company's actual localization standards when closely reviewed
Local market audience unable to easily cross-reference against an authoritative original
vectors: Fabricated localized webpages or landing pages mimicking company branding
Fabricated localized social media ads or announcements
rootCauses: No authoritative, easily-discoverable official source for the company's localized content in the target market
No monitoring for unauthorized localized content bearing the company's branding
controls: Authoritative, discoverable official localized-content hub for each key market
Brand monitoring for unauthorized localized content
Pre-established crisis communications playbook with regional/language variants
ITID-24932.detection: Relies on regional brand monitoring and verification against the company's official localization archive; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24932.response: Confirm no genuine original-language source exists, issue a public denial in the local language directing to the authoritative official source, and pursue takedown of the fabricated content.
metrics: Count of fabricated-localized-content incidents per quarter
Time from detection to takedown/public denial
ITID-24932.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies. Differentiated from ITID-24931 by the absence of any genuine underlying statement — the entire localized artifact is fabricated, not translated from a real source.

playbook.name: Response: Fabricated Localized Version of Legitimate Content
playbook.description: A fabricated, localized version of otherwise legitimate content from this organization (e.g. a fake regional variant of a genuine ad, statement, or product page) has been created and circulated, misrepresenting the organization in that locale.

steps.title: Confirm the localized version is fabricated and not an actual authorized regional variant
steps.desc: Check with regional marketing/communications teams whether an authorized localized version of the content exists, and compare the circulating version against it (or against the genuine global original) to confirm fabrication.
steps.outcome: Documented confirmation the localized version is fabricated, or identification of the genuine authorized version if one exists.
steps.abort: If the circulating version is in fact an authorized regional variant, there is no incident — this may instead indicate an internal communication gap about the authorized content.

steps.title: Report the fabricated content to relevant local platforms
steps.desc: Submit impersonation/misinformation reports to platforms where the fabricated localized version is circulating.

steps.title: Follow up until the fabricated content is removed
steps.desc: Track platform and outlet responses and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Publish the genuine content/accurate translation as the correction
steps.desc: Release the authentic content (with a verified accurate local-language translation where relevant) through official regional channels.

steps.title: Document the case for faster future detection
steps.desc: Record the fabrication method and response for reuse against future fabricated-localization incidents.

steps.title: Have native-language reviewers document the specific fabricated alterations
steps.desc: Identify precisely what was altered, added, or removed in the fabricated localized version compared to the genuine content.

steps.title: Route the response through the region-specific PR/legal team
steps.desc: Have the regional team lead the response and any outreach to local outlets that picked up the fabricated version.
steps.outcome: Regional team engaged and leading response.

ITID-24933.def: An actor identifies a genuine, unintentional machine-translation distortion of real company content (arising from automated translation of a webpage, app, or document) and deliberately amplifies or frames that distortion as intentional or representative, spreading it as misinformation within the affected language market.
ITID-24933.purpose: Captures exploitation of a genuine automated machine-translation error in real company content to spread a misleading claim, without the attacker having fabricated the underlying source.
scopeIncludes: A genuine, verifiable machine-translation error present in real, unaltered company content
Deliberate amplification or reframing of that genuine translation error as if it reflects the company's intended meaning or policy
The underlying source content being real and unaltered by the attacker — only the framing/amplification is the incident
scopeExcludes: Deliberate manual mistranslation crafted by the attacker (ITID-24931)
A wholly fabricated localized artifact with no genuine underlying content (ITID-24932)

An internal quality issue where the company's own automated translation error causes confusion with no evidence of external actor amplification or malicious framing (a localization-quality/QA matter, not a security incident, unless and until such amplification occurs)
ITID-24933.severity: Low-to-Medium; typically resolvable quickly once the genuine translation error is corrected and the context clarified.
ITID-24933.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if the amplified distortion gains significant traction before correction.
ITID-24933.escalation: Escalate to the localization/content team to correct the underlying machine-translation error immediately, and to communications/PR to clarify the context publicly.
indicators: A translation error identifiable and reproducible in the company's actual live localized content
Social/media amplification specifically framing the genuine error as intentional or representative
Rapid correction of the underlying error resolving most of the confusion
vectors: Automated/machine-translation tooling errors in live company content
Social media amplification and reframing of screenshots of the genuine error
rootCauses: Reliance on unreviewed automated translation for customer-facing content in some markets
No monitoring process to catch and rapidly correct machine-translation errors before they are noticed and exploited externally
controls: Human review process for machine-translated customer-facing content in key markets
Rapid correction workflow for identified translation errors
Brand monitoring for amplification of translation-error screenshots
ITID-24933.detection: Relies on localization QA monitoring and social listening for amplification; not a technical/network detection surface.
ITID-24933.response: Correct the underlying machine-translation error immediately, publish a brief factual clarification of the intended meaning, and note the correction publicly where the error gained visible amplification.
metrics: Count of exploited machine-translation-error incidents per quarter
Time from identification to correction of the underlying error
ITID-24933.notes: No MITRE ATT&CK mapping applies. Scope decision: this leaf requires a genuine, unaltered machine-translation error that is then externally amplified/reframed as malicious intent — distinct from deliberately crafted mistranslation (ITID-24931) and wholly fabricated content (ITID-24932). A translation error with no evidence of external amplification is a localization quality issue, not an ITID-classified incident.

playbook.name: Response: Machine-Translation Distortion Exploited for Misinformation
playbook.description: A bad actor has exploited known machine-translation weaknesses (deliberately feeding ambiguous or exploitable source phrasing, or circulating a raw unedited machine translation of legitimate content) to create a distorted, damaging version of this organization's statement or content in a target language.

steps.title: Obtain a professional human translation and compare against the machine-translated version to identify the distortion
steps.desc: Have a qualified native-language human translator produce an accurate translation of the original content and compare it against the circulating machine-translated version to precisely identify where and how the meaning was distorted.
steps.outcome: A documented, precise comparison identifying the specific mistranslation(s) and whether they appear to have been deliberately engineered or are an innocent machine-translation artifact.
steps.abort: If the distortion is a widely-recognized, non-deliberate machine-translation quirk with no evidence of exploitation, treat as a translation-quality correction rather than a security incident.

steps.title: Report the distorted content to relevant local platforms
steps.desc: Submit misinformation reports to platforms where the distorted translation is circulating, including the accurate human-translation comparison.

steps.title: Follow up until the distorted content is corrected or removed
steps.desc: Track responses and escalate as needed.

steps.title: Publish the accurate human translation as the correction
steps.desc: Release the professionally translated, accurate version through official regional channels as the authoritative correction.

steps.title: Document the case and consider human-review requirements for future translated statements
steps.desc: Record the exploited translation weakness and outcome, and consider requiring human review of machine translations for official statements in sensitive markets going forward.

steps.title: Trace how the distorted machine translation originated and spread
steps.desc: Identify who first circulated the machine-translated version and whether there is evidence it was deliberately engineered or selectively amplified.
steps.outcome: Origin and spread documented, with a note on apparent intent.

steps.title: Route the response through the region-specific PR/legal team
steps.desc: Have the regional team lead outreach to local media/outlets that carried the distorted translation.
steps.outcome: Regional team engaged and conducting outreach.

scopeExcludes: Any activity clearly matching Deliberately Mistranslated Official Statement (ITID-24931), Fabricated Localized Version (ITID-24932), or Machine-Translation Distortion Exploitation (ITID-24933) — reclassify once determined
ITID-24934.severity: Assess case-by-case; default to Medium pending clarification.
ITID-24934.priority: P3 by default; re-prioritize once the specific mechanism is identified and reclassified.
ITID-24934.escalation: Escalate to communications/PR for triage, with native-language review engaged as needed; reclassify to a specific sibling ITID as soon as the mechanism is clear.
indicators: Translation-manipulation activity that does not cleanly match an existing sibling pattern
vectors: Varies; any translation-manipulation mechanism not yet catalogued
rootCauses: Novel or hybrid attack technique not yet reflected in the taxonomy
Insufficient information at time of triage to classify precisely
controls: Regional/language social-listening monitoring
Triage process to reclassify into a specific sibling ITID
ITID-24934.detection: Relies on the same regional monitoring tooling as sibling leaves.
ITID-24934.response: Investigate to determine the specific mechanism, reclassify under the appropriate sibling ITID, and follow that leaf's response guidance.

Average time to reclassification
